arxiv:2608.11650.rationale: Pure text-to-speech/speech generation application, out of scope under the rubric despite Speech & Audio preference; technical contribution is incremental over existing transcript-free TTS systems with jointly trained speaker encoders. Quantitative benchmark tables are provided, but there are no ablations, statistical significance tests, or detailed human-evaluation rater information, limiting rigor and evidence strength. Code/checkpoint release claims support reproducibility but do not lift relevance.
evidence: Section 3.2 describes speaker conditioning via w2v-BERT 2.0 and ECAPA-TDNN.
Section 4.2, Table 2 reports CV3-Eval cross-lingual WER/CER compared with baselines.
Section 4.4, Table 5 reports MiniMax-MLS-Test per-language WER/CER and SIM.
Section 5 states release of code, model checkpoints, and demos.

arxiv:2608.11649.rationale: Relevant LLM safety/evaluation and prompting/persona audit with structured quantitative results and public artifacts. Novelty is moderate given prior political-bias audits, and generalizability is limited to Italian entities with English prompts. Rigor is adequate but could be stronger: ordinal 1-5 scores are averaged and correlated as interval data, and some persona-effect claims are less fully tabulated. Evidence is moderately strong with refusal rates, rankings, cross-model agreement, and prompt-sensitivity checks. Reproducibility is good due to released prompts, raw data, and code.
evidence: Section 4.2 reports refusal rates by model, including llama-3.3 at 14.5% and mistral-medium-3-5 at 0.3%.
Table 4 reports entity composite mean scores and between-model SDs.
Section 4.2 reports Kendall's W=0.78 (p<0.01) and mean pairwise Pearson correlation 0.75.
Section 4.4 reports prompt-variant MAE of 0.14 and correlation r=0.97.
Table 7 reports persona shifts relative to the no-persona control.
Data and code availability section states full prompts, raw data, and analysis code are released on GitHub.

arxiv:2608.11648.rationale: No overlap with target LLM/NLP/agent/safety preferences; paper is quantum computational learning theory. Claims are theoretical and oracle-dependent, with no empirical validation or code/data.
evidence: Abstract: studies quantum vs classical examples in PAC learning, not LLM/NLP/agent topics.
Section 4.2: presents hardness construction and proof of separation; no empirical validation.
Section 2.4: relies on one-way permutations and cryptographic assumptions.

arxiv:2608.11646.rationale: Pure computer vision/image denoising paper using lookup tables and filtering; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, or language methodology. Within-domain ablations and benchmarks exist, but the topic is out of scope and capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: presents Hybrid-LUT as a YUV-based asymmetric channel-processing framework for efficient image denoising; no LLM/NLP/agent methodology is present.
Section 4.2/Table 2: reports CPSNR comparisons on CBSD68, Kodak24, Urban100, and McMaster benchmarks.
Section 4.4: provides ablation studies on channel architecture, fusion weights, and LUT configurations.
Section 4.5/Table 7: reports mobile runtime, energy, and storage efficiency evaluations.

arxiv:2608.11645.rationale: Out-of-scope privacy-preserving volumetric video streaming/system paper; mainly computer vision and RGB-D streaming, with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agentic language methodology. It reports quantitative privacy/utility/runtime evaluations, but relevance to stated preferences is minimal and capped at 0.20.
evidence: Section 4 Evaluation reports synthetic Dice/Recall 0.799/0.891, real Dice/Recall 0.792/0.908, and PODR reductions.
Table 5 provides baseline comparisons to SAM, EdgeSAM, EdgeTAM, and Tiny U-Net for segmentation and masking latency.
Section 5 Robustness and Limitations states dependence on detector quality, depth quality, calibration, and sequential static capture epochs.

arxiv:2608.11644.rationale: Relevant to text-to-SQL and LLM-assisted retrieval, but an applied database-search paper rather than core LLM/NLP research. The guided four-phase pipeline is a moderate integration of established grounding, graph exploration, and LLM disambiguation ideas, with no strongly novel architecture or theory. Reported quantitative results on BIRD-DEV and BEAVER support the main precision/F1 claims, but rigor is limited by aggregated baselines, absent ablations, unspecified LLM/embedding details, and no released code/data.
evidence: Section 4.3 reports BIRD-DEV average 94% precision, 89% recall, and 92% F1.
Section 4.4 reports BEAVER precision 70% versus 32% baseline and F1 53% versus 34%, with recall 43% versus 54%.
Section 4.5 discusses recall limitations on noisier/larger enterprise schemas.

arxiv:2608.11643.rationale: Pure computer-vision/generative-image forensics study of AI-art detection under generator shift. CLIP/BLIP are used only for reverse prompting and frozen feature extraction, with no language-model methodology, so topic relevance is low. Empirical evaluation is clearly reported but limited to one OOD generator and narrow art-image setting.
evidence: Section 3.4 constructs a prompt-aligned SD3.5m OOD dataset of 10,000 images across ten art styles via CLIP Interrogator reverse prompting.
Section 3.6.1 uses five frozen-backbone linear probes (ResNet-18, ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B0, ConvNeXt-Base, CLIP ViT-L/14) for binary human-vs-AI detection.
Section 4.3/Table 16 reports OOD balanced accuracy 0.7829 for CLIP ViT-L/14 and recall 0.5676, with all models showing large ID-to-OOD drops.
Section 4.6 Grad-CAM analysis shows weaker and more diffuse activation on OOD false negatives.

arxiv:2608.11641.rationale: Pure UAV delivery routing/robotics domain application with no LLM/NLP/language-model methodology; out of scope under rubric cap. The paper has some formal modeling and simulation results, but evidence is limited to synthetic/log-replay settings and lacks broader applicability.
evidence: Abstract: proposes Energy-Aware Wind-Resilient Routing for truck-UAV delivery under wind uncertainty
V-C Results: reports simulated mission success rates and battery-budget comparisons
V-D Validation with Real-World Wind Logs: compares methods using ASOS wind logs
VI Conclusion: acknowledges limitations such as sudden gusts and battery aging

arxiv:2608.11638.rationale: Pure remote-sensing/forest-biomass domain application using a CNN and Random Forest field calibration; no LLM, language, reasoning, agent, or NLP methodology. Tangential overlap only via CNN, fine-tuning, and general ML. The paper reports quantitative results and a structured workflow, but lacks code/data availability, exact architecture details, and stronger independent validation, limiting reproducibility and relevance to the target preferences.
evidence: Abstract reports global R² ≈ 0.78 and RMSE ≈ 22 Mg/ha, with field calibration to R² ≈ 0.82 and RMSE ≈ 15 Mg/ha.
Section 3.3 (Page 6) describes training on 281,872 patches and validation on 74,388 patches with hybrid log-domain SmoothL1 plus RMSE loss.
Section 3.5.1 (Page 10) describes Random Forest ensemble fine-tuning with 400 trees, max depth five, and 10-fold cross-validation.

arxiv:2608.11635.rationale: Core contribution is task-aware composite visualization construction via Monte Carlo Graph Search and design-space extension. LLM/MLLM use is peripheral: text-embedding similarity and MLLM-as-a-Judge for aesthetic scoring/evaluation, with no language-model methodology or training. Quantitative user-study results are reported with significance tests, but the study is relatively small, lacks baseline composition-generation methods, and key details are deferred to supplements.
evidence: Section 4.1: uses text-embedding-3-small for task-insight content relevance.
Section 4.2.2: uses Gemini-3-Flash in an MLLM-as-a-Judge paradigm for aesthetic coherence.
Section 5.2.2: reports reward function agreement rate 80.0% and Spearman 0.739 versus GPT-5.2 and Gemini-3-Flash.
Section 5.2.2: reports user ratings from 6.17 to 6.44 across task relevance, readability, understandability, and aesthetics.
Section 3.3: extended design space derived from 2,055 composite visualization designs.

arxiv:2608.11634.rationale: Out of scope for the stated preferences: this is pure computer vision/security malware image classification with no LLM/NLP/language methodology. HiResCAM/CAM provides only weak interpretability overlap. The controlled experiments, paired comparisons, and available repository are reasonable, but limitations are substantial: ResNet18-only, validation-only metrics, three seeds, and domain-specific negative results. Rubric caps out-of-scope pure computer vision applications at 0.20.
evidence: Section 1 states the main goal is saliency-guided cutout for image-based malware classification using HiResCAM and ResNet18.
Section 4.1 reports RawMal-TF no-cutout baseline 72.83% ± 0.16% versus best cutout 71.55% ± 0.45%, supporting the negative malware result.
Section 4.2 reports CIFAR-100 low-saliency cutout improving to 63.51% ± 0.36% versus 62.65% ± 0.57% no-cutout baseline.
Section 5.5 lists limitations including ResNet18-only, validation-only, and three-seed analysis.
Section 3.4 and Section 7 provide a GitHub repository and commit hash for reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.11632.rationale: Relevant to Agents & Tool Use: persistent AI agents, untrusted proposers, tools, and state activation. Novelty is incremental over prior transactional agent-memory work such as MemTX, MemTxn, and Cordon. Rigor is limited to a finite bounded model and proof sketches; no real system deployment, physical storage verification, or empirical baselines are provided. Self-critical limitations are explicitly acknowledged in Section 5.3, and Section 5.1 reports bounded-search metrics only. Reproducibility is constrained because the artifact is described but not independently available in the document.
evidence: Section 5.1 reports 2,808,230 reachable states and 5,526,474 state-changing transitions from a bounded model.
Section 5.3 acknowledges that physical storage realization, durable inclusion, and external side-effect atomicity fall outside the abstract model.
Section 6 identifies MemTX, MemTxn, and Cordon as closely related prior systems.

arxiv:2608.11631.rationale: Highly relevant LLM clarification method using uncertainty-driven synthetic data and SFT/GRPO. Moderate novelty over existing semantic-entropy and ClariLM work. Experiments include multi-benchmark evaluation, ablations, and human/LLM judging, but lack statistical error bars and rely partly on embedding/LLM-judge metrics. Code and hyperparameters are reported.
evidence: Table 1 (Section 4) reports main results on ClariLM-test, IN3, and CLAMBER with Acc, F1, CDA, and CQSS across LLM, LRM, SFT, ClariLM, CLAIM-Agent, and CLAIM.
Section 4.5 reports ablations for SFT-Entropy only, SFT-LLM only, SFT-without IG, SFT-IN3, SFT-Full, and GRPO via CLAIM.
Section 4.6 reports pairwise GPT-5 LLM-as-a-Judge and human evaluation results for CLAIM against baselines.
Appendix A specifies the heterogeneous model set, k1=5, k2=3, temperature 0.7, tau=0.45, LoRA settings, GRPO hyperparameters, and four NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada GPUs.
Section 4.4 states CLAIM uses approximately 10k synthetic training instances compared with approximately 120k for ClariLM.

arxiv:2608.11629.rationale: Pure audio/speech ASR domain for language documentation, outside core LLM/NLP scope. Research quality is modest: an open-source no-code pipeline and session-level data-selection comparison are useful but the evaluation is qualitative, uses three small Vanuatu corpora, and lacks statistical testing.
evidence: §3 Easper: The Portable ASR Workflow
§5 Experimental Setup
§6.1 Impact of Selection Strategies on Learning Curves

arxiv:2608.11627.rationale: Pure audio/speech enhancement and microphone-array signal processing using CNN/LSTM models, outside the LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning scope. Simulated quantitative results are presented, but there are no ablations, statistical tests, or real recordings, limiting rigor and generalization.
evidence: Table 1 reports SDR/MSE/LSD/APD/RSE across four simulated scenarios.
Section 4.1 describes simulated room impulse responses with T60=500 ms and Q=7 or Q=12 microphones.
Section 5 reports speech denoising SDR/STOI results for scenarios B and C.

arxiv:2608.11625.rationale: Primarily an educational-technology domain application using LLM-generated feedback as a black-box intervention; it does not advance LLM/NLP methodology or evaluation. Research quality is moderate, but causal claims are limited by a sequential cohort design, model-version confound, and workflow-specific uptake definitions.
evidence: Abstract: reports estimated uptake probabilities of 26.2% Enacted, 14.1% Directed, and 0.1% Self-Directed.
Limitations and future research: acknowledges GPT-4o mini vs GPT-5 mini model-version confound and quasi-experimental sequential cohort design.

arxiv:2608.11624.rationale: Highly relevant LLM safety/agent red-teaming paper; moderate novelty with strong controlled experiments and broad transfer evaluation, but single-turn MCQ scope and LLM-based annotation limit confidence.
evidence: Abstract: reports RL-trained persuaders raise persuasion success from approximately 24% to over 93% against the training-time persuadee and transfer at 25-83% to unseen models.
Section 4.1 Main Results: reports TruthfulQA Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct accuracy drops from 66.2% to 1.8% and PSR rises from 24.3% to 93.7% after training.
Section 4.2 Analysis: reports curriculum continual training improves GPT-4o-mini TruthfulQA PSR from 24.6% to 37.9% and identifies emergent deception and credibility-based strategies.
Appendix E Tables 2-8: provide full PSR/ASR means and standard deviations across five datasets, multiple persuaders and persuadees over five seeds.
Section 7 Limitations: acknowledges single-turn multiple-choice scope, absence of a complete defense, and lack of mechanistic explanation.

arxiv:2608.11623.rationale: Low relevance: although the paper adapts a frozen LLM (Llama-3.2-1B) with MoE, the core task is time-series forecasting, a pure domain application rather than language/NLP methodology. The FAN-based aligner, constrained asymmetric MoE decoder, and hybrid time-frequency loss are moderately novel within time-series LLM adaptation but largely combine existing components. Experiments are extensive across benchmarks, few-shot/zero-shot, and ablations, but rigor is limited by inconsistent metric counts and trainable-parameter figures, single-seed evaluation, no statistical testing, and no code/availability statement.
evidence: Abstract claims state-of-the-art on 59 out of 78 metrics, while Section 4.2/Table 12 reports 51 best and 15 second-best across 70 reported metrics, an internal inconsistency.
Section 4.1.4 states roughly 8.68 million trainable parameters, but Section 4.7/Table 10 lists FM-LLM as 14,329,800 trainable parameters.
Section 4.7/Table 10 reports different trainable parameter counts for GPT4TS across prediction lengths (94,407,376 for Pred=720 vs 12,617,824 for Pred=96), undermining the efficiency comparison.
Section 4.1.4 provides hyperparameters and implementation details but does not mention code release or repeated runs; only a single shared random seed is noted.

arxiv:2608.11618.rationale: Out-of-scope generative video compression using diffusion and transformer attention, with no language/LLM/NLP/agent/safety methodology. Technical content has ablations and quantitative BD-rate claims, but relevance to curated preferences is marginal and the paper is capped as image/video diffusion without language methodology.
evidence: Abstract: reports 50.5% and 54.0% BD-rate gains in LPIPS and DISTS.
Section IV-B1, Table III: reports -50.5% LPIPS and -54.0% DISTS versus GNVC-VD under GOP 32.
Section IV-C2, Table V: ablation shows three-layer hierarchical setting as best among variants.

arxiv:2608.11617.rationale: Medical image segmentation paper using diffusion and Kolmogorov-Arnold networks; matches only low-weight computer vision/medical preferences and is out of scope for LLM/NLP/agent-focused curation. Domain-level evidence includes ablations and quantitative tables, but no limitations discussion and narrow medical dataset evaluation.
evidence: Abstract: proposes KANResDiff for ambiguous medical image segmentation with diffusion and KAN; reports SOTA and code URL.
Section 3.1: two public datasets, RTX 4090, T=1000, batch size 8, Adam lr 1e-4, 600 epochs, five runs.
Table 1 and Table 2: quantitative comparisons on LIDC and ISIC3 subset with GED, HM-IoU, MDM.
Table 3: ablation study for ITE and RSB.
Section 4: conclusion lacks limitations discussion.

arxiv:2608.11613.rationale: Pure scientific machine learning / uncertainty quantification paper on local Sinkhorn optimal transport for random field reconstruction. It does not involve LLMs, language methodology, NLP, agents, or other preferred areas; only low-weight scientific AI and training/optimization topics apply. The work is an incremental extension of prior local W2 methods and provides theory plus numerical benchmarks, but lacks language-methodology relevance and broad generalizability.
evidence: Abstract: proposes local Sinkhorn divergence for conditional distribution reconstruction of random fields using stochastic neural networks for uncertainty quantification and scientific machine learning.
Section 2: Theorem 2.1 and Theorem 2.2 present generalization error bounds for local Sinkhorn divergence with entropic regularization and neighborhood approximation terms.
Section 3: Tables 2 and 3 report quantitative reconstruction errors, training time, and drift/diffusion errors against baselines; Figure 3 includes sensitivity studies.
Appendix C: reports training hyperparameters, PyTorch/GeomLoss/POT packages, hardware, and pseudocode for reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.11612.rationale: This is a systems/training optimization paper for Muon-style orthogonal optimizers used in LLM pretraining. It strongly matches Training & Optimization and Scaling & Efficiency, with moderate Large Language Models relevance, but has no Japanese LLM/NLP, reasoning, prompting, agents, or safety focus. Research quality is solid: formal FLOP analysis, stability analysis, multi-scale experiments, ablations, and open-source package claims. Evidence is quantitative but limited to moderate model scales and some estimates; reproducibility is supported by detailed pseudocode and links.
evidence: Section 4.1: FLOP analysis reports Gram Newton-Schulz saves 55% FLOPs over standard Newton-Schulz for T=5, alpha=4.
Section 8.2, Figure 6: Stacking contributions yields overall optimizer step speedups of 3.6x and 6.5x over standard Muon for larger models.
Section 8.1, Table 2: Dion3 f=1/4 improves validation loss over NorMuon at 3B, 4B, 7B, and 14B, with downstream accuracy wins at 3 of 4 scales.
Section 7, Table 1: Megabatching reduces per-GPU optimizer step time by 35% in the 1B/8-shard FSDP case.

arxiv:2608.11607.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/computer vision instance segmentation paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology. The work has a careful frozen evaluation protocol and matched comparator, but the stated domain cap of 0.20 applies; preference relevance is minimal and limited to transformer-adjacent Mask2Former references.
evidence: Abstract: Topology-aware query selection over fixed Mask2Former candidates for surgical instrument instance segmentation, with instance F1 and set-failure rate outcomes.
Section 3.1: The method begins from fixed Mask2Former candidates with N=100 scored mask queries and selects a subset; no language-model methodology is present.
Results/Table 2: Source test and ROBUST-MIPS support the complete path while Endoscapes is seed-unstable; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, or agent contribution is claimed.

arxiv:2608.11605.rationale: Out-of-scope as a pure robotics/embodied world-action model with video diffusion; language is only a conditioning input and no LLM/NLP methodology is studied. The paper is moderately executed but the relevance cap limits the score.
evidence: Sec. 1 Introduction: proposes ForeWAM with Future-KV and latent-action-supervised dynamics registers.

arxiv:2608.11604.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, and reinforcement learning; proposes LOFA for learning shopping agents from online purchase outcomes and in-dialogue feedback. Novelty is moderate: combines existing GRPO and on-policy distillation ideas with a feedback-aware privileged teacher. Rigor is limited by a single proprietary JD.com dataset, LLM-judge-only success evaluation, no significance tests or explicit limitations, and some table/caption inconsistencies. Quantitative ablations and scaling experiments provide moderate evidence, but generalizability beyond one e-commerce domain is unproven and reproducibility is weak without data/code release.
evidence: Section 4.1.1 describes two datasets built from JD.com logs: JD-Search and JD-conv.

Sections 4.4-4.5 report ablations for reward components and directive feedback types.

arxiv:2608.11601.rationale: This is a driving world-model counterfactual prediction paper with no LLM, NLP, or language methodology; it is a pure vision/video generative modeling application. Although it invokes causal reasoning and foundation world models, it does not align with the preferred LLM/NLP/evaluation topics, so preference relevance is very low and the score is capped at 0.20 for out-of-scope pure CV/video work. The paper provides a controlled CARLA benchmark, quantitative Vista/DrivingWorld comparisons, and ablations, but generalization is limited to short-horizon open-loop simulated driving.
evidence: Section 5.1 describes a 186-case CARLA benchmark across 72 placements and three scenario types
Section 6.3 Table 1 reports direct predictions below 0.5 on recovered-fraction metrics while Ours raises overall recovered fraction to 0.64-0.70

arxiv:2608.11597.rationale: Pure maritime robotics/RL application without language methodology; matches RL and robotics preferences only weakly and falls under the explicit pure-robotics out-of-scope cap. The method combines known curriculum learning, recurrent PPO, and reward shaping, with simulation-only evidence and moderate ablations, but no real-world validation or code release.
evidence: Section IV-A Table III reports quantitative success/collision rates for proposed PPO vs SAC, DDPG, and PPO across three simulated port stages.
Section IV-B and Fig. 10 summarize ablation results on shared policy, curriculum, and reward components, though mostly approximate percentages.
Section V states future work includes hardware-in-the-loop and real-world validation, indicating current evidence is simulation-only.

arxiv:2608.11596.rationale: Relevant as an SLM-based tool-augmented agent with prompting and reasoning, but methodologically incremental and domain-specific; moderate quantitative ablations support quality, though limited generalizability and some reproducibility concerns.
evidence: Section 2.2.4, Algorithm 1: ReAct-style observe-reason-act loop with max_steps=8, tool calls, and nudge recovery for empty final answers.
Section 3, Table 1: benchmark covers sidelobe control, single/multiple jammers, low-snapshot DOA, coherent-source DOA, and underspecified prompts.

Section 3.4, Table 5: DOA examples include ESPRIT/OMP/MUSIC/FSS-MUSIC under varying snapshots, e.g. N=16, L=10 ESPRIT RMSE 0.559°.
Section 3.5, Table 7: local runtime totals 8.99-13.45s across tasks, dominated by SLM inference.
Section 4: limitations state synthetic ULA data, fixed radar-tool suite, and no hardware or learned long-term adaptation.
Section 5: source code claimed at https://github.com/minhaj6/cognitive-radar-SLM.

arxiv:2608.11595.rationale: Pure computer vision RGBT object detection paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology; per rubric out of scope and capped at 0.20. Within its domain it has ablations and multi-benchmark evaluation, but this is not relevant to the target preferences.
evidence: Abstract: RGB-Thermal (RGBT) object detection using prototype hypergraph fusion and distillation
Section 4.2: Comparisons on DroneVehicle, DVTOD, and FLIR datasets
Section 4.3: Ablation studies for module components, loss terms, distillation strategies, and fusion methods

arxiv:2608.11592.rationale: Out-of-scope autonomous-driving test scenario generation; LLM/VLM/RAG are used as auxiliary tools rather than studied as core language methodology. Evaluation is limited to two scenario types with single-run PET values, no statistical testing or ablations, and an internal PET inconsistency.
evidence: Section 4.1.4 describes evaluation on only two scenario categories (unprotected left-turn and cut-in), limiting generalizability.
Section 4.2.1 reports PET errors of 7.0% and 9.7% as single values, with no uncertainty or trial counts.
Table 1 reports Video2Track mean PET (1.3 s, 1.5 s) while Section 4.2.1 reports fidelity minPETs (5.03 s, 3.18 s), with no reconciliation.
Section 4 provides no component ablation for the semantic mapping, diffusion generator, or Stackelberg regulator.
No code, data, or hyperparameter availability statement is provided in Section 4 or the appendices.

arxiv:2608.11590.rationale: Out-of-scope pure audio/speech generation (TTS, singing voice, voice conversion). Only weak overlap with low-weight Speech & Audio and transformer/DiT; no LLM, language-model methodology, reasoning, agents, RAG, or NLP tasks. Moderate comparisons/ablations but evidence limited by absent sample sizes/confidence intervals, no code/checkpoint release, and potential S-SIM metric bias.
evidence: Section 4.4 defines S-SIM via a pre-trained style encoder and F0-RMSE/F0-CORR but does not report sample sizes or confidence intervals for these metrics.
Section 5.2 reports relative gains such as S-SIM +41.48% and F0-CORR +121.10% for TTS based on Table 2 comparisons.
Section 7 acknowledges the model is a 43.51M DiT-S trained on 168 hours and has not been scaled or tested beyond human voice generation.

arxiv:2608.11588.rationale: Strong topical match for GUI/computer-use agents and vision-language model adaptation. The work moderately integrates test-time adaptation, structured workflow context, and LoRA policy updates; evidence is fairly detailed but limited by small held-out sets, use of reported baselines in one setting, no statistical significance testing, and no code release.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 1 reports CoAdapt-GUI 45.00% ± 1.86 versus reported Policy-Only TTA 37.50% on 48 held-out instances, with own results over five runs.
Section 4.3, Table 2 reports AndroidWorld Plus overall success 52.9% for CoAdapt-GUI versus 38.6% for Base Policy over 105 held-out episodes.
Section 5 discusses limitations including leakage control, transfer reliability, sparse feedback, and deployment safety.
Appendix C.1-C.2 provides model revision, LoRA rank, learning rate, and rollout budget details, but no code or artifact release is stated.

arxiv:2608.11587.rationale: Pure audio/speech infant-centered tagging using Whisper and LoRA; out of scope under the rubric, so relevance is capped. Internal evidence shows moderate rigor via family-disjoint splits, baselines, ablations, and quantitative results in Table 2, but the domain is specific and no statistical testing or code release is shown.
evidence: Section 3.1 describes a ~17 hour dataset from 52 families with no family overlap across train/validation/test splits.
Table 2 reports Macro-F1 and Cohen's kappa for Proposed, TL-TR, W2V-LB baselines, and ablations.
Section 4 presents preliminary test-time adaptation results with only modest improvement.

arxiv:2608.11585.rationale: Out-of-scope physical computing/adjoint-method theory paper. It addresses training physical dynamical/photonic systems, not LLMs, Japanese NLP, transformer architectures, reasoning, prompting, retrieval, agents, code, safety, multimodal-language, or any language methodology. The adjoint unification is mathematically developed but irrelevant to the requested topic scope; score capped at 0.19.
evidence: Abstract: states focus on physical computing systems and adjoint method for gradient-based optimization, not language models/NLP.
Sec. 1 Introduction: scope is optimization of parameters in physical dynamics across photonic, mechanical, and related platforms.
Sec. 11 Conclusions: summarizes unification of physical gradient methods and physical learning algorithms.

arxiv:2608.11584.rationale: Strong preference match for LLM/RAG evaluation, instruction following, robustness, and reasoning, but research quality is moderate. The paper reports clear quantitative findings and some reliability checks, but synthetic non-ideal contexts dominate (94.7% of knowledge gaps and 91.3% of conflicts augmented), natural conflict equivalence relies on n=27 with a wide ±0.2 margin, and protocol-effect analyses are observational. Main tables lack confidence intervals, and release is only promised.
evidence: Table 2: reports 13 LLMs and Loose IAS up to 83.8% versus Strict IAS 26.8% for Qwen3-235B-Thinking.
Section 4.2 Finding 2: reports Qwen3-30B-Instruct 6.6% and Claude-Opus-4.5 42.7% rejection accuracy.
Appendix B.3: reports human IAA kappa=0.85 and LLM judge kappa=0.77 on 150 samples.
Appendix A.5 Table 6: knowledge gaps 94.7% augmented and factual conflicts 91.3% augmented.

arxiv:2608.11583.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM safety alignment, interpretability, and safety evaluation. The weight-transplantation localization design is a useful mechanistic contribution, but evidence relies on small filtered subsets (mostly 30 prompts, one 100-prompt validation), manual refusal inspection, and only two matched 7B/8B model pairs. Findings are internally consistent and partially validated at larger sample size, but generalization and statistical rigor are limited.
evidence: Section 4.1, Table 2: MLP-only transplantation exceeds attention-only by at least 2.7 times across six comparisons.
Section 4.2, Table 5: Block 3 (layers 8-11) is selected first in all six greedy searches over model-dataset pairs.
Section 4.3: five of six greedy trajectories show a negative marginal effect where adding aligned blocks reduces refusal performance.
Section 4.6: larger-subset validation reproduces MLP dominance, Block 3 concentration, and non-additive composition for RealSafe-R1-7B.
Section 5.4: limitations include only two 7B/8B model pairs, filtered evaluation subsets, and greedy rather than exhaustive block search.

arxiv:2608.11582.rationale: Pure computer vision/domain application for mosquito video classification using YOLO, ViT, and ConvGRU; no language modeling, NLP, reasoning, or agent methodology. Though it uses a Vision Transformer and temporal modeling, the out-of-scope domain caps the score. Experiments include five-fold CV and component ablations, but the dataset is small/single-domain and key statistical details are lacking.
evidence: Page 1: Abstract/Intro describes a three-step framework using YOLO 11M, ViT, and ConvGRU to classify mosquito videos.
Page 3: Methodology states five-fold cross-validation and reporting of mean and standard deviation across folds.
Page 4: Results report ConvGRU performance of 88.88% accuracy, 84.45% precision, 82.82% recall, and 82.81% F1.
Page 5: Discussion acknowledges evaluation on only a specific mosquito dataset without other species or environmental conditions.

arxiv:2608.11581.rationale: LLM-centric natural-language chart editing system using GPT-5.3-Codex for intent parsing and generative UI; relevant to LLM/NLP/multimodal preferences but largely an application contribution. Modest methodological novelty; evaluation includes user study and pipeline metrics, but condition-order confound, limited comparison to prior systems, and proprietary-model/no-release constraints limit rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 3.2 states core capabilities are built on the GPT-5.3-Codex model.
Section 4.2.2 reports reduced NL requests and lower workload ratings, but total task time difference p=.053 and objective quality scores were comparable/slightly lower.
Section 4.2.3 reports intent-decomposition precision 82.02% and affected-field false-positive ratio 0.84%.
Section 5.3 notes proprietary LLM dependency, lack of automated quality checking, and reproducibility risks.

arxiv:2608.11580.rationale: Autonomous driving simulation/HD map generation is a domain application outside the stated LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent scope; the conditional masked Transformer and VQ-VAE are used only as generative tools, not as language-methodology contributions. Quality is moderate: quantitative topological/geometric results and simulator deployment are reported, but no ablations, explicit limitations, or statistical testing are provided, and reproducibility is limited to a future code release. Overall capped below 0.20 as out-of-scope.
evidence: Section III-B describes VQ-VAE road-field encoding and a conditional masked Transformer for layout generation, with no language-methodology contribution.
Section IV-C, Table II reports RoadWeaver LCC 99.9%, reachability 99.8%, dead-end ratio 10.7%, cycle ratio 85.2%, and endpoint alignment error 0.24 m.
Section IV-D reports RoadWeaver generation time of 1.39-3.50 s and scalability comparisons.
Section IV-E reports 100.0% import success into Tactics2D and 98.7% routing success over 1,000 tasks.

arxiv:2608.11579.rationale: Quantum Hamiltonian simulation compilation; no LLM/NLP/Transformer/reasoning/agents/safety/multimodal or other in-scope topics. evidence: Introduction: Hamiltonian simulation is a core quantum workload
Evaluation Table 3: Geometric mean of compilation optimization rates on HamLib
Ablation Study Table 5: emission weight threshold results

arxiv:2608.11576.rationale: Pure audio/video-to-music generation with no language-methodology component; out-of-scope under the rubric, so capped at 0.20. arxiv:2608.11573.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM reasoning and preference optimization, but the method is an incremental two-stage combination of Step-DPO initialization and self-correction DPO. Quantitative results exist, yet many gains are small or not statistically significant; direct self-correction baselines are limited (Table 3 only on one backbone), ablations are single-model (Table 4), and evaluation is restricted to mathematical reasoning (Limitations). No clear code/data availability or random seeds are described.

arxiv:2608.11572.rationale: Out-of-scope scientific ML/PDE correction and super-resolution paper; no meaningful LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent/multimodal relevance. The combined correction+SR idea has some novelty, but evaluation is limited to 1D PDEs with a single adapted baseline (P2C2Net), no real ablations/statistical significance testing, and higher-dimensional/wall-clock claims are speculative. Code link and detailed setup provide moderate reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: positions RECAST as ML correction and super-resolution of coarse-grid PDE solvers; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent focus.

Section 3.1 and Appendix A: compares with adapted P2C2Net baseline over 1000- and 5000-step rollouts.
Conclusion: acknowledges proof-of-concept limits, need for 2D/3D tests and wall-clock assessment.

arxiv:2608.11567.rationale: Traditional SVM/twin-SVM loss-function paper, not LLM/NLP/transformer/agent work. It matches the preference list mainly through the Training & Optimization category via loss functions and proximal-gradient optimization. The asymmetric RoBoSS extension is incremental, and rigor is limited by inconsistencies in the objective formulation and lack of held-out testing. Experiments cover synthetic, UCI, and financial tracking data, but no code/data availability is stated.
evidence: Section 3.1 defines the aR loss and Properties 1-3 assert C1-smoothness, boundedness, and bounded influence function.

Section 4.4 Table 9 reports annual tracking error across six stock index datasets.

arxiv:2608.11566.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application: webcam gaze tracking and weakly supervised polyp segmentation are medical imaging/computer vision, not LLM/NLP/agents. The capture-clock latency methodology is somewhat novel and the open implementation aids reproducibility, but evidence is N=1, downstream clinical utility confounds hardware with annotator expertise, and generalization is unproven; out-of-scope cap applies.
evidence: §4.1: single-user evaluation (N=1), fixed run order without counterbalancing
§5.2: webcam weak-label test Dice ≈0.000 vs EyeLink control 0.679; hardware confounded with annotator expertise
Abstract: central contribution is browser webcam gaze latency measurement and weakly supervised polyp segmentation application

arxiv:2608.11565.rationale: Pure computer-vision image registration using Fourier-Mellin and auxiliary-function correlation maximization; no LLM/NLP/language/agent methodology, so out of scope under the rubric. The work is an incremental combination of known techniques with a small simulation study (three images, five random pairs each) and limited quantitative/timing comparisons.
evidence: Section 4.1 states three 2K images and five image pairs per image were used with random similarity transformations.

Section 4.2 Table 4 reports execution times showing the proposed method is about 2.75-3.08x slower than baseline.

arxiv:2608.11564.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/robotics depth estimation using a vision foundation model (DINOv3) with no language/NLP methodology. Technical work has ablations and benchmark comparisons, but relevance is capped due to domain.
evidence: Section IV-C/Table I reports RGB-HS (Stereo) Avg AbsRel 0.105 and RMSE 3.548 versus MSCRF (Stereo) 0.120 and 5.068.

arxiv:2608.11563.rationale: This paper addresses quantum modular reduction and fault-tolerant quantum resource analysis, which is out of scope for the specified LLM/NLP/AI preferences. Section 5.4: surface-code execution time simulation for modular reduction circuits

arxiv:2608.11560.rationale: Relevant to reinforcement learning and off-policy evaluation, but outside the core LLM/NLP preferences. evidence: §4.7 reports interval-trap reproduction on the Open Bandit Dataset and public classification datasets such as covertype and digits.

§6 Threats to validity acknowledges single real setting, overlapping intervals, and that N2's zero-headroom case is synthetic.

arxiv:2608.11558.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application: atomistic machine-learning interatomic potentials for electrospray-thruster chemistry, with no LLM/language methodology. Despite quantitative comparisons to DFT/MD and ReaxFF, the relevance to the stated LLM/NLP preferences is negligible and the work is capped at 0.20 per the out-of-scope rule.

arxiv:2608.11555.rationale: Out-of-scope temporal point process / customer-return timing paper with no language-model or listed preference methodology. arxiv:2608.11552.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, and evaluation. The paper offers a systematic empirical comparison of trajectory-adapted UQ families with detailed limitations and ablations. However, novelty is moderate, generality is limited to tool-use benchmarks, and statistical resolution is constrained by small samples and wide intervals.
evidence: Abstract: study of three UQ families across five LLMs and four multi-turn tool-use datasets; transfer often useful but uneven.

arxiv:2608.11551.rationale: Communications-domain application of LLM/foundation-model priors to error-control coding, not core LLM/NLP methodology; out-of-scope cap applies despite moderate technical quality. Framework is largely descriptive, with illustrative text-only experiments and limited ablations.

arxiv:2608.11548.rationale: Pure computer-vision/image-processing color-calibration paper with no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, or language methodology; out of scope per instructions and capped at 0.20. The method is modestly novel and quantitative but evaluated on a single camera pair and small chart dataset.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: proposes a hue-split model tree for cross-camera RGB mapping; no language/LLM methodology.

arxiv:2608.11546.rationale: Out-of-scope under the rubric: this is pure computer vision/diffusion-based artistic style transfer without language methodology, LLM/NLP, reasoning, or agent components. Some method novelty exists in many-to-one global style transfer and h-space guidance, with ablations, but evidence is limited to a few artists, qualitative proprietary comparisons, and no code availability. Capped at <=0.20 for image/video diffusion without language methodology.
evidence: Abstract: proposes Global Style Transfer, Global Style Guidance, and Content Alignment Guidance for artistic image synthesis without language-model methodology.

arxiv:2608.11544.rationale: Technically self-contained generative modeling paper on heavy-tailed distributions and CVaR-penalized Wasserstein flows, but it lacks LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning/language methodology and only superficially matches fine-tuning/pre-trained terminology. Out-of-scope status dominates, keeping the score at the 0.20 cap despite some mathematical content. Experimental evidence is limited to selected baselines and figures; no code availability is stated.

arxiv:2608.11541.rationale: General ML robustness/reliability paper with only moderate relevance via AI safety/robustness and evaluation preferences; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning component. Contributions combine known predictive multiplicity and local robustness ideas using Gwet AC1 and Pareto ranking, which is useful but incremental. Evaluation covers synthetic/UCI/MNIST with statistical tests, but lacks code release and some unsupported claims, notably near-chance accuracy in ambiguous quadrants asserted only in the conclusion.

arxiv:2608.11540.rationale: Falls outside LLM/NLP/AI-methods preferences: proposes an engineering education Workforce Readiness Level rubric for smart manufacturing, with only incidental mentions of prompt engineering and model interpretability. evidence: Section 3.3.1: scoring was retrospective, and no kappa value is reported here

Abstract and Section 2.1: framework focuses on smart-manufacturing competency assessment, not LLM/NLP methodology

arxiv:2608.11539.rationale: Low relevance to AI/ML methodology: this is an HCI/Steam review study of player perceptions of generative AI in games, with DistilBERT used only as an off-the-shelf sentiment classifier and no LLM/NLP/transformer method contribution. arxiv:2608.11537.rationale: Pure computer vision/generative semantic segmentation with diffusion-based image generation; no language-model, NLP, reasoning, or agent methodology, so relevance is out-of-scope and capped. arxiv:2608.11534.rationale: Primary contribution is a medical-imaging benchmark for longitudinal CT difference reporting; despite VLM/LLM components, medical imaging is out of-scope and capped. The task formulation and change-aware metrics have domain-specific novelty, but evidence is limited by LLM-synthesized references, small physician validation (50 cases), and weak zero-shot event-level results. Generalizability beyond longitudinal CT reporting is low.

Section 4.2 Results and Analysis, Table 2 reports very low zero-shot Change-F1 across models.
Appendix A.1 Prompt Template includes synthesis and event-extraction prompts.

arxiv:2608.11532.rationale: Vehicular digital twin federated transfer learning is outside the core LLM/NLP/language-methodology scope, so relevance is minimal despite touching fine-tuning and training. The paper provides some algorithms, baseline comparisons, and quantitative tables, but evidence is domain-specific, lacks statistical detail, and has no code/model release. Novelty is an incremental combination of existing techniques, and limitations are acknowledged but not deeply addressed.
evidence: Abstract states the paper combines Federated Transfer Learning with vehicle clustering and proposes Hierarchical Federated Transfer Learning for DT-VANET.
Section 4.1.6 and Table 3 report average model accuracy 0.822 for Federated Transfer Learning compared with 0.708 CL, 0.721 FL, and 0.752 CFL.
Section 4.1.3 describes using a real-world vehicle mobility trace dataset but does not specify code, model, or processed data availability.
Section 5 lists limitations including data heterogeneity, network limitations, model bias, dynamic contexts, and sparse regions.

arxiv:2608.11531.rationale: Formal concurrency/process-calculus paper on CCSK bisimilarities; no AI/ML, LLM, NLP, or listed preference match. The results are domain-specific, with proofs but no empirical/benchmark evaluation, so overall relevance is low.
evidence: Abstract: focuses on bisimilarities in CCSK, a reversible extension of CCS; no AI/ML/LLM/NLP content.
Section 3, Definition 10 and Definition 11 introduce mixed and directional weak bisimilarity.
Section 5, Theorem 5.1 claims weak mixed bisimilarity is a congruence; proof is by induction.
Document contains no datasets, code, or empirical benchmarks.

arxiv:2608.11528.rationale: Highly relevant LLM alignment/evaluation study on group alignment-induced sycophancy, with DPO/SFT/prompt methods and safety metrics. Novel two-sided evaluation fills a gap but is incremental. Rigorous design with matched budgets, statistical tests, and human validation, though limited by single seed, coarse US-centric demographics, and conditional uncertainty. Evidence is quantitative but some findings are presented only as unresolved trends. Generalizability is limited across languages/populations/model scales. Reproducibility is moderate due detailed appendices but no explicit code/data release.
evidence: §3.4 describes demographically silent sycophancy test inputs and shift measurement
§4.1 reports matched-budget alignment gains with bootstrap CIs and cross-model sign agreement
Appendix B validates social rubric judge and demographic inferability filter via human audits
Appendix C provides training configuration and notes single seed per adapter

arxiv:2608.11526.rationale: Pure cryptography/private set intersection paper with no alignment to the specified LLM/NLP/agent/safety preferences; assigned out-of-scope cap. The paper appears technically substantial within its own domain, with formal protocols, security proofs, and benchmark tables, but is not relevant to the curated AI/ML topic areas.
evidence: Section 8 and Table 2 report comparative running time and communication results for low-dimensional L_inf fuzzy PSI.
Open Science section states artifacts are available at a GitHub repository and Zenodo DOI.

arxiv:2608.11521.rationale: Pure robotics/world-action-model paper focused on robot manipulation benchmarks (LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0) and video-action K/V-cache interventions, with no LLM/NLP methodology; the out-of-scope cap applies. The work has moderate novelty and empirical rigor within its domain, but generalizability is simulation-limited and reproduction is limited by no stated code release.
evidence: Abstract: 'World action models (WAMs) condition robot actions on predicted futures...' and reports evaluation on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0.
Section 1: 'World action models (WAMs) couple future video prediction with robot control.'
Section 5.1 Benchmarks: 'LIBERO has 40 tasks... RoboTwin 2.0 has 50 bimanual tasks...'
Appendix E: 'Evaluation is simulation-only. Physical robots and non-WAM fusion backbones remain future work.'

arxiv:2608.11519.rationale: Out-of-scope PDE surrogate/efficient-attention work with no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning relevance; only weak Transformer Architecture and Scientific AI overlap. Dynamic routing is incremental over FLARE. Quantitative PDE/LRA results and ablations exist but are domain-specific, largely single-seed, and no code availability is stated, so the score is capped near 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: introduces FLARE++ with dynamic token routing and linear O(NM) complexity.
Table 1: reports lowest test relative L2 error across all five PDE benchmarks.
Section 5.2: reports dynamic routing wins in all 21 matched (M,B) cells.
Section C.3: reports 1.3-1.5x FLARE step time and 1.18x peak memory.

arxiv:2608.11518.rationale: Classical multiwavelet filter construction and image/signal processing; no LLM/NLP/agent/safety/reasoning relevance, so preference relevance is near zero. Niche incremental contribution with quantitative benchmark tables, but no ablations, statistical analysis, or code release, limiting rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 3.2 and Table 1 provide exact recursion coefficients for New1/New2 multiwavelet filters.
Section 4.4.2 Tables 4-14 report MSE/PSNR/SSIM/MS-SSIM compression comparisons against GHM, SA4, CL, Alpert, Integer Haar, New1, and New2.
Section 4.4.3 Table 15 reports 1D denoising MAE values for Piece-Polynomial, Cusp, and HeaviSine signals.

arxiv:2608.12314.rationale: Moderate multimodal/video relevance via VLM-driven 3D world construction, evolution, and camera planning, but the core is 3D previsualization rather than LLM/NLP. The state-centric formulation is somewhat novel but builds on existing scene/video generation. Evidence includes benchmark comparisons, user study, and ablations, though metrics are largely perceptual/self-reported and lack statistical rigor; reproducibility is limited by proprietary/future model choices and no code release.
evidence: §4.2 reports CLIP-I/CLIP-T/HPS/Q-Align comparisons in Table 2
§4.3 and Table 1 report VBench comparisons
Table 3 reports user study and MLLM evaluation with N=30 and 12 prompts
§4.5 ablation studies cover BEV layout, conflict resolution, state transition, and camera feedback

arxiv:2608.12313.rationale: Relevant via agentic LLM/VLM workflows, multimodal video representation, knowledge-graph RAG-like structure, and LLM-judge evaluation, though core focus is video representation rather than language-model methodology. Novel combination of agent-native KG auto-encoding with gated textual-gradient loops, but built from existing components. Rigor is limited by small 6+18 clip setup, LLM-as-judge metrics, no confidence intervals or significance tests, and no explicit limitations section. Evidence is quantitative but self-evaluated and partly fragile in downstream subdimensions. Generalizability is only moderately supported by varied clips and four downstream frameworks. Reproducibility is weak because release claims are unverifiable and several model names appear inaccessible.
evidence: Sec. 5.2, Table 1: AVA-Encoder Overall 49.0 vs. soap2soap 28.3.
Sec. 5.3, Table 2: ablations report 49.0 full vs. 42.4 with both loops removed and 43.5 without acceptance gates.
Sec. B.6: reports 710/730 aggregate agreement between automatic ranking and human preference.
Sec. 5.5, Table 3: reports downstream reuse improves Overall for all evaluated frameworks.
Sec. 5 and appendices: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or separate limitations section are provided.

arxiv:2608.12307.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/agent/reasoning/test-time scaffolding paper, with multiple ablations and quantitative results. Moderately novel as a formalized strong-to-weak harness transfer setting, though it builds closely on existing harness-optimization work. Rigor and evidence are moderate: analyses include baselines, repeats, correlations, and item-level significance, but technique attribution is largely associational, some low-contrast comparisons are unreliable, and there is a validation-split inconsistency (5% in setup vs 2% in appendix). Generalizability is limited to text ToM benchmarks, and reproducibility is limited by proprietary future model naming and no stated code/data release.
evidence: §4 Experimental Setup reports a 3900-item hidden test set, 5% validation sample, and 72 runs with GPT-5.4-mini and Gemini-3.5-flash targets.
§5.1 Aspect 0 Main Results reports mean uplift +0.275, 100% of scaffolded runs above baseline, and best run 0.912.
§5.8 Aspect 7 Attribution states technique comparisons are associational rather than strictly causal and flags low-contrast groups with fewer than five runs as unreliable.
Appendix A Instruction Details says a random 2% sample, conflicting with §4's 5% validation claim.
§5.3 Aspect 2 reports best validation score tracks held-out performance at r=0.96, while validation iterations are weakly related to final accuracy at r=0.17.

arxiv:2608.12123.rationale: Relevant LLM-agent serving/control paper with a formal ready-cohort model, exact offline packing oracle, and device-resident decision study. It is a bounded systems measurement rather than an online runtime or LLM methodology result: no achieved share A, synthetic route bodies, one trace panel, and no population inference. Internal rigor and reproducibility descriptions are strong, but evidence strength and generalizability are moderate.
evidence: Section 5.2 describes the stationary replay grid and reports primary cell F=30.19%, P*=43.00%, U=45.85% under route-key grouping, K=256, delta=50ms.
Section 8 reports device-resident path faster in all 36 placement-cells, ratios 1.19x-2.39x, and the nested-launch negative control is slower in all 60 cells across five placements.

Section 11 Scope of inference states the trace is conditioned on one 851-session panel, the mechanism uses synthetic state and named placements, and results do not support hardware-population inference.
Section 12 Reproducibility lists code repository, dataset commit hashes, generated paper artifacts, and validation of retained evidence.

arxiv:2608.12036.rationale: Highly relevant: directly addresses LLM mechanistic interpretability, agentic autonomous research, belief-state reasoning, safety risks, multimodal LLMs, and transformer heads. The methodological contribution is novel but builds on existing AI-scientist and interpretability tooling. Rigor is undercut by author-linked human/LLM judges, small N=3 for subliminal-transfer experiments, and some deferred evaluation prompts/data. Evidence is quantitative with causal ablations and CI-reporting, but central system comparisons remain internal. Generalizability is moderate: belief heads found cross-family but interventions tested mainly in Pythia; DNA case only Evo2-7B.
evidence: §2.2 reports unsafe-response rate 48.6% for student trained on safe teacher data vs 20.3% untuned baseline (Fig. 3d).
§2.3 states zeroing L4.H1 reduces AB accuracy from 0.86 to 0.34 while PB accuracy remains 0.71.
§5.2 reports human-evaluated experiment execution reliability 92.2% for Mechanist, above Claude Code and AI Scientist.

arxiv:2608.11924.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, coding assistants, long-horizon reasoning, and evaluation. The paper presents a skill-based integration rather than a fundamental modeling advance. Quantitative results are offered with confidence intervals and ablations, but the strongest comparisons are self-reported or retrospective audits rather than controlled reruns, the topic sample is small, and reproducibility relies mainly on described artifacts and a repository link.
evidence: Table 3 reports 99.5% citation validity and 96.4% figure editability for Spark-to-Paper, versus 81% citation validity for the single-pass LLM draft.
Table 4 reports fabrication detection improving from 14% for single-pass to 92% for the full stack, with adversarial review precision 74%.
Section 7.2 states citation validity is computed over 384 references from eight Spark-to-Paper papers and 320 references from sampled human preprints.
Section 7.3 states fabrication detection uses 36 seeded probes and Wilson 95% confidence intervals, with review precision assessed by blinded raters over 57 issues.

arxiv:2608.11878.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, agent security, prompt injection, red teaming/evaluation, and alignment. The framework is a meaningful but incremental automation of adversarial environment synthesis; it has broad evaluation, ablations, limitations, and human validation, but some quantitative inconsistencies across aggregate tables and no significance testing limit confidence. Evidence is documented in tables/figures and appendices, and code, prompts, hyperparameters, and cost details support reproducibility.
evidence: Table 1 compares ToolHazard-Bench and ToolHazard-Align with prior benchmarks and alignment datasets.
Figure 2 and Section 5.1 report 512 tools, 87 tasks, and average 15.56 execution steps.
Table 2 in Section 6.3 reports BR/ASR across models and attack strategies.
Figure 3 in Section 7.1 supports claims about injection timing and placement effects.
Table 4 in Section 7.4 reports alignment improvements on ToolHazard-Bench and AgentDojo.
Appendix F reports human validation of environments, task executability, and check-function agreement.
Appendix D and Appendix C provide implementation details, hyperparameters, and token/cost analysis.

arxiv:2608.11616.rationale: Relevant to LLM agents, multimodal evaluation, and RL post-training, but the business-ideation domain is niche. Contributions are incremental over text-only patent ideation. Rigor is moderate: separated judges and ablations help, but single-run results, lack of direct human evaluation, and Table 3 lacking stated standard deviations weaken confidence. Generalizability is limited to image-text ideation and one base model; reproducibility is supported by code/dataset links and detailed hyperparameters.
evidence: Abstract: claims 30K multimodal samples and reports MBA-b/MBA-k gains over caption and multimodal baselines
Section 3.1: describes MLLM-as-a-Judge evaluation across six business-oriented PBIG dimensions
Section 4.1: provides implementation details including Qwen2-VL-7B base, LoRA rank 32, SFT 2 epochs, GRPO 1 epoch
Table 3: reports benchmark results across open-source and proprietary MLLMs

arxiv:2608.11574.rationale: Pure computer vision/hand pose estimation paper with no LLM or language methodology, placing it out of scope. The work is moderately careful with baselines, ablations, and reported quantitative gains, but the task is narrow and downstream triangulation evidence is partially presented in figures rather than detailed tables.
evidence: Section 5.1 Table 1 reports mAP 0.931 for the proposed method versus 0.895 and 0.897 for baselines on HInt.
Section 5.2 Figure 5 reports visibility-weighted triangulation yields lower reprojection errors and up to 10.1% mean improvement on HO3D.
Conclusion claims code is released as a ready-to-use package, with URL in the abstract; availability not independently verified.

arxiv:2608.11562.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/video diffusion dereflection task. The core method uses physics-grounded reflection synthesis and diffusion-based video restoration, not LLM, language modeling, reasoning, prompting, agents, or NLP methodology; only VLM-based data filtering appears. Within its domain the paper claims novelty (first video dereflection benchmark and diffusion-based one-step removal), but relevance to stated preferences is minimal, so the score is capped near 0.20. Evaluation relies heavily on synthetic paired data and human scoring, with no clear code/data release established.
evidence: Abstract: claims first diffusion-based video reflection removal model and first benchmark; no language methodology.
Section 5.2, Table 1: reports PSNR/SSIM/TC comparisons and inference efficiency.
Section 5.4, Table 3: ablates Stage-I and Stage-II losses with quantitative gains.
Appendix I: acknowledges limitations in multi-layer reflections and camera-motion parallax.

arxiv:2608.10450.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM coding agents, multi-agent orchestration, and software engineering. The paper provides detailed self-reported quantitative results, but evidence is descriptive single-run capability without controlled baselines, ablations, or causal isolation; reproducibility is limited by acknowledged missing environment details. Score reflects strong topical fit and moderate novelty, rigor, and evidence strength.
evidence: Abstract: reports a Rust C compiler with 248,989 tracked lines, 120 hours, US$44, passing c-testsuite and most LLVM/Csmith tests.
Section 4.4: reports reimplementation of 13 MESA modules in Rust, 89,946 Rust lines, and median speedups 1.55–6.87x.
Section 5.2: states no controlled comparisons for recursion causality, flat organization, or persistent records; causal boundaries unresolved.
Supplementary Table S3: reports 4,198,686,642 total tokens and US$44.3760 logged cost for compiler formation.
Supplementary Table S8: lists missing reproduction fields such as container digest, package lock, per-tool cgroup limits, exact Rust/linker revisions.

arxiv:2608.11514.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/PET sinogram diffusion paper with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent language methodology. Within its domain it includes controlled baselines and ablations, but topic relevance is minimal and research quality components are moderate, keeping overall score at 0.19.
evidence: Experiments & Results, Comparative Experiments: compares SinoDiff against DIP, ADMM-DIPTV, Residual UNet, and RED; Tables 1-2 report SSIM/PSNR/NMSE/LPIPS for FDG and FDOPA.
Ablation Study, Table 4: full SinoDiff achieves SSIM 0.9275 at 10% dose on FDG, with improvements over V1-V3.
Discussion and Limitations: states major limitation is predefined dose steps and SD sinogram requirement; no clinical reader evaluation or pathology-specific validation.

arxiv:2608.11513.rationale: Relevant large-scale empirical study of prompt framing in LLM code generation, fitting LLM, prompting, code, and evaluation preferences. Novelty is moderate: first use of influence-tactic taxonomy in code prompts but builds on prior emotion/politeness prompting. Rigor and evidence are moderate: multiple models/benchmarks, mixed-effects models, qualitative coding with IRR, and reported replication package, but inference uses only the first trial, the binary GLMM is specified as negative binomial, effect sizes are small, and no confidence intervals are reported. Generalizability is limited to Python code generation and mostly Llama-family open-weight models.
evidence: Section 3.2 operationalizes seven influence tactics plus PressureAlternative and Neutral from IBQ-G items; Table 2 provides prompt templates.
Section 3.5 reports about 123,435 LiveCodeBench and 56,745 SWE-bench Verified generations across five open-weight LLMs with three runs for non-reasoning models.
Section 3.6 reports linear mixed models and GLMM with ProblemID random intercept, and states inferential analysis used the first trial per condition for non-reasoning models.

Section 4.1 and Table 5 report Neutral outperformed Pressure (p=0.002) and PressureAlternative (p=0.03) on functional correctness, and Pressure/PressureAlternative had more Bandit warnings than Neutral (p<0.001).
Section 4.2 reports no significant tactic main effects on most SWE-bench metrics except Pressure produced higher SLOC than Neutral (p=0.0025).

arxiv:2608.11511.rationale: Partially relevant via reinforcement learning, but not aligned with LLM/NLP or language-model priorities. The paper is a moderate-quality RL contribution with clear formalization in Section 3 and quantitative baselines in Section 4, but incremental novelty over deliberation/interaction-cost work and evaluated only in synthetic/game domains.
evidence: Section 3.1 defines LQ-Learning with separate task and waiting Q-estimates and lexicographic tie-breaking.
Section 4.4 reports comparisons against vanilla RL and scalarized RL baselines across Cook, Coffee, Pong, MountainCar, and CartPole, with mean/std over seeds.
Appendix C.1 Tables 3-9 provide quantitative results including scalarization sweep values.
Section 6 Discussion acknowledges limitations to fully observed environments and proof-of-concept policy interleaving.

arxiv:2608.11510.rationale: In-scope LLM/transformer interpretability study using Gemma-2-2B and six Pythia models with quantitative congruency effects, attention/causal attribution, ablations, fine-tuning, and rule-set manipulations. Evidence is moderately strong but limited to one synthetic verbal task, attribution analysis is restricted to Gemma-2-2B, no code/data release is documented, and the in-weight/in-context competition conclusion is partly interpretive.
evidence: Abstract (Page 2): reports Gemma-2-2B and six Pythia models, with six of seven models showing strong congruency effects.
Results section 2 (Page 11): mean delta probability 0.9644 congruent vs 0.5676 incongruent; difference 0.3968, 95% CI [0.3529, 0.4407], p<1e-8.
Results section 5 (Page 13): SC attention ablation reduced incongruent delta probability by 0.8829 vs congruent 0.0962; difference 0.7864, p=1.5622e-34.
Results section 6 (Page 14): fine-tuning to amplify the default same-color tendency lowered incongruent performance while increasing congruent performance.
Results section 7 (Pages 15-16): increasing rule clauses from two to five reduced incongruent delta probability by 0.3039 (p=0.002), with middle-clause effects.
Discussion/Limitations (Page 22): authors note use of a verbal conflict task and caution that multimodal corroboration is needed.

arxiv:2608.11508.rationale: Directly relevant to interpretability/explainability via Shapley/SHAP, but outside the LLM/NLP/agent core. The relational-constraint extension is moderately novel and supported by formal propositions, algorithms, controlled synthetic validation, and broad experiments, though generalization is limited to tabular/relational settings and no human evaluation is provided.
evidence: Section 1 Introduction: proposes RelShap as a framework integrating relational constraints into Shapley attributions and claims controlled ground-truth improvement over Kernel SHAP, Conditional SHAP, and ManifoldShap.
Section 4.1 Validation with Ground Truth: reports RelShap consistently assigns greater attribution to age across all delta while baselines increasingly misattribute life_stage.
Appendix J.1 Detailed experimental setups: describes datasets, models, estimators, hardware, seeds, convergence budget, and code availability.
Appendix L Limitations: acknowledges absence of human judgment and risks from spurious discovered FDs.

arxiv:2608.11506.rationale: Weakly relevant to the LLM/NLP-centric portfolio: touches RL, agent, and interpretability preferences but lacks language modeling, transformer, prompting, reasoning, or Japanese NLP content. The paper is a controlled POMDP/RL agent study with moderate quality: clear frozen benchmark and probe/perturbation results, but limited statistical testing, small single-task gridworld scope, and narrow architecture coverage.
evidence: Section 4.2 reports early internal dynamics predict later full-safe-efficient success above permutation baseline, with Spiking Default ROC-AUC = 0.802 and Trace-GRU ROC-AUC = 0.715.
Appendix B Tables B3-B8 provide quantitative probe, PCA, feature-family, and perturbation results.
Section 6.1 explicitly limits environmental scope to the 7x7 gridworld and notes evaluation-time lesions are not retraining ablations.

arxiv:2608.11500.rationale: Off-topic under the stated preferences: computational social choice/multiwinner voting, with no LLM/NLP/agent/safety/vision/robotics content. The paper is formally developed with definitions, algorithms, and proofs (Sections 3-6, Appendices B-E), but it has no empirical baselines or code/data availability, and its generalizability is limited to approval-based voting and participatory budgeting. Final score is capped at low relevance despite solid domain-specific mathematical development.
evidence: Title/Abstract: addresses approval-based committee elections, FJR+, RBG, priceability, and participatory budgeting.
Section 3.1 and Theorem 3.4: polynomial-time verification via linear programming.
Section 3.2, Algorithm 1, and Theorem 3.5: Residual-Budget Greedy and FJR+ guarantees.
Section 6 and Appendix E: extension to participatory budgeting with project costs.

arxiv:2608.11499.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/CLIP image-classification model merging; no LLM or language methodology despite brief language-domain citations. HyperFix is a modest hypernetwork/LoRA-style correction with useful ablations but limited baselines and strong local theoretical assumptions.
evidence: Method: HyperFix conditions a low-rank correction on subset embedding z_S from task-level Gram matrix and applies it to linearly merged task vectors.
Experiments: Table 1 reports normalized accuracy across 8 image classification tasks and subset sizes, with TIES + HyperFix averaging 95.9%.
Training Cost and Computational Efficiency: reports an 82.6% wall-clock time reduction for the full |S|=8 subset compared with scalar tuning.
Ablation on maximum training subset size: Table 3 shows gains saturate after training through triples, reaching 94.4% average accuracy.

arxiv:2608.11498.rationale: Primarily an autonomous-driving RL/GNN application with LLM-based scenario generation, not core LLM/NLP methodology, so relevance is capped under the out-of-scope rule. The ego-centric relational Q-learning combination is somewhat novel and includes controlled language-structured vs random distributions and ablations, but success differences are small, seed ranges overlap, and no significance testing is reported. Transfer is state-interface only and limited to four interaction types.
evidence: §5.1, Scenario Instantiation Reliability: reports 94.2% valid on first attempt and 98.5% after one retry.
§5.1, Effect of Language-Structured Training: language-structured success 55–58% vs random-control 49–52%, with threat-attention ratio 2.1× vs 1.2×.
§5.1, Relational-Encoder Ablation: MLP 44–47%, GCN 48–51%, single-head GAT 51–54%, transformer set encoder 52–55%, ERQ-Net 55–58%.
§5.1, Recognition–control analysis: best constant action 57%, trained ERQ-Net 55–58%, portfolio union 76%, recognition–control gap 18 points.
§5.2, Scope and Future Work: limited to four controlled highway interactions, simulator-derived kinematics, and a discrete 1 Hz action space; no real-world validation.

arxiv:2608.11495.rationale: GNN model-extraction defense with adversarial/security elements; relevant to GNN and broad AI-safety preferences but not to LLM/NLP/agent priorities. GraphRP combines model reprogramming, spectral OOD gating, and a Fisher-information bound, which is moderately novel. Rigor and evidence are limited by conditional theoretical assumptions, lack of error bars/hyperparameter sensitivity, unsupported AUROC/FPR claims, and suspicious identical baseline l1 norms in Table 2. Generalizability is mainly graph classification; reproducibility has detailed algorithm/hyperparameters and a claimed code link but is unverified.
evidence: Section 6.2.2 claims AUROC >0.91 and FPR <0.06 without a corresponding table.
Table 2 shows identical ℓ1 norm=1.0 for RandP, P-Poison, GRAD, and AM across all datasets, which is not justified.
Appendix A states Theorem 5.1 relies on assumptions A1-A3 and a local second-order approximation.

arxiv:2608.11493.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM reasoning, prompting, alignment, and LLM-as-judge evaluation. The proposed SFT+DPO over paired correct/counterfactual rationales addresses a usefully characterized failure mode, but the adaptation recipe is largely standard. Rigor is limited by a single 8B model, hidden production baseline, no confidence intervals or statistical tests, and unclear training/evaluation splits. Reported lifts are quantitative but lack absolute F1 values, limiting evidence strength. Generalizability is narrow to Netflix engagement prediction, and reproducibility is low due proprietary data and no code release.
evidence: Section 3 reports 77.0% (960/1,246) balanced rationale pairs survive factuality filtering and 95.4% fit the four trade-offs.
Table 3 reports Macro-F1 lift and positive bias for each prompt format against Llama 3.1 8B zero-shot.
Table 4 reports SFT+DPO with reasoning-based inference achieves 32.19% Macro-F1 lift, the best result.
Section 5.2 defines baselines but does not report absolute Macro-F1 values for the production baseline.
Section 6.2 claims statistical parity with the production baseline at difference < 0.1% without reporting significance tests.

arxiv:2608.11492.rationale: Applied LLM fine-tuning for code vulnerability detection is tangentially relevant to LLM/code/safety preferences, but it is a domain benchmark, not core LLM/NLP methodology. The paper claims a human-verified benchmark and broad empirical comparisons, but key details such as dataset size, CWE counts, kappa values, hyperparameters, and variance are absent, and the evaluation design is biased toward the in-house corpus. Quantitative results are aggregated without intervals or sample-size support, and availability is promised rather than provided.
evidence: Section III-B states inter-annotator agreement was measured with Fleiss' kappa but reports no kappa values or category-level agreement.
Section III-F decoders use LoRA/QLoRA while the encoder is fully fine-tuned, confounding architecture and tuning comparisons.
Table II reports performance metrics without confidence intervals, sample sizes, or per-configuration variance.
Section III-H states the dataset and source code 'will be made available' rather than being provided with the paper.

arxiv:2608.11489.rationale: Out-of-scope automotive ECU security paper; no LLM/NLP/AI methods. It has some systems novelty, formal analysis, and hardware measurements, but relevance to preferred AI/ML topics is negligible.
evidence: Abstract: DACER is a runtime decentralized attestation and coordinated repair framework for automotive ECUs.
Section VI-B: reports runtime measurements for self-attestation, self-repair, and decentralized attestation on Raspberry Pi/TrustZone hardware.
Appendix A: provides false positive/false negative analysis and Monte Carlo simulation.
Section VII: related work is automotive firmware attestation/repair, not AI/ML.

arxiv:2608.11486.rationale: Low preference relevance: this is a theoretical/statistical optimization paper on finite-batch particle mean-field variational inference with Wasserstein stability, not LLM/NLP/agent-focused; only tangential match to broad Training & Optimization and Scientific AI. The math is rigorous with detailed proofs, but empirical validation is limited to a synthetic benchmark and assumptions (global smoothness, uniform curvature defect) restrict broader applicability. Reproducibility is high via public code/seeds.
evidence: Section 7, Theorem 7.1 presents the main non-asymptotic stability bound separating initialization, empirical approximation, batch, and discretization errors.
Section 8, Proposition 8.2 constructs an arbitrary-dimensional nonconvex benchmark with closed-form MFVI minimizer.
Section 9.2 reports finite-batch PAVI, full-drift, and CAVI comparisons on the synthetic benchmark.
Appendix B documents a public GitHub repository with scripts, fixed seeds, and raw CSV tables.

arxiv:2608.11483.rationale: Domain-specific agentic application for drug discovery; the LLM is used mainly as an orchestrator/argument extractor, while quantitative decisions are delegated to Bayesian optimization, Boltz-2, and cheminformatics tools. Relevant to Agents & Tool Use and LLM only superficially, and largely out-of-scope as a chemistry domain application. No baselines, ablations, or experimental validation; quantitative results are oracle-predicted and limited to case studies. Reproducibility is stronger due to open-source/code/container claims.
evidence: Abstract (Page 1): SABLE uses an LLM to interpret user-defined goals and route tasks while specialized tools perform enumeration, property prediction, affinity scoring, and Bayesian optimization.
Section 2.2 (Page 4): Single-objective CAMKK2 campaign reports a best-observed predicted logIC50 improvement of 1.03 log units relative to seed.
Section 2.6 (Page 5): METTL3 retrospective run reports a 95-fold decrease in predicted concentration, but candidate was not experimentally tested.
Section 6 (Page 12-13): Code/data availability claims open-source release, Dockerfiles/Apptainer, prompts and JSON state-dumps.

arxiv:2608.11480.rationale: Out-of-scope pure control/PDE reachability paper: no LLM, NLP, language-model, or agent methodology. It offers a moderate technical contribution to PINN-based Hamilton-Jacobi reachability with benchmark and ablation evidence, but relevance to the stated preferences is negligible and the F1Tenth failure limits domain generalizability.
evidence: Section V-C, Table I: benchmark metrics for S2R vs PINNs, RAD-PINNs, and MPC-DeepReach.
Section V-F, Figure 4: ablation studies on constraint functions, noise, and discretization.
Section V-D: discusses F1Tenth performance gap and trajectory rollout inaccuracies.
Section V-B: implementation details and GPU/training configuration; abstract claims GitHub repository.

arxiv:2608.11479.rationale: General neural-network optimization theory; matches only the Training & Optimization preference (gradient descent, learning rate, loss function), with no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning focus. The theoretical contribution is moderately novel and proofs are detailed, but applicability is limited by assumptions excluding ReLU and stochastic/classification settings, with no empirical validation.
evidence: Abstract: states O(1/T^{1/L}) convergence for general feedforward neural networks with Lipschitz smooth activations and MSE loss.
