arxiv:2608.11403.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/CoT/reasoning evaluation. Pre-registered confirmatory design and transparent limitations support rigor/reproducibility, but novelty is incremental and evidence is narrow (one benchmark, two small non-reasoning models; gate results largely null and entropy gate in-sample).
evidence: Section 3 confirms all four pre-registered hypotheses passed on the 151-problem confirmatory split, with backfire rates 60.3% Qwen and 65.6% Llama.
Section 4.1 reports pooled backfire rates of 56.6% (95% CI [49.5,63.6]) for Qwen and 65.7% ([59.1,71.7]) for Llama on 198 GPQA Diamond problems.
Section 6 Limitations discloses Llama single-sample accuracy 0.273 near 0.25 chance, one benchmark, two small non-reasoning models, and in-sample entropy threshold selection.

arxiv:2608.11401.rationale: Pure human-robot interaction/haptic shared-control study; no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, agent, or multimodal language methodology. Passing mention of RL and an unrelated LLM citation do not establish topical relevance. Within its domain the within-subject study has moderate methods, but as out-of-scope pure robotics it is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Section 5.1 reports ANOVA for maximum positional variance (F(1.64,65.70)=65.78, p<.001) and post-hoc differences confirming H1.
Section 5.2 reports usability significantly higher in highVar than lowVar (p=.004, d_z=0.76).
Section 6.4 states the study is limited to an isolated point-to-point movement task and generalizability to more complex pHMI tasks remains open.

arxiv:2608.11399.rationale: Semiparametric efficiency for Cox regression with tied failure times is a statistical survival-analysis contribution, not AI/ML. It has no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agents/multimodal methods. Within its domain, it offers theorems, simulations, and an application, but it is out of scope under the rubric, so the overall score remains low.
evidence: Abstract: derives the efficiency bound and proposes an asymptotically equivalent efficient-score estimator with lower complexity.
Section 5 Simulation: reports 1000 Monte Carlo samples, n=500, comparing Cox exact, Efron approximation, and proposed estimator on MSE, Wald coverage, and baseline cumulative hazard ISE.
Section 6 Application: reports advanced gastric cancer meta-analysis estimates for Proposal, Cox exact, and Cox Efron with standard errors.
Section 4.4 Computational complexity: compares exact Cox score dynamic-programming cost with proposed estimator cost.

arxiv:2608.11396.rationale: Quantum measurement design is outside core LLM/NLP/language-methodology scope; relevant only weakly through scientific AI and GFlowNet/optimization. The paper reports systematic comparisons and ablations, but domain-limited, code/data only upon request, and no language-model contribution.

arxiv:2608.11395.rationale: Position/conceptual paper on scientific data discovery and trust via data-usage graphs. It intersects the rubric mainly through Data & Datasets and Scientific AI, with only passing mentions of language models and agentic workflows; no LLM/NLP methodology contribution. The framework is plausible but lacks quantitative evaluation, baselines, ablations, or implementation details, so rigor and evidence are weak; reproducibility is minimal.
evidence: Abstract proposes data-usage graphs and states a prototype Data Insights discovery service within the National Data Platform, but reports no quantitative results.
Section III-B describes a nine-stage Data Insights pipeline with language-model-assisted mention/use assessment and graph construction, but no baselines, metrics, or evaluation are provided.
Section II-A explicitly cautions that network evidence is fallible and should not be treated as a vote on truth.
Section IV restates the guiding principle and implementation claim, but no empirical performance, code, data, or reproducibility details are given.

arxiv:2608.11394.rationale: Highly relevant code-LLM/code-generation paper. The graph/proof alignment plus injection-consolidation training is moderately novel but builds on existing proof-guidance and program-graph work. Quantitative benchmark and ablation results are useful, but rigor is limited by missing injection data size/steps, proof-pipeline success rates, and no uncertainty estimates; full-benchmark gains are small and reproducibility is constrained by absent code/data/prompt/template details.
evidence: Table 1: GraphAlignCoder reports 50/175 LiveCodeBench v6 and 23/148 BigCodeBench Hard versus CodeRL 38 and 16.
Results RQ3: reports structural injection raises LiveCodeBench v6 from 33 to 44 solved tasks but lowers BigCodeBench Full from 354 to 339; the full model reaches 363.

Training and Hardware Setting: reports LoRA rank 16, 2x NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPUs, 514 consolidation examples, and 65 consolidation steps, but does not specify injection data size or proof-pipeline success.

arxiv:2608.11392.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, AI safety, and LLM-as-judge evaluation. The paper contributes a fine-grained morphology of guardrail loss under single-cycle compaction and uses manipulation checks, behavioral replay, and clustered inference. However, rigor and evidence are limited by a synthetic single-cycle setting, small samples, failed Llama replication of the main contrast, same-model judging/rater dependence, verification bias, one stochastic realization per summary, and confounded normativity/salience; generalizability is narrow. Availability claims include code/data and scripts but archival DOI is pending.
evidence: §4.4 reports all-case degraded-minus-intact gaps of +34 under Qwen and +57 under Llama
§4.3/Table 3 reports unmarked GEE β ≈ 2.47 and Claude hard-cap replication β ≈ 2.29
§3.5 describes LLM judge first-pass, blinded author adjudication, and behavioral replay protocol
§6 lists limitations including single stochastic realization, synthetic setting, verification bias, and same-model judge dependence

arxiv:2608.11391.rationale: Out-of-scope HCI accessibility study on digital mental health tracking for blind users; no AI/ML or language methodology. Mixed-methods quality is moderate for its domain, but contribution is not relevant to the specified AI/ML preferences and is capped as a domain application.
evidence: Section 1 Introduction and Section 3 Methods describe an explanatory sequential mixed-methods survey/interview study; no ML model or language methodology is proposed.
Section 3.6 Interview Analysis cites OpenAI's local Whisper only for transcription, not as a research contribution.
Section 4.2.1 reports Kruskal-Wallis H(9)=5.54, p=.785; findings are descriptive/qualitative rather than algorithmic.
Section 6 Limitations states observational design and scope limited to the U.S. blind community and mental health tracking.

arxiv:2608.11390.rationale: Relevant to LLM generative engines, RAG/citation-factuality, prompt-level defense, AI safety/robustness, and LLM-judge evaluation. The repeated Stackelberg GEO formulation and VCR verifiable-content reward are reasonably novel, but the analysis remains local/quadratic and the main metrics are self-defined simulation utilities, limiting rigor and evidence strength. Broad experiments across datasets/engines/attackers improve generalizability, and code/prompts support reproducibility.
evidence: Section 5.2 Table 1: VCR reported positive Net on all nine dataset-engine settings with claimed 12.1 percentage-point average advantage.
Section 5.4 Figure 5: design-choice probes for reward scope, verification anchor, and rule disclosure.
Appendix E.2 Table 4: paired bootstrap intervals reported to separate VCR Net from baselines on the default-engine datasets.
Section 5.3 Figure 4: ablations for suspicion penalty, verifiable-content reward, soft re-rank, and reward strength.
Appendix A Limitations: acknowledges local quadratic surrogate, single-platform scope, and LLM-oracle errors.

arxiv:2608.11386.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM coding agents and tool-use. The controlled comparison of six tool architectures across multiple actors is technically sound and provides quantitative evidence, but limited statistical testing and partial external validation temper confidence.
evidence: Abstract: reports six tool architectures, three actors, and 11,700 trajectories.
Section 2.2: describes SWE-bench Live subset, repeated rollouts, and actor models.
Section 3.2 Table 2: consistency pass^k results across architectures.
Section 3.4 Figure 4 and Table 8: efficiency results for Python vs BashOnly.
Appendix B.3: error analysis supporting Atomic consistency mechanism.
Appendix B.6: generalization to SWE-bench Verified, Pro, and debugging tasks.

arxiv:2608.11385.rationale: Out-of-scope quantum complexity/QAOA paper with no LLM, Japanese NLP, transformer, reasoning/CoT, agent, or other preference-topic relevance. Formal theorem statements and proofs are present, but no empirical baselines, ablations, code, or data; score capped at 0.20 for non-relevant domain.
evidence: Theorem 1.2 states #P-hardness for Eval_p^MC for every fixed p>=2 and FP for p=1.
Corollary 1.3 extends the same conclusions to a designated two-qubit correlator.
Corollary 2.8 states hardness for exponentially precise additive approximation.
Appendix A gives depth-one QAOA expectation values as exactly tractable.

arxiv:2608.11383.rationale: Contextual bandit/operations-research paper with UCB and LP re-solving; only marginal overlap with the target LLM/NLP/agent agenda via exploration/exploitation under Reinforcement Learning. The regret claim is ambitious but proofs contain internal inconsistencies and rely on strong assumptions, and the empirical evaluation is qualitative with no code/data availability.
evidence: Lemma 3 states sum g_s^2 ≤ 8/3 β_t IJ ln(t), but Appendix A proof of Theorem 3 derives 8 β_t IJ ln(t), an internal inconsistency.
Proposition 7 concludes sum g_s ≤ 12IJβ_t ln(t)/Δ, which does not clearly follow from Lemma 3 under the stated Δ/3 gap.
Proposition 9 skips explicit verification that the derived bound sqrt(log(t^J/δ^2))+1 is covered by β_t as defined in equation (3).
Section 7 Numerical Experiments reports only qualitative trends without code availability or statistical error bars.

arxiv:2608.11381.rationale: Relevant domain-specific study of LLM specialist decomposition and GRPO post-training for financial analysis, with controlled same-model comparisons and a usable benchmark. Evidence is moderate but sample size, one preserved checkpoint, and single-domain focus limit strength and generality.
evidence: Sec. 5.1 reports specialist numerical aggregate 94.7% vs monolithic 78.9% (paired p=0.012) with judgment aggregate unchanged at 47.4%.
Sec. 5.3 reports GRPO post-training raising Qwen3.5-9B development judgment aggregate from 58.6% to 72.8% and five-task overall from 72.2% to 84.2%.
Sec. 4.3 describes 15 expert-reviewed firms/75 tuples and deterministic rubric scoring with per-task tolerances.
Sec. 5.4 reports held-out-firm overall gain +15.2 points and held-out-wrapper +4.3, led by T5 +40.4 on unseen firms.

arxiv:2608.11375.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application: the paper applies standard outlier-detection methods (Z-score, Mahalanobis, PCA, Isolation Forest, Hotelling T-squared) to district heating data, with no relevant LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/transformer methodology. Evaluation is expert-driven with thresholds tuned to expert satisfaction, no labeled ground truth or quantitative metrics, and limited generalizability to one substation.
evidence: Abstract: states the tested methods and adoption of an ensemble based on agreement of PCA, Isolation Forest, and Hotelling method.
Section 3 Methodology: describes per-hour bivariate outlier detection on transmitted heat energy and ambient temperature.
Section 4 Implementation and discussion: reports that thresholds were tuned via expert satisfaction and Table 1 provides only average outlier counts.
Section 5 Conclusion: acknowledges conclusions are weak because method adoption is based on expert inspection; no data or code availability is described.

arxiv:2608.11373.rationale: Out-of-scope quantum machine learning and oncological/medical application; no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, agent, or language methodology. Uses only AutoML classical neural networks and quantum classifiers on medical/omics/spatial data. Some methodological care exists (5-fold CV, statistical tests, classical baseline), but simulator-only, limited baselines, commercial framework, and no language-model relevance cap the overall assessment.
evidence: Abstract: reports benchmarking quantum and classical ML on oncological data and finding no evidence of quantum advantage.
Section II-C4: states training uses an ideal simulator and does not explore noise effects.
Section II-D: classical baseline constrained to AutoML-optimized MLPClassifier via TPOT2.
Section IV: acknowledges simulator-only limitation and that AutoML may not find the best classical model.
Section V: Red Cedar framework is commercial and available upon request; resource estimation tool is public.

arxiv:2608.11368.rationale: Strong topical relevance to LLM RLVR, reasoning-model training, and token efficiency; contribution adapts known U-statistic/Horvitz-Thompson ideas to adaptive rollout allocation, with solid but not exceptional novelty. Rigor is moderate: theoretical sections and ablations are extensive, but main comparisons lack reported confidence intervals/error bars despite bootstrap claims, and exact reproducibility is limited by no code/data release.
evidence: Section 6.1/Table 1 reports Pair Qwen3-1.7B average 49.2 vs DUET 48.0 and tokens 0.49 vs GRPO 1.00.
Section 6.2/Table 2 reports adaptive unweighted bias 2.27e-2 versus Pair HT bias 1.90e-3 at matched relative suffix cost.
Section 6.3/Table 3 reports removing pair-inclusion correction drops accuracy from 49.2 to 47.1 and raises gradient MSE from 0.145 to 0.218.
Limitations state the exact guarantee covers only the unclipped, unstandardized leave-one-out score gradient, with clipping/standardization treated as practical approximations.

arxiv:2608.11367.rationale: Classified as out-of-scope pure computer vision/domain application: the core task is gaze target estimation, with text used only as a conditioning prompt and frozen vision-language encoders, not LLM/NLP methodology. The PGE task and dataset are somewhat novel within that domain, but quantitative claims are unverifiable because the supplied tables are placeholders and no numeric results, statistical tests, or limitations are included, so overall score is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: claims PGE task, Gaze-Co 120K dataset, and open-sourced GazeAnywhere model.
Section 3.2: describes frozen image/text encoders, detector transformer, and three decoders.
Section 5.2: claims SOTA on PGE benchmarks and OOD Child-SC, but no numeric table content is included in the supplied text.
Section 5.3/Appendix 13: lists ablation studies, but the provided tables are placeholders without actual values.

arxiv:2608.11364.rationale: Out-of-scope HCI accessibility paper on non-visual qualitative data visualization for blind and low-vision users. It contains no LLM, NLP, transformer, agent, or language-model methodology; the recommendation layer is explicitly rule-based with no generative model. The RITE user study is formative and transparent about limitations, but the small sample, iterative system changes, and domain-specific focus limit relevance and generalizability for an AI/LLM curation portfolio.
evidence: Section 4.2.1 states the detection layer is entirely rule-based and no generative model is involved at any stage.
Section 5.5 describes a 120-minute RITE-based usability study with 8 BLV participants; it does not evaluate language or AI methods.
Section 7.4 acknowledges small sample size, system changes between sessions, and the need for a fixed-system summative evaluation.

arxiv:2608.11363.rationale: Pure robotics/embodied AI paper on pre-trained VLA robot policy adaptation from minimal demonstrations using RL. Despite using a vision-language-action model and flow-matching/LoRA, it does not advance LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology and is out of scope per rubric. Empirical evaluation is moderately developed with sim and real-world results, ablations, and baselines, but limited seeds/sample sizes and sharp generalization drops under state shifts.

arxiv:2608.11362.rationale: Theoretical molecular computing paper on reversible chemical reaction networks; no LLM/NLP/AI methodology. Only a marginal low-weight match to scientific AI via chemistry/mathematics/proof. Formal definitions exist but proofs are often sketchy, deferred, or handwavy, and there is no empirical validation or code/data.

arxiv:2608.11361.rationale: Relevant to LLM serving/training efficiency but not core language/reasoning/safety directions. The lifecycle-cost framing is incremental over prior tokenizer cost/scaling work. Experiments are controlled but small-scale (<=2.3B, 5k steps, English-only) and rely partly on isolated head measurements without a fully integrated end-to-end serving benchmark; no code/data availability is stated. Quantitative tables support the main batch-dependent shift, but quality differences are within <2% and limitations are acknowledged.
evidence: Section V-B reports V_infer* = 32768 at B=1 and 524288 at B=64, a 16x shift.
Table IV reports <2% BPB spread and training-cost minimum at V=16384.
Table V reports quality optimum at V=65536 at 1.3-2.3B scale.

arxiv:2608.11359.rationale: Pure domain application of a time-series foundation model (Chronos-2) to electricity price forecasting; no language/LLM methodology despite LoRA and foundation-model terms, so the out-of-scope cap applies. The paper includes ablations, controls, and statistical tests, but gains are modest and evaluation is limited to four Chinese provincial markets with degraded interval calibration.
evidence: Section III-B1: Table II reports average MAE/RMSE of 74.63/137.87 for gated LoRA across the four held-out markets.
Section III-B2: Table IV reports pooled Gated-vs-Source DM statistic of -1.45, significant only at p<0.10.
Section III-C4: Limitations acknowledge the modest four-market corpus and that interval calibration remains an open issue.

arxiv:2608.11357.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM multi-agent systems and agent evaluation. The paper proposes a functional taxonomy of collective failures and uses matched mechanism-breaking controls, which is moderately novel but largely a reframing of established multi-agent and group-decision ideas. Rigor is limited by synthetic core ecologies, small natural-task panels, sparse implementation detail, and limited real-world validation. Evidence supports several claimed effects, but many intervals are wide or null, and the paper itself notes simulation and provider-version limits. Generalizability beyond the controlled ecologies is uncertain; reproducibility is low due to missing code, data, and exact prompts.
evidence: Section 4 reports distributed-evidence valid 5-call 8B institution exceeds the 5-call raw 70B system by +0.58 [0.44, 0.72].
Section 7 and Table 1 report fixed-evidence interface results, with graph minus ordered accuracy of -0.067 [-0.128, -0.010].
Section 10 Limitations states adaptive strategic behavior remains simulation evidence and natural execution panels are smaller than the offline retrieval audit.

arxiv:2608.11354.rationale: LLM-centric inverse Theory-of-Mind and abductive reasoning for persona-based user modeling; strongly relevant to LLM, reasoning, and ToM. Moderate novelty in multi-hypothesis persona synthesis, but evaluation is limited to one dataset (OPeRA, N=46) with small per-task samples, limited statistical testing, and no code release. Evidence includes quantitative tables but some results (Hit@3=100%) are fragile and generalization is only illustrative beyond shopping.
evidence: Section 3 describes the five-stage LLM pipeline: action summarization, percept reconstruction, backward belief inference, MMR optimization, and multi-hypothesis persona synthesis.
Section 4.1 states evaluation uses the OPeRA train split of 46 complete user profiles.
Table 1 reports next action prediction results and Table 4 reports Big Five ablation comparing multi-hypothesis to direct inference and questionnaire.
Section 6 Limitations acknowledges single-domain Amazon shopping, N=46, compressed prediction variance, and an illustrative XR case study.

arxiv:2608.11352.rationale: Moderate relevance via Transformer architecture, NLP/multimodal translation, and efficiency, but no LLM/reasoning/agent focus. Applies known ODE/Runge-Kutta updates to iterative sign language translation; incremental novelty. Rigor is moderate: two benchmarks, matched IPSLT baseline, ablations, efficiency metrics, but dev-selected configurations lack significance testing and explicit limitations. Evidence from Tables 1-8 supports quantitative claims.

Section 4.2 and Table 3 compare CSL-Daily BLEU-4 for RK2SLT/RK4SLT and IPSLT baseline

arxiv:2608.11349.rationale: Applied water-treatment RL/offline hyperparameter-selection paper with weak match to RL/training preferences and no LLM/NLP; treated as out-of-scope domain application and capped low. Contributions are mostly a first real-world application of existing calibration models, with mixed DTW/qualitative evidence and limited generality.
evidence: Abstract: claims first application of calibration models in a municipal water treatment plant and proof-of-concept.
Section 3.4: kNN rollouts resemble PIT300 data; NN/GRU baselines collapse after ~50-100 steps.
Table 1: DTW results are mixed across 1-week vs 12-month kNN models.
Section 4.1: calibration model struggles to capture specific distribution shifts, mismatching Online sensitivity curves.
Appendix B: provides training details/hyperparameters but no code/data availability.

arxiv:2608.11348.rationale: Topically relevant to LLM safety/backdoor detection, but the method is simple and evaluated in a narrow, unrealistic setting: 80% poisoned training data, six models, lexical keyword trigger matching, no statistical testing. Evidence is descriptive rather than strongly validated, and generalizability is limited by the artificial attack setup.
evidence: Section III-C reports 80% backdoor samples and 20% benign samples, far above realistic low poisoning rates.
Abstract and Section V-A report 92.0% pooled precision but 19.2% recall, with one model never triggered.
Section V-G acknowledges false positives from keyword-based trigger matching and that realistic poisoning rates were not tested.

arxiv:2608.11345.rationale: Software engineering merge-tool paper; does not address LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, code generation, or AI/ML methods. It is a domain-specific programming-language infrastructure study. Some empirical rigor and artifact availability are noted, but preference relevance is minimal, capping the score at or below 0.20.
evidence: Section 4.3.4 reports 21,615 merge scenarios from 513 repositories
Table 1 in Section 5.1 reports aFPs/aFNs across Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, and Rust
Artifact Availability states a replication package includes dataset, exact tool versions, and scripts

arxiv:2608.11344.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM-based agentic AI, agents/tool use, governance, explainability, and reproducibility. The Verifiability Gap and reproducibility-profile framing are conceptually novel, though they extend known explainability/reproducibility concerns. Rigor is moderate: formal theory and controlled studies are present, but empirical evidence is mechanism-focused with small constructed case samples and limited statistical inference. Generalizability beyond FinTech is claimed but not empirically demonstrated. Reproducibility is comparatively strong due to detailed data/code availability claims.
evidence: Section 7.3 reports release-timeline drift and decoding-control experiments; Table 6 reports local 320/320 reproducibility versus hosted 319/320 and 959/960.
Section 7.4 reports orchestration sweep results with exact trace reproducibility zero in all configurations and verdict-differentiation collapse.
Section 7.5 reports a deterministic credit-model experiment where current outcome reproducibility is 1 but historical fidelity is 0 for case 2270.
Data availability states a pub-code package regenerates every reported statistic offline without an API key, though hosted arms are not reproducible.

arxiv:2608.11343.rationale: Moderately relevant multimodal retrieval evaluation comparing native multimodal embeddings with frontier LLMs as zero-shot visual rankers. It matches Multimodal AI and RAG/embedding preferences but does not advance LLM or NLP methodology. Novelty is modest: an API-based empirical comparison on one hard-negative setup. Rigor is reasonable with bootstrap CIs, McNemar/Wilcoxon tests, and contingency tables, but limited to Flickr30k, 25-image candidate sets, and caption-space hard negatives. Evidence is moderate but based on proprietary snapshots and a single dataset; reproducibility is constrained by paid APIs and no released data/code.
evidence: Abstract: reports first direct comparison of native multimodal embeddings vs LLM visual ranking on Flickr30k and low-latency advantage for precomputed embeddings.
Section 4/Table 1: reports GE2, GPT-4.1, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 statistically indistinguishable on R@1 and MRR, while Amazon Nova 2 is significantly lower.
Appendix B/Table 3: reports R@1, R@3, and MRR with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for all systems.
Limitations: acknowledges single-dataset evaluation, 25-image candidate sets, caption-space hard negatives, and proprietary API access.

arxiv:2608.11342.rationale: Directly relevant LLM personalization/efficiency work with a training-free logit-space method, but evaluation is narrow and evidence is moderate. Novelty is incremental relative to decoding-time steering and NTK-inspired methods. Rigor is limited by small 50-author evaluations, no error bars or significance tests, strong theoretical assumptions, and hand-wavy complexity comparisons. Generalizability is weak beyond three LaMP tasks. Reproducibility is moderate: detailed hyperparameters are provided, but no code or statistical details are supplied.
evidence: Table 1 reports Qwen3-8B average R-1/R-L: WFT 0.335/0.296 vs SFT 0.321/0.293.
Table 2 reports Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct average R-1/R-L: WFT 0.287/0.237 vs SFT 0.259/0.219.

arxiv:2608.11341.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM/agent evaluation and foundation-model engineering through the heavy-duty solver and TRACES benchmark. Novel framework and HDS6 process verification, but empirical support is moderate: many ablations are descriptive/single-run, no statistical testing, missing table references, and hidden ground truth plus limited artifact details reduce reproducibility.
evidence: Section 3.1.2 defines HDS6 as six process dimensions named by TRACES: Tools, Repair, Alternatives, Coherence, Evidence, Scope.
Table 5 reports apodex-1.1 scores of 0.904 viability, 0.635 tropism, 0.649 structure, and 0.180 design versus published SOTA 0.878/0.622/0.605/0.116.
Table 7 reports public-100 normalized continuous scores of GPT-5.5 53.78 no-env vs 56.30 with env, and GPT-5.6-sol 54.21 vs 61.81.
Table 13 reports verification-driven repair aggregate outcome delta +0.155 over 434 deficient trajectories, with 204 improved and 86 declined.
Section 4.3.2 states each instance has one run, so observed run-to-run variance limits causal interpretation of small differences.

arxiv:2608.11340.rationale: In-scope via LLM coding agents and program-repair methodology, though the core application is network verification, which tempers relevance. The CEGIS-style oracle-guided evolution of an SMT network verifier is a novel integration, but evidence is early-stage: three features, one verifier, six LLM runs, no formal coverage guarantees, and no code release.
evidence: Abstract: prototype taught a 3,000-line SMT-based verifier OSPF areas, BGP route reflection, and L3VPN over EVPN using a coding agent and trusted oracle.
§2.2: differential testing is defined via soundness and completeness SMT queries against Oracle routing state.

§3.3: reports significant performance divergence between converged models and two-round improvement under a generic scaling instruction.
§4: explicitly states testing guarantees are incomplete and poses coverage/trust as open problems.

arxiv:2608.11338.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, code-based skill learning, and tool use; clear but incremental contribution over existing programmatic skill methods. Evaluation is fairly broad across three environments and multiple backbones with ablations, but full ablations are limited by cost and statistical/reporting details are partial. Reproducibility is supported by detailed appendices but weakened by no code release and use of a future model version.
evidence: Section 5 Results reports SpeedRunner substantially reduces cost on every benchmark and achieves the strongest final performance on all three benchmarks.
Section 6.1 and Figure 4 report ablations showing removal of the code interpreter degrades efficiency considerably.
Table 1 reports SpeedRunner learns deeper and denser call graphs than ASI and Voyager.
Section 6.3 reports SpeedRunner improves over baseline in every zombie-frequency condition for Crafter.
Appendix H Table 2 reports SpeedRunner learns compact but more structured skill libraries than baselines.

arxiv:2608.11337.rationale: Paper is a formal methods/wireless security study of Bluetooth/Wi-Fi privacy attacks and mitigation. It has no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, multimodal AI, or AI-safety methodology; only tangential keyword overlap with attack/vulnerability/defense. Within its domain it shows moderate formal modeling rigor (Tamarin lemmas, limitations, artifacts), but it is outside the stated AI/ML preference scope, so relevance is near zero and overall score is capped low.

arxiv:2608.11335.rationale: Clinical text-guided medical image segmentation is a domain-specific medical imaging application and is explicitly out of scope despite using a frozen PubMedBERT text encoder and cross-modal components. The method is an incremental combination of spatial cross-attention and DCT/FiLM frequency modulation with limited novelty beyond prior frequency-domain multimodal segmentation. It provides ablations and quantitative comparisons but lacks statistical significance testing, error bars, or a limitations analysis, and generalization is limited to two COVID-19 chest imaging datasets.

Section 3, Table 2 reports component ablations with Dice/mIoU/HD95

arxiv:2608.11047.rationale: Moderate LLM/reasoning/evaluation relevance with financial QA focus; novel but incremental over symbolic benchmark generators. Rigor is undermined by internal contradictions (e.g., OCR vs unit/scale perturbation), small n, no statistical tests, and limited compute acknowledged. Evidence is quantitative but weak due to non-standard model names and no confidence intervals. Generalizability beyond finance is plausible but unproven. Reproducibility is partially supported by code link and hyperparameters, though data/model details are incomplete.
evidence: Abstract claims OCR-style character corruption is the most effective adversarial perturbation; Table 4 shows unit/scale shift is far more harmful (e.g., Gemma-31B 3.0% on 10Q vs OCR 82.0%), contradicting the abstract.
Section 7 acknowledges restricted compute, English-only documents, a single table-formatting convention, small n=90 evaluation set, and no multiple trials.
Section 5.3 reports LoRA hyperparameters selected on the same held-out n=90 (baseline 81.1%, best 85.6%) and FinQA generalization tested on n=100 with +5 points.

arxiv:2608.11045.rationale: Relevant to LLM and quantization/efficiency preferences, but not to Japanese NLP, reasoning, or agent topics. Moderate novelty in using conditional diffusion and spectral selection to guide midpoint-ambiguous rounding. Comparisons and ablations are provided, but reported gains over RTN are often small and lack significance testing or larger-model validation. Reproducibility is strong with code, checkpoints, hyperparameters, and detailed appendices.
evidence: Table 1 and Table 2 compare calibration-free weight-only PTQ across five small LLMs at W4A16 and W3A16.
Table 4 reports component ablations on OLMo 2 1B, isolating reconstruction guidance, position-dependent tolerance, and spectral selection.
Appendix C describes diffusion training and inference details, including patch construction, conditioning, hardware, and hyperparameters.
Section 5 discusses limitations such as per-model diffusion cost, weight-space-only selection, and evaluation restricted to small LLMs.

arxiv:2608.11044.rationale: Moderately relevant LLM/NLP hierarchical text classification paper using LLM-generated keywords and pseudo-samples. Relevance is solid but application-oriented rather than core LLM study. Novelty is incremental over TaxoClass/TELEClass. Rigor is limited: only two datasets, no significance tests or error bars, no ablation results despite a conclusion claiming them, and some reporting inconsistencies. Evidence rests on main comparison tables and one-dataset sensitivity analysis, but lacks ablation/statistical support. Generalizability is moderate across two public English datasets. Implementation details are provided, but no code/release and some methodological ambiguities limit reproducibility.
evidence: Section IV-C / Table II reports TEAMMix Example-F1 0.6331 on Amazon-531 and 0.8590 on DBPedia, while Table III reports GPT-4 subset Example-F1 0.6994.
Section IV-B provides implementation details including ChatGLM-4-9B, BERT-base-uncased, AdamW lr 5e-5, batch size 32, 10 epochs, and RTX 4090.
Section IV-D describes sensitivity analysis for alpha and epsilon on the Amazon-531 dataset only.
Section V claims ablation studies analyze module contributions, but the supplied text contains no ablation section or results.
Table I and Section IV-A1 list DBPedia-298, while Table II header says DBPedia-296, indicating a reporting inconsistency.

arxiv:2608.11042.rationale: Out-of-scope quantum metrology paper with no LLM/NLP/agent/vision/reasoning relevance. It provides a theoretical study of ancilla dimension in quantum channel estimation. Within its domain it has some novelty via the k-ancilla Fisher information and rank characterization, but it lacks empirical evidence and one proof introduces a condition not clearly stated in Theorem 3(i). Overall capped at 0.20 as a non-AI/ML domain contribution.
evidence: Abstract describes k-ancilla Fisher information and entanglement depth in quantum channel estimation.
Section IV Theorem 2 gives a rank characterization of the optimal ancilla dimension.
Section VII provides special-case examples (unitary, depolarizing, amplitude damping).
Theorem 3(i) proof (Section V) additionally assumes each prepared state is realizable as a fixed-input channel output, which is not stated in the theorem.

arxiv:2608.11037.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/computer vision facial phenotyping application with no LLM/NLP language methodology; rubric caps it at 0.20. Within its domain, it has moderate methodological quality including held-out validation, 10-fold CV, paired bootstrap tests, and ablations, but external validity is limited to GMDB/GM-Arc and controlled-access data.
evidence: Abstract: AI-assisted facial phenotyping retrieves visually similar diagnosed cases from facial image reference databases; no language model methodology.
Section 3.4.1: Defines patient-weighted disorder centroids for gallery aggregation.
Section 4.4: Reports top-1 accuracy improvements from 38.52% to 48.82% on GMDB-Freq and 19.38% to 23.79% on GMDB-Rare under full aggregation.
Data and code availability: GMDB v1.1.4 is controlled-access; code will be available upon acceptance.

arxiv:2608.11036.rationale: Pure ASR/speech domain adaptation for Burmese medical audio; ties to Speech/Audio, fine-tuning, and Transformer only, so it is largely out of scope for the stated LLM/NLP/agent preferences. Contributions are incremental domain-specific Whisper fine-tuning on a small corpus. Rigor is limited by internal corpus-size inconsistencies, unsupported SOTA claim relative to a reported 19.0% baseline, single-epoch training, no significance testing, and limited speaker diversity.
evidence: Abstract: describes a high-quality 28-hour corpus, while Section 4/Table 1 reports 52.95 h train and 2.87 h eval with Table 1 total 55.82 h after adding simulated room acoustics, creating inconsistent corpus-size reporting.
Section 1: reports prior myMediCon baseline WER of 19.0%; Section 7 claims state-of-the-art WER of 23.44%, which conflicts with that earlier baseline and weakens the SOTA claim.
Section 4: optimization uses a single epoch with batch size 4 and does not report multiple seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

Section 4: only nine native speakers (two male, seven female) are used, and robustness evaluation relies on simulated noise profiles and synthetic room impulse responses, limiting real-world clinical generalizability.

arxiv:2608.11034.rationale: LLM pre-training reliability is relevant to LLM/training infrastructure but not core language-model methodology. The design is coherent and somewhat novel, but validation is limited to a 16-GPU software fault-injection testbed without competitive baselines or measured production overhead, so evidence and generalizability are weak.
evidence: §10.2/Table 3 reports fault-injection coverage on 16-GPU jobs, including 344/344 dense numerical SDC localization and 120/120 hang launches, but these are software injection cells rather than production physical failures.
§11 explicitly limits evaluation to at most 16 A100 GPUs over two hosts and notes no end-to-end throughput/resource overhead, comparison, or ablations were measured.
§10.3/Table 4 reports MoE shape compression ratios (e.g., 3,457 to 16 representatives), but §11 limits qualification to uniform expert row counts and a fixed environment.

arxiv:2608.11033.rationale: Relevant multi-agent LLM framework for audience-aware XAI narratives with substantial evaluation. Contributions are incremental over prior narrative XAI/agent systems; evaluation is extensive for LLM judges but the human study is small, non-comparative, and only tests XstrAI. Generalizability is limited to SHAP on two tabular medical datasets. Reproducibility is undercut by unverifiable or possibly non-existent model identifiers and code link.
evidence: Section 4.2 describes 11 baseline configurations and model backbones.
Section 5.2.2 reports Elo score rankings with statistical tests.
Section 5.2.3 reports human evaluation with only 15 participants and no baseline comparison.
Section 4.3.1 details semantic-accuracy evaluation using reference corpora.

arxiv:2608.11030.rationale: Relevant LLM/RAG patent matching paper, but incremental and weakly substantiated. Evaluation uses only accuracy on 1,000 PatentMatch instances, with no ablations, statistical tests, or code/prompt release. Table II contradicts the claimed consistent improvement: Qwen2-Instruct-7B Ours scores 52.1 overall vs RAG 58.7, and 34.4 vs 49.2 English.
evidence: Section IV-A1 Dataset: PatentMatch has 1,000 instances (500 Chinese, 500 English), with a 300,000-patent retrieval collection.
Section IV-A2 Evaluation Metrics: Accuracy is the primary metric.

Section IV-B Main Results, Table II: Qwen2-Instruct-7B Ours achieves 34.4 English, 69.8 Chinese, 52.1 overall; RAG achieves 49.2 English, 68.2 Chinese, 58.7 overall, contradicting the claim of consistent enhancement.
Section IV-C Case Study: only qualitative comparison between Vanilla LLM and the proposed prompting.
Section V Conclusion: future work on dynamic ontology and multimodal data is stated, but no explicit limitations or code availability are mentioned.

arxiv:2608.11027.rationale: Directly studies LLM output behavior across 32 models using label-free temporal and cross-family comparisons, with strong preference fit. Multiple constructions and robustness checks support the claims, but limitations include single responses per model-prompt pair, no released code, observational trends, and a fixed English-centric prompt bank.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: applies a 10,000-prompt bank to 32 models from six families and constructs three sentence-level dissimilarities plus token-level MMD.
Page 5 Table 2: reports same-family nearest-neighbor rates of 21/32, 17/32, and 14/32 and Spearman correlations of 0.92 and 0.77 across constructions.
Page 13 Table 7: encoder robustness across four encoders yields Spearman rho 0.92-0.93, same-family nearest-neighbor counts 19-22/32, and convergent trend r -0.52 to -0.55.
Page 7 Discussion and Limitations: notes one response per model-prompt pair, GW 256-prompt subsample, observational release-date trends, and unobserved training-side quantities.

arxiv:2608.11025.rationale: Strongly relevant to LLM safety, alignment, interpretability, and red-teaming/evaluation via SAE-based analysis of emergent misalignment. Methodologically solid with multi-model experiments, random-feature and random-document baselines, and quantitative results, but limited by manual feature curation, LLM-judge evaluation, correlational data attribution, and only promised code/data release.
evidence: Section 3.1 Results reports induced EM across four models with misalignment rates between 16.67% and 35.00% across domains.
Table 2 in Section 4.1 reports Gemma 3 27B steering MR of 62.08% versus fine-tuning maximum MR of 35.00%.
Section 4.2 Random-Feature Baseline reports mean best coherent MR of 0.06%, 0.06%, and 0.20% for random features versus 4.63%, 2.22%, and 3.28% for selected features, with p<.001.
Section 5.3 Tables 3 and 4 show reformatted human-written documents fail to induce coherent EM while synthetic instruction-response pairs from the same content induce MR up to 10.42%.
Limitations state data attribution is correlational and does not establish that identified documents causally contributed during pre-training.

arxiv:2608.11024.rationale: Relevant multimodal VLM hallucination/interpretability study with a mechanistic diagnostic and routed remediation. Strengths include three model families, quantitative FPR comparisons, and explicit limitations. Main weaknesses: the central δ_vis-hallucination correlation is largely tautological because sign(δ_vis) is reported to match the hallucination label; calibration/adapt training details and statistical support are incomplete; no code release; targeted evaluation limits generalizability.
evidence: Abstract: reports VSNR visual/prior decomposition over 10,791 negative-ground-truth samples across three VLM families and three attribute types.
Table II: Spearman correlations show δ_vis 0.755-0.835 versus δ_prior 0.066-0.177, with prior-only accuracy 58.5-59.0%.

Scope and limitations: binary yes/no decomposition may not capture all free-form hallucination; VISOR-Adapt targets six high-FPR material words (16.1% of material test samples) and open-vocabulary coverage is not evaluated.
Reproducibility section: models and greedy decoding/seed are stated, but no code release or detailed LoRA/calibration hyperparameters and train/test splits are provided.

arxiv:2608.11022.rationale: Moderate relevance: uses LLMs as consumers and LLM-as-judge for workflow-provenance QA, with agentic/workflow documentation framing, but not core LLM methodology. Novelty is incremental: extends Model/Data Cards to execution provenance. Rigor is limited by synthetic Benchmark I content, a single real workflow for Benchmark II, LLM-judge self-evaluation, and high reported variability. Evidence is quantified but lacks robust statistical validation. Generalizability beyond ML workflows is unproven, while reproducibility is strong due to released template, prompts, questions, and code.
evidence: Sec. IV-B: Workflow Card reaches 0.619 vs 0.611 all-cards reference and leave-one-out drops to 0.265
Sec. IV-C: moving from schema-based querying to Workflow Cards improves mean rating from ~0.45 to ~0.87
Sec. V: Benchmark I uses synthetically generated fields; Benchmark II covers a single workflow assessed by one human evaluator

arxiv:2608.11020.rationale: PINN/scientific computing paper on finite-difference derivative computation. Low preference relevance: no LLM/NLP/agent/safety methodology, only marginal Scientific AI/Training/Scaling alignment. Some incremental novelty in epsilon calibration and sFD, but rigor and evidence are weakened by internal inconsistencies and limited scope.
evidence: Section 4.1 states 25 independent random seeds while Tables 2-4 report 26 seeds.
Figure 1 caption reports sFD L2 1.15% and AD 1.66%, whereas Table 2 reports sFD 1.11% and AD 1.41%.
Section 7-8 state data and code will be made available upon publication, not currently provided.
Section 5.3 limits results to first/second derivatives, FP32, and three PDE benchmarks.

arxiv:2608.11019.rationale: Largely out of scope for LLM/NLP/agent preferences; only tangential Scientific AI/data-sampling relevance. The method is an incremental combination of top-k Fourier-mode selection and IDFT synthesis. The paper includes a generalization bound and experiments, but abstract-level battery claims conflict with reported results (R^2>0.99 vs Table 2 values 0.827-0.980), and no code/hyperparameters/availability details are provided.
evidence: Abstract states battery test datasets achieve R^2 values exceeding 0.99, but Section 5.3 Table 2 reports CC-CV R^2=0.827 and EV3 R^2=0.845.
Section 5.3 reports transfer to 'liquid-hydrogen cells' without a clear battery-chemistry protocol, weakening evidence quality.
No code availability, model hyperparameters, or training details are provided in the paper.

arxiv:2608.11017.rationale: Moderately relevant multimedia/memory/RAG work for long egocentric video QA, not core LLM methodology. Novelty is incremental around anchor-relative 4D scene-graph memory. Evaluation is limited to a 255-question single-subject EgoLifeQA split with no significance testing and a tiny 15-question why subset.
evidence: Table 2 reports R4DSG Retrieval+ overall 39.6 vs EgoRAG-Text 32.9 under question-only retrieval, and 43.1 vs 30.6 on When.
Section 4.1 states evaluation uses a 255-question object-centric subset from EgoLifeQA A1_JAKE single-subject QA file and warns no multi-subject generalization is implied.
Section 4.2.2 reports an exploratory 15-question why subset gain from 33.3 to 40.0 with WhyMemory.
Section 5 states evidence is limited to the public A1_JAKE single-subject split and the memory is retrospective and offline.

arxiv:2608.11016.rationale: Substantial optimal transport theory but mostly outside the stated LLM/NLP-centric preferences; only marginal match via quantization/pruning and no language methodology. Rigor and reproducibility are reasonable, but low preference relevance and only proof-of-concept evidence limit the overall score.
evidence: Abstract: introduces Gromov-Wasserstein quantization problem, rates, and algorithm; mentions structured pruning of neural networks.
Section 4: establishes two-sided bounds relating GW quantization to Wasserstein quantization and n^{-1/d} rates for Euclidean gauges.
Section 6.4: applies GW quantizer to prune a three-hidden-layer MLP on MNIST, comparing with L1 pruning and layer-wise clustering baselines.
Section 6: reports source code availability at https://github.com/florian-beier/gw-quantization.
Appendices B-D: contain proofs for main theorems and algorithm convergence.

arxiv:2608.11015.rationale: Out-of-scope music streaming recommendation domain application. The paper is a detailed industrial technical report with transformer-based generative retrieval, semantic IDs, knowledge distillation, and live A/B tests, but it is not LLM/NLP research. Quantitative online results and ablations are reported with p<0.01 for main comparisons, though offline metrics lack confidence intervals, code/data are not released, and only one production surface is validated.
evidence: Section 7.5 reports final online A/B results: Active Users +4.53%, Total Listening Time +6.30%, Likes +11.42% on My Vibe smart speakers.
Section 3.1 describes a semantic tokenizer using frozen Qwen2.5-Omni, collaborative refinement, and residual K-means into 3 codebooks of 32,000 entries.
Section 4.2 describes the joint next-token prediction and teacher-distillation training objective.
Section 8 lists limitations including not yet deployed on full traffic and lower catalog coverage.

arxiv:2608.11013.rationale: Multimodal zero-shot video captioning with GPT-2 and text-to-video synthetic latents; relevant to vision-language and language modeling but peripheral to core LLM-focused preferences. The synthetic visual latent polishing/prompter idea is moderately novel, but rigor is limited by the absence of statistical testing, limitations, and some table/equation errors. Evidence rests on standard metric tables and ablations, but reproducibility is constrained by no code release.
evidence: Table I reports quantitative comparisons on MSR-VTT, MSVD, and VATEX
Section IV-E provides ablation results for polisher, synthetic visual, prompter, CNN blocks, attention blocks, CLIP encoder, T2V model, and LM status
Section IV-C describes implementation details including CogVideoX-5B, GPT-2, AdamW, and hardware
No limitations section is present before the conclusion

arxiv:2608.11008.rationale: Highly relevant LLM evaluation and AI-safety-adjacent study of prompt construction in political stance measurement. The paper provides quantitative evidence that templated prompts confound neutral stance estimates, and validates LLM-generated prompts against real/templated prompts with human and LLM annotators. Limitations include only two US-based models, a single generator, small human annotator pool, English-only topics, and setting-level statistical non-independence, tempering rigor and generalizability.
evidence: Table 2 (Section 2.2.1): human realness rankings put real mean rank 1.25, LLM-generated 1.26, and templated 1.53; LLM annotators rank templated least realistic at 2.26 mean rank.
Table 3 (Section 2.2.2): human stance kappa is 0.97 for LLM-generated prompts versus 0.69 for templated prompts.
Section 3.4.3: under neutral framings, templated prompts average 0.48 from neutral versus 0.07 for LLM-generated prompts; Wilcoxon signed-rank p=.001 over 18 neutral settings.
Section Limitations: notes only two examined LLMs, a single generator model, English-only coverage, and lack of human validation of LLM stance judgments.

arxiv:2608.11006.rationale: Policy analysis of national/regional AI strategy documents; no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agent, safety-evaluation, or other technical preference areas. The work has descriptive social-science rigor and a large document corpus but is out of scope for this rubric and is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: the paper codes and analyzes 74 national and 3 regional AI strategies.
Page 23 Conclusion: limitations include exclusion of 11 non-English strategies and temporal scope issues.

arxiv:2608.11286.rationale: Out-of-scope domain-specific anomaly detection for EV charging cybersecurity; no LLM/NLP/transformer/RAG/agent/reasoning alignment methodology. The paper is structured but limited to ACN data and 51 observed updates; quantitative tables support claims, but results have narrow domain generalization.
evidence: Abstract: develops a leakage-controlled session-level benchmark using real ACN sessions and six physically motivated attacks.
Table V: selected Dual-Branch Masked-AE Transition Boost reports test F1 0.823, FPR 0.048, update TNR 1.000.
Table VI: reports CV benign update TNR 0.976 and all 9 test updates accepted.
Code and Data Availability: provides a GitHub repository URL for code and dataset.

arxiv:2608.11003.rationale: Pure information-theoretic optimization/ADMM paper on information bottleneck under perfect privacy. No LLM, Japanese NLP, agents, reasoning, or language-model methodology; privacy here is statistical/information-theoretic and not aligned with listed AI safety/LLM preferences. Theoretical convergence analysis is detailed, but empirical evidence is limited to one synthetic discrete distribution with |U|=2.
evidence: Abstract: studies information bottleneck under perfect privacy with ADMM-based method
Section I-B Contributions: proposes perturbed dual ADMM framework and convergence rates
Section VIII Numerical results: evaluates on a synthetic distribution with |U|=2

arxiv:2608.11002.rationale: Relevance is partial: the paper is multilingual text-to-image generation with language/bias analysis, touching multimodal AI, fairness, and evaluation/dataset preferences but not core LLM/agent topics. Research quality is moderate: broad model coverage and quantitative tables support the findings, but the work is descriptive and relies heavily on VLM-as-judge metrics without significance testing.
evidence: Section 3.1 introduces LingT2I covering 10 languages and two tasks.
Table 2 reports per-language CLIPScore/precision and standard deviations across 17 models.
Section 4.1 reports severe linguistic inequality and language-family stratification.
Appendix B.3 reports GPT-5 cross-checking and 98% semantic consistency in human quality checks.
Figure 11 reports a Spearman correlation of -0.89 between tokenizer fragmentation and CLIPScore.

arxiv:2608.10997.rationale: Pure robotics/maritime sensing infrastructure paper with no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent methodology; out-of-scope per rubric. It provides a descriptive modular blueprint (ROS2/Docker/MCAP) and deployment summaries, but lacks quantitative evaluation, ablations, baselines, or an available public dataset (only planned).
evidence: Abstract: describes a ROS2-based modular sensor platform with RADAR, LiDAR, IMU, GNSS, AIS, RGB/LWIR cameras, and weather sensors.
Section 3.3: details containerized ROS2 nodes with Docker and CycloneDDS.
Section 3.4: specifies MCAP format and FAIR data principles but no public dataset is provided.
Table 2: lists campaign durations and data volumes without quantitative downstream task evaluation.

arxiv:2608.10996.rationale: In-scope LLM/RL methodology applied to medical QA, with central relevance to LLMs, RLHF/alignment, and evaluation rather than a pure domain application. The consensus rubric and exact-tie pairwise advantages are incremental, and the main benchmark claims rest on one training seed with many single-pass evaluations and a small expert study, limiting evidence strength and generalizability. Detailed dataset/training configurations and prompt templates improve reproducibility.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: reports consensus rubric construction, Three-State scoring, Pairwise Sequence Advantages, and HealthBench-Hard score 38.98±1.04.
Page 3 Section 3 Method: defines consensus rubric construction, three-state criterion scoring, and pairwise sequence advantages for exact reward ties.
Page 6 Section 4 Experiments: reports ConRub-Med ranks first on six of nine open-weight benchmarks and gives component ablations.
Page 7 Section 5 Limitations: acknowledges one training seed, limited expert-study scope, and reliance on hosted judges/generators.
Page 11 Supplementary Table 5: provides detailed training configuration and hardware settings.

arxiv:2608.10995.rationale: Pure computer-vision image dehazing using diffusion and atmospheric scattering; no LLM/NLP/language methodology, so out of scope and capped at 0.20. Document shows moderate ablations and multi-dataset evaluation, but topic relevance is minimal.
evidence: Title/Abstract: 'HNDiff: Haze-Noise Diffusion for Image Dehazing' and method is a diffusion framework for image dehazing grounded in atmospheric scattering, with no language-model methodology.
Section 4.1: Evaluations use image dehazing/vision benchmarks (SOTS-Indoor, SOTS-Outdoor, NH-HAZE, O-HAZE, Dense-HAZE, RW2AH, RTTS).
Section 5: Limitations state HNDiff is tailored to the Atmospheric Scattering Model and cannot be directly applied to other degradations.

arxiv:2608.11285.rationale: Pure computer vision adversarial attack on semantic segmentation; out-of-scope per rubric and capped at 0.20 despite moderate technical quality. The work is moderately novel in adapting decision-based sparse attacks to segmentation with class-centric RL and a discrepancy reward, and it provides multi-model/multi-dataset quantitative comparisons, but it has no language/LLM relevance.
evidence: Abstract claims first systematic decision-based black-box sparse attacks for semantic segmentation and reports code availability.
Section 5.1 compares SegPAR with PointWise, SparseEvo, and RFPAR on DeepLabV3, PSPNet, SegFormer, and SETR across Cityscapes, ADE20K, and VOC2012; Table 1 reports R.MIoU, sparsity, and query.
Section 5.2 evaluates adversarially trained models DDCAT and SAT; Table 2 reports R.MIoU and sparsity.
Section 5.4 ablates the discrepancy reward on Pixle, Sparse-RS, and RFPAR; Table 3 reports objective-level comparisons.
Section 5.5 compares with white-box sparse baselines PGD0 and sPGD in Figure 6.

arxiv:2608.10989.rationale: Pure Vision Transformer token pruning for image classification, segmentation, and detection. It matches transformer/vision terms but has no language-model, NLP, reasoning, agent, or multimodal language methodology and is explicitly out-of-scope as pure computer vision. The controlled probes, ablations, and quantitative results are moderately rigorous, but evaluation is limited to ViT-B on three vision benchmarks and no code/availability is reported, so the overall score is capped low.
evidence: Abstract: reports 47.0 mIoU at 1.30x encoder throughput on ADE20K and 53.7 box AP at 1.32x on COCO.
Ablation: Table 4 reports replacing task-conditioned selection with attention loses 0.9 mIoU and 0.5 box AP.
Discussion: acknowledges classification still trails DiffRate by 0.1 point and notes fixed keep rate and task-specific training limitations.

arxiv:2608.10987.rationale: Pure robotics/aerial manipulation paper with no language-model, NLP, reasoning, agent, or multimodal methodology. It is outside the core scope and is capped at 0.20. The work has some domain-specific engineering novelty and quantitative experiments, but its relevance to the stated LLM/NLP preferences is minimal.
evidence: Section IV-C Table II reports ablation results across free-flight, single-contact, friction-less, spring-damper, feedforward, actuation, and full-system configurations.
Section IV-D reports repeated circle tracking accuracy with end-effector MAE rarely exceeding 2 mm.
Section IV-A reports upper-platform camera tracking error of 0.8 mm in xy and 0.2 degrees in yaw compared with Vicon.

arxiv:2608.10986.rationale: The paper is within LLM scope but peripheral to core capability topics: it applies statistical-physics damage-spreading to iterative self-feeding LM probes. Novelty is moderate-high for the CRN coupling and discriminator methodology; rigor and evidence are supported by known-answer validation, controls, ablation, and reported estimator retractions, though key developmental findings are single-family and some analyses are constrained by available checkpoints. Generalizability is medium; reproducibility is strong with code, per-run results, hashes, and archived repository.
evidence: Abstract: claims validated instrument, model-invariant radius scaling, and training checkpoint crossing.
Section 4: reports sharp absorbing-state transition attributed to the probe with BOS-prepend, GPT-2, and masked-LM controls.
Section 5: Table 1 discriminator manipulations separate construction-determined from model-determined readings; reports checkpoint development and ablation response.
Section 6: reports four retracted verdicts and estimator guards caught by known-answer systems.
Reproducibility: states code, per-run result files, SHA-256 stamps, and archived repository are released.

arxiv:2608.10985.rationale: Out-of-scope pure text-to-image diffusion concept erasure; no language model or NLP methodology, with only tangential AI-safety overlap, so overall score is capped at 0.20. Within its domain, the paper includes quantitative comparisons, ablations, and configuration details, but key cross-architecture results are mostly qualitative and no limitations section is provided.
evidence: Section 4.3 Table 1 reports PEAK reduces I2P NudeNet detections from 582 to 6 and attains MS-COCO CS 26.46, FID 41.59, KID 0.0000.
Appendix A Tables 5-7 provide ablations on preservation weight, parameter updating strategy, and feature selection strategy.
Appendix C.1 reports only qualitative SDXL and FLUX cross-architecture erasure results.
Appendix D.1 and D.3 provide training hyperparameters, and the abstract states code and models are available at a GitHub URL.

arxiv:2608.10983.rationale: Out-of-scope recommender system application without LLM/language methodology; only tangential relevance via multimodal diffusion and graph neural networks. Research quality is moderate: 10-seed paired tests, ablations, and noise-robustness experiments are reported, but the work is domain-specific and incremental over DiffMM.
evidence: Section 1 Introduction defines modality time-scale mismatch and two problems
Section 4.1.2 Statistical testing reports 10-seed paired t-tests
Section 4.2 Overall Effectiveness (RQ1) reports gains on TikTok, Amazon-Baby, and Amazon-Sports
Section 4.3 Temporal Necessity (RQ2) reports noise-input ablation with p<0.001
Section 4.5 Component Contributions (RQ4) reports ablations removing router, dual-stream, FiLM, and time-weight
Section 5 Conclusion states limitations on timestamp coverage and modality dominance
Abstract and Section 3 provide code availability at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/TimeRoute

arxiv:2608.10981.rationale: Relevant multimodal VLM reasoning/GRPO work, but 3D affordance grounding is not core LLM/NLP. The decomposition and GRPO proposal selection are moderately novel but build heavily on existing components. Evaluation includes official SceneFun3D, baselines, ablations, cross-dataset transfer, and qualitative real-robot tests; however absolute AP50 is low, some diagnostics use oracle settings, and no code availability or statistical significance is stated.
evidence: Abstract: claims AP50 10.69, AP25 25.46, APG 77.5 R@25, and GRPO VPAR 72.1% selection accuracy versus SFT 63.4%.
4.2 Quantitative Results: Table 1 reports official SceneFun3D validation comparisons and notes the strict-IoU lead shrinks.
4.4 Ablation Studies: Tables 2-4 provide component ablations, APG coverage, and VPAR selection accuracy.
4.5 Cross-Dataset Generalization: Table 5 reports zero-shot transfer results on 3RScan, MultiScan, ScanNet, and ScanNet++.
5 Conclusion: states cross-dataset and real-world transfer but does not provide manipulation success-rate evaluation.

arxiv:2608.10980.rationale: Pure audio/music information retrieval study using CNN era classifiers; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning relevance. Out-of-scope cap applied.
evidence: Abstract: CNN classifiers trained from scratch on Billboard Hot 100 audio are applied to Korean Melon chart songs.
Section 4.2: Audio converted to mono 16 kHz spectrograms; CNN training protocol described.
Section 7: Limitations include production lag, 30-second crops, and YouTube audio matching.

arxiv:2608.10978.rationale: Out-of-scope optical music recognition dataset/benchmark, not LLM/NLP/agent/safety/vision-language work. It uses a Transformer decoder baseline and provides quantitative benchmarks, but the domain application does not match curator preferences and is capped at low relevance.
evidence: Abstract: introduces OSSQ-OMR as a dataset dedicated to multi-part optical music recognition.
Section 3.1: baselines are Zeus (LSTM/ResNet) and Sheet Music Transformer (ConvNeXt + Transformer decoder).
Table 4: reports OMR-NED across tokenization schemes.

arxiv:2608.10977.rationale: Out-of-scope cosmology/particle theory paper on primordial black hole dark matter fine-tuning. It contains no LLM, NLP, ML, or AI-relevant methodology, tasks, or evaluations, so preference relevance is zero. Some theoretical derivation quality is present, but it does not contribute meaningfully under the AI/ML rubric.
evidence: Abstract: investigates fine-tuning of tripartite dark matter with primordial black hole relics.
Section 3: defines Barbieri-Giudice fine-tuning measure for DM abundance.
Section 6: concludes on PBH formation and dark matter, with no ML relevance.

arxiv:2608.10976.rationale: Relevant to CoT/reasoning and multimodal VLA methods, but focused on an autonomous-driving domain application rather than core LLM/NLP. XCoT combines existing VLA, flow-matching, token routing, and RL ideas; contribution is incremental. Rigor is moderate: controlled variants and ablations are present, but no closed-loop evaluation or statistical significance is reported, and XCPO is not quantitatively evaluated. Evidence consists of internal open-loop tables and latency estimates without uncertainty. Reproducibility is limited by absence of code/data and proprietary dataset details.
evidence: §4.3 Table 4 reports XCoT-VLA and baseline open-loop ADE/FDE improvements on general and lane-change sets, but only internal controlled variants.
§3.4 Evaluation scope states XCPO is optional and not quantitatively evaluated in the current version.
§4.5 Table 6 reports worst-case reasoning-interface latency estimates using 2-6 tokens for XCoT and 40-80 tokens for verbose CoT.
§4.4 Table 5 shows XCoT-only and XCoT+Navigation ablations on a controlled lane-change diagnostic split.
§4.6 Table 7 shows decoupled XCoT FT preserves short-horizon longitudinal accuracy but remains above SFT baseline for long-horizon longitudinal ADE/FDE.

arxiv:2608.10974.rationale: Relevant to NLP/scientific information extraction and LLM fine-tuning, but only partially aligned with high-weight preferences such as Japanese LLM, agents, safety, or chain-of-thought reasoning. The P-S-R schema and full-text KB are a meaningful incremental contribution, though not highly novel. Rigor is moderate: multi-stage extraction evaluations are fairly thorough, but the seed is small, expert agreement details are limited, large-scale KB quality is weakly verified, and the LLM-tuning study is preliminary with base models strongest overall.
evidence: Abstract: reports 579 expert-annotated full-text paragraphs and 36,960 P-S-R triplets; includes preliminary rationale-supervised LLM experiment.
Section 3.2: seed set contains 579 manually annotated paragraphs; agreement described as very high but formal inter-annotator metrics are limited.
Section 5.1 and Tables 2-5: report cascaded paragraph classification, entity extraction, and relation extraction results.
Section 5.3: LLM-judge evaluation shows rationale specificity/completeness only moderate; manual review covers 50 examples after refinement.
Section 6.2 and Table 12: preliminary tuning shows base models strongest in absolute overall score, with rationale supervision helping only on stratified complex problems.

arxiv:2608.10970.rationale: Relevant LLM/NLP knowledge-structure paper using zero-shot LLM generation and a fine-tuned path-aware classifier for taxonomy expansion. Within scope for LLM, prompting, knowledge, and NLP preferences. It provides formalization, adapted metrics, multi-LLM experiments, human and LLM evaluation, and ablations, but lacks a direct generative baseline, has limited statistical/comparative evidence, and some consistency gaps between ablation and main results.
evidence: Section 6.1 Table 2 reports R@K, SoftRecall@K, MRR, and WuP across four LLMs on two taxonomies, with Mistral strongest on Schema.org and Llama3.2 strongest on SemEval Environment.
Section 6.2 reports Fleiss kappa=0.695 and majority-vote human evaluation results, e.g., Qwen3 achieving 1.000 HC and 1.000 GC on Schema.org.
Appendix D Table 7 shows Local context with Classifier validation obtains R@K 34.62 and SR@K 42.31, above semantic and LLM-judge validation variants.

Section 6.1 states no directly comparable baseline exists because existing taxonomy expansion methods assume a predefined candidate set; Limitations reiterates this and notes use of compact open-source models.

arxiv:2608.10969.rationale: Domain-specific clinical ICU multivariate time series model, not LLM/NLP/agent methodology; only weak relevance via attention mechanisms and interpretability. LLM use is peripheral post-hoc graph plausibility check. Quality indicators include baselines, ablations, perturbation tests, limitations, and code link, but overall constrained to low score due to out-of-scope domain application.
evidence: Section 4.1, Table 1: Reports AUROC/AUPRC for GARLIC and baselines; GARLIC 86.40/56.89 (P12), 90.96/55.29 (P19), 90.09/64.85 (MIMIC-III).
Appendix D.1, Table 11: Component ablations (e.g., w/o GRU, w/o graph message passing) with performance drops.
Section 4.3, Table 2: Perturbation-based attribution evaluation with TOST and Page's L tests.
Section 5 Limitations: Acknowledges lack of forecasting, fixed-size windows, no static features, class imbalance, and no streaming support.
Reproducibility Statement: Code link https://github.com/SCAI-Lab/GARLIC.

arxiv:2608.10964.rationale: Medical VQA/radiology-pathology imaging application is explicitly out-of-scope under the stated rubric, capping relevance and final score. The paper combines SFT and GRPO with a confidence-aware reward, but evidence is limited to benchmark tables without statistical significance, and the HR metric and Eq. (3) have weaknesses.
evidence: Abstract: proposes CARE with dual-stage SFT/RL pipeline and Confidence-Aware Reward for Medical VQA; claims highest accuracy and lowest ECE/Hallucination Rate.
Section 3.1: evaluates on VQA-RAD, SLAKE, and PathVQA against compact and 7B-8B medical MLLMs.
Table 1: reports CARE-7B accuracy 0.767/0.873/0.689 and ECE 0.202/0.115/0.290, but lacks confidence intervals or significance tests.
Section 2.3: Eq. (3) defines importance weight with identical numerator and denominator, undermining rigor.
Section 3.2: reports implementation details including Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, full-parameter fine-tuning, K=4, and lambda=0.5; code URL is claimed but not verifiable from the document.

arxiv:2608.10963.rationale: Strong topical alignment with LLMs, chain-of-thought prompting, knowledge base construction/evaluation, and inference/serving. The paper is a system-style combination of known techniques (CoT, relation-specific prompts, deterministic parsing) with modest novelty. Evaluation includes zero-shot comparisons, test results, and subtractive ablations, but no significance testing and limited validation size; evidence is quantitative but sparse on parsing claims and prompts. Generalizability is constrained to the six shared-task relations. Reproducibility is aided by code availability and specified models/hardware.
evidence: Abstract reports macro-F1 0.62 on official test set and highlights strong relations.
§4.2 reports zero-shot vs pipeline gains and model selection.
§4.3/Table 2 reports relation-level test macro-F1 and overall 0.62.
§5/Table 3 reports ablation contributions of task decomposition, empty-set gate, and CoT.
§7/Limitations lists failure modes and stochastic variation.

arxiv:2608.10959.rationale: Relevant to AI safety/adversarial attacks on vision-language models, but research quality is only moderate. The any-to-any caption-control backdoor is a meaningful extension over fixed VLM backdoors and text-conditioned classification attacks, with experiments on LLaVA-1.6, Qwen3-VL, and MiniGPT-v2. However, rigor is limited by threshold-based ASR without statistical intervals or formal significance testing, many claims rely on appendix qualitative examples, and no code release is explicitly stated. Evidence is mostly quantitative but uneven; generalizability is reasonable across models/datasets but still within captioning-style VLM settings.
evidence: Methodology: heuristic poisoning strategy and feature-space trigger steganography
Experiment: Main Experiments Tables 1 and 2 report ASR and utility
Table 3 compares baselines on seen vs unseen trigger-target pairs
Trigger Analysis Table 4/Table 5(a) report ablations and defense robustness
Attacker simulation Table 5(b) reports synthetic target-caption results
Appendix C reports Hidden State Forensics and Neural Attention Distillation experiments

arxiv:2608.10956.rationale: Paper is a high-performance computing cluster benchmarking/regression testing framework. It does not match any preferred AI/LLM/NLP/reasoning/agents/evaluation topics; as an out-of-scope HPC systems paper it is capped at 0.20. Technical documentation is present, but correlations are largely qualitative and Slurm-only support limits generalizability.
evidence: Section III describes ClusterBench architecture with SQLite/DuckDB databases, background workers, and metric collection, none related to language models.
Section IV lists the benchmark collection: HPL, DGEMM/SGEMM, TheBandwidthBenchmark, OSU Micro-Benchmarks, and fio, all HPC component benchmarks.

arxiv:2608.10954.rationale: Relevant MLLM reasoning/evaluation paper with chain-of-evidence benchmark and RL-trained visual grounding. Strengths include broad external benchmarks, component ablations, and evaluator calibration. Limitations include reliance on private LLM judges, no statistical significance testing, no code/model release, and incremental novelty over existing grounded reasoning models.
evidence: Sec. 3.4 defines HRS, LRS, SCS, EAS trustworthiness metrics
Sec. 4.2 defines Evidence Atoms and Locate-Attend-Describe
Sec. 4.3 details SFT and GRPO training with HRGW spatial reward
Sec. 5.3 Table 2 reports EGVOR 67.7 average vs Qwen2.5-VL-7B 55.0
Sec. 5.4 Table 3 reports V* Bench 91.9 EGVOR vs 74.3 Qwen2.5-VL-7B
Sec. 5.6 Table 7 reports incremental ablations from 55.0 to 67.7
Appendix 7.12 Table 16 reports evaluator calibration against human experts

arxiv:2608.10952.rationale: Pure learned image compression paper with no language, reasoning, agent, or safety methodology; only marginal relation to the weak Computer Vision preference. The multi-scale latent contribution is incremental over prior coarse-to-fine/hierarchical approaches. Quantitative comparisons and ablations exist, but evidence is self-reported with no statistical significance and some citation/label inconsistencies. Out-of-scope cap applied to final score.
evidence: Abstract claims 17.9% BD-rate reduction over VVC on Kodak.
Section 4.2 reports BD-rate results on Kodak, CLIC, and Tecnick.
Section 3.3 describes end-to-end rate-distortion optimization with SGA.
Section 4.4 provides ablations on channel count, latent scales, and residual block.

arxiv:2608.10950.rationale: Out-of-scope LiFi/optical wireless network simulation; no match to LLM/NLP/agent/vision/robotics preferences. Intrinsically, the paper provides a cross-validated ns-3/Python framework and quantified design space, but the out-of-scope relevance ceiling caps the score at 0.18.
evidence: Abstract: describes LD LiFi system model, IM/DD receiver, adaptive M-QAM, and ns-3/Python cross-validation.
Section I-A Contributions: lists link model, open ns-3 module, cross-validation, quantified design space, and prototype forensics.
Section VI-B: states Python engine independently validates BER curves and ns-3 tests pin agreement to 0.1%.
Section VIII: states hardware prototype established feasibility but could not establish multi-Mb/s throughput; higher-rate figures are model-based.

arxiv:2608.10949.rationale: Relevant multimodal MLLM memory/efficiency paper with strong topical overlap across multimodal AI, long-context/memory, video understanding, and inference efficiency. Methodology is a reasonable but somewhat incremental combination of pre-ViT residual filtering, two-tier memory consolidation, and VAS-guided retrieval. Rigor is moderate: experiments include ablations, sensitivity, efficiency, and same-backbone controlled comparisons, but the main comparison mixes backbone sizes and many baselines are unreported. Evidence is fairly strong from tables/figures for benchmark, grounding, and efficiency claims, though mostly self-reported. Generalizability is good across streaming and offline video benchmarks but limited to one backbone family. Reproducibility is moderate: detailed hyperparameters and pseudocode are provided, but no code release or seeds are stated.
evidence: Section 4.2 and Table 1 report StreamFlow overall StreamingBench 67.73 and VideoMME overall 73.52; Appendix C.1 provides controlled same-backbone Qwen3.5-9B comparisons.
Section 4.3 and Figure 4(a) report mean VAS gain of 59.1% over Vanilla; Table 3 reports complete-task latency and peak memory reductions of 50.4% and 21.1%.
Appendix A.4 provides hyperparameters and Algorithm 1 describes label construction, but no code availability or random seed details are reported.

arxiv:2608.10947.rationale: Out-of-scope pure learned image compression/low-level vision task with no language methodology; only tangential MoE/transformer relevance. Quantitative comparisons and ablations are present, but domain mismatch caps the score.
evidence: Abstract: proposes MoE-based Entropy model for learned image compression and reports BD-Rate improvement over VVC of -16.85% on Kodak.
Section 4.2: reports BD-Rate on Kodak, Tecnick, and CLIC 2020 Professional datasets.
Section 4.3: ablation comparing constant versus spread expert channel dimensions.

arxiv:2608.10941.rationale: The paper describes a physics-informed diffusion generative model for industrial time-series synthesis. It is not an LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning/vision-language paper and is best treated as a pure domain application, so relevance is capped low despite some low-weight matches to synthetic data/data augmentation and diffusion. Methodologically it has moderate novelty via stepwise physics embedding, but evidence relies heavily on relative percentage gains and domain-specific constraints; generalizability is shown only across industrial datasets, not broader settings. Reproducibility is partially supported by code/data links and implementation details.
evidence: Abstract: introduces PhysDGM, embedding physical laws into each reverse diffusion step, and reports downstream task improvements of 48%, 15%, 22%, and 20%.
Introduction: frames the work around data augmentation and synthetic data generation for time-series, citing diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion and DALL-E 3 as analogous.
Method: describes stepwise physical embedding, dynamic physical constraint training, and gradient-guided physical sampling.
Code availability: states the complete pipeline is available at https://github.com/Dolphin-wang/PhysDGM.

arxiv:2608.10939.rationale: Relevant mainly via multilingual NLP, inference/serving, and efficiency categories, but not LLM/Japanese/reasoning/agent-focused; uses compact sentence encoders and translation routing. Rigor is moderate: two benchmarks, deterministic reruns, paired significance tests, but hand-crafted tiers and limited scope. Reproducibility is relatively strong due to code/environment availability.
evidence: Section V-A and Table III report SIB-200 R1 low-tier Macro-F1 rises from 0.4632 to 0.6828 while high/mid tiers remain unchanged.
Section V-B and Table V report MASSIVE R1 low-tier Macro-F1 rises from 0.2143 to 0.4417, with best overall configuration R3 at Macro-F1 0.4647.
