Section IV-D states code, configuration files, notebooks, and experiment artifacts will be made available on GitHub and lists the execution environment.

arxiv:2608.10938.rationale: Out-of-scope visual localization/robotics paper using 3D Gaussian Splatting for camera pose estimation; no LLM/NLP/language-model methodology. Moderate experimental benchmarking and ablations, but incremental novelty and limited generalization/reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: describes 6-DoF camera pose estimation via 3D Gaussian Splatting, with no language-model component.
Section V-D: reports 7Scenes and Cambridge Landmarks pose-error tables but no statistical significance tests.
Section V-G: ablation is limited to the Office sequence and evaluates only two components.

arxiv:2608.10936.rationale: Out-of-scope theoretical stochastic optimal control/POMDP paper. Only weak connection via reinforcement learning and policy concepts; no LLM, NLP, agent, code, safety, or multimodal relevance. The formal threshold results are mathematically structured but lack empirical validation and implementation, so overall contribution is low for this curation scope.
evidence: Abstract: states threshold structure of optimal policies for discounted and total undiscounted cost criteria.
Section IV-A, Theorem 1: establishes threshold structure for discounted optimal deterministic stationary policies under Assumption 1.
Section V-B, Theorem 5: extends the threshold structure to average-cost optimal policies under Assumptions 1, 2, and 3.

arxiv:2608.10934.rationale: Directly relevant to coding agents, tool use, and LLMs, but primarily descriptive/exploratory. The 10-task ArkBench evaluation uses one model and a single run with no baselines or ablations, limiting rigor and generalizability; architecture comparison is qualitative.
evidence: Abstract states Ark solved 8 of 10 ArkBench tasks with gpt-5.4-mini.
Section 4.2 Table 4 reports per-task success, tokens, time, and tool calls, and describes the two failures.
Section 5 compares Ark with Codex CLI and OpenCode using a taxonomy, but no quantitative baselines or ablations are presented.

arxiv:2608.10933.rationale: Text-to-video diffusion jailbreak defense is largely outside the language-model preference scope despite AI-safety keywords; it is a video diffusion safety method with no LLM/NLP methodology. Quality is limited by modest ASR gains, inconsistent tables, large clean SSIM degradation, no statistical tests, and no code/data release.
evidence: Table 3/Section 4.4: No Defense SSIM=1 and Temporal LPIPS=0.0605 vs Ours SSIM=0.3449 and Temporal LPIPS=0.0585, showing major clean-frame quality degradation.
Table 2/Section 4.3 and Table 4/Section 4.5 present inconsistent T2VShield/Ours ASR values across T2VSafetyBench and Open-Sora evaluations.
Section 3.4 describes a semantic adapter but does not fully specify the deviation strength d_t^b computation.
Section 4.1 lists commercial models Sora/Kling/Luma but Section 4.5 provides only qualitative Sora illustration, no quantitative commercial results.

arxiv:2608.10932.rationale: Multimodal MLLM/video benchmark and distillation method are in scope, but the core task is camera-motion perception rather than LLM/NLP methodology. Novelty is moderate: a new compositional temporal benchmark plus distillation of 3D camera tokens, though the distillation approach itself is standard. Rigor is fairly good with multiple baselines, ablations, and external benchmarks, but lacks statistical significance/error bars. Evidence is mostly quantitative and internally consistent but based on single runs. Generalizability is shown only across camera-motion tasks. Reproducibility is strong due to detailed appendices, prompts, hyperparameters, and planned release.
evidence: Section 5.2, Table 2: CamDistill-4B reaches 67.5 frame-level micro F1, matching CamInject-4B, versus Gemini-3.1-Pro 43.3.
Table 3: CamDistill adds 0.1s latency and 1.8GB peak memory over Qwen3-VL-4B, while CamInject adds 5.9s and 4.8GB.
Appendix D: taxonomy includes 12 movement types and 20 direction-aware labels with annotation rules.
Table 5: ablations vary feature-layer region, module depth, token position, and teacher.

arxiv:2608.10929.rationale: Domain-specific federated cross-domain generative recommendation paper, out of scope for LLM/NLP/agent preferences despite using Transformer/MoE components. Within its domain it provides moderate ablations and quantitative comparisons, but evidence is limited to Amazon recommendation scenarios and no formal significance testing; capped as an out-of-scope domain application.
evidence: Section 4.2 Table 3 reports full-ranking H@10/N@10 results for FK, GS, GBS, and GKBS scenarios.
Section 4.3 Table 5 reports ablation results, including a -12.8% average N@10 drop without the CF residual.
Section 4.1.4 states the code is publicly available and lists implementation hyperparameters.

arxiv:2608.10928.rationale: Directly relevant LLM reasoning/RAG paper with strong experimental controls and ablations, though novelty is incremental and generalization is constrained to domain-matched corpora. Minor table-numbering inconsistencies and best-accuracy comparisons temper rigor.
evidence: Section 4 reports best accuracy across five reasoning models on GSM-8K, MATH-500, AIME 2025, and SciQ, with ST, TTS, S-ICL, and Rand baselines.
Section 5 and Appendix E report predictive entropy and per-step confidence analyses; ThinkRetrieve lowers entropy from 1.51 to 0.96 nats on a MATH-500 subset.
Appendix H describes an answer-distinct retrieval filter showing accuracy essentially unchanged, supporting no answer-level leakage.
Section 7 Limitations notes reliance on domain-matched corpora and unproven cross-domain robustness.

arxiv:2608.10920.rationale: Strong topical fit as an LLM-agent, multi-agent, safety/red-teaming simulation with LLM-as-judge measurement and matched baseline comparison. The framework is clearly motivated and formalized, but evidence is simulator-internal rather than real-world, judge validation is absent, and no code/artifact release is apparent, limiting reproducibility.
evidence: Section 3 presents the control, simulation, and evaluation planes with run controller, actors, study models, measurement, and evidence layers.
Section 4 defines the three actor categories: civilians, IO operators, and the non-public manager.
Section 6 defines the deterministic construct-update rule and the matched active-vs-baseline directional lift protocol.
Section 7 reports 13 matched replicates with 10,000 civilians, plus a 100,000-civilian validation run, and p<0.001 after Holm correction for three primary construct endpoints.
Section 8 acknowledges that LLM judges are not ground truth, results are model-dependent, and external validation/calibration is needed.

arxiv:2608.10916.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/CoT evaluation paper: studies faithfulness of autoformalisation systems for mathematical chain-of-thought, with LLM-based perturbation and Lean proof checking to detect error induction and silent correction. Proposes a benchmark, reports quantitative FNR/FPR/AFFR/UFLB, includes human/LLM validation and regex robustness checks, and releases code/data, though it relies partly on LLM judges and explicitly acknowledges incompleteness for semantic drift.
evidence: Page 5, Section 5.2: 'The perturbations were judged on average as effective in 97.8% of the total 12,784 reasoning steps.'

Page 6, Section 6.1: Figure 3 reports FNR/FPR/AFFR/UFLB for the four specialised AFs; 'Goedel consistently attains the highest FPR' and 'attains this lead despite having the highest FPR, with its advantage driven by its much lower FNR and AFFR.'
Page 7, Limitations: 'Our method does not assess semantic drift in full generality, and is therefore not complete... we recommend that FaithformBench be used as one diagnostic measure among others.'

arxiv:2608.10908.rationale: Relevant to LLM-as-judge, multimodal evaluation, reasoning, and position-bias preferences. The paper contributes controlled visual-temporal benchmarks and diagnostics of positional asymmetries, but causal claims about RoPE/causal masking are not directly tested, quantitative results lack significance/confidence intervals, human agreement is low, and no verifiable code/data release is provided. Some claims of catastrophic collapse exceed the reported results.
evidence: Section F.2 states human inter-rater correlation on this task is low (r_H=0.34).
Table S2 shows the best 7B PRISM pairwise accuracy is 0.72 and F1 0.47, weak but not fully random.
Appendix F explicitly says attribution of primacy/recency to causal masking and RoPE 'rests on prior literature rather than on direct measurement.'
Table S18 reports Gemma-4-31B reaches Acc=0.91 on Prism but with 1622 invalid answers, while Qwen3.6-27B reaches Acc=0.56.
Section F.1 provides training details (LoRA, Optuna, DeepSpeed, H200 GPUs) but no verifiable dataset/code availability.

arxiv:2608.10906.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM agents and tool use as a large-scale dataset of agent skill files. The dataset construction is documented and access links are provided, but the paper is descriptive and lacks empirical evaluation, baselines, ablations, or validated quality metrics, limiting evidence strength and rigor.
evidence: High-Level Overview reports 3,797,117 SKILL.md files, 282,200 repositories, and 1,877,981 distinct contents collected in July 2026.
Appendix A Dataset Construction describes the read-only GitHub API pipeline, size-partitioned discovery, content-hash deduplication, enrichment, and anonymization.
How to Access states that the full SQLite dataset is on Zenodo, with a Parquet mirror on Hugging Face and a sample on GitHub.

arxiv:2608.10905.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/on-policy distillation paper with reasoning and code evaluation. Novelty is moderate: prompt-level reliability ordering is an incremental but useful curriculum layer over existing OPD methods. Experiments span multiple model families, student scales, and tasks, but statistical significance is not assessed and many gains are within reported standard deviations; some robustness/composition studies use only one seed. No code release is claimed.
evidence: Abstract: ReOrder-OPD improves every matched aggregate comparison across Qwen3 and Gemma4 mathematics settings and Qwen3 code settings.
Main Results, Table 1: ReOrder raises the Six-set aggregate for all five student configurations, with gains of 1.09-2.58 percentage points.
Reliability and Proxy Analysis, Table 4: Full-pool descending-R training outperforms vanilla OPD by 1.94 points while ascending order is 1.94 below.

arxiv:2608.10903.rationale: Medical imaging/ultrasound segmentation paper with no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent/code methodology; falls under explicit out-of-scope categories. Method adapts VIDS uncertainty to a 1x1 segmentation head and evaluates on EchoNet adult-to-pediatric shift; comparisons and statistics are present but baselines are limited (Ensemble, PHiSeg), no component ablations, and generalization is confined to one anatomy/dataset pair.
evidence: Section 4.1.1: Datasets are EchoNet-Dynamic and EchoNet-Pediatric for left ventricular echocardiography segmentation.
Section 3.2: VIDS-Seg applies amortized variational inference only to a 1x1 prediction head on a frozen U-Net, with no language-model methodology.
Section 4.2.2: Table 1 reports NCC uncertainty-error alignment and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for VIDS-Seg versus Ensemble.

arxiv:2608.10897.rationale: Pure logistics/dispatch RL application outside LLM/NLP scope; it matches only peripheral preferences (MARL, attention, optimization). Experimental evaluation is moderate with baselines, ablations, multiple scales/platform counts, but has no language methodology and is domain-specific, so score is capped low.
evidence: Section 2.2 formulates the problem as partially observable MARL with platform-grid agents; Section 3.1.2 describes the multi-head self-attention inter-courier encoder.
Section 4.4 Table 3 reports GMV and ACTD across three scales and one to three platforms comparing POLO with seven baselines.
Section 4.6 Table 5 ablates the attention module and Table 6 ablates counterfactual/distance reward coefficients.
Section 4.1 describes a Meituan-based simulator and states implementation availability at a GitHub link.

arxiv:2608.10896.rationale: Moderately relevant RL/statistical inference paper on constant-stepsize TD learning; matches the Reinforcement Learning preference but not higher-weight LLM/NLP/agent categories. Strong formal theory and a novel self-normalized RR/horizon-indexed design, with honest but small-scale finite-state MDP experiments. Generalizability is limited by linear, bounded, stationary, fixed-dimensional assumptions.
evidence: Section 1.2 (Contributions) lists C1-C3: fixed-stepsize path theory, self-normalized RR inference, and horizon-indexed Bellman inference.
Section 2.2 defines θ_RR,α as the fixed-stepsize RR stationary target and distinguishes it from the projected Bellman solution θ*.
Section 7.2 reports Garnet RR-SN coverage 0.927-0.963 and FrozenLake smaller-stepsize d=10 coverage 0.877/0.923/0.920 at n=10^6.
Section 7.3 reports No-RR SN covers Rθ* about 0.81 and RR reduces mean absolute target shift from ~1.75e-2 to 4.9e-4 (~36-fold).
Section 7.4 Table 5 reports fitted slopes at ν=1/3, e.g., -0.168/-0.167, close to proof-based benchmark exponents -1/6/-1/6.
Section 8 states limitations: fixed-dimensional, linear, bounded stationary, uniformly geometrically ergodic Markov sampling, pointwise at a prespecified horizon.
Section 7.1 states code and archived result summaries are available at https://github.com/MinZenggit/SN-TD.

arxiv:2608.10893.rationale: Falls mainly in statistical risk control and certification under covariate shift rather than core LLM/Japanese NLP/reasoning methods; lightly touches AI safety/RAG/NLP evaluation. Theory is novel and rigorous with detailed proofs, but empirical evidence is largely synthetic or negative, validity is conditional on a shift model, and nuisance necessity remains partially open.
evidence: §4.1 Theorem 1 defines the Floor Certification Map and model-split lower/upper bounds
§5.1 reports pre-registered bite slope -2.002 and Table 4 full-grid audit with 0 violations for formal arms
§5.3 reports hard refusal on SQuAD→NewsQA and post-hoc frontier below floor
Appendix H establishes only a K-free necessary core, leaving unknown-η nuisance necessity open

arxiv:2608.10891.rationale: Time-series forecasting/synthetic-data privacy benchmark with no LLM, NLP, agent, or language-model methodology. Only incidental keyword overlap such as 'benchmark', 'privacy', and a cited time-series foundation model; not aligned with the stated preferences. Research quality is moderate: controlled TSTR protocol across seven datasets, multiple baselines, statistical tests, and public code, but the method is an incremental Grasynda extension, uses a single forecasting architecture, univariate data, and empirical distance-based privacy rather than formal guarantees.
evidence: Abstract: evaluates synthetic series generation and noise-based anonymization under Train on Synthetic, Test on Real across seven datasets.
Section 4.3: Forecasting protocol uses NHITS and MASE for evaluation.
Section 5.2 and Table 3: Grasynda-P shows statistically significant DCR improvement over Grasynda.
Section 6 Limitations: acknowledges empirical privacy metrics are not formal differential privacy, and results are limited to univariate monthly/quarterly series with NHITS.

arxiv:2608.10888.rationale: Purely out-of-scope structured-light optical metrology / 3D imaging paper. It has no LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, agent, safety, or other preference-relevant AI methodology. Despite controlled experiments and quantitative baselines, the topical relevance is zero and the work is capped as a domain application.
evidence: Abstract: describes sensor-informed covariance for structured-light 3D imaging; no language model or NLP content.
Section IV and Table III: G-ICP registration is only a downstream evaluation, and the proposed covariance underperforms the geometry-derived baseline on the reported dataset.
Section VI: acknowledges no complete multivariate validation against independent 3D perturbation ground truth and notes controlled-regime limits.

arxiv:2608.10886.rationale: Primarily an embodied/robotics scene-memory paper; it uses VLM/LLM components and a tool-calling QA agent but contributes no language-model methodology, so preference relevance is capped at the pure-robotics/domain-application limit. Evaluation has baseline comparisons and ablations on one benchmark, plus qualitative egocentric transfer, but no statistical testing and code is only promised on acceptance.
evidence: Section V-B, Table I: GESTO reports text accuracy 0.71, binary F1 0.75, and time accuracy 0.70; fully automatic EGG drops to 0.33/0.29/0.50.
Section V-C, Table II: ablations show removing the event hierarchy reduces time accuracy to 0.40 and Space2Event to 0.53.
Section V-D: egocentric transfer is qualitative only, with no quantitative egocentric evaluation.
Section VI: limitations note VLM object-localization degradation and missing or incorrect segmentation masks under occlusion.

arxiv:2608.10885.rationale: LLM-based medical triage with calibration and selective deferral; moderately relevant to LLM/evaluation but domain-specific and single-dataset. Strengths include multi-vendor comparison, ablations, bootstrap/FDR testing, Platt calibration, and explicit limitations. However summary statistics are internally inconsistent, theoretical contributions are mostly classical tools applied to the framework, and LOO consensus evaluation on reader-nodule instances may inflate apparent performance.
evidence: Key Findings at a Glance reports mean text-to-image AUC gap Δ=0.358 and image-statistics AUC range [0.443,0.576], while Section VI-B and Table III report Δ≈0.327 and range [0.499,0.580].
Section VII-D Limitations states LIDC-IDRI labels are radiologist-based rather than pathology-confirmed and no prospective clinical validation was conducted.
Section VI-F states ConfTriage/LLM/Certain-Net are evaluated on 2049 reader-nodule LOO instances, not unique nodules, while individual readers use 357-611 instances, which may affect comparability.

arxiv:2608.10882.rationale: Quantum software pattern mining and composition analysis; LLM/embedding use is ancillary, not core language-model methodology. The final score is capped at 0.20 as an out-of-scope domain application despite moderate intrinsic rigor and reproducible artifacts.
evidence: Section 3.6.1 reports Qrisp micro-F1 0.712 with vocabulary expansion versus 0.449 without; Table 2 gives per-pattern metrics.
Section 3.4 reports LLM ensemble agreement Fleiss' kappa 0.78 on 50 components and reproduces 160/214 prior manual labels.
Section 4.3.1 defines directness ratio and Table 5 reports low-directness components such as Classiq qft_no_swap with rho=0.00.
Section 5 describes threats including dataset composition and exclusion of three framework-maintained example repositories.

arxiv:2608.10881.rationale: Out-of-scope pure constraint programming/combinatorial optimization for Euclidean TSP/GTSP; no LLM, NLP, agent, multimodal, safety, or language methodology. Formal proofs and experiments exist, but relevance to target preferences is negligible and the paper is capped at 0.20 as a pure domain application.
evidence: Abstract: focus on Euclidean TSP and Constraint Logic Programming filtering algorithms.
Section 1: techniques are intended for complete Euclidean instances and do not cover settings with unavoidable crossings.
Section 6: experimental evaluation on TSPLIB/random TSP/GTSP instances compares HK-RMC and GEO models.
Section 7: limitation that methods do not apply to all TSP variants such as TSP with Time Windows.

arxiv:2608.10878.rationale: Pure speech/audio paper on joint streaming ASR and turn-state prediction; only tangential preference match under Speech & Audio. Uses an LLM only as a data annotator and does not advance LLM/NLP methodology, so out-of-scope cap applies. Quantitative tables and a delay ablation support modest evidence, but no statistical testing, limited hyperparameter ablations, no explicit limitations, and no method code release limit rigor/reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: frame-synchronous turn state prediction via delayed-stream modeling, evaluated on bilingual EasyTurn test sets.
Section 2.1: proposes a parallel turn state head over shared hidden states from Voxtral Realtime.
Section 3.2: uses Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime and two-stage fine-tuning with delay tau sampled per batch.
Table 1: reports bilingual turn state accuracy and latency; Table 2 ablates delay tau.
Section 5: conclusion and future work, without explicit limitations or code release for the proposed X2-Turn method.

arxiv:2608.10876.rationale: Out-of-scope stochastic analysis paper on reflection coupling for underdamped Langevin diffusions. It contains no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, agent, safety, or adjacent AI/ML methodology, and is a pure applied probability/SDE theory result. The proofs and numerical simulations are domain-specific and do not address any stated preference area.
evidence: Abstract
Section 5

arxiv:2608.11283.rationale: Domain-specific LLM application for MOF validation via chemically informed textualization, with clear LLM/fine-tuning/interpretability components but limited alignment with core preferences such as Japanese NLP, reasoning, agents, or safety. Quantitative benchmarking supports the main claim, though narrow domain scope, absent error bars/statistical tests, and limited generalizability constrain the score. Code/data availability improves reproducibility.
evidence: Results and Discussion, Page 4-5: benchmarks nine descriptors across pre-trained and fine-tuned LLMs with four metrics.
Table 1, Page 6-7: reports accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 for baselines and fine-tuned LLMs; Qwen-3-4B with mof2text accuracy 0.757.
Conclusion, Page 10: claims fine-tuned LLMs achieve validation performance comparable to graph-based models and provide interpretable rationales.
Data Availability Statement, Page 10-11: provides GitHub, Zenodo, and Hugging Face links for code, models, and data.

arxiv:2608.10872.rationale: Out-of-scope control-theoretic safety filtering for underactuated linear systems; no AI/ML/NLP/LLM/agent methodology or evaluation. The paper has some formal rigor and simulation comparisons, but evidence is limited to a linearized two-wheeled balancing robot, and the contribution does not match the curation scope.
evidence: Abstract: proposes robust safety filtering with H-infinity baseline, disturbance observer, and robust HOCBF constraints.
Section IV: numerical evaluation on linearized two-wheeled balancing robot under three disturbances.
Section V: conclusion states the proposed controller respected state and actuator limits in the linearized TWBR study.

arxiv:2608.10870.rationale: Relevant mainly through multimodal VLM conditioning and adversarial AI safety, but the core contribution is image-editing protection rather than LLM/NLP methodology. The balanced VLM condition redirection with cross-prompt averaging is moderately novel. Experiments cover two editors, two datasets, held-out prompts, ablations, and multiple metrics, but lack statistical significance testing and an explicit limitations section, and the user study is small.
evidence: Abstract: reports average 0.813 IF reduction relative to SOTA and preserved source identity/content.
Experiments Main Results Table 1: NullEdit achieves IF -1.218/-1.178 on Step1X-Edit and -0.897/-0.900 on Qwen-Image-Edit across CelebA-HQ/VGGFace2.
Prompt Generalization Table 2: held-out prompts reduce IF from 0.310 Clean to -1.353 NullEdit on CelebA-HQ Step1X-Edit.
Ablation Studies Figure 5: reports loss balance, prompt-gradient aggregation, and perturbation-budget sensitivity.
Experimental Setup: two VLM-conditioned DiT editors, 50 identities, 12 instructions, 8 optimization prompts and 4 held-out prompts.

arxiv:2608.10869.rationale: This is rigorous theoretical PAC learning work with matching optimistic-rate upper/lower bounds and Lean formalization, but it has essentially no overlap with the stated LLM/NLP/agent/safety/efficiency preference topics. High research quality yields a moderate score despite zero preference relevance.
evidence: Abstract states optimal multiclass excess risk and Lean 4 verification
Theorem 3.1 in Section 3 states the main upper bound
Theorem 4.1 in Section 4 states the matching lower bound
Appendix D describes the Lean formalization and axiom audit

arxiv:2608.10868.rationale: Out-of-scope condensed-matter physics paper on Anderson localization and anomalous diffusion with heavy-tailed hopping. No LLM/NLP/ML preference topics are present, so relevance is zero; despite analytical derivations and a numerical simulation check, the score is capped below 0.20.
evidence: Model and conductivity correlation function defines an Anderson Hamiltonian with heavy-tailed hopping amplitudes and conductivity correlation functions, with no listed AI/ML/NLP topics.
Direct numerical simulations reports mean-square displacement results for the unitary symmetry class at mu=1.6, but this does not address any preferred AI/ML/NLP methodology.

arxiv:2608.10867.rationale: Strong topical relevance to LLM post-training and reasoning benchmarks, but the work is preliminary: small run counts, overlapping confidence intervals, limited ablations, and incomplete reproducibility moderate confidence despite useful negative results about selection overfitting.
evidence: Abstract: proposes Bayesian optimization within a random linear embedding and claims 5x fewer candidate evaluations matches or exceeds RandOpt.
Section 4, Table 1: reports mean±SD selection reward and test K=1/K=20 across Countdown, GSM8k, MATH500 for Qwen2.5-Instruct 0.5B-3B.
Section 4, Figure 3: shows selection reward stops resolving above a threshold when ranking GSM8k candidates.
Section 5: lists planned experiments and acknowledges pending ablations and untested assumptions.

arxiv:2608.10866.rationale: Moderately relevant via MCP tool servers, Skill documentation, and LLM agent orchestration, but the core contribution is an astronomy catalog built on an existing decomposition; the language-model methodology is thin and the catalog run is deterministic. Astronomy validation is reasonably rigorous, though the agent-recovery claim rests on a single demonstration.
evidence: Section III.5 describes MCP servers and a LangGraph plan-call-observe-decide agent; the full-sample catalog run is deterministic and does not use the vision node.
Section IV.1 reports 74.4% benchmark recovery at an 8.1% validated control false-positive rate.
Section IV.2 reports 41,466 flagged SB2 candidates from 238,205 dwarfs and states control false-positive rate implies close to 40% may be falsely flagged singles.
Section IV.6 reports blind-agent ablation of two decisions: self-consistent normalization was recovered, luminosity weighting was not.
Data Availability states release of MCP servers, Skill, catalog, benchmark list, training manifest, and trained network weights, but notes the EB18 reference network weights are not redistributable.

arxiv:2608.10864.rationale: In-scope multimodal/vision-language paper on spatial reasoning and knowledge distillation. It is not pure CV or robotics; it directly concerns vision-language models, multi-view spatial reasoning, and distillation. Novelty is moderate because relational distillation is known and the contribution is an adaptation to multi-view VLM geometry grounding with a diagnostic analysis and dual-pathway variant. Empirical evaluation is fairly extensive with multiple backbones, ablations, and 3D scene understanding, but lacks statistical significance testing and is limited to indoor ScanNet-family benchmarks and one teacher. Reproducibility is reasonable due to detailed hyperparameters but no code-release evidence.
evidence: Table 2 reports VSI-Bench comparisons and efficiency claims
Table 3 reports ablations on distillation target and dual pathway
Section 5.2 reports cross-backbone and 3D scene understanding results
Appendix C.1 provides training hyperparameters

arxiv:2608.10860.rationale: Pure robotics/embodied AI world-action model for manipulation; not LLM/NLP language methodology. Although it uses a mixture-of-transformers backbone and frozen text conditioning via umT5, the contribution is robot policy learning with visual streams (RGB/pointmap/DINO), flow matching, and real-robot evaluation, placing it under the out-of-scope cap. Quantitative results and ablations are present (Sec. 4.4, Sec. 4.5, Figure 6), but relevance is minimal and most evidence is domain-specific; reproducibility is limited by absent code/checkpoint availability in the text.
evidence: Sec. 3.1 Input Visual Streams and Model Backbone
Sec. 4.4 (Q3): Large-scale comparison of Flex-pi against many VLAs and WAMs
Sec. 4.5 (Q4): Impact of Flex-pi's Additional Inputs and Outputs in Policy Performance
Figure 6: Real-world results
Appendix J Training Hyperparameters

arxiv:2608.10858.rationale: Meta-research process paper with moderate LLM/agent relevance but no core ML methodology or validated empirical gains; protocol has substantial pre-registration but results are provisional, self-run, uncontrolled, and many metrics null/missing.
evidence: Section 6 Results: 'All card observations carry status PROVISIONAL... no observation in this section carries confirmatory standing.'
Section 7 Honest Boundaries: 'There is no control group... Every claim here is therefore a system claim...'
Section 9 Resource Availability: 'Derived data and metadata will be deposited at Zenodo under no embargo... The corresponding repository DOI will be added before acceptance.'

arxiv:2608.10857.rationale: Low relevance: this is an intrinsic-dimension and multimodal autoencoder/representation-learning method, not LLM/NLP/agent research; it only tangentially touches multimodal and interpretability preferences. Methodological work is fairly novel and has extensive simulations, ablations, baseline comparisons, and reproducibility details, but theoretical guarantees are informal and results show under/over-estimation and leakage.
evidence: Table 2 reports FiGuRO average deviation from ground truth 2.9 versus 9.5-36.3 for JIVE/AJIVE/SLIDE/ShIndICA.
Table 3 ablation shows rank-reduction-only variant collapses to rank 1 on all B datasets while FiGuRO tracks ground-truth scales.
Section 5.4 reports shared-subspace classification accuracy 0.94 on Audio MNIST and 0.55 on So2Sat.
Supplementary Table 1 reports hyperparameter sweep N=1080 with average rank estimate 4.89±0.01 for true ID 5.
Introduction states code availability on GitHub; Appendix B.3/B.6 provides architecture and training details.

arxiv:2608.10850.rationale: Highly relevant LLM training-dynamics study using SVD to analyze continual pre-training across math, code, instruction, and text. Novel observations on CPT head heterogeneity, selective rewind, and domain connectivity are supported by multi-scale OLMo 2 experiments and ablations, though novelty is incremental over prior HTSR and model-merging work. Rigor and evidence are moderate: strong reproducibility and quantitative results, but generalizability is limited to OLMo-family models, AdamW, and a narrow benchmark set.
evidence: Abstract: reports SVD-based CPT analysis, head heterogeneity, up to 60% head-update removal, and open-source Diffract toolkit.
Section 3.1 Training Setup: describes OLMo 2 1B/7B/13B pre-training and CPT on math, instruction, code, and text domains.
Section 4.4 Drivers of Domain Quality in CPT Deltas: reports up to +4% GSM8K gain for 7B math CPT via head rewind and 50-70% singular value truncation tolerance.
Section 4.5 Domain Connectivity: reports linear interpolation between CPT checkpoints and improved interpolation with larger pre-train budgets and model size.
Section 6 Discussion and Directions for Further Work: acknowledges limitations to OLMo family, AdamW recipe, and limited benchmark coverage.
Appendix D Statistical Robustness: provides bootstrap evaluation variability with 5 seeds and reports small variance.

arxiv:2608.10847.rationale: Pure robotics/human-robot interaction paper on kinesthetic teaching and observer-based hand-guiding. It has no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/prompting/RAG/agents/code/safety/alignment/evaluation methodology, so the out-of-scope cap applies. Within its domain it provides a controlled user study with statistical comparisons, but limited to one robot platform and lacks ablation/code release.
evidence: Section IV-B: user study on KUKA LWR iiwa with 16 participants and 256 evaluated trials
Table I: significant ANOVA for normalized human effort (F=9.29, p<10^-4) and user preference (F=9.71, p<10^-5); task quality missed beats not significant (F=0.51, p>0.05)
Section V: future work notes validation on other platforms and ablation of design components are still needed

arxiv:2608.10845.rationale: Pure statistical network analysis paper on degree-normalized spectral embeddings under random dot product graphs. It does not address LLMs, NLP, agents, reasoning, or other preferred topics, so preference relevance is negligible. The paper is mathematically detailed with proofs in the appendix, but as a domain-specific graph/statistics contribution it is outside the scope of this curation. Novelty is limited to extending known spectral embedding CLTs, and validation relies on simulations rather than preferred-task or empirical evidence.
evidence: Abstract: studies degree-normalized spectral embeddings and row-wise CLT under random dot product graphs
Section 4: specializes to DCSBM and block models
Section 5.3: reports simulated misclassification rates for row-normalized spectral clustering
Appendix A: contains proof of Theorem 1

arxiv:2608.10843.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM and reasoning preferences via verifier-guided LLM-symbolic search, but narrowly scoped to first-order induction rather than mainstream LLM/NLP tasks. Novelty is moderate relative to execution-guided synthesis and Reflexion. Controlled matched comparisons and exact evaluation support train-validity claims, though one trajectory per cell and weak holdout generalization limit rigor and evidence. Reproducibility is partial: offline artifact verification is described, but model inference is not rerunnable.
evidence: Section 5 and Table 1: across matched models, task sets, and LLM-round limits, Hypothesis Frontier outperforms repeated generation in 9 of 9 comparisons by +6.2 to +25.0 percentage points, with 7 paired bootstrap intervals excluding zero.

Section 5: final exact simplification lowers mean AST from 40.9 to 32.5 on Benchmark300 and 128.3 to 98.4 on Challenge64, while H-exact rises modestly from 30.4% to 33.6% and 18.9% to 20.0%, respectively.

Section 7 Limitations: results concern small, fully observed finite worlds over a fixed vocabulary and do not extend to larger or partially observed structures, theorem proving, or unrestricted first-order synthesis.

Appendix G Reproducibility: release contains task definitions, holdout worlds, aggregate results, parser/evaluator, and an offline verification script, but it does not rerun model inference or symbolic search.

arxiv:2608.10839.rationale: Out of scope for LLM/NLP-focused preferences: this is speech-driven gesture generation evaluation with motion capture, human studies, and no language-model methodology. It has moderate domain-specific evaluation rigor (large crowdsourced studies, attention checks, bootstrapped CIs), but limited relevance to the requested LLM/NLP/agent/transformer preferences and low generalizability beyond gesture generation.
evidence: Abstract: large-scale human evaluation with four user studies, 23,000 votes from 869 test-takers.
Sec. 3: task-dependent methodology with audio mismatching, dyadic mismatching, and text mismatching plus attention checks.
Sec. 4: reports appropriateness scores, bootstrapped confidence intervals, and challenge submission results.

arxiv:2608.10838.rationale: Relevant through VLM-guided placement, RAG context planning, prompting, and structured function-call extraction, but applied retail layout generation rather than core LLM/NLP research; hybrid contribution is incremental and evaluation is small-room, single-backbone, with the hardest settings descriptive only.
evidence: Section 3.1.2 describes VLM-guided semantic placement with RAG context planning and structured place_object extraction.
Table 2 reports PolyLayout plausibility 2.74, in-bounds 1.000, placement ratio 0.973, and latency 70.5s versus baselines.
Section 4.4 reports blind human preference of 61% for PolyLayout but only fair inter-rater agreement (Fleiss kappa 0.26).
Table 4 reports in-bounds 1.000 and plausibility 2.48 on non-rectangular plans, explicitly descriptive without a comparator baseline.
Section 4.6 ablations show clustering and solver significantly affect plausibility/robustness, while RAG plan differences are not significant after correction.

arxiv:2608.10837.rationale: Relevant to transformer compression, adapters, in-context learning, and foundation-model efficiency, but focuses on tabular foundation models rather than LLMs/NLP. Method combines known layer pruning and adapter healing with task-aware search; moderate novelty. Evaluation includes exhaustive and greedy search on 47 TabArena datasets, baselines, ablations, and OOD perturbations, but lacks statistical significance testing and only covers TabPFNv2/v2.5. Evidence supports main claims via figures/sections, though some speed-up and fine-tuning claims rely on limited data. Generalizability limited to TabPFN-family tabular models. Code URL and detailed appendices support reproducibility, but raw results and prior data are not included.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports exhaustive evaluation of all 4096 compression configurations for TabPFNv2 across 47 TabArena datasets.
Figure 3 and Section 4.2 report that structural proxy metrics fail to predict performance impact, motivating AUC-guided greedy search.
Section 4.3 describes perturbation and cross-dataset experiments supporting retention of ICL robustness.
Section 4.5 reports measured speed-ups of 1.25x, 1.63x, and 2.83x for classification at three budgets.
Appendix H lists fine-tuning hyperparameters and prior injection details.
Submission Checklist states code availability at GitHub but no raw results or pretraining data included.

arxiv:2608.10836.rationale: Out-of-scope speech/audio ASR domain application; although it uses an Audio-LLM wrapper, the core contribution is acoustic uncertainty for whispered speech recognition and does not advance LLM/NLP methodology, so relevance is capped low. Quantitative tables and ablation provide moderate evidence, but lack of limitations, statistical significance, and code release weakens rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: reports 17% relative CER reduction on AISHELL6-Whisper and hallucination rate drop from over 25% to 4.5%.
Table 2: compares CER on AISHELL6-Whisper; Ours 1.31% whispered versus Seed-ASR 1.58%.
Table 5: ablation shows Baseline 3.98%, Attention Modulation 3.45%, Global Instruction 1.84%, Full 1.31% CER.
Sec 3.1.1: defines Noise Hallucination Set and Hallucination Rate metric.
Sec 3.1.2: reports AdamW, learning rate 1e-5, LoRA rank=64/alpha=32, auxiliary loss 0.1, and training steps.

arxiv:2608.10835.rationale: Relevant multimodal hallucination-detection and safety work using frozen LVLM internal representations; strong multi-benchmark, multi-backbone evaluation and ablations, but novelty is somewhat incremental over prior structured-trace text-only detectors, generalization is limited by per-backbone training and open-weight access, and reproducibility is moderate without explicit code release.
evidence: Table 1 (MHALO) reports UniProbe F1M/F1IoU 61.7/51.2 on Qwen-3-VL and 63.2/52.9 on GLM-4V, versus HaloDet 55.4/46.7 and 59.1/49.8.
Table 4 reports CHAIR_i reduction from 18.0 to 8.2 and CHAIR_s from 37.2 to 16.6 after streaming decoding with self-adaptation, at 1.06x latency.
Table 5 validates the architecture by ablation: full model F1M 63.2; removing the graph module drops to 53.1, with individual GNN/ViT/GRU modules performing below the full model.
Appendix A gives implementation details including hidden width 256, L=2 blocks, Adam lr 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, and per-backbone read-out layers; no explicit code or data release claim is present.

Limitations state the method requires hidden states and attention maps, applies mainly to open-source models, and trains a separate readout per backbone, with cross-backbone transfer left to future work.

arxiv:2608.10827.rationale: Medical imaging agentic-VLM paper with clear LLM/tool-use/reasoning/RL methodology, so not treated as pure medical imaging, but domain specificity limits topic relevance. It combines MCTS-generated tool trajectories, reflection synthesis, GRPO with consistency reward, and validation-gated reflection memory; somewhat novel but incremental over prior medical visual-agent work. Rigor is moderate: multiple benchmarks, baselines, ablations, and tool-use necessity analysis are provided, but no confidence intervals or statistical tests, and reliance on proprietary LLM teachers/judges raises contamination and reward-hacking concerns. Generalizability is constrained to medical VQA and not tested beyond medical image tasks. Reproducibility is partial: hyperparameters and prompts are documented and artifacts are claimed, but API-based teachers/judges and compute requirements make full replication difficult.
evidence: Page 4, Section 2.2: MCTS tool-use synthesis with 20 simulations, max depth 4, branching factor 3, and teacher models Seed1.8/Gemini2.5Pro/GPT-5.2
Page 11, Table 1: MIRA-VL-8B average 64.73 vs Qwen3-VL-8B 57.29 across nine medical VQA benchmarks
Page 12, Table 3: SFT ablation shows progressive average gains, reaching 62.12 with full reflection/intention data
Page 13, Table 4: RL ablation reports MIRA-RL w/o Tools 61.35, Format+Accuracy 62.58, +Consistency 62.69, +On-policy reflection memory 64.73
Page 14, Section 5 Limitations: acknowledges base model capability constraints and limited reflection-memory generalization

arxiv:2608.10824.rationale: Moderately relevant to transformer KV-cache, inference efficiency, and vision-language-action topics, but the work is robotics-domain and does not advance core LLM/NLP methodology. The logit-margin gating is an incremental training-free extension of VLA-Cache. Quantitative results and sensitivity analyses provide some evidence, but lack statistical significance testing, error bars, and real-robot validation.
evidence: Table I and Section V-B report OpenVLA success rates and TFLOPs, including recovery of lost accuracy on Goal and Long.
Section V-E reports the gate fires on about 24% of LIBERO-Long steps.
Section V-F reports threshold sensitivity sweeps showing a broad plateau.
Section VI Limitations notes simulation-only evaluation and per-model threshold calibration.

arxiv:2608.10823.rationale: Relevant to LLM RL post-training, MoE, and training/efficiency preferences. The method is moderately novel but evaluation is narrow (GSM8K only), fault reproduction evidence is mostly qualitative, and no code/data, significance testing, or limitations are provided.
evidence: Abstract: claims 50%-87.5% accelerator reduction and up to 33.3x per-step NPU-hour reduction
Experiments, Computational Efficiency: Table 2 reports Qwen3-30B-A3B and DeepSeek-V3.2 NPU costs
Experiments, Ablation and Expert Selection Analysis: Tables 3 and 4 report GSM8K accuracy comparisons
Experiments, Fault Reproduction Capability: Figures 3 and 4 report qualitative fault-trend comparisons

arxiv:2608.10818.rationale: Pilot educational-application study of LLM-generated interactive fiction. Uses Qwen3 14B but offers no LLM/NLP methodology; treated as a domain application with capped relevance. Small N=22, single pipeline/model/domain, descriptive analysis, single-rater qualitative coding, though data/stimuli are public.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: describes a pilot user-centred evaluation of AI-generated interactive fiction for educational use.
Page 2 Section 2.2: describes the SINE pipeline using Qwen3 14B via OpenRouter.
Pages 3-4 Sections 2.3-2.5: reports N=22, descriptive analysis plan, and public dataset.
Page 6 Section 4.3: acknowledges single pipeline/model/domain, small sample, and single-rater coding limitations.

arxiv:2608.10817.rationale: Pure embodied/robotics object-goal navigation paper; LLM only used offline to generate confuser categories, with no core LLM/agent/language methodology. Per rubric, pure robotics is out of scope, so final score is capped below 0.20 despite moderate experimental content.
evidence: Abstract states AECNav is zero-shot open-vocabulary object navigation, with benchmark SR 84.7/57.3/51.3 on HM3D-v2/HM3D-OVON/MP3D and 95% over 40 physical quadruped trials.
Section IV-A lists datasets and implementation: HM3D-v2, MP3D, HM3D-OVON, Habitat simulator, C-RADIOv4 encoder, and SAM3 decoder.
Section IV-C Tables IV-V report ablations for evidence-gated perception, evidence consolidation, active evidence acquisition, and negative evidence types.
Section IV-D Table VI and Table VII report real-world deployment on Unitree Go2 with 38/40 success and roughly 5 Hz decision rate.
Section III-B states confuser categories are generated by DeepSeek-V4-Flash and cached across episodes, indicating only offline LLM use.

arxiv:2608.10810.rationale: Relevant LLM/NLP benchmark with structured matrix-guided CoT prompting and multi-task evaluation. Strengths include a principled explicit-implicit stance framework, multiple LLM baselines, oracle ablations, and explicit limitations. However, much of the final data is model-agreement or LLM-adjudicated rather than fully human-verified, inter-annotator agreement is low to moderate, evaluations are prompting-only without statistical testing or supervised baselines, and abstract improvement claims are not cleanly matched in Table 3. Chinese-specific design also limits generalizability.
evidence: Abstract: introduces CUE-Bench for Chinese unsaid emotion and matrix-guided CoT evaluation.
Section 3.4: reports inter-annotator agreement alpha 0.5197 for Affective Stance, 0.3388 for Pragmatic Intent, and 0.3146 for Fine-grained Emotion.
Appendix B.3: states final benchmark contains 51,823 instances from 60,000 candidates, with 20,000 model-agreement, 10,000 human-verified, and 21,823 retained LLM-adjudicated instances.
Table 3: reports main results across DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA-4-Maverick, LLaMA-3.1-8B, and Qwen 3-8B with direct, few-shot, CoT, and matrix-guided prompting.
Section 5.3: provides oracle-conditioning ablations on DeepSeek-V4-Flash and LLaMA-4-Maverick.
Section 7: lists limitations including residual annotation noise, coarse orientation space, and long-tailed culturally situated labels.

arxiv:2608.10807.rationale: This is a pure medical imaging/ophthalmology application using implicit neural representations to model geographic atrophy progression from fundus autofluorescence images. It does not address LLMs, NLP, transformers, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, code, safety, or other in-scope language methods. Medical imaging is explicitly out of scope and capped at 0.20. Methodologically, the paper includes comparisons, ablations, metrics, and code availability, but the dataset is small, in-house, and domain-specific, limiting generalizability and evidence strength.
evidence: Title/Abstract: 'Modelling Geographic Atrophy Progression using Implicit Neural Representations' and focus on 'Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF)' indicate an ophthalmology/medical imaging domain application.
Section 3 Experimental Setup: 'The method was evaluated on the OMEGA dataset... scans of 37 eyes... short-wavelength FAF images' confirms a domain-specific medical imaging evaluation.

Section 5 Conclusion: 'first application of INRs for modelling the progression of GA secondary to AMD' confirms the contribution is disease-specific medical image modeling rather than language or agent methodology.

arxiv:2608.11282.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/domain application with no meaningful LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, or other weighted language methodology relevance. The INR/PINN extension is incremental over prior voxelwise PINN work and is evaluated only in simulation, limiting generalizability and strength of clinical claims.
evidence: Section 3.1 reports ST-PINN DRO mean NMSE 0.09 versus PINN 0.13 and NLLS 0.17.
Section 3.2 reports ST-PINN overall median NMSE 0.212 versus 0.884 for NLLS on simulated CMR.
Section 4 states the method is evaluated entirely in simulation and patient validation remains an essential next step.

arxiv:2608.11281.rationale: Out-of-scope pure industrial/CNC application of federated learning; no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent/safety methodology. Only weak overlap with Computer Vision preference via a ResNet50 image regression pipeline. Research quality is moderate: it includes baselines and an air-cut removal ablation, but uses one dataset, one fixed seed, simulated three-client partitioning, no repeated runs or significance testing, and some table/reference inconsistencies. Overall score capped below 0.20 due to domain mismatch.
evidence: Section 1 frames the task as CNC tool wear prediction using federated learning on the MATWI dataset.
Section 3.2 reports the air-cut removal ablation reducing total MAE from 26.24 to 16.40 micrometers.
Section 5 Table 1 reports sensor modality total MAE: centralized 16.40, federated 17.90, Client B 33.28.
Section 7 acknowledges limitations including a single benchmark dataset and potential FedAvg instability under stronger client heterogeneity.

arxiv:2608.10806.rationale: Moderately relevant NLP/transformer QA reliability study, touching evaluation/robustness but not core LLM reasoning/prompting/agent topics. Method is largely standard MCD plus paraphrase perturbation; quantitative tables contain internal inconsistencies, and key claims about non-disruptive dropout rely on correlations without formal tests. Human evaluation and code/data availability improve reproducibility somewhat, but rigor and evidence are modest.
evidence: Section 3.5 specifies N=50 stochastic samples, MC dropout, the BART paraphrase model, and the S-BERT similarity interval 0.75-0.98.
Table 3 reports DistilBERT SQuAD answerable cosine similarity 0.8992 and no-answer 0.8184 but total 0.7912, inconsistent with the stated class counts.
Section 4.2 reports a Welch's t-test of RoBERTa vs DistilBERT with p=0.0 on SQuAD and p=0.4547 on QuAC, and Table 5 reports high perturbed/unperturbed correlations without formal tests.
Section 4.3 reports human evaluation on a 10% stratified sample with Fleiss' kappa of 0.7947 for RoBERTa and 0.7671 for DistilBERT.

arxiv:2608.10805.rationale: Strong systems/CNN optimization with formal I/O modeling, ablations, end-to-end benchmarks, numerical agreement, and hardware-counter validation. However, this is pure computer-vision/efficiency infrastructure without LLM, language, reasoning, prompting, agent, RAG, alignment, or safety methodology. Out of scope, so final score is capped at 0.18 despite solid execution.
evidence: §3 derives the roofline and reference I/O cost Q_ref
§4.1-4.3 describe Haar analysis fusion, bit-indexed synthesis collapse, and scale folding
§4.4 and Table 1 report 2.54x-2.56x modeled HBM traffic reduction
§5.2 and Table 2 report 3.71x-4.35x training speedup over reference
Appendix B validates the I/O model with hardware performance counters
§6 Limitations notes the reformulation is Haar-specific

arxiv:2608.10804.rationale: Pure computer vision/domain incremental learning paper using ViT-B/16 and CLIP backbones with no language-model methodology; out of scope per policy and capped at 0.20. Technically it has solid ablations and multi-benchmark results, but relevance to LLM/NLP/agents/reasoning is minimal.
evidence: Section I Introduction: defines DIL for image classification with ViT/CLIP and no language methodology.
Section IV-B, Table IV: DomainNet ViT A_T=72.19 and CLIP A_T=75.72 reported.
Section IV-C, Table VII: ablations for BPG-Adapter and BPG-Inference.
Section IV-G, Tables XII-XIII: parameter budget and latency analysis.

arxiv:2608.10801.rationale: Out-of-scope remote-sensing domain application of a vision-language foundation model for PV segmentation. The language component is limited to fixed noun-phrase prompts and prompt selection, not LLM/NLP methodology; core contribution is computer-vision/domain-specific. Despite controlled experiments and statistical analysis, relevance to target LLM/NLP preferences is minimal, capping the overall score.
evidence: Abstract states focus on SAM3 for small-scale PV segmentation in remote sensing imagery and comparison of textual/geometric/hybrid prompting.
Section III-C describes SAM3 prompt modalities and architecture; Section III-D describes fixed noun-phrase prompt selection, not LLM/NLP modeling.
Section IV-B reports statistical performance hierarchy across prompting strategies; Section IV-D reports cross-dataset consistency.
Section V-F acknowledges limitations: single target category, single model architecture, and ground-truth-derived bounding boxes.
Section III-F lists hyperparameters but no code or public data availability is stated.

arxiv:2608.10798.rationale: Out-of-scope pure image colorization/diffusion work; although it uses a FLUX image-editing foundation model and text-prompt conditioning, it has no language-model methodology and falls under the pure computer vision/diffusion exclusion. Research quality is moderate with multiple benchmarks, baselines, metrics, a human study, and stated limitations, but relevance is too low, so the overall score is capped below 0.20.
evidence: §4.3 reports quantitative results across COCO, ImageNet, and Multi-Instance under panchromatic and orthochromatic settings in Tables 1-3.
§3 describes LoRA rank 16, AdamW lr 1e-4, batch size 12, and 10 epochs on 34,745 ImageNet subset.
§5 Limitations acknowledges simplified orthochromatic simulation and LoRA-only adaptation.
§4.4 describes a human study with 25 participants and 30 evaluation inputs.

arxiv:2608.10796.rationale: Multimodal MLLM benchmark with agent-based scoring is relevant to multimodal AI, evaluation, and agent preferences, but is domain-specific affective computing rather than core LLM/NLP. The dual-perspective benchmark and BPA are moderately novel, with formal equations and extensive baseline tables; however, rigor is limited by sparse validation statistics, few ablations, and deferral to Supp. Evidence is quantitative but lacks error bars and significance testing, and only partially supports annotation-quality/cost claims. Generalizability beyond emotion/VAD is unproven; reproducibility is low due to absent code/data release and reliance on proprietary model versions.
evidence: Tables 1-2 report perception and recognition results for multiple MLLMs under Evoked/Expressed sections.
Bayesian Pairwise Alignment Framework gives equations and algorithm details for BPA.
Table 4 provides an ablation for E3mo-Score optimization and pair dispatch on evoked valence.
Experimental Setup states detailed descriptions and hyperparameters are in Supp.; no code/data release is specified in main text.
Conclusion summarizes contributions but does not provide additional quantitative validation or limitations.

arxiv:2608.10795.rationale: Topically strong for LLM-driven evolutionary code search, agents, prompting, code and memory retrieval. Novelty is moderate as persistent cross-run memory extends existing GigaEvo/AlphaEvolve-style pipelines. Empirical breadth is useful, but claims are supported with high variance, no significance testing, and only limited ablations; mechanism audit shows low absolute idea-acceptance rates. Reproducibility is aided by detailed hyperparameters and a code claim, though run-level replication details are incomplete.
evidence: §4 describes cross-task memory generation and target-benchmark memory exclusion.
Table 1 reports average gain 6.40% and average speedup 5.93, but minimum gain 0.00% and minimum speedup 0.05, indicating high variability.
§8 Limitations acknowledges run-to-run variance, sensitivity to memory pipeline quality, and lack of complete component-wise ablations.
§6.2 reports default retrieval acceptance of 4.05% versus 0.25% for random memory.
Appendix A Table 3 shows full EvoMem closes 97.4% ± 3.6% of the Circle Packing (32) target gap versus weaker baselines.

arxiv:2608.11280.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/computer vision paper with no language-model or NLP methodology. It applies an incremental ensemble of MaxViT-Tiny, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and EfficientNetV2-B0 with MC Dropout and Grad-CAM++ to HAM10000. No baselines, ablations, statistical tests, or comparisons are provided, and evaluation is limited to one filtered benchmark. Reproducibility is only partially supported by training details and no code/data availability claims.
evidence: Abstract claims 96% accuracy and 99% ROC-AUC on HAM10000 under uncertainty-aware filtering.
Methodology Section II-A states evaluation uses the HAM10000 dermoscopic dataset.
Section III-B Table I reports class-wise metrics on the uncertainty-filtered test set.
Section IV discusses clinical deployment scenarios but provides no additional quantitative validation.

arxiv:2608.10792.rationale: Domain-specific chemistry simulation environment for autonomous agents with no language-model/NLP contribution; only marginal agent-tool relevance. Internal qualification is systematic and replay/reproducibility claims are strong, but evidence is self-referential, no independent baselines or physical validation, and generalizability is explicitly limited.
evidence: Section 4.2 reports 64/64 reference units, 52/52 generated compositions, and all module/interface probes passed, but these are internal qualification counts.
Section 5.2 reports one independent 15-action agent lifecycle with resource usage and zero replay mismatch, not a comparative agent benchmark.
Section 6.3 explicitly limits conclusions to declared component/model domains and states the study does not establish reproduction of real chemical systems.

arxiv:2608.10791.rationale: Pure robotics/control paper on runtime safety monitoring for MPC navigation, with no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/RAG/agent methodology. Despite preregistered simulation, matched baselines, and statistical intervals, it is out of scope and capped at 0.20.
evidence: Section V-A: 309 brakeable collisions among 2,000 held-out scenarios; stress-only rate 4.25% (85/2000) with 95% CI [3.45, 5.23].
Section V-C Table II: thresholds frozen across 11 perturbations; stress-only share remains 17.0-27.5% of brakeable collisions.
Section VI: scope is limited to a physics-simulated 1/10-scale plant with scripted constant-velocity obstacles, excluding reactive traffic, full-size vehicles, and real perception.

arxiv:2608.10790.rationale: Out-of-scope for the stated LLM/NLP/agent/safety preferences: this is a pure compressed-domain computer-vision video tracking method using H.264 motion vectors, with only tangential relevance via efficiency/evaluation topics. The paper has moderate methodological content including ablations, encoding-variation tests, and RGB baseline comparisons, but evidence is limited to one surveillance benchmark and no code availability is stated; final score capped at 0.20.
evidence: Sec. 1 Introduction: proposes always-fast H.264 bitstream tracking without RGB reconstruction
Sec. 4.4.1, Tab. 2: ablations for temporal aggregation and MB partition metadata
Sec. 4.5, Tab. 6: reports MVDet 41K params and 139M FLOPs vs YOLO26n 2.5M params and 5.4B FLOPs
Sec. 5 Summary and Future Work: discusses limitations and future directions

arxiv:2608.10789.rationale: Quantum control/ML domain paper with only weak Scientific AI/physics simulation relevance; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, evaluation, or other core preferences. Out-of-scope cap applied. Research quality is moderate: detailed formulation and some quantitative CM values, but limited baselines, no uncertainty quantification, only d=2 numerical demonstration, and code/data only on request.
evidence: IV.4 Numerical controllability results: reports CM values approximately 0.000, 0.014, and 0.021 for amplitude scaling, and 0.000, 0.015, and 0.021 for bandwidth scaling across closed-system, classical-noise, and quantum-plus-classical-noise regimes.
V Discussion: states limitations include chosen model, finite pulse libraries, finite Haar-random samples, and time-limited validity of the graybox model.
Data and code availability: source code and data are available only upon request from the corresponding author.

arxiv:2608.11279.rationale: Numerical optimization library for Rust is largely outside the requested LLM/NLP/agent scope; weak relevance via Training & Optimization only. The manuscript describes design and feature comparisons but lacks in-text quantitative benchmark results or formal empirical evaluation, limiting rigor and evidence. Reproducibility is moderate due to open-source crate and documentation claims.
evidence: Statement of Need and Software Design describe solver catalog, constraint support, compile-time correctness, and WebAssembly compatibility, but these are design/feature descriptions rather than empirical evaluation.
State of the Field compares Basin to argmin, gomez, and nlopt, describing feature differences without providing performance data.

Research Impact Statement claims Basin generally outperforms argmin and nlopt and is on par with gomez, but refers to external benchmarks at basin.rs and provides no quantitative data in the document.

arxiv:2608.10785.rationale: Model-driven engineering/formal methods paper on triple graph grammars and view definitions. No alignment with LLMs, NLP, reasoning, agents, or other requested AI/ML topics. Although it provides formal definitions and worked examples, it lacks quantitative/empirical evaluation and most formal results are stated as future work; out-of-scope domain, capped at ≤0.20.
evidence: Page 1: Abstract describes 'Triple Graph Grammars' and 'model views' as formal semantics for NeoJoin view definitions.
Section 7: states formal results for aggregation, joins, overlapping queries, and confluence are not yet proven and are future work.

arxiv:2608.10784.rationale: Out-of-scope wireless ISAC radar/UAV tracking paper; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning/multimodal/vision/robotics-AI preference topics are addressed. The work has moderate domain-specific rigor with detailed ablations and limitations, but it is emulation-only with one geometry and no relevance to the target preferences, so the final score is capped low.
evidence: Abstract: multi-UAV tracking using 5G uplink signals on an O-RAN ISAC simulation testbed for counter-UAS C2.
Section I Scope and limitations: emulation-only, no radios, 10 noise seeds, one deterministic trajectory and one gNB siting.
Sections IX-C and XI: results reported as mechanism-level, with wall-clock vs sensor timeline analysis and GOSPA metrics.
Appendix A-E: code and data availability claims are stated but not independently verifiable from the document.

arxiv:2608.10780.rationale: Pure robot manipulation/WAM paper with language-conditioned control; per rubric this is out-of-scope robotics, so the final score is capped at <=0.20 despite moderate methodological quality. The JEPA stage-guidance plus WAM design is incremental over prior VLA-JEPA/hierarchical subgoal work, with solid RoboTwin simulation, ablations, and implementation details, but limited real-world evidence and no statistical testing.
evidence: Abstract: robot manipulation and RoboTwin evaluation
Method: Stage-JEPA and Stage-II WAM training
Ablation Study: Table 2 component ablations
Appendix A Implementation Details: hyperparameters and training details
Appendix B More Experimental Results: two-task real-robot evaluation

arxiv:2608.10777.rationale: Moderately relevant as continuous-time reinforcement learning/stochastic optimal control, matching the RL preference but not high-weight LLM/NLP/agent themes. The recursive path-integral TD formulation is somewhat novel but incremental; rigor is weakened by a convergence theorem requiring positive running cost while several experiments use f=0, and by inconsistencies in dimension claims and table references. Quantitative comparisons and ablations support efficiency and scalability claims, though without significance testing.
evidence: Section 5 Table 1 reports PI-VM runtimes of 7-8ms versus baseline runtimes of 21-194ms on unimodal SOC tasks.
Appendix B Theorem 3.3 proof relies on Assumption A1 f(x,t)>=f_inf>0, but Appendix H sets f=0 for Linear OU, GMM, and Many Well tasks.
Section 5.2 text describes a 50-dimensional Many-well experiment, while Appendix H.3 lists dimension d=10 for Many Well.
Section 5.3 refers to ablation results as Table 4, but the corresponding ablation table is numbered Table 3.

arxiv:2608.10775.rationale: Agentic VLM/GUI paper with retrieval-augmented visual skill memory and on-policy distillation, clearly matching Agents, Multimodal AI, and RAG preferences; not pure CV/domain application. Novelty is moderate over existing multimodal skill and distillation work. Rigor is limited by table-reference errors, no limitations section, and inconsistent baseline patterns, though ablations and negative controls are present. Evidence includes quantitative gains and some CIs, but main results lack broad significance testing. Generalizability across three GUI benchmarks and several model families is reasonable but domain-specific. Reproducibility is weak due to no code/data/checkpoint release and missing full training details.
evidence: Table 1 reports SkillLens gains for GPT-5.4-mini: Mind2Web Step SR 77.2->88.8 (+11.6) and OSWorld-G Grounding Acc. 45.0->66.5 (+21.5).
Table 5 negative controls show retrieved VSC exact Step Acc. 92.0 vs random 72.0 and irrelevant 71.0; OSWorld-G Grounding Acc. 66.5 vs 10.5/12.5.
CardDistill Results section reports Mind2Web Step SR +12.0 (95% CI [7.5,17.5]) and WebLINX-BG Overall +3.2 (95% CI [0.88,5.85]).
SkillLens Retrieval and Selective Expansion section defines the retrieval/reranking equations and bounded evidence budgets K_e/K_v.

arxiv:2608.10773.rationale: Qualitative journalism-domain study of GenAI use without language methodology; out of scope under the rubric cap. Touches LLM/AI safety topics but lacks computational baselines, ablations, or quantitative results, relying on small self-report interview evidence.
evidence: Section 3.1: data consists of 13 semi-structured interviews with nine informants from four Norwegian news organizations over ten months.
Section 4.3: TV2 journalist reported four or five errors in the party selection quiz due to unchecked GenAI output.
Section 4.4: none of the party selection quizzes were labelled with AI use despite extensive GenAI use among most journalists.
Section 5: proposes a GenAI Catch-22 where extensive GenAI use risks deterioration of human expertise needed to monitor GenAI systems.

arxiv:2608.10766.rationale: Moderately relevant XAI/LLM contribution: proposes RoT feature importance via predictiveness, with zero-shot LLM API experiments. Reasonable method detail and code availability, but limited datasets, no statistical significance testing, and some overclaims about adversarial invulnerability and speedups temper rigor and evidence.
evidence: §3.1.1 Table 1 reports weighted AUROC alignment: RoT 0.77, SHAP 0.74, Integrated Gradients 0.65, LIME 0.62, random 0.47.
§3.3.2/Table S7 reports across 10 adversarial experiments RoT recovers the sensitive feature as most important at least 89%, while LIME/SHAP often select foil features.
§3.4 reports first RoT explanation took 1160s and subsequent explanations <0.1 ms, compared to average 1320s per SHAP explanation.
Data and materials availability states all code is at the GitHub URL and relies on permissively licensed public datasets.

arxiv:2608.10765.rationale: Pure computer vision / human action recognition benchmark synthesis paper using skeleton and video action corpora. It does not address LLMs, NLP, reasoning, prompting, agents, code, or other in-scope language methodology. Although transformer baselines are mentioned, no transformer architecture or language contribution is made; under the rubric pure CV is out-of-scope and capped at 0.20.
evidence: Page 7, Table 4: Benchmark composition reports 15,002 episodes and realized subject-usage Gini of 0.248.
Page 5, Section 5 Validity by Design: Describes disjoint generation and evaluation rules to avoid circular supervision.
Page 8, Table 7: Reports first-order-logic violation rates with GroupY semantic rules above the 2.5% intrinsic data rate.

arxiv:2608.10764.rationale: Relevant to multimodal video-language models, SFT/RL training, and counterfactual video reasoning, but not core language-only LLM/NLP. The supplied text truncates at the Experiments heading; quantitative claims appear only in the Introduction without supporting tables, ablations, or limitations, limiting evidence and reproducibility.
evidence: Introduction reports GPT-5.6 falls from 84.0 in MCQ to 40.4 in OQA and 25.8 in captioning, and Qwen3-VL-8B drops from 57.3 to 27.3 and 16.2.
FADE section describes Stage I evidence-internalized SFT and Stage II fading-anchor RL in equations 1-12.
Document ends after the Experiments heading, with no experiment tables, ablations, limitations, or availability claims supplied.

arxiv:2608.10763.rationale: Out-of-scope HCI/serious-games manuscript: a qualitative critical design-document analysis of a VR emergency-response game using affective dramaturgy. No LLM, NLP, agentic, reasoning, RAG, or other preference-related methodology is present. Components reflect some interpretive clarity but zero topical relevance, limited generalizability, and non-public records.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: describes VR emergency-response serious game and affective dramaturgy, not language-model research.
Page 8-10: corpus is two non-public production records; qualitative document analysis only.

arxiv:2608.11277.rationale: In-scope applied LLM/RAG/KG work using an LLM as a reasoning/decision layer for explainable fault localization, but domain-specific automotive HIL application and narrow evaluation limit preference fit. Novelty is incremental over prior KG-RAG industrial fault diagnosis. Rigor is limited by a small 13-recording/60+18-window dataset, no significance tests, and no ablations isolating KG/RAG contributions. Evidence is quantitative but small-sample and partly cherry-picked. Generalizability is only shown for gain faults in two similar HIL setups. No code/data/prompt/hyperparameter disclosures reduce reproducibility.
evidence: Section V-A Table I reports best Top-1 accuracies of 0.900 (ASM) and 0.944 (EV).
Section IV-C states the evaluation subset contains 13 CSV recordings (10 ASM, 3 EV).
Section V-B Table II reports leave-one-recording-out file-level Top-1 of 1.000 for both cases.
Section VI identifies limitations: limited dataset size, gain faults only, and single-fault localization.

arxiv:2608.10760.rationale: Clearly relevant to Agents & Tool Use/MCP and enterprise agent authentication, with explicit MCP, agent identity, tool orchestration, and zero-trust security content. It offers a practical gateway architecture and OAuth delegation flows, but as an experience report it lacks quantitative evaluation, baselines, ablations, formal limitations, or code/data, and generalizability claims rest on one production deployment.
evidence: Section 3 presents the two-axis persona/credential authentication model.
Section 5 details three end-to-end identity flows, including User->Service-Account.
Section 6.3 describes the User->Service-Account authorization gate.
Section 7.3 reports deployment evolution from CDN/WAF edge to private tunnels.

arxiv:2608.10758.rationale: Moderately relevant to multimodal interpretability and vision-language analysis, but not LLM-centric. The causal-spatial tracing adaptation is incremental, and rigor is limited by small/unclear sample sizes, lack of statistical testing, unexplained metric values, and overclaimed conclusions. Evidence remains preliminary, with much of the analysis deferred to future work.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports CLIP Corr(Γ, IoU)=0.062 over 100 samples, indicating weak causal-spatial alignment.
Table 1 reports low correlations across VLMs but includes Intersection Top-k values exceeding 1 (e.g., 2.0176 for LLaVA-1.5 DDPM) without normalization explanation.
Section 4.6 notes InternVL evaluated with 6 runs and SmolVLM with only 1 run, limiting statistical stability.
Appendix A.4 describes string-puzzle observations from a single dataset instance and one model (Gemini-3.1 Pro), with no quantitative accuracy table.

arxiv:2608.10756.rationale: Out-of-scope embodied robotics/mobile manipulation paper centered on Semantic-3DGS and VLA; only tangential multimodal-language relevance to target preferences. Real-robot trials and ablations are reported, but the setting is narrow few-shot quasi-static manipulation, with limited evidence for open-vocabulary generalization and no code/data release.
evidence: Section 3.5 describes Semantic-3DGS-conditioned VLA injection into late action-expert blocks.
Table 1 in Section 4.3.2 reports 60% full-system long-horizon success versus 40% PointVLA and 28% DexVLA with 95% CIs.
Table 4 in Section 4.3.5 reports 74% full-system cluttered success versus 52% single-view and 46% PointVLA.
Section 'Scope and limitations' notes off-board GPU, quasi-static scope, and no zero-shot arbitrary skill claim.

arxiv:2608.10755.rationale: Out of scope for the stated preferences: this is a formal methods/program analysis paper on probabilistic Datalog and minimal unsatisfiable subsets, with no LLM, NLP, transformer, agent, RAG, or language methodology. Technical quality is moderate, with formal definitions, algorithms, baselines, and ablations, but relevance to the target topics is negligible. Score is capped well below 0.20 due to out-of-scope domain.
evidence: Abstract: proposes PPProbe for conflict extraction in probabilistic Datalog and reports 2.5-24x throughput claims.
Section 7.2: compares PPProbe with MARCO, ReMUS, and TOME, reporting throughput and ablation results.
Section 7.4: reports false-positive reduction statistics in Table 3.
Section 10: Data Availability Statement mentions an artifact link but provides no concrete URL.

arxiv:2608.10753.rationale: Moderately relevant as an LLM capability evaluation applied to theoretical algorithm simplification, but not an LLM/NLP methodology contribution. The empirical study is small (10 tasks, 2 prompt variants, one run per condition) and classifications are author-made with no inter-rater or statistical testing; theoretical sections are rigorous, but LLM-focused claims are limited in generalizability.
evidence: Section 2 Empirical Study describes selecting 10 algorithmic problems, three commercial LLMs, strict/non-strict prompts, and a six-category classification.
Table 1 reports per-problem/per-model results; Table 2 aggregates total simplifications, known algorithms, reductions, no benefit, gave up, and wrong counts.
Section 3 Vertex Coloring presents the claimed O(log n log Delta) list-sampling algorithm and proofs, attributed to Claude.
Appendix A contains an example prompt, showing the strict/non-strict prompt variant.

arxiv:2608.10752.rationale: Out-of-scope visible light communication and fog computing resource allocation paper with no LLM/NLP/ML content. It presents a MILP model and baseline comparison, but relevance to target preferences is zero, capping overall score at or below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: states joint optimization of AP selection, wavelength assignment and fog computing resources to minimize processing and networking power consumption.
Section IV: compares the OVP model against the OP baseline across Scenario 1 and Scenario 2 with reported power consumption results.
Section V: concludes that joint optimization achieved lower total power consumption compared with a preconfigured maximum-SINR baseline.

arxiv:2608.10743.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM-based multi-turn search agents, context refinement, retrieval-augmented QA, and RL training. Provides systematic masking analysis, multiple baselines, and quantitative EM/ART results across seven QA benchmarks, though novelty is incremental and no variance or statistical testing; reproducibility partially supported by code link and training details.
evidence: Table 1 in Sec 3.2 Analysis and Findings compares IRCoT masking variants on EM/ART, supporting the context interference findings.
Table 2 in Sec 3.3 Results and Analysis compares Context Refiner with GPT-Compress, GPT-Refine, and Self-Refine.
Table 3 and Table 4 in Sec 4.3 Results and Analysis report CRRL reliability/efficiency gains over baselines.
Limitations section acknowledges task-setting and paradigm-design constraints.

arxiv:2608.10740.rationale: Strongly relevant LLM-agent framework for research ideation with reasoning over citation trajectories. Novelty is moderate incremental over chain/graph ideation. Evaluation is quantitative but subjective and small-scale, with model-vs-human ranking discrepancy and no downstream validation; ablation text contains an internal average inconsistency.
evidence: Abstract reports ToI achieves 6.27 average vs 5.36 for strongest automatic baseline and 6.29 for Real Paper reference.
Section 4.3 Table 1 shows model-based dimension scores: ToI Novelty 6.36, Groundedness 7.00, average 6.27.
Section 4.3 Table 2 shows human evaluation: ToI average 6.62 vs CoI-Agent 6.71, with ToI first in Novelty 6.78 and Groundedness 7.17.
Section 4.4 ablation text says full ToI average is 6.04, while Table 3 lists full ToI as 6.27, an internal inconsistency.
Section 5 Limitations states evaluation is idea-stage only without downstream implementation and relies on citation-graph completeness.

arxiv:2608.10738.rationale: Out-of-scope scientific ML/dynamical systems paper on neural ODE long-time approximation; no LLM, language model, Japanese NLP, reasoning, agent, or other high-weight preference content. Formal theory and quantitative experiments exist, but relevance to the stated preferences is negligible, so the overall score is capped.
evidence: Abstract and Section 1.1 define SA-NODE long-time trajectory approximation; no LLM/language-model methodology.
Section 5.2 reports forced Duffing composite error 0.519 vs monolithic 1.98; Section 5.4 reports periodic-encoding monodromy spectral radius medians 0.044/0.101.
Appendix A contains theorem/lemma proofs (e.g., Lemma 2.2, Theorem 4.13, Theorem 4.22), indicating formal structure.

arxiv:2608.11276.rationale: Out-of-scope gravitational-wave astrophysics/Bayesian spectral inference paper; no LLM, NLP, transformer, agent, reasoning, RAG, or language-related methodology. The work includes simulation validation and posterior estimation, but it is a pure domain application and therefore capped at 0.20.
evidence: Section 2.2 describes component-wise validation with 1000 Triangle-Simulator realizations.
Section 3.2 and Table 3 report posterior recovery for astrophysical background parameters across configurations.
