arxiv:2608.10736.rationale: Out-of-scope cryptographic hardware fault-detection paper focused on Barrett Modular Multiplication/NTT protection for PQC/FHE. It does not address LLMs, NLP, reasoning, agents, prompting, RAG, alignment, interpretability, or any preferred AI/ML methodology, so preference relevance is zero. Technical quality is moderate within its domain, with algorithms, tables, and hardware comparisons, but it has limited generalizability and unverified availability claims.
evidence: Page 1, Abstract: indicates focus on fault detection in Barrett Modular Multiplication for lattice-based PQC and FHE hardware accelerators, not AI/LLM/NLP.
Page 10, Table X: reports hardware overhead comparisons for protected NTT designs on FPGA, not language model evaluation or agents.

arxiv:2608.10731.rationale: Out-of-scope psychometric factor analysis paper on bifactor models; it does not match any listed LLM/NLP/AI preferences and is a domain statistics contribution, so it is capped at most 0.20. The work contains formal propositions, simulations, and empirical datasets, but its topic is not relevant to this AI/ML curation rubric.

arxiv:2608.10730.rationale: Philosophical/evolutionary critique of AGI value; weakly relevant to AI safety and alignment preferences but not an ML/empirical research contribution. No quantitative methods, experiments, or artifacts; conceptual argument is structured and engages counterarguments but relies on cited evolutionary literature rather than original evidence.
evidence: Section 3.2: cites cyanobacteria, horseshoe crabs, sharks, nautiloids, and crocodilians as long-surviving lineages lacking general intelligence.
Section 3.4.1: states K-Pg survival factors were small body size, dietary generalism, burrowing/aquatic lifestyle, and metabolic flexibility, not cognitive sophistication.
Section 5.2: author acknowledges reliance on species persistence, survivorship bias, and imperfect biological/artificial analogy, describing the argument as suggestive rather than conclusive.

arxiv:2608.10729.rationale: Directly targets foundation model/LLM self-refinement with in-context feedback and code optimization, giving moderate-to-high topical relevance. The optimal stopping formulation and threshold characterization are reasonably novel for this setting, with formal dynamic-programming proofs. However, empirical validation is limited to one coding benchmark, 50 held-out tasks, three seeds, and lacks significance testing, which weakens evidence strength and generalizability. Reproduction is aided by stated setup and code link, but details are incomplete for independent verification.
evidence: Abstract: formalizes self-refinement as an optimal stopping problem and reports cost-efficient coding-benchmark results.
Section V-B: uses effibench with 50 tasks, N=10 refinement iterations, and three foundation models.
Section VIII: compares optimized threshold policy against fixed-iteration and UCB baselines and states highest expected value in all configurations.

arxiv:2608.10728.rationale: Biostatistics/causal survival methodology for win-ratio regression with censoring; no LLM, NLP, transformer, agent, or other in-scope AI methodology. Out-of-scope domain application, so score is capped and low despite statistical development.
evidence: Title and Abstract: win-ratio regression for prioritized composite outcomes in observational studies with future-score correction; no LLM/NLP/AI content.
Section 5: simulations under 30%, 50%, and 65% censoring report relative efficiency reaching 1.50 and near-nominal coverage for AIPW-FC.
Section 6: applied to OneFlorida EHR data with death prioritized over hospitalization.

arxiv:2608.10725.rationale: LLM/verification paper with reasoning/RAG relevance, not pure medical imaging, but medical-domain focus and prompt-level pipeline limit preference fit. Abstention-triggered SNOMED refinement is incremental; empirical support includes baselines, ablation, and McNemar tests, but single deterministic runs, a small 100-question ablation, limited external validity, and no code/data release weaken rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 3.5 describes the two-stage pipeline: Stage 1 self-generated reasoning trace, Stage 2 SNOMED CT retrieval only for UNKNOWN options.
Table 2 in Section 4.3 reports MedReason GPT-5.5 Self 92.0% to Ont 96.2% and MedQA DeepSeek-R1 Self 94.2% to Ont 96.0% with p-values.
Section 4.4 reports the ablation of re-evaluation without SNOMED on 100 MedReason questions as +0.2 pp and not significant.
Limitations notes dependence on SNOMED CT retrieval quality and risk of over-reliance on abstention in clinical settings.
Appendix B provides prompt templates, but the paper does not report code release, split seed, or multi-seed variance.

arxiv:2608.10724.rationale: Multimodal RGB-infrared object detection with structured pruning; language priors are auxiliary frozen VLM/CLIP scene embeddings rather than LLM/NLP methodology. This is an out-of-scope computer vision application and is capped below 0.20. Within its domain, the paper reports broad baselines and ablations, but lacks explicit limitations and has minimal relevance to target LLM/NLP/agent areas.
evidence: Table 1 compares mAP50 across multiple baselines on DroneVehicle and FLIR at 30/50/70% pruning ratios.
Table 3 ablates TIC, MIRA, and SPCA on FLIR.
Section 4.3.2 reports Taylor expansion order ablations.
Section 4.2 gives implementation details and states code will be available on GitHub.

arxiv:2608.10723.rationale: Pure computer vision paper on CNN-to-ViT knowledge distillation under data scarcity. It has no LLM/NLP/language methodology and is out-of-scope per the rubric, so the final score is capped at <=0.20 despite relatively thorough in-domain ablations and baseline comparisons.
evidence: Abstract: proposes iBKD/IBAM for CNN-to-ViT distillation under data scarcity.
Experiments/Table 1: reports results across seven Transformer backbones and six data-scarce benchmarks.
Attributing the Gains: single-factor experiments removing the teacher, substituting token-space attention, and permuting the teacher grid.
Ablation Studies: module/loss ablation and alignment strategy comparisons.

arxiv:2608.10718.rationale: Robotics-centric deformable manipulation competition report; mentions VLA and prompts but contains no substantive LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning methodology, so it is largely out-of-scope. Technical contributions are application-specific hardware/perception/data-loop engineering with self-reported results, no ablations or statistical validation, limited generalization, and insufficient reproduction details.
evidence: §9 Table 5 reports 25 completed T-shirts, 22 smooth, and approximately 23 seconds per attempt.
§4.2 describes the custom gripper modifications for single-layer fabric separation.
§5.2 reports four wrist-mounted camera streams resized to 224x224.
§6.1 reports 600 UMI-style and 500 real-robot raw demonstrations, with 600 final mixed episodes in §6.2.
§10 states long-horizon recovery remains challenging and that human observation, not an autonomous detector, decided early termination.

arxiv:2608.10716.rationale: Relevant voice-agent benchmark with tool calling and agentic evaluation, aligning with agent/tool/evaluation preferences but speech-centric rather than core LLM methodology. It offers moderate novelty via Pathfinding and effort metrics, with substantial quantitative analysis and explicit limitations, but uses synthetic speech, proprietary APIs, small Pathfinding cells, and judge metrics not re-validated on this corpus, limiting generalizability and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 1: six worlds, 156 scenarios, eleven conversation types, 3,825 scored conversations
Section 4.3: twelve metrics in three pillars with no composite
Table 3: Pass@1, turn-taking, DNSMOS and bootstrap intervals across systems and worlds
Limitations: synthetic speech, English-only, binary reward, judge metrics not re-validated on this corpus

arxiv:2608.10715.rationale: Pure domain application to biomedical publication analysis rather than an LLM/NLP methodology contribution. The proposed estimator is a word-frequency lower-bound method with simulation-only validation and strong counterfactual assumptions; evidence is quantitative but does not establish ground-truth accuracy. Data/code availability is stated.
evidence: Results/Table 1 reports full-paper beta-hat=0.89 for Dec 2025.
Methods describes extracting 1,194,287 English PMC papers after filtering from 7,125,722.
Simulation experiment reports |beta-hat - beta|<0.02 for simulated beta in [0,1].
Discussion/Limitations acknowledges linear extrapolation of p_human becomes tenuous over time.

arxiv:2608.10714.rationale: Relevant to LLM-driven agents, tool use, edge/local LLM, and RL-based training for orchestration, but it is a domain-specific 6G systems paper rather than a core language-modeling contribution. The architecture is described conceptually; evaluation is limited to synthetic simulations with no strong external baselines, and the verifier LLM doubles as the reference/baseline, creating circularity. Reproducibility is weak due to absent code/data/hyperparameters.
evidence: Abstract: proposes LLM-driven domain agents, A2A overlay, compact reasoning model with self-verification and shadow updates.
Section III-A: describes agent architecture, MCP/legacy adapters, and A2A overlay control plane.
Section III-C: describes offline self-verification training with GDPO and online shadow updates; uses DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B and DeepSeek-R1 verifier.
Section IV-A: reports synthetic control-plane message-volume simulations for N=10,20,30 domains and a domain join at slot 60.
Section IV-B: reports 12-domain synthetic scenarios with 3000 cases, objective switch at epoch 50, and three variants normalized to DeepSeek-R1.

arxiv:2608.10712.rationale: Pure computer-vision/3D Gaussian splatting paper with no LLM, NLP, or language methodology; out-of-scope and capped. It proposes saliency-guided superpixel merging with Set Transformer modules for compact feed-forward 3DGS. Evaluation across three backbones and benchmarks provides moderate quantitative evidence, but relevance to target preferences is negligible.
evidence: Sec. 5.1 Experimental Setup reports evaluation on DL3DV-Bench, MipNeRF360, and Tanks & Temples with frozen AnySplat, DepthSplat, and DA3 backbones.
Sec. 5.2 Main Results and Table 1 report relative primitive counts and PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS for all backbone variants and baselines.
Sec. 5.3 Ablation Studies describes removing the refiner degrading metrics and disabling cross-view merging reducing compression.

arxiv:2608.10710.rationale: Directly uses LLMs, few-shot prompting, and explanation outputs, which are relevant; however, it is an automotive application with a straightforward ensemble method. Tables support main accuracy claims, but lack of code/data, no statistical uncertainty, overlapping test windows, unexplained zero-shot results, and unknown sample sizes limit rigor, reproducibility, and evidence strength.
evidence: Section 3.3 specifies structured JSON output with predicted class, confidence, ranked classes, fault locations, and explanation.
Table 1 in Section 5.1 reports the best single-model Mistral Small 24B with Top-1 0.903, MCC 0.887, and Brier 0.102.
Table 3 in Section 5.2 reports the final Top-3 confidence-weighted ensemble with scenario-averaged Top-1 0.917, macro F1 0.913, and MCC 0.902.
Section 5.2 states the Top-5 ensemble reaches 0.910 Top-1, 0.905 macro F1, and 0.894 MCC, below the Top-3 result.
Section 4.3 states evaluation covers three settings and ten single-fault classes, while Sections 4.1-4.2 describe two HiL platforms.
Section 4.3 states zero-shot and few-shot experiments, but Section 5.1 reports only few-shot single-model results.

arxiv:2608.10709.rationale: Relevant to quantization, knowledge distillation, efficiency/training, and NLP/transformer settings, but not core LLM/agent/reasoning topics. Contribution is incremental over QFD/SQAKD, and the theoretical claim is largely definitional. Empirical support includes ablations across CNN/ViT/BERT and detailed hyperparameters, though no significance testing and some numerical inconsistencies limit rigor.
evidence: Section 4.2 Tables 1-3 report CIFAR/ImageNet accuracy comparisons against SQAKD and EWGS.
Section 4.4 Table 7 ablates Non-aware/Teacher-aware/Student-aware projection strategies.
Section 4.3 Tables 4-5 show DeiT-Tiny and BERT GLUE results supporting architectural/domain generality.
Appendix A provides implementation details and hyperparameters.

arxiv:2608.10706.rationale: Domain-specific multimodal art dataset using VLM/RAG-based annotation; relevant to Multimodal AI and dataset preferences but not central LLM/reasoning/agent research. The multi-perspective annotation and complementarity analyses are somewhat novel, but annotations are model-generated, human/judge validation is limited, and some claims (e.g., historical least replaceable across both tasks) are not fully supported by the retrieval evidence.
evidence: Section 3.2 Annotation Pipeline: narrative/emotional via Qwen3-VL-8B, formal via GalleryGPT, historical via ArtRAG; unified via Qwen3-8B.
Section 3.3 Quality Control and Data Validation: CLIP cosine similarity <0.55; Gemma-3-27B judge on 300 paintings; formal fidelity 3.70±1.17, depth 3.03±0.74.
Abstract and Section 4.1: narrative retrieval R@1=44.0%, formal R@1=7.8%, historical R@1=2.2%; reconstruction uses FLUX.2-Klein and Qwen-Image, retrieval uses Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B and Jina-CLIP-v2.
Section 4.3 Human Evaluation: 25 paintings, 9 annotators, 312 judgments; MMArt preferred in 67% of cases.

arxiv:2608.10703.rationale: High relevance as an LLM activation-steering and behavioral-control study, with moderate novelty in the situated B-data framework and thought-derived BMAs. Rigor is supported by multi-model sweeps, held-out probes, unknown-rate constraints, and norm-matched random-direction controls, but lacks statistical significance testing and relies on synthetic LLM-generated scenarios. Evidence is quantitative and section-grounded, though largely descriptive. Generalizes across Llama/Qwen/Gemma and registers within scope. Reproducibility is aided by a code/data link and detailed method appendices, though unverified.
evidence: Abstract: code and data availability claim; 3,200 scenarios and BMA framework summary.
Section 4.2 Behavioral Profiles Across Registers (RQ1): self-report gaps, split-half correlations, and cross-register profile correlations.
Section 4.3 Behavioral Mode Axes and BCL Bands (RQ2): clean directional range, BCL localization, cross-model generalization, and cross-register steering table.
Section 4.4 BMA Source and Trait Drift (RQ3): thought-derived vs response-derived BMA comparisons and trait drift.
Appendix F Behavioral Specificity of BMA Control: axis geometry, off-target transfer, and norm-matched random-direction control.

arxiv:2608.10700.rationale: Out-of-scope sequential recommender-systems application using visual+collaborative gating; no LLM/NLP/language methodology and only future-work mention of LLMs. It has reasonable domain-specific experiments, but target-topic relevance is minimal, so overall score is capped near 0.20.
evidence: Table 2 (Section 4.2) reports VisGate Hit@5 0.2207 on IKEA vs HM4SR 0.1910, +15.5%.
Section 4.6 Table 6 shows removing the contrastive loss lowers IKEA Hit@10 from 0.2889 to 0.2311.
Section 4.4 Table 4 reports early vs recent gate means on IKEA as 0.441 vs 0.468.

arxiv:2608.10699.rationale: Moderately relevant as a graph anomaly detection foundation model that uses LLM-agent pseudo-labeling and textual/graph prototypes; core problem is domain-specific TAG anomaly detection rather than LLM/NLP. Research quality is moderate: many baselines, ablations, and AUROC/AUPRC tables are provided, but there is no code release, mixed supervised/unsupervised baselines, limited generalizability beyond TAG anomaly detection, and no external validation.
evidence: Section 4.1 describes the Agents-Skills-Review-Confidence LLM pseudo-labeling mechanism.
Section 5.2 Table 2 reports ProTAGAD achieves best AUROC on seven of eight target graphs with average rank 1.12.
Section 5.3 Table 3 reports ablation results for backbone, structural prototype, and textual prototype variants.
Appendix B provides hyperparameters, hardware, and LLM-agent preprocessing details, but no code availability.

arxiv:2608.10698.rationale: Relevant LLM/NLP shared task paper on Chinese LLM-generated text detection. High topical fit for LLM/NLP, but contribution is an incremental ensemble system; evidence is mostly internal, lacks limitations and statistical testing, and the first-place claim is not independently corroborated.
evidence: Abstract reports macro-F1 0.8888 and first-place claim
Section 4.2, Table 4 reports testp1/testp2 macro-F1 and per-class F1
Section 4.3, Table 5 reports component analysis on testp1
Section 4.4, Table 7 reports ablation results on testp2
Section 4.1.3 describes implementation and module configurations

arxiv:2608.10694.rationale: Highly relevant LLM prompt-optimization/efficiency paper with direct matches to LLM, prompting, and optimization preferences. The approach is a relatively simple but systematic cost-aware decoupling of answerer/reflector/deployment tiers; novelty is moderate since weak-to-strong transfer and role decoupling were partly observed before. Empirical evidence is extensive, with multi-task/multi-model comparisons, ablations, limitations, and cost analyses, though n=3 seeds and lack of code/data release limit reproducibility and some statistical strength.
evidence: Abstract reports 96% of search tokens placed on the cheapest tier and 5.6-14x search-cost reduction.
Section 5 states cheap search is at or above parity in 36 of 48 deployments.
Appendix C, Table 5 role ablation shows reflector upgrade gives +15.1 points at Haiku deploy tier.
Section 9 Limitations discusses cheap-tier competence and prompt-insensitive ceilings.

arxiv:2608.10690.rationale: The paper studies corpus ratio estimation from released LLM tokenizer vocabularies, which is moderately relevant to LLM training-data transparency and NLP tokenization but does not address higher-weight topics such as reasoning, agents, or model behavior. QGDE extends prior tokenizer-based corpus inference with multiple quantile trends and local density weighting, and evaluation includes controlled language/domain settings, baselines, K ablations, and a realistic SmolLM validation. However, best-case claims are highlighted while typical real-world errors are higher (~5.7-6.1%), and no statistical significance or confidence intervals are reported. Reproducibility is partially supported by code and equations, but key hyperparameters are not clearly specified.
evidence: Section 6 reports token-level comparisons against Transfer and PoCTrace; Table 1 shows QGDE K=14 reaches token-level MRE around 3.5-5.9 depending on source/target settings.
Section 8 validates on the released SmolLM tokenizer; Table 2 reports QGDE token-level MRE 5.72-5.78 and category-level MRE 5.90-6.08.
Section 7 and Appendix E compare QGDE aggregation with DMI, with category-level language error around 3.0-3.3 and domain error around 5.3-5.5.
Limitations section states scarcity of ground truth for released LLM tokenizers, limiting broader real-world validation.

arxiv:2608.10689.rationale: Out-of-scope for LLM/NLP methodology: a terminal HCI/status-display design for conversational agents, with no language model, training, reasoning, or NLP contribution. The central usability claim is explicitly untested and left as future work, weakening evidence and generalizability; reproducibility is relatively strong via a normative spec, reference implementation, and conformance harness.
evidence: Section 12 states no user study yet and that identifiability from pattern alone is an untested design hypothesis.
Section 10 describes the reference implementation, golden tests, and cross-language conformance harness.
Abstract states behavioral evaluation is outlined as future work and only structural distinguishability is established.

arxiv:2608.10688.rationale: Moderately relevant NLP/keyphrase extraction study using BERT/RoBERTa/MacBERT/T5 with eye-tracking features, but not LLM-focused. Novelty is incremental over prior eye-tracking KPE work. Rigor is limited by 10 webcam participants, 60Hz sampling, small corpus, modest F1 gains, and limited statistical controls. Evidence tables are present but lack confidence intervals or multiple-comparison correction.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: reports CLIS-ET construction and FN+TFD best on Att-BiLSTM+CRF.
Page 11 Section 3.2.2: reports ten participants and SearchGazer webcam-based collection at up to 60Hz.
Page 19 Table 7: reports modest F1 gains from single eye-tracking features across KPE models.
Page 24 Table 9: reports p-values from five-fold paired t-tests, with heterogeneous significance across models.
Page 26 Ethics Statement: describes informed consent and use of publicly available journal data.

arxiv:2608.10684.rationale: Scene text recognition is pure computer vision/OCR, outside the LLM/NLP scope; only tangential transformer/attention relevance. The work includes ablations and benchmark comparisons, but the theoretical proof is only cited in Appendix A and no code release or availability is described.
evidence: Section 3.3.1 claims rotation invariance of cross-attention and refers to Appendix A for proof.
Table 2 reports ablation accuracies across 0/90/180/270 degree rotations on IC13.
Table 7 reports Union14M-Benchmark and Common Benchmark comparisons.

arxiv:2608.10682.rationale: Out-of-scope: pure computer vision/autonomous driving 3D reconstruction using a visual geometry foundation model and 3D Gaussian Splatting. No LLM/NLP/reasoning/agents/prompting/RAG/safety methodology; only tangential 'foundation model' and transformer-backbone terminology. The paper has benchmark comparisons and ablations, but evidence is limited to one driving dataset and novelty is incremental over Omni-Scene/VGD.
evidence: Table I reports nuScenes single-frame surround-view metrics comparing VGGD to baselines, Section V-B.
Section IV-B describes VGGT feature extraction with DINO-aligned, frame, and global tokens and freezing the frontend.
Table II reports Scale Warmup and Dual-Path Neck ablations under a controlled 10k-iteration setup, Section V-D.
Section VI states the limitation that the framework does not model scene dynamics.

arxiv:2608.10680.rationale: Pure computer vision paper on visible-infrared oriented object detection with no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning relevance; out-of-scope cap applies. Technical work has moderate novelty and some ablations, but evaluation is limited to a synthetic DVMA benchmark, lacks real-world generalizability and statistical testing, and code/dataset are only promised.
evidence: Abstract: proposes JFRDet and reports 69.7% mAP50 on DVMA.
Table 2: comparative results show JFRDet 69.7 mAP50 versus DMM+S2ANet 66.7 mAP50.
Table 3: component-wise ablation shows contributions from CMAA, IGCF, and AQCG.
Section 4.1: DVMA constructed from DroneVehicle with controlled affine perturbations.

arxiv:2608.10679.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/RAG/agentic QA evaluation benchmark. Introduces latent organizational reasoning with an audited truth graph and withheld target relations. Strong multi-model and access-condition matrix with disclosed limitations, but fine-grained release fidelity is not statistically supported and some analyses are post-hoc; reproducibility is partly limited by the withheld truth graph.
evidence: Section 3.4 defines L1 stated lookup, L2 stated composition, and L3 latent organizational reasoning with target relation absent from released sources.
Experiments, Table 1 reports answer accuracy across eight models and seven access conditions.
Section 4.4 RQ3 reports that gold documents still leave 30.4% of latent questions unanswered versus 12.6% explicit and 6.2% compositional.
Section 4.5 RQ4 reports release-fidelity rank statistic ρ=0.71 with exact permutation p=0.06, so fine rankings are unproven.
Appendix G describes code/data availability under MIT License and reports scoring and limitations.

arxiv:2608.10678.rationale: This paper audits Chinese web-scale corpora for polluted tokens using sampled BPE statistics. It is relevant to LLM pretraining data, data quality, and corpus auditing, but it is not a core LLM methods paper and has no Japanese-specific relevance. The method is a useful but incremental combination of sampling, BPE tokenization, and LLM-based category mapping, with moderate quantitative support and ablations. Claims are mostly supported by reported numbers, but there is no comparison to alternative auditing methods beyond full-scan/sampling/random-vs-streaming, limited statistical rigor, and generalization beyond Chinese is untested.
evidence: Abstract: claims 148.4x speedup, 35.8x memory reduction, and 4.25% relative error for pollution categories.
Section 3.2: reports 0.25% sampling recovers 76.83% of Full tokens, with Spearman 86.88% and Pearson 99.93%.
Table 1: Pollution ratios across 11 open Chinese corpora range from 0.50% to 83.38%.
Appendix C: streaming sampling is 22.4x faster than random sampling with comparable token coverage and category weighted relative error.
Limitations: transfer beyond Chinese requires multilingual annotators and language-specific search evidence.

arxiv:2608.10677.rationale: Relevant multimodal chart-understanding benchmark with LLM-judge evaluation, matching multimodal AI and evaluation preferences but not core LLM methodology. Expert authoring and 30-config evaluation add rigor, but small 100-task scale, LLM-judge grading without reported human-validation, and adversarial selection limit generalizability.
evidence: §3.1 describes expert authoring and three-expert independent verification
§5.1 Table 3 reports best pass@1 of 45.0% with 95% CIs across 30 configurations
§4.2 describes Gemini 3.5 Flash LLM judge and grading rules
§5.4 reports failure modes including missed visual elements and domain-convention errors
§3.2 Table 2 reports dataset composition and release profile

arxiv:2608.10676.rationale: Core LLM search-agent memory paper with strong relevance to LLM, agents, RAG, long-context memory, and multi-step QA. ReTree offers a plausible revision-aware tree memory and reports gains over Full-Trajectory ReAct and bounded baselines, but evidence is limited by one Qwen3-8B configuration, fixed subsets, no statistical significance testing, and no stated code release.
evidence: Abstract: ReTree constructs a bounded per-step reasoning context while preserving source-linked evidence and supports contradiction-triggered backtracking.
Table 1: Pooled ReTree accuracy 44.0% vs Full-Trajectory ReAct 30.1% over 2,149 questions.
Table 1: Full-Trajectory ReAct average maximum per-step reasoning context is 1.27-1.51x ReTree.
Table 2: ReTree CitePrec 44.5 and CiteRec 41.3 on a fixed 600-question FRAMES attribution subset.
Section 5.3: All agents use Qwen3-8B, seed 0, same search backend, and at most eight searches per question.
Section 6 Limitations: Hard pruning may over-invalidate useful state, and ReTree uses 7-11% more model calls and 10-13% more tokens than FlatUpdate.

arxiv:2608.10672.rationale: Relevant to LLM and AI safety via longitudinal study of ChatGPT-4o relational behavior, but it is a social-science/HCI user study rather than ML methodology. Novelty is moderate in focusing on system-side relational behavior. Rigor is limited by small N, T1 non-equivalence risk, preregistration deviations, and aggregated disclosure preventing planned trajectory tests. Evidence strength is mixed: quantitative stats and qualitative triangulation exist, but central system-leading claims are partly confounded by 12:1 output volume and AI-assisted coding. Generalizability constrained to one retired model, one prompt, and a German sample. Reproducibility is partial: scripts/supplements are available but chat transcripts are restricted.
evidence: Abstract/Page 1: pre-registered 4-week longitudinal study with N=72 ChatGPT-4o users under relational vs unmodified system prompt
Page 4 Results Finding 1: 30,793 coded disclosure segments; ChatGPT 21,914 vs users 8,879, with system word output about 12x user output
Page 24 Data Analysis Deviations: preregistered H2/H3 word-count and disclosure-depth trajectories could not be tested because scores were aggregated per participant
Page 13 Discussion limitations: acknowledges no pre-manipulation baseline and exploratory reversal finding requiring confirmatory replication
Methods Page 19 Data Availability: chat transcripts not publicly available due sensitivity; analysis pipeline available with access restrictions

arxiv:2608.10670.rationale: Core low-resource dialectal ASR paper; pure audio is out of scope under stated preferences, with only incidental LLM-assisted appendix error categorization. It is methodologically careful (multi-seed protocol, paired tests, power analysis, per-seed release), but domain fit caps the final score at 0.20.
evidence: Section 3.2 describes five-seed protocol with paired Wilcoxon and Holm correction
Appendix B.2 describes LLM-assisted single-seed error categorization as a directional cross-check
Conclusion states robust levers are pretraining and speed augmentation

arxiv:2608.10669.rationale: Directly in scope for LLM agents, tool use, AI safety, and red-teaming/evaluation. The benchmark has broad coverage, multiple harnesses/models, human audit, and statistical tests, but novelty is moderate because it largely integrates existing executable-state, harness-aware, and judge-reliability methods. Some internal inconsistencies and no explicit code/data release limit reproducibility.
evidence: §4.2 reports benchmark-wide ASR across six models and three harnesses in Table 2.
§4.3 reports paired trajectory-state judge comparisons with McNemar tests and label disagreements.
§4.5 reports Recognition–Execution Gap rates among state-confirmed violations in Table 3.

arxiv:2608.10668.rationale: Relevant via knowledge graphs, link prediction, and GNN message passing, but core methodology is structural temporal KG reasoning rather than LLM/NLP; novelty is moderate as an extension of ULTRA with sinusoidal temporal encoding and local/global fusion. Rigor is fairly strong with broad cross-domain experiments, ablations, and limitations, though no repeated runs or standard deviations. Evidence is quantitative but lacks significance testing; generalizability across datasets is strong but limited to TKG link prediction.
evidence: Section 6: fully-inductive cross-domain evaluation over six TKG benchmarks and code URL in footnote 1.
Table 1: FITTER outperforms INGRAM/ULTRA/TRIX across 15 transfer settings, e.g., ICEWS14-trained average MRR 44.5 vs ULTRA 34.4.
Table 4: ablation shows TE adds +8.1 MRR and +10.8 H@1 transductive, +4.0 MRR and +8.9 H@1 cross-domain.
Appendix D: limitations include dense-graph computational cost and no relation/time prediction.
Appendix F Table 7: detailed hyperparameters incl. AdamW, lr=0.0005, d=64, batch sizes.

arxiv:2608.10665.rationale: Relevant multimodal LLM reasoning/verification method with multi-agent consensus. However, core mathematical claims are inconsistent (mean preservation asserted in Section 4 is contradicted by the heterogeneous-lambda derivation in Section 13.4 and by the paper's own numerical example), and baseline comparisons are self-reported. Extensive ablations and cross-benchmark/model-family tests are positive, but fixed-seed uncertainty reporting and code availability limit reproducibility.
evidence: Section 4 states mean consensus score equals mean raw score, but Section 13.4 and the numerical example (0.9,0.3,0.9) show the unweighted mean shifts under heterogeneous lambda, contradicting the stated separation of collective doubt and conflict.
Section 10.1 reports fixing base model seed across methods, so the reported standard errors across five runs reflect 'verification noise alone,' which is unclear and weakens uncertainty estimates.
Table 2 reports domain-specific critic baselines and gains of +2.90 to +5.95, but these comparisons appear self-reported rather than independently reproduced.

arxiv:2608.10664.rationale: Theoretical causal inference/identifiability paper with only weak overlap to the 'causal reasoning' preference; no LLM/NLP, agents, RAG, safety, or other core topics. Formal proofs support the non-identifiability and recovery claims, but the setting is narrow and lacks empirical validation or code/data release.
evidence: Section 2, Theorem 1 states the backbone non-identifiability result and constructs a one-parameter family of compatible kernels.
Appendix D.1 provides Propositions 4-6 and the proof of Theorem 1.
Section 2, Proposition 2 gives the additive separability recovery result.
Section 3 states that private local causal marginals do not determine a unique backbone and communication of causal response functions is required.

arxiv:2608.10662.rationale: Relevant to LLM-based workflow automation, NLP, and prompting evaluation via design-time LLM pipeline and prompt-based baselines, but the contribution is domain-specific to quantitative syntax rather than core LLM advancement. Internal results are tabulated with baselines and three runs, but single GLM-5 backend, private code/data, approximate latency, and a local non-community benchmark limit rigor, evidence, and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 4.2 Table 4 reports QLWF L1=100.0%, L2=100.0%, L3=98.4% compared with Single-prompt L3=32.8%.
Section 4.3 Table 7 reports QLWF patch success 36/36 and token use roughly one-third of Single-prompt rebuild on the 12-task lifecycle benchmark.
Section 5.3 states QL-Bench is a researcher-built local benchmark, not community-endorsed, and code/benchmark are in a private GitHub repository during peer review.

arxiv:2608.10660.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/autonomous driving localization with only tangential transformer/attention relevance. The paper provides quantitative comparisons and ablations, but lacks code availability, statistical significance testing, and uses a small KITTI-CVL test split; final score capped at 0.20 due to domain scope.
evidence: Page 7, Table 4: CVIS test reports Ours Full mean error 1.57 m and R@1m 40.22%, versus TACV mean 3.80 m and R@1m 8.14%.
Page 9, Table 6: ablation shows Baseline mean error 12.25 m, +Multi-level Features 5.92 m, and +Temporal Context 1.57 m on CVIS.
Page 11, Table 9: real-vehicle all scenes mean error 2.84 m and R@5m 96.86%.
Page 12, Section V: limitations/future work include multimodal fusion, motion constraints, and deployment efficiency; no code availability statement is present.

arxiv:2608.10659.rationale: Out of scope as pure audio representation learning without language/NLP/LLM methodology; despite a coherent controlled comparison and quantitative results, the scope cap applies. The paper is not relevant to core LLM/NLP preferences.
evidence: Section 5.1 Table 1 reports DINO-A ViT 8x8 average 70.07 vs BYOL-A v2 82.03.
Section 4.1 states pretraining on FSD50K with no labels.
Section 6.4 lists limitations including FSD50K-only pretraining and linear probing only.

arxiv:2608.10657.rationale: Out-of-scope pure medical imaging/computer vision and biology foundation model application without language methodology; vision towers of CLIP/BiomedCLIP are used, not LLM/NLP methods. Capped at 0.20 despite quantitative benchmarking, detailed setup, and negative-result reporting.
evidence: Abstract and Section 4.5 describe vision encoders DinoBloom, BiomedCLIP, and CLIP with no text input, using vision towers only.
Section 5, Tables 4 and 8 report Stage 1 accuracy and Stage 2 held-out macro recall near 0.50, indicating AML-class collapse.
Section 5.6 and Table 9 compare random-split versus held-out evaluation, highlighting domain-specific artifact reliance.

arxiv:2608.10656.rationale: Pure robotics/control paper on underactuated aerial manipulators, outside LLM/NLP scope; only weak topical match to Robotics & Embodied AI. Method combines SMC with admittance control and is validated in SITL only. The paper provides equations, gains, and comparative metrics, but lacks physical experiments, repeated trials, or a limitations section, limiting generalizability and evidence strength.
evidence: Section V reports SITL force-tracking RMSE of 0.12 N and compares SMC with PID in free-flight tracking.
Section V-B states active arm compensation was needed to exceed 9 N, with stability up to 20 N.
Section VI describes future experimental validation on a physical prototype, confirming current results are simulation-only.
Section III-B provides a Lyapunov-based stability proof for the proposed SMC law.

arxiv:2608.10651.rationale: Out-of-scope for the stated preferences: this is a pure speech/audio and human-drone teleoperation study, using off-the-shelf Whisper/PyAnnote only for transcription/diarization. It lacks LLM/NLP methodology, transformer/reasoning/prompting/RAG/agent methods, so the final score is capped at the out-of-scope limit despite statistical validation and corpus availability.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: 'spontaneous vocal guidance consistently organizes into three kinematically and linguistically distinct phases: Orientation, Approach, and Adjustment.'
Page 2 Section II-D: 'A Binary Segmentation algorithm... was applied to the resulting 3D signal.'
Page 3 Table II: 'LINGUISTIC CHARACTERISTICS PER PHASE.'

arxiv:2608.10650.rationale: Out-of-scope Dempster–Shafer/belief-function combinatorial optimization paper; no match to LLM/NLP, agents, reasoning, safety, or other preferred topics. It has some formal content and synthetic experiments, but domain relevance is negligible and the final score is capped low.
evidence: Sec. 3 defines decision-aware approximation regret and proves the one-point bound (Thm. 3.1).
Sec. 4 reports static and online synthetic shortest-path experiments with 2500 instances and 95% confidence intervals.
Sec. 5 states limitations, including exact vector grouping open and monotonicity only conjectured for minimax regret.
No code or data availability statement is provided in the paper.

arxiv:2608.10649.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/computer vision application for colorectal polyp classification and segmentation; no LLM, language, reasoning, or agent methodology. The pipeline combines standard components (EfficientNetV2-M, UNet++, Focal Loss, transfer learning) with limited methodological novelty. Rigor is weak: no ablations, no exact segmentation Dice/IoU results despite an evaluation protocol, and approximate AUC reporting. Evidence is limited to comparative tables and qualitative Grad-CAM, without sufficient support for SOTA claims. Code is not released; only public datasets and a web app are noted.
evidence: Abstract (Page 1): describes a three-stage colorectal polyp classification and segmentation framework using EfficientNetV2-M and UNet++; no language or LLM methodology.
Experiments and Results (Page 6): Table 2 reports mAP@50 and Table 3 reports AUC ~0.99, but no Dice/IoU values are provided despite Section 5.1 specifying segmentation metrics.
Data Availability Statement (Page 8): lists public datasets and a web app, but no code release is stated.

arxiv:2608.10648.rationale: Pure computer vision/robotics fabric segmentation; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, or language methodology, and explicitly out-of-scope per instructions. Method adds known edge/shape auxiliary branches; evidence is limited to ablation results on a 235-image dataset with unclear availability and no direct established-baseline comparison.
evidence: Abstract and Section III describe a pure encoder-decoder segmentation model with edge-aware and shape-aware branches for fabric destacking; no language/LLM methodology.
Section IV Table I provides only ablation comparisons (Baseline, Baseline+EA, Baseline+EA+SA) rather than direct established-baseline comparisons.
Section IV dataset description reports a 235-image real-world collar fabric dataset with no stated public availability.

arxiv:2608.10647.rationale: EEG mental workload recognition is a pure domain application with no language-model or NLP methodology; only weak relevance via GNN/healthcare preferences. The proposed SGIB+CTS combination is incremental within EEG graph modeling, with experiments and ablations present but limited domain scope.
evidence: Abstract: proposes ProtoGIB-Workload with SGIB and CTS for subject-independent EEG workload recognition.
Method: objective includes I(Z;Y), I(A;X,R), and I(A;D|Y).
Experiments: reports cross-subject Macro-F1 improvement averaging 5.15%.
Conclusion: future work extends to dynamic temporal graphs.

arxiv:2608.10646.rationale: Directly targets LLM-based multi-agent systems failure attribution, spanning agent/step/failure-mode attribution with substantial relevance to agents, LLMs, and evaluation. The unified reciprocal agent-step contextualization is moderately novel but incremental. Rigor and evidence are solid via multiple benchmarks, baselines, ablations, and out-of-domain tests, though limited by absent statistical significance testing and limited hyperparameter sensitivity analysis. Reproducibility is supported by code availability and detailed parameters, but seed/reliability details are incomplete.
evidence: Main Results Table 1 reports ASCon macro-accuracy of 81.58 for agent and 63.90 for step attribution, with gains over StepFinder of 3.38 and 7.57 percentage points respectively.
Ablations Table 4 shows all component-removal variants degrade overall performance, including DGAT to BiGRU causing 9.14% drop in Agent MF1.
Out-of-domain Table 3 shows ASCon outperforms StepFinder and improves LLM-based baselines when incorporated as auxiliary evidence.

arxiv:2608.10644.rationale: Moderate topical relevance to RAG/Knowledge and Agents/Data via knowledge graph construction, ontology tagging, and a proposed LLM triage agent, but the core is production KG/entity-resolution engineering and the agent is designed but never run. Quality is limited by acknowledged missing identity benchmark, non-quiescent single-run measurements, enriched non-uniform samples, and unreleased/unreproducible defense data.
evidence: Section 2.3 describes the record-identity ladder; Section 7 states the ladder is unevaluated and no identity benchmark is reported.
Section 3.4 reports name-versus-type evidence asymmetry and Figure 12 shows role assignments fell from 36 to 4 on an enriched non-uniform sample of 2,500 entities.
Section 6 explicitly states the triage agent is designed and scaffolded, never run.
Table 1 states no number was taken on a quiescent graph and the identity incident is argued, not benchmarked.
Section 7.2 states the defence document set cannot be released and a synthetic substitute has not been built.

arxiv:2608.10635.rationale: Primarily a medical vision-language segmentation/grounding application, which falls under the medical imaging/domain-application out-of-scope rule; despite LLM/mask-token and CoT elements, relevance is low. Research quality is further limited by internal table-reference inconsistencies, deferred ablations, near-ceiling benchmark subsets, and limited reproducibility evidence.
evidence: Section 4.2 and Section 4.6 repeatedly cite Table 4 for main results/VQA breakdown, but Table 1 is the main results table and Table 2 is the VQA breakdown.
Section 4.6 says additional ablations including round-trip filtering are left for future versions, but Section 4.7 immediately presents round-trip filtering results.
Appendix E Tables 8-10 report many exact-match and token-recall values at 1.000, indicating limited discriminative power in the curated benchmark subset evaluation.

arxiv:2608.10634.rationale: Model-based RL paper with causal inference and off-policy evaluation is moderately relevant via the Reinforcement Learning preference, but lacks LLM/NLP/agent/code/safety themes. The IADD-TR combination is reasonably novel, with theoretical identifiability and double-robustness results; empirical validation is limited to five MuJoCo tasks with five seeds and one single-seed synthetic diagnostic, without statistical tests or code availability.
evidence: Section IV-A defines the zero-action-anchored IADD model and Theorems 1-2 for identifiability.
Section V-A describes MuJoCo benchmarks and baselines SAC, PPO, SLBO, MBPO with five random seeds.
Section V-B and Figure 3 report competitive returns, with the clearest gains on Ant and Humanoid.
Section V-B Q3 reports controlled synthetic zero-action sweep: MSE 4.043 to 0.0109 and correlation 0.346 to 0.973 for seed 1.
Section V-B Q4 reports TR improves Hopper policy-gradient cosine similarity at every checkpoint, e.g., 0.728 to 0.771 at epoch 50.
Appendices A-B provide implementation and synthetic protocol details, but no code availability claim is made.

arxiv:2608.10630.rationale: Paper evaluates wind farm blockage deficit models and multi-objective layout optimization using linear mixed-effects models; no LLM/NLP/ML methodology and falls outside all preferred topics. Within its domain it has quantitative statistics and limitations, but as AI/ML research it receives out-of-scope cap.

arxiv:2608.10627.rationale: Highly relevant LLM factuality/hallucination and mechanistic interpretability study. The central mechanistic claim is moderately supported with bootstrap CIs, permutation tests, and human verification, but scope is deliberately limited to synthetic elicited decompositions, Qwen2.5-specific primary evidence, Mistral non-replication, and very low natural occurrence. Rigor is solid in transparency and controls, though post-hoc layer-selection and small positive samples temper the evidence.
evidence: Section 4.2: reports DI-CC vs legit AUC 0.881 [0.841, 0.916] and DI-CC vs DI-UE AUC 0.863 [0.806, 0.913] at n=64, permutation p<0.0005.
Section 4.5: SelfCheckGPT-style self-consistency sampling yields AUC 0.508 for DI-CC vs legit, chance-level.
Section 5: natural injection rate is 0.2-0.4% of atomic claims, too sparse for stable regression.
Section 8 Cross-cutting: Mistral-7B cross-model probe did not replicate; DI-CC vs legit AUC 0.397 with CI below chance.
Section 6: CAD suppresses DI-CC from 4.16% to 2.57% but 19.4% of coreference-heavy decompositions fail to parse.

arxiv:2608.10626.rationale: Highly relevant LLM+RL dialogue training method with Qwen3-8B, GRPO, and multi-turn empathetic dialogue. Novelty is moderate: it adapts curriculum/experience distribution using verifiable emotion rewards, combining existing adaptive curriculum, prioritized replay, and RL ideas. Rigor is adequate with controlled baselines, multi-run SAGE results, ablations, human evaluation, and state validation, though no significance tests or explicit limitations. Evidence is multi-benchmark but some ablations are single-run; no code/data availability claims. Generalizability is limited to empathetic dialogue despite transfer across ESConv, ESC-Eval, EIBench, and human ratings.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 1: Ours reaches 79.24 SAGE Overall vs RLVER 72.01, with ESConv, ESC-Eval, EIBench, and human-rating gains.
Section 4.4, Table 5: Ablations show drops for Interaction State Only (-8.69), no hierarchical sharing (-3.04), no uncertainty bonus (-4.19), and variance-gated pass-rate controller (-16.66).
Section 4.5: Interaction-state validation reports recovery accuracies 86.7/92.5/82.5 for disclosure/activation/trust and 92.5% semantic preservation.
Section 5: Discussion and Conclusion lacks explicit limitations and makes no code/data availability statement.

arxiv:2608.11275.rationale: The paper is a formal study of probability/confidence pooling rules with synthetic Monte Carlo validation. It is only tangentially relevant to LLM/NLP preferences: it cites LLM confidence elicitation, RAG marginalization, model panels, and self-consistency as motivating applications, but its core contribution is probability combination theory, not language-model methodology. Within that limited scope, the work is rigorous, with analytic derivations, controlled cost-mismatch experiments, proper scoring analysis, and public code. Generalizability is constrained by two-source/binary settings and known generating mechanisms rather than learned or real-world LLM systems.
evidence: Section 1 Introduction positions LLM confidence aggregation, retrieval marginalization, and sampled-answer voting as related work while framing the paper around probability combination rules.
Section 3.10 Summary of part one maps each pooling rule to exactness conditions in controlled Monte Carlo worlds.
Section 4.1 Logarithmic score defines the oracle gap and betting-based evidence for mismatched rules.
Appendix A reports public release v2.0, commit 40f2cac, fixed random seeds, and expected_output.txt for reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.10623.rationale: Pure robotics/state-estimation paper with no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent/vision-language methodology; only tangential match to the low-weight Robotics & Embodied AI preference, and instruction caps pure robotics at 0.20. The spectral-analysis introspection is somewhat novel and has quantitative results, but evidence is from a single self-collected 23-minute aerial dataset with consensus/manual labeling, no direct comparison to existing health-monitoring baselines, and no code/data release.
evidence: Abstract reports detection of 51-58% of labeled failures with 60-84% precision across visual-inertial, LiDAR-inertial, and radar-inertial odometry.
Section IV-A describes the 23 min aerial robot dataset and failure labeling by estimator consensus/manual labeling.
Section VI-B reports 85% correct classification on a groundtruth dataset, with early spikes attributed to unconverged IMU biases.
Section VIII Limitations identifies smooth drift/dropouts as difficult to detect, fixed-threshold generalizability limits, and low-velocity/imbalanced dataset bias.

arxiv:2608.10622.rationale: Moderately relevant empirical study of Cursor .cursorrules prompt configuration files, touching prompting, coding agents, code generation, and security. Rigor is adequate with mixed methods and clear RQs, but analysis is descriptive, qualitative sample is small, and generalizability is limited to public GitHub repositories.
evidence: §3.1: collected 12,110 unique .cursorrules files from 11,427 repositories, snapshots April and October 2025.
§4.1.1/RQ1.3: web technologies account for 51.7% of language occurrences; 68.5% of repositories are single-maintainer.
§4.2.1/RQ3: Code Quality and Engineering Practices is the largest theme at 30.4%, security at 4.2%.
§5: limitations include GitHub API incompleteness, public-repository focus, small qualitative sample, and author interpretation.

arxiv:2608.10621.rationale: Highly relevant LLM safety/guardrail work with broad evaluation across models, datasets, and jailbreaks. However, baseline probability extraction is unspecified, no code/data or limitations are provided, and Table 1 shows ProbGuard is not best ECE in all nine settings, weakening the strong calibration claims.
evidence: Abstract: proposes ProbGuard as a probabilistic architecture-agnostic guardrail and reports calibration and ASR results.
Table 1: ProbGuard-8B is listed, but for Llama3-8B-it/SEval ECE, ShieldHead has 0.0942 vs ProbGuard 0.0989, contradicting a strict best-across-all-nine-settings claim.
Experimental Settings: lists datasets, models, and metrics but does not report code/data availability or how baseline classifiers are mapped to continuous risk probabilities.

arxiv:2608.10619.rationale: Low preference relevance: paper is entirely graph neural network/graph rewiring research, matching only the low-weight Graph Neural Networks preference and no LLM/NLP/multimodal/safety topics. Novelty is moderate: pair-centric shortage and OT-guided budget allocation are a meaningful but incremental combination over prior rewiring methods. Rigor is moderate: the paper provides formal definitions and propositions but proofs are not included in the supplied text, and some baseline comparisons are weakened by TIMEOUT entries. Evidence strength is moderate: broad benchmark tables and ablations are reported, but no significance testing or code release is stated. Generalizability within graph learning is reasonable across node/graph classification and heterophilic datasets. Reproducibility is limited by absence of code/availability statement despite Algorithm 1.
evidence: Abstract and Section III-B define pairwise communication shortage for MPNN over-squashing.
Table I reports GCN/GIN node classification with PAR average rank best among rewiring methods.
Table IV reports ablations on Texas, Roman-Empire, and MUTAG showing full PAR best on task, ΔShortage, and Coverage@10.
Tables II and III contain TIMEOUT entries for BORF on COLLAB, Tolokers, and Questions.
Section III-D provides Algorithm 1 and complexity analysis, but no code availability statement is present.

arxiv:2608.10618.rationale: Pure embodied/robotics autonomous racing paper with no LLM or language methodology; despite using attention/transformer components and world-model/agent framing, it falls outside the core LLM/NLP/RAG/safety evaluation scope, so the overall score is capped at 0.20. Research quality is moderate: detailed methods and quantitative simulation/real-vehicle results are provided, but there is little statistical rigor, limited benchmark depth, and code/data are only available on request, limiting reproducibility and generalizability beyond racing simulation.
evidence: Abstract: describes a world-model-centric autonomous racing agent and reports 88.3% interaction success rate in simulated racing scenarios.
Results, Future-Aware Reasoning for Adversarial Interaction: reports 88.3% success rate with gains of 40.8% over BC and 29.3% over SAC.
Methods, Experimental Platform and Validation: states validation was conducted in the Autoverse simulator with virtual opponent vehicles, with 358 valid trials.
Data availability and Code availability: state datasets and source code are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.

arxiv:2608.11273.rationale: Out-of-scope point cloud compression paper with no language, reasoning, agent, safety, or other target methodology. It has moderate domain-specific evaluation but does not match the stated preferences.
evidence: Abstract: proposes KLT over color attributes followed by multiple attribute coders with intra prediction.
Section III: evaluation uses G-PCC TMC13 version 10.0 and the 8iVSLF dataset, comparing to Sandri et al. and MV-HEVC.
Table III: BD-PSNR comparisons for depth-12 and depth-10 PPCs.

arxiv:2608.10614.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/MoE safety and serving attack paper. Novel combination of checkpoint router poisoning and EP straggler creation, with a clear ablation showing direct trigger-only training fails. Rigor is moderate: formal threat model, three model families, four corpora, utility and live serving evaluation, but key hyperparameters are under-specified. Generalizability is limited by the fixed contiguous placement assumption and single live-serving setup. Evidence is quantitative and tied to named sections/tables.
evidence: Section 4, Table 2: triggered target-expert share is 92.3%-95.6% across all twelve model-corpus combinations, while benign shares stay within 1.1 percentage points of clean reference.
Section 4.3, Table 4: direct trigger-only training routes 100% of both triggered and benign assignments to target experts; full Stage 3 yields 94.5% triggered and 23.4% benign versus 24.5% clean.
Section 4.4, Table 5: live Mixtral EP serving shows triggered p99 TTFT at 1.43x benign and throughput at 0.86x benign, with victim-to-peer SM utilization ratio 1.60x.
Section 2.4: threat model assumes fixed known contiguous expert placement; dynamic remapping is outside scope.
Section 4.5, Table 6: LBL router repair reduces target-share gap from 71.1 to 0.2 percentage points.

arxiv:2608.10613.rationale: In scope due to LLM-based automated program repair with DeepSeek-V3/GPT-4o, directly matching LLM and Code & Programming preferences. The paper proposes a moderately novel dual-slicing causal-context method and provides substantial quantitative comparisons and ablations. However, rigor is limited by main results using perfect fault localization, manual patch correctness review, no statistical testing, and Java-only implementation. Evidence is reasonably tabulated but lacks independent verification of reproduced baselines and has limited formal validation.
evidence: Table 2 reports CausalRepair fixing 313 correct/365 plausible bugs on Defects4J with DeepSeek-V3, compared with ReinFix and TSAPR.
Section 5.3 Table 4 reports ablations with drop rates for source dynamic slicing (26.5%), test static slicing line-only (38.3%), iterative repair (18.5%), and patch augmentation (16.9%).
Section 6.2 claims 232 fixed bugs under realistic SBFL but provides no detailed table or statistical comparison for that setting.
Section 4.4 defines plausible vs correct fixes using manual review; no automated semantic equivalence or significance tests are described.
Section 7 notes Java-only limitation due to Slicer4J, and Section 10 claims a Zenodo artifact.

arxiv:2608.11272.rationale: Out-of-scope pure 3D character skinning/graphics with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, safety, or language methodology; only peripheral GNN/CV/data relevance. Technical quality is moderate with baseline comparisons and runtime benchmarks, but lacks statistical testing and code release, and generalizability is limited to 3D meshes.
evidence: §4.4/Table 1 reports RigNet avg L1 0.432 vs RigNet+Ours 0.367 and E_def 8.58 vs 6.06.
§4.2 states 660 of 1,997 test assets appear in the training set and introduces a de-duplicated split.
§3.1/Algorithm 1 describes graph construction using ray casting and generalized winding number queries.
§5 notes limitations including sensitivity to inverted triangles/thin shells and Euclidean fallback for disconnected components.

arxiv:2608.10606.rationale: Out-of-scope pure speech/TTS evaluation with no core LLM/NLP methodology; only marginal Speech & Audio preference. The audit has some strengths such as a complete denominator, IAA subset, and cross-system controls, but it is a targeted mechanism study with limited generalizability and explicitly does not estimate production prevalence.
evidence: Abstract: ASR-roundtrip can mask context- and convention-dependent reading errors in Chinese news TTS
Section 4.1, Table 1: targeted 110-row MiMo audit reports 46 confirmed masked, 9 exposed TTS errors, and 55 no Raw TTS error
Section 5: 110-row audit is targeted rather than random and establishes mechanism and evaluator dependence, not production incidence

arxiv:2608.10605.rationale: LLM/MoE pretraining scaling and hardware-aware co-design are highly relevant. The contribution is meaningful but incremental over prior MoE scaling laws and systems co-design; validation rests on fitted scaling law, performance model, and only four staged runs. Generalizability is limited by fixed B200/Megatron/ladder and extrapolation.
evidence: Abstract: proposes MOSAIC for systems-aware scaling of sparse MoE LLMs under deliverable model FLOPs.
Section 4.2/Table 2: joint scaling law fits eta≈+0.951 with 95% BCa CI [+0.911,+0.954].
Section 7.2.1: reported MFU MAPE under 15% (9.6%/9.0%/13.2%) and Top-5 overlap 100%/100%/80%.
Section 7.5/Table 5: four staged runs reported with normalized actual MFU 0.84/0.69/0.91/1.0; ordering differs on model-FLOPs vs hardware-compute axes.
Section 9/Limitations: results are conditional on geometry ladder, hardware platform, and training recipe, with substantial extrapolation beyond the scaling-law training regime.

arxiv:2608.10602.rationale: Pure computer vision/graphics surface reconstruction via 3D Gaussian Splatting and SDF optimization. No LLM, NLP, agent, alignment, reasoning, or language-methodology connection. Out-of-scope per rubric, so preference relevance is zero and total is capped; technical comparisons and ablations provide limited quality evidence but only for object-level reconstruction.
evidence: Abstract describes Gaussian Sculpting for surface reconstruction via SDF and Gaussian Splatting.
Section 4 reports quantitative Chamfer Distance comparisons on OmniObject3D and NeRF Synthetic.
Section 5 Limitations notes object-level scope, long reconstruction time, and GPU memory constraints.

arxiv:2608.10601.rationale: Doctrinal legal analysis of EU AI Act/GDPR inference and agentic AI. It is not machine learning or NLP methodology research: no models, datasets, benchmarks, experiments, baselines, or quantitative results. Some vocabulary overlap with agents and AI safety, but the contribution is legal interpretation and governance, not computational research. Evidence is legal citation only, and Section 1.5 explicitly notes the paper is doctrinal rather than empirical.
evidence: Section 1.5 Scope limits states: 'It is doctrinal rather than empirical: no user study, benchmark or system evaluation is offered.'
Title and Abstract focus on EU legal scope for inferential capability, AI Act, and GDPR, not machine learning methods.

arxiv:2608.10600.rationale: Moderate relevance: language-conditioned robot skill transfer uses CLIP-based cross-modal vision-language and embodied AI, but is not core LLM/NLP/agent research. The paper provides baselines, ablations, quantitative tables, and limitations, supporting reasonable rigor, though code availability is limited to a project page.
evidence: Section V, Table I reports few-shot success rates with 95% CIs for BooST and five baselines across LIBERO benchmarks at 50/20/10 demonstrations.
Section V-C, Table II reports distractor-augmented pretraining results against LAPA and UniVLA.
Section V-D, Table III ablates the action pathway and task-aware encoder, and Table IV varies downstream model size.
Section V-E states limitations including 2D image skill extraction and viewpoint challenges for the distilled non-CLIP prior.

arxiv:2608.10599.rationale: Unsupervised beta-VAE latent-spectroscopy study on WorldClim has no LLM/NLP/agent/language methodology relevance; treated as out-of-scope domain application. The tolerance-dependent effective dimension framing has moderate conceptual interest, and the appendix provides hyperparameters/data splits, but evidence relies on a single seed and one dataset with no code availability, limiting rigor and generalizability.
evidence: Section II defines normalized temperature T and signal fraction M_k^2 as active coordinate criterion; Section III gives linear baseline threshold/utility equality; Section IV reports R^2≈0.98 over plotted ranks and first thirteen modes agreement; Table 1 reports PCA vs VAE required ranks; Section VI reports seed 0, one saved representative VAE run, 121 scan points, WorldClim 19 bioclimatic variables.

arxiv:2608.10598.rationale: Out-of-scope protein structure generation/retrieval paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology; despite some ablations and calibration, it is a domain application and capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: focuses on protein backbone generation, domain retrieval, and CATH S40.
Experiments: evaluates eight protein backbone generation models and introduces DRR/RetFold.
Method/Appendix G: reports calibration and quantitative retrieval results.

arxiv:2608.11271.rationale: Out-of-scope remote-sensing learned image compression and FPGA deployment; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent methodology. Only minor relevance via quantization/efficiency preferences. The paper has some ablations and documentation but is capped at <=0.20.
evidence: Abstract: first deployment of joint SAR despeckling and learned compression on FPGA; evaluates four topologies across CPU, GPU, FPGA.
Section V-A: replacing GDN with ReLU improves rate-distortion by 1.67±0.10 dB and 0.26±0.07 bpp at the highest evaluated rate.
Section V-B: Table I shows residual architectures require about 10x compute with only modest quality gain; lightweight FP is recommended for onboard deployment.
Section V-C: reports int8 FPGA PSNR higher than float32 GPU by +0.50 to +1.55 dB at highest rate, but SSIM drops about 0.02.
Section IV-C: training configurations, spatial splits, six seeds, and code repository are provided.

arxiv:2608.10595.rationale: Pure domain application in PROTAC/drug discovery with no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, or language methodology; under the stated out-of-scope rule it is capped at 0.20. The paper is relatively careful within its benchmark, with paired seeds, ablations, and leakage audits, but domain-specific and limited by weak target–E3 generalization and a relational-null control that does not isolate observed pairing semantics.
evidence: §4.2, Table 1: reports DegradeQuery-CTP AUROC 0.9065 and accuracy 0.8500 on PROTAC-8K.
§4.3: unlabeled-only CTP reaches AUROC 0.9007±0.0032 using 7,134 label-missing records.
§5: authors state the study is retrospective and benchmark-limited, with context-dependent variation in target–E3 holdouts.
§A.4, Table 19: relational-null control shows no observed-tuple advantage over shuffled target–E3 pairs (AUROC +0.0029, 95% CI [-0.0258, 0.0317]).

arxiv:2608.10592.rationale: This is a statistical inference paper on predictively oriented posteriors, convex duality, and finite-sample predictive risk. It does not substantively address LLMs, NLP, transformers, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, code, safety, alignment, interpretability, multimodal, or other listed preference topics; the only mention of language models is an acknowledgement of drafting assistance. As a pure statistical methodology application, it is out of scope and capped at or below 0.20 despite mathematical depth.
evidence: Abstract: PrO inference quantifies uncertainty by selecting a distribution over model parameters to optimize a scoring rule applied to the induced predictive distribution.
Section 4: Derives a finite-dimensional dual problem with n+1 variables and states optimality conditions.
Section 5: Provides a finite-sample excess predictive-risk bound separating sampling, approximation, regularization, and numerical optimization error.
Section 6.2.2: Reports numerical dual computation using L-BFGS-B for sample sizes 8 through 4096.

arxiv:2608.10590.rationale: Pure computer vision paper on ViT-CNN feature alignment for industrial dense prediction; no language model, NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, code/language methodology, or multimodal language component. The paper presents controlled industrial CV experiments and ablations, but it is out of scope under the rubric and must be capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: industrial dense prediction and ViT-CNN pretraining incoherence
Section 1.1: industrial object detection/segmentation under annotation scarcity
Section 5.1: four real-world industrial datasets and COCO-10 subsets
Section 6.1: main comparative results with mAP metrics

arxiv:2608.10589.rationale: Purely underwater image enhancement / computer vision with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agents, code, or language methodology. It has some domain-specific novelty in physics-inspired synthetic data and includes ablations, but it is out of scope and the final score is capped at 0.20.
