arxiv:2608.10588.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision / sign-language handshape recognition dataset paper. It contains no LLM, language-model, reasoning, agent, or NLP language methodology; per rubric, pure domain applications are capped at 0.20. The dataset and baselines are reasonably documented, but relevance to the stated preferences is negligible.
evidence: Section 3.5 reports 144,000 RGB images, 160 HamNoSys-defined classes, and 15 participants.
Section 4.3.1 reports subject-dependent ViT-B/16 top-1 accuracy of 86.20% on the proposed dataset.
Section 5 Limitations notes data were collected from 15 university students in a controlled indoor environment with a single RGB camera.

arxiv:2608.10587.rationale: Relevant to interpretability/XAI through LIME-based model-agnostic feature attribution, but outside LLM/NLP/Japanese preferences; method is a moderate incremental modification of LIME with baseline-referenced sampling/kernel and asymptotic sparsity proof. Rigor is good with formal assumptions/proofs, 1000-run simulations, and real case study; evidence includes quantitative faithfulness/robustness/stability and runtime. Generalizability limited to anomaly diagnosis/SPM and mean-shift settings; reproducibility supported by pseudocode, equations, and hyperparameters but no code availability.
evidence: Section 3.3 Theorem 3.3 and Appendix C provide asymptotic sparsity proof under Assumptions 3.1-3.2
Section 4.1.3 reports faithfulness versus mean shifts with 1000 runs and random-guess comparison
Section 4.2.2 reports escalator case study where BREAD correctly identifies shutdown escalators 08/13/14
Section 5 states limitations: point estimates, single in-control reference, no feature selection

arxiv:2608.10584.rationale: Moderately relevant LLM-based evaluation/evidence-reasoning paper, but limited novelty and mixed evidence; calibration improves absolute agreement while rank gains are inconsistent. Evaluation is CS-centric and lacks significance testing or code/data release.
evidence: Abstract: proposes LLM-based evidence-driven scholar assessment and reports dimension-dependent agreement.
Table 2: HexEval + Ridge improves MAE for D1/D3 but not Spearman for D2/D3.
Table 4: HexEval-D5 achieves similar Spearman/Kendall to zero-shot but better MAE/Acc@0.5.
Discussion: acknowledges public-record coverage, author disambiguation, and h-index limitations.

arxiv:2608.10579.rationale: Highly relevant LLM and agentic data-curation paper. The intent-conditioned four-stage selection cascade is a moderate combination of existing techniques rather than a fundamental new method. Evaluation is fairly broad across models, domains, pools, and baselines, but single-seed with no variance/significance limits rigor and evidence strength. Reproducibility is supported by detailed prompts, hyperparameters, and availability claims, though not independently verified.
evidence: Abstract: claims DataMaster outperforms static baselines and full-pool training, with public implementation available.
Table 1: reports single-domain benchmark averages across 18 model/pool settings.
Table 2: reports multi-domain results for Qwen2.5-7B across five settings.
Section 4 Ablation Study: reports Stage 1 and Stages 2-4 cascade ablations.
Appendix I Reproducibility Details: specifies single seed 42, hardware, software, and fine-tuning protocol; no multi-seed variance is reported.

arxiv:2608.10569.rationale: Out-of-scope computational fluid dynamics paper on a fifth-order finite-volume HWENO scheme for compressible Navier-Stokes equations. No LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, agent, safety, alignment, or other AI/ML methodology is present. The numerical analysis is detailed within CFD but is not relevant to the requested AI/ML research domains.
evidence: Abstract: proposes fifth-order finite-volume HWENO scheme with gradient reconstruction for compressible Navier-Stokes equations
Section 5: numerical tests cover accuracy, CPU time, and robustness

arxiv:2608.10567.rationale: Relevant LLM/VLM benchmark and evaluation paper, but domain-specific to interactive dashboard generation. Novel interaction-evidence protocol is a useful extension of existing multimodal judging, with solid human calibration, ablations, and robustness checks, though generalizability beyond single-file web dashboards is limited.
evidence: Experiments: DashJudge-8B achieves 79.8% human agreement and kappa=0.600 on 99 evaluable pairs (Table 2).
Does Interaction-Aware Evaluation Matter?: removing interaction evidence lowers agreement from 79.8% to 71.7% (Table 3).
Leaderboard Robustness: Bradley-Terry, Thurstone-Mosteller, and average-win-rate aggregation produce the same eight-model order.
Main Leaderboard: GPT-5.5 ranks first and Grok 4.3 last; render/replay rates remain below 86%/74% (Table 5).

arxiv:2608.10566.rationale: Methodological critique of iterative erasure/probing counts; directly matches interpretability/probing but not core LLM/NLP preferences. Theorems are rigorous, with controlled finite stress tests and clearly labeled exploratory visual case study; limitations are well documented.
evidence: Abstract: distinguishes population-defined quantities from procedure-defined quantities and reports exact integer-count changes under invertible reparameterization.
§3.2 Proposition 1: proves Euclidean erasure under transformed coordinates differs from original-coordinate erasure despite preserved linear predictions.
§3.3 Theorem 1: shows population ridge count is one for a=0 and two for every a≠0 with fixed sufficient and guarding rank.
§5.2: finite circular bridge reports identity mixing K=1 in all 20 runs while shears accept at least two updates; visual case study reports dense-map rank-ten AUROC changes.
§6 Limitations: acknowledges exploratory visual study, validation reuse, fixed map families, and that visual results are not confirmatory.

arxiv:2608.10562.rationale: Out-of-scope computational advertising/CVR paper with no LLM, NLP, or language-model methodology. The work is moderately novel within ads ranking and provides internal theoretical/empirical evidence, but it lacks the preferred topic alignment and has no public code/data; capped at 0.20 as a domain application.
evidence: Title/Abstract: computational advertising, click-through rate, post-click conversion rate; no LLM/NLP/language topics
Section 6, Table 2: reports >99% per-intent calibration-error reduction for MARCO
Section 6.2: online results report +2.80% conversions per click and +0.98% topline lift

arxiv:2608.10553.rationale: Time-series conformal prediction with retrieval-augmented residuals; outside core LLM/NLP scope, with only superficial RAG/embedding keyword overlap. Method is moderately novel and tested on four benchmarks, but domain-specific and not language methodology.
evidence: Abstract: proposes RCCP, a retrieval-augmented calibration method for time series prediction intervals.
Section 4.2 Results & Analysis: reports RCCP avoids empirical undercoverage at alpha=0.1 and achieves best/tied-best Winkler scores.
Section 4.3 Ablation Studies: Tables 4-5 isolate asymmetric residuals, correction, retrieval key/metric.
Limitations: notes dependence on retrieval representation and univariate/multi-step limits.

arxiv:2608.10549.rationale: Out-of-scope pure domain application: reinforcement learning for laser cutting parameter optimization, with no LLM/NLP/language methodology. Only tangential relevance via Q-learning/RL preference. Novelty is incremental tabular Q-learning with dynamic Q-table updates; evaluation lacks ablations, statistical testing, and robust baselines, and uses a single proprietary dataset.
evidence: Abstract: describes RL2C as Q-learning with epsilon-greedy for laser cutting parameter optimization.
Section 4.2 and Algorithm 1: method is tabular Q-learning with Bellman updates and dynamic Q-table updates.
Section 5.2: baselines are Random Search, RL-based Bayesian Optimization, and RL-based PSO.
Section 5.1 and Table 1: reports 210 lots (90 training/120 testing) and step/time averages, but no statistical testing or ablations.
Data availability statement: NPS dataset cannot be shared; requests via nps@npstech.co.kr; no code availability mentioned.

arxiv:2608.10545.rationale: In-scope LLM serving/efficiency paper on importance-aware KV cache transfer for edge LLM handover. Relevant to LLMs, long context/memory, inference serving, and transformer KV cache. The combination of importance ordering with multi-user backhaul allocation and sigmoid utility shaping is moderately novel. Formal optimization with KKT proof and ablations is reasonably rigorous, but main results rely heavily on fitted sigmoid simulation rather than full end-to-end inference, and no code/data release is stated.
evidence: Section IV-2 reports algebraic sigmoid R^2>0.999 for Qwen3-8B at 8K and R^2>0.99 across additional models.
Section VI-B reports the proposed allocator attains 93.7% average accuracy, within 0.5pp of the full-cache ceiling.
Section VI-C reports sub-tau starvation rate drops from 20.8% without admission to 0.65% with EB at rho=12 users/s.
Table II reports average per-user latency of 391 ms for Ours versus 847 ms re-prefill and 434 ms hybrid for Qwen3-8B.

arxiv:2608.10544.rationale: Pure computer vision image restoration using flow matching and perceptual losses; no LLM, language methodology, reasoning, agents, safety, or multimodal language components. Out-of-scope cap applies. The method combines existing latent consistency flow matching, latent perceptual losses, and gradient projection; ablations and tables are present but gains are mostly FID improvements over ELIR rather than clear wins over stronger PMRF baselines, with no statistical testing and face-only evaluations.
evidence: Section 4.2 and Table 1 report BFR results: PCFlow achieves FID 35.89 on CelebA-Test vs ELIR 44.64, but PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS are worse than PMRF.
Section 4.4 and Tables 3-5 show ablations for preheating, gradient alignment, and lambda scheduling with small metric changes and no significance testing.
Appendix 0.A provides hyperparameters and training hardware but no code availability statement is present.

arxiv:2608.10542.rationale: Pure robotics/control paper on SCP-based NMPC for drone-to-drone docking; no LLM/NLP/agent/vision-language relevance, so preference_relevance=0.0 and final score capped below 0.20. Simulation-only evaluation with some quantitative metrics but no baselines, ablations, or code/data availability.
evidence: Section IV, Table II reports docking time, peak cone violation, and control energy under wind sigma=0.1/0.3/0.5/1.0 for 10 trials.
Section V notes future work on physical deployment, formal recursive feasibility, and systematic comparison with PID/SQP, indicating limitations.

arxiv:2608.10538.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM/agent/tool-use preferences, and the language-level RL-over-skills idea is moderately novel over prior verbal RL/skill-evolution work. However, credibility is undermined by internal inconsistencies between the abstract and experimental setup, contradictions with reported baseline wins, absence of statistical significance testing or limitations, and narrow selected benchmark subsets. Quantitative ablations and cost analyses provide some evidence, but claims are not fully supported by the reported results.
evidence: Abstract claims actor/critic uses GPT-5.5 or Claude opus 4.8; Experimental Setup states GPT-5.4 is used
Table 1 shows Qwen3.5-4B SkillsBench: SKILLER 42.03 vs SkillX 43.48, contradicting abstract claim of outperforming all baselines
Table 2 shows Qwen3.5-4B EarthBench: Manus 70.97 vs SKILLER 69.62, so not all zero-shot baselines are beaten
Tables 5-7 in Appendices A-C report ablations as three-run averages with no variance or statistical tests
No Limitations section is present; Appendix D uses selected subsets and split sizes of 83/124, limiting generalizability

arxiv:2608.10537.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM interpretability, reasoning, and AI safety. FNL is a novel, label-free metric with cross-dataset/model validation and limited but honest downstream applications. Evidence is mostly correlational: injection AUCs are moderate-strong but paraphrase correlation is weak; steering gains are model-specific and marginal. Reproducibility is strong with code, seeds, and hyperparameters.
evidence: Token injection susceptibility: Table 2 reports Spearman correlations between FNL and token-injection recovery from -0.39 to -0.46, with AUC 0.73-0.84 separating token-driven from context-dependent features.
FNL-Guided Steering: Table 4 reports high-FNL steering at avg@4 0.911 versus unsteered 0.865 (+4.6), low-FNL 0.903, random 0.901; text states gains are model-specific.
Auditing Jailbreaking-mitigation mechanisms: reports 21 of 25 selected features have 0 nonlocality; Table 3 shows positional subset held-out safety 0.911 versus content subset 0.504.
Data and Code Availability and Appendix D: repository link/release v1.0.0, seeds, hyperparameters, and infrastructure are provided for reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.10535.rationale: Out-of-scope pure domain application for recommender/personalized search systems. The paper does not address LLMs, Japanese NLP, reasoning, agents, safety, or language-model methodology; transformer/attention use is incidental to a domain architecture. Within its niche it offers incremental multi-interest modeling, with standard experiments, ablations, and hyperparameter studies, but limited relevance to the requested preferences and no strong language-methodology contribution.
evidence: Abstract
§5.1.1 Datasets
§5.2 Model Performance
§5.3 Ablation Study

arxiv:2608.10532.rationale: Relevant as an LLM-based closed-loop control-plane and tool-use evaluation with reasoning-mode ablations. Systematic 240-run sweep and strong reproducibility support the score; limited generalizability, single-seed/fault-class design, and primarily descriptive evidence temper it.
evidence: Section 3.5 defines the 240-run matrix, seed 42, and factor combinations.
Section 5.1 reports the approximate 3B active-parameter capability threshold and ~88% median 5xx reduction.
Section 6.4 acknowledges single seed, one fault class, one load balancer/backend stack, fleet <=9, and single GPU as threats.
Appendix A lists GGUF repos, commits, and quantization for reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.10530.rationale: Highly relevant systematic review of agentic LLM security, aligning with LLM, agents/tool use, AI safety, prompting, RAG, and red teaming preferences. Novelty is moderate: it offers a PRISMA-based review and four-layer taxonomy but no new empirical method. Rigor is weakened by inconsistent counts (Section 6.1 reports 17 defense-focused studies vs Table 11 reporting 12) and placeholder reference entries, limiting evidence strength and reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have undergone a shift... agents... vulnerabilities.
Section 1.5 Contributions: claims first PRISMA-based systematic review specifically focused on vulnerabilities associated with agentic LLMs.
Section 2.4 Search Strategy, Search Strings and Databases: search process described but exact query strings and data extraction artifacts not fully provided.
Section 4.2-4.5: four-layer vulnerability taxonomy covering perception, brain, action, and interaction layers.
Section 6.1 and Table 11: defense-focused study count inconsistency (17 vs 12).
References: multiple entries contain placeholder citation notes, limiting reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.10529.rationale: Broadly a multi-agent bandit/RL theory paper with no LLM, NLP, Japanese, reasoning, prompting, safety, or language methodology; only weak relevance via the RL/multi-agent preference. The theoretical treatment is coherent but incremental, with no lower bounds, only a small toy experiment lacking external baselines or ablations, and no code/data availability.
evidence: Section II-C defines the robust UCB estimator and concentration bound used by all algorithms.
Section VI-B reports only a toy M=2,K=2 experiment with no external baselines or ablations.
Section VII acknowledges known tail parameters and missing lower bounds as limitations.

arxiv:2608.10528.rationale: Strongly relevant LLM reranking/retrieval evaluation study with robust statistical correction and high reproducibility; novelty is limited to stress-testing an existing method rather than introducing a new architecture.
evidence: Section 4.2 catalogues eight undocumented implementation choices and reports an initial paper-only reimplementation nDCG@10 drop from 0.66 to 0.24.
Section 5 reports Holm-Bonferroni correction reduces PAGC-vs-GCCP significance from 8/22 to 5/22 and PAGC-vs-RG-YN from 15/22 to 12/22.
Section 6 reports under E5 retrieval PAGC does not significantly improve over GCCP on any of 8 BEIR datasets and is significantly worse on DBPedia-Entity (Δ=-0.0144, pHolm=0.032).
Section 7 reports spectral MDS is never the best anchor on the 8 BEIR datasets; top-3 composite wins 5/8 and Random wins 3/8.

arxiv:2608.10526.rationale: Relevant only tangentially through RL/multi-agent preferences; no LLM/NLP/agent focus. The multi-player Lipschitz bandit extension is incremental but has a non-trivial dithering coordination idea. Theoretical results are partially supported by sketched proofs, but experiments are idealized and do not directly simulate the proposed signalling/dithering mechanisms, weakening evidence and reproducibility.
evidence: Section VII states that information structures are modeled at the feedback level and direct simulation of signalling and dithering is left to an extended version.
Appendix B gives a proof sketch but leaves choices of alpha and gamma unspecified.
Algorithm 1 in Section III-B provides pseudo-code for the main algorithm.

arxiv:2608.10525.rationale: Proposes adapter-based historical visual context injection into a frozen VLM/LLM for vision-language navigation. Moderately relevant via multimodal LLMs, efficiency, and embodied navigation, but it is not core LLM/Japanese NLP/reasoning/agent methodology. Novelty is incremental. Rigor is limited by inconsistent efficiency claims, questionable architecture descriptions, missing limitations, and single-benchmark evaluation. Evidence is quantitative but partly conflicting, and no code release is indicated.
evidence: Abstract: claims 'over 25% reduction in attention FLOPs and 13% memory savings'.
Section 4.2/Table 1: reports total FLOPs 4.77T to 4.23T and peak memory 37.84GB to 34.31GB, about 11.3% and 9.3% reductions, conflicting with abstract claims.
Section 3.1.2: states the integration process operates on 'encoder-only multi-layer language models' despite the Phi-2 LLM backbone identified in Section 3.
Section 4.3/Table 2: primary results are limited to VLN-CE R2R Val-Unseen; no broader benchmarks are reported.
Section 4.5/Table 3: reports ablations on fusion, compression, and memory capacity but lacks a limitations discussion.

arxiv:2608.10524.rationale: Moderately relevant multimodal vision-language retrieval paper that uses LLM/VLM-assisted benchmark construction and CLIP-like fine-tuning, but is not core LLM/NLP/agent/safety. The method is an incremental combination of existing soft-label supervision and structural distillation, with broad but self-reported quantitative results. No significance testing or explicit limitations; code not provided, though hyperparameters and prompts improve reproducibility.
evidence: Table 1 reports SAFT and baseline mAP@10/20/30 across six CLIP-like models on SecMM-TBIR pedestrian and vehicle subsets.
Section 4.3 Table 6 ablates ITC, SASS, and ISD with incremental mAP@20 gains.
Table 3 reports general-domain results on Flickr30K and MS-COCO.
Appendix B Table 8 lists fine-tuning hyperparameters including batch size, optimizer, and learning rate.

arxiv:2608.10523.rationale: Randomized sketching paper for polynomial kernels with only tangential relevance via efficiency/compression; no LLM/NLP/transformer/agent/safety alignment. The CtR TensorSketch extension is incremental, proofs contain notation inconsistencies, and empirical support is limited to small low-dimensional dense datasets with weak downstream gains and no code release.
evidence: Abstract: claims O(p(nnz(x)+D log D)) sketching time and 2^p/D variance dependence
Theorem 2: states unbiasedness, variance bound, and time complexity
Section 5: reports KL divergence and wall-clock time on COD-RNA and MAGIC datasets
Appendix C.3 Table 3: downstream SVM accuracy 0.5289 vs baselines, exact kernel 0.8756

arxiv:2608.10522.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/tabular multimodal pre-training with no LLM/NLP/language methodology, so capped at 0.20. It addresses low-weight Medical/Healthcare AI and multimodal image-tabular learning, but not the core language-model, reasoning, agents, safety, or NLP preferences. The paper reports quantitative dermatology/ophthalmology benchmarks and ablations, but claims are from untrusted text and not language-related.
evidence: Abstract describes semantic-aware multimodal pre-training for medical tabular data.
Table 1 reports SOTA comparisons on SLICE-3D, HOP, and EyePACS.
Section 3.1 describes experimental setup and datasets.

arxiv:2608.10521.rationale: Pure hardware-security/formal-methods paper on probabilistic saturating counters and differential privacy. No LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent methodology; only marginal AI Safety/security keyword overlap. Internal formal apparatus and gem5/SPEC experiments are present, but overall outside the target preference scope.
evidence: Abstract names formal DP analysis of PSCs under Prime+Probe attacks.
Sect. 5.1 reports gem5 and SPEC CPU 2017 performance evaluation.
Sect. 5.2 compares theoretical and experimental misprediction rates on MergeSort.
Appendix 0.C contains formal k-bit PSC definitions and proofs.

arxiv:2608.10519.rationale: Out-of-scope pure visual/video autoregressive synthesis with no language methodology; despite reasonable ablations and quantitative VBench/fidelity results, topic mismatch imposes a hard 0.20 cap.
evidence: Section Analysis reports cross-scale pattern reuse causes ~35.6% average attention mass drop while fresh block-wise Top-K has only a 4.64% gap to token-wise upper bound.
Table 1 reports SparSTAR on 720p T2V: PSNR 31.22, SSIM 0.898, LPIPS 0.065, VBench 83.83, and 1.60x speedup versus dense InfinityStar.
Section B.2 Code Availability states code, prompts, seeds, manifests, and raw outputs will be made publicly available upon publication.

arxiv:2608.10517.rationale: Optical-network physical-layer modeling with domain-specific neural networks; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/multimodal language methodology, so relevance is capped. Simulation-only validation using GNPy, limited to equivalent-span C+L/SSMF, no code or experimental verification, but quantitative baseline comparisons and unseen-scenario few-shot adaptation are reported.
evidence: Section 5.1 reports RMSE improvements over BaseCondNet for NLI/ASE/signal power and GSNR estimation
Section 5.2 reports few-shot fine-tuning results on 12 unseen scenarios with 20 samples per scenario
Table 4 reports runtime comparison between GNPy simulation and DeepModNet inference
Section 4.2 describes GNPy-generated training data across 35 scenarios

arxiv:2608.10513.rationale: Highly relevant to multimodal LLM safety, RLHF/alignment, and LLM evaluation. The caption-mediated GRPO objective is a moderate integration of prior captioning/reward ideas rather than a fundamentally new paradigm. Evidence from five safety and six utility benchmarks, multiple protocols, SFT/DPO/SafeGRPO comparisons, and ablations supports the main DirectCap safety-utility claims, but rigor is tempered by reliance on automatic judges, limited full-run seed/statistical coverage, and small Qwen-only models. Reproducibility is aided by code links, training configuration, and prompt appendices.
evidence: Abstract: reports gains of 3.7-19.0 points in safety average across four model settings under DirectCap while maintaining comparable or improved vision utility.
Experiments/Table 2: SafeCap DirectCap safety-average changes vs zero-training are +4.0 (2B), +3.7 (2B-Base), +6.6 (4B), +19.0 (4B-Base), with utility changes +6.4, +7.1, +4.5, -0.1 respectively.

Ablation Studies/Table 4: removing the direct answer reward lowers safety by 5.31 under Direct and 6.49 under DirectCap; removing the caption reward or decoupled normalization also degrades most safety/utility metrics.
Appendix A: provides hardware, SPA-VL data, GRPO hyperparameters, frozen LLM and judge models, seed robustness, and response-length diagnostics.
Appendix D: acknowledges limitations including frozen-LLM capability bounds, no factual visual-correctness reward, and small Qwen3.5-scale evaluation.

arxiv:2608.10512.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision low-light image enhancement paper; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology beyond using transformer-based baselines. The paper provides domain-specific experiments, ablations, and human evaluation, but relevance to the stated preferences is negligible and the final score is capped below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract proposes CAGE with AdaLAB and AdaCCT for color-faithful low-light image enhancement.
Table 1 reports PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS improvements on LOLv1, LOLv2-real, and LOLv2-synthetic across Retinexformer, DarkIR, and HVI-CIDNet backbones.
Section 4.4 ablations show the full parameter set reaches 24.2355 PSNR on LOLv2-real and that removing hue-shift parameters causes the largest PSNR drop.
Appendix B.5 Table 9 reports small overheads of +0.070M parameters and +0.005G FLOPs when adding CAGE to LLIE backbones.

arxiv:2608.10509.rationale: Strongly within scope for agents, shared memory/retrieval, and safety, but evaluated mainly on synthetic templated tasks with single-run controlled results and adapted baselines. The contribution is a reasonable combination of provenance, permission filtering, trust reranking, and action gating rather than a major conceptual advance. Quantitative ablations and backbone transfer are useful but do not establish deployment-scale or run-to-run robustness.
evidence: Section 4.4 reports MAP-Graph TSR 94.96%, Acc 72.70%, clean 90.22%, unsafe 1.52%, and ASR/leakage/revocation 0% on 2,700 synthetic tasks
Table 2 ablations show removing permission filter raises UAcc to 100% while improving utility, indicating utility can mask access-control failure
Section 4.5 reports backbone transfer on a 540-task subset with highest exact accuracy and lowest unsafe rate across Qwen, GLM, and Llama
Section 4.4 and Section 4.6 state limitations including synthetic templated tasks, simulated actions, one four-agent round, and single-run results

arxiv:2608.10508.rationale: Pure molecular spectroscopy/physics paper on CO-Ar frequency comb Fourier-transform spectroscopy and collisional line-shape parameters. No LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, or AI/ML methodology; outside all relevant preference categories. Domain-specific quantitative precision noted but not relevant to the requested AI/ML scope, so capped as out-of-scope domain application.

arxiv:2608.10506.rationale: Out-of-scope CNN inference-cost/deployment-screening systems paper with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, or language-model methodology. The experimental characterization and CARB ensembling show moderate internal rigor, but final relevance is capped at 0.20 because this is pure computer-vision/systems efficiency work outside the language-model focus.
evidence: Section 3.1 describes hardware setup, clock locking, and measurement protocol
Section 5.3 describes the CARB cascade ensemble with XGBoost, LightGBM, and ExtraTrees
Section 6.3 reports runtime feature ablation comparing M1, M2, and M3
Section 7.2 describes reducing 3072 candidates to a Pareto shortlist on RTX 3080

arxiv:2608.10505.rationale: Low relevance due to medical imaging application, which the rubric caps at 0.20, despite LLM rewriting and multimodal NLP components. The threshold-controllable report generation idea is somewhat novel but incremental. Rigor is limited by a partly circular closed-loop evaluation, lack of statistical testing, and limited external baselines. Evidence is provided mainly in tables/figures without error bars; generalizability is limited to MIMIC-CXR; reproducibility is limited by closed models and no code release.
evidence: Section 3.1 describes fusing a classifier, QRad report generator, and LLM rewriter.
Section 4.2 describes the closed-loop ROC evaluation and threshold sweep on MIMIC-CXR.
Section 5.1 and Table 1 report classifier implementation ablation AUC-ROC values.
Section 5.2 and Tables 2-3 report LLM rewriter ablations across model sizes and reasoning effort.
Section 7 lists limitations including error propagation, template tuning, predefined class scope, and label-extraction error.

arxiv:2608.10504.rationale: Highly relevant to agent/LLM workflow optimization, coding agents, knowledge graph retrieval, and evaluation. However, the paper is mainly architectural with selective disclosure; quantitative results lack significance tests, ablations, or equal validation splits, and several baselines are cited rather than reproduced.
evidence: Section 1.2 describes MEGA as a self-evolving agent optimization infrastructure with typed Wisdom Graph and multi-agent optimization.
Section 3 Scope of Disclosure states that algorithmic details are selectively disclosed at design objectives, limiting reproducibility and rigorous assessment.
Section 7.1 reports SkillsBench pass rate 46.5% and efficiency 0.566 score/Mtok versus SkillNet 41.7% and AgentSkillOS 41.1%.
Section 7.2 reports aggregate score 76.55 on GPT-4.1Mini versus GEPA 69.52, but baseline scores for MIPROv2/TextGrad/GEPA are cited directly from prior work and MEGA uses smaller validation sets.
Section 7.2 states the gains reflect the integrated infrastructure rather than any single component, and no explicit ablation/limitations section is provided.

arxiv:2608.10503.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM bias/safety evaluation via token-level PMFs and factorial designs, but empirical validation is limited to one construct, English, and logprob-accessible models. The distributional ANOVA and ordinal consensus extension are moderately novel, with a formal appendix, yet evidence is descriptive rather than externally validated, and no code/data availability is shown.
evidence: Abstract: proposes an exact token-level PMF framework for measuring LLM attitudes and biases
Section 4.2: reports main and interaction effects with SNR and dPD, including aggregate vs factorial sign reversals
Limitations: empirical experiments focus exclusively on consumer ethnocentrism, English, and require token probability access
Appendix A.8: quantitatively compares exact PMFs against Monte Carlo sampling and decoding bias

arxiv:2608.10502.rationale: In-scope agentic LLM memory and tool-use recovery. Dependency-guided rollback integrates provenance/slicing with independent-support checking and selective replay, a moderate but well-specified contribution. Controlled and transfer benchmarks, ablations, and cost analyses support core claims, though single-run temperature-0 evaluations, an author-constructed controlled benchmark, no statistical variability, and no stated code/data release limit rigor, reproducibility, and generalizability.
evidence: Table 2: Ours recovery 0.853 vs LLM-judge repair 0.773, with replay ratio 0.123 vs 0.217.
Section 5.2 ablations: removing the rollback planner drops recovery to 0.713; removing selective replay raises replay ratio to 0.755.
Section 5.3: adapted LongMemEval-V2 recovery 0.680 vs AgentTrace-style 0.540, with claim invalidation F1 0.669 vs 0.603.
Section 6 acknowledges remaining recurrence gaps and identifies future work on recurrence robustness and claim-state identification.

arxiv:2608.10500.rationale: Out-of-scope pure CV/graphics avatar rendering with cloth dynamics; no LLM/NLP/agents/safety. Only incidental causal attention matches a low-weight transformer topic. Reported quantitative comparisons and ablations are moderate, but no error bars, no code, limited baselines, and per-subject training limit overall quality.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 1: reports PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS for HumanNeRF, GaussianAvatar, Animatable-GS, and Ours.
Section 4.3, Table 2: reports ND (MMD=0.23) and FD (MMD=0.87) ablation variants with PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS.
Section 0.A.4, Table 3: reports temporal window/memory bank size ablation for n,m configurations.
Section 0.A.6: states limitations including per-subject training and no modeling of topological changes.

arxiv:2608.10499.rationale: Pure RL/federated RL paper has limited relevance to LLM/NLP curation despite the RL preference; contribution is incremental RND plus exploration-summary aggregation. Evaluation uses only two modified classic control tasks, lacks statistical testing or error bars, gives incomplete environment details, and makes broad privacy claims without formal analysis.
evidence: Section III-A: Evaluation is limited to modified MountainCar-v0 and CartPole-sparse with N=10 clients.
Section III-B: Tables and figures report average returns without standard deviations, error bars, or significance tests.
Section III-A: Hyperparameters are partially listed (T=100, E=10, Adam, lr=3e-4, gamma=0.99), but code/data availability and seed settings are not stated.
Section IV: Claims no compromise in privacy despite only sharing aggregated exploration summaries and no formal privacy analysis.

arxiv:2608.10497.rationale: Out-of-scope pure biometrics/computer vision work on face/person/gait recognition. It uses an MLLM only as an offline pseudo-labeler/distillation teacher, not advancing LLM, Japanese NLP, reasoning, agents, or language methodology. Technical content is moderately developed but incremental; quantitative tables are garbled and hard to verify, and no code/release is evidenced.
evidence: Abstract: proposes SapiensID 2.0, transferring zero-shot semantic knowledge from Multimodal Large Language Models into a discriminative embedding space.
Section 3.3: uses Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct offline for semantic subspace construction.
Section 4: reports zero-shot benchmarks on CCVID, CCPG, Market1501, MSMT17, LFW, etc.
Appendix B: states limitations including dependence on teacher MLLM capabilities and offline computational overhead.

arxiv:2608.10494.rationale: Core LLM agent/tool-use/memory methodology is strongly relevant, though applied to Earth observation. The three-memory self-evolving design is incremental over existing self-evolving agent memory systems, and the EO-specific evaluation limits generality. Experiments are broad across benchmarks and LLM backbones, but lack statistical testing, error bars, and a limitations analysis, and no code release is stated. Some reported results are inconsistent across metrics (e.g., GPT-4o Tool-In-Order drops below baselines).
evidence: Methodology > Evidence-Grounded Execution: GeoForge assembles retrieved graph context, action-level experiences, adapted SOP, and deterministic EO guidance.
Table 1: GeoForge reports best accuracy on four backbones (GPT-5 74.33, DeepSeek-V3.1 77.09, Gemini-2.5-Flash 67.91, Qwen3-Max 69.72).
Table 3: Ablation shows all three memory components contribute; no-memory accuracy 52.23 vs full 74.33.
Figure 5: Sensitivity analysis shows robustness to Top-k and retrieval threshold.
Table 2: GeoPlan-Bench Recall_key 1.00 and Holistic 1100.65; ThinkGeo Answer 60.98.

arxiv:2608.10492.rationale: Relevant to LLM/CoT/fine-tuning and code generation with LLM-as-judge evaluation, but applied to education simulation. Method is somewhat incremental, lacks significance tests and broad generalization.
evidence: Section 3.4 defines Experiment 1 and Experiment 2 comparing SFT and INSIDE against CoT/BloomCoT baselines.
Section 4.2 reports LLM-judge validation on n=209 and manual agreement kappa=0.754.
Section 5.1 Table 1 reports Wasserstein distances; INSIDE is lowest on test_OP but comparable to SFT on test_NP.
Section 6 notes reconstructed reasoning traces are teacher approximations and test_OP/test_NP differ in pass-rate distributions.

arxiv:2608.10489.rationale: Relevant to multimodal VLM token pruning and efficient inference, but not core LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/safety. Method has moderate novelty combining residual subspace scoring with attention and diversity. Quantitative benchmarks and ablations support claims, but no significance tests/limitations/hardware details and pruning-layer schedule/code availability are unclear.

arxiv:2608.10485.rationale: Out-of-scope pure UAV multi-object tracking / robotics / computer vision paper with no LLM or language methodology. arxiv:2608.10480.rationale: LLM-centric molecular property prediction with instruction tuning, LoRA, and GNN-derived textual rationale. Relevant to LLM and interpretability preferences, but domain-specific chemistry application rather than a general language methodology contribution. Rigor is moderate: three-run ablations, multiple diagnostics, and significance tests are strengths, but generalist baselines are evaluated with uneven task coverage and limited seed runs. Evidence from Tables 1-7 and the diagnostics section supports the main claims. Generalizability is limited to MoleculeNet-style property prediction. Reproducibility is strong with code URL, hyperparameters, splits, and prompt templates.

arxiv:2608.10473.rationale: Out-of-scope offline-to-online RL/robotic manipulation paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology. arxiv:2608.10471.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM prompting, prompt optimization, agents/tool use, and evaluation. arxiv:2608.10462.rationale: Moderately high relevance: the paper targets LLM data contamination detection and black-box membership inference, intersecting LLM, AI safety/privacy, and NLP, though outside Japanese LLM/agent/reasoning core areas. arxiv:2608.10441.rationale: Directly addresses LLM acquisition agents and a reward-SNR detectability floor, making it highly relevant to LLM/agent preferences. Experiments include CIs, placebos, positive controls, robustness checks, and stated limitations, but key positive downstream gains are small and several nulls are power-limited. Reproducibility is partly strong via claimed code/ledger but constrained by unverifiable GPT-5.4/GPT-5.5 configurations and a credential-free proxy.

Generalizability is moderate for read-only tool settings, with untested multimodal extensions, while reproducibility is weak due to absence of code, data, or experimental results.

arxiv:2608.10416.rationale: Moderately relevant as transformer attention/optimization theory, but not LLM/NLP-specific and purely theoretical. evidence: Section 2.3, Theorem 2.2 proof contains an algebra error in the softmax lower-bound derivation.

arxiv:2608.10400.rationale: Relevant to interpretability and AI safety/fairness preferences via Rashomon-set analysis of judicial decision-making, but not LLM/NLP; moderate novelty and rigor. evidence: Summary of experiments and results: reports unexplainable cases 2%-33%, 100% of sampled unexplainable cases attributed to data/form errors, outside-county charges, or case-specific details; small decision trees depth<=5 achieve 75%-100% accuracy, with >=85% for 17/21 judges; variable importance highlights age, warrant count, and crime flags; cross-judge transfer deteriorates; triplet self-consistency ~76% vs ~55% cross-judge.
When do judges not follow any reasonable algorithm?: describes using TreeFARMS Rashomon sets and manual case review of 100 unexplainable cases falling into three noise categories.
Can each judge be described by an algorithm?: reports GOSDT models with depth budget 5, regularization 0.001, and balanced accuracy in Figure 8; 17/21 judges captured at >=85% accuracy.

Are judges consistent with themselves and each other?: pairwise loss distributions, FP-Growth disagreement rules with support/confidence/lift, and triplet analysis show self-consistency above cross-judge agreement, with cross-judge agreement near 50%.
Appendix D and Data and Processing: provide feature engineering, filtering to 22,361 usable cases, TreeFARMS regularization 0.005, Rashomon bound multiplier 0.01, and public code URL.
