Appendix A.2 Table 6 reports text-only FS input improves Qwen3-Omni average BERTScore-F1 by +0.017 over audio input.

arxiv:2608.10357.rationale: Highly relevant to agentic tool-use RL, long-context attention, and efficiency. However, the paper is preliminary: one observed training run, no baselines or ablations, dashboard-estimated metrics, no multiple seeds, and peak-VRAM-only memory evidence limit rigor and generalizability. Novelty is mostly systems integration of existing GRPO, Gymnasium, FlexAttention, and sink-scaling ideas.
evidence: {'section': '6.2.1 Preliminary Retail Training Results', 'claim': 'Reports retail validation reward rising from 0.25 to 0.44 and states values are visually estimated from dashboard screenshots.'}

{'section': '6.2.2 Peak-Memory Results', 'claim': 'Reports optimized sink-aware FlexAttention path reduces peak VRAM from 28.06 GB to 22.52 GB at 4096 tokens and completes 8192-token configuration where eager baseline is OOM.'}
{'section': '7 Discussion and Limitations', 'claim': 'Notes lack of multiple seeds, optimizer baseline, and exported scalar logs, limiting causal and statistical claims.'}

arxiv:2608.10356.rationale: Statistically rigorous paper on prediction-powered inference for spatial data, but it does not match the stated LLM/NLP/agent/evaluation preference areas. The main contributions are formal design-based finite-population results and simulations/empirical spatial analyses; no language-model methodology is present. Research quality is high (formal proofs, simulations, real enumerated population), but personal topic relevance is very low, so the overall score remains modest.
evidence: Abstract: introduces design-based prediction-powered inference for spatial data and double robustness.
Section 5.3: validates Theorem 1 on a real fully enumerated 48,175-cell Estonian land-cover population.
Appendix A: contains formal assumptions and proofs with provenance.
Section 6.1: empirical land-cover analysis with reconstructed LUCAS design weights.
Data and code paragraph: references public data and distributed scripts with fixed seeds.

arxiv:2608.10351.rationale: The paper proposes Tensor-Featured training with randomized CPD tensor decomposition to accelerate DNN optimization for high-dimensional function/PDE learning. It has no LLM/NLP/agent/vision/speech focus and only weak relevance to training optimization, scaling/efficiency, and scientific AI. The method is modestly novel but empirical, limited to two synthetic PDE benchmarks with no statistical rigor or broad baselines; reported improvements are mixed and sometimes CPD interpolation alone outperforms the proposed DNN.
evidence: Section III specifies DNN architecture (3 layers, 100 features, relu/relu/identity), ADAM, 3000 epochs, domain/grid and training/validation set sizes.
Section IV.1 reports Tensor-Featured training improves over conventional training in some cases but CPD approximation alone outperforms it (Fig. 1, Fig. 3).
Section IV.2 reports rank-1 features combined with CPD features accelerate convergence; Table 2 shows rank-1 feature training cost is only marginally higher.

arxiv:2608.10350.rationale: Out-of-scope scientific/domain application: quantum-magnet Hamiltonian inference from inelastic neutron scattering using neural surrogates and Bayesian experimental design. No core LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/prompting methodology; incidental mentions of ChatGPT for language polishing and future agentic lab automation do not make it relevant. Within physics the methods are somewhat detailed, but model-dependent powder source separation and unavailable code/data weaken reproducibility; final score capped at 0.20 for out-of-scope domain application.
evidence: Abstract: framework combines Hamiltonian-conditioned neural surrogates, Bayesian inference, and observation geometry for INS of NiPS3; no language-model methodology.
Discussion: mentions agentic AI-driven laboratory automation only as future direction, not core contribution.
Code availability: source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance; Data availability: experimental data from corresponding author upon reasonable request.

arxiv:2608.10349.rationale: Pure-domain IoT intrusion detection/XAI study; relevant only via interpretability and efficiency categories and has no LLM/NLP/Transformer methodology, so preference_relevance is capped. The work is methodologically careful with a leakage audit, ablations, and reproducibility artifacts, but it is limited to one dataset and host environment, lacks external validation and formal significance testing, and some full-test costs are projections.
evidence: Section 5.5 and Section 5.7 specify classical ML models (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost) and reproducibility controls; no language-model methods appear.
Section 11 acknowledges single-dataset CICIoT2023 scope, host-based timing, no external validation, and point-estimate predictive metrics without formal significance testing.

Section 7 reports TreeSHAP costs and Section 9 reports selective-explanation cost-coverage, but Section 11 notes full-test explanation times are throughput-based projections rather than direct runtime measurements.

arxiv:2608.10346.rationale: Pure computer vision face landmark detection; uses transformer attention and a SentenceBERT text encoder only for face-part labels, with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent methodology. Out-of-scope per rubric, capped at <=0.20. Domain methodology shows moderate novelty and rigor, but relevance to preferred AI topics is minimal.
evidence: Abstract: 'Face landmark detection (FLD) aims to predict the coordinates of predefined landmarks in facial images.'
Section 4 Implementation Details: 'We employ the pretrained SentenceBERT as the face part text encoder, FaRL pretrained ViT-B or ResNet as the facial image encoder.'
Section 4 Experiments: 'We train and evaluate our framework on three benchmark datasets: AFLW, 300W, and WFLW.'
Table 2: Comparison with SOTA methods on WFLW, 300W, and AFLW-19.
Appendix A.6 Table 4: Held-out landmark prediction compared with cubic-spline interpolation.

arxiv:2608.10345.rationale: Pure computer vision/3D Gaussian splatting and deblurring with no LLM/NLP/language/agent methodology; out-of-scope so preference relevance is very low. The cascade has moderate novelty but mostly assembles frozen NAFNet/RAFT/NoPoSplat modules. Evaluation is limited to 85 fixed tuples across 15 scenes with no variance/statistical tests and some baseline setting mismatch. Generalizability is narrow (two-view static scenes, known intrinsics).
evidence: Abstract reports 1.19 dB real-world and 2.11 dB synthetic PSNR gains.
Table 1 shows quantitative NVS results against SE-GS, GAURA, CoherentGS, DAVANet, and Difix3D+; Sec. 5.2 discusses baseline setting differences.
Table 2 shows progressive ablation gains on real-world scenes; Sec. 5.3 describes Stage 1 and Stage 2 contributions.
Sec. 6 Limitations states assumptions of known intrinsics, static scenes, and possible failure under extreme blur or large occlusions.

arxiv:2608.10344.rationale: Out-of-scope mechanical topology optimization paper using physics-informed ML. It has no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning relevance; only generic training/optimization terms such as Adam and loss weakly match low-weight preferences. Domain-specific rigor is moderate, but the work is a pure domain application and is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: multi-material topology optimization of thermally actuated compliant devices
Section 1: Physics-informed ML embeds governing equations and objectives into learning
Section 2.4: all parameters are trained simultaneously with Adam on a combined loss

arxiv:2608.10343.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging low-dose CT denoising paper; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agents, or language methodology. Within its domain it has quantitative comparisons and ablations, but relevance to the stated preferences is minimal, so the score is capped near 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: proposes ENCORE for low-dose CT denoising, confirming medical imaging focus.
IV-A Datasets: evaluates Mayo2016, Mayo2020, and tabletop CT data.
IV-B Training and Evaluation Details: reports PSNR/SSIM/AUHOC and statistical significance testing.
V-C Ablation Studies: reports ablations on noise modeling, zero-shot control, context estimation, and FlyingConv configurations.

arxiv:2608.10339.rationale: Moderately relevant LLM/causal-reasoning methodology applied to hospital QI. The paper proposes a novel synthesis of Gantt charts, g-computation, and LLM-based expert scaling with explicit identification assumptions and simulations. However, real-world causal estimates lack ground truth, human validation is small, and data/code access is limited.
evidence: Section 4.1 Table 1: DAG-extractor + Gantt-timing achieves 0.00 +/- 0.00 bias, while Single-DAG variants show biases up to about 14 hours.

Section 4.2.1 Table 2: LLM-human concordance edge precision is 91.8% (early discharge planning) and 94.2% (disposition-critical imaging), but mean difference in estimated time saved intervals include zero.
Section 4.2.2 Table 3: ICL (GPT-5) wait-time MAE is 24.12 hours versus 27.23-36.58 hours for baselines, with zero-gap 28.30 hours.
Section 4.2.3 and Appendix M Tables 10-11: expected impact ranking top three stable in 89% of bootstrap resamples, but confidence intervals are wide and no external outcome validation is provided.

arxiv:2608.10338.rationale: Out-of-scope domain-specific visualization/audio study for therapeutic music composition; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/alignment methodology. It has moderate HCI design-study novelty and reporting, but small samples (n=7 students, n=2 composers), self-reported SUS/confidence, no clinical validation, limited generalizability, and no code/data release beyond OSF supplement. Final score capped at 0.20 for pure audio/domain application.
evidence: Abstract: reports SUS=72.23 and evaluation with eight music students and two experienced composers.
Section 3.1: uses uCue interaction logs and audio features from sessions with children with ASD.
Section 4.5/Discussion: reports SUS scores 70.71 and 73.75 and confidence increases but small samples.
Section 6.4 Limitations: acknowledges modest uCue dataset, limited participant diversity, subset of musical parameters, and no clinical trials.

arxiv:2608.10337.rationale: Applied LLM/HCI creative-writing interface using GPT-4.1; relevant only as an application of LLM text generation, with no language-model methodology or NLP model contribution. The interaction idea is moderately novel but incremental over prior writing tools. Evaluations include quantitative and qualitative results with a small user study and one baseline, giving moderate evidence but limited generalizability and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 5.6: implementation uses Next.js, React Flow, Slate.js, OpenAI API, GPT-4.1; source code promised upon publication.
Section 6.1.2: WQRM-PRE pairwise preference 72/100; paired t-test M=6.24 vs 5.74, t=6.52, p<.001; human majority preference for characterization 29/30 and overall 25/30.

Section 6.2.2: within-subjects n=12; AI System Experience and CSI surveys show significant gains in think-through, transparency, controllability, enjoyment, immersion, exploration, and expressiveness.
Section 7.2: limitations include 12 participants, short three-act task, single baseline, and limited support for non-linear plots.

arxiv:2608.10333.rationale: Directly in-scope for LLM agents, tool use, routing, code generation, and fine-tuning. The contribution is a conservative integration of routing, skill memory, and small-model adaptation, but it is somewhat incremental. Main code-generation gains are quantified, though router baselines are matched adaptations rather than official checkpoints and TAU-2 evidence is underpowered. Limitations are clearly disclosed, but reproducibility is constrained by nonstandard/future model endpoints and private finance assumptions.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 1: multi-cycle SFT+GRPO reaches 49.7% direct pass versus 28.7% base SLM.
Section 4.3, Table 2: verifier-backed fallback yields 88.3% pass at 60.8% cost; router baselines are matched adaptations.
Section 4.4 and 6.4: TAU-2 improves from 14/35 to 18/35 with one-sided McNemar p=0.171875, reported as underpowered.
Section 7 Limitations: weak pre-router, verifier coverage, trace-centric evaluation constraints.

arxiv:2608.10332.rationale: Out-of-scope learning-based control paper with no LLM/NLP/agent methodology. It addresses differentiable predictive control and control barrier functions; despite a theoretical contribution, the feasibility guarantees are conditional/existence-level with strong assumptions and limited simulation-only evidence, so overall relevance and score are low.
evidence: Abstract claims deterministic feasibility guarantees for DPC via topological analysis and CBF proxy loss.
Section 5 acknowledges the results 'primarily serve as existence proofs' and constructive bounds remain future work.
Assumption 3.2 assumes CBF condition satisfaction; Proposition 4.1 is conditional on dense dataset covering the reachable safe set.
Section 6 reports monotonic violation-ratio decreases for mobile robot, unstable linear system, and quadcopter simulations, with limited quantitative baselines.

arxiv:2608.11269.rationale: Out-of-scope for the stated preferences: CosMAP is a UMAP/contrastive dimensionality-reduction method applied to omics, handwritten digits, and genealogical data, with no LLM/NLP/agent/safety/reasoning methodology beyond a brief mention of transformer attention. The contribution is an incremental combination of cosine kNN, NT-Xent temperature normalization, heavy-tailed low-dimensional kernel, and two-phase refinement. Evaluation is largely qualitative on MNIST/USPS; quantitative NMI is limited to Retina, Cortex, and kinship. Ablations use synthetic make_blobs rather than real data. Code and algorithms are described, improving reproducibility, but results are untrusted and not independently verified.
evidence: Abstract: states CosMAP is graph-based unsupervised DR for omics and genealogical data and evaluated on MNIST, USPS, mouse retina, cortex, and BALSAC-CARTaGENE.
Section 3.1: describes cosine kNN graph with temperature-scaled NT-Xent-style affinities.
Section 4.2 and Section 4.3: report NMI comparisons on Retina and Cortex scRNA-seq datasets.
Section 4.4: reports kinship matrix qualitative and NMI results.
Appendix 7.1: ablation on synthetic make_blobs with Euclidean vs cosine metric.
Section 4.5: describes PyTorch/GPU implementation and GitHub availability.
Section 5: acknowledges refinement is not universally optimal and may over-separate small datasets.

arxiv:2608.10330.rationale: Relevant to AI agents and LLM baselines, but the core method is symbolic/heuristic (ASP + compositional hierarchy) rather than LLM methodology. The paper provides hypotheses, baselines, ablations, and quantitative comparisons in one simulated 66-entity household with 5 users; however, limitations are not explicitly analyzed, statistical details are sparse, and generalization/reproducibility are limited.
evidence: Section 4.1 Experimental Setup reports 66 entities, 4 rooms, 12 actions, 5 users, 10 sessions, 3,000 ambiguous commands.
Section 4.2 Baselines defines B0-B7 including GPT-5.1 LLM baselines and ablations isolating concept, pattern, thematic, and ASP filtering components.
Tables 1-2 report noask/ask accuracy and clarification rates, claiming the proposed method outperforms all baselines.
Section 6 Conclusion frames limitations as future work such as larger domains, partial observability, and physical robots.

arxiv:2608.10329.rationale: Applied LLM-as-judge/NLP study for EPA regulatory text auditing; relevant but not core LLM/NLP research. The framework and audit transparency are strengths, but the evidence is descriptive, Finding 3 is small and proxy-dependent, and key measurement components have unaudited recall/proxy limitations.
evidence: §6.3 reports 69.0% vs 49.5% revised and docket-FE OR=1.93 (p=0.037) for high-engagement obligations
§6.5 reports the cosine outcome classifier achieves SE/MO κ=0.137 against human audit while human inter-rater κ=0.816
§6.4 reports audit-corrected Finding 3 Fisher OR=4.90, p=0.044, n=115; §8.2 states submitter-type reconstruction is heuristic and Finding 3 conditional
§8.1 notes no recall measurement for the obligation-comment matcher and no deduplication of mass comments

arxiv:2608.11350.rationale: Relevant as frozen VLM/foundation-model agent adaptation via textual skill and harness optimization, but embodied/robotics domain and limited evaluation reduce fit and strength. Novelty is incremental over SkillOpt/EmbodiSkill/AutoHarness. Results are descriptive with small adaptation sets, custom VLABench splits, no statistical error bars, weak SFT/TTS comparisons, and small category-level samples; the ESI-Bench GPT-5 PS comparison is external and unpaired. Reproducibility is supported by appendix prompt/harness templates and cost accounting, though no code/data release is stated.
evidence: Section 4.1 describes custom VLABench C1-C4 held-out splits and the ESI-Bench 231-question subset.
Section 4.2 Table 2 reports SHAPER overall 34.50% versus Seed Agent 28.25% and SFT 24.00%.
Section 4.3 Table 3 reports ESI-Bench micro accuracy 49.8% for SHAPER versus 32.5% for Seed Agent.
Appendix A includes prompt templates, harness code details, and optimization cost accounting.

arxiv:2608.11274.rationale: Highly relevant to AI safety, agent tool use, and alignment critique. It is a position paper with a conceptual runtime-contract framework and public audits, but novelty is moderate because it synthesizes existing guardrail, sandboxing, and CI/evidence practices. Rigor is limited by title-level proceedings audit, counterfactual incident coding, and row-level data being referenced but not included; no experimental baselines or ablations. Evidence supports recurring failures and product gaps but not strong causal proof. Generalizability is solid for verifiable consequential-agent tasks, weaker for open-ended tasks. Reproducibility depends on unavailable supplementary JSON.
evidence: Abstract: positions agent safety as a runtime contract with preventive and evidential faces
Section 4.2: formalizes Agent Trajectory Schema and Evidence Chain with hard/soft evidence
Table 2: trajectory schema audit of 12 public agent systems showing only 2 with submission-like evidence gates
Section 5: reports 52-incident survey, 31+1 false-completion audit, and 28,560-paper proceedings audit headline numbers
Appendix A: acknowledges limitations including no goal control and polynomial verification only under independent verifiers

arxiv:2608.11205.rationale: Technically substantive visual-generation paper with ablations and quantitative gains, but it is a pure image generation/diffusion post-training method with no language methodology. Thus it is out of scope and capped at <=0.20 despite moderate research quality.
evidence: Section 5.2 Main Results / Table 1: AdvFD improves JiT-L FID from 0.77 to 0.73, FD-r6 from 3.24 to 2.01, and FD-r3 from 5.46 to 3.20.
Section 5.3 Ablation Study / Table 2(b): Removing real-feature whitening degrades FID to 10.69, FD-r6 to 58.50, and FD-r3 to 40.54.
Appendix F Limitations: Evaluation is limited to class-conditional ImageNet 256x256 generation; higher-resolution, text-conditioned, and video generation remain unvalidated.

arxiv:2608.11079.rationale: Highly relevant to agents/tool use and prompt compression for LLM agents. The evaluation-free typed MDL formulation is moderately novel, but rigor is limited by no significance tests or ablations and by inconsistent claims (e.g., abstract says one structured extraction call while Table II reports 4-8 LLM calls). Evidence is quantitative but mostly point estimates without variance. Generalizability is partly supported across three benchmarks/models and cross-model transfer, while reproducibility benefits from appendix prompts/schema but lacks verified code release.
evidence: Section VI-C, Table I reports SkillZip average compression rate 31.2% and macro-average performance 0.577 vs evolved skill 0.570.
Section VI-D, Table II reports zero rollouts and average speedup over SkillReducer, but reports 4-8 LLM calls, conflicting with the abstract/one-shot extraction claim.
Section IV-A defines the shortest faithful explanation objective with a hard coverage constraint; Proposition IV.1 and Corollary IV.2 state parsed-contract and rare-rule preservation.
Appendix B includes CLI, schema, and prompt details supporting reproducibility, though no actual code release is verified.

arxiv:2608.10915.rationale: Highly relevant position paper on LLM-based agentic AI, agents/tool use, edge/local LLMs, and AI safety, but it is conceptual with no experiments, baselines, ablations, or quantitative results. Formal framework and evaluation agenda are described but not empirically validated; low reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: introduces Combodied Agents as a human-centered Agentic AI paradigm and outlines closed-loop perception/memory/prediction/intervention.
Section 2.4: formalizes closed-loop state estimation, memory, prediction, and intervention with equations but no empirical tests.
Section 5.2.3: defines edge-native personal Combodied Agents with local memory, PWM, intervention policy and selective cloud use.
Section 6: proposes evaluation matrix, agency-preservation metrics, and CombodiedBench but does not provide implementation, results, or benchmark data.

arxiv:2608.10875.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, long-horizon memory, and safety evaluation. The benchmark is moderately novel in combining proactivity, living-world dynamics, and long horizons, but rigor and evidence are limited: no ablations, significance tests, or validation of scoring checks, and open-source availability is asserted but not demonstrated.
evidence: Section 2.2: defines 200 long-horizon tasks across ten everyday-life domains with 22 mock services and weighted checks.
Section 2.4: reports 200 tasks, 7,453 events including 1,483 silent mutations, and 12,261 checks.
Section 4.1, Table 5: reports avg@3 scores from 21.1 to 32.5 across seven evaluated models.
Section 5.1, Table 7: reports capability-axis pass rates showing low proactivity and persistence.

arxiv:2608.10812.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM post-training, RLHF/GRPO, and multilingual MT, with broad multilingual benchmarking. Novelty is incremental given prior GRPO/QE-based MT work, though checkpoint interpolation and OPD analysis add useful evidence. Rigor is solid with baselines, ablations, and detailed appendices, but evaluation partly relies on the same learned quality metrics used as rewards, and no human or significance testing is reported.
evidence: Abstract: applies GRPO with reference-free QE reward gated by language identification and SFT-RL checkpoint interpolation.
Section 4.1 Main Results: averaged over scales, WMT24++ XCOMET/COMETKiwi improve by 2.75 and 2.44 points over SFT.
Section 4.2 Analysis: Figure 2 reports interpolation trade-off, with alpha=0.5 recovering 2.79-4.21 spBLEU at different scales.
Section 5 On-Policy Distillation Analysis: OPD approaches but does not surpass RL+interpolation, with Table 2 comparing students.
Appendix C: reports complete GRPO hyperparameters shared across scales.

arxiv:2608.10744.rationale: Out of scope: video diffusion and 4D reconstruction without language methodology. The direct latent-to-4D interface is somewhat novel, but the evidence relies on projection-based DINO proxies and a shared VAE setting, limiting rigor and generalizability; cap applied.
evidence: Abstract: describes direct latent-to-4D generation and Text4D-200/I4D-200 evaluations.
Experiments: reports DINO-F1 gains over matched Wan+4RC cascades and component ablations on 7-Scenes/NRGBD.

arxiv:2608.10720.rationale: Moderately relevant multimodal LLM dialogue/speech/video paper with structured LLM-generated visual planning and streaming distillation. It has strong ablations and explicit limitations, but is specialized generative avatar/video work, not core LLM research, and has no Japanese relevance.
evidence: Section 3.2, Page 4: Qwen3-8B emits a structured Visual Thought Plan with five fields before the user-facing response.
Section 4.7, Page 10: Prefix Streaming reduces late-chunk subject error slope from 0.00783 to 0.00599 and last-minus-first consistency error by 21.4% over 200 paired videos.
Section 4.8, Page 11 Table 5: Replacing the response-specific VTP with a fixed neutral plan changes SC, Sync-C, and DD, showing sensitivity but not a uniform visual-quality advantage.

Section 5, Pages 11-12: Limitations include weak reference-speaker similarity, VTP not being independently sufficient, speech-QA/reasoning trade-off, expensive Teacher, and lower Student IQ/DD/Sync-C.

arxiv:2608.10708.rationale: Pure computer vision / 3D geometry foundation model work with no language-model methodology; out of scope and capped at 0.20. It has experimental ablations and multiple datasets, but topical relevance is minimal.
evidence: Abstract: proposes a plug-and-play test-time adaptation pipeline for geometrically consistent 3D Vision Foundation Models.
Section IV-A: evaluates VGGT, pi^3, and DA3 variants on 7Scenes, ETH3D, ScanNet++, and HiRoom.
Section V: contains ablation studies for GDO, correspondence filtering, and FAN; Section S.VI states limitations.

arxiv:2608.10692.rationale: Highly relevant LLM agent/tool-use/retrieval evaluation benchmark with moderate novelty as a synthetic mobile personal-information benchmark; moderately rigorous human curation and controlled evaluation, though claims rely on self-reported results with some table/figure inconsistencies and no explicit limitations.
evidence: Section 3.3 describes human curation, cross-validation, and gold-answer verification for 250 tasks over 4,335 records and 10 apps.
Section 5 reports best model GPT-5.5 (xhigh) at 57.3% and weakest at 16.4% across nine LLMs.
Section 6 analyzes failure modes and retrieval behavior, including 79% failures from incorrect parameter values and <2% advanced retrieval use.

arxiv:2608.10636.rationale: Moderately relevant via multimodal retrieval/RAG, dense retrieval, distillation/efficiency, and VLM teacher, but not core LLM reasoning, Japanese NLP, safety, or agents. Method is incremental bilateral distillation with an asymmetric design rather than conceptually novel. Empirical rigor is decent with 12 reproduced baselines, ablations, and efficiency profiling, but no significance testing and no from-scratch contrastive control. Quantitative evidence is strong within the paper but single-team and unverified. Generalizability is limited to Latin-script languages and ViDoRe-style corpora. Reproducibility is supported by detailed data, hyperparameters, and code availability claims.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports full 22-dataset ViDoRe v1+v2+v3 evaluation and training data details.
Table 1 reports NDCG@5: DistilVDR-HiRes 61.74 and Fast 59.98 average versus baselines.
Table 3 reports deployment efficiency including 3.4 ms query latency, 99.04 docs/sec Fast throughput, and 16.4 GB/1M index footprint.
Table 4 reports ablations on tile budget, data scale, output dimension, and query backbone.
Limitations notes absence of from-scratch contrastive control, single teacher sweep, and non-Latin script query support.

arxiv:2608.10628.rationale: Highly relevant to agentic tool use, multimodal LLM reasoning, and chain-of-thought. Strong empirical evaluation with SFT vs SFT+RL ablations, trajectory-quality metrics, and efficiency analyses; however, novelty is incremental over existing coarse-to-fine visual search, and some cross-paper comparisons are not fully controlled.
evidence: Abstract: proposes InSight-doc, an agentic visual perception framework with region-level zoom-in trajectories and SFT+RL; claims 4.3-16.4 accuracy improvement and 41%-68% latency reduction.
Section 5.2 Table 2: InSight-doc-8B (SFT+RL) at r=0.25 achieves 66.9% average accuracy vs Qwen3-VL-8B 50.5%, a 16.4-point gain.
Section 5.3: reports 54% latency reduction at 70 DPI and 69% token reduction on longest-document examples.
Section 5.4 Table 4: not-answerable F1 on DUDE/MMLongBench-Doc is 69.1/74.4 vs Qwen3-VL-8B 44.5/48.5.
Section 6 Limitations: only evaluated SFT+RL on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and did not experiment with advanced RL or reward design.
Abstract availability claim: code, datasets, and model released at https://github.com/m-Just/InSight-doc.

arxiv:2608.10615.rationale: The paper is relevant as a language-modeling/categorical-generation method with transformer backbones and OpenWebText text generation, but it is not central to LLM, reasoning, agents, or other higher-weight preference areas. Novelty is moderate: an exact Dirichlet-categorical augmentation and Rao-Blackwellized objective are clearly derived, but the contribution is specialized and builds on existing discrete-diffusion and simplex-diffusion work. Rigor is moderate: detailed proofs and baseline comparisons are provided, but no statistical uncertainty or multi-seed robustness is shown. Evidence strength is moderate: quantitative tables support the main claims, though conclusions rely on selected checkpoints and one text benchmark plus Sudoku. Generalizability is limited to uniform discrete diffusion, and reproducibility is reasonable due to detailed hyperparameters but no code availability is documented.
evidence: Section 3.2, Proposition 2: the relaxed discrete bridge objective admits an exact closed form (Equation 15).
Section 4.3, Table 1: Simplax reports the lowest Gen. PPL under all three evaluators at NFE=16 and NFE=1,024, and under GPT-2 Large/XL at NFE=128.
Section 4.4, Table 2: Simplax achieves the highest conditional Sudoku accuracy across 40, 35, 30, 25, 20, and 17 clues, and the highest unconditional validity (95.85%).
Section 6, Limitations: the formulation is specialized to uniform categorical corruption, and overhead and concentration schedule remain open issues.

arxiv:2608.10366.rationale: Highly relevant to agent/tool-use, computer-control, coding, and multimodal LLM evaluation; not an LLM methodology paper but squarely in agentic benchmarking. Moderately novel as a real-OS end-to-end data-science agent benchmark, though it builds directly on OSWorld and prior sandboxed DS benchmarks. Rigor is reasonable: deterministic evaluators, dual-annotator verification, multiple models, ablations, and error analysis, but human baseline is small and open-source models lack A11y evaluation. Evidence is well-tabulated but self-reported. Reproducibility claims include code/config release and fixed parameters.
evidence: Abstract: Claims 275 tasks, evaluation of 15 closed/open models, Claude-4.6-Sonnet 56.70%, open-source below 1%.
Section 3.2.3 Dual Annotator Verification: Reports 86% initial agreement and all 275 tasks ultimately receiving mutual approval.
Section 5.3 Main Results, Table 3: Screenshot+A11y overall accuracy is 56.70% for Claude-4.6-Sonnet, 29.81% for GPT-5, and 85.09% for human performance.
Section 5.4 Ablation Studies, Table 11: Increasing step budget from 15 to 50 yields only 24.54% to 25.81% success and average score 0.55 to 0.57.
Section 6 Error Analysis, Table 10: GUI-OWL-7B and UI-Tars grounding failures are 97.09% and 98.18%; Claude-4.6-Sonnet shows 32.77% grounding, 43.70% code, and 14.29% logic failures.

arxiv:2608.10327.rationale: Highly relevant critical meta-review of LLM value alignment, RLHF, and AI safety, but qualitative rather than technical; moderate novelty and evidence, limited reproducibility due to undisclosed full corpus/annotation data.
evidence: Abstract: The authors state they annotated 94 AI value alignment research papers to discern their implicit theory of values in AI.
Methods: Snowball sampling from four seed papers produced an initial corpus of 576 papers, reduced to 94 after excluding papers using 'value alignment' only in a cursory sense.
Findings: Reports 79% of papers neither defined nor described 'values', 90% treat values as measurable, and 82% treat preferences as a stand-in for values.
Table 1: Inter-rater reliability is documented with low-to-moderate kappas, e.g., 0.028-0.541, indicating subjective annotation.
Limitations: Acknowledges small sample size, lack of completeness, and limitations of the scoring rubric.

arxiv:2608.10326.rationale: The paper addresses computational fair division/envy elimination and has no overlap with the stated AI/ML preferences (LLMs, NLP, transformers, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, code, safety, alignment, multimodal AI, etc.). Though the proofs appear formally developed within its own domain, the work is outside scope and receives a near-zero relevance assessment with limited transferability to the requested topics.

arxiv:2608.10323.rationale: Non-language artificial-life/neuroevolution paper with only tangential overlap to RL, training optimization, and evaluation preferences. It presents a transparent nested evaluation protocol but relies on descriptive n=3 analysis, has confounded contexts and floor effects, and offers limited generalizability to LLM/NLP topics. Code/data/model availability supports reproducibility but does not overcome weak topical fit.
evidence: Section 4.2 Training Results: reports RL-enabled regimes reached 335K and 299K fitness vs 150K for EvoEvo in MLP4.

Section 4.3 Formal Frozen Competition Results: reports only 4 of 15 condition pairs retained the same effect direction across aligned run blocks and pairwise majority directions changed with architecture.
Section 5.5 Limitations: states n = 3 independent runs, 198 computational jobs are not independent replicates, contexts are confounded, and there is no full cross-run artifact pairing.

arxiv:2608.10320.rationale: Human visualization/cognitive psychology study of divided attention and colormap interpretation; no LLM, NLP, transformer, agent, multimodal AI, or other in-scope methodology. Though the paper has preregistered human experiments, mixed-effects models, and LBA modeling, it is out of scope and capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: reports two human experiments on colormap interpretation under single-task vs dual-task conditions.
Section 2.1: methods include Prolific participants, a colormap task, and a phone-message dual task.
Section 4.3: LBA parameter interpretation of divided attention and expectation violation.
Section 5: limitations note only two kinds of biases and one class of visualization task.

arxiv:2608.10319.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM-powered coding agents and agent skills, with a reasonable two-stage personalization framework and simulation-based replay evaluation. However, conclusions rest on a small filtered SWE-chat subset of 206 sessions from 13 developers, improvements are mostly non-significant, and evaluation uses an LLM simulator rather than real users, limiting rigor and generalizability.
evidence: Section 3.1: after filtering, the dataset contains only 206 sessions from 13 developers, yielding 164 evolution and 42 test sessions.
Section 3.3 Table 1: no-skill score 65.02 vs personalized 65.99 vs generic 68.80; generic improvement p=.063, personalized p=.399.
Section 4.1 Table 2: personalized skill beats no-skill by +10.17 only for tasks with at least 6 relevant evolution sessions.
Section 4.2: simulator follow-ups were 59.65% exact matches and 89.47% at least partially semantically consistent with real developer messages.
Section 4.4 Table 4: generic skill contains more rules than personalized skills (25 vs 14.15 average), and 64.7% of personalized rules are lexically developer-unique.

arxiv:2608.10318.rationale: Pure audio/speech privacy metric paper with no LLM/NLP or language methodology; out-of-scope and capped at 0.20. It gives a careful conceptual discussion of perfect secrecy, LLR, EER, and rank-based metrics, but is an in-progress study with limited empirical evidence (seven VPC 2024 systems, no ground-truth LLR) and domain-specific scope.
evidence: §4.3 demonstrates that EER=50% does not imply perfect secrecy using simulated data.
§7 Table 3 reports EER and epsilon_max for VPC 2024 systems.
§1 provides a Jupyter notebook DOI for reproducing results.

arxiv:2608.10317.rationale: Relevant multimodal video-language benchmark with chain-of-thought reasoning and fine-tuning, but domain-specific traffic surveillance limits scope. Novelty is incremental over prior video anomaly language datasets; methods and ablations are clear but auto-generated training labels lack controlled audit and the test set is small and source-correlated.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 3: zero-shot evaluation of eleven VLMs; best model Cosmos3-Super 48.8% mean, no model without TAR exposure exceeds 40%.
Section 4.3, Table 4: multi-task fine-tuning ablation on Cosmos-Reason2-8B improves aggregate mean from 34.3 to 55.7 (+21.4).
Section 3.5: TAR-Bench has 960 human-curated items; reviewers corrected 170 questions (17.7%) and 356 answers (37.1%).
Section 6: limitations include 80 clips from 17 YouTube videos, source-level correlation risk, and auto-generated training labels as residual-noise supervision.

arxiv:2608.10316.rationale: Medical-imaging domain application using a VLM with LoRA and modality-alignment losses. Multimodal/VLM elements are present, but the task is medical diagnosis and is out of scope per curation policy, so relevance is capped low. The method assembles established components (unimodal supervision, MSE alignment, supervised contrastive learning, GradNorm), with limited novelty and evidence only on two single-institution medical datasets. Quantitative claims are supported in tables, but main results lack variance, some table/caption references are inconsistent, and no code/release is stated.
evidence: Table 1 reports UniMod AUC 0.850 on Harvard-Glaucoma and 0.966 on CheXpert Plus, compared in Section 5.2 against baselines.

Section 5.4 and Tables 3-4 provide ablations and missing-modality comparisons, but main results in Table 1 lack seed-level variance and Section 5.4 refers to Table 4 for ablations while its caption concerns robustness.
Section 4.5 and Section 5.1 describe LoRA and training settings but do not state code/model release, limiting reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.10315.rationale: Core LLM evaluation paper with strong topic relevance to LLMs, prompting, and evaluation. The C3 idea is a moderate extension of semantic-uncertainty/agreement work, with broad empirical coverage but limited statistical rigor, minimal limitations, and no code release.
evidence: Table 1 reports C3 vs self-consistency, paraphrasing, and self-report across six benchmarks averaged over 16 models, with C3 best on most ECE/AUROC/AUPRC entries.
Appendix F ablates perturbation source on SimpleQA, showing C3 remains competitive with Qwen3-8B and web-sourced noise.
Appendix G ablates MMD by replacing it with a simpler cross-comparison distance, preserving most of the C3 signal.
Section 5.3 and Figure 4 describe the benchmark diagnosis framework, partitioning instances into mastered, brittle, biased, and unlearned regions.

arxiv:2608.10314.rationale: In-scope LLM prompt/renderer-format study with strong preregistered exact randomization methodology. Relevance is moderate-to-high via LLM/prompting/evaluation and theory-to-program translation, but lacks Japanese NLP, reasoning, agents, or multimodal focus. Novelty is moderate; the contribution is mainly a rigorous null result around a narrow prompt-format contrast. Rigor and evidence are high for the registered not_supported verdict, though effective N is only 16 and one endpoint disagrees across pipelines. Generalizability is explicitly limited to fixed snapshots, cards, and language. Reproducibility is excellent with datasets, code, digests, and attestation.
evidence: Abstract: reports a prospective randomized experiment on renderer format in LLM theory-to-program translation with 320 preauthorized API requests.
Section 2.1: describes 16 blocks, 32 anonymous renderer slots, NIST Randomness Beacon assignment, and exact enumeration of 65,536 renderer-label assignments under Fisher sharp null.

Section 4.4 and Table 7: primary endpoints show H1 not supported; H2 linear matched-distance reduction p=0.0012512207 but rank pipeline p=0.0284729 and misses magnitude floor; identifiability chance-level.
Section 5.3: limitations state two model snapshots, effective N=16, no extrapolation beyond fixed renderers/models/probes.
Data and code availability and Appendix D: SPECFORM-H1/H2 datasets, reproduction software, digests, and schema released.

arxiv:2608.10312.rationale: Particle physics flavor-mixing paper on CKM/PMNS parameterizations; no overlap with the listed AI/LLM/NLP/agents/safety preferences. Out of scope, so preference_relevance is 0 and overall score is capped below 0.20. The paper has internal quantitative structure but is not relevant to this curation task.
evidence: Title and Abstract: concerns quark and lepton mixing, unitarity triangles, CKM/PMNS parameters, not AI/LLM/NLP methodology.

arxiv:2608.10309.rationale: Out-of-scope pure robotics/aerodynamics application with a U-Net flow surrogate and no language methodology. Some experimental validation exists, but only two geometries and three trials per path, with post-hoc metric tuning in Scenario 2 and no statistical testing. Data availability is only on request.
evidence: Section 2.3.1 reports a U-Net with 9.9e7 parameters trained on 3072 Lattice-Boltzmann time-averaged flow fields and a final test error of 8.71% on 64 held-out samples.
Section 3.1.1 reports mean displacements of 7.7 cm CFD-informed, 7.4 cm surrogate-informed, and 18.8 cm flow-naive across three trials.

Section 3.1.2 reports Scenario 2 mean displacement of 6.7 cm for surrogate-informed versus 5.4 cm CFD-informed and 5.5 cm naive, noting surrogate over-smoothing required flight-challenge metric tuning; Section 5 states data and flight logs are available upon request.

arxiv:2608.10305.rationale: Out-of-scope statistical causal-inference and dimension-reduction paper with no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology. It proposes COMPACT spectral adjustment scores with theoretical results and simulations on ABCD/CATIE-style health data, but the topic does not align with the requested AI/LLM preferences, so relevance and overall score are capped low.
evidence: Section 1 introduces COMPACT as a causal adjustment and spectral dimension-reduction method.
Section 7.3 reports synthetic simulations comparing COMPACT with propensity-score and dimension-reduction baselines.
Section S8 describes the simulation setup and bootstrap inference design.

arxiv:2608.10304.rationale: Out-of-scope optical meta-optics/computer-vision inference paper using MNIST classification. It does not address LLMs, Japanese NLP, transformer architecture, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, code, or language methodology, so the score is capped at ≤0.20. The work is internally formal with baselines and ablations, but its claims are domain-specific and code/data are only available by request.
evidence: Methods III.1: uses MNIST and an MLP backend, not LLM/NLP methods.
Methods III.9–III.10: code and model/data availability are only on reasonable request.
Section I.4.3: conclusions concern optical inference versus imaging/communication, not language-model methodology.

fallback:b8f02050bde5819d.rationale: Abstract-only locked business article about AI agent governance; no methods, results, baselines, limitations, or reproducibility. Only weak topical overlap with agents/workflow preferences and no language methodology.

arxiv:2608.10300.rationale: This is a healthcare EHR interoperability architecture that uses an LLM logit boundary but contributes no language-model methodology; as a domain application it is largely out of scope and is capped low. The evidence is mostly a negative frozen benchmark with zero accepted outputs and toy numerical certificates, with no baselines, ablations, or clinical validation. Code and benchmark artifacts are available, but held-out references are withheld.
evidence: Section 11 reports 768 completed executions with 369 safe_parse_reject and 399 safe_schema_reject, yielding zero accepted outputs and coverage 0.
Section 7.3 and Appendix A explicitly state the stalk-energy table is a projector-based toy surrogate and not a validated mapping-cone diagnostic.
Section 12.2-12.3 frame the contribution as hallucination containment/admission control, not hallucination elimination; Section 12.4-12.5 are synthetic illustrative examples.

arxiv:2608.10297.rationale: Out-of-scope recommender-systems/graph-CF paper with little match to LLM/NLP preferences; only low-weight GNN relevance. Method has modest novelty via node-specific depth from a degree-imbalance curvature proxy, but evidence is limited: small absolute gains, no significance tests or standard deviations, no explicit limitations, and theory depends on standard over-smoothing contraction assumptions. Overall low priority under the stated rubric.
evidence: Abstract: claims code is available at GitHub and proposes curvature-aware node-specific propagation depth.
Table 1: reports R@K/N@K results; NTCF improvements over LightGCN are small, e.g., Kindle R@10 0.1600 vs 0.1570.
Table 1 ablation: the 'w/o curvature' row exactly matches NGCF row across all metrics.
Table 2: reports backbone replacement results for SimGCL, LightGCL, RecDCL, and NLGCL.
Section 4.2: states results are averaged over 5 runs but no standard deviations or significance tests are reported.
Section 4.5: ablation covers curvature removal and mean aggregation only, not all mask/depth components.
Proposition 2: proof assumes a rho-Lipschitz contraction on the energy-relevant subspace, which is not empirically validated.

arxiv:2608.10296.rationale: In-scope LLM, transformer, and long-context study with controlled multi-model ablations. Novelty is moderate because prior work identified QK-norm effects, but the controlled compound-ablation design and OlmPool release are substantial. Rigor is good but limited by one seed per configuration and incomplete initialization/hyperparameter standardization. Quantitative evidence is strong across tables and ablations, though without statistical error bars. Generalizability is constrained to dense 7-8B English LLMs with one data mix. Reproducibility is supported by released checkpoints and configurations but high compute cost limits verification.
evidence: Abstract reports that combining three or more architectural choices can drop downstream performance by up to 47% and describes the released OlmPool set of 26 comparable 7B models.
Section 4 reports that the feature count of four architectural choices is the most predictive single feature for downstream long-context performance with in-sample R2=0.67 and LOO R2=0.61.
Appendix A Table 1 reports HELMET 32K scores ranging from 29.9 to 56.4 across OlmPool models, supporting the claimed wide downstream variation.
Section 5.3 compares YaRN 2-stage and NTK 1-stage extension strategies on three models and reports that architecture ranking is preserved across methods.

arxiv:2608.10295.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/brain-MRI foundation-model audit; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, agents, or language-methodology component. Some within-domain controls exist, but the explicit out-of-scope cap limits the score.
evidence: Abstract: study audits frozen brain-MRI foundation-model embeddings for acquisition-site decodability.
Section 3.1: uses T1-weighted MRI from ABIDE-I/ABIDE-II; no text/language task.
Section 4.2: reports random-initialized encoders are ~0.9 site classifiers, indicating low-level image statistics.
Section 5.4: limitations are brain-MRI-specific cohorts and SynthSeg labels.
Data and Code Availability: releases audit code for the MRI site-fingerprint analysis.

arxiv:2608.10291.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/generative-modeling work with no LLM/language methodology, so capped at 0.20 despite moderate experimental breadth and usable quantitative tables. Some claims are unsupported in text (unresolved TOST p-value placeholder; listed ablations not shown).
evidence: Abstract: claims statistically equivalent 20:1 JPEG2000 synthesis vs uncompressed, but TOST p-value appears as unresolved placeholder '[[p]]'.
Table 1: reports 40.37 GB BraTS training set reduced to 3.13 GB at 20:1 JPEG2000, a 12.9x reduction.
Table 3: lists per-modality PSNR/SSIM across JPEG2000 ratios, with marked degradation mainly at 200:1 and 400:1.
Table 5: downstream segmentation reports WT Dice 0.814 for JPEG2000 2:1 but low TC Dice 0.238, indicating fragile fine substructure preservation.
Contribution list: claims ablations on sampling steps and informed prior, but the main text/tables do not report these ablation results.

arxiv:2608.10290.rationale: Moderately relevant LLM/code-comprehension tool paper with deterministic graph-grounded prompt construction, but evaluation is narrow: one small Java project, token-cost comparisons only, coarse accuracy rubric, no human study, and no comparison to retrieval/compression baselines.
evidence: Section V, Table III reports prompt-token counts across modes and states counts are identical across LLM families; Section VI caveats token estimation as character-count/4.
Section VI lists single benchmark project, keyword-match accuracy saturating to 2/2, no human-comprehension claim, and no embedding-retrieval baseline as limitations.
Section IV specifies deterministic GACP phases and complexity; Section V and Table IV report algorithm-only reshapes on collapse fixtures.

arxiv:2608.10289.rationale: Primarily a computer vision DNN robustness-testing framework; it uses vision-language models and diffusion as tools but is not a language-model/LLM research contribution, so preference relevance is low. The evaluation reports quantitative metrics but lacks baselines and uses a limited convenience sample of feature trees, weakening rigor and generalizability.
evidence: Section 5.2.1 reports average precondition satisfaction of 93.4% across datasets.
Section 5.2.2 reports an average of 16.3% of tests revealing feature non-robustness.
Section 5.1.2 states the feature trees are a 'limited convenience sample' selected to facilitate the evaluation.
Section 5.1.3 describes the models under test as ResNet34, YOLOv8, and DeepLabV3.
Section 4.4 names Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, and all-mpnet-base-v2 as components.

arxiv:2608.10286.rationale: Out-of-scope for the stated preferences: a pure computer-vision/3DGS sparse-view reconstruction paper using video diffusion without language/NLP/LLM/agent/safety/reasoning methodology. It has ablations and benchmark results, but topical relevance is minimal, so the score is capped at or below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: describes on-policy trajectory distillation for sparse-view 3DGS restoration with privileged geometry.
Section 4 Experiments: reports PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS on DL3DV, Mip-NeRF 360, and NeRFBusters.
Table 3: ablation of privileged geometry and on-policy supervision.

arxiv:2608.10281.rationale: Strongly relevant to AI safety, tool-calling agents, prompt injection, and red teaming. The LLM-to-web-vulnerability taxonomy is useful but largely derivative of prior prompt-to-SQL, AgentDojo, InjecAgent, and related work; several variants are constructed scenarios without experimental validation. The empirical case study is limited to one Flask testbed, seven models, and ten sequential trials per condition, with success counts but no uncertainty estimates, statistical testing, or detailed prompt/system-prompt disclosure. Reproducibility is modestly supported by the open-source testbed and model list, but small samples and partial prompt/configuration details limit strength.
evidence: Section 4.1 describes the TicketOracle testbed and fetch_event_data tool.
Section 4.3 reports seven evaluated LLMs and ten sequential trials per scenario.
Section 4.4 and Table 2 report success rates by model and attack scenario.
Section 5 presents layered defenses including prompt, model, application, and network mitigations.

arxiv:2608.10280.rationale: Out-of-scope astronomy domain application of tabular foundation models (TabPFN 2.5, RealTabPFN 2.5, TabICL) to quasar photometric redshift estimation. It contains transformer/foundation-model elements but no language methodology. Although the benchmark has controlled comparisons, standard errors, and ablations, the contribution is domain-specific and capped at <=0.20 under the rubric.
evidence: Table 2 reports density metrics with standard errors; Section V discusses limitations and S-PLUS-specific conclusions.

arxiv:2608.10279.rationale: Topically relevant LLM streaming safety/guardrails paper, but contribution is narrow and largely a straightforward deterministic two-predicate withholding rule. Evaluations provide clear conformance evidence for very few synthetic rule families, while external safe/unsafe subsets have limited size and mixed label provenance; exact detector strings and policy code are withheld.
evidence: Section 6.2: all 32 pair trials were detected, labels matched the buffered scanner, completing chunks were withheld, and all 8 single-predicate controls passed.
Section 6.6: fixed scanner detected 0/394 AEGIS2.0 jury-labelled unsafe responses, limiting broad recall claims.
Section 15: exact detector strings, corpus material, and executable policy code are omitted, and sanitized artifact release is pending review.

arxiv:2608.10278.rationale: Relevant to multimodal VLM reasoning, CoT, and LoRA/GRPO training, but centered on spatial/3D vision rather than core LLM/NLP. The paper provides benchmark comparisons and ablations but lacks significance testing, the RL reward is VSI-specific, and the architecture-agnostic claim is only demonstrated on Qwen3-VL-8B backbones.
evidence: Abstract: reports 4.3% improvement for Qwen3-VL-8B and 1.3% for SenseNova-SI-1.3 on VSI-Bench, plus 79.2% object size and 75.7% room size.
Experiments Table 1: reports full VSI-Bench comparisons across proprietary, open-source, architecture-customized, and training-only baselines.
Ablations Table 3: VICA-322K data-only fine-tuning decreases to 67.1 while Space Tokens stages reach 68.6/68.9, attributing gains to tokens rather than data scaling.
Appendix C.2: attention masking on spatial tokens reduces VSI-Bench performance, with a 15.3-point drop on object size.
Implementation Details and Appendix A.3: LoRA rank 16, GRPO training, and VSI-Bench-specific reward design are described.

arxiv:2608.10277.rationale: Out-of-scope climate-model emulation paper with no LLM/NLP/transformer/agent/language methodology; closest rubric category is weak Scientific AI. It has domain-specific baseline comparisons, quantitative spectral evaluations, and data/code release, but topic mismatch and pure domain application cap the score.
evidence: Abstract: presents a stochastic coupled emulator of E3SM version 3 built on SamudrACE/ACE2 and evaluated on 400 independent years.
Section 2.2.4: describes coupled fine-tuning with a CRPS/energy score probabilistic objective and a deterministic baseline.
Section 3.3: reports Niño 3.4 power spectra comparing deterministic and stochastic emulators against E3SMv3.
Open Research Section: states training data, code, and checkpoints are available via Globus, Zenodo, and Hugging Face.

arxiv:2608.10276.rationale: Relevant LLM fine-tuning/NLP study using LoRA for codebook-guided text coding, but domain-specific and methodologically modest: single small test set (n=347), rare classes (e.g., family D n=6), no confidence intervals in main text, and limited novelty beyond applying known LoRA fine-tuning to educational metaphor coding. Quantitative results support improved open-weight performance, but broad claims of outperforming proprietary models are fragile.
evidence: Abstract: reports fine-tuning substantially improved open-weight models and made them competitive with or outperform proprietary prompt-only models.
§3 Methods: human-coded corpus of 2,265 responses split into train/validation/test; LoRA fine-tuning hyperparameters and temperature 0 are specified.
§4 Results: fine-tuned DeepSeek-R1 1.5B valence accuracy improved from 0.369 to 0.787 on food subset; Mistral 7B improved from 0.207 to 0.778.
Table 4: rare thematic family D n=6; fine-tuned DeepSeek-R1 1.5B grouped exact-code F1 remains 0.000.
§5 Limitations: only temperature 0 evaluated; corpus limited to Grades 6-8 food/animal metaphors; rare thematic families remain less stable.

arxiv:2608.10273.rationale: Moderate relevance: an LLM fine-tuning benchmark for clinical NLP, touching LLMs, training/optimization, prompting, and evaluation, but domain-specific and incremental. Novelty is limited by closely following a prior ED decision-support benchmark and standard PEFT methods. Rigor has clear splits, seeds, baselines, and hyperparameters, but lacks statistical significance testing and uses synthetic/LLM-judged reference labels. Evidence supports descriptive comparisons, but some outperformance claims rely on observed means and small ESI-1 subgroup counts. Generalizability is limited to MIMIC-IV-ED and ED task formulations. Reproducibility is moderate: methods and hyperparameters are described, but no code or processed data release is reported.
evidence: Abstract: benchmarked eight open-source SLMs using zero-shot prompting, prefix tuning, LoRA, and full fine-tuning on three ED tasks.
Methods, Pages 2-5: used 2,083 MIMIC-IV-ED cases, 60/20/20 train/validation/test split, five random seeds, and specified LoRA/prefix/full fine-tuning hyperparameters.
Results, Pages 5-6: Qwen3-4B-Instruct with LoRA exact-match triage accuracy 65.98% vs Claude Sonnet 4.5 62.68%; Mistral-7B-Instruct LoRA referral matched accuracy 75.24%.
Discussion, Page 9: notes imbalanced ESI distribution, Claude-generated referral labels, Llama-3.1-70B judge for diagnosis, single clinical database, and no external/prospective validation.

arxiv:2608.10271.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/domain generalization paper; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agentic relevance despite using Swin Transformer. Internal 5-fold benchmarks and external dataset evaluation provide some evidence, but the paper lacks formal ablations, significance testing, and a limitations section.
evidence: Section 5.2 Table 1 reports internal 5-fold CV metrics for multiple backbones
Section 5.2 Figure 4 reports external TNMammo/LUMINA evaluation
Section 3 describes dataset sizes and annotations
Section 4.1 describes foreground-only histogram matching

arxiv:2608.10268.rationale: Directly on-topic for LLM evaluation, legal reasoning, and AI safety, but evidence is preliminary and validation is weak: small expert-annotated pilot, no reported inter-item consistency, and low calibration agreement. Novel in targeting international human rights law, but scope is limited to right-to-water scenarios and the Rule Application task is acknowledged as only slightly extending Rule Recall.
evidence: Section 3.2 and Table 3 report expert ratings for scenarios 1-5 and 9, with no ratings for scenarios 6-8 and no IIC computed.
Section 4.1 reports remedy-scoring calibration with inter-annotator agreement kappa=0.02 and LOOCV kappa=0.12.
Table 4 reports overall accuracy range 0.339-0.577 across models.
Section 5 states pilot scenarios are limited primarily to the right to water and acknowledges the current Rule Application task only slightly moves analysis from Rule Recall to Rule Application.

arxiv:2608.10265.rationale: Out of scope: smart-contract/blockchain symbolic-execution tooling for false-positive reduction; only incidental mention of ChatGPT/LLMs in related work. No LLM/NLP/agent/safety methodology. Evaluation is an internal before/after study on 140 Gigahorse contracts with limited rigor and no validated portability.
evidence: {'section': 'Abstract', 'detail': 'Focuses on false positives in Mythril for Ethereum smart contracts.'}
{'section': 'Table III', 'detail': 'Reports vanilla vs improved Mythril precision, FDR, recall, and F1 on Gigahorse benchmarks.'}

arxiv:2608.10262.rationale: Topically relevant LLM multi-agent cooperation study. The fixed-converter design removes a plausible coding-ability confound and the pre-registered H6 lab-divergence result is supported by Holm-Bonferroni tests and a converter robustness check. However, H5 is qualified and converter-sensitive, the Western comparison is only a literature contrast, and generalizability is limited to four Chinese labs in one IPD setup.
evidence: Section 3.1 describes the fixed-converter design; Section 3.7 states pre-registered H5 and H6.
Section 4.4 Table 6 reports four of six pairwise P_A comparisons survive Holm-Bonferroni; Section 4.7 reports converter robustness.
Section 5.4 lists limitations including literature contrast, converter sensitivity, English-only prompting, and four labs.

arxiv:2608.10260.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM/Transformer interpretability, safety, and scaling; combines low-rank lenses with Subset-KL, moderately novel as an integration of existing techniques. Rigor supported by ablations, Theorem 1, seed studies, and limitations; evidence strong with quantitative tables across GPT-2, LLaMA-8B/70B/405B case studies. Generalizability moderate across model scales but limited architectures.
evidence: Abstract: describes OmniLens and claims 482 lenses for LLaMA-3.3-70B, 90.5% fewer parameters, up to 70% lower peak memory on GPT-2.
Section 3 and Table 1: rank ablation on GPT-2 Small reports r=64 uses 16.7% parameters with final-layer top-1 agreement 0.888.
Section 4.2 and Theorem 1: Top-k+IS estimator is unbiased for full KL and yields unbiased gradients; proof in Appendix E.
Section 5: case studies report prompt-injection AUROC 0.997, causal memory-injection lift 6.6x at 8B, and toxicity localization where detection and intervention rankings differ.
Appendix B: reports models, Pile training data, AdamW hyperparameters, distributed configurations, and code links.

arxiv:2608.10258.rationale: Highly relevant LLM safety and evaluation study; moderate novelty. Strong internal rigor with physician validation, bootstrap confidence intervals, and detailed protocol, but synthetic fixed-turn medical scope and weak Leaky-class reliability limit generality.
evidence: Section 3.1 Benchmark Development: 500 physician-reviewed synthetic scenarios with fixed allocation.
Section 3.3 Response Evaluation and Physician Validation: GPT-4o judge and 400-conversation physician-adjudicated subset.
Section 4.1 Primary Results: 71.6% any-turn Unsafe and 61.4% collapse after Safe U1.
Section 4.2 Physician Validation of the Automated Judge: 94.3% exact agreement, kappa=0.895.
Section 7 Limitations acknowledges synthetic fixed three-turn design and automated labels.

arxiv:2608.10257.rationale: LLM-centric recommendation paper with direct relevance to LLM post-training, reward-weighted alignment, long-context verbalization, and serving efficiency. However, it is a domain-specific industrial application rather than core LLM/NLP methodology, and the report is high-level with sparse statistical detail, unnamed metrics, no code/data/model release, and limited reproducible ablations.
evidence: §5.1 reports GenRec trained with ~40x fewer Phase-2 labeled examples achieved ~+1.6% relative offline MRR and statistically significant online gains.
§5.2 reports monotonic MRR improvements with increased Phase-2 training data and larger backbone sizes.
§5.3 Table 1 reports Phase 1 contributes +10-20% and Phase 2 +35-50% offline MRR.
§5.4 reports context length reduced to roughly one third, from about 5000 tokens to about 1700 tokens, with negligible offline metric loss.
§4.5 describes a decoder-only Transformer with catalog-aware scoring head using pooled representation and softmax over the catalog.
§4.6 describes reward-weighted ranking loss using multiple reward models instead of full reinforcement learning.
§4.7 describes vLLM serving in prefill-only mode and cost optimization via smaller/distilled models and verbalization compaction.

arxiv:2608.10256.rationale: Pure maritime trajectory prediction domain application with only minimal Transformer/attention preference relevance. Methods are incremental (online K-means sampling plus CNN-Transformer) and evaluation is limited to few baselines without significance testing or full ablations; geographic and vessel-type scope is narrow. Capped at 0.20 as an out-of-scope domain application.
evidence: Abstract: proposes CRHT with online K-means cluster sampling and hybrid CNN-Transformer; reports lowest errors at 1-hour horizon.
IV-A Table I: CRHT 1-hour ADE 1.21 km, FDE 2.07 km; 2-hour ADE 2.55 km, FDE 5.85 km vs TrAISformer FDE 5.42 km.

arxiv:2608.10251.rationale: Highly relevant to transformer interpretability, attention mechanisms, and language model representation geometry. The paper offers mechanistic measurements of off-axis residual computation and interventions, with matched controls and quantitative results. However, evidence is limited to one GPT-2-class scale, one corpus, and small seed counts; generalizability is explicitly limited, and reproducibility is moderately supported by detailed setup but no code/availability claims.
evidence: Section 3.1 reports rotating attention values toward the read-out is 64x more damaging than matched random rotation at 10 degrees and 84x at 20 degrees, with asymmetry collapsing to about 1x when cross-token averaging is removed.
Section 3.2 reports orthogonal Procrustes across the commit span yields R^2_rot=0.38, 64% new content, and residual norm growth of 1.74x.
Section 6.2 and Table 4 report dense-device convergence of 7/8 seeds versus 2/8 for the frameless step, with LAMBADA 0.257 and perplexity 19.3.
Section 9.4 explicitly limits the work to a single architecture family, one scale, one corpus, and small seed counts.

arxiv:2608.10249.rationale: Domain-specific maritime trajectory clustering/anomaly detection using a BERT-style transformer on AIS data. This is not LLM/NLP/language methodology and falls under pure domain application, so relevance is capped. The paper reports some quantitative results but lacks strong baseline comparisons, ablations, and verifiable code release.
evidence: Abstract: presents a custom BERT-based model trained via masked token modeling and clustered using CURE, demonstrated on AIS data.
III-A Sequence encoding: reduced Transformer with four encoder layers, four attention heads, hidden size 256, 15% masking.
IV Experiments and results: validation MSE ~0.0044 after 17 epochs; WARD linkage adopted; k=3 and k=5 analyzed.

arxiv:2608.10248.rationale: Relevant to AI safety/fairness via bias and fairness debt, but not focused on LLMs, Japanese NLP, or other high-weight preference areas. Qualitative software engineering case study with conceptual novelty (bias smells), moderate rigor using interviews, observations, and document triangulation, but single organization, convenience sampling, no quantitative validation, and explicitly limited generalizability. Evidence is mostly participant quotes and field notes; artifacts are only partially available.

arxiv:2608.10247.rationale: Recommender-systems/collaborative filtering paper with no language-modeling, NLP, or agent methodology; only weak graph/GNN relevance. The sign-aware spectral extension is incremental within its domain, with some quantitative experiments and reproducibility, but lacks statistical significance, omits some sweep details, and generalizes only across CF backbones. arxiv:2608.10245.rationale: Pure supply-chain optimization domain application with only tangential GNN relevance and no language methodology, so capped as out-of-scope. The paper provides clear problem formulation, matched-seed comparisons, ablations, and statistical tests, but exact held-out evidence is limited (Instance 13 only; Instances 14-15 use best-known incumbents), independent tests are mixed, and scope is narrow synthetic single-period complete networks.

arxiv:2608.10240.rationale: Out-of-scope pure domain recommendation application with only incidental multimodal feature use, so relevance is capped. arxiv:2608.10239.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM safety/evaluation and agentic multi-turn defenders. arxiv:2608.10237.rationale: Image-only adversarial attack on contrastive verification systems; no language/LLM methodology, so capped as out-of-scope pure computer vision despite AI-safety keyword overlap. The manifold-level attack has some novelty and includes baselines/ablations, but rigor is limited by inconsistent data-split/no-overlap claims and lack of statistical testing; cross-system evidence is only image verification.

arxiv:2608.10235.rationale: Out-of-scope pure physics-informed machine learning domain application with no language methodology; only weak Scientific AI relevance. arxiv:2608.10234.rationale: Pure scientific AI/PDE operator learning paper with no LLM, NLP, agent, safety, or language methodology. Despite detailed benchmark results, ablations, and resolution-transfer analysis, the topic remains outside the target preferences.

arxiv:2608.10233.rationale: Out-of-scope hydrology/remote-sensing domain application using standard Isolation Forest on GRACE-derived groundwater storage anomalies. No LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning/prompting or other weighted methodology. Method is a routine application to Ghana with limited novelty. Some equations and limitations are present, but evaluation is largely qualitative, lacks quantitative metrics/ground truth, and no code/data product availability is specified.

Limitations and Recommendations: acknowledges coarse GRACE resolution; no code/data availability statement.

arxiv:2608.10232.rationale: Primarily a pure robotics/vision-language-action world-action model with no LLM/NLP methodology; intersects low-weight robotics/multimodal/video categories but is out-of-scope under the provided rubric. It has moderate ablations and real/sim results, but domain-specific and limited generalization.

arxiv:2608.10224.rationale: Topically strong for agentic LLM/RAG/prompt optimization, but evidence is limited: small offline datasets (N=30 for prompt evolution, 100 chats for RAG/evaluator), no confidence intervals for offline results, the online treatment bundles multiple components without factorial attribution, and the A/B was stopped at two weeks after a four-week plan. Closed-source/proprietary deployment and absent code/data reduce reproducibility and generalizability.

fallback:32861f4533a0492e.rationale: Abstract-only locked blog post on sending code as an image to reduce LLM input token counts. Relevant to LLM/code and multimodal token usage, but no methods, results, baselines, or reproducible details are provided.

arxiv:2608.10220.rationale: Pure robotics/whole-body planning for humanoid navigation; out of scope for LLM/NLP/agents/transformers. Only tangential matches are reinforcement learning and robotics/embodied AI. Research quality is moderate: includes baselines, ablations, and quantitative simulation results but no hardware validation, limited trials, and no code/data release.

arxiv:2608.10218.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, multi-agent systems, AI safety, and red teaming. The paper provides an empirical study of self-propagating mind viruses across two agent settings, with model/topology/payload comparisons, ablations, case studies, and limitations. Rigor and evidence are moderate because outcomes rely heavily on LLM judges, evolutionary stochasticity, and somewhat artificial setups; generalizability is limited by model-specific optimization. Reproducibility is supported by detailed appendices and stated code links, though not independently verifiable from the document.
evidence: Abstract states the paper studies mind viruses propagating through multi-agent LLM systems and identifies factors influencing spread.
Section 2.2 reports infection rates across models, payloads, and fully connected vs. separate topologies.
Figure 8 shows model-dependent susceptibility and soul-configuration infection rates.
Section 6.1 Limitations acknowledges artificial experimental setups, limited affordances, and model-specific optimization.
Introduction (page 3) states code availability at two GitHub repositories.

arxiv:2608.10216.rationale: Topically relevant to agent guardrails, AI safety evaluation, and semantic similarity in NLP. The controlled factorial audit and pre-registered repair tests are moderately novel, but rigor and evidence strength are constrained by small single-annotator corpora, one deployed system, and field-level rather than broad generalization. Reproducibility is strong via the released pinned offline artifact.
evidence: Abstract: production drift guard caught 0 of 56 meaning-breaking mutations, including one approved reversal scored at cosine 0.9608.
§5: balanced accuracy across 90 configuration-threshold-task cells never exceeded 0.700, median 0.525; production configuration near chance.
§7: overlap-conditioned gate scored 0.750 in-sample but 0.533 held-out; NLI drop-in held-out AUROC 0.533.
§10: limitations include 10 pairs per cell, single-annotator labels, one end-to-end deployed system, and corpora generated within one project register.
Artifact availability: public offline harness with pinned local models, frozen results, DOI, and one-command reproduction.

arxiv:2608.10214.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM interpretability and multilingual NLP. The controlled subject-vs-language design, multi-model evaluation, and random baselines are strengths. However, the central granularity principle is inferred without measuring pretraining data composition, results lack statistical uncertainty estimates, evaluation pools are small, and code availability is only promised, limiting rigor and evidentiary support.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports zero subject-level neurons exceed 0.60 max-share across 939,008 combined FFN neurons and subject damage matrices show diagonal/off-diagonal means of 0.121-0.181 vs 0.031-0.076 accuracy points.
Section 4.2 reports language-level diagonal dNLL means of 1.82, 2.19, and 3.37 nats and off-diagonal means of -0.012, -0.060, and +0.006 nats, with near-diagonal damage matrices.
Section 4.4 Table 1 reports masking code-selective neurons reduces GSM8K accuracy by 17.3, 24.0, and 16.0 percentage points net of random across the three models.
Section 6 Limitations notes the analysis covers only three instruction-tuned model families in the 1.5B-7B range and activation-magnitude identification may miss functionally relevant neurons.

arxiv:2608.10213.rationale: Strongly relevant to LLM verification, reasoning, RAG/grounding and evaluation, though financial-domain-specific and not Japanese. Moderately novel neurosymbolic acceptance-control framework; evaluation has same-candidate baselines and multiple generators but lacks recent financial verifier baselines and statistical tests. Reported zero false accepts is well-documented but accompanied by high false-reject/coverage trade-offs.
evidence: Abstract: reports zero false accepts and baseline comparisons on XBRLFiling and FinanceBench.
Section 5.1: reports VeriFin metrics including 92.2% accuracy/98.8% coverage on XBRLFiling and 83.3% accuracy/80.6% coverage on FinanceBench.
Table 2: reports zero false accepts and 100% precision across six answer-generator models.
Section 5.3/Table 3: reports verifier-guided repair recovery up to 69.9%.

arxiv:2608.10209.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM alignment/safety through ECT post-training with SFT/PPO. Controlled proof-of-concept with shuffled-label baselines and seeds, but limited by small synthetic single-turn tasks, model-based evaluators, high seed variance, and no comparisons to related methods such as inoculation prompting.
evidence: Section 4.1.4 reports ECT increases even-handedness to 64.8% versus 49.8% baseline and 49.4% shuffled baseline, with lower refusal rates.
Section 4.2.3 reports ECT reduces sycophancy false-positive rate to 21.6±15.8% versus baseline 47.9±2.3%, but notes large seed-driven variance.
Appendix B provides detailed hyperparameters, templates, and seeds for both experiments, and the paper includes a code link.
Limitations acknowledges use of synthetic frontier-LLM data, model-based evaluators, and single-turn simple output spaces.

arxiv:2608.10207.rationale: Out-of-scope transportation/domain application; uses offline LLM-derived semantic embeddings and DQN for bus holding but is not core LLM/RL methodology. Quantitative tables support some within-route and transfer claims, but no significance testing and missing key implementation details limit rigor/reproducibility; only two university shuttle routes in simulation.

arxiv:2608.10206.rationale: Pure speech/phoneme recognition application without language-model or NLP methodology; age-auxiliary training is incremental multi-task learning. arxiv:2608.10196.rationale: In-scope LLM/code/DPO paper using Qwen3-8B for execution-grounded program evolution; relevant to LLMs, code/program synthesis, DPO alignment, training optimization, and NLP. arxiv:2608.10195.rationale: Out of scope: pure computer vision/visualization/psychophysics evaluation of vision models and VLMs without language methodology. arxiv:2608.10194.rationale: Out of scope for LLM/NLP: the paper presents an AI auditing framework and a motion-capture skeleton-inference case study, with no language-model methodology. arxiv:2608.10181.rationale: Pure computer vision/visual saliency and eye-tracking paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, or code. arxiv:2608.10178.rationale: Strongly relevant to LLM agents, coding agents, and self-evolving harnesses. arxiv:2608.10176.rationale: In-scope RAG/LLM/KG paper with hallucination and constraint-satisfaction evaluation. Relevance is moderate-high due to retrieval-augmented generation and LLM evaluation, but the contribution is an integration/application rather than new language-model methodology. Rigor is limited: synthetic self-derived benchmark, no statistical tests/human validation, limited implementation details, and only one pantry domain.

Claims rest on a self-reported human track record and a synthetic scenario, with proprietary details withheld; no baselines, ablations, or quantitative AI results support the framework.

arxiv:2608.10173.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging / proton therapy dose prediction using a diffusion bridge; no LLM/NLP/language methodology, so preference relevance is very low. arxiv:2608.10172.rationale: Topically relevant to LLM/transformer mechanistic interpretability and identifiability; not an out-of-scope pure domain application. The formal Koopman/EDMD treatment is substantial and the paper honestly reports negative and failed-control results. However, empirical support is partial: the predicted M^{-1/2} rate is observed mainly on Qwen3-8B-Base with conflicting robust summaries; the universality criterion fails on seed replicas; and several findings depend on feature-selection conventions. No code/availability claim and exact invariance assumptions limit reproducibility and generalizability.

arxiv:2608.10171.rationale: Strong topical alignment with LLM red-teaming and AI safety, but the paper is an incremental extension of prior GFlowNet-based red-teaming with Turkish data and mostly qualitative or summary-level experimental evidence.
