Section IV-B: evaluator model comparison is described only qualitatively, with no numeric success/toxicity/similarity values.
Section IV-C: transfer results to Gemma3-12b are described only as retaining high success for English and substantial loss for Turkish, without numeric success rates.

arxiv:2608.10170.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging paper on 3D brain MRI motion artifact reduction; no large language model, NLP, reasoning, agent, prompting, or code methodology. Despite reported ablations and multi-dataset evaluation, relevance to the stated preferences is minimal, and the paper is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract reports SSRL-MAR achieved PSNR 23.81dB, SSIM 91.55%, and NMSE 0.79% on in-silico dataset.
Section 4.3.4 Table 1 compares SSRL-MAR with CycleGAN, UDDN, AutoDPS, and supervised baselines on in-silico and in-vivo datasets.
Section 4.4 Table 4 reports component-wise ablations and unsupervised domain adaptation results.

arxiv:2608.10169.rationale: Out of scope for the stated preferences: the paper studies human affective judgments of visualization colors using color-space regression and psychology experiments, not LLM/NLP/reasoning/agents/safety or other listed AI language methodologies. Though the experiments are described with statistical tests and limitations, relevance to the rubric is negligible.
evidence: Abstract: predicts affective connotation of visualizations from constituent colors; no LLM/NLP/reasoning methodology.
Section 2 Experiment 1: uses LabC Cyl2 color space regression fitted on 71 colors to estimate emotion associations.
General Discussion and Conclusion: discusses visualization design automation and limitations including pixel-based weighting, mark frequency, and group variation.

arxiv:2608.10166.rationale: Out-of-scope image/video diffusion watermark-removal paper; no LLM/language methodology. Although it includes quantitative comparisons and ablation-style appendices, its relevance to requested NLP/LLM/preferences is minimal, capping the overall score at 0.20.
evidence: Section 7.2.1 reports MarkNull average BA 53.14% and MarkNull-A 57.10% across multi-bit watermarking schemes.
Table 2 compares detection rates across nine image watermarking methods.
Section 7.3 reports 100% ASR against SynthID-Image in Table 4.
Section 9 concludes a model-agnostic watermark removal framework without language-model methodology.

arxiv:2608.10162.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application: text-conditioned 3D hand-object motion generation, not LLM/NLP methodology. It uses a transformer and flow matching but contributes no language-modeling advances. Empirical comparisons and ablations are moderate, but limited datasets, no code release, small user study, and mixed plausibility on GRAB limit quality. Overall capped at 0.20 due to pure CV/robotics domain scope.
evidence: Sec. 4.2 describes the masked autoregressive transformer and flow-matching head.
Sec. 5, Table 2 reports ARCTIC/GRAB retrieval and generation metrics.
Sec. 5, Table 3 reports geometric and physical-plausibility metrics with mixed GRAB results.
Appendix B.4 lists training details but gives no code availability statement.
Sec. 7 mentions future work for unseen objects, indicating limited generalization.

arxiv:2608.10157.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, planning, and harness optimization, but relevance is not enough to overcome methodological limitations. The proposed verifier-grounded block-coordinate harness optimizer is moderately novel relative to prior verifier and harness-optimization work, though largely a structured combination of existing ideas. Rigor is limited by only two runs, no significance testing, and evaluation on train+validation rather than held-out data. Quantitative tables support the main claims but lack uncertainty estimates and detailed ablations. Generalizability is only partially demonstrated via two planning domains and cross-model transfer on a weaker LLM. Reproducibility is weakened by absence of code/data release and high-level implementation details.
evidence: Abstract claims SBCO matches or exceeds HGM-C at 4-5.5x lower compute budget.
Section 4 Evaluation Protocol states final performance is reported on full training+validation set and all numbers are the mean of two runs.
Table 1 reports Travel composite 84 vs HGM-C 83 and Shopping match 94 vs HGM-C 91 with budgets 733/989 vs 4000.
Section 5.2 Tables 4 and 5 show verifier reliability varies widely, with some geo-spatial verifiers at F1=0.
Section 6 Limitations acknowledges evaluation is restricted to two constraint-based planning domains and notes gains are bounded by the base LLM.

arxiv:2608.10155.rationale: Highly formal statistical hypothesis testing paper on optimal inference with black-box predictions, with strong theorems, proofs, and simulations, but it lacks alignment with the requested LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning focus; relevance is minimal, limiting overall score despite strong methodology.
evidence: Section 1.1 states main theoretical results (Theorems 1-5) for oracle and adaptive tests.
Section 6 provides simulation comparisons of chi-squared, projection, intrinsic projection, and adaptive tests.
Appendix C.1 contains proof of Lemma 1 for oracle test performance.
Section 4 derives adaptivity gap for orthogonal predictions and Theorem 3/4.

arxiv:2608.10154.rationale: LLM-based multimodal fine-tuning for psychometric item parameter estimation is relevant but a domain application rather than core LLM methodology. The approach extends prior work with Qwen3.5, LoRA, and continuous ability-binned probabilities; results show improved difficulty prediction (b correlation 0.85) versus text regression baselines, but there are no significance tests, limited ablations, proprietary data, and unclear code availability, which limit rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 3.1, Table 5: Qwen3.5-9B achieves Pearson 0.85 and RMSE 0.55 for difficulty b, versus MetaMath 0.75/0.68 and MathBERT 0.68/0.78.
Section 2.1.1, Table 1: dataset contains 970 item models, 4,848 items, 13.88M responses with split by item model.
Section 2.4.1: LoRA is applied conservatively only to Gated Attention components in Qwen3.5-4B/9B.
Section 4: authors acknowledge weak discrimination parameter recovery, approximation error, and limited adaptation of Gated DeltaNet layers.

arxiv:2608.10153.rationale: Highly relevant to agentic AI governance, multi-agent systems, and AI safety. Conceptual synthesis of control theory, complex adaptive systems, cybernetics, and SRE is novel, but the paper lacks ablations or traditional empirical baselines. Empirical evidence relies on public coding with acknowledged disclosure biases and small samples; quantitative results are descriptive rather than independently replicated. Reproducibility is partially supported by detailed protocols and a claimed code release, but data verification is limited.
evidence: Title/Abstract: framework for governing enterprise agentic AI across individual agents, collectives, human-agent teams, and fleets.
Section 5.1: coded 62 documented production failures; 82% multi-layer; kappa values reported.
Section 5.2: coded 22 agent-operations tools; 0% full Layer 2 coverage; Fisher exact p reported.
Section 5.3: scored 35 public enterprise deployments; all fall in the L0 maturity band.
Section 9: limitations acknowledge formal spareness, public evidence biases, and limited practitioner generality.

arxiv:2608.10152.rationale: Out of scope: the paper describes SEM-based hardware recovery of automotive EDR data from a damaged SRS EEPROM. It contains no AI/ML, LLM, NLP, or language-model methodology and matches none of the listed preference topics.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: describes SEM-based recovery from automotive EEPROM, not AI/ML.
Page 1 Introduction: focuses on SRS/airbag module and EDR extraction background.

arxiv:2608.10149.rationale: The paper applies LLM reasoning, chain-of-thought, and GRPO to time series ensemble forecasting. Despite LLM/CoT components, the core task is a domain-specific numerical forecasting application outside the listed language/NLP/safety/multimodal preference areas, so preference_relevance is capped. The work reports extensive benchmark tables and ablations, but lacks stated limitations, variance/multiple seeds, and code release; generalizability is limited to univariate fixed-length settings.
evidence: Section 4.2, Tables 2(a)-(b) report main MSE comparisons across foundation and small model candidates.
Section 3.3 describes hybrid textual-numerical input and rule-based CoT construction.
Section 4.4, Table 3(b) reports ablations for CoT, RAG, and weight format.
Section 4.3, Figure 5 analyzes reciprocal reward mapping against alternatives.
Section 4.7, Figure 4 reports transfer learning comparisons.

arxiv:2608.10146.rationale: Out-of-scope optical semiconductor metrology paper with no LLM/NLP/agent/safety or other matching AI/ML methodology. Within its own domain it provides a quantitative production-wafer comparison of FFT, LRZ, and optical model fitting against WLI, but novelty, generalizability, and reproducibility are limited for this curation scope.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: describes FFT-based thick-film reflectometry comparison with WLI, not AI/ML.
Page 3: reports 81 production-wafer measurements and RMSE/correlation comparisons against WLI.
Page 5: attributes systematic FFT bias to spectral leakage from finite measurement windows.

arxiv:2608.10145.rationale: Reproduction study of a pixel-based world model with no language methodology; only weak preference overlap via transformer architecture, training/evaluation, and planning. High transparency and reproducibility, but single seed and one environment limit generalizability.
evidence: Section 3.2: source-level fidelity audit identifies four undocumented pipeline conventions.
Section 4.2: authors' released checkpoint reaches 84.0% under repository evaluation config vs 14.0% under Appendix F.1 protocol.
Section 4.3: BatchNorm recalibration table shows evaluation-mode loss inflation by up to 302.7x.
Section 5.2: pre-registered same-room vs cross-wall advantage falls from +39.1 to -6.4 across checkpoints.
Section 7: limitations include single seed, ten epochs vs one hundred, and confounded context length.

arxiv:2608.10144.rationale: Relevant to LLM/PEFT fine-tuning and NLP: proposes sketch-aggregated federated LoRA for heterogeneous client ranks, uses RoBERTa-Large on GLUE. Not Japanese or high-priority reasoning/safety/agent work. Novelty is moderate: linear sketching is imported to federated LoRA, but convergence theory only covers the rank-homogeneous version. Experiments compare several baselines on four GLUE tasks with three seeds, but empirical gains are often within noise and no code release is stated.
evidence: Abstract: proposes SeFoRA, a sketch-aggregated federated LoRA algorithm addressing rank heterogeneity and bilinear mismatch.
Section 4 Theorem 1: convergence guarantee is for rank-homogeneous SeFoRA-Ho, not the rank-heterogeneous SeFoRA.
Section 5 Experiments: RoBERTa-Large fine-tuned on SST-2, QNLI, QQP, MNLI with 40 clients, Dirichlet alpha=0.5, 500 rounds, three seeds; Tables 2 and 3 report mean accuracy and standard deviation.
Section 5 Table 2: SeFoRA-Ho results are close to FedIT, and some differences are within reported standard deviations.

arxiv:2608.10137.rationale: Core LLM constrained-decoding paper with relevant topics (structured generation, text-to-SQL, inference latency). The method is a modest but reasonable extension over masking and online sampling, but evaluation is narrow: one base model, one masking tool, only four Spider queries, ASAp capped/simplified, and no statistical testing. Quantitative tables support the main claim but up-to-113x/235x figures are cherry-picked.
evidence: Table 1 reports KL divergence and average latency for Syncode, ASAp, MLP, LR_FULL, and LR_NT across 14 BV4 grammars.
Section 4, part (4) reports only four Spider query pairs and notes ASAp was simplified for cre_theme_park.
Section 4, Metrics describes KL estimation from 1000 LLM samples and renormalization over valid samples.
Section 4, Experimental setup uses Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 as the only base LLM.

arxiv:2608.10131.rationale: Out-of-scope per rubric: vision/medical imaging and biology foundation model work without LLM/language methodology, so final score is capped at 0.20. It has some relevance to interpretability and vision foundation models, but not to prioritized LLM/NLP topics. The method is a simple region-conditioned PCA with exploratory case studies and limited quantitative evidence.
evidence: Section 2.2 defines P3CA as fitting PCA within a prompted region via region-conditioned covariance and applies the top eigenvectors to the full tensor; Section 2.4 describes case studies across natural images, colorectal pathology embeddings, and spatial transcriptomics.

Table 1 reports LDA balanced accuracy using frozen 3D projections: e.g., GigaPath adenocarcinoma 69.07 ± 16.23 for global PCA vs 85.71 ± 11.97 for P3CA prompt 1; H0-mini smooth muscle 53.63 ± 7.15 vs 79.50 ± 12.43 for prompt 2.
Section Limitations states the output depends on the selected prompt, the projection is linear, and larger studies are needed for prompt stability and clinical performance.

arxiv:2608.10127.rationale: Primordial black hole cosmology paper with no ML/LLM/NLP methodology; falls outside stated scope. Internally appears detailed with code, equations, and quantitative tables, but relevance to the preference categories is negligible and overall score is capped at 0.20 for out-of-domain work.
evidence: Abstract: presents PBH evaporation, FRISHBEE code, mass/spin distributions; no ML/LLM content.
Sec. 4.1 and Table 3: report ΔNeff ratios for extended PBH mass distributions; no ML baselines or ablations.
Sec. 5: conclusions focus on cosmological observables and CMB-S4/Simons Observatory, not language/ML methods.

arxiv:2608.10126.rationale: Topically central to RLHF, alignment, and fairness, but research quality is limited: controlled simulated raters, logistic-regression reward models, no policy optimization or statistical testing, and explicit diagnostic scope. Quantitative results support the claim only weakly due to no uncertainty estimates or ablations beyond a single table.
evidence: Methodology: dataset contains 971 pairwise comparisons from 60 simulated raters across 20 prompts, with train/test split by raters.
Methodology: reward model is Logistic Regression on 768-dim prompt embedding plus response-difference features, without full policy optimization.
Results: Table 1 reports overall accuracy 46.9% baseline vs 67.9% PA-RLHF and fairness gap 15.9 pp vs 9.6 pp.
Discussion: authors state the controlled setting limits generalizability beyond diagnostic context.

arxiv:2608.10120.rationale: Relevant mainly through SSM/Mamba architecture preference, but not LLM/NLP and heavily application-oriented (process traces, clinical events, network traffic, TKGs). Controlled Joint vs Two-Stage comparison and quantitative diagnostics/ablations provide moderate evidence, but Mamba2 results do not replicate with GPT-2 and generation-quality gains are mixed; no code release, only future availability.
evidence: Section 5.2 and Table 1 report Joint improves TCS/probe R2 and lowers probe MAE over Two-Stage across four domains.
Section 6.2 and Table 2 show mixed generation quality: identical BPI2018 DLS, mixed MIMIC-IV, improved network traffic and temporal KG metrics.
Appendix C reports GPT-2 backbone results are heterogeneous and do not consistently reproduce Mamba2 findings.
Section 8.3 acknowledges no standardized evaluation for joint event/timestamp generation fidelity.

arxiv:2608.10115.rationale: Out of scope for the stated preferences: this is a social computing/HCI study of controlled content manipulation in the Reddit interface, with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, prompting, safety, or language-model methodology. The work has modest methodological strengths and clear limitations, but relevance to the target topics is negligible, capping the overall score low.
evidence: §5.1.1 reports ART ANOVA and exploratory TOST equivalence results
§7.4 states limitations to desktop Old Reddit and sample-specific fidelity
§4.2 describes open-source availability but omits the repository address for anonymous review

arxiv:2608.10109.rationale: Relevant to NLP and dataset construction with LLM-assisted annotation/prompting, but not aligned with core LLM methods, Japanese LLM, reasoning, agents, safety, or multimodal preferences. Resource fills a Persian-English code-mixing POS gap; human validation and quantitative analyses are moderate, but some comparisons lack significance tests and generalization is untested beyond the stated transferability claim.
evidence: Section 3.1 reports LLM vs gold token identification F1 90.8%, POS accuracy 97.0%, macro F1 76.8%.
Section 4.2 reports chi-square test for positional distribution: χ²(4)=8.38, p=0.079.
Section 4.3 reports length-controlled triggering effect percentages without a significance test.
Section 5 Limitations states findings are specific to Persian-English and platform coverage.

arxiv:2608.10108.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, long-term/agent memory, RAG-style retrieval, and NLP QA. The adaptive multi-structure evidence selection is a moderate incremental contribution over fixed multi-memory and routing methods, with a useful controlled subset sweep. Quantitative evidence is fairly detailed across two benchmarks and two answer LLMs, but the main gains rely on train/val/test tuning that may advantage MESA over fixed baselines, no significance testing is shown, and code availability is not specified.
evidence: Section 5.2, Table 1: MESA reports 65.1% overall accuracy on AMA-Bench with Qwen3-32B versus 56.6% for AMA-Agent.
Section 5.3, Table 3: MESA uses 11.0k evidence tokens per query versus 18.7k for the all-structure configuration, about 41% fewer tokens.
Section 5.2, Table 2: MESA reaches 49.0 F1 on LoCoMo versus 47.2 for EMem.
Section 5.3, Table 3: Ablations show route-to-one 57.0%, w/o priors 63.1%, and w/o UCB 64.3%, supporting learned subset selection.
Appendix F.1, Table 6: Judge robustness is tested with Qwen3-32B, Gemma-4-31B, and GPT-5.4, with MESA ranked first across judges.
Appendix G: Limitations note evaluation is limited to controlled long-horizon agent and conversational benchmarks, without continuous or multimodal memory updates.

arxiv:2608.10107.rationale: Domain-specific autonomous driving world-action model using video diffusion and geometric foundation model supervision. It is not an LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology paper, so preference relevance is very low and an out-of-scope cap applies. The work has some novelty in combining 4D consistency supervision with decision-oriented timestep sampling, and it reports benchmark comparisons and ablations, but lacks statistical testing, explicit limitations, quantitative cross-domain evaluation, and code/data availability.
evidence: Abstract: proposes 4D-WAM, leveraging geometric foundation models for training-time 4D consistency supervision in autonomous driving.
Method: defines feature consistency and depth consistency losses against frozen VGGT-Ω outputs.
Experiments: Table 1 reports EPDMS 90.6 on NAVSIM v2 navtest; Table 4 reports cumulative component-wise ablation gains.
Ablation Studies: Table 5 reports decision-region sampling probability peaking at 50%, and Table 6 reports EPDMS saturating after two denoising steps.
Supplementary S3: zero-shot Waymo evaluation is qualitative only, with no quantitative metrics.

arxiv:2608.10103.rationale: Relevant mainly through quantization, inference optimization, and LLM-serving motivation, but the core is low-level GPU GEMM/Tensor Core engineering rather than LLM/NLP methodology. The controlled profiling and ablation are useful, but confidence is limited by single-GPU scope, square-only workloads, no statistical error bars, and internal table inconsistencies.
evidence: Abstract reports same-precision PTX speedups of 1.4x-1.8x for INT8 and 2.9x-4.3x for INT4, plus 34.4x and 98.7x relative to FP16 WMMA.
Section III-A describes one-variable-at-a-time kernel design; Listings 1 and 2 show cp.async/ldmatrix/mma.sync PTX paths.
Table III and Table V conflict on FP16 wall-clock durations, e.g., N=512 is 0.184 ms in Table III versus 680.155 ms in Table V.
Section VI limits scope to a single NVIDIA L4 GPU, square matrices, fixed tiling, and excludes quantized numerical accuracy evaluation.
Artifact availability statement claims code, build scripts, and Nsight Compute profiles on GitHub and Zenodo.

arxiv:2608.10101.rationale: Out-of-scope pure code-review/software-engineering study using UniXcoder embeddings; no LLM/NLP/language methodology. It weakly matches Code & Programming but is a domain application, so relevance is capped. Methods are careful but heuristic trajectory linking is unvalidated, sample is one Linux subsystem, and the main finding is a limitation of whole-function embedding resolution.
evidence: Section 3 reports 10,117 endpoint trajectories and 75.3% byte-identical v1/vN bodies.
Section 4 M2 reports mean endpoint similarity 0.997 for all trajectories and 0.990 for the 2,501 edited-only trajectories vs a 0.909 null.
Section 4 M3 reports the first-round concentration weakens after filtering and rank-biserial correlation r≈0.05.
Artifact Availability states pipeline, scripts, metric tables, and notebook are available at a Zenodo DOI.

arxiv:2608.10096.rationale: Pure GAN/generative image modeling without language methodology; out-of-scope for LLM/NLP curation and capped at 0.20. The e-process adaptive training scheme is somewhat novel and the paper provides formal propositions plus CIFAR-10/synthetic experiments, but relevance to LLM preferences is only tangential via general training optimization. Empirical comparisons lack significance testing and use best-checkpoint selection, limiting rigor/evidence.
evidence: Experiments / Table 1: reports CIFAR-10 mean IS/FID for fixed, TTUR, and adaptive schedules under softplus and hinge objectives.
Supplementary Material Appendix D: provides network architecture, shared training settings, method-specific configurations, and evaluation protocol.

arxiv:2608.10091.rationale: Pure visual watermarking for images/video; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agents, or language methodology. The work has some within-domain contributions on decoder-aware watermark coexistence and video extension, with ablations and quantitative tables, but it is out of scope for the stated preferences and is evaluated accordingly.
evidence: Abstract: claims contributions on video watermark coexistence and decoder-aware training.
Section 4.1: describes image/video datasets, baselines, and coexistence evaluation protocol.
Table 1: reports solo PSNR 52.4 dB for the proposed image/video signpost and joint quality results.
Table 4: ablation compares noCoexist, single-decoder, leave-one-out, and full decoder-aware training variants.

arxiv:2608.10090.rationale: LLM code-generation/post-training paper for hardware verification testbenches, using SFT, RL, model merging, and adaptive multi-teacher distillation. Highly relevant to LLM, code, agentic, and RL preferences; strong ablations and appendices but limited to one application family and not tested beyond hardware verification.
evidence: Table 1 reports CHORUS Merge (post-training) 88.0% Pass@1 on CVDP-ECov agentic, compared with DeepSeek-R1 74.5% and LLM4Cov-Qwen3-4B 69.2%.
Section 5.2 reports an oracle union of experts at 90.8% Pass@1 and Figure 5 shows per-design complementary behavior.
Table 3 ablates reward gating and skip-vs-fallback, with continued pure RL at 85.1% and adaptive OPD at 88.0%.
Appendix A defines Pass@1/Pass@5/Cov@1/Cov@5 metrics and reports invalid simulations as zero coverage.
Appendix B Tables 4-5 provide RL hyperparameters and 1000-step trajectories for the three SFT initializations.
Section 6 states limitations: study confined to hardware testbench generation and diversity tied to the specific LLM4Cov SFT curriculum.

arxiv:2608.10089.rationale: Strong topical relevance to LLM fairness/bias evaluation and safety benchmarking; moderate novelty because the association-to-behavior gap is known, though the surname/abstention/equivalence design is a useful instantiation. Rigor is solid with predeclared frozen protocols and equivalence testing, but the central cross-model correlation has only n=8 and the robustness layer was unexecuted. Evidence is quantitatively detailed but the main transfer result is imprecise. Generalizability is limited by synthetic Chilean surname tasks. Reproducibility is high with frozen instruments, hashes, and full response archives.
evidence: Section 5.1 reports elite-minus-common association contrasts ranging from +7.00 to +62.10 across models and significant elite-vs-rare contrasts in all eight models.
Section 5.2 and Table 1 report decision leakage effects mostly near zero, with five models meeting the predeclared +/-0.10 SD equivalence criterion.
Section 5.3 reports model-level Pearson r=0.201 (p=0.633) and surname-pair-level r=0.065 (p=0.565) for association-to-leakage coupling.
Section 7 states the predeclared robustness layer remained unexecuted due to a budget gate, limiting confirmatory claims to the frozen primary conditions.
Section 9 reports 8,256 verified responses, frozen prompt hashes, provider routing, and reproducibility artifacts.

arxiv:2608.10084.rationale: Medical imaging application analyzing chest radiograph repository labels; out of scope for LLM/language-model methodology despite mention of report-derived NLP labels. Methodologically clear but limited to a single repository and single index finding, with no head-to-head downstream supervision comparison, so capped low.
evidence: Abstract: reports near-zero agreement and DenseNet121 test ROC-AUC 0.853.
Section 3, Table 1: cardiomegaly Cohen's kappa 0.011 and PPA 1.3%.
Limitations and Future Work: acknowledges retrospective single public repository and no head-to-head repository-vs-expert supervision comparison.
Section 2: describes DenseNet121 fine-tuning and subject-independent cohort splits.

arxiv:2608.10077.rationale: Out-of-scope astrophysics paper on gyrochronology and stellar rotation periods; no LLM/NLP/AI methodology or any preferred AI topic. Preference relevance is zero. Domain-specific empirical work has limited internal methodological rigor for an AI venue, with no ML baselines or ablations, so overall score is capped well below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: states the paper maps stellar rotation and calibrates gyrochronology using NGC-752.
Section III: describes TARS catalog period vetting and binary flags, not AI/ML methodology.
Section IV.1: compares empirical gyrochronology models as astronomy applications only.

arxiv:2608.09931.rationale: Highly relevant multimodal LLM self-distillation paper in the preferred Multimodal AI and Training/Optimization areas. The counterfactual blind-spot criterion is a plausibly novel self-contained alternative to externally constructed privileged visual context. Evaluation is fairly extensive across 12 benchmarks and two model sizes, but rigor is limited by no statistical significance testing, no explicit limitations section, and one model family. Evidence from Tables 1-4 supports the main gains and ablations, though all validation is internal.
evidence: Section 5.1, Table 1: CVPD reports best performance across twelve benchmarks at 4B and 8B scales, with Qwen3-VL-8B gains of +3.60 OCRBench, +3.38 MMStar Fine-Grained Perception, and +3.08 MMStar Logical Reasoning.

Section 5.2, Table 2: Ablations show replacing curation with random regions and removing contrastive ranking produce the largest drops, supporting the Counterfactual Criterion and ghost-conditioned negative teacher.
Section 5.3, Table 3: Hyperparameter sensitivity reports limited variation around default rank weight, margin, and KL target settings.
Section 4.1, Figure 3: Curation suppresses ghost-side divergence from 0.387 to 0.016 and reverses entropy delta from -0.211 to +0.378 on 6,791 candidate regions from 500 raw images.

arxiv:2608.09930.rationale: Pure TTS/speech evaluation benchmark; only tangential Audio-LLM and prompting overlap. Falls under the pure audio out-of-scope clause despite Audio-LLM judges. Controlled contribution, but limited by low inter-rater agreement for some dimensions, binary labels, and single TTS architecture for IPA manipulation.
evidence: Table 3 reports significant MOS sensitivity mainly for acoustic-manipulation dimensions such as Human Plausibility and Speech Rate, with no significant Phonetic Accuracy or Lexical Stress detection by MOS models.
Table 4 shows undefined correlations from output collapse for several Audio-LLM conditions and sparse inconsistent sensitivity.
Section 3.3/Table 2 reports Krippendorff alpha below 0.7 for Intonation (0.469) and Expressiveness (0.460).
Table 9 indicates 32.3% of intended failures were not perceived by majority vote, highest for Emotional Appropriateness (46.2%) and Speaker Identity Consistency (48.4%).

arxiv:2608.09928.rationale: The paper aligns strongly with LLM/multimodal interpretability, sparse autoencoders, and safety evaluation. It combines existing model diffing, SAE training, and activation steering for MLLMs; the contribution is incremental but useful. Rigor is moderate: multiple models and controls are used, but key safety/OCR results are only on PaliGemma 2 and many headline numbers come from selected top features rather than aggregate pre-registered tests. Evidence includes causal ablation controls and selection ablations, but no confidence intervals are reported. Generalizability and reproducibility are limited by SAE-suite availability and absent code release.
evidence: Abstract: reports 12% average spatial and 17% OCR degradation from feature removal, 24% ASR reduction, and +3.6%/+1.8% steering gains.
Sec 5.1 Table 1: per-feature VSR ablation across three models gives mean deltas -10.1/-12.3/-14.6 with |ΔVQA| ≤ 1.5%.
Sec 5.2 Table 4: per-category top safety features reduce VLSBench ASR 17-28% with |ΔVQA| ≤1% and ΔCtrl ≤1%.
Sec 6.1 Table 7: full MMDiff selection yields -12.3% VSR and -0.1% VQA vs -25.9% VQA for firing-only features.
Sec 8 Limitations: safety and OCR evaluated on PaliGemma 2 only; larger backbones untested; steering recipe assumes instruction-tuned reference model.

arxiv:2608.10057.rationale: Moderately relevant via CLIP/LLM scene-graph spatial reasoning, but the core contribution is 3D Gaussian open-vocabulary segmentation rather than language-model methodology. Novelty is incremental over prior granularity/scale-based 3D segmentation. Evaluation covers multiple datasets, but rigor is limited by a single-scene ablation, no statistical significance/error bars, and no explicit limitations. Reproducibility is partially supported by implementation details but no code release is confirmed.
evidence: Sec. 3.1 describes local peak-based mask level assignment from multi-view SAM masks and physical scales.
Sec. 3.3 defines the Optimal View Selection CLIP grounding score and hierarchical/spatial scene graph edges for LLM-guided retrieval.
Table 5 reports CoR mIoU overall: LEGO 51.6 vs LaGa w/ CoR 14.3, THGS 9.5, BBQ 6.1.
Table 6 ablation row with all loss components shows 93.1 mAcc/67.3 mIoU; lowest row is 82.8/60.7.
Appendix 0.B documents SAM ViT-H, L=8 levels with d=8, 30k+10k iterations, and 20-60 min per scene.

arxiv:2608.09926.rationale: Video world model with latent dynamics reasoning, but no language methodology; falls outside the LLM/NLP/agent focus despite the low-weight video/temporal preference. Domain evaluation shows controlled ablations and quantitative comparisons, but only simulated balls, one seed, no statistical error bars, and limited generalizability.
evidence: Abstract: reports >20x smaller ID-OOD gap, 26x fewer parameters, and 143x faster than DiT-S baseline.
Table 1: under single-task training at 256^2, LDR average position gap is 0.013 vs DiT-S 0.300.
Implementation details: 'All runs use seed 42 and report a single run'.
Limitation: 'we validate LDR as a principle on simulated scenes with simple objects'.

arxiv:2608.10056.rationale: Pure robotics/human-following navigation paper; out of scope per the stated curation rules. It uses transformer attention and constrained RL, but has no LLM/NLP/language methodology, so relevance is capped. Within its domain, the paper has a clear decomposition approach, ablations, and several OOD simulation tests, but lacks statistical significance testing and clear code/data release, and real-world evidence is a small pilot (7/10 trajectories).
evidence: Abstract describes human-following robot navigation in pedestrian crowds.
III-C describes the transformer policy network and ACI uncertainty estimation.
III-D describes the CMDP/PPO-Lagrangian cost decomposition.
Table I and Table III report in-distribution and OOD results.
IV-H reports 7 of 10 real-robot trajectories completed.

arxiv:2608.09925.rationale: Relevant LLM evaluation and safety/benchmark work for Dutch governmental use, matching LLM, evaluation, NLP, safety, data, and efficiency preferences, but not Japanese-specific or reasoning/agent topics. Novelty is moderate: a value-grounded integration of existing benchmarks plus a new HonestCityBench and non-expert leaderboard, though findings are not highly novel. Rigor is limited by small expert sample, tiny benchmark subsets, GPT-4o-based translation, no statistical significance testing, and missing energy data for API models. Evidence is quantitative but largely descriptive. Reproducibility is supported by code, prompts, and model list, but HonestCityBench is only planned for release.

arxiv:2608.09919.rationale: Relevant LLM/code-analysis application using a foundation-model oracle with zero-shot prompting for Python refactoring behavior detection. The approach is incremental over prior refactoring-oracle and SafeRefactorPy work; validation is limited by a single-project/single-tool setup, a single human expert baseline, no inter-rater reliability, no comparison to tests or static analysis, and limited external validity. Quantitative results and issue-tracker acceptance provide moderate evidence, but generalizability is weak.
evidence: Section 4.2.1 states a single Python developer with ten years of experience served as the sole human-expert baseline judge.
Section 4.3.1 reports gpt-oss-20b modal predictions achieved precision 0.67, recall 0.91, accuracy 0.84, and F1 0.77.
Section 4.3.2 states 64 expert-labeled behavior-change instances among 217 pairs were consolidated into 13 distinct behavioral changes.
Section 4.3.3 reports 12 of 13 bug reports were accepted by Rope developers, with issue #750 reclassified as an enhancement.

Section 5 acknowledges threats including a single expert baseline, single TextBlob project, lack of comparison to test suites/static analyses, and absence of confidence intervals.

Contributions combine existing tokenization, mean-variance teacher, and policy-optimization ideas. The paper has chronological splits, leakage controls, and quantitative ablation, but evidence is limited by single training seed, narrow five-ETF universe, short/partial test periods, contextual FinTexTS comparison, no formal significance tests, and no code release stated.

arxiv:2608.09867.rationale: Highly relevant LLM safety/reasoning/red-teaming paper. arxiv:2608.09842.rationale: Specialized table-parsing paper relevant through agentic VLM control, multimodal parsing, evaluation/benchmarks, and inference-time routing, but not core LLM/NLP. arxiv:2608.09836.rationale: Highly relevant LLM post-training/distillation methodology for mathematical reasoning. Novelty is moderate: the paper identifies a degenerate agreement failure mode and proposes TIDE with Hellinger suppression plus analytic top-K deficit recovery, but builds on existing OPD baselines (FiRe-OPD, PowerOPD, AOPD). Evidence is fairly strong with formal propositions, multi-benchmark results, ablations, sensitivity checks, and case studies, but generalization is limited to two teacher-student pairs and math-only data. Reproducibility is supported by detailed hyperparameters and code availability.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 1 reports strong-mismatch Avg@8: TIDE 20.3 vs OPD 6.9 and weak-mismatch TIDE 46.7 vs OPD 45.7.
Section 4.3, Table 4 ablation reports Sampled OPD 6.87, Selection only 14.58, Excess branch 18.57, Deficit branch 18.32, and TIDE 20.34.
Section 4.3, Table 3 reports strong-mismatch generation length OPD 22,395 vs TIDE 7,294 and missing-box rate 65.5% vs 5.4%.
Appendix A provides proofs for Proposition 1 and Proposition 2.
Appendix D.2 and D.4 provide hyperparameters and evaluation details, and the abstract gives a code URL.

arxiv:2608.09834.rationale: Moderately relevant NLP/FinBERT/LoRA paper on financial sentiment classification. It connects to NLP, transformer training, and efficiency, but is a small BERT-based domain application rather than LLM-focused. Contributions are incremental rule-feature fusion, with single-split evaluation, weak VADER-derived labels, no feature ablations, and no uncertainty estimates limiting rigor and evidence.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: reports RA-FinBERT test accuracy 69.89% and macro F1 0.634 versus text-only FinBERT 63.44% accuracy and 0.526 macro F1.
Page 6 Section 3.2: dataset contains 614 examples; test set has 93 examples, including 11 neutral items.
Page 8 Section 4.2 Table 1: lists test performance for DistilBERT, text-only FinBERT, and RA-FinBERT, including class-specific F1 and neutral recall.
Page 10 Section 4.4: acknowledges results come from one split and one seed, labels are VADER-derived weak labels, and repeated runs or cross-validation are needed.

arxiv:2608.09830.rationale: Out-of-scope pure wearable sensor health application with no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent methodology; multimodal refers to sensor fusion rather than vision-language or language-based multimodal AI, so score is capped at 0.20. Within-domain methods are moderately described, but clinical domain application is not relevant to the target preferences.
evidence: Section 2.1 describes the CMI wearable sensor dataset with 8,151 sequences from 81 participants, but also reports an implausible average of ~7,098 replicates per participant, indicating a reporting inconsistency.
Table 2 reports ALL-Modality binary F1=0.985 and multi-class macro F1=0.700 against IMU, THM, and ToF unimodal baselines.
Section 2.9 uses a stratified grouped participant-level train/validation/test split (5,810/714/1,627 sequences).
Section 4 acknowledges controlled-setting limitations and suggests future in-the-wild deployment.

arxiv:2608.09828.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents and AI safety: structured multi-role workflows, constitutional/executable governance, guardrails, and agent recovery. The study is a reasonably rigorous frozen benchmark with pre-specified statistics, exact paired tests, and detailed limitations, but novelty is incremental over institutional AI/provenance-laundering work and generalizability is limited by the synthetic terminal-delegation environment.
evidence: Section 2.2 defines six governance treatments and separates violation attempt, realized violation, compliant completion, and safe recovery.
Section 3.1 Table 4 reports 0/384 realized violations for constitutional prompt and provenance guard, 22/384 for local guard, with compliant completions.
Section 3.2 reports the matched laundering contrast: 22/96 local guard vs 0/96 provenance guard, exact paired p=4.77e-7.
Section 6 states the environment is synthetic and small, delegation is terminal, and open-ended multi-agent interaction lies outside the study.
Appendix D reports 5,280 episodes, canonical execution SHA, protocol fingerprint, seed, token counts, and archival claims.

arxiv:2608.09826.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM reasoning, RLVR, and on-policy distillation, with strong preference weight. The method is moderately novel: shared-parameter skill-conditioned self-distillation plus annealed Rényi-type cross-entropy builds clearly on OPSD/GKD and skill-context work. Rigor is fairly strong with multi-scale runs, ablation, leakage audits, equal-FLOP baselines, and uncertainty intervals, but is limited to Qwen3-Base math benchmarks and ordered ablations. Evidence for the zero-variance mechanism is good, though generalizability is narrow and no code release is indicated.
evidence: Abstract and Table 1: reports overall avg@8 gains over GRPO of +2.46, +4.85, and +12.01 at 0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B, with per-benchmark avg@8/pass@8.
Experiments: zero-variance groups account for 63.0-68.0% of groups; at 1.7B zero-variance-only distillation reaches 49.63 (+4.11), recovering 84.7% of the full gain.
Dissecting the Gain, Table 2: ordered 1.7B ablation shows OPSD 48.51, +skill abstraction 49.06, +tilted risk 49.94, +usefulness gate 50.37.
Robustness to Alternative Explanations: equal-FLOP GRPO reaches 46.31 vs SKALD 50.37 at 1.7B; tuned 4B equal-FLOP GRPO reaches 52.19 vs SKALD 63.38.

arxiv:2608.09819.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, continual learning, coding, long context, RL, and serving. However, rigor and evidence are limited: internal benchmarks use same-family judges, routing accuracy is measured on a training-distribution trace, many comparisons lack confidence intervals or paired ablations, and the paper explicitly leaves cross-generation compounding and component attribution open. Reproducibility is incomplete despite public model/harness references and some hyperparameters.
evidence: Section 2.3: reports 99.12% routing accuracy on a 6,448-sample trace but states the trace is drawn from LoRA training data and is not an independent held-out split.

Section 3.2.5: reports 122/122 expansion coverage on selected base-failure tasks under adaptive configuration search, but acknowledges it measures configuration-search coverage, not full RSI training improvement.
Section 6 and Table 8: benchmark point estimates are given without confidence intervals; ChatBench uses a private GLM-5.2 judge, and the paper notes possible same-family favor.
Section 7.2: lists material limitations including no cross-generation compounding, no complete per-specialist training specification, and no standalone safety/red-team evaluation.
Appendix B.6: provides adapter hyperparameters but lacks full training data and reproducibility details for the reported checkpoints.

arxiv:2608.09818.rationale: MedPixel is a multimodal medical pixel-language model using Qwen2.5-VL and SAM2, with moderate relevance to multimodal LLM/reasoning/alignment topics, but its heavy medical imaging and segmentation focus limits preference fit. The synthetic mask-derived supervision and PPLO add some novelty, though the architecture and data recipe largely combine known components. Tables and ablations provide quantitative support, but evidence is limited by weak external clinical validation, sparse statistical testing, and future-only code/checkpoint release.
evidence: Table 1: Reports MedPixel-7B Dice/NSD across T1-T5 tasks, including 85.0 T1 Dice and 66.7 T2 Dice.
Table 2: Shows zero-shot transfer on MeCoVQA-G+ with MedPixel-7B slice Dice 41.1 and modality Dice 47.4.
Table 4 and Appendix E.2: PLPO improves T2 and T4 segmentation metrics over SFT.
Appendix C: Provides training mixture sizes, hyperparameters, and Stage 2 preference-pair construction details.
Limitations: Acknowledges templated language diversity, source dataset coverage limits, and 2D/slice-based evaluation.

arxiv:2608.09816.rationale: Relevant to agentic ReAct/VLM and multimodal preferences but remains an embodied navigation application, limiting preference fit. Benchmarking, ablations, and statistical CIs support claims; novelty is incremental over VLFM/ASCENT, and reproducibility lacks code/model details.
evidence: Section 4.2 (Table 1): reports 68.75% SR and 33.97% SPL on HM3D v1 val, 47.29% SR and 18.01% SPL on MP3D val.
Section 4.3 (Table 2): Greedy Frontier ablation costs 3.40 SR points, 95% CI [1.70,5.05], McNemar p<0.001.
Appendix B: lists RTX 3090, PyTorch 2.1.0, Habitat-Sim/Lab 0.3.1, Ubuntu 20.04 for experimental setup.

arxiv:2608.09807.rationale: Pure robotics localization/state-estimation paper on a Wasserstein-robust adaptive EKF/ESKF plug-in. No LLM/NLP language methodology; incidental Transformer/Mamba backbones in a learned adapter do not bring it in scope. Capped at <=0.20 as pure robotics. Technical content is moderately rigorous with ablations, but GNSS evaluation is in-sample and UWB radius selection is not a fully frozen test set, limiting evidence strength and generalization.
evidence: Abstract: Robotic localization under changing sensing conditions ... nonlinear extended Kalman filter (EKF) and error-state Kalman filter (ESKF) stacks.
Section 4: We evaluate WRAP on two robot-localization settings: UWB–IMU indoor localization and GNSS–INS outdoor localization.
Section 4.2: ... instantiate this architecture with Mamba, Transformer, and gated recurrent unit (GRU) sequence backbones.
Section 5: The UWB trials are held out from adapter training but cross-validated for radii; GNSS is in-sample.

arxiv:2608.09805.rationale: Highly relevant LLM post-training/RLVR paper focused on GRPO and parameter-space exploration for reasoning and code generation. Novelty is moderate because parameter-space exploration has prior classical RL work and a cited concurrent extension; the main contribution is the chunked C3PO variant and empirical study. Rigor is reasonable with two 7B model families, multiple benchmarks, ablations, and baselines, but many gains are modest and only limited multi-seed validation is reported. Evidence is quantitative and tied to sections/tables/figures. Generalizability is limited to 7B math/code RLVR settings. Reproducibility is supported by detailed hyperparameters and algorithms but wall-clock/systems overhead and compute limits remain.
evidence: Section 4.2 Table 1 reports Pass@1 across AIME, MATH-500, AMC, and Minerva for OLMo-3-1025-7B and Qwen2.5-Math-7B comparing GRPO, B3PO, M3PO, C3PO, and action-space baselines.
Section 4.3 Figure 3 reports zero-advantage group rescue and malformed/incorrect rollout rates relative to GRPO.
Section 4.4 Figure 4 reports reward and accuracy curves on LiveCodeBench-v6, with C3PO outperforming other methods.
Section 5 and Table 2 ablate ESS lambda, MC sample count M, chunk size N, and Hessian initialization.
Appendix A provides hyperparameters, FLOPs, and per-step wall-clock times; Section 7 states limitations including compute constraints and approximately 1.5x wall-clock overhead.

arxiv:2608.09802.rationale: Strongly relevant to coding agents, code generation, and evaluation/benchmarks. The paper contributes a multilingual refactoring benchmark with detailed curation and quantitative results, but rigor is limited by unverifiable expert-curation claims, no significance testing or limitations section, uneven language coverage (TypeScript from only 2 repos), and behavior analysis limited to two models.
evidence: Abstract reports 170 instances, seven languages, and best model 41.2% resolve rate.
Section 3.2 Stage 3 describes filtering from 29,782 candidates to 170 and manual review of overly narrow/broad tests.
Section 5.1 Table 3 provides per-model/scaffold resolve rates, steps, and costs.
Appendix A Table 5 shows TypeScript has 28 instances from only 2 repositories, indicating limited language-level diversity.
Section 5.2 behavior analysis uses only two representative models and descriptive CDFs without statistical testing.
Section 6 Conclusion lacks a limitations section and does not report significance or repeated-run variability.

arxiv:2608.09801.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging and pure computer vision object-detection application for mammography; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/alignment methodology. The work compares DETR backbones in a controlled setup and reports quantitative metrics, but it is an incremental domain application with limited statistical evidence and strictly capped relevance at 0.20.

arxiv:2608.09799.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM coding agents, code generation, agent evaluation, and prompting/history sensitivity. Introduces specification-path sensitivity and paired CPV measurement with controlled histories, audits, and randomized execution. However, evidence is bounded by five curated Python PR tasks, incomplete blocks and attrition, so claims support tested behavior rather than general population prevalence or internal mechanism.
evidence: Abstract: 35 of 100 complete blocks that succeed on the direct specification fail on at least one equivalent history.
Results: any-CPV task-macro estimate is 36.4% with 95% CI 25.6–45.1%.
Experimental Design: 1,470 planned rows cross five task families, seven model deployments, two scaffolds, seven conditions, and three repeats.
Threats to Validity: only five task/PR-family clusters and 127 of 210 complete core-history blocks, limiting external and statistical validity.

arxiv:2608.09798.rationale: Out of scope as a pure domain bioinformatics application: FlowGRN infers gene regulatory networks from scRNA-seq data via conditional flow matching and dynGENIE3, with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/RAG/prompting or language methodology. Research quality is moderate: standard BEELINE benchmark and ablations, but several performance differences are small or within standard deviations, and applicability is domain-specific. Code/data availability is stated.
evidence: Section 6.3 Table 2 shows mixed top-tier performance with many overlapping standard deviations.
Section 6.6 Table 6 ablation differences are largely within standard deviations.
Data and Code Availability states public data and a GitHub code repository.

arxiv:2608.09793.rationale: Quantum key distribution security analysis with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/AI-safety relevance. The paper contains domain-specific mathematical proofs and satellite QKD estimates but lacks ML baselines, ablations, and generalizable AI methodology; out of scope under the stated rubric.

arxiv:2608.09792.rationale: Domain-specific corpus linguistics/accessibility study comparing UK and US audio description. It uses NLP parsing and a small BERT scene-boundary model, but does not address core preferences such as LLMs, Japanese NLP, reasoning, agents, RAG, or safety. Quantitative evidence is descriptive rather than a machine learning contribution, and overall scope is out of preference range.

Quantitative statistical comparisons and a small human evaluation provide some evidence, but no code/data availability, limited ablations, and inconsistencies in human-evaluation reporting weaken rigor and reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.09782.rationale: Pure computer vision low-light RAW burst enhancement challenge report with no LLM/language/reasoning/agent methodology; out of scope per rubric and capped at 0.20. It provides a clear evaluation protocol and quantitative leaderboard, but task-specific novelty/generalizability is limited and method descriptions are largely self-reported.

arxiv:2608.09779.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM/RAG/reasoning QA and knowledge grounding. Method is a modest extension of existing hybrid KG+RAG approaches such as HybridContextQA and Think-on-Graph, with LLM-guided traversal and clue expansion. Quantitative comparisons across four LLMs and two QA datasets support the main claim, but evidence is weakened by no significance testing, dev-only evaluation, and an inconsistency in ConditionalQA subset counts. Code and implementation details improve reproducibility, though limitations are not explicitly discussed.
evidence: Table 1 in Section 6 reports F1 scores for KGCaRe versus baselines across Mistral, Mixtral, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4o on ConditionalQA and HotpotQA.
Appendix 8.1 states ConditionalQA has 271 questions after removing unanswerable questions but also lists 143 Yes/No, 102 Span, and 63 Conditional pairs, which sum inconsistently.
Section 11.2 provides implementation details, including max_depth=3 and similarity_top_k=10, with no hyperparameter search.
Section 11.3 provides experimental environment details and a public code repository link.

arxiv:2608.09778.rationale: Primarily an embodied AI/robotic manipulation application using off-the-shelf Qwen3-VL, SAM3, and AnyGrasp; no language-model methodology or NLP contribution, so treated as out-of-scope and capped near 0.20. Integration is incremental, with limited physical trials, partial offline baseline alignment, no ablations or runtime profiling, and no code/data release.
evidence: Section V-B reports 83.4% mIoU on manually labeled objects and a four-object PartField comparison (RoboSeg 86.7% vs PartField 83.2%).
Section V-D reports 24 physical trials with 21/24 physical successes, 24/24 task-part contacts, and 21/24 combined task successes.
Section V-C Table I reports aggregate geometry metrics comparing kinematic poses and RGB-D odometry.
Section VI acknowledges limitations including 24 physical trials, small object set, incomplete metric-frame alignment, and absence of component-level runtime profiling.

arxiv:2608.09775.rationale: Air quality forecasting is a pure domain application without LLM/language methodology, so preference relevance is very low despite incidental use of attention/state-space components. The proposed combination of normalization routing and dual-stream state modeling has moderate novelty but largely assembles existing techniques. Evaluation is reasonably broad across cities and pollutants, but lacks standard deviations, significance testing, and code availability, and ablations are not fully isolated. This keeps the weighted score below the out-of-scope ceiling.
evidence: Abstract: proposes AirFlow, a pollutant-aware dual-stream framework using statistic-guided normalization routing and hierarchical dual-stream state modeling.
Section 4.2: reports AirFlow ranks first in 34 of 36 comparisons with RMSE reductions up to 11.11%.
Section 4.3: ablation table reports full model RMSE 14.42, MAE 7.47, R2 0.8513 on Beijing PM2.5.
Section 5: limitations cite only limited external covariates and do not discuss statistical uncertainty.
Appendix A.1: provides hyperparameters and software environment but no code release link.

arxiv:2608.09774.rationale: Pure medical imaging/computer vision paper: C^2A couples class-specific spatial attention with a label co-occurrence graph for multi-label chest X-ray classification. No LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, agent, or language methodology is present, so preference relevance is severely limited and the out-of-scope cap applies. Method is incremental over GCG/attention baselines and evaluated only on CheXpert five-task subset; some formal analysis and ablations exist but no confidence intervals or external validation.
evidence: Abstract: proposes C^2A for multi-label chest X-ray classification
Section 3.1: evaluation on CheXpert five competition tasks
Table 1: reports macro-mean AUROC and efficiency metrics against CBAM, Triplet, GC, and GCG

arxiv:2608.11267.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/representation geometry audit using skin-lesion datasets and no LLM/NLP language methodology. The statistical auditing is moderately careful, but single architecture, small n=13, and no independent replication limit evidence and generalizability.

Section 2.2: datasets are ISIC 2018 and PAD-UFES-20 skin lesion data.
Section 4.4: reports limitations including single architecture, n=13 checkpoints, and no independent domain replication.

arxiv:2608.09772.rationale: Relevant multimodal LVLM benchmark evaluating pragmatic sarcasm detection with CoT and shortcut diagnostics. The controlled relation-level design is a useful contribution but domain-specific and partly text-solvable; rigor is moderate due to limited human validation, no significance testing, and some perturbation validity concerns.

Table 1 reports Qwen2.5-VL-7B zero-shot P accuracy 13.9, M accuracy 99.3, paired accuracy 13.4, and grouped accuracy 5.6.
Table 2 reports Qwen2.5-VL-7B zero-shot P-M AUROC 90.0 while paired accuracy is only 13.4, showing threshold-independent separation.
Table 3 reports LLaVA-v1.6-7B M accuracy falls from 85.9 to 9.4 after OCR injection.
Section 3.4 reports caption-only BERT achieves 99.6% item accuracy and human evaluation reaches Cohen's kappa 0.618 with 77.5% agreement.

arxiv:2608.09771.rationale: Out-of-scope pure robot manipulation/VLA paper; only incidental frozen T5-small language conditioning and a Mixture-of-Transformers policy backbone, so LLM/NLP relevance is minimal despite embodied results. The action-grounded latent objectives are incremental over JEPA/VLA-JEPA/DeFI-style work, and the paper has reasonable benchmarks and ablations but limited scale/embodiment and no code release.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports SLIM achieves 97.5% on LIBERO, 77.45% on zero-shot LIBERO-Plus, and 4.556 average sequence length on CALVIN ABC->D.
Section 4.3 reports Stage-1 masked trajectory learning improves over Stage-2-only and EMA removal drops LIBERO-Plus from 77.45% to 66.82%.
Appendix A.4 documents optimizer, learning rates, batch sizes, and training epochs.

arxiv:2608.09768.rationale: Relevant mainly through AI safety/robustness and training-time constrained optimization, but not connected to LLMs, language modeling, agents, or other high-weight preferences. The paper is technically coherent with formal inner-outer chance-constraint approximations and finite-sample certificates, and it includes broad baseline comparisons across tabular and image datasets. However stress-test evidence is often summarized in figures without full numerical tables, no code is provided, and generalizability is limited to scalar-confidence classification.
evidence: Section 5.2, Table 3/Table 4: ReliableNet attains 5/5 Clopper-Pearson certifications across six datasets while all baselines fail at least one seed.
Section 5.3.2, Figure 2: ReliableNet reports lowest AURC on Adult, German Credit, ColoredMNIST, and CIFAR-10 under stress, with exact values in figure captions.
Section 6 Limitations: scalar confidence classification only; larger-scale and foundation-model settings not studied; high-dimensional surrogate certificate can be conservative.

arxiv:2608.09767.rationale: Out of scope: audio/articulatory rtMRI speech classification without language methodology or LLM/NLP components. Minor Speech & Audio and Medical & Healthcare AI relevance only. The work has baselines and multiple protocols, but the filtered dataset is small and teacher-supervision gains are modest.
evidence: Abstract: real-time MRI vocal-tract articulation with audio-derived PhonoQ/WavLM/HuBERT representations; no LLM/language modeling.
Section II-E: final filtered subset contains 12 usable speakers and 16 speech tasks.
Table II: contour-only teacher-supervision gains are modest (+1.5 to +2.3 macro-F1).

arxiv:2608.09766.rationale: Relevant as a machine translation evaluation benchmark with locale-contrastive design; moderate novelty and rigor. Strong empirical scope (32 models, human co-creation) but contamination conclusions are suggestive and manual error analysis is limited to Chinese-to-English by one annotator.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: benchmarks 32 open-weight models and reports MT-specialised models are less robust, potential FLORES overfitting, and better translation of US content.
Page 2 Section 2: describes a three-stage localisation pipeline over FLORES using named entity-rich instance selection, LLM-assisted paraphrasing, and human annotation.
Page 5 Section 3.2: defines BLEU, chrF, mean pairwise delta metrics, and false-positive/false-negative locale-specific word recall.

Page 7 Table 3: aggregate results show average delta BLEU of -0.49 and delta chrF of -1.10; aya-expanse-8b and Seed-X-PPO-7B show BLEU drops >8.
Page 9-10 Section 5: manual error analysis of Chinese-to-English outputs finds named entity errors most frequent and >50% of all recorded errors.

arxiv:2608.09765.rationale: Multimodal video-language/audio-description generation and evaluation paper using Qwen/Gemini LLMs; not pure CV/audio because it centers language generation, prompting, and QA-based evaluation. Preference relevance is moderate since it maps mainly to multimodal AI, video, speech/audio, LLM evaluation, and datasets rather than core LLM/NLP methodology. Novelty is solid: joint when/what AD formulation, multi-reference dataset, and adapted temporal/QA metrics. Rigor is good with baselines, ablations, significance tests, and acknowledged limitations, though no human subjective evaluation of generated AD. Evidence strength is supported by quantitative tables and appendix analyses. Generalizability is limited to English movie AD. Reproducibility is moderate: prompts and hyperparameters are provided, but full-movie data is restricted and some APIs/models are proprietary.

arxiv:2608.09764.rationale: Out-of-scope pure PDE/scientific neural operator without language methodology; only tangential Transformer/efficiency relevance. The paper has domain-specific strengths in optimal-transport latent assignment, benchmarks, ablations, and code, but overall relevance to LLM/NLP priorities is minimal and score is capped at 0.20.

arxiv:2608.09763.rationale: Relevant to training/optimization and efficiency preferences, but not core LLM/NLP topics. The matched spectral oracle and variance-lag analysis are incremental over prior Muon/K-FAC/Mousse/FISMO work. Empirical evidence is small-scale and partly exploratory, with one-seed modular-addition screens and training-loss-only endpoints; no code release is claimed.

arxiv:2608.09762.rationale: Pure real-world robot manipulation RL paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology, so as pure robotics it is out of scope and capped below 0.20. It includes quantitative comparisons and implementation details, but lacks ablations and limitations.

arxiv:2608.09752.rationale: Pure medical imaging/computer vision multi-label fundus classification without language/LLM methodology is out of scope per rubric (cap <=0.20). Sparse MoE and attention provide slight transformer-adjacent relevance, but there is no language modeling, prompting, agents, or NLP. Evaluation includes patient-disjoint 5-fold ODIR results, ablations, and JSD permutation tests, but claimed baseline significance tests are not shown, no code/data availability is stated, and scope is a single retinal dataset.

arxiv:2608.09749.rationale: Out-of-scope quantum many-body physics paper on stabilizer Renyi entropy and fermionic SPT transitions. arxiv:2608.09748.rationale: Paper is a formal ontology for decentralization in distributed/blockchain/federated systems; topics do not substantively match the requested LLM/NLP/agents/code/safety methodology. Formal definitions and proofs are relatively strong, and the implementation supports reproducibility, but evidence is limited to toy instantiations and ad hoc metrics, with negligible preference relevance.
evidence: Abstract: proposes a graph-based ontology defining decentralization with novel metrics Void Tolerance and Imperviousness, applied to federated learning and blockchain.
Section VIII: Core ontology introduces primitive concepts System, Topology, Subject and relations, with graph-realistic commitments.
Section IX: Logical layer provides formal semantics, axiomatization, and proofs for consistency, disjointness, satisfiability, and entailment.
Section XI: Analytical layer defines subject-specific metrics and evaluates them on federated learning and blockchain instantiations.
Section XII: Implementation describes a browser-based application with deterministic simulation and computational complexity.
Section XIV: Limitations acknowledge ad hoc metric construction and graph-realist scope, limiting empirical validation.

arxiv:2608.09745.rationale: Core LLM training/on-policy self-distillation paper using Rényi divergence and reference anchoring; highly relevant to LLM, reasoning, RL, and code. Novelty is moderate, mainly combining existing techniques. Theory is explicitly limited to fixed rollout contexts.
evidence: Abstract: describes SR-OPSD and reports experiments across scientific evaluation, mathematical reasoning, and coding generation with multiple LLMs.
Section 4.1: Table 1 reports Avg@16 results on SciKnowEval for Qwen3-8B and Olmo3-7B-Instruct compared with GRPO, SDPO, and SR-OPSD.

arxiv:2608.09742.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM fine-tuning, LoRA/PEFT, and NLP. The adaptive factor-sharing selection is moderately novel relative to prior fixed Share-A/Share-B methods. Empirical coverage is broad across GLUE/GSM8K, ranks, heterogeneity, and baselines, but no significance testing or explicit limitations are provided, and no code release is claimed.
evidence: Section V, Table I: FedAS-LoRA reaches 90.77% average GLUE accuracy, 0.93 points above FedSA-LoRA.
Section V-B: On GSM8K with LLaMA3-8B, FedAS-LoRA achieves 56.28% accuracy vs LoRA 55.14% and FFA-LoRA 54.51%.
Appendix E, Table VIII: RSS decisions match the empirically better fixed strategy in all 33 strict accuracy cases and 5 ties across 38 evaluated settings.
Section IV-A: RSS is computed from frozen LLM representations with null and bootstrap 95th-percentile thresholds (Equations 7-9).
Section V-C3 and Table IV: Evaluation spans LoRA ranks r=2,4,8,16.

arxiv:2608.09740.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM code generation, AI safety, and evaluation, with a controlled empirical methodology. Contributions are moderately novel but prior self-debugging/repair work is close. Rigor and evidence strength are limited by small task counts, descriptive/non-significant comparisons, and reliance on constructed oracles; generalizability is bounded to Python and small components. Reproducibility is comparatively strong via a detailed release package.
evidence: Abstract: reports 2,705 trajectories, 31 task instances, three secure-code benchmarks, 16 CWE categories, two model families, +19.3 pp average improvement in 7/9 conditions, structured feedback repairs 80 with 0 joint regressions.
Section 5.2, Table 4: M triggers 252/465 cells and repairs 80 with no joint regression; fixed raw feedback repairs 83 with 3 joint regressions.
Section 7 Threats to Validity: only 31 benchmark task instances, no Holm-adjusted comparison below 0.05, Python-only tasks, and remote API outputs may not be reproducible.
Data Availability: anonymized replication package includes frozen protocols, oracles, sandbox runners, prompts, hashes, raw responses, and the 2,705 trajectory records.

arxiv:2608.09735.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/clinical neural rendering application for digital hand goniometry; no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, or language methodology. Modest clinical evidence with Bland-Altman and hill-climbing ablation but small n and limited generalizability.
evidence: Section III-B: final evaluation on n=20 hands with exclusions for severe self-occlusion, incomplete multi-view coverage, or segmentation failures.
Section III-D: hill climbing narrowed range of agreement by 14% compared with no adjustment (61.2°).
Table I: Bland-Altman analysis for radius/iterations; r=0.015 with 20 iterations had bias 1.08, upper LOA 27.43, lower LOA -25.27.
Sections III-E and III-F: per-finger and per-joint analyses show small finger bias +5.71°, DIP bias +9.01°, and MCP bias -4.73°.
Section III-G: limitations include segmentation failures, MediaPipe anatomical artifacts, and manual goniometry variability; future work for broader poses, skin tones, and pathology.

arxiv:2608.09732.rationale: Strongly in-scope for LLM agents, AI safety, and red-teaming. Claims of high ASR are supported by tables but limited by absent statistical significance, sparse dataset/scanner details, no limitations, and missing appendices.

arxiv:2608.09731.rationale: Pure robotics/teleoperation paper on task-aware multi-view adaptive video streaming. arxiv:2608.09730.rationale: Low preference relevance: this is an embodied robotics/VLA method using a pretrained VLM and video world model, not core LLM/NLP. evidence: Section 4.2 and Table 1: World Tokens reports 98.2% LIBERO average and 61.85 ms per chunk.

arxiv:2608.09727.rationale: Pure quantum error correction / magic state distillation paper with no AI/ML, NLP, LLM, reasoning, agent, or multimodal language methodology. arxiv:2608.09721.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging radiogenomics application using PET/CT CNN classification; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/alignment methodology. arxiv:2608.09719.rationale: Out-of-scope HCI/educational-technology study using AI-generated pedagogical avatars for history learning. The study is a small within-subjects HCI experiment (N=36) with counterbalancing and mixed methods, but generalizability and technical reproducibility are limited, and no language model contributions are present.
evidence: Abstract: states a within-subjects study (N=36) comparing a Digital Self agent with a non-self pedagogical agent and reports enhanced experiential measures but no improved immediate learning outcomes.
Section 3.3: describes a counterbalanced within-subjects design with content/condition and order counterbalancing.

arxiv:2608.09717.rationale: Relevant LLM evaluation and bias study with repeated multi-model ratings and human comparison, but limited stimulus diversity, social-psychology domain focus, and constrained generalizability temper the score.
evidence: Abstract: reports 34 LLMs rating 12 persona profiles across three runs, matched gender-presentation tests, and 198 human participants.
Study 1 Results: reports mean ICC .965, tier effect F(2,66)=800.94 p<.001, and Kendall's W=.948 across models.
Study 2 Results: reports no significant gender-presentation effect, F(1,13)=0.03 p=.876, and pronoun-only F(2,26)=1.52 p=.238.
Study 3 Results: reports human-LLM profile correlations of Pearson r=.981 (Original) and r=.979 (Gender-swapped), with LLM ratings more extreme for attractive/unattractive profiles.
Limitations and Future Research: acknowledges only six persona identities in direct comparison, controlled stimuli, no behavioral outcomes, and limited gender/intersectional cues.

arxiv:2608.09715.rationale: Pure domain application in simulation-based nursing education with no AI/ML/NLP/LLM methodology: PULSE is a real-time annotation tool for debriefing. It does not cover any listed preference area, so relevance is zero and the overall score is capped below 0.20. evidence: Abstract: 'A real-time annotation tool to support debriefing, called PULSE, was co-designed with nursing educators.'
Abstract: 'Outcomes were assessed using the Debriefing Assessment for Simulation in Healthcare (DASH) student survey and a follow-up instructor interview.'
Field Study Methods: 'One experienced nursing faculty member and her university-assigned class group of six pre-licensure nursing students... participated in the study.'

Limitations and Future Research: '...sample size was small and lacked diversity... ceiling effects in the DASH survey data... within-subjects study design may have influenced results...'

fallback:2e60040f15d46f81.rationale: Abstract-only blog-style article about using AI transcription tools for meeting minutes; no LLM/NLP methodology, experiments, or quantitative evidence. arxiv:2608.09712.rationale: Pure stochastic calculus/probability paper on nonlinear mean-reverting diffusions and Novikov criteria. arxiv:2608.09707.rationale: Out-of-scope operations-research paper on input convex neural networks as surrogates in mathematical optimisation. arxiv:2608.09706.rationale: Relevant LLM/code-generation inference-time selection method for text-to-CAD, but domain-specific and mostly applies established MBR/self-consistency ideas. arxiv:2608.09703.rationale: Relevant LLM/transformer/training/inference efficiency paper with no Japanese-specific angle. evidence: Section 3.1 Experimental Setup describes training a 3B nested suite (500M/1.5B/3B) on 35B FineWeb-Edu tokens with a matched Vanilla baseline; Table 1 lists architectures.

Section 3.2.1 (Table 2) reports zero-shot accuracy on ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, OpenBookQA, PIQA, and Winogrande, plus OOD byte perplexity, showing near-parity within 0.5 average accuracy points of token-matched baselines.

The paper states checkpoints and a HuggingFace transformers-compatible implementation are released at https://huggingface.co/nthngdy/matryoshka-3B, and provides detailed hyperparameters and compute formulas in Appendices A-B.

arxiv:2608.09698.rationale: Relevant LLM/graph-RAG HCI writing system, not out-of-scope. arxiv:2608.09696.rationale: Highly relevant LLM-agent methodology for scientific discovery with Bayesian experiment design, but novelty is largely incremental over ModelSMC/SMC-S and validation is synthetic-benchmark only. arxiv:2608.09692.rationale: Pure time-series generative-model evaluation with no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, agent, or language methodology. Within its niche it has careful matched protocols, five seeds, and a permutation control, but it is outside scope and capped at 0.20.

arxiv:2608.09690.rationale: RNN-based multi-view sequence-learning framework with no substantive LLM/Japanese/transformer/NLP/alignment focus. arxiv:2608.09688.rationale: Pure computer vision/adversarial training on long-tailed CIFAR/TinyImageNet image classification, with no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, agent, or language methodology. arxiv:2608.09687.rationale: Out of scope for the stated LLM/NLP-centered preferences: this is a domain federated learning paper for LEO satellite remote-sensing classification with CNN models, not a language-model or NLP contribution. arxiv:2608.09685.rationale: Pure recommender-system domain application with only incidental transformer decoder use; no LLM/NLP methodology in scope. arxiv:2608.09683.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application: deep learning for tropical cyclone missing data imputation. No LLM/language, reasoning, prompting, safety, agents, or core alignment/interpretability topics; only weak Scientific AI relevance. arxiv:2608.09682.rationale: Directly relevant multimodal VLM/agentic tool-use reasoning paper. arxiv:2608.09681.rationale: Pure symplectic geometry and geometric quantization paper with no AI/ML, NLP, or language-model methodology; out of scope for the specified preferences. Mathematical category-theoretic content is present but irrelevant to the requested topics.

arxiv:2608.09672.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/domain application with no language-model, NLP, reasoning, or agent methodology; only a plug-and-play zero-shot CNN denoiser for MPI super-resolution.
