Section 3.5 states OpenMPI real-data parameters were selected by visual inspection and no ground-truth quantitative comparison is available.
Section 1 states the GitHub link 'will be provided upon publication,' leaving availability unverifiable.
Section 4 mentions future transformer-based zero-shot denoisers, but the current method uses a CNN/DRUNet.

arxiv:2608.10050.rationale: Out-of-scope financial/accounting domain application with only incidental LLM use (Qwen3 embeddings and zero-shot Claude baseline); core contribution is offline policy learning, not language methodology. CAR-PL is an incremental action-wise R-learner with support shrinkage. Evaluation relies on model-assisted observational scores without prospective or deployed-outcome validation, and proprietary data limits reproducibility.
evidence: Section 3.1 describes proprietary SMB accounting data and Qwen3-Embedding state representation
Section 4.3 defines CAR-PL as an action-wise R-learner with support shrinkage
Section 6 reports KPI-specific point-estimate leaders under a shared model-assisted scorer
Section 7.5 notes proprietary accounting records and detector thresholds
Section 7.6 acknowledges observational reliance, fitted nuisance models, and lack of prospective validation

arxiv:2608.09669.rationale: Pure computer vision fairness auditing for face analysis, with no LLM/NLP/agent language methodology. Although it touches AI safety fairness, it is out of scope under the rubric and capped low. Within domain, it provides structured audits, datasets, mitigation, and limitations, but evidence is domain-specific and not relevant to the requested LLM/NLP focus.
evidence: Abstract: fairness evaluation in computer vision and evaluation on gender classification using ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 across FairFace, CelebA, UTKFace.
§3.1 defines CIFA as a contextual-intersectional fairness auditing framework for visual models.
§4.5 Table 3 reports worst-group gaps up to 26.43% with no language-model component.

arxiv:2608.09666.rationale: In scope due to LLM/agentic evaluation methodology despite visual-generation target. Strong agent/tool/evaluation relevance, but contribution is incremental and quantitative support is mixed: cost reductions are clear, tier-prediction exact accuracy is often weak, and open-ended evaluation is mostly qualitative.
evidence: Abstract: proposes Evaluation Agent with multi-round tool-grounded loop and EA-CoT-10K / EA-3B.
Section III-B: describes Plan Agent, PromptGen Agent, visual generation sampling, and Evaluation Toolkit including VLM-based VQA.
Section III-C: describes EA-CoT-10K construction and EA-3B fine-tuning from Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct with LLaMA-Factory.
Table IV: reports cost comparison showing substantially lower wall-clock time and sample counts for Evaluation Agent versus VBench/T2I-CompBench.
Table V: shows Open-EA exact/within-one tier accuracy across in-domain and out-of-domain T2V generators with partial transfer.

arxiv:2608.09661.rationale: Out-of-scope quantum Variational Quantum Linear Solver/CFD paper with no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology; only weak Scientific AI/simulation relevance. The LLM mention is assistance acknowledgment, not method. Within its domain it provides benchmark comparisons, but lacks ML-style ablations/statistical rigor and no code release.
evidence: Section IV-E reports >10,000x per-iteration speedup for SVD-based decomposition at 8 qubits.
Section III-F lists PennyLane, PyTorch, and SciPy versions but no code/data availability statement.
Table I and Section IV-D report weak correlation between expressibility/entanglement metrics and VQLS convergence.

arxiv:2608.09659.rationale: The paper describes a domain-specific language for hybrid quantum-classical meta-solver workflows. It is outside all weighted AI/ML preference areas: no language models, NLP, agents, reasoning, or transformer methods. Within its own domain it has modest design novelty relative to graph-based workflow tools, but lacks quantitative baselines, ablations, or systematic evaluation; evidence is limited to a two-instance VRP case study. Capped at 0.20 due to out-of-scope domain.
evidence: Abstract: proposes a domain-specific language for hybrid quantum-classical Meta-Solver Strategies.
Section 5: case study executes the same Meta-Solver Strategy on two VRP instances but explicitly does not evaluate performance.

arxiv:2608.09658.rationale: Out-of-scope pure robotics/computer-vision/HRC paper with no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, prompting, agent, or language methodology. It reports empirical 5G network and YOLO11-obb CV results across two sites, but relevance to the requested preferences is minimal; rigor is limited by hardware-network interoperability failures, lack of ablations and baselines, and no code/data availability.
evidence: Section V-C reports mAP@50-95 of 97.74 ± 0.10% and mean inference time of 12.5 ms.
Section V-B and Table I report network KPIs such as response time, jitter, throughput, and MTU across different 5G deployments.
Section V-D acknowledges network interoperability, occlusion, and battery constraints.

arxiv:2608.09656.rationale: Out of scope pure computer vision/embodied AI visual query localization; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, or language methodology. CV-domain engineering has ablations but does not match target preferences.
evidence: Abstract: defines tasks as VQL-2D/VQL-3D in egocentric videos, with no language model or text methodology.
Section 1 Introduction: frames motivation around embodied AI, robotics, AR/VR, and human visual hierarchy, not language tasks.
Section 3.4 Regional Adaptation Module: uses a Pyramid Vision Transformer backbone for dense visual feature fusion, not language transformer methodology.
Table 1: reports Ego4D-VQ2D localization metrics, not NLP/LLM benchmarks.

arxiv:2608.09654.rationale: Relevant to GUI agents and multimodal LLM use, but primarily a visual-grounding application. Novelty is moderate. Rigor is weakened by contradiction between claimed regression-free design and DINO regression losses, lack of shown ablations/limitations, and suspicious table anomalies. Evidence is mostly aggregate benchmarks without statistical tests.
evidence: Abstract: claims over 20% improvement on ScreenSpot-Pro and over 15% on Mind2Web.
Section 3.2.1: uses DINO detector with L1/GIoU regression loss despite regression-free framing.
Section 4.1 Table 1: Fuyu and CogAgent rows are identical; Section 4 Table 4 shows Ours Operation F1 below SeeClick and QwenVL.

arxiv:2608.09653.rationale: Pure vehicle dynamics control/RL application, not LLM/NLP/agentic AI; only tangential relevance via reinforcement learning and curriculum learning. Incremental combination of known control and safety-filter techniques. Limited baselines, small result tables, and mixed generalization (worse on human-driver maneuver). No code/data release.
evidence: Section III-A describes curriculum stages, actions, states, and reward.
Section IV-C Table I reports RMSE baseline 2.72, CL w/ safety filter 1.44, CL w/o safety filter 2.41.
Section IV-F Table II reports Jturn 2.17 vs 2.44 baseline, human driver 5.67 vs 2.09 baseline.

arxiv:2608.09651.rationale: Out-of-scope automotive HIL fault-injection/dataset-generation paper. It mentions NLP only for future text-log root-cause analysis, with no LLM/language methodology or model evaluation. No baselines, ablations, or quantitative downstream results are provided.
evidence: Abstract: proposes HIL simulation and real-time Fault Injection to generate sequential and textual data including fault logs for ML applications during system validation.
Section 5 Result and Discussion: reports 40 experiments, 18 single-fault files, 30 simultaneous-fault files, and 50 CSV files collected; figures show qualitative system behavior only.
Section 6 Conclusion and Future Work: states future work will develop ML-based detection using collected data; no trained model or quantitative benchmark is presented.

arxiv:2608.09650.rationale: Moderately relevant via LLM rerankers, retrieval/reranking, and agentic prompt optimization, but tied to a narrow medical-insurance domain. The study is systematic (18-cell grid, Optuna, 5 seeds, held-out test) but incremental in novelty and limited to one dataset/organization; evidence is quantitative with limitations acknowledged.
evidence: §6.3 Table 2 reports MedCPT+ListNet no_freeze test NDCG@3 0.961±0.002 vs prompt-optimized Qwen3-Reranker-4B 0.936, a 2.5-2.6pp gap with 5 seeds.
§3.2 reports human validation on 100 sampled rankings with top-1 acceptance 92% and 97% by two experts and Cohen's κ=0.52.
§6.2 and Appendix B report Optuna tuning (50 trials per config) and final multi-seed training details.
Limitations states the dataset is from one organization, labels inherit GPT-4o teacher bias, and only two cross-encoder backbones and one instruction reranker are compared.

arxiv:2608.09643.rationale: The paper sits in LLM interpretability and code security: it trains linear probes on open-weight code LLMs and evaluates zero-shot on held-out CVEs. Relevant to LLM, interpretability, code, and safety/evaluation, but not to Japanese NLP or core language modeling. Methodological strengths include project-grouped CV, held-out CWE evaluation, multiple models, and paired statistical tests; however n=152 training/eval and 147/234 out-of-distribution pairs are small, win rates are modest (61-69%), the probe advantage over chain-of-thought is narrow or not consistently significant, only Python/four CWEs are covered, and no code/exact prompts/data pipeline availability is stated.
evidence: Section 2: probes trained on four SVEN-Python CWEs and evaluated on 234 unseen PatchEval CVEs
Table 2: probe paired win-rate on 147 unseen single-function CVEs is 61.2-66.9% across five models
Section 3: prompted logit win-rates are mostly 33.6-57.8% and written verdicts tie on 72-97% of pairs
Limitations: only four SVEN CWEs with substantial Python coverage; Python only; paired comparison rather than calibrated detector
Appendix A.1: reports model, layer, pooling, GroupKFold AUC, and prompted baseline details

arxiv:2608.09638.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM reasoning, ToM, interpretability, and evaluation; presents a game-based 2x2 ToM benchmark with mechanistic ablations. Moderate rigor from 28 models, 408 balanced items, and probing/steering ablations, but limited generalizability due to single-game/self-played binary data.
evidence: Abstract: decomposes ToM into a 2x2 taxonomy and benchmarks 28 LLMs.
Table 1: reports accuracy and macro-F1 per ability plus a 34-item rules control.
§5.1 and Figure 4: probes recover 77-82% accuracy vs 62-70% from CoT output, supporting the expression-not-representation claim.

arxiv:2608.09637.rationale: Out-of-scope video diffusion distillation paper: no LLM/NLP/language-model methodology; focuses on two-step video generation with sCM/DMD experts. Although it uses RL (GRPO) and efficiency techniques, the topic is image/video diffusion without language methodology, so relevance is capped. Research quality is moderate with comparisons and ablations but limited to Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B and no code release.
evidence: Section 5.1: Experimental Setup uses Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B and exactly two sampling steps.
Table 1: Quantitative results compare sCM, DMD, rCM, DP-DMD, DUET, DUET+.
Section 5.4: Ablations for switch time and reward choice.
Appendix C: Training and evaluation configurations provided.

arxiv:2608.09636.rationale: Domain is fluorescence microscopy neuron segmentation/medical imaging, which is explicitly out-of-scope and capped at 0.20 despite multi-agent LLM tool use. The method shows some novelty but limited generalizability, no statistical testing or code/data availability in the supplied text.
evidence: Abstract: proposes NeuroRefiner, a multi-agent system for 3D fluorescence microscopy neuron segmentation refinement.
Section 4.2 and Table 1: report quantitative benchmark gains but no confidence intervals or significance tests.
Section 5 Limitation: acknowledges 2D MIP loses depth information, limiting 3D topological error localization.
Section 4.1: implementation details are given but no code or data availability statement is present.

arxiv:2608.09634.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application: generative travel/POI recommendation, not an LLM/NLP/agent paper. Weak preference match via transformer/attention mechanisms only. Architecture has ablations and offline/online results, but evidence is single-domain, production A/B is unverifiable, and no code availability is shown. Capped at 0.20 under domain-application rule.
evidence: Section 1: Inspired by Large Language Models (LLMs), the community has moved toward Generative Recommendation; IntHQ is a multi-task generative recommender for travel recommendation.
Section 4.2.1: IntTravel dataset contains about 4.1 billion interactions from 163 million users over 7.3 million POIs and covers four coupled tasks.
Table 1: IntHQ outperforms all encoder baselines on all ten metrics under each multi-task head.
Section 4.6.2: IntHQ improved UVCTR by 1.60% relative in online A/B tests on Amap.

arxiv:2608.09633.rationale: Out-of-scope face presentation attack detection application using vision encoders/VLMs and LoRA, with no language-modeling/NLP methodology contribution; therefore capped at 0.20 despite internal quantitative benchmarking. The paper is systematic but limited to single-source MCIO protocols and lacks broader methodological or domain-generalizable value for the stated preferences.
evidence: Section 4.3, Table 2: zero-shot VLM PAD remains near chance (35-50% ACER)
Section 4.4, Table 3: LoRA adaptation yields below 2% intra-dataset ACER in most cases
Section 4.6, Table 4: cross-dataset ACER remains 19.8-42.6% across 32 adapted encoders
Section 4.8, Figure 4: adapted embeddings cluster by acquisition domain rather than attack class
Section 5: limitation notes MCIO-only, no deepfake attacks, single-source protocol, LoRA only

arxiv:2608.09630.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/scientific domain application: UDA and multitask balancing for CTAO telescope image analysis, with no LLM/NLP/agent/safety methodology. Although the paper has ablations, multiple seeds on digit benchmarks, and open code, relevance to stated preferences is marginal and capped at 0.20 overall. CTAO results lack uncertainty estimates and generalizability is domain-specific.
evidence: Abstract and Section 1 frame the work as unsupervised domain adaptation for multitask image analysis on CTAO LST simulations, not language-model methodology.
Section 4.3 Tables 2-3 report mean accuracy over ten seeds for digit domain adaptation; Sections 5.4.4-5.4.5 Tables 7-9 report CTAO ablations for DANN, DeepCORAL, and DeepJDOT.
Section 6 notes limitations: simulations only, DeepJDOT scaling issues, and no real telescope data results yet.
Section 1 and Abstract state code and results are available as open-source resources on Zenodo [13].

arxiv:2608.09629.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents and optimization; reframes prescribed pipelines as a question of where optimization responsibility lives. Novelty is moderate because it builds on existing LM-as-optimizer and self-evolving-agent work. Rigor is limited by single-run evaluations, no error bars, and token-budget accounting that is not exactly matched. Evidence is quantitative and transparent but lacks statistical testing. Generalizability is moderate across benchmarks and target models but tied to one frontier optimizer and skill-optimization artifacts. Reproducibility is moderate given detailed protocols but no code or prompt release.
evidence: Table 2 reports sealed-split scores across SearchQA, SpreadsheetBench, OfficeQA, and LiveMath under the frontier optimizer.
Section 3.1 states OEO records 7 wins and 1 tie against SkillOpt and 5 wins against GEPA, with 34.3% median target-interaction token use.
Table 4 shows the optimizer-capability ladder with weak OEO blocked and medium SkillOpt leading.
Appendix A.1 states each reported numerical score corresponds to one completed optimization run and describes sealed splits.

arxiv:2608.09628.rationale: Pure aerospace/RL domain application without LLM, language, or foundation-model methodology triggers the domain-application cap. The paper reports deterministic 1,000-run comparisons and provides open-source/config details, but relevance to the preferred LLM/NLP/agent topics is minimal. Rigor is limited by reporting inconsistencies (Table II success rate vs Table III success/fuel-depleted counts) and citation-reference mismatches, while evidence has no statistical variation or ablations.
evidence: Abstract: reports 97.5% collision avoidance success and baseline success rates of 20.7% (rule-based) and 27.5% (impulsive).
Section V Results, Table II and Table III: Table II reports PPO 2.50% collision rate/25 collisions and 97.50% success rate, while Table III lists PPO Success 970, Collision 25, Fuel Depleted 5.
Section III-A3: text credits 'Kazemi et al. (2024)' but reference [35] is authored by Mu et al.; text credits 'Smith et al. (2024)' but reference [44] is authored by Solomon and Păduraru.
Section VI Limitations: acknowledges perfect sensing, full noise-free state knowledge, simplified thrust model, and lack of formal safety guarantees.
Appendix B Tables IX-X and Section IV-C2: provide evaluation/config details and describe shared seeds, per-episode logs, and telemetry exports.

arxiv:2608.09625.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application: quantum state tomography with diffusion models, only weak relevance via 'diffusion model' and 'scientific AI'. Some niche novelty in systematic parameterization study, but rigor is limited by mismatched training protocols (different learning rates and measurement-consistency losses), small validation scale (n=3 for correlation, 100 states), and inconsistent ordering claims without CFG. Reproducibility is only promised, not provided. Final score capped at or below 0.20 for pure domain application.
evidence: Section 4.2 Caveat: Bloch vs. Herm B comparison is not controlled; models used different measurement-consistency losses and different learning rates.
Section 4.5 Two-by-two cross-validation: varies lambda_meas but not the learning-rate difference; reports no-CFG ordering and CFG-induced reversal.
Section 5.5 Limitations: full experimental validation limited to d=4; learning rates differed between models.
Appendix D Reproducibility Statement: code and checkpoints will be made publicly available upon formal publication, not currently provided.

arxiv:2608.09624.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM AI safety, jailbreak evaluation, and interpretability. Strong matched factorial design with multiple measurement channels, targets, judges, and CIs; honest limitations. Weaknesses include automated judges, small positive counts in some cells, single greedy decode for primary outcomes, and many derived-channel results limited to Llama. Overall high-quality audit with robust evidence and controls.
evidence: Section 5.2 RQ1 reports harmful intent AUROC falls from 0.936 to 0.803 while wrapped harmful generation rises from 0.05 to 0.27, with outcome AUROC 0.220 (CI [0.109,0.343]).
Table 1 crosses native score sources and generators (Llama, Mistral, Qwen), reporting outcome AUROC with bootstrap 95% CIs, most below chance.
Section 5.3 Table 3 separates ranking, calibration, and threshold transfer under distribution shift, e.g., WildJailbreak AUROC 0.850 and ECE 0.366.
Appendix A includes ablations for readout sensitivity, norm-matched controls, and calibration; Section 6 acknowledges limitations such as automated judges and small positive counts.

arxiv:2608.09623.rationale: Pure kernel methods/theory paper on diffusion maps kernel ridge regression; no LLM/NLP/agent/safety/vision/speech relevance, only tangential scientific-mathematical ML foundations. Theorems and proofs are rigorous, but empirical validation is limited to synthetic manifolds and no code is provided.
evidence: Section 5.1 reports heat kernel estimation convergence on circle and flat torus, with DM error decreasing as N increases and plateauing.
Theorem 3.1 provides a uniform convergence bound for the empirical diffusion kernel to the heat kernel under manifold, uniform sampling, and bandwidth assumptions.
Theorem 4.1 states that the oracle inequality is valid for DMKRR via isometric isomorphism with the Gaussian RKHS and continuous embedding into a Matérn/Sobolev RKHS.
Appendix C.3 details semi-torus experiments where DMKRR generally achieves lower RMSE than Gaussian RBF KRR, though the gap narrows with higher ambient dimension.

arxiv:2608.09622.rationale: Out-of-scope domain-specific semiconductor reliability qualification with no LLM/language methodology. Uses established MCTS/EKF/planning methods; simulation is detailed but domain application and no hardware validation.
evidence: Section VII-D1 reports CY increasing from 20.4% to 54.2% across 500-iteration windows and 39.2% cumulative; Table V reports random baseline 16% CY and fixed-stress 22% CY.

Section VII-D10 reports ablations: removing the safety barrier raises catastrophe rate to 78%, removing early shaping reduces CY to 31%, and removing the per-epoch cost increases average test length by 25%.
Section VIII-E lists limitations including simulation-only validation, limited technology coverage, omitted degradation recovery, and computational cost.

fallback:c32f4790b15b1955.rationale: Abstract-only blog-style glossary article about AI-driven development and AI agents; it is not a research paper and provides no methods, baselines, ablations, results, or reproducible artifacts. Some topical mention of AI agents yields minimal preference relevance, but novelty, rigor, evidence, generalizability, and reproducibility are absent.

arxiv:2608.09620.rationale: Out-of-scope robotics/edge computer vision paper for this LLM/NLP-focused rubric: no language model, NLP, reasoning, prompting, retrieval, or safety methodology. It applies known split-inference/semantic communication ideas to fiducial marker processing in 5G Edge SLAM. Evaluation is limited: localization is reported on a single representative sample, and there is no full baseline comparison or ablation.
evidence: Section IV-C2 reports localization on a representative sample only
Section IV-C1 reports mean keypoint error over the test set
Section IV-B reports measured RTT and link model

arxiv:2608.09617.rationale: Peripheral relevance to the stated preferences: the paper uses reinforcement learning, a transformer policy, and scientific-AI benchmarks, but has no LLM/NLP/agent/alignment focus. The methodological combination is moderately novel over prior GFN-SR work, and the paper includes formalization, ablations, and benchmark comparisons, though statistical rigor is limited and generalization beyond symbolic regression is not demonstrated. Reproducibility is relatively strong due to code availability claims and detailed hyperparameters.
evidence: Section 3.2 defines the entropy-regularized RL and trajectory-balance objective used for posterior sampling.
Results, Table 1 reports synthetic posterior predictive metrics against PySIPS, including NLL, test R2, and R2PP.
Results, Fit Quality reports ERRLESS Feynman AUC 0.924 vs DSR 0.873, PhySO 0.893, and BSR 0.702.
Results, Blackbox benchmark reports ERRLESS AUC 0.350 vs BSR 0.19 and XGBoost 0.625.
Appendix D, Tables 6-8 report ablations for expression prior, training objective, and replay-buffer mixing.
Appendix B documents policy architecture, hyperparameters, and training details, and the abstract claims code availability.

arxiv:2608.09613.rationale: Pure computer vision paper on unified 4D reconstruction and point tracking via Optimal Transport and ODEs. It does not address LLMs, NLP, reasoning, agents, safety, or other core preferences; mentioning ViT/attention does not bring it into scope. The work has some domain-specific novelty and ablations, but evidence is self-reported and generalization/reproducibility are limited. Overall capped as out-of-scope.
evidence: Abstract: proposes Uni4R for unified continuous-time 4D reconstruction and point tracking using OT and ODE.
Section 3 Methodology: describes ViT encoder, Flow Matching Guided Decoder, and local velocity prediction.
Section 4 Experiments: reports point tracking, 4D reconstruction, continuous-time kinematic coherence, and ablations.

arxiv:2608.09610.rationale: Pure computer-vision lane detection using anchor-based detection and attention-style feature modules; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent methodology. Although the paper includes ablations and multiple lane benchmarks, it is out-of-scope under the rubric and capped near 0.20.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 1 reports VIL-100 F1@50 improvement from 89.97 to 91.28
Section 4.4, Table 4 provides sequential ablation of GHVT and LQAS
Section 4.5, Table 5 reports GHVT branch and stage placement ablations

arxiv:2608.09609.rationale: Pure photonics/metasurface fiber-optics paper with no relevance to LLMs, NLP, reasoning, agents, or other preferred topics. Experimental work appears substantive but is out of scope; relevance is zero and score is capped at or below 0.20.
evidence: Page 6, Figs. 4j-4k: measured angle-resolved transmission and reflection spectra of the on-fiber metasurface.
Page 7, Fig. 5c: measured far-field vortex profiles and polarization imaging.
Page 8, Fig. 6: robustness tests under bending and dynamic perturbations compared with bare MMF.

arxiv:2608.09605.rationale: Moderately relevant LLM/efficiency paper for sequential recommendation; token-selection policy and preference optimization connect to LLM/efficiency topics, but the recommendation setting is domain-specific. Novelty is moderate. Evidence includes quantitative tables, ablations, and inference-time measurements, but headline gains are inflated by comparing against weak SASRec rather than the strongest HLLM first-k baseline; no error bars or significance tests and limited ablations. Code link is unverified.
evidence: §4.2 Table 1 reports TSPORec vs baselines on Amazon Books and Pixel with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, showing TSPORec metric gains mainly over SASRec.
§4.2 Table 2 reports inference time: 326 ms at 64 tokens vs 843 ms at 256 tokens, supporting efficiency reduction claims.
§4.2 The Generalization capability subsection reports Table 3 (TinyLlama) and Table 4 (LLMinit) with smaller average improvements (4.12% and 3.76%).
Appendix C reports chunk-size ablation and stage-wise training time, showing extra training overhead.
Limitations acknowledges additional training time from Stages 2 and 3.

arxiv:2608.09604.rationale: Paper proposes a hybrid neural-microfacet BRDF for real-time rendering, a pure graphics/rendering topic outside the preferred LLM/NLP/agent/AI-safety scope. It has moderate domain-specific comparisons, ablations, and limitations, but no preferred-topic relevance and no code availability keep the score low.
evidence: Abstract: proposes a hybrid neural-microfacet BRDF model, not a language model or NLP method.
Section 4.1: reports quantitative SMAPE and rendering MAE comparisons against a neural baseline on MERL, RGL, and UTIA datasets.
Section 4.2: provides ablation studies for architecture variants and sparse training.
Section 6: acknowledges limitations such as iridescent materials and lack of energy conservation or Helmholtz reciprocity constraints.

arxiv:2608.09602.rationale: Out-of-scope pure soft robotics and model predictive control for a robotic esophagus; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agents, or other targeted language methodology. Although the paper includes stability analysis and quantitative tracking results, preference relevance is minimal and the rubric caps pure robotics at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: describes a Robotic Soft Esophagus with TOF and pressure sensors and SINDYC-based MPC; no LLM/NLP methods.
I Introduction: frames the work as soft robotics/MPC for esophageal stent testing, citing control and soft robotics literature.
VII-C MPC Performance Testing: reports RMSE and execution times for peristaltic tracking, with domain-specific quantitative results.
VIII Conclusion: claims extension to any soft robotic system with a SINDYC model and notes model mismatch as a limitation.

arxiv:2608.09597.rationale: Pure computer vision/3D graphics pipeline for LEGO-style brick reconstruction from photographs. No LLM/NLP, reasoning, agents, or language methodology; out-of-scope relative to stated preferences. Within its niche, the paper reports ablations, baselines, and quantitative stability metrics, but topic relevance is negligible.
evidence: Abstract: Producing a hand-buildable, colored brick model of a 3D object from a few casual photographs.
Section 4.1: Reports MS-SSIM, LPIPS, and stability certified by exact Gurobi force-balance solver.
Appendix H.1: Only grounded connectivity is guaranteed by construction; static stability and hand-buildability are empirical.

arxiv:2608.09596.rationale: GNN-focused method lies in a low-weight preference area (Graph Neural Networks) with no LLM/language methodology. LEED is somewhat novel as a local over-smoothing metric and centrality replacement, but evaluation is limited to GCN on TUDataset graph-level tasks, baseline results are partly reused rather than consistently rerun, and no significance testing or code release is shown, reducing rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: proposes LEED as a node-level metric for over-smoothing and virtual node selection
Table I: reports LVN-LEED and PANDA-LEED accuracy across MUTAG, ENZYMES, PROTEINS, REDDIT-Binary, IMDB-Binary, and COLLAB
Section VI: states some baseline results are taken from prior papers and LVN reported scores are retained
Section VIII: notes evaluation is restricted to GCN architecture and extension to GIN is future work

arxiv:2608.09595.rationale: Relevant LLM quantization/efficiency paper proposing a schedule-level seam-revisiting variant of cross-block PTQ. Novelty is moderate: the interleaving schedule is incremental over CBQ, though the depth-wise contraction framing adds value. Rigor is constrained by strong, largely uncertified assumptions and a bound-to-bound theorem rather than realized-error guarantees. Experiments cover seven models and two inner quantizers with ablations, but lack variance/statistical evidence and public code is not clearly provided.
evidence: Section 5.2, Table 1 reports lower PPL for ICBQ than Sequential CBQ in all reported PPL comparisons across seven models.
Section 5.3, Table 2 reports transfer to GPTQ W3/W2g128 with best or tied-best PPL on five of seven models at each precision.
Section 5.4, Table 3 ablation shows PPL generally improves as chunk size K decreases.
Appendix B.11 states gamma is an aggregate diagnostic, not a uniform per-sample contraction certificate.
Appendix C.1 provides hyperparameters and model details, mentions a supplementary numpy simulation, but no public code/data link is given.

arxiv:2608.09594.rationale: Out-of-scope video quality assessment benchmark for AIGC using multi-view geometry and optical flow, not language methodology. The paper has moderate niche novelty but limited relevance to LLM/NLP/reasoning/agents/safety preferences. Rigor is constrained by fixed, non-ablated thresholds, no comparative VQA baselines in results, and a small dataset; evidence is mostly internal and release is deferred.
evidence: Abstract: presents a benchmark evaluating AIGC videos via geometrical consistency across frames; no LLM/language methodology.
Section 4.1: pipeline uses DUSt3R, SAM-2, RAFT, homography/fundamental-matrix geometry; no language model component.
Section 6.2: states background inlier gates are kept fixed and are not ablated.
Section 1: states GeoCon-Bench will be publicly available after acceptance.

fallback:800cad95f27e0336.rationale: Abstract-only practitioner checklist about securely using Amazon Bedrock/LLMs; topical keywords overlap with LLM and generative AI but no research claims, methods, results, or analysis are present.

arxiv:2608.09593.rationale: Audio deepfake detection benchmark with no LLM/language methodology; omni models are evaluated only as black boxes. This is out of scope under the pure audio/domain-application rule, so preference relevance is very low and the final score is capped at 0.20. Dataset construction and protocol breadth are moderate, but the paper lacks statistical significance testing, a limitations section, and explicit release information.
evidence: Section 3.1-3.5 describes independent speech/environmental component construction and quality control.
Table 1 reports 1,892 eligible source clips and 16,536 final audio-visual samples.
Section 5.1 Table 2 reports pretrained A-V detectors near chance (AUC 0.518-0.534) while frozen A-V encoders exceed 0.91 AUC.
Section 5.2 reports environmental audio manipulation is consistently easier for frozen A-V encoders and fake environmental audio degrades speech detection for ImageBind and CAV-MAE Sync.
Section 5.4 Table 5 reports audio-only versus audio-visual ablation results.

arxiv:2608.09591.rationale: Moderately relevant: the paper uses VLM-based chain-of-thought reasoning and RL post-training (GRPO/MCTS), intersecting Reasoning & CoT, Reinforcement Learning, Multimodal AI, and Training/Optimization, but it remains a specialized autonomous-driving application with no Japanese NLP, safety, or agent focus. Novelty is incremental: adaptive planning-critical-factor reasoning and MCTS-guided GRPO are reasonable extensions of existing fast-slow CoT and search-guided RL methods. Rigor is adequate but limited by single evaluation runs, no statistical significance testing, and narrow ablations. Quantitative evidence from Tables 1-5 supports the claims, though SOTA margins are small. Generalizability is narrow to nuScenes/NAVSIM driving benchmarks. Reproducibility is partial: detailed training/reward/data configuration and a release promise, but data generation depends on proprietary models and code/checkpoints are not yet available.

arxiv:2608.09590.rationale: Pure 2D-3D cross-modal matching/computer vision paper outside LLM/NLP scope; training-time probe regularization is somewhat novel within its niche and benchmark ablations support domain claims, but lacking language methodology, limitations, full hyperparameters, and code, so global score is capped low.

The hierarchical multi-database schema-linking framework is a reasonable but somewhat incremental combination of existing components compared with LinkAlign and AutoLink. Evaluation is fairly thorough with multiple datasets, baselines, ablations, efficiency, and downstream SQL results, but absolute schema exact match remains low on Spider2-Snow, no statistical testing or code release is noted, and limitations are brief.

arxiv:2608.09586.rationale: Out-of-scope poker tournament/game-theory paper. Core contribution is Strategic-Continuation Optimization vs ICM, not LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agents methodology; LLMs appear only as fixed opponent profiles in Section 7 ('Two information-restricted model profiles'), with no LLM capability or safety evaluation. Within the finite 3-player jam/fold domain the paper reports extensive matched checks and reproducibility artifacts, but domain relevance to the stated preferences is minimal and generalizability is limited to tiny toy tournament settings.
evidence: Abstract: mentions comparing SCO with LLMs as opponents, not studying LLMs.

Section 10: conclusion is about ICM tournament strategy and SCO, not LLM/NLP methodology.

arxiv:2608.10047.rationale: This is a systematic review of physics-informed machine learning for prognostics and health management (PHM). It is a domain-specific applied ML survey with no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning language methodology, placing it outside the core preferences; relevance is minimal. The four-class taxonomy (observational, inductive, learning bias, hybrid) refines existing PIML pathways and is incremental. The review reports a systematic search and screening workflow, but there are internal inconsistencies (e.g., 212 records, 129 presented, 118 discussed) and no quantitative meta-analysis. Evidence is synthesized critically with acknowledged limitations, but findings are qualitative and domain-constrained. Reproducibility is moderate because search terms, databases, and inclusion criteria are documented, though no code or dataset is provided.
evidence: Section 4.1 Classification: proposes four classes: observational bias, inductive bias, learning bias, and hybrid approaches.
Section 3.5 Results: states final set comprised 212 records and 129 records will be presented, while Section 4.1 Figure 4 refers to 118 studies discussed.
Section 5.2.7 Caveats on Reported Effects: acknowledges absence of ablation experiments, evaluation leakage risk, and benefit-skewed evidence base.
Section 5.3 Contextual Limitations: notes concentration on lithium-ion batteries and bearings and data-availability bias.
Section 3.6 Limitations: notes ASReview stopping criterion implies about 5% of relevant studies may remain unidentified and quality thresholds were based on expert judgment.

arxiv:2608.09581.rationale: Pure computer-vision multi-object tracking paper using particle filters, PSO, and Hungarian association; no language-model, NLP, agent, or reasoning methodology. It is out of scope and scored low. Evaluation is limited to two MOT sequences (MOT17-04, MOT20-05) with mixed results and no full-benchmark or statistical support; code availability is a positive reproducibility factor.

arxiv:2608.09580.rationale: Out-of-scope pure domain application (cross-domain sequential recommendation) with no LLM/language methodology; use of self/cross-attention gives minimal preference relevance. The Cross-Reconstruction and FocalNCE ideas are incremental within CDSR. Experiments include multiple datasets, baselines, ablations, and paired t-tests, but domain-specific application limits generalizability; code and hyperparameters aid reproducibility. Final score capped at 0.20 due to out-of-scope status.

arxiv:2608.09579.rationale: Out-of-scope pure radar human pose estimation with no LLM/language methodology; the transformer backbone and uncertainty quantification do not align with the stated preferences. arxiv:2608.09577.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM-agent security, AI safety, and red-teaming preferences. The proposed conditional single-skill backdoor is a moderate novelty, but builds heavily on existing techniques (AutoDAN-style search, SBERT, saliency). Rigor is limited by single deterministic queries per skill, no error bars, and limited defense implementation details; quantitative evidence is present but self-reported, and reproducibility is limited by no code/data release.

arxiv:2608.09575.rationale: Pure hyperspectral object tracking/computer vision paper. It uses visual prompts, MoE-style routing, and visual Transformer attention, but has no LLM/NLP/language methodology and is explicitly out of scope, so overall score is capped low despite domain-specific empirical evaluation.

arxiv:2608.09574.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, multi-agent behavior, and AI safety/deception, but weakened by point estimates without variance, small effect sizes, classifier self-family bias, and an internal baseline inconsistency. The hierarchical public-goods setup is a moderately novel institutional extension, but evidence quality is limited.

arxiv:2608.09573.rationale: Relevant multimodal/agent/code-evaluation benchmark with video-grounded diagnosis; not out-of-scope. Moderate novelty in moving to interaction-trace failure diagnosis and gated multi-agent refinement. Rigor and evidence are moderate: tables/ablations are provided, but no inter-annotator agreement, confidence intervals, or artifact availability are reported. Reproducibility is weak without code/data release.

arxiv:2608.09572.rationale: In-scope multimodal vision-language continual learning paper using hyperbolic CLIP-style representations; relevant to Multimodal AI and Training/Optimization but not to LLM, Japanese NLP, reasoning, agents, code, safety, or interpretability. Provides a theoretically framed geometric update (shared Lorentz isometry/null-space projection) with experiments across three hyperbolic backbones and drift analysis. Strengths include formal proofs, multiple baselines/backbones, ablations, and limitations. Concerns: large claimed gains, method is a known null-space projection combined with existing hyperbolic CLIP, significance testing is limited, code URL is not provided, and generalizability is confined to hyperbolic vision-language models.

arxiv:2608.09568.rationale: Highly relevant LLM alignment/DPO paper. Novelty is moderate: online self-evolving token credit with reference-entropy calibration is a reasonable increment over token-level DPO variants. Rigor and evidence are moderate: includes a proposition with proof, ablations, length analysis, and cost data, but lacks multiple seeds/confidence intervals, and MT-Bench scores decline in full fine-tuning settings. Generalizability is moderate across three model sizes and two reward annotators. Reproducibility is adequate via Algorithm 1 and Appendix C hyperparameters but no code release is stated.
evidence: Abstract: 'Experiments show that Se-DPO improves over DPO by up to 9.8 points on AlpacaEval 2 and 12.2 points on Arena-Hard.'

arxiv:2608.09567.rationale: Relevant to LLM/agent vulnerability validation, benchmarking, and AI-safety evaluation, but it is a meta-audit rather than a core LLM/NLP methodology contribution. The pre-registered protocol with patched-counterfactual oracles is somewhat novel, and reproducibility artifacts are strong, but confirmatory statistics are incomplete, some execution denominators are inconsistent, and external validity is explicitly limited to a single corpus/sample.

arxiv:2608.09566.rationale: Astronomy/computer-vision domain application using a compact CNN for low-surface-brightness galaxy detection; no LLM, language, reasoning, or agent methodology. Out of scope, so capped at 0.20. The pipeline is quantitatively described and limitations are noted, but the work is domain-specific with limited generalizability and no stated code/data release.

arxiv:2608.10046.rationale: Domain-focused empirical study of soft-skill articulation in CVs; uses an LLM extraction pipeline only as a methodological enabler, so relevance to core LLM/NLP research is limited. The hypothesis-testing design, effect sizes, and robustness analyses are strengths, but extraction validity is moderate (F1 0.72) and the study is non-preregistered with narrow English/public self-selected sampling.
evidence: Section 3.1 defines 13 confirmatory hypotheses and Section 3.6 specifies Fisher/chi-square/McNemar tests, Holm-Bonferroni, FDR, effect sizes, and sensitivity constraints.
Section 4 reports extraction performance: precision 0.69, recall 0.74, F1 0.72 against a 100-CV human-annotated ground truth.

arxiv:2608.09565.rationale: Decentralized optimization/streaming data theory paper with no LLM, NLP, or language methodology relevance; only weak topical overlap with broad optimization/distributed training interests. The analysis is mathematically developed, but strong assumptions and synthetic quadratic experiments limit evidence and generalizability, and the paper is effectively out of scope for the target preferences.

arxiv:2608.10045.rationale: Relevant to reward-model/preference-learning and RLHF-adjacent human feedback, but the paper does not evaluate LLMs or language tasks; its contribution is a general crowdsourced pairwise-comparison method. The Pólya-Gamma EM derivation is incremental over prior Boltzmann-rational/worker-competence models, and the matrix-sensing theory relies on restrictive assumptions. Real-data gains over HBTL/CrowdBT are very small, and the main robustness claim is not backed by reported confidence intervals.
evidence: Abstract introduces joint reward and worker-reliability learning from pairwise comparisons and mentions LLM fine-tuning only as an application context.
Section 5 imposes acyclic per-worker comparison graphs and fixes R=0.1 for the RIP/Theorem 1 analysis, limiting theoretical applicability.

arxiv:2608.09564.rationale: Moderately relevant multimodal vision-language navigation with an LLM-based decoder (Qwen2.5-VL) and GRPO, but primarily a domain-specific UAV navigation system rather than core LLM/NLP methodology. Components are mostly established techniques combined; evaluation is quantitative but lacks paired significance testing and is limited to two simulation benchmarks.

arxiv:2608.09558.rationale: Directly relevant to transformer prompting, soft prompts, and in-context learning, though the model is a simplified single-layer attention architecture rather than an applied LLM. Generalizability is limited to one-layer, single-head, scalar regression on compact manifolds; no code-release statement is present.

arxiv:2608.09556.rationale: Pure robotics/networked-control co-design for cooperative multi-robot transport over TDMA; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompt, agent, or multimodal language methodology. Robotics is out of scope and capped at 0.20. The paper has a clear simulation setup, quantitative scenario comparisons, sensitivity/stability/scalability analyses, and reported limitations, but no hardware validation, no statistical testing, no code/data release, and limited generalizability.

arxiv:2608.09555.rationale: Core LLM-agent RL work combining skill-conditioned self-distillation with GRPO; strongly relevant to Agents & Tool Use, LLM, and Reinforcement Learning preferences. Empirical results on ALFWorld and WebShop with ablations provide moderate evidence, but lack of statistical significance, limited task diversity, and self-reported results constrain rigor and generalizability.

Experiments compares BCSD against Skill_GRPO, RLSD, Skill-SD, and SDAR on ALFWorld and WebShop across Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-3B, and Qwen3-1.7B.

arxiv:2608.09551.rationale: Highly relevant LLM safety/jailbreak paper. The pragmatic presupposition attack framing has some novelty, but rigor and evidence are limited by inconsistency and weak verification: explicit prompt wording undermines the implicit-context claim, benchmark naming is inconsistent, model identifiers are unverifiable, and no statistical testing or clear metric denominators are provided. Multi-benchmark/multi-model evaluation supports moderate generalizability, and prompt templates aid reproducibility, but the overall evidential weight is limited.
evidence: Section 4.1 lists target models as GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.6, Qwen3.6-27B, and Gemini 3.6 Flash, with benchmarks BBQ, Implicit Hate, and PolyGuard.

Tables 2 and 3 use a 'Toxicity' benchmark not defined in Section 4.1, which defines Implicit Hate instead.
Tables 8 and 10 in Appendix A.1 include explicitly harmful wording ('harmful stereotypes') in attack prompts despite the paper's implicit-context framing.
Section 4.3 reports automatic-human agreement of 91.5% and kappa=0.785 for attack-success decisions.
Appendix A.2 states the LLM judge is DeepSeek-v4-Flash and sees only the final visible answer.

arxiv:2608.09550.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/ubiquitous sensing paper on 3D human mesh estimation from pressure images, with no language-model methodology. It uses Transformer and Mixture of Experts as components, giving only weak preference relevance, and lacks LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/safety content. Research quality is modest within its domain: a new multi-device pressure dataset and MDP-Net are proposed with ablations, but evidence is limited and no code/data release or strong generalizability claims are established. Overall capped at or below 0.20 as a pure computer vision domain application.

arxiv:2608.09548.rationale: Highly relevant LLM safety and evaluation benchmark with four-module education-focused design. Methods include HITL curation, judge calibration, and bootstrap confidence intervals, but novelty is incremental over recent education/safety suites and evidence is limited by a small model sample (n=9), uneven module sizes, reliance on LLM judging, and limited reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.09547.rationale: This is a design-phase MBSE/SysML/ROS 2 framework for autonomous UAV systems. It is pure robotics/systems engineering with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, agent-language methodology, or multimodal AI focus; therefore it falls under the out-of-scope pure robotics cap. The paper presents conceptual mappings and diagrams only, with no quantitative experiments, baselines, ablations, or completed simulation/hardware validation, so rigor and evidence strength are limited. Minor novelty comes from tailoring SysML-to-ROS 2 mapping to autonomous UAVs, but it builds on existing MeROS/ROS2ML work.

arxiv:2608.09542.rationale: Highly relevant to AI safety, alignment, red-teaming, and reasoning LLMs. The dual-adversarial pipeline meaningfully combines agentic jailbreak synthesis with teacher-guided threat deconstruction, though it is incremental over prior reasoning-trace distillation methods. Empirical coverage is broad across models, benchmarks, ablations, and OOD attacks, but rigor is limited by the lack of statistical significance testing and incomplete public release of offensive components. Evidence is detailed and internally consistent.

Appendix C.2: Provides detailed LoRA, optimizer, and hardware configurations.
Appendix G: DeepSeek judge agrees with Llama Guard on 361/400 responses (90.25%) and labels 246/252 AdvSafe responses safe.

arxiv:2608.09541.rationale: This is an autonomous driving/V2X collaborative perception and motion prediction paper, outside the LLM/NLP/agent/code/safety/reasoning preference scope. It provides quantitative fusion-timing and end-to-end prototype experiments, but the domain is not relevant to the stated preferences, and generalization/reproducibility are limited to one dataset and implementation details.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: states the work focuses on Collaborative Joint Perception and Prediction via V2X, not LLM/NLP or language methodology.

arxiv:2608.09539.rationale: Arabic stance-detection dataset extension with NLP and dataset relevance, plus zero-shot LLM baselines, but outside prioritized core (no Japanese LLM/NLP, no LLM methodology, reasoning, or agents). Contribution is incremental and mostly resource-oriented.

Table 10 reports F_avg2 results for Arabic BERT, multilingual, and zero-shot LLM baselines under Protocol 1 and Protocol 2.

arxiv:2608.09538.rationale: In-scope LLM reasoning/evaluation benchmark, but rigor is limited by reliance on an imperfect automated verifier, no released dataset or code, no human baseline, and cross-model selection partly tuned on the benchmark itself.
evidence: Abstract reports a benchmark of 300 theorem-proving tasks and a reference verifier achieving over 90% accuracy on expert-labeled proofs.
Section 3.2 describes dependency DAG extraction and rank-based task difficulty, but does not provide enough detail to reproduce the extraction pipeline exactly.
Section 3.4 lists automated structural and semantic checks with no independent validation of these LLM-based filters.

Table 1 reports model accuracies ranging from 30.3% to 68%, but with no confidence intervals, statistical tests, or human baseline.
Section 5 reports cross-model selection gains, but notes direction and thresholds were selected using accuracy measured on TCS-Bench, raising leakage concerns.
No dataset URL, code repository, or model checkpoint is provided, limiting reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.09537.rationale: Out-of-scope world-model/embodied video optimization with no language methodology; the agent/retrieval framing is adjacent to agents and RAG preferences but is not an LLM/NLP contribution. The supplied text shows detailed protocols and ablations, but the core evidence concerns video world models, robotics, and optimization transfer, so the out-of-scope cap applies.
evidence: Abstract: describes Verdi as continual framework for world model optimization and reports reductions in search cost, GPU cost, and negative transfer.
Section 4: reports experiments on Ctrl-World, Cosmos family, and RoboCoin, indicating embodied/video world-model focus.
Appendix B.2: agent-level controls mention a shared frozen LLM, but the core method is fingerprinting, retrieval, and target-side validation rather than language methodology.

arxiv:2608.09536.rationale: Pure document image restoration work on deblurring/denoising/compression artifact reduction/deshadowing. It uses Transformer blocks and cross-attention only as a computer vision backbone, with no LLM, Japanese NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, or language methodology. Although ablations, datasets, and quantitative comparisons are reported, this is out of scope as pure computer vision and is capped accordingly.
evidence: Abstract: addresses document deblurring, denoising, compression artifact reduction, and deshadowing; no language-model method.
Section III-A: U-Net-style restoration network with Transformer blocks and structure-guided wavelet interaction; methodological focus is image restoration.
Section IV-C: evaluation uses PSNR, SSIM, and OCR accuracy rather than NLP/LLM tasks.

arxiv:2608.09532.rationale: Relevant LLM/agentic data-analytics demo with interactive query planning and execution; however, it is a demonstration paper with no quantitative experiments, baselines, or ablations, so rigor and evidence strength are low.
evidence: Abstract: Carnot compiles natural language requests into physical execution graphs and surfaces them through an interactive notebook interface.

2.1 Carnot Frontend: Users can inspect any cell at three levels of abstraction: a natural language summary of the operator's intent, the generated code or LLM prompt, and the raw input/output data pairs.
2.3 Carnot Library: The QueryPlanner is an LLM agent with few-shot demonstrations for composing plans in Carnot's operator vocabulary.
3 Demonstration Scenarios: The attendee will issue a free-form natural language query and examine the DAG of operators before executing a single operator.
4 Limitations and Future Work: Carnot does not provide guarantees on plan accuracy or correctness.

arxiv:2608.09530.rationale: Out-of-scope compiler/systems performance paper. No LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agentic, multimodal, safety, or alignment methodology; only marginal overlap with broad software-engineering preferences. The study is systematic within its domain (54 benchmarks, PMU metrics, binary patching validation), but domain mismatch keeps the overall score below the 0.20 out-of-scope ceiling.
evidence: Abstract: introduces a top-down differential analysis methodology for compiler optimization differences using microarchitectural metrics.
Sec. 4.2: evaluates 54 real-world benchmarks compiled with GCC 15.1.0 and Clang/LLVM 20.1.0.
Sec. 4.5: reports binary patching improvements including 80.5% and 68.1% on Clang-compiled hot and flow benchmarks.

arxiv:2608.09529.rationale: Out-of-scope audio-to-image diffusion paper: the core contribution is audio-conditioned image generation with a diffusion backbone and multimodal data pipeline, without language methodology central to the rubric. arxiv:2608.09524.rationale: Moderately relevant as an LLM-based agentic workflow with retrieval/tool use, but it is a domain-specific cybersecurity application with no core LLM/NLP/Japanese methodology. arxiv:2608.09523.rationale: Relevant mainly through the general training/optimization preference; no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, safety, or language-model methodology. The generalized convexity/smoothness framework has some novelty but is weakened by overly flexible definitions (any DNN objective can be made to satisfy them by increasing constants) and arbitrary zero surrogate gradients. Validation is qualitative figure-based with reported correlations but no exact quantitative metrics, baselines, or significance tests.
evidence: Section 3.2 sets surrogate gradients to zero at non-differentiable points and Proposition 5 claims any neural network training objective is both generalized smooth and convex by choosing energy constants.
Section 6.3.2 reports that local Pearson correlations approach 1 across Figures 6-15 but provides no numeric tables or exact correlation values.
Section 6.1 specifies Python/PyTorch/GPU and datasets but no code release or random seeds are reported.

arxiv:2608.09522.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/domain application for GPR cavity detection; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, or language methodology. Despite seeded ablations and field-only evaluation, relevance is minimal and final score capped at 0.20.

arxiv:2608.09449.rationale: Video dataset for long-horizon world modeling with camera trajectories and VLM-generated temporal semantics. It matches low-weight video/data/multimodal topics but is not LLM/language methodology and is near the out-of-scope video/CV boundary. Dataset novelty is moderate: it extends Sekai with unified annotations and a revisit-rich panoramic subset. Rigor and evidence are fairly strong for a dataset paper, with corpus-wide pose checks, cross-run geometric consistency, epipolar negative controls, and caption quality audits, but validation relies on self-generated annotations and estimated poses rather than independent ground truth. Generalizability is limited by geographic/source skew and only partial public release of the panoramic subset. Reproducibility is moderate: code/config/prompts are described and URLs provided, but public panoramic data is restricted.
evidence: Sec. 5.1 reports Sekai2 aesthetic score 5.23 vs MiraData 5.45 and higher local motion metrics.
Table 3 reports weighted cross-run median rotation RPE 0.103° at 1s and normalized ATE 0.0176.

Limitations and future work notes monocular trajectory errors, automatic annotation noise, and no dense user actions; Panoramic data release states only about 20 of 119 hours are publicly downloadable.

arxiv:2608.09444.rationale: Strongly relevant to LLM inference/serving and transformer efficiency. The paper is systems-focused but directly targets looped LLM serving, KV cache, batching, latency/throughput. Novelty is moderate: first end-to-end CDB implementation and lookahead gate/depth-aware KV cache, but builds on Bae et al. 2025a. Rigor is reasonable with FLOP bound, roofline model, two-model/offline/online evaluation, and ablations, though no error bars. Evidence from single H100 with replayed exits and referenced sections/figures. Generalizability across two looped architectures and workloads is moderate. No code/artifact release indicated, limiting reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: claims up to 99% theoretical speed-up, 1.5-1.9x throughput, 45-90% lower normalized latency.
Section 6.2 Offline Throughput: reports CDB (refill) reaches 94-99% of FLOP bound on Ouro and up to 1.9x on Huginn.
Section 6.3 Online Serving: reports CDB (refill) reduces normalized latency by 45-57% on ShareGPT and 84-88% on Alpaca.
Appendix C.1 KV Cache Sharing: Table 1 reports GSM8K accuracy under KV layouts, showing Ouro collapse under single shared cache.
Section 4.3 Efficient Asynchronous Execution: Figure 3 shows lookahead gate reduces per-step device idle to 0.67%.

arxiv:2608.09443.rationale: Moderate relevance: strong agentic/LLM-agent framing and evaluation, but the core system is a medical-domain symbolic graph-policy method with no external LLM at inference. Evidence is quantitative but lacks uncertainty estimates and real-world validation. Generalizability is constrained to synthetic guideline-derived cases. Reproducibility is partially supported by a code link and supplementary details but unverified.

Table II: ATLAS reports Final Strict 23.68 and Agent OSRS 64.09 on GeriMedBench.

arxiv:2608.09417.rationale: Relevant core transformer optimization/architecture paper studying Post-Norm collapse, attention amplification, and gradient contraction. Moderate novelty: extends rank-collapse signal-propagation work to decoder-only SwiGLU/RMSNorm and adds backward repair and collapsed-network characterization. Rigor is solid with formal assumptions, theorems, and proofs, though key approximations (equal-correlation, prefix-averaging, ratio-of-expectations) limit exactness. Evidence includes 48-layer C4 experiments, intervention, learning-rate ablations, and repeated run, but single architecture/dataset and visible theory-experiment mismatch. Generalizability is limited to Post-Norm decoder-only stability. Reproducibility is moderate due to detailed setup but no stated code/availability.
evidence: Section 3.1 Theorem 3.2 gives a closed-form one-step attention similarity increase and Corollary 3.3 supports a prefix-averaging intervention.
Section 3.2 Theorem 3.6 derives backward gradient contraction under collapse with RMSNorm shrinkage.
Section 3.3 Theorem 3.8 characterizes frequency-distribution loss floor and gradient vanishing in collapsed networks.
Section 4 Experiments uses a 48-layer Llama-2-style decoder-only Transformer on C4 and matches initialization-time similarity growth and collapse-time gradient contraction.
Section 4.1 Figure 2 reports removing the prefix-averaging component suppresses similarity growth.
Section 5 Limitations acknowledges the paper does not explain the sharp transition onset.

arxiv:2608.09303.rationale: Out-of-scope for this curation: the paper concerns robotic chemistry lab automation with imitation learning and uncertainty-aware switching, with no LLM/NLP/language methodology. Although it reports quantitative experiments and ablations, relevance to the preferred topic areas is minimal, so the overall score is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: proposes SAFE-CHEM, an ensemble-based uncertainty-aware policy switching framework for robotic chemistry manipulation.
Section IV-A: evaluates on three simulated manipulation tasks using IsaacLab and a Franka Production 3 manipulator.
Section IV-D: reports calibration of switching logic using KDE and peak detection metrics.
Section IV-E: Tables III and IV report success rates and safety violation rates across confidence thresholds.

arxiv:2608.09302.rationale: Domain-specific medical/surgical scene segmentation with only abstract-level information; though a vision-language model is mentioned, the work is a pure medical imaging/computer vision application without language methodology and is capped at 0.20 per rubric. No method, baseline, quantitative result, or reproducibility detail is available.
evidence: abstract: proposes first vision-language model (VLM)-based hysteroscopic surgical scene segmentation
abstract: task challenges include morphological similarity and artifacts such as specular reflections, motion blur, and fluid occlusions

arxiv:2608.09298.rationale: Embodied manipulation/action-conditioned world-model benchmark with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, agent, or language-methodology core; Qwen3-VL appears only as an evaluator. Robotics is low-preference and explicitly out-of-scope, so the score is capped at 0.20 despite a fairly systematic benchmark construction and available code/data.
evidence: Section 5.1 reports approximately 5,500 RoboTwin, 6,600 ManiSkill, and 6,500 LIBERO evaluation instances, totaling more than 18,000.
Table 2 reports suite-level Task 1-5 and overall scores for six action-conditioned world models.
Section 5.5 reports human-evaluation agreement and downstream synthetic-data utility.

arxiv:2608.09296.rationale: CAD-focused multimodal LLM benchmark for programmatic CAD generation, assembly reasoning, and FEA; relevant to LLM/code/multimodal/evaluation preferences but domain-specific. Rigorous layered scoring, bootstrap CIs, paired tests, and detailed prompts/algorithms. Novelty moderate over prior CAD benchmarks; generalizability limited to CAD/engineering. Reproducibility partially supported by detailed settings but no explicit code/data artifact release.
evidence: Abstract: two-track benchmark with 600 parametric tasks and 150 assembly pairs; eight multimodal code-capable models.
Benchmark Design: layered L0-L3 and A1-A2 checks from validity to FEA and exact B-Rep entity retrieval.
Results and Analysis: only 432/1030 executable outputs pass L1; weak cross-track rank correlations.
Limitations and Future Work: L1 not manufacturing certification; one parameter/edit; assembly pairs only; linear FEA only.
Appendix J Statistical Analysis: 95% bootstrap intervals and Holm-corrected McNemar tests.

arxiv:2608.09294.rationale: Topically relevant through LLM extraction, knowledge graphs, and conversational agents, but this is a qualitative HCI health study rather than core ML methodology. It lacks baselines, ablations, quantitative metrics, and releases no code or prompts; findings rely on self-reported participant feedback with limited generalizability.
evidence: Section 3 System Architecture: extraction uses LangExtract with OpenAI gpt-4o/gpt-4o-mini and a Neo4j knowledge graph.
Section 5.1 Theme 1: Human Algorithm Narrative Gap: reports n=17 entity-level failures and n=12 co-reference splits.
Section 6.5 Limitations and Future Work: evaluation was conducted in a controlled, in-the-lab setting with 16 participants.

arxiv:2608.09292.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, reasoning, and self-evolution. The method combines known zeroth-order LLM tuning with self-evolving agents and instance-specific LoRA; the answer-perplexity loss and parallel LoRA perturbation are useful but mostly engineering increments. Rigor is moderate: controlled comparison is limited mainly to ReAct, many strong baselines are paper-reported rather than controlled, and key ablations use small 50-example subsets. Evidence is quantitatively rich but some headline gains rely on contextual comparisons. Generalizability is limited to deep-research/web-agent benchmarks with small transfer. Reproducibility is good due to code link and detailed implementation/compute settings.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 1 reports controlled GAIA/WebWalkerQA results and paper-reported baselines; Ours-SFT Qwen-3-8B GAIA avg 47.5 vs ReAct 23.3.
Section 4.3.2 reports improvement from 22.0% to 53.9% Pass@1 on 304 training examples after zeroth-order optimization.
Section 4.5.1, Table 6 compares fixed-trajectory first-order, RL, and the proposed ZO method on 50 difficult examples.
Section 4.6.3, Table 11 reports five random seed means with confidence intervals.
Appendix A.5 lists compute resources, tools, hyperparameters, and code availability.

arxiv:2608.09291.rationale: Relevant LLM inference/efficiency systems paper with clear kernel and end-to-end evaluation, but moderate novelty over prior sparse LLM kernels; baseline fairness and lack of accuracy validation limit rigor and evidence strength.
evidence: Abstract: reports W4A4 30-70% sparsity speedups over FlashLLM, SpInfer, CUTLASS, and cuBLAS and provides code URL.
VII-C: controlled ablation isolates LSPD, double-buffer, and reorder contributions with latency and profiling metrics.
VII-E: end-to-end OPT-13B evaluation reports speedups but notes non-SpMM/system bottlenecks limit gains.
VII-A: describes Jetson AGX Orin setup, baselines, W4A4 corpus, and exclusion of offline preprocessing from reported latency.

arxiv:2608.09290.rationale: Directly relevant LLM-based code review agent with multi-agent and tool-use components, but quality is moderate: single benchmark, limited baselines, no ablations isolating the three proposed modules, and no statistical significance testing. Quantitative results support core claims but causal attributions are not fully isolated.
evidence: Section 4.2 Overall Results and Table 3 report SEM-F1, precision, recall, token, and time comparisons for OpenCodeReview versus Claude Code and Codex.
Section 4.3 Cost Efficiency reports 5-15x fewer tokens and 1.3-2.2x higher SEM-F1.
Section 6 Threats to Validity acknowledges limitations including LLM-judge metrics, only two baselines, and construct-validity concerns for SEM-F1.
Abstract claims up to 2.17x higher SEM-F1 and 5-15x fewer tokens versus mainstream coding agents.

arxiv:2608.09289.rationale: Pure domain application of LLMs to automated EFL writing evaluation; no AI/ML methodology advance. Uses LLM correction layers and CEFR-J grammar profiling, with descriptive statistics but no baselines, limited human validation, and narrow single-site learner population.
evidence: Abstract: reports a layered LLM-correction pipeline on 3,830 Japanese EFL writing samples using the CEFR-J regex grammar extractor.
Section 3.3: describes generating literal error correction and idiomatic native revision versions via an LLM.
Section 4.1: reports accuracy gap shifts with G2 and log ratio in Table 2.
Section 4.2: reports idiomatic gap shifts in Figure 3.
Section 5: acknowledges manual validation was restricted to a small subset and the grammar extractor may fail to recognize some error types.

arxiv:2608.10039.rationale: Strongly relevant to LLM agents and tool use; directly targets tool-integrated agentic workflow generation with LLM nodes and tool-calling nodes. Novelty is moderate: combines existing process mining, MCTS, and execution feedback, extending AFlow/PM4Py rather than introducing a fundamentally new paradigm. Evaluation includes four ToolBench domains, ablations, and tool/LLM replacement, but the abstract's 'at least' improvement claims conflict with per-domain variation, AFlow tool-invocation correctness is omitted, domain tasks have short tool chains, and artifact availability is unverified.
evidence: Abstract: proposes FlowScout, execution-guided tool-integrated agentic workflow generation from historical task-solving records.
Section IV-B, Table II: reports average TC and ES across finance, sports, travel, and weather domains, with FlowScout TC 0.7515 and ES 0.7381.
Section IV-D, Table III: ablation variants FlowScout-NoMCTS, FlowScout-NoMiner, and FlowScout-Beam show contributions of miner and MCTS.
Section V: acknowledges threats including limited domains, short tool invocation chains, and possible LLM evaluator bias.
Section VIII: states source code and data availability.

arxiv:2608.09288.rationale: Audio-visual speech separation is a pure audio/vision domain application without language-model methodology, so it is out of scope and capped at 0.20. The paper provides quantitative ablations and challenge results, but no code release, limited statistical validation, and modest domain-specific novelty.
evidence: Section 2 states DAVE-Corpus totals 219,411 training mixtures.
Table 2 reports stepwise ablation metrics on the official development set.
Table 3 reports DAVE Track 1 rank 4.00 and Track 2 rank 4.14.

arxiv:2608.09287.rationale: Out-of-scope as a vision-centric data-free knowledge distillation paper; LLMs and CLIP-style text embeddings are used only as auxiliary semantic prompts/encoders, not as language-model or NLP methodology. The work reports multi-architecture experiments and ablations, but relevance to the requested LLM/NLP/agent/safety topics is insufficient, and the supplied text lacks code availability or statistical significance reporting, capping the overall score.
evidence: Abstract: proposes UniDFKD with Categorical Semantic Conditioning using language-derived embeddings, Spatial Semantic Anchoring with a Gaussian prior, and Spatial Semantic Distillation.
Experiments: Table 1 reports averages of 82.50% homogeneous and 78.33% heterogeneous across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet-100.
Appendix G: discusses limitations of the center-biased Gaussian prior for non-object-centric domains.
Appendix F: provides implementation details and hyperparameters, but no code availability statement is present in the supplied text.

arxiv:2608.09286.rationale: Pure domain application in weather forecasting with no language methodology, LLM, NLP, reasoning, agents, or safety alignment. Only weak topical overlap through graph-based relational modeling and scientific AI. The paper presents ablations and quantitative comparisons, but the domain mismatch and single benchmark/closed 69-field setting limit overall relevance and generalizability.
evidence: Experiments, Table 2: reports RMSE and ACC for selected variables against baselines.
Ablation Study, Table 3: removing dynamic field graph and graph-conditioned fusion degrades performance.
Conclusion: limitations include deterministic 1.5-degree forecasts over a fixed 69-field set.

arxiv:2608.09285.rationale: Out-of-scope wireless localization domain application: no LLM, NLP, agent, code, safety, or language methodology; only incidental transformer/foundation-model terminology. Technical work has moderate novelty and ablations, but final score is capped by the out-of-scope policy.
evidence: Abstract: GLocFM is a geometry-aware foundation model for 3D indoor wireless localization using WiFi measurements and 3D point clouds.
Section 5.2.1 Table 1 reports GLocFM mean error 0.1429 m (N_R=4) versus 0.2827 m for LocGPT delay-AoA.
Section 5.3.1 Table 3 provides ablations for grid size, cosine-only scorer, and LoS-only path model.
Section 5.2.2 Table 2 reports real-measurement NeRF2 evaluation with angular spectra and fine-tuning, not full CSI.

arxiv:2608.09282.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, and benchmark/evaluation, with additional reasoning content. The paper presents a solidly designed agentic shopping benchmark with solution-first feasibility, deterministic constraint validation, 291 tasks, 22 agent configurations, and human-adjudicated evaluator checks. Rigor and evidence are strong, though novelty is benchmark-level rather than methodological and reproducibility is limited by unclear artifact release. Generalizability is moderate due to the simulated single-environment setting.
evidence: Abstract: introduces ComboShoppingBench for budget-constrained basket shopping with coupons and hybrid evaluation combining LLM judges and deterministic validation.
Table 2 (Experiments): reports pass rates across 22 configurations, with GPT-5.5 Think achieving only 61.2% Overall success.
Section 4 Failure Analysis: reports Think improves coupon optimality from 68% to 83% and identifies mutually exclusive coupon selection as a bottleneck.
Appendix G / Table 3: reports LLM evaluator agreement of 97.00-97.57% with an expert-adjudicated human reference over 700 rubric decisions.
Appendix F: witness independence audit reports 33.1% of Overall-success outputs use an entirely disjoint SKU set from the hidden witness.

arxiv:2608.09281.rationale: In-scope MLLM visual reasoning benchmark with evaluation and CoT prompting; not a pure domain application. Construction pipeline is detailed and evaluated across 18 MLLMs with human baseline and error analysis, but domain is narrowly AEC, key prompts/human panel details are sparse, and single-run/no statistical testing limit confidence.
evidence: Section 3.2: decoupled planner-writer pipeline with answer freezing, automated screening thresholds (8/4/2 trials), blind three-agent audit, dual verification, and unanimous expert review.
Table 2: accuracy per AEC subdomain for 18 open/proprietary MLLMs and a human panel baseline.
Section 4.3: CoT and panel-identifier prompting produce small/inconsistent gains.
Section 5: pooled error categories include composition 35.8%, principle 21.7%, perception 20.3%, grounding 14.5%, consistency 7.7%.

arxiv:2608.09280.rationale: NLP meta-research on responsible-checklist compliance; touches AI safety/evaluation and NLP but is not core LLM/agent/reasoning methodology. Novelty is moderate: a first checklist-to-section linked corpus, but methods use existing tools. Rigor is limited by word-count-only NO-justification quality and a small validation sample (71 checklists, no reported annotator agreement or confidence intervals). Evidence is quantitative but descriptive, without statistical testing. Generalizability is limited to one venue/year (EMNLP 2025), and reproducibility is partial (dataset website and pipeline described, but proprietary LLM and no code/annotator protocol).
evidence: Section 4.1 reports manual validation of 71 papers/2,911 items with three errors and a claimed 99.9% item-level accuracy.
Section 5.1 reports over half of authors disregard potential risks/social impacts (A2).
Section 5.3 reports 44.9% of NO justifications were brief or empty based on word count.
Section 5.4 reports 281 main-track papers (15.5%) contain logical parent-child contradictions.

arxiv:2608.09278.rationale: Centrally about LLM-based GUI agents and software engineering, strongly matching agents/LLM/evaluation/safety preferences. As a survey it synthesizes existing work rather than providing new experiments; systematic coding is described with multiple research questions, but no inter-coder reliability or released corpus, and scores are counts rather than validated evidence, limiting reproducibility and evidence strength.
