arxiv:2608.09277.rationale: Strongly in scope as LLM-based agentic code generation with formal proof and a new benchmark. The joint program-and-proof planning idea is a plausible but incremental transfer of classic co-derivation to LLM workflows. Empirical evaluation spans multiple models/benchmarks but uses single runs and no statistical testing, and generalization beyond Lean 4 is not established.
evidence: Abstract: reports P^3 highest solve rate across benchmarks and Lean4Commit0 benchmark.
Table 2: solve rates across four models and three benchmarks.
Table 3: Plan-Seq ablation showing 3.3-8.3 point gains.
Appendix C: limitations include Lean 4 only, single runs, closed-source backends.

arxiv:2608.09276.rationale: Relevant as a multimodal vision-language model study with LLM adaptation and retrieval-augmented grounded generation, but the lunar geology domain is niche relative to core preferences. Rigor is strong, with spatial splits, cluster bootstrap intervals, ablation controls, and causal probes, but novelty and generalizability are moderate and domain-specific.
evidence: Sec. 1.1 reports grounding metrics and baseline comparisons
Sec. 1.4 reports age-value failure and probe localization
Sec. 1.5 reports retrieval transfer and causal perturbation results
Sec. 3.5 describes deterministic raster-derived target construction
Data availability lists public data, code, and weights

arxiv:2608.09273.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM agents, code generation, and long-horizon memory. The adversarial entropy/text-gradient/memory-tree combination is moderately novel, but rigor and evidence are limited by a three-repository benchmark, LLM-judge metrics without human validation, and use of unverifiable future model versions; generalization beyond Android-to-HarmonyOS and the tested applications is not established.
evidence: Section 4.2 states all methods use DeepSeek-V4-Pro as the underlying LLM and Qwen3.7-Plus for dynamic entropy evaluation.
Table 1 reports ECAT average 74.7% versus ReCodeAgent 46.4% and gives standard deviations only for ECAT.
Appendix A Table 2 shows removing the independent discriminator reduces average score to 28.4%.
Section 4.3 Figure 5 reports memory-tree transfer reduces Gallery iterations from 66 to 38 and cumulative tokens from ~125M to ~65M.
Section 5 notes limitations including increased inference latency/token consumption.

arxiv:2608.09272.rationale: Pure robotics/control paper on real-time nonlinear MPC for underactuated double-pendulum swing-up. It has no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/prompting/RAG/agents/code/safety methodology and is out of scope, so final score is capped at or below 0.20. The work applies existing SQP/ADMM/HPIPM methods with quantitative hardware results but limited novelty and narrow generalizability.
evidence: Abstract: 'presents an optimal-control-based approach employing real-time nonlinear model predictive control implemented using sequential quadratic programming' with no language-model or NLP component.
Section IV: Reports Pendubot median uptime 55.5s without disturbances and 52.38s with torque disturbances; Acrobot 51.48s without and 41.82s with disturbances.
Section V: Notes a swing-up success rate greater than 90% on average and acknowledges Acrobot friction compensation as a current limitation.

arxiv:2608.09271.rationale: Highly relevant LLM reasoning/RL method. Proposes bounded softmax group advantages over GRPO with exact finite-M binary-reward theory and asymptotic scalar-reward objective; claims are explicitly scoped. Empirical comparisons are matched and include ablations, but scale is limited, no significance intervals, and the softmax/RAML construction itself is incremental.
evidence: Section 3.2 and Table 1: finite and large-group binary prompt-weighting derivations show GRPO blow-up and SoftmaxGRPO boundedness.
Section 6.2 and Table 2: SoftmaxGRPO-Exact reaches 75.8 on GSM8K, 58.1 on Countdown, 51.8 on DeepMath, improving over GRPO.
Section 6.3 and Table 3: measured gradient allocation shows 10.0% vs 36.4% to near-solved GSM8K prompts.
Section 6.5 and Table 5: temperature and rollout ablations show low tau stability and degradation at high tau.
Appendix B.1 and Tables B.1-B.2: detailed hyperparameters and matched comparison settings provide reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.09270.rationale: Moderately relevant as a vision-language/multimodal retrieval method, but not LLM-centric and largely an aerial drone-view CV application; no Japanese, reasoning, agent, or safety content. Method is incremental over prior negative-augmentation and region-alignment work, with reasonable ablations but no statistical testing or limitations analysis.
evidence: Table 1: GRASP reports fine-tuned mR 38.04% on GeoText-1652 versus GeoText-1652 baseline 36.05%.
Table 2: Ablation shows mR improves from 36.05% baseline to 38.04% with combined RFA/TSP/VSP.
Table 3: Zero-shot ERA mR 39.47% for GRASP versus GeoText-1652 baseline 38.00%.
Section 4.2: Implementation details include SPC size, loss weights, optimizer, two-stage training, and code link.

arxiv:2608.09268.rationale: Strong topical relevance to coding agents, code representation, and multimodal LLM workflows. The study is exploratory but provides controlled agent variants and quantitative token/accuracy comparisons; however, a 100-instance single-run design limits statistical confidence and generalizability.
evidence: Section 5.2 reports accuracy and token reductions in Table 1 and Table 2.
Appendix D reports model settings and the 100-instance stratified SWE-bench Verified sampling.
Table 3 provides LET phase-level token and editor-cost breakdown.

arxiv:2608.09266.rationale: Out-of-scope medical world-model/echocardiography preprocessing paper with no language methodology. Conceptual observation-clock taxonomy is modestly novel and formally defined, but empirical support is limited to one de-identified echo interval and a controlled synthetic check, with no code/data or broad validation. Capped as medical imaging/domain application.
evidence: Section 4 Worked example: 'EndoClock therefore returns external_witness_only for this single de-identified acquisition.'
Section 4 Controlled synthetic check: 'coarse target at 0.915 AUC while the fine in-interval target stays at chance (0.524, 95% CI [0.482, 0.564])'
Section 4: 'It does not establish the prevalence of this failure mode or validate the audit across devices, institutions, or acquisition workflows.'

arxiv:2608.09265.rationale: Mathematically rigorous optimal transport/Gromov-Wasserstein paper for Gaussian mixtures, but outside the core LLM/NLP/agent/alignment preferences; only tangential mathematical relevance. Theoretical results are formally proven, while empirical evidence is synthetic and qualitative with no quantitative baselines or ablations.
evidence: Section 3, Theorem 3.4 proves a large-penalty value estimate for finite EPOT.
Section 4, Theorem 4.1 proves narrow convergence of induced continuous Gaussian-mixture transport plans.
Section 5, Theorem 5.1 states metric property and large-penalty convergence for partial mixture GW.
Section 7 provides only synthetic qualitative experiments without quantitative metrics or ablations.
Section 8 provides a GitHub code availability statement.

arxiv:2608.09264.rationale: Out-of-scope pure medical imaging/MRI translation paper with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, safety, or language methodology. Method adapts content-style disentanglement and GAN losses to cross-field MRI, which is incremental. Quantitative paired-test metrics and a loss ablation are reported, but no external baselines or significance testing support claims. Code is stated as available; implementation details are adequate. Final score capped at 0.20 per rubric for medical imaging applications.
evidence: Abstract: proposes a 3D unpaired cross-field MRI translation framework with no language-model components.
Section 2.2: describes content encoder, style encoder, AdaIN-modulated generator, multi-field discriminator, cycle, identity, content, style, and diversity losses.
Table 1 in Results: reports nRMSE, MAE, PSNR, and SSIM for Task 1, Task 2, and Task 3 across T1W, T2W, and FLAIR.
Table 2 in Ablation Study: reports loss-ablation results on a representative T1W Any-to-Any subset without external baseline comparisons.
Section 2.4 Implementation Details: provides optimizer settings, patch sizes, learning rates, and states code availability in the abstract link.

arxiv:2608.09263.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/reasoning/RL methodology with formal analysis of token credit in on-policy self-distillation. Novelty is moderate: the paper synthesizes known identities into three diagnostic checks and reports a credible negative result. Rigor is good for propositions and diagnostics, though empirical scope is narrow (one model, one seed, AIME 2025) and feedback-template confounds limit strength. Detailed protocol supports reproducibility, but no code/data release is stated.
evidence: Section 3.1, Proposition 1: exact local affine equivalence requires d(s,v)=alpha(s)+beta(s)Q_U^pi(s,v) with beta>0; ranking alone is insufficient.
Section 5.1, Table 2: implemented additive token score has raw pooled AUC 0.505 [0.483, 0.524], length-adjusted AUC 0.474, within-prompt AUC 0.499.
Section 5.3, Table 3: paired AIME 2025 avg@4 shows outcome-only 64.2% versus token-score variants 24.2%-33.9%, with exact p-values <= 1.755e-4.
Section A.12 Limitations: acknowledges one seed, AIME 2025, unequal run lengths, external LLM judge, and positive/negative template violations in two audited runs.

arxiv:2608.09260.rationale: Highly relevant LLM-based Text-to-SQL refinement work under code/NLP preferences. Search-based refinement over regeneration is moderately novel and includes formalization, baselines, and ablations, but internal organizational inconsistencies, sparse formal limitations, and lack of statistical testing limit rigor and evidence strength.
evidence: Section 7.2.1, Table 3 reports SafeQL hybrid improves Bird full dev execution accuracy to 63.3% with DAIL-SQL (+5.8) and 69.4% with OpenSearch-SQL (+5.2).
Section 7.2.2, Table 4 reports Spider execution accuracy 91.7% for SafeQL hybrid, +4.6 over no refinement.
Section 7.3.1, Table 2 reports model-wise gains across Qwen, Llama, and GPT models on Bird mini dev.
Section 7.4 reports ablations showing pruning and systematic optimizations reduce refinement time without accuracy loss.

arxiv:2608.09258.rationale: Pure robotics/multi-robot formation decision using RL; no LLM, language, or NLP methodology, so out of scope and capped at <=0.20. The work has some technical depth in RL-based formation parameter optimization and includes simulations/experiments, but it does not align with the requested AI/LLM research priorities.
evidence: Abstract: frames task as multi-robot formation decision for herding; no LLM/NLP focus.
Section IV-B: uses DDPG to update formation parameters.
Section V-D: comparative simulations against baselines.

arxiv:2608.09256.rationale: Tangential match only through generic multi-agent/orchestration terms in Agents & Tool Use; no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/prompting/RAG/tool-use methodology. The paper is a theoretical multi-agent game-theory study of zero-sum potential team games with supervisor networks and Byzantine resilience. Formal claims are presented, but experiments are small synthetic simulations and not in a language-agent setting, limiting relevance and evidence strength.
evidence: Section III-A defines ZSPTGs, team-Nash gap, and smoothed best response; Section III-B introduces supervisor network.
Section IV-A describes DTOA; Section IV-B Theorem 1 bounds belief-estimation errors; Section IV-C Theorem 2 gives TNG bound.
Section VI reports small synthetic experiments with binary actions, 5 teams, 3 supervisors, 2 agents per team, and an MDP extension.

arxiv:2608.09255.rationale: Out-of-scope pure building-energy ML application with no LLM/NLP/agent/language methodology. Tangential overlap with SHAP interpretability and dataset comparisons only. Domain analysis has some rigor but US-specific, low reproducibility, and no relevance to priority topics; capped <=0.20.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: 'CatBoost consistently achieved the highest predictive performance for the full-feature analysis, reaching R² ≈ 0.90 for ResStock and R² ≈ 0.73 for RECS.'
Page 30 Section 6 Conclusions: 'Total-energy estimation performance declined from R² = 0.726 to 0.61 for RECS and from R² = 0.905 to 0.62 for ResStock.'

Page 29 Section 5.2 Limitations: 'both RECS and ResStock represent snapshots of buildings at a single point in time, which limits the models’ ability to capture temporal variation or changes in energy use related to occupant behavior.'

arxiv:2608.09254.rationale: Highly relevant LLM agent/text-to-SQL evaluation with pre-registration, deterministic scoring, and strong replay reproducibility, but confirmatory evidence is weak due to disclosed test-split contamination, a confounded system-vs-scale comparison, absence of component ablation, synthetic single-family data, and family-level intervals including zero.
evidence: Section 3.5: five hand-authored lexicon phrases matched the entire test ambiguous stratum and could only have been written from the held-out split.
Section 6.3: resampling template families rather than tasks widens both accuracy intervals to include zero, so magnitude is poorly determined.
Section 7: headline comparison is confounded; QueryProof and the 32B baseline differ in parameter count and in everything the scaffolding provides.
Section 6.5: routing helped on validation but reverses on test; no resolved difference is claimed for routing ablation.
Section 3.4: review was performed by one person; reported agreement is test-retest, not inter-annotator agreement.
Section 7: 400 tasks, two synthetic domains generated from a single seed, one model family, one SQL dialect, and no external benchmark.
Appendix B: one-command reproduction from committed raw outputs is claimed, but generation reproducibility is weaker.

arxiv:2608.09253.rationale: Clearly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, and runtime assurance. Method is moderately novel but lacks direct baselines; evaluation is multi-agent/multi-model with ablations and statistics, though limited to 15 filtered skills and a 30-query test set. Evidence is mostly self-reported quantitative results; reproducibility is limited by an anonymous code/data link.
evidence: Section IV-B Table II reports mean success rate and SD across 15 skills and four agent-model configurations, with average base 62.6% vs SkillSentry 77.7%.
Section IV-D Fig. 8 reports self-evolution improvements over 10 iterations on macroeconomic-timeseries-detrending.
Section IV-E Table IV shows ablations for on_enter, failure_patterns, and system-prompt delivery.
Section V Threats to Validity discusses limited skill/agent/model selection and reliance on verifiers.

arxiv:2608.09252.rationale: Hardware accelerator/DSE paper targeting LLM workloads; relevant to LLM inference/efficiency but not a language-model or NLP methodology contribution. Fused/sparse dataflow representation is incremental over prior generators. Quantitative PPA and power-model results are present, but the paper lacks ablations, limitations, and statistical rigor; replication is constrained by commercial ASIC tooling despite a GitHub availability claim.
evidence: Sec. 7.2 reports up to 120k token/s prefill and up to 110 tps decode on MHA benchmarks.
Table 1 reports a FoM 58x higher than prior art and lists PPA metrics for designs D1-D4.
Sec. 7.3 reports 10x better performance at a 700mW constraint and 1.4x better power at the same cycle count.
Sec. 7.4 reports primitive-level power model error of 12.8% and R=0.97 on validation designs.

arxiv:2608.09251.rationale: Highly relevant to core preferences: LLM-based multi-agent systems, Mixture of LoRA experts, hierarchical GRPO/RL, transformer parameter-efficient adaptation, and code generation. Novelty is moderate: combines existing DAG-based MAS, MoE-LoRA, and GRPO with a dual role/subtask factorization and two-layer credit assignment, but is incremental over recent MoE-GRPO and multi-agent RL work. Rigor and evidence are moderate: extensive ablations, OOD tests, budget accounting, formal variance-reduction analysis, and an execution-verified evaluation, but most results are single-seed, trained comparisons are confined to held-out test splits, and evaluation is limited to code-generation benchmarks. Reproducibility is high due to detailed hyperparameters, algorithm pseudocode, and code availability.
evidence: Section 3.2 defines the Mixture of Role-Subtask LoRA Experts with prototype-based semantic router.
Section 3.3 defines hierarchical GRPO with two-layer credit assignment and Proposition 3.1.
Section 4 Experiment reports SRDD and SciCode results across Qwen3-4B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Gemma-4-31B.
Appendix I Implementation Details provides hyperparameters, LoRA rank 8, Ks=4, B=4, M=4, and learning rates.
Appendix J Detailed Experimental Analysis includes budget-accounted trained comparisons and execution-verified evaluation.

arxiv:2608.09250.rationale: Moderately relevant via training/optimization, scaling/efficiency, and data partitioning, but outside core LLM/NLP preferences. arxiv:2608.09225.rationale: Relevant to LLM inference, multi-tenant serving, and AI safety/side-channel defenses, but the core HMAC-salt isolation is a standard per-tenant cache-keying technique already exposed by vLLM, and much of the evaluation is deterministic simulation with analytic controls rather than a measured end-to-end defense. Internal inconsistencies and admitted mismatches weaken rigor and evidence: Table 7 is called a five-point sweep but omits the cited 30%/35% rows; noise-injection ASR differs between Figure 2 text and Table 4; Section 5.5 uses a heuristic different from Theorem 1's payoff. Section 5.5 admits the load benchmark uses v_j/(1-p_j), which differs from the payoff optimized in Theorem 1, so reported breach reductions are not a validation of theorem optimality.
Section 5.6/Table 7 is described as a five-point sweep but lists only four rows and omits the 30%/35% samples cited in the text.
Section 4.2 states boundary salting efficiency is extrapolated from hardware measurements rather than measured directly, and the needed offset parameter is not exposed by current engines.
Section 7 notes that semantic-cache attacks require a different instantiation not evaluated here, and that extended field experiments with real adversarial tenants remain future work.

arxiv:2608.09185.rationale: Relevant as an LLM/coding-agent system with tool use, orchestration, code generation, and retrieval; not Japanese/NLP/safety-focused. Production deployment provides quantitative evidence, but contributions are largely integration of existing agent/repair/skill-memory ideas, evaluation relies on a private benchmark, and some product/model claims are not independently reproducible.
evidence: Abstract: deployment served 3,600 MAU and 18,240 sessions with 87.2% end-to-end success and 73.5% autonomous submission.
Section 4.2/Table 1: Claude Code + SiriusDeliver improves average success to 86.0% from 71.5% and reduces tokens from 124.0K to 86.9K.
Section 4.2 ablation: removing hierarchical skill orchestration drops success from 86.0% to 74.5%.
Section 4.3/Figure 8: A/B test reports median delivery time reduced from 228 to 23 minutes and engineer effort from 95 to 11 minutes.
Appendix A.2: private benchmark cannot be released and public DataClawEval is not used for reported results.

arxiv:2608.09184.rationale: Relevant LLM-agent/RAG/LoRA methodology applied to a narrow network CLI domain, but experimental support is largely qualitative: figures are cited without numeric results, error bars, or significance tests, and reproducibility details are thin.
evidence: Section IV-A describes 140 interaction turns, K=5, Qwen3-1.7B/8B/14B, and 300 initialization records but no code/data/hyperparameter availability.
Section IV-B reports conclusions from Fig. 3-5 without providing numeric top-1 success, recall@5, or statistical significance.
Section III-B outlines proposal-side memory and selection-side LoRA updates but lacks implementation details needed for reproduction.

arxiv:2608.09182.rationale: Out-of-scope pure medical imaging/computer vision paper on landmark localization; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, or language methodology. Technical contributions are moderate and supported by experiments on three datasets, but relevance is negligible, so the final score is capped at <=0.20.
evidence: Section 3, Table 1: Reports quantitative MRE/SDR and AoP comparisons on CE, FHU, and IUGC datasets.
Section 3, Table 2: Ablation study for Refinement Paradigm and Error-aware Regularization on CE.
Section 3, Table 3: Hyperparameter study for iteration steps T and tolerance gamma on CE-Test1.
Section 3, Implementation Details: PyTorch, ResNet18, AdamW, batch size, epochs, seeds, and loss weights are described.

arxiv:2608.09181.rationale: Moderately relevant LLM/RAG/code-security application with memory-augmented SAST false-positive triage, but applied rather than core LLM research. Novelty is moderate abstraction of historical FP cases into memories. Rigor and evidence are limited by a small Java benchmark, no confidence intervals or statistical tests, an abstract/Table I mismatch, and tiny confidential industrial validation. Reproducibility is partial via anonymous repo with limited implementation detail.
evidence: Abstract reports F1-score 99.43%, Recall 98.88%, and perfect Precision.
Table I reports Memoir (GPT-4o) Precision 1.0000, Recall 0.9843, and F1-score 0.9921, conflicting with the Abstract Recall/F1.
Section III-C states 865 CodeQL alerts are split 7:1.5:1.5 and the test set is reserved exclusively for final evaluation.
Section III-D states the industrial dataset cannot be released publicly and only aggregated results are reported.
Table III reports small industrial case counts: CodeQL baseline FP 30 reduced to 6; XCheck baseline FP 149 reduced to 8.
Section VII-C lists limitations: memory quality depends on historical labels, no formal soundness guarantees, and evaluation is Java/CodeQL-focused.

arxiv:2608.09177.rationale: Out-of-scope haptics/immersive-sensing paper with no language-model, NLP, transformer, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agent, or safety methodology. Slight robotics/embodied overlap via actuators and micromanipulation, but pure domain application, so score capped at 0.20. Subject experiments, statistical comparisons, and a hardware demonstration give moderate internal validity, but sample size is small, hardware is specialized, and generalizability is limited.
evidence: Abstract and Section I describe wearable fabric actuators and McKibben artificial muscles for directional guidance in immersive space; no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/RAG/agent/code/safety methodology is present.
Section V-A reports 15 healthy subjects aged 21-25 and four guidance conditions: surface haptic with/without pressure adjustment, simple haptic, and synthesized speech.
Section V-B reports horizontal and vertical gaze errors across conditions, with synthesized speech significantly lower than haptic conditions (Friedman test with Dunn-Bonferroni correction, p<0.001).
Section VI-B reports identified target objects and states the proposed method had significantly higher counts than the other conditions (Friedman test with Dunn-Bonferroni correction, p<0.05).

arxiv:2608.09176.rationale: Relevant to multimodal VLM efficiency and scaling/efficiency, but peripheral to core LLM/NLP preferences. The consequence-sensitive allocation idea is a modestly novel adaptation of cost-sensitive principles to visual token budgets, with a controlled within-task design. Rigor is moderate: statistical protocols and multiple metrics are reported, but some generalization results have CIs including zero and the latency claim is not fully reconciled with the latency table. Reproducibility is limited by detailed supplement but no clear code/data release.
evidence: Section 5.1 Table 2: cost-aware allocation reduces high-tier error from 0.300 to 0.133 (McNemar 54:4), while average error rises from 0.337 to 0.488, showing explicit CWE tradeoff.
Appendix K Limitations: consequence weights are predefined design parameters rather than measured downstream costs.
Section 5.4/Appendix E: LLaVA-OneVision r=5 ΔCWE CI [-0.009,0.073] and ChartQA CI [-0.019,0.065] include zero, weakening generalization claims.
Section 5.6 Table 15: 304-token resolution reports 26.1% latency reduction, while text claims approximately 21% for the deployed allocation, a minor inconsistency.

arxiv:2608.09174.rationale: Pure bearing fault-diagnosis CNN application with no LLM/NLP/agent/language methodology or listed preference topics; evaluated quality is moderate with ablations and comparisons but limited to one dataset, one load condition, and no statistical replication.
evidence: Abstract: proposes time-frequency dual-domain multi-scale CNN for bearing fault diagnosis under noise.
Section III: architecture uses time-domain and FFT frequency-domain branches; no language-model or NLP methodology.
Section IV-A: single CWRU dataset, 1 HP load, stratified 75/25 split, CPU training, fixed seed 42.
Section IV-D: ablation reports time-domain multi-scale +5.56 pp and frequency-domain +1.68 pp contributions.
Section V: limitations include only CWRU 1 HP validation and future multi-load/Paderborn/XJTU-SY generalization work.

arxiv:2608.09168.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, skill/tool use, retrieval, and selective execution. The post-retrieval utility gate is a plausible incremental contribution, but the evidence base is small (288 rollouts/72 queries) and much of the main evaluation rests on binary reward labels with limited held-out query coverage. Cross-retriever and cross-agent analyses add generalization support, though several target-agent rows are underpowered or have acknowledged leakage limits, and no code/data release is indicated.
evidence: Abstract: RADEG evaluated on 288 collected rollouts; claims reduced unnecessary agent executions while preserving downstream verifier reward.
Section 5.1: source dataset contains 288 rollouts from 72 queries with 194 zero-reward and 94 positive-reward executions; query-level 70/30 splits used.
Table 3: RADEG reports AUROC 0.717, AUPRC 0.570, 68% calls saved, 61% reward retained at tau=0.5.
Table 4: fixed-budget reward retention at 20% budget is 40% for RADEG versus 15% for PPR-Gate and 19% for Random-Gate.
Section C.3: cross-agent limitations include multiple bundle variants per query and underpowered target streams.

arxiv:2608.09167.rationale: Pure robotics/haptics study on wearable McKibben actuators for hand positional guidance. No LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, prompting, agents, or language methodology. Per rubric, pure robotics applications are out of scope and must receive at most 0.20. Empirical work has some rigor but no relevance to target preferences.
evidence: Abstract: proposes hand positional guidance using McKibben-based surface tactile sensations; no LLM/NLP methods
Index Terms: Haptics and Haptic Interfaces, Wearable Robotics, Physically Assistive Devices

arxiv:2608.09166.rationale: Pure robotics/conformal prediction paper with no LLM, NLP, or language methodology. Technically reasonable with formal guarantees and simulation evaluations, but the domain is explicitly out of scope (pure robotics), so relevance is very low and the final score is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract describes CaPTURe as a geometry-aware, conformal prediction-based algorithm for contact-aware uncertainty calibration in robot configuration spaces.
Section 6.1 Table 1 reports empirical coverage and C-space volume over 427,680 marble labyrinth test cases.
Section 6.3 Limitations states guarantees are single-step and the method assumes known environmental constraints and a correct stratum indexer.

arxiv:2608.09164.rationale: Relevant LLM privacy-preference alignment and evaluation paper using in-context personalization. Strong evidence for main quantitative claims and high reproducibility, but limited to one English-language interpersonal privacy dataset, no formal significance testing, and moderate novelty.
evidence: Section 3.3: CIDER contains 1,650 contextual disclosure boundaries from 169 users across 60 scenarios, with variants varying granularity and identifiability.
Section 4.2.1 and Table 1: HC k=6 vs no-history accuracy increases from 60.57% to 71.98% for Claude Sonnet 4.6 (11.41 pp) and 61.87% to 72.45% for GPT-5.4.
Section 4.2.2: only Claude Sonnet 4.6 demonstrates consistent reduction in both FP and FN rates across all variants.
Appendix A.2 and Reproducibility Statement: full prompts, code, dataset links, and random seed are provided.
Limitations: dataset is a single-session snapshot and privacy preferences may evolve over time, limiting generalizability.

arxiv:2608.09162.rationale: Low preference relevance: tabular numeric feature transformation, not LLM/language/NLP; only weak overlap with Training & Optimization/Data preferences. Method has some principled novelty in the supervised smoothness objective, but empirical claims overstate: Table 1 shows mixed raw gaps and supervised stretch is not uniformly best (e.g., MLP score 0.6343 vs PLE 0.6835; RealMLP Avg Acc 0.837 vs Minmax 0.839). Evaluation uses a fixed split, custom seed-std significance, and no code release, though 38 datasets/5 models provide breadth.
evidence: Abstract claims supervised stretch consistently outperforms all baselines
Table 1 shows mixed per-model normalized scores and small raw Avg Acc/R2 differences, with supervised stretch not top for all model rows
Section 4.2 uses custom pairwise statistical criterion; Appendix B.4 defines fixed split and seed-std-based filtering
Appendix B provides detailed hyperparameters/protocol but no code availability statement

arxiv:2608.09160.rationale: Core LLM serving/efficiency paper targeting TP QK-Norm, so preference relevance is high. The work is a plausible systems contribution but largely combines existing scalar aggregation with overlap and persistent execution; evaluation covers multiple OLMo models and baselines, but lacks error bars/statistical tests, code release, and detailed ablations, limiting strength and reproducibility.
evidence: §II-C reports TP QK-Norm overhead grows from 20.0% on two GPUs to 30.1% on four GPUs for OLMo2.
§IV-B reports SwiftQK reduces QK-Norm latency by 81.4–93.9% vs All-Gather QK-Norm and by 29.4–77.0% vs MiniMax(fusion).
§IV-D reports SwiftQK reduces TPOT by 29.5% and increases saturated request throughput by 25.4% on average vs All-Gather baseline.

arxiv:2608.10033.rationale: Out-of-scope pure robotics/haptics micromanipulation paper with no language-model or NLP methodology; relevant only to a low-weight robotics/manipulation preference. Research quality is modest: within-subject experiment with N=6 novices, microbeads instead of biological oocytes, appropriate non-parametric statistics, but limited clinical generalizability. Hard capped at 0.20 as non-language pure domain application.
evidence: Section IV-A: six novice participants, microbead transfer task under five conditions with completion time, NASA-TLX, and Likert questionnaires.
Section IV-B: Friedman test p<0.001, W=0.59, with Dunn post hoc comparisons showing immersive conditions faster than conventional.
Section V: limitations include small sample, microbeads rather than oocytes, and inability to exclude false negatives.
Section III-C: McKibben-based fabric actuators provide aspiration, discharge, and contact haptic sensations.

arxiv:2608.09158.rationale: Audio-language model safety/red-teaming paper. Relevant to AI safety, red teaming, and multimodal speech-audio preferences, but the core methodology is audio-signal adversarial attack rather than language-model or NLP advances, limiting topical fit. The paper provides quantitative baselines, ablations, multi-model transfer, and statistical tests, but lacks real over-the-air validation and code/data release.
evidence: Experiments, Table 1: reports ILL accuracy drops including 67 pp on StepAudio RAVDESS and transfer across six LALMs.
Acoustic Stealthiness, Table 2 and Figure 3: reports ILL ANR 0.06-0.08% and mean human audibility 1.33 vs clean 1.17.
Defense Evaluation, Table 3 and Figure 4: reports DRG detection F1 89.69-99.00% and mean attacked accuracy recovery from 28.5% to 46.1%.
Limitations: explicitly notes simulated microphone reception, no complete real acoustic path, and no established causal mechanism.
Appendix E: provides paired statistical tests comparing ILL with baselines.

arxiv:2608.09156.rationale: Out-of-scope esports/HCI coaching framework paper with no LLM/NLP/AI methodology. It presents a conceptual synthesis and hypothetical League of Legends scenarios rather than computational modeling, empirical results, or quantitative evaluation. Implications are explicitly described as unvalidated possibilities.
evidence: Abstract: framework is demonstrated through illustrative esports scenarios rather than empirical or computational validation.
Section 6: implications are stated as conceptual and applied possibilities rather than empirically validated outcomes.
Section 7: future research calls for experimental studies, indicating current lack of empirical evaluation.

arxiv:2608.09155.rationale: Relevant to LLM routing and multi-agent orchestration with a controlled role/deployment-conditioned substitution study, but synthetic tasks, limited seeds/tasks, no statistical significance tests or external routing baselines weaken rigor and evidence.
evidence: Section 4.1/Table 1 reports Mixed Qwen/GPT frequency-count RMSE 4.818 medium vs 1.538 strong, while Qwen-only is 4.843 vs 5.091, showing a deployment-dependent reversal.
Section 4.2/Table 2 reports matched merge-node interventions: Mixed 192/192 improve, Qwen-only 126/192 improve and 66 harm.
Appendix Table 8 reports homogeneous ladders GPT-5.4 RMSE 1.558 to 1.070 and Qwen3 4.503 to 2.997, with evolved allocation using two strong calls per task.
Appendix S1/S2 provide seed/protocol details: seeds 101-103, 16 training/32 test tasks, five acquisition iterations, and full system prompts.

arxiv:2608.09154.rationale: Highly relevant LLM instruction-following/constraint-synthesis benchmark. Common-constraint generation and post-summarization evaluation are moderately novel but incremental. Empirical support relies heavily on LLM judges with small human evaluation and no significance testing; moderate rigor and reproducibility via released code/prompts.
evidence: Section 3.2 and Table 1 report satisfaction-rate drops for GPT-5 Mini and Llama-3 8B and naturalness win-rate improvements.
Section 3.1.3 reports 100 human comparisons, 60% agreement, and Cohen's kappa of 0.310.
Appendix C includes prompts/templates; Section 4.1 covers three-domain benchmark construction.

arxiv:2608.09153.rationale: Highly relevant to AI agents, reasoning, and RAG/context engineering, with moderate methodological novelty. However, evaluation is synthetic-only with a small sample, no external baselines or production validation, and no public code/data, limiting rigor, evidence strength, and generalizability.
evidence: Section 8.2 Table 1 reports 72.7% root cause node accuracy and Acc@3 85%.
Section 8.3 Table 2 reports 96% operation accuracy and 82% path accuracy on synthetic traces.
Appendix D.1 states evaluation uses synthetic simulation due to proprietary constraints and absence of open benchmarks.
Appendix I.1 Table 5 reports holistic 40% vs iterative 20% node accuracy on only 10 complex traces.

arxiv:2608.09152.rationale: Vision-language person anomaly search using CLIP/X2VLM-style encoders and null-space/Riemannian optimization. Relevant to multimodal AI and computer vision but lacks LLM/agent/reasoning/NLP methodology; near out-of-scope domain application. Method is incremental: combines existing null-space projection, semantic codebook, and Riemannian gradient rectification. Quantitative comparisons and ablations support gains, but no significance testing and task-specific scope limit strength.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 2
Appendix C, Table 7
Section 4.1.2 Implementation Details

arxiv:2608.09150.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision image super-resolution with no LLM/NLP/language methodology, so capped low. The gradient conflict method is incremental over existing MGDA/projection and residual-calibration ideas. Experiments are broad but limited to one UAV thermal benchmark, lack significance testing and code release, and some model gains are negative.
evidence: Table 1 reports average PSNR/MSE/SSIM/NIQE across UAV-BD and UAV-BI at x4 and x8 with and without OGG-FR.
Experimental Setup specifies the Low-light UAV thermal benchmark split with 925 training and 237 testing images and details hyperparameters.
Ablation Studies reports kappa and beta ablations on UAV-BI x4 for ShuffleMixer, HAT, and HiT.

arxiv:2608.09148.rationale: The paper is a wireless-communications domain application on demand-aware energy-efficient cooperative transmission for LEO satellite networks. It proposes hybrid precoding, RF-chain activation, UE association, and power allocation using cross-entropy and Dinkelbach/quadratic-transform methods. Despite internal mathematical detail and simulation comparisons in Sections IV-V, it contains no substantive LLM, NLP, reasoning, RAG, agent, multimodal, AI-safety, or other listed preference methodology; the only neural/GNN references are incidental prior-work citations. As a pure domain application, it is out of scope and capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract frames the work around LEO satellite networks, cooperative transmission, energy efficiency, and non-uniform traffic demand.
Section I and Section II confirm the scope is satellite communication system design, not language-model or NLP/AI methodology.
Section IV details the proposed cross-entropy and fractional-programming algorithms; Section V provides numerical simulations and benchmark comparisons.

arxiv:2608.09147.rationale: Moderately relevant via VLM/CoT/action-token methodology, but core task is monocular 3D detection; no Japanese LLM, safety, RAG, or code relevance. Novelty is incremental but creative. Rigor is moderate: extensive ablations and appendices, but no code/data release, no error bars, and some internal benchmark dependence. Evidence rests on self-reported tables with broad but unverified gains. Generalizes across several detectors and shifts, though largely within related benchmarks. Reproducibility limited by explicit no-code/no-data statement.
evidence: Section 5.1 reports RefineAny3D gains on the Refine3D benchmark over Qwen3-VL baselines.
Appendix B provides implementation details, hyperparameters, and hardware.
Appendix A compares RefineAny3D against geometric projection fitting and a DINOv2 classifier.
NeurIPS Paper Checklist item 5 states code and data are not released at submission time.

arxiv:2608.09146.rationale: Out of scope: this is a neural SLAM/robotic perception paper using vision foundation descriptors (SALAD/DINOv2) and ViT-based depth, with no language model, NLP, reasoning, or agent methodology. The work is an incremental integration of known components (tri-plane submaps, DROID-SLAM-style DBA, SALAD loop closure, distillation), which limits novelty. Quantitative tables and ablations are present, but statistical significance is absent, code is only promised, and custom hardware limits reproducibility. Cap applied for pure robotics/computer vision.
evidence: Abstract: describes multi-submap neural SLAM with local-to-global loop closure and foundation-model descriptor.
Section III-C: states SALAD descriptors from DINO v2 are used for loop closure and DROID-SLAM-based DBA tracking.
Table I: reports PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS on Tanks and Temples against BARF, NoPe-NeRF, LocalRF, and Flow-NeRF.
Table VII: ablation reports ATE, PSNR, memory, and FPS; without multi-submap the system hits OOM, and without online distillation PSNR drops.

arxiv:2608.09145.rationale: Relevant via multimodal MLLM evaluation, LLM-as-judge, and multi-agent feedback, but domain-specific infrared scope limits preference fit and it is not a core LLM methods contribution. The paper provides quantitative diagnosis across 11 models and 5 settings, human-anchor judge calibration, and before/after TGF gains, but lacks error bars/significance tests, has no TGF ablation, limited generalization, and no stated code/data release.
evidence: Table 1 reports human-consensus κ=0.80-0.89 for the Dual-LLM Consensus Judge calibration.
Table 2 reports Acc, τ, F@C, and EQ across IR-only, Translated-RGB, IR+prior, IR+RGB, and IR+RGB+prior for all 11 models.
Figure 3 reports mean IR-only F@C=0.631 and hidden-failure rate HF=36.9%.
Table 5 reports local-200 before/after F@C of 0.878→0.950 (IR+RGB) and 0.872→0.929 (IR+RGB+prior), with answers fixed.
Figure 5 reports r=-0.903 for the association between IR-only accuracy and thermal-grounding drop under Translated-RGB substitution.

arxiv:2608.09144.rationale: This paper is an autonomous driving/ITS system using digital twins and multi-agent RL with self-attention. It is out of scope as a pure robotics/embodied domain application with no LLM/NLP/language methodology; only tangential relevance through reinforcement learning and self-attention. The work provides some quantitative simulation and PoC results but lacks code release and statistical rigor, and evidence is mostly single-site with limited generalizability. Final score limited to 0.20 by out-of-scope policy.
evidence: Abstract: proposes a V2I2V cooperative system using digital twins on roadside units and hierarchical reinforcement learning for CAVs
Section III-D: offline pre-training uses CQL and behavior cloning on the InD dataset
Section III-E: online fine-tuning uses MAPPO with self-attention mechanisms
Section IV-B: multi-intersection simulation validated on Fukuoka, Hyogo, and Tokushima intersections
Section VI: PoC trial reports decision latency approximately 42 ms and stopping distance 8.5 m

arxiv:2608.09143.rationale: This is an instruction-driven 3D human motion editing/generation paper using flow matching and synthetic data from Qwen3-8B. The core contribution is motion modeling/computer vision, not language modeling or LLM research; Qwen is used only for data synthesis, so it is out of scope under the rubric cap. Evidence is moderately strong within its domain, but relevance to the stated preferences is minimal.

arxiv:2608.09142.rationale: Domain-specific clinical LLM application for colorectal cancer treatment planning; largely out of scope despite LLM/agentic/RAG components. Methods assemble existing techniques (continued pretraining, model merging, SFT, GRPO, agentic RAG) with limited methodological novelty. Human evaluation is from five same-institution oncologists on 79 cases, lacks ablations for key components, and automatic/human comparisons are limited. Single-disease/single-institution design and non-public clinical data constrain generalizability and reproducibility.
evidence: Page 4, Results: describes multi-stage training, agentic RAG, and hierarchical reward function.
Page 9-10, Results: reports F1 scores compared with Llama-3.3-70B and MedGemma.
Page 12-13, Results: human evaluation with five UF Health oncologists and mixed-effects model.
Page 17, Discussion: limitations include single disease domain and single institution.

arxiv:2608.09140.rationale: The paper is an LLM privacy/query-delegation study combining PAPILLON with k-anonymity estimation and introducing a small self-disclosure dataset. It is relevant to generic LLM and prompt-optimization preferences, but less aligned with higher-weight preferences beyond LLM and AI safety/privacy. Novelty is incremental because it mainly integrates prior PAPILLON and BRANCH methods. Rigor and evidence are limited by a 166-instance dataset, no confidence intervals, uncalibrated k-anonymity estimates, and mixed optimization results; the authors explicitly acknowledge key limitations. Generalizability is moderate due to held-out PUPA-TNB evaluation and multiple local models, but is constrained by English-only data and small scale. Reproducibility is moderate: prompts and models are documented, but code/data release is not indicated.
evidence: Section 3.2 states PUPA-SD contains 166 turns after filtering 40,000 initial conversation turns from WildChat and LMSYS-Chat-1M.
Table 2 reports post-optimization Llama-3.2-3B quality 67.37, PII leakage 11.03, and k-anonymity 95.46 on PUPA-TNB.
Section 5.1 reports Spearman correlation -0.4045 (p<10^-12) between number of PIIs and estimated k-anonymity, framed only as a sanity check.
Limitation section states the k-anonymity estimator is not calibrated against real population statistics and PUPA-SD contains only 166 instances.

arxiv:2608.09139.rationale: Moderate relevance: uses VLM post-training with GRPO, reasoning, and benchmark/evaluation, but the core task is video codec quality assessment, a domain-specific multimodal/vision application rather than core LLM/NLP. Novelty is moderate for facet-anchored GRPO and the codec-quality benchmark, but builds closely on Q-Insight/VQ-Insight. Rigor is limited by absent inter-annotator agreement, no statistical significance tests, and no explicit limitations. Evidence is adequate from quantitative tables and ablations but lacks uncertainty quantification. Generalization is tested on source-disjoint content and extrapolated temporal context. Reproducibility is partial: hyperparameters and models are given, but exact fusion weights, code, and full data pipeline are not available in the main text.
evidence: Quantitative Results, Table 1: CodecArena Qwen2.5-VL-7B reports SRCC 0.871/0.902/0.906 and PLCC 0.906/0.912/0.908 at K=1/7/14; Qwen3-VL-8B reports SRCC 0.877/0.895/0.894 and PLCC 0.909/0.923/0.924.
Quantitative Results, Table 2: pairwise accuracy for Qwen2.5-VL-7B is 89.5/92.7/92.3 and for Qwen3-VL-8B is 93.7/94.9/93.0 at K=1/7/14.
Ablation Study, Table 3: cumulative additions from Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct improve SRCC from 0.716 to 0.877 at K=1 and from 0.695 to 0.894 at K=14.
Implementation Details: uses Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, N=8, β=1e-3, λf=0.6, λt=0.2, 2 epochs, 8 NVIDIA A800 GPUs, learning rate 1e-6, effective batch size 128.

arxiv:2608.09138.rationale: Pure robotics manipulation paper: it accelerates imitation-learned policies with an RL speed policy. Although it uses Transformer-based ACT and RL, it has no language modeling, NLP, or LLM methodology, so it is out-of-scope and capped at 0.20. Within that scope, it has reasonable ablations and sim/real results but limited generalizability and moderate statistical support.
evidence: Section IV-C reports over 2.4x speed-up across six tasks compared with the original ACT policy and states SpeedTuning retains success at increased speeds.
Section V contains ablations on base task policy, image observations, speed reward exponent, and frame skip using Simulated Tea Bag Transfer.
Section IV-B describes evaluation on six manipulation tasks, split between simulated and real-world ALOHA setups.

arxiv:2608.09137.rationale: Pure low-light image enhancement/computer vision paper with no language methodology, so relevance is minimal under the rubric. The NB model is explicitly diagnostic and does not drive the fixed bilateral post-processing; evaluation is limited to 15 test pairs from LOL-v1 without confidence bounds.
evidence: Abstract: describes training-free low-light enhancement with bright-channel Retinex and conditional negative-binomial noise analysis; no LLM/NLP methodology.
Section IV: states neither r nor conditional variance is used to determine output or fixed bilateral-filter parameters.
Section V-A: evaluation on LOL-v1 Eval15, containing 15 test pairs.
Section V-C/Table I: Retinexformer (trained) substantially stronger in PSNR/SSIM/FSIMc; Ours-B best only among non-trained conventional and image processing methods.
Section V-D: TV-regularised NB-MAP variants all achieve PSNR <=16.61 dB versus 17.17 dB baseline; adaptive variance variants do not improve fixed filter.

fallback:06deac5c77308e1b.rationale: Abstract-only product announcement about Google Ads/Analytics Advisor UI; no LLM/NLP methodology, no research evaluation, and no results or reproduction details, so it is out of scope and unsupported.

arxiv:2608.09133.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer-vision/diffusion super-resolution paper with no language methodology; despite incidental transformer/attention/LoRA terms, it does not target LLM/NLP/agent/alignment topics. The dual pixel-grounding contribution is incremental over prior pixel-guided SR methods; internal ablations and benchmark tables support claims but lack independent verification and broad applicability beyond FLUX-based SR.
evidence: Abstract: describes image SR and latent diffusion transformer fidelity bottleneck.
Section 3.2: details Condition-Side Trajectory Guidance and Decoder-Side Pixel Grounding.
Table 1: quantitative comparison on DIV2K-Val, DRealSR, RealSR.
Table 2 and Section 4.2: ablation of pathway components.
Appendix A: implementation details; no code availability or external verification.

arxiv:2608.09132.rationale: Game security anomaly-detection paper outside LLM/NLP/AI-ML scope; no relevant preference topics. Some domain novelty via role-normalized behavioral fingerprints, but limited rigor due to no baselines, no true misuse labels, small controlled validation, and single-game evaluation.
evidence: Section 5.1 describes data collection via Riot Games API, 100 accounts, and controlled behavioral-change validation with 10 accounts.
Section 5.2 reports intra-account distances (max 3.293) below inter-account distances (min 4.489).
Section 6.1 reports 8/10 controlled accounts exceeded threshold 4.62.
Section 6.2 acknowledges limitations including small dataset, one game, controlled setting, and long-term misuse.

arxiv:2608.09130.rationale: Moderately relevant as a multi-agent reinforcement learning and resource-allocation systems paper; no LLM/NLP/core language methodology. The work has useful quantitative comparisons, ablations, and stress tests, but is simulation-only and lacks code availability or statistical significance testing.
evidence: Section 5.2, Table 1: reports capped MAE and budget-success accuracy for FM vs WLS.
Section 5.3, Table 2: reports main allocation success rates with standard deviations.
Section 5.8, Table 5: reports reward shaping ablation results.

arxiv:2608.09128.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, multi-agent social reasoning, AI-safety-related deception/ToM, and evaluation. Proposes a broad verifiable game benchmark (Social Gym) and training-free self-play reflection-transfer method (SPaRTan). Strengths include 21 games, Elo/Bradley-Terry with bootstrap CIs, cross-game and cross-model transfer experiments, open-weights replication, and code/prompt release. Rigor is moderate: many ablations, but per-condition n=30 yields wide CIs, no placebo-playbook control, and several effects are within noise or null.
evidence: Abstract and Section 3: introduces Social Gym with 21 multi-agent social games and an Elo tournament, plus SPaRTan, a training-free play-reflect-transfer loop.
Section 3.4 and Figure 2: reports per-game and overall Elo/win rate for seven LLMs; GPT-5-mini tops at 1110 Elo, Qwen2.5-3B last at 926.
Table 1 and Section 5.1: GPT-5-mini within-game iterated reflection shows non-monotonic alt-side gains peaking at R3, while main-side tradeoffs vary by game.
Section 5.1 and Figure 3: cross-game transfer shows alt-side injection median +7 pp and main-side negative effects, excluding a saturated Chameleon target.
Section 5.3 and Appendix M: Qwen3-32B replication is largely null except Prisoner's Dilemma and Resistance action-channel setups.
Limitations: acknowledges n=30 per condition with roughly +/-18 pp binomial 95% CIs and no placebo-playbook control.
Appendix A: states code, game implementations, prompts, and experiment pipeline are released under MIT license.

Evaluation is confined to one dataset, limiting generalizability.

arxiv:2608.09125.rationale: Surgical VLA deployment with a test-time trajectory-divergence gate is a domain robotics/embodied application rather than LLM/NLP methodology, so preference relevance is capped. Real-robot comparisons and ablations provide some support, but evidence is limited by small trial counts, no statistical significance testing, omitted threshold/training details, and narrow phantom tasks.
evidence: Abstract: reports VLA-based surgical autonomy and hardware success-rate changes (needle 55% to 60%, tissue 55% to 80%).

arxiv:2608.09124.rationale: In-scope LLM/NLP work on hidden elapsed-time conditioning in a frozen-backbone LLM. The benchmark has controlled splits, causal interventions, and explicit limitations, supporting a narrow claim. However, it is synthetic, uses one model with missing ablations, loses to prompt+LoRA, and shows weak held-out family transfer.
evidence: Table 3 reports CI hidden time accuracy 0.9305±0.0134, no-time control 0.5511±0.0042, shuffled time 0.3323±0.0097, and prompt+LoRA timestamp 0.9893±0.0052.
Table 4 reports shuffled-time wrong-state consistency of 0.9115, 0.9230, and 0.8835 across seeds.
Table 5 reports held-out template 0.9357, held-out duration 0.8375, held-out composition 0.8652, and held-out quota-family 0.5065 accuracy.
Section 5.1 states the benchmark is synthetic, limited to Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct with three seeds, uses a fixed not-ablated time encoding, and does not record the exact upstream model revision.
Section 4.5.2 states the work does not show autonomous time tracking, superiority over prompt timestamps, or broad unseen-family transfer.

arxiv:2608.09123.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM reinforcement learning, alignment, prompting, and open-ended NLP. The method is a useful but incremental combination of rubric-selective guidance, policy-support shaping, and decoupled auxiliary optimization. Empirical coverage is broad across two model scales and four domains with several ablations, but evidence lacks reported error bars/statistical tests and explicit limitations, so some point-estimate claims are not fully supported. Reproducibility is aided by detailed hyperparameters though no code/availability statement is included.

Moderately novel but builds on existing self-distillation and feedback-learning methods. arxiv:2608.09095.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM safety, alignment, interpretability, and multilingual NLP. The pathway-level cross-lingual safety transfer is a meaningful but somewhat incremental extension beyond neuron-level baselines. Experiments cover three LLMs, multiple languages, two safety benchmarks, ablations, and leave-one-language-out transfer. Rigor is limited by GPT-4o-based judging with modest low-resource agreement, absent significance testing, and no released code, while hyperparameters and limitations are documented.

arxiv:2608.09087.rationale: Topically relevant to AI safety and multi-agent generative AI governance, but not LLM/NLP methodology. The work is formal control-theoretic analysis under an idealized linear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model. The mathematical development is mostly coherent, but there is a notable internal inconsistency: Section 6.2 retargets attestation to a static once-per-configuration spectral certificate, while Section 7.3/7.5 describe daily per-epoch proof submission. Numerical studies only verify the assumed linear model, with no real generative system evidence, no baselines or ablations, and no released code artifact.

Section 7.6 acknowledges linear isotropic quadratic assumptions and non-convex heterogeneous open problems.

arxiv:2608.09083.rationale: Pure computer vision/biomechanics application for joint torque estimation from RGB images, with no language-model methodology; out-of-scope per stated boundaries. arxiv:2608.09074.rationale: Strong statistical federated-learning methodology with rigorous theory and broad vision experiments, but very low relevance to the stated LLM/NLP/agents/reasoning preferences; only peripheral LLM/LoRA mention and training/optimization/CV overlap.

arxiv:2608.09072.rationale: Highly relevant to coding agents, code generation, and benchmark evaluation. Moderate novelty as a stage-aware repository-level benchmark with intermediate requirement/planning ground truths. Rigor and evidence are moderate: quantitative results and validation are reported, but statistical significance is absent and LLM-judge/human audits use small samples. arxiv:2608.09071.rationale: Technically solid probabilistic operator learning/UQ paper, but topically outside the core LLM/NLP/agent preferences; only weakly matches Scientific AI and training/optimization themes. Sections 3.1-3.3 report quantitative comparisons with Prob-DeepONet on reaction-diffusion, Burgers, and Darcy equations, including relative L2 errors, covariance error curves, correlation maps, and PICP/MPIW.
Section 3.4 presents a hypersonic blunt-body aerothermal case with CFD validation, VAE latent reduction, and wall heat flux covariance results.

arxiv:2608.09069.rationale: Relevant mainly through self-adapting generative AI/LLM governance and adversarial detection, but not language-model methodology. arxiv:2608.09066.rationale: Out-of-scope applied cybersecurity/SSH intrusion detection paper using LightGBM; no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, or other preferred methodology. arxiv:2608.09057.rationale: Text-guided visual autoregressive image editing without LLM/language-model methodology; closest preference areas are computer vision and multimodal AI, but this is out-of-scope as pure CV/image editing. arxiv:2608.09055.rationale: Relevant to LLM/AI-safety infrastructure via verifiable LLM inference and adversarial provider economics, but the core method is economic mechanism design rather than language-model research. arxiv:2608.09052.rationale: Pure computer vision semi-supervised image classification using vision foundation models and LoRA experts; no LLM, NLP, Japanese language methodology, reasoning, agents, or language-based multimodal work. arxiv:2608.09049.rationale: Moderate relevance: uses LLMs for filtering, extractive pseudo-labeling, and node naming in an NLP/taxonomy-induction pipeline, but the contribution is domain-applied to mobile app privacy/security rather than core LLM/reasoning/alignment methodology. arxiv:2608.09048.rationale: Out of scope: pure remote sensing/GIS computer vision application for building footprint quality control, with no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, or language methodology. SAM-LoRA is used as a segmentation backbone, not as a language foundation model. arxiv:2608.09047.rationale: Out-of-scope vision backdoor/data-poisoning paper with no language methodology; only tangential AI safety/attack relevance. arxiv:2608.09046.rationale: Relevant to LLM tokenization, multilingual NLP fairness, evaluation, context-window efficiency, and cost, but the study is a small descriptive benchmark rather than a methodological advance.
