Implementation Details specifies PoolFormer visual encoder, Llama-3.2-1B, LoRA rank 4, Adam optimizer, 50 epochs, batch size 3, and half-precision training.
Limitations acknowledges rule-based pseudo-gloss generation and increased training cost from dual forward passes.

arxiv:2608.09004.rationale: Pure stochastic optimization lower-bound theory with no LLM/NLP/agent methodology; matches only the broad Training & Optimization preference. Formal theorem-proof structure but limited alignment with the core language-model agenda; narrow K=1 fixed-law oracle and discontinuous constructed gradient limit generalizability.
evidence: Section 4, Theorem 4.1 states the Ω(ΔL/ε² + ΔLσ²/ε⁴) lower bound for bounded-noise stochastic first-order oracles.
Section 10, Discussion and limitations states the result applies only to the K=1 fixed-law oracle class and discontinuous g(·,z).

fallback:a122889467738064.rationale: Abstract-only submission on evaluating LLM UI interpretation via HTML/CSS and OpenTelemetry. Topically relevant to LLM/evaluation, but no methods, results, baselines, ablations, or implementation details are provided, so rigor/evidence/reproducibility are very low.
evidence: Document status: abstract_only; no results, methods, or experiments are provided.
はじめに: proposes designing HTML/CSS for LLM interpretation while preserving human-facing appearance and measuring UI interpretation with OpenTelemetry.

arxiv:2608.09001.rationale: Relevant to RAG, AI safety, and evaluation; active-path audit is moderately novel but numeric findings are stack-specific and not a universal ranking. Rigor is limited by single-seed cells, heuristic NEL scorer, and underidentified MI metric, though the canary evidence is strong. Code release is promised but not yet available.
evidence: §III and Table I document DP-R, CA-DP, and Private-RAG generation hooks as stubs.
§VI-A reports OOV email canary recovery of 53/150 under No-Defense and 0/150 under LPRAG.
§VII states single-seed, one-stack, and synthetic-corpus limitations and that NEL_strict is precision-only while MI is not identified.

arxiv:2608.08999.rationale: Out-of-scope image/video diffusion watermarking with no language methodology; only weak relevance via diffusion/vision. Shows some novelty in learnable frequency-domain embeddings and Slerp-based attack simulation, but rigor is limited by single-model evaluation (SD v1.5), no error bars, and reliance on published baseline metrics. Evidence is primarily quantitative BER tables and qualitative figures; generalizability beyond DCT/FFT on SD v1.5 is not established. Code availability is claimed but optimizer and loss-balancing details are incomplete.
evidence: Section 3.4 describes Slerp-based attack simulation and Table 1 lists MSE under attacks.
Section 4.1 describes training setup with Stable Diffusion v1.5 and DiffusionDB prompts.
Table 2 reports BER for DCT/FFT models with and without Slerp simulation.

arxiv:2608.08996.rationale: Relevant mainly as an LLM-based multi-agent application to quantum LDPC discovery; agentic orchestration is central but the paper does not evaluate language-model methodology itself. Quantitative search results and deterministic validation are reported, but lack controlled ablations of the agent components, and several headline code distances remain upper bounds. Reproducibility is limited by code/data availability promised only upon publication.
evidence: Abstract: develops a multi-agent framework for discovering practical qLDPC codes; Methods A: implemented using Claude Code with Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5
Methods B: deterministic evaluator with validity checks, canonical labeling, QDistEvol scoring, and Methods F: MILP distance certification
Tables 1-3: reported code parameters, comparisons, and BP-OSD code-capacity performance; Data and Code availability: will be made publicly available upon publication

arxiv:2608.08995.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, multi-agent systems, and memory/personalization. The compile-vs-retrieve position is moderately novel but builds on skill-library and procedural-memory work. Rigor is limited by synthetic-only evaluation, no formal ablations, and no significance testing. Quantitative evidence from 90 held-out scenarios is suggestive but LLM-judged, single-model-family, and the headline 32/36 win rate excludes false-positive firings. Generalizability is constrained to five synthetic personas; reproducibility is moderate due to a referenced public codebase but incomplete data/prompt specification.
evidence: Section 5.2 Table 2 reports an 88.9% win rate (32-4) with +2.05 personalization gain and -0.28 accuracy cost when mini-agents fire.
Section 5.2 reports trigger accuracy of 72% (36/50 similar scenarios) and a 20% false-positive rate (8/40 different-domain scenarios).
Section 6 Limitations acknowledges synthetic evaluation, a single model family, and static agent triggers as limitations.

arxiv:2608.08994.rationale: Relevant to RAG, LLM augmentation, and LLM-as-judge evaluation, but contributes a small synthetic testbed combining existing retrieval/reranking components with no significance testing or human validation; results are descriptive and domain-specific.
evidence: Abstract reports P@10=1.00 and NDCG@10=0.94 under risk-based reranking and 36/41 judge-supported bullets.
Section 4.5 states the experiment does not include significance tests, bootstrap intervals, or permutation tests and uses only 10 queries.
Section 4.3 states qrels are rule-derived and were not validated through human relevance assessment.
Section 6 notes the corpus is synthetic, the task is domain-specific, and the LLM judge is not ground truth.

arxiv:2608.08993.rationale: This is a theoretical cryptography/complexity paper on Proofs of Space from derandomization and cryptographic assumptions. It has no connection to LLMs, NLP, agents, transformer architectures, reasoning in the LLM sense, multimodal AI, or other preferred topics. Therefore preference relevance is zero and the overall score is very low despite formal theoretical content.
evidence: Abstract states a framework for constructing Proof of Space from derandomization assumptions and cryptographic assumptions.
Section 1 Introduction discusses PoS protocols and plain model constructions.
Section 6 provides Proof of Space constructions from non-interactive and interactive arguments.

arxiv:2608.08990.rationale: Applied educational HCI dissertation using deep speech/video processing; touches LLM summarization (GPT-3.5) and multimodal analysis, but contributes little to core LLM/NLP/transformer methods and has small, mostly English-focused evaluations.
evidence: Chapter 2, Section 5 Evaluation: AIxSpeed attained average playback 1.30x (LibriSpeech) and 1.29x (UME-ERJ) with lower CER/WER than matched constant-speed baselines; MOS ratings were higher but no significance test was reported.

Chapter 3, Section 4 Evaluation of Learning Effectiveness: In 40 participants, FastPerson reduced viewing time by ~53% with t-test p<0.01, while quiz-score differences were non-significant (p=0.864 for Video 1 and p=0.598 for Video 2).

Chapter 4, Section 4 Results: In 10 Japanese learners of English, Profy showed larger observed intelligibility improvement than elicited imitation, but no direct paired significance test was reported; only non-overlapping pre/post confidence intervals are described.

arxiv:2608.08989.rationale: Pure audio domain application: cross-corpus infant-cry transfer audit with frozen audio encoders and an ontology. No LLM/NLP methodology beyond a post-hoc zero-shot audio MLLM appendix, so out of scope under the pure-audio rule and capped at 0.20. The paper is internally detailed and reports many controls, but its contribution is domain-specific and does not align with the stated language-model, reasoning, or agent preferences.
evidence: Section 3.3: frozen audio encoders audited are wav2vec 2.0, WavLM, CLAP, and AST, with handcrafted baselines.
Section 4.1 and Table 2: in-domain macro-F1 comparisons across infant-cry corpora.
Appendix A9: zero-shot audio-language MLLM baseline reported under deliberately asymmetric conditions only.

arxiv:2608.10030.rationale: Highly relevant multi-agent LLM framework for automated behavioral research on AI agents, with clear safety/evaluation implications. Strong methodological detail and empirical checks, though LLM-as-judge scoring and exploratory findings temper confidence.
evidence: Sec. 2.2 describes the multi-agent pipeline for hypothesis generation, matched configuration design, simulation, and blind review.
Sec. 3.1 reports 79 tested hypotheses with 26 reaching BF10≥3, and Sec. 3.2 reports Spearman ρ 0.697-0.939 across three subject LLMs.
Appendix B and E.3 detail the Bayesian monotone-increment model, prior sensitivity, and Monte Carlo error analysis.

arxiv:2608.08984.rationale: Paper is a generic binary-classification evaluation metric study, not an LLM/language-model/transformer/agent/NLP contribution, so preference relevance is low despite inclusion of evaluation and benchmark terms. Methodological rigor is moderate with formal propositions, statistical tests, and transparent limitations, but evidence is bounded, utility results are mixed, and generalizability is limited to tabular imbalanced settings.
evidence: Abstract: reports 18 settings, 12 duplicate-safe grouped repeats, SoftMCC stability mean rank 2.31 and Kendall W 0.659, with selected-model utility showing no advantage.
Section 3 Methodology: defines SoftMCC core score and provides propositions including reduction to hard MCC and one-way equality with Brier skill score under perfect population calibration.
Section 5 Results: Finding 1 states only F1@best survives Holm correction; Finding 2 reports stability advantage; Finding 3 reports calibration sensitivity.
Section 6 Discussion: acknowledges the evidence is limited to binary tabular selection, related settings, and a single ARM evidence family.
Data and Code Availability: states public GitHub repository with code, environment versions, manifests, and artifact hashes.

arxiv:2608.08982.rationale: Out-of-scope interactive video world model/diffusion work without language methodology; only tangential Video & Temporal/RL relevance. Contributions are formal but unsupported: experiments are forthcoming and the sole illustration is an existence proof in a small grid world, so evidence and reproducibility are minimal.
evidence: Abstract: 'experiments are forthcoming.'
Section 5 Limitations: 'The illustration in Figure 1 is an existence proof in a deliberately small environment, not evidence of scale.'

arxiv:2608.08981.rationale: This is a theoretical distributed-computing paper on deterministic rendezvous of anonymous mobile agents in graphs with footprints. It has no substantive LLM/NLP/AI methodology and is out of scope for the stated preferences, so the final score is capped at 0.20. The work provides formal definitions, lemmas, and pseudocode, but no empirical evaluation and no relevance to AI agents, language models, or other target areas.
evidence: Abstract: deterministic rendezvous for two anonymous mobile agents in an anonymous connected graph with footprints
Section 2.3 Detailed description of the algorithm provides pseudocode
Section 2.4 Correctness includes Lemma 2.1, Lemma 2.2, and Theorem 2.1

arxiv:2608.08977.rationale: Pure computer vision/biometrics paper on iris contact-lens detection; no LLM, NLP, agents, reasoning, RAG, safety, or other high-weight language methodology. Per the out-of-scope rule for pure computer vision, relevance is capped low. The paper has reasonable domain-specific experiments, ablations, and training details, but limited generalizability and small datasets keep the overall score low.
evidence: Abstract: focuses on contact lens detection for iris recognition using a two-stage mask-guided attention approach.
Section 1: frames the task as iris biometrics and presentation attack detection, not language-based AI.
Table 1: reports accuracy across UND and IITD iris datasets.
Section 4.4 Table 5: cross-dataset results are limited to iris sensors and show severe degradation in some transfer settings.

arxiv:2608.08976.rationale: Parkinson's screening is a pure medical domain application using face/voice encoders; mechanistic interpretability is mentioned, but there is no LLM/NLP/agent methodology, so relevance is low under the rubric. The label-free synthetic-degradation CAA and alignment principle have some novelty, but the single small YouTubePD subset, post-hoc face-encoder selection, and self-flagged overfitting concerns limit rigor and generalizability.
evidence: Abstract reports voice CAA AUROC 0.765, face anomaly AUROC 0.751, and late fusion AUROC 0.802.
Section 4.1 Setup and Metrics reports evaluated test subset n=157 with 20 PD and 137 controls and bootstrap 95% CIs.
Section 4.2 Main Results Table 1 reports fusion 95% CI [0.70, 0.89] and NPV 0.95.
Section 4.6 Integrity Audits reports permutation p<0.01 and near-zero confound correlations.

arxiv:2608.08975.rationale: Highly relevant LLM-as-judge/evaluation robustness study with a controlled full-paper rhetorical rewrite corpus, multiple AI reviewers, bootstrapped CIs, and detailed limitation analysis. Novelty is moderate; generalizability is limited to ICLR 2026 ML papers and specific model families, and many analyses are descriptive with single-review primary sampling. Reproducibility is partially supported by prompt templates, execution details, and a project page.
evidence: Section 3.1: controlled corpus of 120 anonymized ICLR 2026 submissions and 4,080 rewrites across six rhetorical dimensions.
Table 3: evidence framing and novelty stance produce the largest positive-negative OA contrasts, followed by scope framing.
Section 4.3: AI reviewer starting score conditions score movement, with lower scores tending to rise and higher scores tending to fall.
Limitations: restricted to ICLR 2026 submissions with recoverable source; missingness may not be random; six rhetorical dimensions are not orthogonal.
Appendix B: 42,396 valid structured review records and direct API cost accounting.

arxiv:2608.08971.rationale: Out-of-scope HCI/AR interface synthesis paper. It uses LLMs only as auxiliary components for ergonomic scoring and semantic enrichment, not as a language-model methodology contribution. Evaluation is expert-focused and small-sample with no task-specific baseline, so even within HCI the evidence is suggestive rather than strong.
evidence: Abstract: presents Generative Proxy for proxy-based AR interfaces using scene, intent, and device capabilities
Section 4.3: uses LLM-based ergonomic score alongside rule-based costs for ranking candidates
Section 5: LLM calls reserved for ergonomic plausibility and semantic enrichment; GPT 5.5 mentioned
Section 8.3: expert evaluation with N=12 reports Likert ratings and ranking agreement

arxiv:2608.08968.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, software engineering/RCA, and reasoning preferences. The graph-augmented agentic workflow, STRIX scoring, and SURE-Score are moderately novel but largely incremental over prior LLM RCA agents. Evaluation includes many baselines, ablations, parameter studies, and significance tests, raising rigor, but main results rely on two small microservice benchmarks with incomplete reporting for AegisLab, SURE-Score evaluator divergence, and some inconsistency in improvement claims. Reproducibility is limited by unavailable code and restricted data.
evidence: Abstract: GALA+ surpasses the best LLM-based baseline by more than 25 percentage points in AC@1 and receives highest SURE-Score and human SRE ratings.
Section 5.3.1 Table 1: GALA+ achieves 74.44% AC@1 on OnlineBoutique and 73.33% on TrainTicket versus Flow-of-Action at 48.35% and 47.78%.
Section 5.3.2 Table 3: human SRE evaluation gives GALA+ final scores of 4.4 on OnlineBoutique and 4.2 on TrainTicket.
Section 5.3.3 Table 4: ablations show STRIX components and graph-guided investigation contribute to performance.
Section 8: threats to validity include single-organization expert checklist and controlled fault-injection benchmarks.
Data Availability: source code cannot be released due to an industrial partner agreement; aggregate data are available on request.

arxiv:2608.08965.rationale: Pure low-level computer vision paper on underwater image enhancement. Uses Mixture-of-Experts and HSIC but has no LLM, NLP, language modeling, reasoning, prompting, or agent methodology. Out-of-scope for the stated preferences despite marginal MoE overlap. Quantitative results and ablations are present, but generalization is limited to underwater benchmarks and no code/data availability claims are made.
evidence: Abstract: proposes CoRe-UIE for underwater image enhancement with region-wise degradation and routed experts.
Methodology: describes shared-backbone routed experts, region-adaptive Top-k routing, and HSIC-based disentanglement.
Experiments: reports quantitative comparisons on UIEB, LSUI, and U45 in Tables 1 and 2.
Ablation Study: Table 3 reports ablations for routed experts, shared expert, HSIC, and Top-k settings.

arxiv:2608.10299.rationale: Strong topical relevance to agentic systems, LLM agents, multi-agent self-evolution, and AI safety, though the paper is a qualitative survey rather than an empirical study. It proposes a plausible three-stage taxonomy and distinguishes itself from adjacent surveys, but provides no primary experimental results, baselines, ablations, or quantitative validation. Survey methodology and selection criteria are not sufficiently operationalized for reproduction; limitations are stated but safety and meta co-evolution remain unoperationalized.
evidence: Abstract: describes a survey of co-evolution in agentic systems with a progressive three-stage taxonomy
§2.3 Three-Stage Taxonomy: defines Agent-Agent, Agent-Environment, and Meta Co-Evolution
Limitations: states Meta co-evolution is early-stage and safety/governance are not operationalized
Appendix C: Figure 4 summarizes prior reported results rather than new experiments; within-paper matched comparisons are used

arxiv:2608.10288.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/attention architecture paper with careful epistemic labels and machine-checked proof cores, but empirical support is single-group/small-sample and many key claims are conditional or conjectural; novelty is constrained by formalizing previously introduced PLDR-LLM/PLGA.

arxiv:2608.09900.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM robustness, reasoning, and evaluation. The decoding-time logit-masking stress test is a modest extension of constrained decoding, but framing it as an off-path diagnostic with injected surprisal adds some novelty. Rigor is moderate: multiple families, base/instruct comparisons, ablations, precision controls, and confidence intervals support the main trends, though some scale/70B claims rely on small samples and no multiple-comparison correction. Generalizability is limited to English open-weight autoregressive models and selected tasks. Reproducibility is aided by public benchmarks, code link, and hardware details, but exact prompts are not fully specified.
evidence: Section 2 defines word-initial taboo masking and injected surprisal metric
Section 3.1 reports model families, quantization, and precision controls
Section 4.1 reports alignment gains, Llama exception, and task-specificity
Limitations note English-only scope, open-weights, and no multiple-comparison correction
Appendix H reports code availability and computational setup

arxiv:2608.08964.rationale: Relevant due to LLM benchmark, multimodal diagram generation, and code generation. However, the work has weak rigor: synthesized prompts measure caption-conditioned reconstruction, only 50 SME-validated prompts, edge metrics near floor with limited discriminability, no human evaluation of generated diagrams, and reported significance lacks actual p-values/matrix data. Claims of full open-sourcing are unverifiable.
evidence: Section 4.3, Table 4 reports per-model compile rates and mean DISTS/CLIP/Edge IoU/Edge F1 with 95% CIs.
Section 3.5 reports SME prompt-sufficiency checks on only 50 prompt-image pairs, with grand mean 4.86/5.
Section 7.3 Limitations states edge metrics operate at the floor of their range (best Edge IoU 0.100) and Canny parameters may be insufficiently discriminative.
Section 7.1 describes a manual error analysis of 200 diagrams but does not report inter-rater reliability or a detailed evaluation rubric.

arxiv:2608.08963.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision generalized category discovery paper; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology. The reported ablations and benchmarks are relevant to CV but do not match the target preferences.
evidence: Abstract: 'Generalized Category Discovery aims to recognize known categories while identifying novel ones within unlabeled data.'
Section 5.1 Datasets lists CUB-200, FGVC-Aircraft, Stanford-Cars, Herbarium, Oxford-IIIT Pet.
Table 4 reports ablation of low-frequency, high-frequency, and classification losses.

arxiv:2608.08961.rationale: Relevant to LLM/transformer training efficiency, but not to core LLM/NLP capabilities. The paper benchmarks known optimizers and gradient-memory strategies rather than proposing new methods. Rigor is weak: no statistical variation, single dataset/seed, no hyperparameter tuning, inconsistent method classification (CGD listed as a memory-efficient technique despite being an optimizer), and no explicit limitations. Quantitative tables are reported, but many causal interpretations are unsupported. Generalizability is limited by small models, one hardware setup, and short training.
evidence: §2.1: models include Llama 3.1 1B, ModernBERT, NanoVLM, and Google ViT
§3: hardware and hyperparameters listed; 25 epochs except NanoVLM single epoch
§4.1: reports training-loss tables and best configurations
§4.4: reports training time and checkpointing overhead

arxiv:2608.08960.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, reasoning, and RL-based training; language methodology is central despite the visual-history compression setting. Novelty is moderate: the diagnostic agentic-policy-gap framing is useful, but the proposed two-stage offline/online self-distillation builds on existing GRPO and on-policy distillation methods. Rigor is fairly strong with multi-level diagnostics, ablations, and detailed appendices, but lacks statistical significance testing and relies on an LLM judge. Quantitative evidence supports the main claims, though no error bars are provided. Generalizes across SearchQA/ALFWorld and 3B/7B scales but only one VLM family. Reproducibility is aided by detailed hyperparameters and prompts, but code is only promised for future release.
evidence: Abstract: reports CAPS improves over AgentOCR by 5.0% and 3.4% on SearchQA with 3B and 7B backbones, and by 15.6% and 14.5% on full-history ALFWorld.
Diagnosing the Visual-History Policy Gap, Figure 1(b): GRPO raises SearchQA task success while History QA does not improve, indicating the gap is not OCR-only.
Experiments, Table 1: CAPS reaches 39.2 average EM for 3B and 43.5 for 7B on SearchQA.
Experiments, Table 2: CAPS reaches 93.8% and 95.7% success on full-history ALFWorld for 3B and 7B.
Ablation Studies, Table 3: combining offline and online self-distillation outperforms either stage alone.
Appendix D Limitations: renderer choices are not ablated, method depends on successful text-policy trajectories, and the LLM judge introduces model dependence.

arxiv:2608.08959.rationale: Pure geophysical/domain application using implicit neural representations for 3D gravity inversion. No LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agent, or language methodology. Some Scientific AI relevance is weak, but the paper is out of scope under the rubric, capping final relevance. Method is incremental over prior implicit gravity inversion baselines and validation is mostly synthetic with no ground truth for field data.
evidence: Abstract: proposes unsupervised depth-aware implicit neural representation for 3D gravity inversion without language-model methodology.
Section III-B: reports synthetic PSNR/RMSE/SSIM comparisons against IRLS and IGI baselines.
Section III-C: field experiment lacks ground-truth density, so model-domain metrics are not reported.
Section VII: claims public code availability, but this is untrusted and does not offset domain scope.

arxiv:2608.08958.rationale: Relevant LLM/test-time tree-search method for code mutation with idea prompts. Moderately novel dynamic execution-verified idea bank, but evaluation is narrow: single task, one backbone LLM, five trials, no significance testing, gains near trial variance. Ablations and limitations are present, but generalizability is low and no code release is stated.
evidence: Section 5.3 'Scope of the results' states standard deviation across 5 trials is comparable to mean improvement over baseline and practical signal sits in best-of-n solutions.
Section 6 'Limitations' states all results come from a single task with one backbone LLM, validation split, and gains on the order of trial-to-trial spread.
Section 5.1 reports baseline mean 0.678 and Idea Search mean 0.697 with max 0.728, showing a relatively small plateau break.

arxiv:2608.08957.rationale: Pure computer vision image restoration for road defect detection; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agents, or language methodology. Explicitly out of scope and capped accordingly. The method is moderately evaluated with controlled synthetic degradations, baselines, and ablations, but generalization and reproducibility are limited.
evidence: Abstract reports highest mAP50 in seven of eight held-out degradation conditions.
Section III-B states conditioning records are saved synthetic-corruption parameters, not validated vehicle telemetry.
Section IV-D notes 1.34M parameters, 114 ms latency, duplicate/temporally adjacent frames, and no field generalization.
Table III provides the eight-condition frozen-YOLO11s detection comparison.
Table IV provides the sequential PCM-defocus ablation with non-monotonic module contributions.

arxiv:2608.08955.rationale: Pure 3D point-cloud/2D computer vision damage-assessment application with no language-model, NLP, reasoning, or agent methodology. The mention of vision foundation models/YOLO is incidental and does not align with core preferences. Evidence is qualitative and preliminary, lacking quantitative metrics, baselines, ablations, and reproducibility details.
evidence: Abstract: proposes 3PDA via PointNet, TDA, and anomaly detection, and 2PDA via multi-view 2D projections with vision foundation models.
§2.2: describes PointNet segmentation, Alpha-Complex TDA, and Isolation Forest/one-class SVM anomaly detection.
§2.3: reports one-class SVM false alarms and example isolation forest scores but provides no quantitative metrics.
§3.1: 2PDA uses YOLO detectors on orthogonal projections with IoU matching.
§3.2: describes synthetic damage but reports no quantitative results.
Conclusion: claims preliminary encouraging performance and future fusion work.

arxiv:2608.08954.rationale: Out-of-scope geophysical/scientific ML application using a diffusion model for coastal sea-level ensemble forecasting; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning/vision-language relevance. The marginal-vs-joint calibration finding is interesting and the controlled Lorenz-96 comparisons are informative, but relevance to the stated LLM-centric preferences is minimal, so overall score is capped at 0.20. Methodologically, it uses proper scoring rules and bootstrapping, but limited domain and one architecture limit generalizability.
evidence: Abstract and Section 1 frame the study as probabilistic AI weather/coastal sea-level forecasting with a diffusion model; no LLM, NLP, agents, reasoning, or language methodology appears.
Section 2.1 defines CRPS, Energy Score, Variogram Score and the shuffle-based permutation decomposition; Section 2.2-2.3 describe training/test splits, bootstrap CIs, and Lorenz-96 experiments.
Section 3.1 reports positive CRPS skill but negative VS skill; Section 3.2.2 reports VS/CRPS ratios (dynamical 1.02/0.91, DDPM 0.75, deterministic emulator 0.42-0.58).
Open Research Statement says code and processed data are publicly available.

arxiv:2608.08951.rationale: Pure computer-vision biometric application using Mamba/SSM; no LLM/NLP language methodology, so capped at 0.20. The contribution is an incremental composition of established components (multi-scale depthwise conv, Sobel edge prior, four-direction SSM), with useful quantitative comparison but baselines quoted rather than retrained and limited datasets.
evidence: Section 2.2: defines the Sobel-magnitude structural prior and states it is not a topological invariant.
Section 3.4/Table 1: reports HKPU-NIR and VERA accuracy/EER/params/FLOPs against ResNet50, Vim-S, ViT-S, GLVM.
Section 4: acknowledges the baseline comparison is not a re-run under one training pipeline and notes 7.28G FLOPs cost.
Abstract: states code is available upon request.

arxiv:2608.08950.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM coding agents, code repair, and agent verification. The bidirectional reconstruction idea is moderately novel, but evaluation relies on single-run greedy results without statistical significance or code/data release, and only one benchmark (SWE-bench Verified, mainly Python) is used. Tables provide useful quantitative evidence, but inconsistent Self-Refine behavior and small ablations limit confidence.
evidence: Experiments > Experiment and Results > Table 1 reports GPT-5-mini mini-SWE-agent baseline 56.2% vs RETRACE 63.2%, and MiniMax M2.5 baseline 75.8% vs RETRACE 79.4%.
Experiments > Ablation Studies > Table 2 reports baseline 50.0%, forward-only 56.7%, backward-only 56.7%, and full RETRACE 60.8% on a 120-issue subset with GPT-5-mini.
Experiments > Generalizability to other scaffolds > Table 3 reports OpenHands GPT-5-mini 37.5% to 56.7% and MiniMax M2.5 62.5% to 70.0%.
Limitations notes evaluation is on SWE-bench Verified, primarily Python projects, and that forward/backward stages rely on the same backbone model.

arxiv:2608.08949.rationale: Out-of-scope domain-specific endoscopic SLAM/3D reconstruction paper with no LLM/language methodology. Although it reports ablations and quantitative comparisons, it matches only low-weight medical imaging/computer vision/robotics preferences and is capped at 0.20 per rubric.
evidence: Abstract
Section IV-B Main Results
Section IV-C Ablation Study

arxiv:2608.08947.rationale: Out-of-scope autonomous driving/webcam gaze study without LLM or language methodology; transformer and alignment terms are incidental. The negative result uses multi-seed paired t-tests and a geometric root-cause analysis, but domain-specific and capped at 0.20.
evidence: Table 4, Page 5: all experiments report non-significant gaze benefit with p=0.919, 0.578, 0.667.
Section 5, Page 4: geometric proof reports median hazard object width 36 px vs WebGazer error 196 px, with 93% of objects smaller than the error radius.
Section 4.4, Page 4: causal Transformer experiment uses five random seeds and paired t-test, mean AUC improvement +0.008, p=0.667.

arxiv:2608.08944.rationale: Strongly relevant to RAG, LLM evaluation, and failure diagnosis preferences, with a moderately novel same-failure counterfactual response audit. Rigor and evidence are solid but bounded by a single primary reader, oracle-like edits, and two English multihop benchmarks; exact response recovery is weak. Reproducibility is supported by a described artifact package.

arxiv:2608.10029.rationale: Out of scope for the stated AI/ML preferences: the paper concerns numerical linear algebra and symmetry-exploiting SVD for cryo-EM template matching, with no LLM, NLP, transformer, agent, reasoning, RAG, multimodal-language, or other targeted methodology. Although the paper reports quantitative runtime improvements and code availability within its domain, it is a pure computational biology/imaging application and is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: States focus on 'high-resolution template matching' and diagonalization for cryo-EM, not LLM/NLP/agentic methods.
Section 2 Fast Diagonalization: Discusses block-circulant matrices and Davis' analysis, a classical numerical linear algebra approach.
Section 3: Reports speedups such as '205 times faster per feature' and '25 times less time than computing the full-scale matrix', but these are domain-specific computational results.
Datasets and Code: Provides a Python package at github.com/Lucaslab-Berkeley/Panther-EM, supporting reproducibility within the cryo-EM domain.

arxiv:2608.08942.rationale: In scope: the paper concerns LLM prompting, accessibility/fairness, and an LLM-based prompt-rewriting agent. However, the empirical evidence is weak: reported accuracy spread is only ~1 percentage point, only one pairwise comparison is statistically significant before PET, no semantic-fidelity metric is reported despite a preservation constraint, and no sample size/code/statistical tests are fully specified. The conclusion that PET 'eliminates' disparities overstates non-significant post-hoc pairwise results.
evidence: Section III-E defines PES as 1 - sigma/mu across prompt styles.
Table I reports baseline accuracies from 82.4% (Low Literacy) to 83.4% (Prompt Engineer).
Table II reports only Low Literacy vs Prompt Engineer as significant, with Delta=-1.0 pp and 95% CI [-1.9,-0.1].
Table III and Table IV report post-PET accuracies and pairwise CIs all overlapping zero.
Section V acknowledges limitations: single domain (MedQA), single model family, and synthetic rather than real user cohorts.

arxiv:2608.08941.rationale: Autonomous driving behavioral taxonomy with no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/prompting/RAG/agents/code methodology; only tangential robotics/embodied AI relevance. The paper is systematic and standards-grounded but purely conceptual and illustrative, with no empirical experiments, baselines, or quantitative validation, and no code/data release. Out-of-scope domain application keeps the score very low.
evidence: Abstract: states the taxonomy is illustrative and not complete or comprehensive.
Section 5.3 Table 1: enumerates 21 behaviors across Highway, Urban, and Hub domains.
Section 7.1: defines scenario family generation via ODD x Behavior formalization.
Section 9.1: identifies future directions but provides no code, data, or benchmark release.

arxiv:2608.08940.rationale: Moderately relevant IR/retrieval paper using LLM-generated reasoning views and QPP-based rank fusion; not out of scope but marginal to core LLM methodology. Novelty is incremental combination of known query expansion, QPP, and rank fusion. Rigor limited to one benchmark (Tempo) with leave-one-task-out and some ablations; evidence includes tables and significance tests but hyperparameters and exact training details are incomplete.
evidence: Abstract reports improvement across six retrievers on Tempo and nDCG@10 of 0.297 and 0.303 with p<0.001.
Table 1 reports per-task and mean nDCG@10 for original query and +Ours across six backbones, with mean gains from +2.3 to +6.3 points.
Section 3 reports paired bootstrap over n=1730 queries with mean per-query improvement +0.013 and p<0.001 for SFR K=3.
Table 2 reports SFR original query 0.265, equal-weight fusion 0.284, difficulty-gated K=3 0.297, and per-query oracle 0.364.

arxiv:2608.08939.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, prompt injection, and AI safety. The controlled benchmark offers useful taxonomy and quantitative comparisons, but novelty is incremental given prior mobile-agent prompt injection work, and rigor is limited by only five trials, manual labels, one device family, and no evaluated defenses.
evidence: Section 4.2 describes the evaluation matrix with 340 MobileRun trials and 80 Mobile-Use trials.
Section 6, Table 2 and Table 4 report ASR, CDR, and UAR by vector, model, and framework.
Section 7.2 acknowledges limitations including five trials per configuration, one Android device family, and manual trial labeling.

arxiv:2608.08938.rationale: Qualitative HCI/music-technology study of Musical Metaverse user needs. It does not address LLMs, NLP, reasoning, agents, or any preferred language-model methodology; as a pure audio/metaverse domain application it is out of scope. Workshop-based thematic analysis provides some qualitative evidence but no quantitative or ML validation.
evidence: Abstract: workshops with electroacoustic composers, classical musicians, and music producers on composition, performance, and education.
Page 5: half-day workshops and thematic analysis methods.
Page 18: all groups identify education/preparation as most promising rather than virtual performance.

arxiv:2608.08936.rationale: This paper is a gravitational-wave interferometer quantum optics study of optical-axis misalignment, squeezed states, and spatial-mode entanglement. It contains no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, multimodal, safety, or other preferred AI/ML methodology and is outside all stated preference categories, so it is scored as out of scope.
evidence: Title/Abstract: 'Multimode Quantum Effects of Optical-Axis Misalignment in Gravitational-Wave Interferometers'
Section III Results: quantum-noise-limited sensitivity and squeezing spectra

arxiv:2608.08935.rationale: Moderately relevant due to RAG/LLM/multimodal content, but largely applied sensing/CV with weak language-method evidence. Small n=40 preference-vote RAG comparison, post-hoc categorization, no statistical tests, missing static-prompting results despite abstract claim, and mainly qualitative wireless evidence limit rigor and validity.
evidence: Section 2 Methodology: reports llama3.2 via Ollama, nomic-embed-text, Chroma, and 250-token chunking.
Section 2 Results: Table 1 reports 40 query preference votes with 11 vector wins, 19 graph wins, and 10 ties.
Abstract: claims controlled comparisons against static few-shot prompting, but Section 2 Results provides no corresponding static prompting results.
Section 3.2 Results: Table 2 reports mean detection rates of 91.8% IR-only, 44.2% EO-only, and 94.2% fused over 40 Anti-UAV sequences.
Section 4 Results: Figure 3 only shows detected wireless emitter frequencies and strengths, with no quantitative evaluation.

arxiv:2608.08929.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/affordance grounding with vision-language backbones; no LLM/NLP/agent methodology. Relevance to stated preferences is minimal despite some VLM/CLIP use. Novelty is moderate for introducing NAT benchmarks, but the method is an incremental combination of Grounded-SAM, CLIP, and trainable fusion. Rigor and evidence are limited by one-shot/small benchmarks and table mislabeling; results are quantitative but lack significance testing. Generalizability is domain-limited. Reproducibility is fairly described but code availability is only claimed.
evidence: Sec. 5.1 describes NAT benchmarks and baselines; Table 1/Table 2 report quantitative comparisons.
Sec. 5.4 and Tables 4-6 report ablations for proposed modules; Sec. A6 contains additional ablations.
Sec. A10 discusses limitations including backbone dependence and inference time; Sec. A11 contains failure cases.

arxiv:2608.08927.rationale: Out-of-scope biomedical knowledge graph/data harmonization and software engineering perspective. LLM/agent content is minor and speculative (Sections 9, 10, 12), not a language-model methodology, so capped at <=0.20. The paper is a qualitative synthesis/case study with no quantitative experiments or artifacts; limitations acknowledged in Section 11.
evidence: Abstract: presents biomedical KG infrastructure and software engineering challenges.
Section 11 Scope and Limitations: states engineering-centric focus, qualitative claims, forward-looking AI/agent speculation.
Section 10: LLM-assisted visualization via MCP described as an emerging opportunity, not evaluated.

arxiv:2608.08926.rationale: Out-of-scope biology/medical imaging domain application using genomic language models rather than LLM/NLP methodology; incremental FiLM-style modulation plus uncertainty gating evaluated on a small single-cohort ADNI dataset. Some ablation and statistical evidence, but limited generalizability and no code/data availability.
evidence: §1: proposes GeneFuse, a multimodal learning framework that aligns genetic representations from pre-trained Genomic Language Models (GLMs) with features extracted from images.
§2.1: instantiates the genomic backbone using the Nucleotide Transformer v2 (NT-v2-100M).
§3: final dataset contained N=182 subjects (52 NC, 53 MCI, 77 AD).
Table 1: GeneFuse achieves AUROCs of 0.77 and 0.83 on NC vs. MCI and NC vs. AD.
§4: limitation states experiments were conducted using a single cohort, which may limit generalizability.
§3: no code/data availability statement is provided.

arxiv:2608.08924.rationale: Out-of-scope face-recognition/biometrics security paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology. The proposed combination of VSS, adaptive LSB steganography, SHA-256, and DWT watermarking is incremental; evaluation lacks numeric FR accuracy baselines and some broad security claims conflict with reported table values.
evidence: Abstract and Section 5 claim >99.9% detection against bit-flipping, cropping, substitution, and compression attacks, but Table 8 reports cropping 10% border detection 98.3% and JPEG Q=70 detection 95.2%.
Section 4.4 states Figure 3 shows the proposed technique performs better than Softmax and ArcFace on all benchmarks, but no numeric accuracy values are provided in the text.
Section 3.1 assumptions restrict the framework to frontal faces, trusted third party processing, and distributed storage, limiting generalizability.

arxiv:2608.08922.rationale: Theoretical study of normalized self-attention dynamics; directly relevant to Transformer Architecture/attention mechanism but not to high-weight LLM, Japanese NLP, reasoning, or agent topics. Novelty is moderate relative to prior self-attention clustering and mean-field work. Rigor is limited by heuristic large-N arguments with proofs deferred to an unavailable supplement. Numerical collapse results support claims, but lack full experimental detail and no code/data availability is stated.
evidence: Model and diagnostics.– defines the normalized self-attention dynamics, overlap logits, attention IPR, and participation rank.
Clustered attractor manifold.– derives the overlap-gap condition and clustered fixed-point manifold.
Dynamical accessibility from Gaussian initial conditions.– reports three regimes: diffuse rank collapse, condensed coexistence with a macroscopic cluster, and extensive microscopic fragmentation.
Discussion.– states limitations including d~N scaling and the need for exponential softmax selectivity rather than linear attention.

arxiv:2608.08920.rationale: Pure healthcare/clinical ML application using EHR data; no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent methodology, so relevance is minimal. The domain-structured stacking is incremental but includes patient-grouped CV, ablations, temporal validation, calibration/DCA, and limitations. Evidence is moderate but limited to one health information exchange, one outcome, matched case-control sampling, and no external validation.
evidence: Abstract reports AUROC 0.899 and a domain-structured ensemble for perioperative outcome prediction using EHR data.
Methods II-G describes domain-specific LightGBM models and logistic regression meta-learner with patient-grouped 5-fold CV.
Results III-C domain ablation shows full ensemble AUROC 0.899 vs surgery-only 0.879, with no language-model methodology present.

arxiv:2608.08919.rationale: Medical imaging diffusion-based CBCT-to-CT synthesis with no language methodology, so out of scope by instruction and capped at 0.20. The study compares FDK vs DICOM CBCT conditioning for conditional DDPM on a single anthropomorphic phantom only; no patient data, no statistical testing, limited generalizability. Reported SSIM/PSNR gains are quantitative but unsupported by external validation or code/data release.
evidence: Page 1 Purpose: states low-dose CBCT is insufficient and study develops conditional DDPM-based CBCT-to-CT synthesis for radiotherapy planning.
Page 4 Dataset: uses a solid anthropomorphic head-and-neck phantom with 920 aligned CT-CBCT slice pairs, split 736 train / 184 test.
Page 5 Results: reports DICOM CBCT baseline SSIM≈0.83/PSNR≈25.9 dB; FDK baseline SSIM≈0.26/PSNR≈14.6 dB; FDK-conditioned synthetic CT SSIM=0.817±0.165, PSNR=34.49±6.51 dB.
Page 8 Conclusion: notes limited access to clinical raw CBCT projection data and future work for patient-based validation, multi-scanner evaluation, and dosimetric impact.

arxiv:2608.08915.rationale: Moderately relevant to multimodal AI and NLP/dialogue via CLIP/Qwen3-VL and referential dialogue, but lacks core LLM, Japanese NLP, reasoning, agents, or safety methodology. Methodologically sound with cross-validation, statistical tests, ablations, and a VLM baseline, though novelty is mostly incremental over prior co-speech gesture work and generalization is limited to one controlled Dutch referential task.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports gesture-only top-1 of 19.5-20.4% versus 5.9% chance and top-5 of 55.5-56.4%.
Section 4.2 reports speech-only top-1 of 46.5% and consistent but modest fusion improvement of about 1.6 points.
Section 5.2 reports fusion adds +7.49 points in the least-confident speech quartile and gains near zero in the most confident quartiles.
Limitations note the closed-set 16-object Dutch referential task and unclear generalization to other languages, domains, and interaction types.

arxiv:2608.08911.rationale: Out-of-scope pure audio/acoustic localization for bioacoustics. Only tangential overlap with preference topics via TabPFN/transformer attention and physics-informed ML; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agents, or multimodal language methodology. Method combines physics-derived features, TabPFN regression, gating, and GDOP-scaled conformal uncertainty, with some quantitative field/simulation results, but domain application plus pure audio content caps score at or below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract describes passive acoustic monitoring, physics-informed acoustic features, TabPFN-based learned refinement, and calibrated geometry-aware uncertainty.
Section 4.2 Table 2 reports frozen-lake field and simulation localization errors comparing hyperbolic solver and hybrid gate.
Section 4.4 Table 4 reports empirical coverage for fixed and GDOP-scaled conformal calibration.

arxiv:2608.08910.rationale: Highly relevant LLM quantization/serving systems paper focused on tied trit-plane quantization for MoE experts. Novelty is incremental: the ratio-3 tie and persistent folded format are explicitly situated against prior patents and concurrent work, with the contribution framed as application and measurement. Rigor and evidence are limited by very small behavioral fixtures (n=5), a 100-item MMLU subset, some condition-sensitive/unstable fixtures, no formal equivalence margins, single model family/hardware, and speed claims from short single-stream runs; these limitations are candidly disclosed but constrain strength. Reproducibility is strong with code, pinned commit, model revision, fixture provenance, seeds, and build flags reported.
evidence: Abstract: PTQTP decomposes LLM weight matrices into two ternary (trit) planes with two free per-group scales.
Table 1: Tied ternary shows no detected fidelity difference from q4_k at 4.06 bits.
§6 Limitations: The fixture set is small (n=5 prompts, 14 captured steps whose positions are dependent within a prompt).
§7 Reproducibility: Engine, converter, format, store, and kernel code is in the open-source fucina repository (MIT) at commit d30ce52.

arxiv:2608.08907.rationale: Highly relevant to visual tool use, multimodal LLMs, and RL. The capability-aligned SFT and necessity-gated reward design is a plausible but incremental improvement over Thyme/CodeVision/CodeDance. Stage-wise ablations and behavioral analyses support the claims, but single-run training, one base model, and the absence of significance tests limit confidence. Reproducibility details are strong, though releases are prospective.
evidence: Section 3.2: capability-aligned SFT trajectory synthesis with stepwise committee evidence-gain scoring.
Table 3: stage-wise ablations comparing Distilled SFT, MUT RL, uniform bonus, and ToolVision.
Appendix H.2: each reported configuration is trained once, with seeds documented.
Table 1: main benchmark results and comparisons to Thyme-7B, CodeVision-8B, CodeDance-7B, and base model.
Appendix H.1: code/data release is prospective and full public images are not redistributed.

arxiv:2608.08906.rationale: Federated anomaly detection with memory-augmented autoencoders falls outside the targeted LLM/NLP/agent focus; only tangential attention-mechanism relevance. Novelty is modest for a niche FL aggregation method, but validation is limited to one tabular dataset with no statistical significance testing.
evidence: Section III-A proposes naive aggregation and random row permutation aggregation for MemAE memory modules.
Section IV Tables II and III report F1 and AUC ROC for E=3 and E=50 on KDDCUP10; Table IV reports local training statistics.
Section V acknowledges broader validation is needed across datasets, baselines, and modalities.

arxiv:2608.08904.rationale: Relevant to multimodal VLM interpretability through layer-wise probing and causal ablation of MLP writes, but not core LLM/NLP. Novelty is moderate: weight-matched VLM/VLA comparison and late-MLP localization are useful, though prior representation-degradation work exists. Rigor is limited by a single model pair, one dataset, pseudo-ground-truth depth, and single-seed causal claims. Evidence is quantitative and controlled but not statistically replicated. Generalizability is low. Reproducibility is moderate due to open models and detailed supplementary hyperparameters.
evidence: Section 4.1/Table 2: VLM final-layer d1=0.752 versus VLA d1=0.506; terminal L28->L35 slope +0.040 for VLM versus -0.123 for VLA.

Section 4.2/Table 3: Ablating VLA late MLP writes (L33-35) raises final-layer depth decodability from 0.506 to 0.584 (+0.078), while late attention ablation yields +0.031 and VLM MLP ablation yields +0.015.
Section 4.3/Fig 5: In the VLA, accumulated MLP deposit depth decodability collapses from approximately 0.68 to 0.38 in final blocks, whereas VLM deposits remain highly decodable.
Section 5 Limitations: Study is restricted to one VLM-VLA pair (Molmo2-ER/MolmoAct2-LIBERO) on LIBERO frames, uses Depth-Anything-3 pseudo-ground truth, and acknowledges single-seed causal claims.

arxiv:2608.08898.rationale: Out of scope for preferences: no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agents/safety/multimodal methodology; the paper concerns evolutionary optimization problem characterization via program complexity measures. Quality is preliminary: quantitative correlations are reported but limited to BBOB and simple neural network code, with no strong baselines or statistical confidence, and code availability is only promised after acceptance.
evidence: Abstract: proposes Halstead volume and Shannon entropy over programmatic representations and applies them to BBOB and feed-forward neural network training.
Section 4.3, Table 1: reports Halstead volume and entropy values for 24 BBOB C implementations.
Section 5.2, Table 3: reports negative Spearman correlations between Halstead volume and algorithm AUC, ranging from -0.138 to -0.531.
Section 4.2: discusses limitations of language/style dependence of code complexity measures.
Section 6: states code and data to reproduce experiments are provided via Zenodo URL to be provided after acceptance.

arxiv:2608.08897.rationale: Out-of-scope computational social choice / formal methods paper on voting-rule synthesis; no substantive LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, or multimodal methodology. Although it uses SAT/SMT, CHC, polyhedral computation, and Lean, these are not among the preference topics and the domain is a non-AI/ML application, so the overall score is capped below 0.20.

arxiv:2608.08896.rationale: Domain-specific medical equipment QA application fine-tuning MedGemma via QLoRA. Relevant to LLMs and training/data topics, but it is a pure domain application using a medical foundation model and imaging-system manuals, so capped at out-of-scope relevance. Limited methodological novelty and only baseline comparison constrain rigor and evidence.
evidence: Abstract and Table 2 report F1 0.22 to 0.38, ROUGE-2 0.18 to 0.41, and BERTScore F1 0.86 to 0.91.
Section 3.3 describes QLoRA fine-tuning with rank 16, 15 epochs, and train/validation/test splits.
Section 6 notes lack of comparative benchmarks against other open-source or commercial LLMs and lack of expert human validation.

arxiv:2608.08892.rationale: Data-splitting/leakage audit with only weak relevance to Data & Datasets/evaluation preferences; no LLM/NLP modeling contribution. Novelty is explicitly disclaimed, and evidence is limited by a small outcome-enriched 6-source panel, failure to identify a bridge-specific mechanism, and lack of raw end-to-end reproduction.
evidence: Section 3/Table 1: Doc2Dial union largest-component share is 0.988039 vs 0.013132 content-only and 0.015632 container-only; MyFixit union share is 0.416427; 2 of 6 sources qualify.

Section 5/Table 3-4: bridge_edge_density and mean_union_degree both separate qualifiers; the negative-control Spearman correlation 0.829 meets the registered >=0.8 condition, so mechanism discrimination is not met.
Section 10.1: the six-source panel is outcome-enriched and non-random; 2/6 is explicitly a descriptive panel fraction, not a prevalence estimate.
Section 11.2: raw corpora are not redistributed, no complete one-command raw pipeline is provided, and the Human Know-How loader has an unresolved unicode_escape/mojibake parser risk.

arxiv:2608.08889.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM reasoning, RLVR/GRPO post-training, and LLM-as-judge evaluation, not a pure domain application. The reasoning-collapse finding and conditional length-penalized reward are moderately novel, but persona routing remains preliminary and untrained. Empirical evidence is reasonably detailed but lacks public data/code and uses anonymous proprietary APIs, limiting reproducibility and external validation.
evidence: Section 2.2 Table 1: explicit reasoning degrades proprietary verifier macro-F1 (e.g., Query Sensitivity 0.901 to 0.887).
Section 3.2 Figure 2: completion length drops after ~70 steps under GRPO.
Section 4.2 Table 4: conditional reward recovers Qwen Query Sensitivity to 0.851 and ID Response Quality to 0.572.
Section 5.1 Figure 3: persona-conditioned F1 spans 0.416 to 0.792.
Limitations: persona-routing architecture is not fully trained and proprietary data cannot be publicly released.

arxiv:2608.08888.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM pretraining, transformer architecture, reasoning/CoT, code generation, training efficiency, and inference. The latent-feedback idea is incremental over Feedback Transformer, LRT, and related latent reasoning work, though the gated external feedback and multi-pass scheduling are useful variants. Rigor is moderate: controlled 1B-scale experiments and synthetic probes, but limited ablations and no uncertainty on many generation results. Evidence is mostly self-reported quantitative gains. Reproducibility is limited by proprietary data mixture and no released code.
evidence: Sec. 4 reports 1B-parameter pretraining up to 400B tokens and Fig. 4 shows fused prefill improves validation loss and 5-shot LM Eval accuracy.
Fig. 5 and Table 1 report GSM8K, MATH-500, HumanEval, and MBPP improvements under Soft/Fused decoding and after instruction tuning.
Sec. 3.3 and Fig. 3 describe multi-pass scheduling and show a small fraction of three-pass batches stabilizes long-horizon feedback.
Sec. 6 acknowledges limited 1B scale and heuristic feedback-pass scheduling.

arxiv:2608.08887.rationale: Pure computer-vision smart-surveillance application using YOLOv8/InsightFace/EasyOCR; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, safety, or alignment methodology. The work is an engineering integration of known components, with modest quantitative reporting but small-scale validation and limited independent evidence.
evidence: Section V-A reports 91.2% face match rate, 85.7% ANPR accuracy, and mAP@0.5 0.846-0.889 for fire/knife/weapon modules.
Section V-C states third-party system values are indicative rather than independently confirmed under identical settings.
Section V-D reports a user-acceptance test with only three participants and average task times.
Section V-F lists limitations including no permanent multi-object tracking and a single global face-recognition threshold.

arxiv:2608.08886.rationale: Aerospace domain application with computer-vision pose estimation and spacecraft inertia estimation; no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent/RAG/safety/interpretability/evaluation methodology. The mention of ChatGPT/Gemini is only for language editing. Quantitative simulation comparisons exist, but the paper is out of scope and capped at 0.20 as a pure domain/vision/robotics application.
evidence: Section 3.4 Table 1: KKT+Elliptic reports MAE 3.56e-07 and 0.1849 s vs KKT+EKF 2.27e-06 and 11.1043 s over 100 Monte Carlo runs.
Section 5.3 Table 4: image-based pose estimation median attitude errors are 0.660 deg single-arc and 0.964 deg multi-arc.
Section 6.2 Figure 12: KKT+Elliptic has lower median inertia-tensor error than KKT and KKT+EKF across tested arc lengths.

arxiv:2608.08885.rationale: Pure domain application using GPT-5.1 as a lyric scorer; involves prompting and artifact release but no core LLM/NLP methodological advance. Calibration lacks quantitative human-agreement metrics and the model alias is unpinned, so relevance and research quality are limited.
evidence: Section 2.2 describes calibration on about ten songs and a five-song held-out set, but reports no quantitative agreement metrics.
Section 2.4 states gpt-5.1 is a model alias rather than a pinned snapshot, limiting exact numerical replication.
Section 3.3 reports longitudinal trends with p-values and some artist-demeaned bootstrap confidence intervals.
Section 3.4 reports 456 of 1,259 songs scored as sexually explicit by the method but not flagged by Spotify.

arxiv:2608.08884.rationale: LLM-based robot task planning/HCI system using GPT-5.1 and natural language prompts; relevant to LLM/NLP/prompting/robotics but not a core language-model methodology contribution, and no Japanese/transformer/safety alignment topics. User study is reasonably rigorous with counterbalanced conditions and LMMs, but evidence is mostly self-report; no significant usability/task success improvements.
evidence: Abstract: describes SHRIMP as natural-language robot primitive planning with simulation refinement and N=35 user study showing improved perceived control/transparency.
Section 3.2.2: uses GPT 5.1 as LLM with robot configuration, primitive list, object positions, and user task description to generate plans.
Section 4.1: ablation study compares Plan+Edit vs Plan-Only vs No-Plan within participants.
Section 5: reports significant perceived autonomy p=0.007 and transparency p=0.026 for Plan+Edit vs No-Plan, but no significant SUS or task success differences.
Section 6.3: limitations include slow plan generation, lighting sensitivity, manual grasp points, and simple short-horizon tasks.

arxiv:2608.08883.rationale: Directly relevant as an open-weight RAG-LLM framework with local inference, memory, and research-workflow integration, but largely a system engineering report rather than a methodological or empirical contribution. No quantitative evaluation, ablations, or baselines for the new architecture; limitations are acknowledged but unmeasured.
evidence: Abstract: Recent advances in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and large language models (LLMs) enable researchers to integrate AI into scientific workflows.

Section 3: We deploy AquiLLM on Jetstream2 using separate development and production environments ... Qwen3.6-27B as our default chat model ... vLLM ... local embedding and reranking ... Whisper-large-v3-turbo for transcription.

Section 4 Limitations: we have not yet benchmarked our current approach on informal knowledge artifacts produced collaboratively by research groups such as meeting minutes, Slack messages, code comments, or collection-specific playbooks.

arxiv:2608.08882.rationale: The paper proposes a conceptual framework and evaluation protocol for epistemic transfer in AI-assisted verification. It intersects with factuality/misinformation and evaluation, but it is a human-subjects/HCI methodology paper rather than a technical LLM/NLP contribution, so preference relevance is low. The framework is clearly structured with formal estimands and an analysis plan, but it reports no empirical study, making evidence strength weak and generalizability/reproducibility only potential.
evidence: Abstract and Section 3.1 define epistemic transfer as the effect of prior AI-assisted verification on later unassisted performance; no experimental results are reported.

Section 4 proposes a randomized protocol with conditions, measures, timing, and analysis, but Section 4.7 provides only illustrative power and sample size considerations rather than actual study data.
Section 8 states that the framework is still a proposal needing testing and refinement, and describes boundary conditions.

arxiv:2608.08881.rationale: Moderately relevant empirical LLM/RAG evaluation applied to deception detection. The study is large and statistically detailed, but it is a domain application rather than a core ML methodology contribution; no code/data availability or decoding settings are reported, and findings are text-only and domain-specific.

arxiv:2608.08880.rationale: Domain-specific applied UI screen retrieval/clustering method using frozen CLIP/BERT embeddings and graph propagation. It is not a language-model methodology paper and has minimal LLM/reasoning/agent relevance; treated as out-of-scope domain application with score capped at 0.20. Some novelty in Vietoris-Rips weighting, but evaluation is limited to mobile UI datasets, uses weak baselines, and clustering accuracy remains very low. Code/data are available, supporting reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.08878.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM inference/efficiency and reinforcement learning, with a clear method and transparent limitations, but contribution is incremental amid concurrent learned KV-eviction work. Rigor is limited by approximate reimplemented baselines and an unsupported exact Plackett-Luce subset-probability derivation in Appendix C; reported gains are modest and rely partly on non-official comparisons.

Section 5 Limitations acknowledges 130 GPU-hours, doubled memory, +1.4ms/token overhead, and reimplementation-based comparisons.
Appendix C presents an exact DP log-partition for subset probability that is not adequately supported.

arxiv:2608.08876.rationale: Graph layout/visualization with implicit neural fields; out-of-scope relative to LLM/NLP/agents/core preferences. The paper has moderate methodological substance (ablations, baselines, repo) but domain relevance is very low, so overall score is capped at 0.18.
evidence: Table 1 reports FlingStress vs linear/kernel/PivotMDS/landmark MDS with mean±s.d. over five seeds.
Appendix B.2 provides hyperparameters and the repository URL appears in the Conclusion.

Section 5: no stable significant correlation between Shuffle-Dyck gains and percentage of crossing dependencies; only 154M+GT has some stable correlations.
Limitations: acknowledges only six European languages sharing Latin script and non-Chinchilla-optimal training (~655M tokens).
Appendix A.2 and A.3: provide training hyperparameters, seeds 17/42/3407, and token-efficiency gain algorithm.

arxiv:2608.11261.rationale: This is a materials-science/physics study on organic photovoltaic power conversion efficiency forecasting using molecular dynamics, graph neural networks, and sequential time-series models. It is a pure domain application outside the core LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning scope; Transformer/LSTM appear only as off-the-shelf sequence forecasters, not as language methodology contributions. Quantitative validation and reproducibility claims are present, but AI/ML relevance to the stated preferences is minimal, so the overall score is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: Climate-Native computational framework combines GFN2-xTB molecular dynamics with an equivariant graph neural network surrogate and sequential deep learning models trained on annual time series.
2.5 Architectural Comparison of Sequential Models: Four sequential deep learning architectures were evaluated including Transformer encoder-decoder with multi-head self-attention.
3.5 GNN Surrogate and Sequential Forecasting Models: Sequential forecasting models (LSTM, GRU, Transformer, RNN) were implemented in PyTorch.

arxiv:2608.08795.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, prompt injection/red-teaming, and reflection-based reasoning. The one-shot attacker-tool-disjoint transfer setting and OpenClaw-IPI benchmark add some novelty, but the method largely combines existing reflection and memory mechanisms. Empirical evidence is limited to single-run point estimates with no repeated-run confidence intervals, and the paper explicitly marks repeated-run uncertainty as further work; Validation queries are excluded from the main query ledger, weakening the deployment-budget claims. Reproducibility is constrained by gated artifacts and future/unverifiable model names.
evidence: Table 2 reports ASR/DCSR across ASB and OpenClaw-IPI for three victim models, but states all entries are single-run point estimates on fixed-size splits.
Appendix A Table 5 marks repeated-run uncertainty and validation reuse audit as 'Further experiments required'.
Appendix E documents the one-query Test budget and explicitly excludes Validation from the accounting ledger.
Table 3 provides ablations for Memory Refiner, cross-defense transfer, Attack Generator choice, and fixed synthesis angle.

arxiv:2608.08794.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM/multimodal inference efficiency: it addresses omni-modal LLM token compression, KV-cache pruning, and throughput/memory reduction on Qwen2.5-Omni. The proposed stage-dependent audio-preserving compression is a moderate but useful combination of known tools; evidence includes multi-benchmark tables, ablations, and efficiency analyses, though some baseline comparisons use OOM/dagger averages and code is not released, limiting rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: Table 1 reports A-PACK results across four benchmarks on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B/3B at two prefill-FLOPs tiers.
Table 2 and Figure 4 report memory, prefill speedup, end-to-end speedup, and decoding throughput comparisons.
Table 3 provides stage-combination ablations showing pre-LLM and inner-LLM contributions.
Table 4 compares alignment-scoring alternatives, including Gated CKA.
Supplementary Tables S1 and S5 document hyperparameters and parameter sensitivity.

arxiv:2608.08793.rationale: In-scope agent/coding-agent observability study: passive runtime reconstruction for Agent Skills, relevant to Agents & Tool Use and Code & Programming. The work is useful systems/empirical engineering but incremental over existing trajectory diagnosis and telemetry; claims are descriptive and controlled rather than population-level. Strong preregistration, frozen fixtures, and retained failures support rigor; limited to six repositories, three agents, and one run per cell constrains generalizability.
evidence: Section 4.2 defines 126 cells across six frozen repository profiles, three coding agents, and seven conditions with integrity/response gates.

Section 5.1 Table 4 reports harness-dependent reconstruction: Codex 0/42 Skill runs, OpenCode 0/24 failure-like events, Qoder 6/6 clean failure-like events; all 126 sessions correlate but adapter semantics diverge.
Section 5.2 Table 5 reports Qwen exact/boundary/status/citation entailment counts, including Raw failure status on 18 clean cases and Panorama zero clean false positives.
Section 5.6 and Section 8 state external-validity limitations: controlled overlays, one execution per cell, descriptive counts, no population inference.
Section 9 claims public source, frozen artifact, data release, and 279 passing tests with 10 environment-dependent skips.

arxiv:2608.08791.rationale: Relevant to LLM robustness, calibration, and interpretability, with thorough ablations and clear metrics, but effects are modest, diffusion-specific, and generalize only partially across tasks.
evidence: Results: Table 1 reports LCR AUROC 0.665 versus base 0.575, while TS/DATS improve ECE to 0.133 but leave AUROC unchanged at 0.575.
Generalization and limitations: across eleven benchmarks the tool helps on five and gives no test gain on six; WinoGrande hurts by 0.070.
Experimental Setup: evaluates LLaDA-8B-Instruct, DREAM-7B-Instruct, LLaMA-3-8B, and Qwen-2.5-7B on GSM8K/ARC-Challenge with four noise types and matched clean prompts.

arxiv:2608.08788.rationale: Pure time-series forecasting paper on Koopman operators and neural decomposition, outside LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning scope. Only incidental Transformer/attention mentions as baselines. Some novelty in unified end-to-end decomposition and frequency-dependent Koopman modeling, but rigor is limited by no ablations, no statistical significance, and narrow benchmark evaluation.
evidence: Abstract states focus on Koopman theory, deep learning, and forecasting, with no language/NLP methodology.
II-C describes learnable signal decomposition, NVMD, and Koopman networks.
III-A Experimental Setup lists ECL, ETTh2, ILI, and ECG benchmarks and reproduced baselines.
Table I reports MSE/MAE results but without standard deviations or significance tests.

arxiv:2608.08786.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM reasoning, chain-of-thought verification, neuro-symbolic diagnosis, and evaluation. The proposed self-audited translation-vs-reasoning error disentanglement is moderately novel, but empirical support is limited: only a 240-instance manually audited set is used, Table 1 and Figure 4 are described without most quantitative values, only an overall F1 of 70.7 is reported, and no significance testing or release details are provided.
evidence: Section 3.4 states the core manually audited gold set contains 240 instances, with a larger automatically constructed corpus of 437,792 instances.
Section 5.1 reports SymDiag overall faithfulness detection F1 of 70.7, but per-dataset values in Table 1 are not supplied in the document text.
Section 6.3 reports Self-Auditor reductions from 46.6% total error before auditing to 81.4% pass rate, with translation errors dropping from 20.1% to near zero by Round 3.
Section 6.2 describes a heatmap of reasoning error types across models but provides mainly qualitative distribution findings.
Section 4.1 details models and configuration but gives no code or data release information.

arxiv:2608.08782.rationale: Scientific-AI/physics-informed ML paper on quantum-classical Kolmogorov-Arnold networks for fuzzy PDEs; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning relevance. Quality is moderate with an error-bound analysis and several PDE examples, but only PIKAN is compared, experiments use ideal quantum simulation, fuzzy constraints are soft, and no code/data or statistical evaluation is provided.
evidence: Section 2.2 QCPIKAN for Fuzzy Differential Equations, Page 7
Section 2.3 Theoretical Error Advantage of QCPIKAN over PIKAN, Page 11
Section 3 Numerical Examples, Page 14
Section 4 Conclusions, Page 25

arxiv:2608.08776.rationale: This is an implementation report on rules-based automation for freshman course placement/registration using Banner and ETL workflows. It does not present LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, or agent methodology; generative AI and chatbot are only mentioned as future work. Evaluation is internal, self-reported, and lacks controlled baselines, statistical testing, code, or data artifacts.
evidence: Page 7-8: Evaluation Methods and Metrics describes internal test cases and dashboard-based stakeholder review.
Page 8-9: Results and Outcomes reports estimated 350 hours annual time savings validated by staff time logs and system processing metrics.
Page 12: Sustainability and Future Development mentions planned generative AI integration for rule deployment and a student-facing chatbot.

arxiv:2608.08775.rationale: Strongly aligned with agentic LLM evaluation, multilingual/Japanese NLP, and benchmark/judge design. The paper provides extensive ablations, CIs, stratified error attribution, and human validation, but novelty is incremental over prior multilingual agent benchmarks and some analyses rely on small samples or LLM-based triage.
evidence: §5.1/Table 1 reports a universal cross-lingual gap of 8.8-18.4 pass@3 points across seven agents.
§6.2/Tables 3-4 report a stratified decomposition of the gap into 55.4% agent, 34.5% translation, 10.1% verifier, with a 6.4% whole-benchmark contamination bound.
§3.3/Appendix C reports judge calibration with κ=0.971 on the English LLM-touched slice and cross-lingual κ from 0.886 (tur) to 0.971 (cmn).
§5.5/Appendix E shows the cross-lingual gap widening with scale from +8.1 to +12.7 pp in a same-family size ladder.
Appendix I reports human re-adjudication of automatic triage labels at 91.4% agreement over 140 items.
Limitations section acknowledges excluded GAIA2 capabilities, residual translation defects, judge reliability ceiling, and fixed-harness/proprietary reasoning settings.

fallback:ae0e35c189497aaf.rationale: Abstract-only article on AI-agent development and technical debt; moderately relevant to Agents/Tool Use and Code/Programming, but the supplied text lacks methods, results, baselines, or enough detail for rigorous evaluation. Evidence is limited to summary claims.
evidence: abstract_only text: states AI agents plan, email, rewrite files and references 31 types of technical debt transformed in agent systems; no method/results sections present.

arxiv:2608.08773.rationale: Pure robotics disassembly and sampling-based motion planning paper. It has no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, multimodal, or language methodology; only weak match is Robotics & Embodied AI. Methodologically it reports benchmarks and ablations, but out-of-scope domain caps the score.
evidence: Abstract: proposes PEEL for long-horizon multi-part object disassembly via scale-invariant sampling and MAB-RRT
Section VI: reports 100% success on 76 single-object Automate assemblies and four multi-part assemblies
Section VI-C: parameter sensitivity studies for window size, validity bounds, initial radius, and sample size

arxiv:2608.08772.rationale: Mechanistic interpretability of large audio-language models is moderately relevant: it matches LLM/multimodal/interpretability preferences but centers on speech-emotion recognition, an audio-domain task. The paper is well documented with causal interventions, multiple LALMs, and held-out languages; however, no statistical significance tests are provided and language/corpus identity is confounded.
evidence: Abstract states the first neuron-level interpretability study of multilingual emotion in LALMs and introduces CR-Fusion.
Section 5.3, Table 1 reports deactivation ESS, with CR-Fusion exceeding best monolingual masks for three models.
Section 6.3 reports leave-one-out analysis showing asymmetric transfer and non-redundant language contributions.
Appendix A provides dataset/model identifiers, prompt template, decoding details, and computational resource estimates.

arxiv:2608.08771.rationale: Pure medical-imaging/fundus segmentation and quantification paper; no LLM/NLP/agents/reasoning/language methodology. Per the rubric, such out-of-scope papers are capped at 0.20. Domain-specific comparisons, ablations, and subgroup analyses provide some internal rigor, but external validation is limited and no code/data availability is stated.
evidence: Title/Abstract: fundus photographs, optic disc/peripapillary atrophy segmentation and quantification; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology.
Section V-A Dataset: internal cohort 388 myopic fundus images; external cohort 66 graded myopic images.
Section V-B Implementation details: AdamW, 150 epochs, seed 42, 2 NVIDIA RTX 3060 GPUs, polar grid radius 362 pixels.
Section V-E/Table II: main comparisons report OD/PPA Dice and HVDR/PMW/PVDR MAE across CNN, ViT, hybrid baselines.
Section V-F/Table III: ablation study isolates RADr, RADθ, and boundary decoder under polar representation.
Section VI Limitations: modest external cohort size and need for larger multicenter validation.

arxiv:2608.08770.rationale: Not aligned with LLM/NLP, agents, reasoning, or safety preferences; primarily diffusion-model distributional control with protein applications, peripheral to image/video diffusion and without language methodology. Methodologically it contributes a mean-field/Feynman-Kac framework and proofs, with low-dimensional quantitative validation, but high-dimensional results are largely qualitative and no code release is stated.
evidence: Section 3.2 Theorem 3.2 derives weighted McKean-Vlasov dynamics and Proposition 3.3 gives an implicit equation for the weight time-derivative.
Section 4.1 and Figure 3 report low-dimensional MMD objective gaps comparing mean-field and gradient steering across noise schedules.
Appendix C.2 and C.5 provide protein conformation and electron-density experiments with mainly qualitative comparison and proxy objectives.
Section 5 Limitations notes reliance on resampling and additional solver cost; no code release is stated.

arxiv:2608.08768.rationale: Highly relevant LLM search-agent/RAG/DPO paper with a novel brief-guided corrective preference distillation approach. Evaluation is fairly broad across multi-hop QA and deep-search benchmarks, with ablations and teacher/backbone comparisons, but rigor is limited by small manual inspections, few significance tests, and no reported multi-seed variance. Code and detailed appendices support reproducibility.
evidence: Table 1 reports main results across HotpotQA, MuSiQue, 2Wiki, Bamboogle, FRAMES, and GAIA, with BOUND leading on five datasets and 12 of 14 metrics.
Table 3 reports ablations on Bamboogle and BrowseComp-Plus, showing drops when rerouting supervision, teacher correction, or student-specific correction is removed.
Table 6 reports brief-guided teacher assessment improvements under DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Qwen3-32B.
Abstract and Section 4.1 provide code availability and training hyperparameters; Appendix D describes construction interfaces and validation.

arxiv:2608.08764.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM reasoning and training/alignment via unsupervised on-policy self-distillation with consensus/disagreement and KTO-style calibration. The dual-signal design is moderately novel, but evaluation is limited to math benchmarks on two small Qwen models, with no significance testing/multi-seed evidence, some incomplete s=20 results, and no code or full hyperparameter disclosure.
evidence: Section 4.1 describes OpenThoughts training and AIME/HMMT/AMO evaluation with avg@16.
Section 5.1 Table 1 reports CoDA-Full average 54.57% (Qwen3-4B) and 36.12% (Qwen3-1.7B) versus baselines.
Section 5.3 Table 3 and Figure 4 analyze false-consensus and training stability.

arxiv:2608.08761.rationale: VLSI/edge-CNN accelerator paper addressing energy-proportional AI and precision scaling; only tangential preference match via Scaling & Efficiency, with no LLM/NLP/language methodology.
