Incremental over prior zero-skipping/DVFS/approximate-computing work. Quantitative claims rely on self-reported synthesis and simulations without accuracy, precision-loss, statistical, or independent validation; tools are named but no RTL/scripts/data are released. Overall out-of-scope and capped low.
evidence: Abstract reports 42% switching activity reduction, 4.8% area overhead, and 1.1-year carbon payback
Section 5.2 Table 1 summarizes dynamic power, static leakage, die area, EDP, and MTTF results
Section 5.1 states synthesis used Synopsys Design Compiler and power analysis used ModelSim/PrimeTime PX with ResNet-50/MobileNetV2 activation maps

arxiv:2608.08757.rationale: Audio-domain music retrieval paper using sparse autoencoders and multimodal audio-text embeddings. Relevant to interpretability/SAE methods but outside the core LLM/NLP scope and treated as a pure audio/domain application, so preference relevance is low. The inversion-based attribution is moderately novel but niche. Evaluations include baselines, multiple sparsity levels, and quantitative metrics, though results are largely figure-based with only partial ablations. Code and data links support reproducibility.
evidence: Section 4.2 reports inverse supports yield 10-70% better bundle recall and substantially better probe performance (~50% AUROC to ~65-80%).
Section 5.3 reports inverse methods occupy better high-score edit-preservation frontiers than cosine probing.
Introduction provides code and companion website links.
Section 6 discusses limitations from embedding-space quality and SAE fidelity.

arxiv:2608.08753.rationale: Medical imaging/neuroimaging application for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis using transformer-based longitudinal MRI modeling, which is out of scope for the language/LLM-focused preferences. Despite internal ablations, benchmark comparisons, and interpretability analyses, the domain cap applies.
evidence: Section 4.1 Datasets and Preprocessing
Table 1
Section 3.3 Efficiency Analysis

arxiv:2608.08751.rationale: This is a billion-scale vector-search/ANN systems paper motivated by LLM/RAG workloads but with no language-model or NLP methodology contribution; it is best treated as out-of-scope domain infrastructure, so relevance is capped low. The engineering evaluation is fairly extensive with baselines, ablations, latency distributions, and appendices, but claims are self-reported and some baselines could not be reproduced.
evidence: Abstract mentions LLM/RAG workloads and billion-scale vector search.
Section 5.1 reports QPS/recall comparisons against Rummy, DiskANN, HNSW, Faiss-CPU, and PipeANN.
Figure 5 and Appendix F provide 1B-scale and 100M-scale trade-off results.
Section 5.5 and Table 4 report index construction times for InSituANN, DiskANN, and HNSW.
Appendix B describes baseline configurations, memory limits, and evaluation protocol.
Section 5.4 and Figure 10 report ablations for GPU offloading and pipelining.

arxiv:2608.08749.rationale: Pure robotics/VLA memory paper, out of scope with only tangential memory/retrieval relevance. Novelty is moderate but evaluation is limited to one frozen base policy and few tasks, with no ablations or error bars.
evidence: Section 4, Table 1: reports LiberoLong-10 Avg. 86.2/88.6/90.2 and RMBench SwapBlocks 0/10/14, SwapT 0/8/10.
Section 3 Method: describes hierarchical short-term, elite, and transition memory with value-guided writing and frozen-policy online update.
Section 5 Conclusion: states improvements remain moderate and RMBench success rates are still limited.

arxiv:2608.08746.rationale: Domain-specific healthcare application using small local LMs for structured symptom scoring. Relevant mainly through local LM/structured-output preferences; lacks Japanese or core LLM methodology. Frozen split and bootstrap support some rigor, but offline label-conditioned utterances, one Chinese dataset, small sample, and absent code URL limit evidence and generalizability.
evidence: Methods 2.1: mcPHASES data; 36 frozen evaluation participants, 360 participant-days, 2,160 labels.
Methods 2.5: offline evaluation used generated initial narratives from highest-severity symptoms and deterministic label-conditioned follow-ups rather than real user dialogue.
Results 3.2: fixed six-item QWK 0.976, fixed three-cluster QWK 0.913, bootstrap QWK difference -0.0623 (95% CI -0.0761 to -0.0483).
Data and code availability: repository URL to be inserted before public submission; mcPHASES requires PhysioNet DUA.

arxiv:2608.08744.rationale: Relevant LLM/efficiency fine-tuning topic, but the central carbon surrogate is problematic: for Gemma/Llama the weight is entirely on a shape-based FLOP proxy, providing no meaningful parameter gradient for those models, so claimed effects may be noise. Results are limited to three MMLU subjects with no significance testing and model/subject selection documented in Appendix A.3; calibration uses only three points and within-sample R2. Reproducibility is limited by unreleased code ('soon').
evidence: Section 2.1/Equation 1 defines the joint task/carbon objective.
Table 1 and Section 2.2 show Gemma/Llama surrogate weight w2=1.000 on a forward-pass tensor-shape FLOP proxy and Qwen w1=0.988 on parameter L2 norm.
Section 2.2 states the surrogate is fit on three calibration points and R2 is within-sample/local only.
Appendix A.3 states the main paper selected the three families with the cleanest break-even behavior and reports omitted models with up to 21.2% inference carbon increases.
Table 2 reports break-even F1/CO2 deltas but no confidence intervals or significance tests.
A.11 claims release of logs/tables but the main text says codebase will be released 'soon', with no available artifact.

arxiv:2608.08743.rationale: The paper is relevant via reinforcement learning and AI safety/fairness preferences but has no LLM/NLP/agent component. It presents a novel quantile-mapping preprocessing method with formal bounds and broad empirical comparisons; assumptions and limited data/code availability constrain generalizability and reproducibility somewhat.
evidence: Section 1 Contributions describe CFSMDM extending prior sequential data preprocessing beyond additive noise with theoretical guarantees and real-data application.
Section 5 Numerical Experiments compares CFSMDM with Full, Unaware, Random, FLAP_M, ECOCF_M, and CFSDP on policy value and CF metric under nonadditive noise.
Section 6 Application to the PowerED Study reports CF metric and value across education, ethnicity, sex, and age; CFSMDM is best on most attributes but slightly more unfair than Unaware for sex.
Appendix J includes additional experiments varying sample size, effect strength, horizon length, and quantile-grid size.
Data Availability Statement says code will be provided when manuscript is published and PowerED data are available on reasonable request.

arxiv:2608.08740.rationale: Low-to-moderate relevance: ML training/efficiency systems rather than LLM/NLP core topics. The contribution combines known sliding-window and Hirschberg techniques in a PyTorch knapsack solver, with limited algorithmic novelty. Rigor is weakened by a malformed Algorithm 1 stack.push line and no formal correctness proof. Evaluation is synthetic-only, and evidence for the n=2,000 peak and PyTorch 2.10 merge is asserted rather than demonstrated in Table 1.
evidence: Section 3, Algorithm 1
Section 4, Table 1

arxiv:2608.08736.rationale: Multimodal LLM evaluation benchmark with video QA, moderately relevant to Multimodal AI, Evaluation, Video, and LLM preferences but not core language methodology. Contribution is a domain benchmark with a unified error taxonomy and hierarchical tasks; novelty is moderate. Rigor is reasonable due to expert review, quality validation, baselines, and ablations, though answer generation relies on GPT and statistical significance is absent. Evidence is mostly quantitative but limited to benchmark performance; reproducibility is partial because videos are not redistributed.
evidence: Experiments, Main Results: reports Gemini-3.1-pro-preview highest perception Q-MAcc 54.3% and judgement F1 72.1%, while open-source models fall below uniform-random F1.
Dataset Quality Validation: reports 98.4% exact-answer agreement for perception and 97.3% mIoU for temporal grounding on a 10% sample.
Controlled Perception-Oracle Evaluation, Table 2: shows GPT-5.5 reaches 94.4% judgement F1 with ground-truth perception evidence.
Appendix E Limitations: states equipment-based exercises are not covered and the long-video subset is smaller and less diverse.

arxiv:2608.08734.rationale: Diffusion-based unrestricted adversarial transfer attack on visual models; adversarial attack touches AI safety preference, but the work is pure computer vision/image diffusion with no LLM or language methodology and is capped as out-of-scope. Method is an incremental combination of EDICT-style invertible diffusion and DWT low-frequency constraints; quantitative claims are self-reported with metric ambiguity.
evidence: Section 5.2 and Table 1 report IDATA AVG values of 62.7, 43.0, 65.0, and 56.6 across four surrogate settings compared with baselines.
Table 4 reports IDM reduces peak GPU memory from 37.9 GB to 13.1 GB and LFCM reduces LPIPS from 0.162 to 0.143.
Section 4.2 describes DWT-based decomposition restricting perturbations to low-frequency components.
Section 5.3 and Figure 1 select tau=20 under an LPIPS<=0.14 budget.

arxiv:2608.08733.rationale: Astrophysics domain application using simulation-based inference with neural spline flows; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning/transformer alignment with stated preferences, so preference relevance is zero. The paper reports calibration tests, hyperparameter search, and quantitative posteriors, but the contribution is domain-specific and generalizability is limited.
evidence: Section 2.2.2 describes the neural spline flow architecture, permutation-invariant encoder, Optuna hyperparameter search, and SBC/TARP/coverage calibration tests.
Section 3 reports MMD p=0.994 and L-C2ST p=0.82 for misspecification/posterior validity, and Figure 1 shows SBI parameter posteriors.
Table A2 gives architecture hyperparameters and Table A3 lists calibration metrics across 10 seeds.

arxiv:2608.08732.rationale: Moderately relevant to multimodal vision-language dense retrieval and embedding efficiency, but not core LLM/reasoning/agents/safety. The training-free focus-then-fold method has some novelty over existing pruning/merging baselines, and evaluation is extensive across three backbones and benchmark suites with ablations. However, the scope is limited to visual document retrieval, and no code release is indicated.
evidence: Section 4.2 reports mean NDCG@5 retention of 98.3% at gamma=0.20 across six backbone-benchmark pairs.
Table 3 in Appendix B.1 provides benchmark-level NDCG@5 and retention values for ViDoRe v1/v2 and REAL-MM-RAG.
Table 1 in Section 4.5 reports ablation results on ViDoRe v2 with ColQwen2.5 at gamma=0.20.

arxiv:2608.08730.rationale: Relevant LLM inference/efficiency work for browser/edge WebGPU deployment, but it is a systems characterization rather than a language-modeling contribution. The controlled fusion experiment is a strength, though the causal claim rests on one model/platform with no reported variance or broader baseline comparison.
evidence: Section 5.1 reports sequential per-dispatch cost of 24-36 µs on Vulkan and 32-71 µs on Metal and notes independence from data type.
Section 5.2 reports a dispatch reduction from 876 to 564 yielding 53% throughput improvement while shaders and memory traffic are held essentially constant.
Section 6 Scope states the causal fusion experiment is single-platform, single-pipeline (RTX 5090, Dawn, Vulkan, batch size 1, float32), limiting generality.

arxiv:2608.08729.rationale: Out-of-scope HCI/psychomotor training paper on CPR with mixed reality and haptic feedback. It contains no LLM, transformer, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, safety, or other in-scope AI/ML methodology. The controlled user study is modestly rigorous within its domain but not relevant to the curator's AI/ML preferences.
evidence: Abstract: describes Kinesthetic-CPR as a stage-adaptive multimodal mixed reality CPR training system.
Section 4: System overview describes MR visual front end, pneumatic manikin, closed-loop control backend.
Section 5: Evaluation reports a controlled user study with 60 participants across five groups.

arxiv:2608.08727.rationale: Relevant as a multimodal VLM/VQA benchmark with evaluation and LoRA fine-tuning, but agriculture-specific domain focus limits breadth. Quality concerns include inconsistent dataset counts, an absent cited baseline (AgriCLIP) in the main table, TomaLLaVA missing the CSI task in comparisons, and no statistical significance or error bars.
evidence: Section 3.2 reports 28,808 images and 213,119 conversations, while Section 3.1 reports 124,367 training plus 42,626 MCQs plus 37,816 OEQs, which does not sum to 213,119.
Table 1 shows TomaLLaVA lacks CSI results while other models are averaged across seven tasks.
Section 4.3 claims comparison with AgriCLIP at 93.73% Acc, but AgriCLIP is absent from Table 1.
Table 2 provides no error bars or significance tests for OEQ results.

arxiv:2608.08726.rationale: Highly relevant LLM reasoning and on-policy training paper with formal projection analysis and controlled ablations. However, empirical scope is narrow (three math benchmarks, small models, limited seeds), the 4B extension is one-seed and mixed, and no code release is indicated.
evidence: Section 5.2: PAST macro average 48.426 vs Vanilla OPSD 42.809 (+5.617, 95% CI [2.592, 8.333]).
Section 5.3 Table 2: factorial cells show trajectory-only 43.364, teacher-only 42.901, and PAST 48.426.
Section 5.4: trajectory removal lowers teacher success by 0.064 and raises JSD by 0.067; shuffling lowers success by 0.089 and raises JSD by 0.110.
Section 5.6 Table 8: adaptive sampling uses 850 teacher samples vs 1,032 fixed-8, with macro 47.284 vs 46.728.
Limitations: main evidence uses a 1.7B student; one-seed 4B extension gives mixed task-level results.

arxiv:2608.08725.rationale: Moderate relevance: the paper uses VLA/LLM speculative decoding and multimodal inference, but its core domain is embodied robotics. The world-aware bias plus next-frame latent loss is a relatively incremental addition to existing relaxed speculative decoding. Evaluation is fairly broad across benchmarks and verifier families with ablations and robustness sweeps, but lacks statistical significance testing and a limitations section; code is not yet available.
evidence: Table 1 compares WA-SpecDec and Standard SpecDec across LIBERO-Spatial/Object/Goal/Long under rho, KERV, and HeiSD, listing Success, Speedup, and NCF.
Section 4.4/Table 5 reports tolerance sweep; WA-SpecDec mean success is 71.3/71.0/67.0/63.5 at rho=5/10/15/20 vs Spec-VLA 67.7/65.4/61.2/55.1.
Section 4.6/Table 6 ablation shows WA-SpecDec full achieves 71.0 success and 4.22 accepted length at rho=10, compared with WA w/o video loss 69.4/4.09 and Spec-VLA 65.4/3.59.
Appendix A states code and evaluation scripts will be released upon acceptance and reports 50 rollouts per task with implementation details.

arxiv:2608.08722.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM-driven code generation, agentic search loops, benchmark evaluation, and reward hacking. The paper offers a useful taxonomy and formal analysis, but empirical scope is narrow: one hardware target, small configuration pools, single trajectory per cell, and generalizability beyond GPU kernels is asserted rather than demonstrated. Rigor is supported by audit protocol, redaction experiment, and replication probes, though statistical strength is limited. Reproducibility is strong via released artifacts, prompts, and hardware details.
evidence: Section 3 and Table 1 report 16/53 non-transferring in-distribution wins with mechanism grades A-D and held-out regressions.
Appendix C describes audit protocol, blind second-grader pass, and controlled redaction experiment.
Appendix B provides formal model and lower-bound Theorem B.6 for fingerprinting under selection pressure.

arxiv:2608.08721.rationale: Core LLM inference/efficiency work proposing dynamic speculative-length selection for diffusion-based drafters. Relevant to LLM serving and efficiency, with broad empirical comparisons. Novelty is moderate: it reframes existing dynamic-length selection as expected-speedup optimization. Rigor is limited by partly self-referential theoretical bounds, a brief unimodality proof, and absence of a limitations section. Quantitative speedups are reported but without statistical significance or error bars. Reproducibility is partial: algorithm and hyperparameters are provided, but no code or artifact availability is stated.
evidence: Section 4.2 and Table 1 report speedup and acceptance-length comparisons on Qwen2.5 models across MATH-500, GSM8K, HumanEval, and MT-Bench.
Section 4.5 and Table 4 report alpha hyperparameter sensitivity for FastdLLM and DFlash configurations.
Appendix B.2 gives baseline implementation and hyperparameter details but states no code release.
Theorems 3.3-3.4 define position-wise bounds using self-referential epsilon expressions, and Section 3.5 claims unimodality with a brief proof.

arxiv:2608.08720.rationale: Pure computer-vision image enhancement using Stable Diffusion and regression models, with no LLM/language methodology; out-of-scope per rubric caps score at 0.20. The paper includes ablations, multi-dataset evaluation, and limitations, but relevance to preferred topics is negligible.
evidence: Abstract: proposes DPEC using diffusion-based image generation priors for exposure correction.
Section IV-A1: evaluates on LCDP, MSEC, SICE and generalization on LIME, DICM, NPE.
Section IV-C: includes ablation studies on fine-tuning strategy, noise level, diffusion-regression integration, and attention module.
Section IV-D: reports failure cases and computational limitations.

arxiv:2608.08713.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/radiology report generation. Although it uses LLM/VLM projectors and token compression, the domain application is capped at low relevance. Research quality is modest: broad ablations exist, but hyperparameter search is limited to one vision encoder/dataset, clinical metrics rely on automated labels, and code/models are only promised.
evidence: Abstract: reports systematic evaluation of 4 VEs, 5 projectors, 5 LLMs on CT-RATE and Merlin and claims SOTA clinical macro F1.
Table 4 / Section 4.1: ROI cropping improves clinical macro F1 in 19 of 20 configurations; High Res benefits are projector-dependent.
Section 5: limitations include frozen VEs, hyperparameter search only for Primus-1B on CT-RATE, flawed automated labeler, and systems not deployable.

arxiv:2608.08709.rationale: Relevant conceptual position paper on LLM/VLM evaluation, verification cost, and AI safety, but it provides no benchmark, experiments, baselines, ablations, or original quantitative results. The formalization and limitations are thoughtful, yet evidence is illustrative and external, and no concrete instantiation or data/code is released.
evidence: Section 6 'Illustrative instantiation (non-estimative)' states the walk-through 'carries no empirical weight'.
Section 9 'Concluding Remarks' states the instruments are 'deliberately conceptual' and concrete instantiations are left to future work.
Abstract defines Verification-Cost Errors but reports no original quantitative evaluation or empirical results.

arxiv:2608.08704.rationale: Out-of-scope mathematical statistics paper on multi-kernel spectral clustering with no LLM/NLP/transformer/agent/safety/multimodal content. The closest weak preference match is Scientific AI via theorem/proof, but the work is not an AI-for-science contribution. The theory appears rigorous with full appendices, but empirical evidence is limited to Gaussian-mixture simulations and no code/data release is stated.
evidence: Abstract and Section 2 develop multi-kernel spectral clustering with row-wise ell_{2,\infty} eigenvector perturbation bounds.
Theorem 2.2 and Theorem 2.3 state eigenvalue and eigenvector perturbation rates under Assumptions 1-4.
Section 3 Algorithm 1 specifies quantile-based bandwidth selection and K-means; Theorem 3.3 states exact recovery.
Figure 4 reports misclassification rates over 500 replications for Gaussian-mixture simulations; no real datasets or code release are described.

arxiv:2608.08702.rationale: Pure computer-vision facial expression recognition using a DINOv3 vision backbone; no LLM, NLP, language methodology, or multimodal language reasoning, so out of scope under the rubric. The regional residual adapter and AU-guided training are incremental within FER, and the paper provides ablations and benchmark results, but is limited to aligned facial images and lacks capacity-matched baselines or code release.
evidence: Abstract: fine-grained facial expression recognition with DINOv3 patch tokens and regional residual evidence, no language modeling.
Sec. 4.4: progressive ablation study on RAF-DB.
Sec. 5: notes fixed quadrants assume roughly aligned faces and unmatched readout baselines.

arxiv:2608.08701.rationale: Out of scope: automotive radar object detection using a modified YOLO/CNN pipeline; no language model, NLP, reasoning, prompting, agent, or language-based methodology. It does include quantitative ablations and tracking-method comparisons, but domain-specific, limited generalization, no public code/data.
evidence: Section V-B2 Table III reports RMSE and false-negative rates for NativeDB, ChassisDB, and WheelExtDB across distance intervals.
Section V-C Table IV reports RGB vs RGB-DIL false-negative reduction from 29 to 6 in overlap scenarios.
Section III-A3 describes the radar-image dilation method on feature input channels.

arxiv:2608.08700.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents/tool use, function calling, and evaluation, with a Chinese-language benchmark and LLM-as-judge component. Research quality is moderate: the closed-loop construction and fine-grained error attribution are incremental over prior function-calling benchmarks, no code/data release is stated, statistical detail is limited, and human verification is sampled rather than exhaustive for the final set.
evidence: Abstract: claims a two-stage closed-loop construction framework and gold-anchored judge for error attribution.
Experiments: reports PluginEval with 3,000 instances across 54 plugins and evaluation of five model families.
Table 1: reports Recall, Accuracy, and error breakdowns under two difficulty distributions.
Table 4: reports human audit of reference quality across sampled cases.
Table 5: reports human audit of judge reliability across error categories.

arxiv:2608.08698.rationale: Out-of-scope wireless video token communication paper. It uses tokenizer/detokenizer and mentions vision foundation models and SwinIR, but has no LLM, language modeling, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, safety, or other preferred methodology. Research quality is moderate for its domain but relevance is very low, so score is capped below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: proposes loss-resilient wireless video token communication over block fading channels.
Section II-C: receiver reconstructs video from zero-filled token tensor via fine-tuned detokenizer and SwinIR.
Section V: reports LPIPS/FID comparisons with DCVC-RT, DCVC-FM, VVC, and H.265.

arxiv:2608.08696.rationale: Pure computer-vision 3D occupancy prediction paper; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, safety, alignment, or language methodology. The 'depth foundation model' term is not language-model relevance, so preference_relevance is near zero. Internal quantitative tables and ablations exist, but the work is explicitly out of scope and capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: introduces Cross-Scene 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction and OccAnyScene as a Gaussian-based occupancy method.
Section 4.3 / Tables 2-3: reports IoU/mIoU comparisons and cross-scene vs scene-specific results.
Section 4.4 / Table 4: provides ablation of PFFA and FPGC components.

arxiv:2608.08694.rationale: Quantum graph-coloring/chromatic-number optimization paper; does not match LLM/NLP/AI preferences and is out-of-scope. Method proposes a feasible-subspace mixer and one-body chromatic-number term, with qiskit emulation on small graphs, but evidence is limited and Sec. III-A contains conflicting chromatic-number statements for graph (d), reducing rigor.
evidence: Sec. II: memory-efficient encoding and proposed mixer Hamiltonian
Sec. III-A and Fig. 3: QAA simulation on small graphs; textual conflict about graph (d) chromatic number vs footnote 4
Sec. V and Table I: constrained truck loading emulation probabilities for -X and proposed mixer

arxiv:2608.08693.rationale: Pure medical imaging / quantitative MRI paper with no language methodology, so out of scope per instructions. The methods are described clearly and include baselines, ablations, and code, but relevance to LLM/NLP/agents or other core topics is minimal.
evidence: Abstract: proposes CUPA-T2* for quantitative T2* mapping in accelerated MRI.
Methods: describes unrolled multi-echo reconstruction with MC dropout, covariance estimation, and heteroscedastic MLP.
Experiments and Results: reports Tables 1-4 with NRMSE/SSIM, AURC/ECE, and ablation at R=4.
Conclusion: states code availability at https://github.com/compai-lab/2026-miccai-rouwendaal.

arxiv:2608.08691.rationale: EnergyBridge is a domain-specific energy-management benchmark that uses LLM-based user simulation, an LLM agent with memory/tool use, and retrieval-augmented capacity reporting. It maps partially to agent, RAG, evaluation, prompting, and dataset preferences, but remains an application-oriented integration benchmark rather than a core LLM/NLP contribution. Novelty is moderate; rigor and evidence are reasonable due to human grounding, ablations, and quantitative baselines, though main outcomes rely heavily on simulated judgments and generalizability is limited by regional/domain scope. Code/data release supports reproducibility.
evidence: Section 5.5 reports 584 complete consented human role-play responses and Table 2 shows LLM-human acceptance ordering alignment with 5.3-point MAE.
Section 4.3 describes retrieval-augmented capacity reporting using top-k similar historical events for pre-event capacity estimates.
Section 5.4 ablates household grounding components, showing acceptance drops from 77.1% to 37.1% when personalized explanations are removed.
Abstract and Section 1 state release of human data, codes, environments, physical models, and baseline implementations on GitHub.

arxiv:2608.08689.rationale: Low relevance to LLM/NLP/agent preferences; only partial alignment with graph neural networks and scientific AI. Moderately novel structural contract idea, but incremental over hybrid physics-residual and graph world models. Rigor is careful with explicit limitations, though pre-registration is self-attested and many statistical tests underpowered. Evidence supports narrow claims within synthetic/semi-synthetic/small real settings but not broad accuracy advantages. Reproducibility is relatively strong via artifacts, manifests, seeds, and hyperparameters.
evidence: Section 7.2 Threats to Validity states pre-freezing is self-attested, not OSF-style pre-archived registration.
Section 6.7 RQ7 Table 14 reports 90-min RMSE: SD-GWM (w/R) 29.349 vs STGCN 96.901 and LSTM 157.365.
Appendix A describes frozen artifacts, manifest, hyperparameters, and seeds.

arxiv:2608.08685.rationale: Pure computer vision paper on semi-dense image matching uncertainty and geometric estimation; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent relevance. The post-hoc Laplace-mixture calibration/refit is incremental within CV, with ablations and implementation details but no statistical significance tests or direct probabilistic-matcher baselines. Out-of-scope cap applied.
evidence: Abstract
Section 3.2
Section 4.2
Section 4.3
Appendix A

arxiv:2608.08684.rationale: Highly relevant LLM long-context inference/KV cache compression paper. Novelty is moderate: replaces depth/attention proxies with output KL after value-cache perturbation. Experiments cover three model families, multiple budgets, competitive baselines, ablations, and efficiency, but no significance testing/confidence intervals, no explicit limitations, and calibration/alpha/gamma details are incomplete.
evidence: Abstract: proposes RippleKV perturbation-based cross-layer KV cache allocation and reports highest average LongBench performance under matched budgets.
Experiments: Table 2 compares RippleKV against StreamingLLM, H2O, SnapKV, and PyramidKV on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 at 10/20/30% budgets.
Methodology: Algorithm 1 details sensitivity profiling via value-cache perturbations, KL divergence, normalization, exponential mapping, clipping, and budget rounding.
Experiments: Table 3 and Figure 3 report latency, throughput, and peak memory efficiency comparisons.
Ablation Study: Tables 4 and 5 report LBA/DS ablations and allocation-ratio sensitivity.

arxiv:2608.08678.rationale: Pure mathematical Markov-chain/probability paper on spectral gaps, Poincaré inequalities, and count kernels. It does not address LLMs, NLP, agents, training, multimodal AI, or other primary preferences; the only weak topical overlap is Scientific AI via mathematics/theorem/proof. The paper is deductively detailed but lacks empirical ML evaluation, baselines, ablations, or code/data, and strict positivity limits practical generality.
evidence: Section 1 states the spectral-gap lower bound and proof strategy
Theorem 3.3 gives the Poincaré inequality under strict positivity
Section 5 provides the matching upper bound
Section 9 discusses limitations of strict positivity and an unresolved general comparison conjecture
Section 8 applies the inequality to matrix-valued empirical averages

arxiv:2608.08677.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, reasoning, and skill evolution, with strong multi-benchmark and multi-model experiments. Novelty is moderate: sibling-prefix evidence extraction from MCTS is a useful extension but builds closely on SkillOpt, SIGMA, and tree-search literature. Rigor is limited by no reported statistical variability, no explicit limitations section, and no released code. Evidence supports main efficiency and performance claims via Section 4.2 and Tables 2-4, but reproducibility is weakened by unspecified prompts and code availability.
evidence: Abstract: reports 73.2% fewer tokens than SkillOpt and superior performance.
Section 4.2: reports Branch2Skill ranked best or tied in 26 of 30 settings and outperformed SkillOpt in 27, with aggregate gain from 117.8 to 128.7 percentage points.
Table 3: provides ablations for maximum depth, child-node count, iteration budget, and evidence selection on SearchQA and LiveMath.
Section 4.5: reports cross-model and cross-dataset transfer results, including gains on Omni-MATH without target-domain update.

arxiv:2608.08676.rationale: Relevant mainly to multimodal vision-language modeling and image generation/editing with an LLM backbone, but not core LLM or Japanese NLP methodology. The controlled patch-embedding diagnostic and multi-encoder evaluation are useful, but internal data, self-reported benchmarks, no statistical testing, and limited system-level understanding evidence temper confidence.
evidence: Abstract: describes 8B Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts unified model for understanding, generation, and editing.
Sec 3.1, Fig 1: random patch embedding raises last-layer PSNR by 3.70 dB with frozen Transformer blocks.
Table 4: PR-SigLIP2 and PR-Qwen-ViT preserve multimodal understanding benchmarks.
Sec 5.2.1, Table 6: UniSpace ImgEdit overall 4.28 versus BAGEL 3.20 and SenseNova-U1 3.90.
Sec 6 Limitation: system-level understanding lags dedicated VLMs and unified encoder cannot be freely updated.

arxiv:2608.08675.rationale: Moderately relevant as LLM-based test-time scaling and coarse-to-fine refinement for forecasting, but it is a domain-specific time-series application rather than core LLM/NLP. Novelty is moderate (shape-anchored fixed-step refinement); rigor is weakened by internal metric inconsistencies and run-count discrepancies. Evidence is quantitative but partially conflicted; generalization across long/short/zero-shot benchmarks is good; code and hyperparameters aid reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract claims SCALER is 7 times faster than standard test-time scaling, while Section 4.5/Figure 3 reports about 6.7-6.8x faster than TimeReasoner.
Section 4.1 states results are averaged over three runs, but Table 1 and Table 2 captions say five runs.
Table 4 default MSE values conflict with Table 1 SCALER results, e.g., ETTh1 average MSE 0.407 in Table 4 versus 0.376 in Table 1.

arxiv:2608.08674.rationale: Tangentially relevant through interpretability/explainability and model-update training, but not a strong match for the LLM/NLP/agent-focused preferences. The paper provides a defined tree-based explanation compatibility loss, an efficient CART extension with complexity analysis, and experiments on 10 datasets over 100 trials; however, evidence is largely qualitative trade-off plots and the approach is specific to decision trees with limited generalizability. Code availability is good.
evidence: Section 5.1 and Figures 2-3 report trade-offs on 10 real-world classification/regression datasets averaged over 100 trials.
Section 5.3 and Figure 5 report computation times comparable to CART.
Resource Availability states source code is available at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.32521632.

arxiv:2608.08673.rationale: The paper is a UCL MSc report on continual reinforcement learning using tabular Q-learning on Voronoi graph tasks. It matches the Reinforcement Learning preference but is not an LLM/NLP/agent methodology paper, limiting relevance. The methodology is detailed, but the findings are largely inconclusive with high variability, uneven similarity distributions, and no statistical significance; generalizability is explicitly limited to deterministic tabular graph settings.
evidence: Abstract: states no evidence of statistical significance that task similarity independently affects forgetting in continual RL.
Chapter 5.1.3: reports high variability in forgetting measures and uneven distribution of graph differences, and concludes the relationship remains unclear.
Chapter 5.2 Limitations: notes results may only be indicative for tabular RL in deterministic graphical settings and that Graph Edit Distance could not be used due to computational cost.
Chapter 4.3.3 Experiments: 100 trials, three task complexity levels (3, 5, 15 internal sites), and 2500 training episodes.

arxiv:2608.10023.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/aviation integrity paper with no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, or language methodology. It adapts RAIM protection levels to nonlinear PnP pose estimation; mathematical derivation is detailed but validation is simulation-only, with no baselines, real data, or code release, limiting rigor/evidence/reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: derives protection levels for vision-based pose estimation (VBPE) with PnP in an aviation setting.
Section VI-A: simulation setup uses four runway corners, 4000x3000 px camera, sigma=1 px; no real imagery.
Section VII: future work will validate on LARD dataset; no code or data release is stated.

arxiv:2608.08671.rationale: Visual analytics system for data-fact outlier detection; LLM use is limited to summary/label generation via a staged prompting pipeline, making topic relevance marginal. Evaluation is qualitative (12-person interview and usage scenarios) without quantitative baselines, but the pipeline is described and code/data links are provided.
evidence: §4 Cluster Insights details an LLM pipeline using the OpenAI API and staged prompting to generate cluster summaries.
§3.4 defines the combined outlier score using LOF and an entropy-based pattern score.
§6.3 reports Likert-based interview results from 12 participants (e.g., Q9 M=4.75).
§8 states the source code is publicly available at https://github.com/lyk6666/FOX.

arxiv:2608.08668.rationale: Pure quantum chemistry/physics paper on Born-Oppenheimer and exact factorization; no LLM, NLP, or AI-methodology relevance. Analytical treatment is detailed but the models are simple one-dimensional toy benchmarks, largely recasting known results; no code/data release and limited generalizability.
evidence: Section 6 states the vibronic model is standard and claims no novelty.
Section 9 acknowledges the limitation to one nuclear coordinate and no conical intersections.
Section 7 reports numerical grid convergence but no code/data availability.

arxiv:2608.08664.rationale: Out-of-scope visual counterfactual/diffusion/XAI work with no language-model methodology; final score capped at 0.19. The paper shows moderate technical novelty and ablations in a CV/medical-imaging domain, but lacks relevance to LLMs, NLP, or language-grounded methods.
evidence: Abstract: proposes FiRe, a Fixed-noise Refinement framework for visual counterfactual explanations using Pixel Mean Flow.
Section 4.1: evaluations use CelebA, CelebA-HQ, and CheXpert with face-attribute and medical shortcut-removal tasks, not language-model tasks.
Section 4.5: ablation study compares PMF-One Step, PMF-Reverse, PMF-Fixed, masking, adaptive guidance, and early stopping.

arxiv:2608.08663.rationale: Relevant to multimodal language-grounding and interpretability, but not LLM/Japanese-LLM/agent focused. Uses classical SIFT/UQI plus symbolic pact tracking with honest leakage analysis; however, no interactive loop, no learned baseline, and point estimates from a single retrieval pass limit strength.
evidence: Section 4.3 reports top-1 accuracy drops from 41.66% to 29.2% and top-5 from 83.56% to 67.8% under conservative filtering for retrieval leakage.
Table 1 reports augmentation ablation: no augmentation 33.3%, rotation only 38.1%, grayscale inversion only 36.4%, both 41.66%.
Section 5.2 states the MCP is a passive matcher and does not reproduce interactive entrainment.
Section 6.4 states accuracy numbers are point estimates from a single retrieval pass and notes Bing responses drift over time.
Section 6.5 states no comparison against a learned perceptual baseline such as CLIP was performed.

arxiv:2608.08662.rationale: The paper is a theoretical optimal stopping / prophet inequality study using kernel methods. It has no substantive connection to LLMs, NLP, transformers, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, code, multimodal AI, or other preferred topics. It is out of scope and is capped accordingly.
evidence: Abstract: frames the paper around single-selection prophet inequality, bounded variance, and kernel methods for thresholds, with no preferred LLM/NLP topic.
Section 1 Introduction: defines the prophet inequality model, threshold rules, and variance-constrained competitive ratios, confirming pure optimal stopping / mechanism design content.

arxiv:2608.08661.rationale: Pure computer vision underwater image restoration with no LLM/NLP/language methodology. Despite detailed ablations, multiple benchmarks, and diagnostics, the paper is out of scope for this rubric and must receive at most 0.20.
evidence: Introduction: formulates underwater image restoration and degradation-guided feature adaptation.
Experiments: reports results on five paired and four non-reference underwater benchmarks.
Ablation Study: Table 4 reports component ablations on the UIEB dataset.
Supplementary Material: provides limitations and same-checkpoint control diagnostics.

arxiv:2608.08659.rationale: Pure computer vision / 3D Gaussian Splatting paper with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, or language methodology; out of scope per rubric, so score is capped. The JPEG quantization-table-guided DCT supervision has some technical novelty and includes ablations and comparisons, but evidence is limited to seven scenes, controlled JPEG encoding, a single-scene ablation, and no significance testing.
evidence: Abstract: proposes JSGS and reports lowest LPIPS and highest mean SSIM across seven scenes and three mixed-quality schedules.
Experiments: four LLFF and three Mip-NeRF 360 scenes, 7:1 train-test split, controlled JPEG encoding of training views only, with implementation details and one NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU.
Ablation Study: Table 2 reports five configurations on LLFF flower under the Gaussian schedule, showing incremental effects of JO, DS, and GC.
Conclusion and Limitations: acknowledges no double JPEG compression and limited real-world encoder/device diversity.

arxiv:2608.08657.rationale: Out-of-scope public-health visualization corpus study. GPT-5-mini is used only as an annotation/filtering tool, not to study or advance language-model methodology. Although the paper reports a sizable corpus, exact percentages, and validation checks, it lacks ML baselines/ablations and the findings are domain-specific to visualization practices rather than AI/ML research.
evidence: Section 2.6 describes GPT-5-mini annotation and manual validation of the corpus.
Section 3 reports corpus-level descriptive results and color-blind accessibility risk.
Section 6 states that code/scripts are available but some nonprofit/international visualizations will not be redistributed.

arxiv:2608.08654.rationale: Directly relevant to Agents & Tool Use, LLM cost/evaluation, and code-agent tool interfaces, but evidence is limited to one GitHub task with small samples, confounded delivery-method comparisons, and no statistical testing.
evidence: Section 2.2 describes repository-state verification of branch, patched content, pull request, and file count after each run.
Section 4.1 reports thirteen strictly paired MCP-to-CLI ratios spanning 0.43 to 29.06 and calls the conventional comparison inconclusive.
Section 8.1 reports median run-to-run spread of 1.51x and widest 5.41x across repeated configurations.
Section 3.2 reports command-line-only comparisons ranging from 5.0x to 28x cheaper for scaffoldings without MCP clients.
Section 8 acknowledges one task, one domain, confounded delivery-method comparison, and uneven coverage.

arxiv:2608.08652.rationale: Relevant LLM compression/efficiency paper with quantitative comparisons and ablations, but rigor is weakened by internal contradictions: §3 Theorem 3 gives f_out≈12% for K=8 while §6 states ≈3%; Figure 1 says outliers are stored as fp16 while §4 CR formula uses 32-bit kept-weight storage; no error bars or statistical significance; some calibrated baselines are estimated and not directly comparable. Novelty is incremental over prior weight sharing and dense-sparse quantization, though the data-free framing and scale analysis add some value.
evidence: §3 Failure Mode II/Theorem 3 states for K=8, f_out≈12%; §6 K* Phase Transition states f_out(K=8)≈3%.
Figure 1 states outlier weights are stored as fp16, while §4 Compression Ratio uses n_k·32 for kept-exact weights.
Table 3 marks GPTQ-4bit as estimated from community benchmarks and not directly comparable, yet main text claims competitiveness.

arxiv:2608.08650.rationale: Highly relevant survey on MoE architectures in LLMs with a conceptual four-plane framework, but it provides no new empirical experiments or quantitative results; evidence is citation-based and proposed ablations are not executed, limiting rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract describes synthesis of prior work and a framework rather than new quantitative findings.
Section 9 Experimental Design for Foundation-Model Pretraining proposes equal-budget ablation matrices but does not report executed experimental results.
Table 2 Criteria for the division of the four control planes indicates a conceptual taxonomy with typical failure modes, not measured outcomes.

arxiv:2608.08648.rationale: Medical imaging/whole-slide pathology domain is out of scope per rubric, so overall capped at 0.20 despite agentic LLM and VQA components. Paper reports multi-benchmark comparisons, ablations, and a pathologist study (Sections 4.4-4.6), but relevance to core preferences is low.
evidence: Section 4.4 reports SlideBench-VQA, WSI-VQA, and PathVQA accuracies.
Section 4.5 provides ablations of ROI selection, magnification, budget, and modules.
Section 4.6.1 reports a blinded pathologist diagnostic-utility study.
Section 5 states limitations including H&E-only evidence.

arxiv:2608.08646.rationale: Out-of-scope pure trajectory-user linking/human mobility application with no LLM/language methodology; knowledge graph and attention are used only as domain-specific techniques. Experiments include multiple datasets and ablations but lack statistical tests, limitations, and broader relevance.
evidence: Section 5.4 Table 3 reports best results on all five metrics across six settings.
Section 5.5 Figure 3 reports ablation variants.
Section 5.1 describes Foursquare-NYC/TKY/JKT datasets and user scales.

arxiv:2608.08645.rationale: Moderately relevant: strong fit to RAG/vector-database provenance and AI safety/adversarial robustness, but not core LLM or Japanese NLP methodology. Novelty is incremental composition of standard primitives with one protocol change; the spectral threshold is empirical and explicitly left underived. Rigor is transparent about theoretical gaps but the adaptive-security claim is primarily empirical. Evidence includes detailed tables/CIs and deploy-scale tests, though the threshold rests on a narrow straddle and below-threshold failures limit strength. Reproducibility is described via code link, Dockerfile, and fixed seeds, but external availability was not verified.
evidence: Abstract: 'We present HaloMark, a watermark for embedding vectors cryptographically bound to a C2PA manifest... across eight baselines and ten adaptive attackers.'
§IV-A: 'The verifier reads c from the manifest to derive {s_i} instead of recomputing Commit(K,xhat)'; published commit is described as the sole protocol change.
§VI-D and Table IV: eleven embedders separate at empirical threshold eff_rank(Σ)/d≈0.19; above threshold DAE-C4 AUROC 0.965–0.997, below threshold 0.594–0.706.
§VI-E: reports 64-key multi-tenant isolation, C2PA reference-SDK interop with three bindings, and Qdrant admission-filter verification at 284 μs/vector.
§VII: discloses theoretical looseness, below-threshold failures, and verifier-oracle leakage as dominant residual risk.

arxiv:2608.08644.rationale: The paper is a general GFlowNet/RL training methodology, matching only the Reinforcement Learning, Training & Optimization, and Graph Neural Networks preferences; it has little relevance to LLM/NLP/agentic language tasks. The lifted path-dependent sampler is moderately novel with formal expressivity claims and benchmark results, but rigor is weakened by apparent proof inconsistencies (e.g., reversed inclusion in Appendix A.2; wrong proposition reference in A.3). Evidence consists of FCS/TV tables and ablations, but scale and statistical rigor are limited.
evidence: Section 5, Tables 1-2: FCS values for path-dependent models are substantially lower than Markovian baselines on set generation and sequence design tasks.
Appendix A.2: proof states 'R_P(S) ⊆ R_M(S)' after arguing the path-dependent model is at least as expressive, contradicting Proposition 3.2.
Appendix A.3: 'Corollaries 4.6, 4.7, B.1 follow directly from Proposition 3.2' appears to cite the wrong proposition.
Appendix F.3, Figure 13: ablation shows removing the rotation matrix hinders convergence in GridWorld and Lazy Random Walk.

arxiv:2608.10022.rationale: Out-of-scope pure ocean/climate downscaling application using U-Net and iterative residual correction; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning/alignment methodology. It only weakly connects to Scientific AI and SHAP interpretability. Research has moderate ablations, baselines, and metrics, but is a domain-specific single-region/single-variable study, so preference relevance is near zero and the score is capped low.
evidence: Abstract and Section 2.1 describe RCNN as a U-Net initial prediction plus iterative residual correction for SST downscaling from ACCESS-S2 to ROMS.
Table 3 in Section 3.1 reports RMSE/R2/SSIM versus interpolation, U-Net, and one-step RCNN.
Section 2.1 and Figure 5 describe synthetic MHW-like data and custom loss; Table 4 reports 2011 marine heatwave metrics.
Section 3.4 and Table 5 report 100-seed RMSE sensitivity; Open Research Section gives Zenodo code and data availability.

arxiv:2608.08642.rationale: Out-of-scope graph clustering/low-rank optimal transport optimization paper; no LLM, NLP, agent, vision, safety, or other stated preference relevance. The methodological quality is moderate: it presents an exact KL projection theorem and ablations, but key convergence proofs are omitted and experiments are limited clustering benchmarks without code release.
evidence: Section III-D Theorem 1 states the exact rank-space KL projection and complexity claims.
Section IV-A defines the clean matched protocol; Section IV-B reports medium-scale results.
Section V explicitly limits convergence analysis to nonvanishing latent masses and strictly positive accumulation points.
No code availability or artifact release is mentioned; Section IV-A references only a single-thread reference implementation.

arxiv:2608.08641.rationale: Strongly relevant to AI safety, red-teaming/evaluation, and multimodal guardrails. The paper contributes a novel decomposition of defended-pipeline refusals into guard vs model refusals and shows evaluation-protocol artifacts can manufacture large apparent safety benefits. It reports quantitative exact-match counts, McNemar tests, multi-judge checks, a designed replicate, multiplicity control, and explicit limitations. Generalizability is deliberately constrained to specific defenses, targets, and encodings, and several findings rely on small or single-model cells, so magnitudes should not transfer. Reproducibility is strong via detailed artifacts and implementation disclosure. Assessment is based only on the supplied document, treated as untrusted data.
evidence: §4.1 reports exact-match guard blocks vs judge-scored model refusals, with guard share ranging from 0% to 99% across the three read settings.

§4.2 Table 2 shows text-only guards dropping from 100/100 and 81/100 blocks to 0/100 when the same unencoded harmful payload moves from text to image, while a multimodal guard blocks 99/100 in both channels.
§4.6 Table 6 reports deployable vs granted protocol differences, including a -63pp granted effect that becomes -3pp and non-significant when deployable.
§4.8 Table 9 isolates read position inside ECSO, finding SAFE answer regeneration carries -18pp and -26pp while TELL and CAP stage grants are not significant.
§4.16 describes a designed end-to-end replicate of the protocol grid and drift band of 0-10pp, with architecture-ordered inflation reproducing across campaigns.

arxiv:2608.08640.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, reasoning/CoT, and retrieval. The paper proposes a benchmark and a two-stage method combining teacher CoT supervision with retrieval-guided GRPO, but novelty is moderate since it builds on existing reasoning-enhanced retrieval ideas. Rigor is fair due to multiple baselines, ablations, and sensitivity analyses, though it lacks significance testing/error bars and a clear limitations section. Evidence is self-reported quantitative but covers retrieval, reranking, end-task accuracy, and latency. Generalizability is supported across three benchmarks plus a diagnostic benchmark and multiple downstream LLMs. Reproducibility is moderate because prompts and hyperparameters are detailed but no code/data release URLs are confirmed.
evidence: Experiments, Table 2: SkillReason-4B and SkillReason-0.6B results compared with BM25, embedding models, and skill-specific retrievers across three benchmarks.
Ablation Study, Table 3: cumulative ablations show gains from Raw CL through CoT CL, distribution transfer, CoT LM, and Stage II retrieval-guided GRPO.
Appendix A.2, Tables 7-8: sensitivity analysis using validated alternative skills shows ranking stability across retrievers.
Appendix B.5, Table 11: latency analysis shows no measurable retrieval overhead from SkillReason training but large added cost from self-CoT generation.

arxiv:2608.08639.rationale: Out-of-scope database lakehouse compaction/ML-for-systems paper with no language-model, NLP, reasoning, agent, safety, or multimodal methodology. It has some low-weight relevance only via synthetic data/dataset and tabular ML training, but does not match the user's core LLM/NLP preferences. Research quality within its domain is moderate-to-strong with ablations, bootstrap CIs, cross-schema TPC-H validation, and public code/data, but the domain mismatch caps the final score at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract states 2,376 simulated Apache Iceberg tables, XGBoost regression R^2=0.998, TPC-H cross-schema R^2=0.976, and public code/data.
Section III-E reports leave-one-out ablations with R^2>=0.988 and top-k feature results.
Section III-G reports bootstrap 95% CIs and prevalence robustness.
Section III-I5 acknowledges synthetic payload, MoR/delete files, sort/z-order, and temporal evolution limitations.

arxiv:2608.08638.rationale: Pure audio/speech TTS paper with only incidental transformer/autoregressive components; it does not target LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, safety, or other preferred topics. The rubric treats pure audio as out of scope and caps overall relevance at 0.20. Within its domain the paper provides ablations and quantitative metrics, but relevance to target preferences is negligible and reproducibility is limited by the internal 550k-hour dataset.
evidence: Abstract: presents CuteTTS as a continuous-autoregressive TTS system evaluated on LibriSpeech and Seed-TTS benchmarks.
Section 3.1: describes a causal audio VAE mapping 24-kHz waveforms to 12.5 Hz continuous latents with semantic alignment.
Section 4.1: reports training on an internal multilingual dataset of approximately 550,000 hours and evaluation metrics including WER and speaker similarity.

arxiv:2608.08637.rationale: Relevant to Code & Programming and LLM-assisted program synthesis, but Rust-specific fuzz target generation rather than core LLM/NLP methodology. The generics-aware type matching and dependency-graph plus LLM synthesis are a plausible incremental combination. Evaluation provides quantitative compilation/coverage results and ablations, but uses filtered API denominators, lacks statistical testing or bug-finding validation, and has limited reproducibility due to LLM service dependence and artifact availability.
evidence: §3.6: GRAFT uses qwen3.5-plus via DashScope to concretize API sequences into compilable fuzz targets with compiler-error feedback.
§4.2 Table 2: reports macro-average compilation success 96.19% and macro-average API coverage 80.75% across 13 crates.
§4.4 Table 4: on 8 crates where all three tools run, GRAFT reports 4.76x RULF and 2.43x RPG average API coverage.
§4.5: acknowledges LLM nondeterminism, API counting/filtering limitations, and absence of bug-finding evaluation.

arxiv:2608.08636.rationale: LLM-based SciNER with type filtering, auxiliary typing, and ICL demonstration selection. Relevant to LLM/prompting/NLP; moderate novelty as combination of established ideas. Ablations and quantitative comparisons support component contributions, but baselines are partly from prior papers, no confidence intervals, and domain-specific SOTA is not surpassed. Generalizability limited to three scientific datasets; code/hyperparameters provided.
evidence: Page 25, Table 6: TdSciNER F1 results and baseline comparisons on SciERC, JNLPBA, BC5CDR.
Page 34, Table 14: Ablation removing entity type filter, auxiliary task, and ICL shows F1 drops.
Page 38, Section 5.2: Limitations acknowledge not surpassing SciBERT/BioBERT and domain/dataset constraints.
Page 23, Section 4.2.2: Implementation details including hyperparameters and LoRA; code link provided on Page 5.

arxiv:2608.08634.rationale: Relevant LLM/RAG/benchmark evaluation of open-weight and proprietary models on financial long-document QA, with hallucination and content-filter analysis, but domain-specific and incremental over prior work. Rigor is moderate due to LLM-as-judge, partially unpinned model endpoints, and judge version differences; evidence is quantitative but self-reported. Generalizability is limited to English annual reports and six question types.
evidence: Section 5.1 reports Claude Opus 4.6 accuracy 88.4%, Kimi K2.6 accuracy 83.5%, and Gemini 2.5 Pro hallucination rate 0.08%.
Table 2 documents Kimi K2.6 native-route refusals of 20 questions and zero refusals on the same questions via a proxy route.
Section 5.6 reports pooled accuracy of 77.9% with sufficient retrieval versus 12.0% under retrieval failure.
Appendix A.3 notes provider-default temperatures were used and Kimi K2.6 rejects temperature=0, making outputs non-deterministic.

arxiv:2608.08632.rationale: Airport landside traffic optimization paper is outside the AI/LLM/NLP scope: no LLM, reasoning, prompting, agents, safety, or multimodal content. The simulation study has clear equations, scenario design, two case airports, and numerical results, but relies heavily on inferred parameters and simulation-only validation, so quality components are moderate. Overall capped at 0.20 as a pure domain application.
evidence: Section 1: main contribution is an airport landside passenger-vehicle-facility-road state model with bottleneck diagnosis and MPC/QUBO-inspired dispatch.
Section 6.2: reports final passenger queue reduction from 3445.4 to 2476.5 at Shanghai Pudong and 2053.3 to 1481.9 at Hangzhou Xiaoshan under QUBO-inspired simulated annealing.
Section 6.3: reports robustness experiments under demand, supply, service, road-capacity, modal-share, and random-noise perturbations.
Section 7: acknowledges facility parameters are inferred from public information and BPR-based speed output is treated as a pressure indicator rather than measured traffic speed.

arxiv:2608.08631.rationale: Out of scope as a pure RL/control digital-twin calibration study with no language-model methodology; preference relevance is minimal. The paper combines established components and is explicitly exploratory, with no controlled ablations, single training runs, no significance tests, and simulated low-dimensional environments, limiting rigor, evidence strength, and generalizability.
evidence: Abstract: reports MAE 0.0066 with no queries and 0.0092 under a three-query budget vs 0.2031 uncalibrated.
Section 4.1: Random Forest diagnostic recovers gravity weakly (R^2 ~0.02) and not mass/length; GRU estimator reaches MAE 0.0066.
Section 4.2: terminal error 0.0092 vs 0.2031 uncalibrated, but no query-free control under the same 300-step protocol is reported.
Section 4.3: controller-conditioned error profiles vary, but checkpoints differ in mixture, architecture, data volume, and evaluation protocol, preventing attribution.

Discussion and Limitations: stagewise training, single runs per configuration, differing protocols, non-binding budget in the static Pendulum setting, and simulated low-dimensional settings are acknowledged.

arxiv:2608.08630.rationale: Relevant multimodal long-context VLM compression work with clear transformer/efficiency ties; provides ablations, baselines, hyperparameters, and code URL. However, novelty is moderate as it extends existing text soft-prompt compression and visual DeepStack ideas, the new LongVLBench is small (140 samples) and LLM-judged, some SOTA claims are overstated, and the 2M-token scalability evidence is based on synthetic prefill memory scaling rather than full end-to-end evaluation.
evidence: Abstract: claims code availability at https://github.com/ShareLab-SII/VLZip.
Section 3.1: defines hierarchical visual/text compressors and layer-specific injection via Q-Former modules and element-wise addition.
Table 1: reports LongVLBench average 61.9 for VLZip vs 47.1 for Qwen2.5-VL-7B, with 100% inference success across length bins.
Table 2: reports ICL-128k 58.8 for VLZip compared with 44.0 for Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
Section 5.3/Table 4: reports maximum trainable sequence length increasing from 20K to 120K tokens with unified compression.
Table 6 and Table 7: ablate chunk size/tokens per chunk and injection layer strategy.
Appendix 0.E: acknowledges short-context retrieval trade-offs, symmetric compression parameter limits, and suboptimal zero-effort 7B transfer.

arxiv:2608.08624.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision domain-generalization/pruning paper; only weak relevance via pruning/efficiency preference. Method has some novelty in combining cross-domain gradient alignment with differentiable masking, but evaluation is limited to ResNet-50 image classification benchmarks and does not involve LLM/NLP/agents/reasoning. Rigor is reduced by inconsistencies in the manuscript, including experimental step counts (T=200 in Appendix A vs 100,000 in Section 4) and an erroneous EMA equation (Equation 8). No code availability is stated.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports DAP results on PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita, and DomainNet with ResNet-50
Section 4.4 compares against Random, Magnitude, Taylor, IoR, and DSS pruning baselines
Appendix A Table 6 lists hyperparameters but shows total steps T=200 conflicting with Section 4 setup T=100,000
Section 5 Limitations states unstructured pruning and lack of speedup without sparse tensor support
Section 4.7 ablation compares full DAP with alpha>0 against domain-agnostic alpha=0 variant

arxiv:2608.10021.rationale: Topically relevant survey of transformer position encoding, RoPE, and long-context methods for LLMs. It provides formula derivations, method comparisons, and evaluation guidance, but is non-empirical: no original experiments, baselines, ablations, quantitative results, or artifacts; support comes from cited literature and in-text derivations, limiting evidence strength and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 5 derives RoPE and discusses KV cache behavior.
Section 6 compares PI, NTK-aware, Dynamic NTK, NTK-by-parts, YaRN, LongRoPE, and LongRoPE2.
Appendix A Table 4 lists position-encoding choices in representative LLMs.

arxiv:2608.08623.rationale: Relevant LLM/RLVR reasoning paper with safety-sensitive medical numerical reasoning, but novelty is incremental and evidence is narrow. Rigor is weakened by internal inconsistency between Section 4.5 text and Table 2 ablation values, and no significance testing. Generalization is limited to small gains on GSM8K/GPQA/CalcQA and one main medical benchmark. Reproducibility is partial: hyperparameters are given but code is only promised upon acceptance.
evidence: Section 4.4 Main Results, Table 1 reports MedCalc-R1 3B avg 51.34 vs Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct 39.03, with closed models at 67.84-73.95.
Section 4.5 Ablation Study text claims knowledge reward in isolation underperforms the baseline, but Table 2 shows w/o HyRe 46.28 vs w/o Both 39.60, contradicting the claim.
Appendix B Experiment Setting gives learning rates, batch sizes, rollout size 5, and verifier Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, but code release is only upon acceptance.
Section 4.7 Generalization Analysis reports gains of 3.13% on GSM8K and 6.06% on GPQA for Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct.

arxiv:2608.08622.rationale: Relevant multimodal video-LLM hallucination mitigation method with training-free attention intervention and contrastive decoding. Moderate novelty over prior contrastive/attention calibration methods; reasonable ablations and multi-backbone benchmarks, but hyperparameters are selected on EventHallusion and reused, with no statistical significance testing or code availability.
evidence: Abstract: proposes VADER, a training-free framework combining Visual Focus Reallocation and Selective Evidence Erasure for video LLM hallucination mitigation.
Section 4.2 Table 1: reports LLaVA-Video-7B EventHallusion accuracy of 72.60% and gains across Qwen3-VL-8B, LLaVA-OV-7B, and LLaVA-Video-7B.
Section 4.5 Table 4: core-component ablation shows VFR and SEE each improve over baseline and are complementary.
Section 5 Limitations: notes additional inference-time computation and memory from gradient-based selection and multi-branch passes.

arxiv:2608.08621.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, and evaluation. Presents a comprehensive business-agent benchmark with diagnostic ablations and reliability analyses, but limited to one simulated cross-border B2B domain and lacks explicit code/data availability in the text, tempering novelty, reproducibility, and generalizability.
evidence: Section 6.1 Performance Landscape reports 15 models, mean final net worth from $20,856 to $188,488, ICC=0.944 over 10 runs, and only four models preserve starting capital in every trial.
Section 6.5 Mechanism Ablations and Appendix G compare intended policies to neglect/shortcut baselines across portfolio selection, market events, pricing, tariffs, and customer service.
Section 6.4 Tracing Realized Value Back to Decisions details action-level attribution for tariff-shock and pricing decisions.
Section 7 Limitations states the arena abstracts external operating systems behind structured tools and is limited to cross-border B2B commerce.
Appendix H Reliability Under Business Variance reports split-half Spearman correlation 0.898 and single-run ICC(1,1)=0.626, with ten-run ICC(1,10)=0.944.

arxiv:2608.08618.rationale: Relevant applied RAG+LLM system with structured output, safety gates, and evaluation, but limited by small synthetic proof-of-concept, complete OPC-UA generation failure, narrow real-document case study, and no verifiable artifact link despite claimed harness release.
evidence: Section VI-B/Table II reports hybrid+Cross-encoder HitRate@10 0.964, MRR 0.625, nDCG 0.679.
Section VI-C reports 8.6x score separation and threshold band (0.061,0.526), but production tau=0.72 causes one false abstention.
Section VI-D/Table III reports OPC-UA field-level F1 0.000 in 3/3 runs while other protocols are perfect.
Section VI-E/Table IV reports zero safety-constraint violations and 100% failure detection across 15 runs, but on a small proof-of-concept benchmark.
Section VI-H notes UR5e HitRate@10 falls to 0.40 and tau must be recalibrated per corpus.

arxiv:2608.08617.rationale: Domain-focused mobile visual analytics application for classroom discussion, with LLM/NLP used only as an analysis component rather than as a methodological contribution. Falls below the 0.20 threshold for out-of-scope domain applications despite mentioning LLMs, ASR, and topic analysis. Evaluation is preliminary and qualitative with small pilot deployments.
evidence: Section 4.2.1 Semantic Analysis states Qwen-Max is used for interaction recognition, topic extraction, and topic tracking.
Section 6.1.3 Comparative Study reports 10 and 11 expert-annotated anomalies with MobileGroupVis identifying 8 and 9 anomalies versus 3 and 4 for the baseline.
Section 6.2 Expert Feedback reports qualitative interviews with seven experts and no statistical significance testing.
Section 8 conclusion states case studies and expert interviews provide preliminary evidence.

arxiv:2608.08612.rationale: Strong topical alignment with agentic multimodal QA, RAG/memory, long-context and reasoning preferences, though no Japanese-specific relevance. Method is moderately novel in moving rubric-based sufficiency verification into a long-video agent loop, but it combines familiar components. Experiments include broad benchmarks, ablations and efficiency analyses, but evidence is weakened by single-run reporting, no variance or significance testing, and reliance on claimed future baselines. Generalizability is reasonable across five video QA datasets but remains within one task family. Reproducibility is aided by detailed appendices and hyperparameters, though no code release is explicitly provided.
evidence: Section 3.3 describes a rubric-guided retrieve–verify–answer agent loop with a shared VLM serving as planner, verifier, and answerer.
Section 3.1 describes the offline-online hierarchical video memory and retrieval structure.
Table 1 reports REVEAL-27B results across five long-video QA benchmarks.
Table 2 ablates iterative retrieval, offline memory, online memory, and rubric-guided sufficiency verification.

arxiv:2608.08611.rationale: Out-of-scope EDA/hardware design automation paper: despite using LLM communication traces, it contributes chip-to-chip interconnect simulation and Bayesian DSE rather than language modeling, NLP, transformer, or other core AI/ML methodology. It reports moderate systems validation (FPGA-prototype timing error, speedups, and LLM-workload case studies), but the work is domain-specific and not aligned with core LLM/NLP research preferences; overall capped at 0.20 as an out-of-scope systems/hardware application.
evidence: Abstract claims 2.46-8.23% timing error and 44.1% goodput improvement.
Section 4.1 reports validation against a 4-XPU FPGA-based prototype across three traffic patterns.
Section 6 reports a 32-XPU case study using DeepSeek-R1-671B inference, LLaMA3.1-405B inference, and Qwen3-30B training communication traces.

arxiv:2608.08608.rationale: Out-of-scope pure scientific ML/CFD neural operator. The paper addresses Fourier Neural Operators for PDEs on varying geometries and CFD solver initialization, with no LLM/NLP/agents/reasoning/language methodology. Scientific AI is the only weak preference match, so final score is capped at most 0.20 despite detailed quantitative CFD reporting.
evidence: Abstract: FNO geometry framework and CFD initialization, no language-model component.
Section 3.3: main contributions are RANS/URANS/DNS solver-work reductions, not NLP/LLM.

arxiv:2608.08607.rationale: Conceptual perspective on NLP for mental healthcare in Algeria. Partially relevant to NLP and medical AI but lacks LLM, Japanese, reasoning, agent, or evaluation methodology. No experiments, datasets, or models; claims rely on narrative synthesis. Framework transferability is proposed but untested.
evidence: Abstract describes a conceptual framework and roadmap rather than an empirical study.
Section 4 maps NLP capabilities to four failure axes without presenting experimental validation.
Section 5 provides research recommendations by time horizon but no quantitative evaluation or reproducibility artifacts.

arxiv:2608.08606.rationale: Highly relevant due to fine-tuned LLM gender classification and bias mitigation in MT, though not Japanese-specific. Moderate novelty: new En-Ro datasets and pipeline, but core tag-based MT and LLM classification are established. Rigor is limited by single-native-speaker manual evaluation on WinoMT/WinoGender without inter-annotator agreement or significance testing, and the GPT-5.2 comparison is not reproducible. Quantitative gains are large but externally weak; dataset release and hyperparameter details support reproducibility.
evidence: §5.1 reports curriculum fine-tuning, LoRA configuration, and Table 4 joint F1 up to 0.96.
§5.2/Table 5 reports validation BLEU/chrF/TER/COMET; best full fine-tuning COMET 0.853.
§6/Table 6 reports WinoMT Pro 96.34%, Anti 93.68%, and WinoGender 91.53% versus raw 59.05/50.13/50.28.
§6 states manual evaluation was conducted by a native Romanian speaker with spot checks, without inter-annotator agreement statistics.

arxiv:2608.08605.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM multi-agent evaluation, aligning with Agents & Tool Use, Red Teaming & Evaluation, and LLM preferences. The unified graph abstraction and reference-forest evaluation are moderately novel, and the paper provides quantitative robustness, perturbation, and cost studies. However, rigor is limited by lack of statistical significance/error bars, LLM-based filtering and diagnostic subjectivity, and some robustness results are reported only as aggregate rankings. Reproducibility is supported by data/code availability claims and detailed appendices.
evidence: Section 4.2: filtering pipeline retains 844 queries from seven public datasets.
Table 1 (Section 5.2): reports Accuracy, Forest Match, Node Validity, Mean Uptake, Content Redundancy, Best Similarity, Tokens, and Efficiency for six frameworks; accuracy range is 0.531-0.569.
Section 5.3 and Tables 2-3: held-out reference-generator and gold-conditioned vs open-ended robustness; Kendall tau ranges 0.60-1.00 and 0.867, with Top-3 preserved in most settings.
Section 5.4 and Appendix A: controlled perturbations; node deletion at p=0.5 produces largest Forest Match decrease of 0.058, and 36 TSP threshold settings preserve ranking with Kendall tau=1.00.
Section 5.6: cost analysis reports ForestBench evaluates 1000 traces in 0.7s with zero inference tokens vs LLM-as-Judge roughly 34 minutes.

arxiv:2608.08604.rationale: Multi-agent reinforcement learning with preference-based reward modeling; relevant to Reinforcement Learning and multi-agent preferences but not LLM/NLP/Japanese NLP methodology. Theoretical contributions are moderate but rely on strong alignment assumptions, and empirical validation is limited to small MPE tasks and a custom production simulation. Reproducibility is supported by pseudocode, hyperparameters, and a code link.
evidence: Section IV-A presents Assumptions 1-7 and Nash equilibrium convergence theorems.
Section V-B reports comparable performance to QMIX on Simple-Spread, Simple-Speaker-Listener, and Simple-Reference.
Section V-D includes ablations and comparisons to MAPT, Global-PbRL, and MATD3.
Section V-A provides hyperparameters and a code link.

arxiv:2608.08601.rationale: Highly relevant to AI agents, workplace automation, and AI safety/risk taxonomies. The paper provides a multi-layer framework, a large LLM-generated risk corpus grounded in O*NET tasks, and validation via workers and LLM-as-judge, but it is a socio-technical taxonomy study rather than a technical ML contribution. Rigor is moderate: documented methodology and quantitative comparisons, but small human samples and reliance on LLM-generated scenarios limit strength. Generalizability is constrained by U.S.-centric O*NET tasks.
evidence: §3.3 states gpt-4o-mini generated 8,356 risk scenarios from 2,078 O*NET job task descriptions.
§3.4 reports worker plausibility 4.03/5 and LLM-judge plausibility 4.81/5, with task alignment worker 3.94/5 and LLM 4.60/5.
§4 Finding 2 reports Erroneous Agent Actions as 30.6% of scenarios and 88.2% rated high or critical.
§4 Finding 4 reports usability mean 5.75 vs 5.46 (p=.027) and 64% preference in non-tied comparisons against GenAI Risk Taxonomy.
§5.3 notes limitations that scenario frequencies should not be interpreted as real workplace occurrence estimates and that O*NET is U.S.-centric.

arxiv:2608.08600.rationale: This is a visual multi-agent world model with a diffusion renderer and no language/LLM methodology, so it is largely out of scope despite the multi-agent keyword. The architecture has moderate novelty, but evidence is limited to self-ablation, qualitative evaluations, and sparse implementation/training details.
evidence: Abstract: proposes Khora as a multi-agent visual world model; no LLM/language methodology is present.
Section 6: states evaluation is primarily qualitative and requires a coarse static prior per environment.
Table 2: visual-quality comparison is limited to Khora and Khora w/o Cross-Agent State, with no independent baselines.
Section 5.2: user study reports mean ratings but does not provide sample sizes or numerical confidence intervals.

arxiv:2608.08598.rationale: Pure robotics/RL control for underwater vehicles with no language or LLM/NLP methodology; out-of-scope for the stated preferences and capped at 0.20. The paper has simulation-only evaluation, but includes quantitative ablations and a stated lack of physical experiments limits generalizability.
evidence: Abstract and Table 8 report consistent quantitative reductions versus P-PID, including position error to 42.7% and settling time to 10.6%.
Section 5.1 Tables 6-7 provide ablation and baseline evaluation results over 1,000 simulation episodes.
Section 6 Conclusions and Future work states physical experiments could not be conducted due to facility limitations, limiting sim-to-real validation.

arxiv:2608.08596.rationale: Moderate relevance: the work is multimodal language/instruction generation with MLLMs and embodied navigation, touching Multimodal AI, Reasoning, RLHF/training, and NLP, but it is not a core LLM/agent-safety paper and has lower-weight robotics/embodied relevance. Research quality is moderate: it introduces a benchmark and curriculum method with ablations and downstream navigation, but is simulator-only, lacks statistical testing and code/data availability, and contains some table inconsistencies.
evidence: Sec 3.2 describes the VideoNIG benchmark construction from R2R-CE/RxR-CE with Gold/Tyro/Curiosity/Explorer tour types and filtering.
Table 2 reports Rouge-L/SPICE and multiple-choice/orthogonal-choice results across MLLMs and fine-tuned Qwen3-VL variants.
Table 3 reports downstream VLN execution metrics (SR/SPL/OS/NE), showing lower performance on Explorer Tour than Gold Route.
Sec 5.3 and Tables 4-5 present chain-of-thought and curriculum learning ablations.

arxiv:2608.08594.rationale: Pure diffusion bridge model for image restoration (deraining, super-resolution, inpainting) with no language/LLM/NLP methodology; under the rubric, image/video diffusion without language methodology is out of scope. The paper provides formal derivations and quantitative comparisons, but relevance to the stated preferences is minimal, constraining the overall score.
evidence: {'section': 'Abstract', 'content': 'Diffusion bridge models ... image-to-image translation and restoration'}
{'section': 'Section 5', 'content': 'evaluate our models on image super-resolution, image deraining, and image inpainting'}

arxiv:2608.08590.rationale: Out-of-scope computational social choice/fair-division proof paper. It contains SMT verification and mentions AI-assisted proof, but has no LLM, NLP, agent-methodology, reasoning, or other AI/ML research contribution matching the preferences. Domain-level verification appears substantial, but overall score is capped low as a non-AI/ML application.
evidence: Section 5: describes independent certifier and negative controls.
Section 6: reports 122,553 unsat certificates and zero coverage gaps.
Section 9: discloses AI-assisted proof but no language-model methodology contribution.

arxiv:2608.08589.rationale: Out-of-scope industrial surface-defect computer vision application with a peripheral LLM reporting wrapper; no LLM/language methodology or NLP contribution. The core contribution is CNN classification and Grad-CAM on NEU-DET, with controlled Llama-3.1-8B-Instant report generation. Quantitative evaluation exists but is domain-specific and limited.
evidence: Abstract (Page 1): describes RobustDefect-LLM as an industrial surface-defect inspection framework integrating deep-learning classification, Grad-CAM, confidence-aware decision support, and controlled AI-assisted reporting.
Section 3.2 (Page 5-6): states the reporting module uses Llama-3.1-8B-Instant through the Groq API and validates/falls back to deterministic rule-based reports.
Section 4 (Page 8): reports using NEU-DET with 1,799 grayscale images from six steel surface defect categories.
Section 6 (Page 13, Table 10): reports 100/100 controlled LLM reports passed validation checks under nominal conditions.
