arxiv:2608.08588.rationale: This paper concerns lazy Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for infinite-dimensional probabilistic programs, with no substantive match to LLM/NLP or other listed preference topics. It contains formal PACAP and stationarity analysis and reproducible code, but the problem domain is outside the curator's target scope, so the final score is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Section 3.1.2 Theorem 3 claims compositional PACAP guarantees via logical relations.
Section 4.4 Framework A and Theorem 5 provide stationarity conditions and acceptance-ratio reduction.
Section 6 Experiments reports quantitative comparisons such as geometric distribution TVD values and random walk ESS/s, and includes a GitHub implementation link.

arxiv:2608.08585.rationale: Pure computer vision paper on event-camera 3D reconstruction with 3D Gaussian Splatting; no LLM/NLP/transformer-centered methodology, so it is out-of-scope and capped at low relevance. The method includes ablations and quantitative comparisons, but the domain is narrow, evaluated on limited scenes, and no code or statistical significance tests are reported.
evidence: Section V-A describes the Replica and TUM-VIE datasets and evaluation metrics.
Section V-B, Table II reports PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS improvements over baselines.
Section V-C, Table IV reports component ablation results.

arxiv:2608.08584.rationale: This is a wireless communications paper on fluid antenna systems and interference alignment. It does not address large language models, NLP, agents, reasoning, multimodal AI, safety, or any other in-scope preference area, so preference relevance is zero and the overall score is capped as an out-of-scope domain application. The technical content appears internally coherent with theoretical derivations and simulations, but it has no relevance to the requested AI/ML topics.
evidence: Abstract: describes FAS-enabled interference alignment for multiuser wireless networks and outage probability analysis.
Section I Introduction: frames the work in wireless interference alignment and fluid antenna systems, with no AI/LLM/NLP methodology.

arxiv:2608.08583.rationale: LLM-based sequential recommendation is a domain application, not a core LLM/NLP methodology contribution; under the rubric it is out-of-scope and capped at 0.20. The paper proposes cosine similarity and contrastive structure-preserving losses, with some useful shuffle diagnostics and ablations, but evidence is limited to LastFM/MovieLens-100K, significance is marginal on MovieLens, and no code release or broad generalization is shown.
evidence: §1 Introduction: embedding-shuffle diagnostic on MovieLens reports HR@1 changes of 0.4531 to 0.4542 for Direct and 0.4743 to 0.4678 for LLaRA, indicating weak reliance on collaborative embeddings.

§3.3 Overall Recommendation Performance and Table 2: Contrastive-LM achieves HR@1 0.5546 on LastFM and 0.4881 on MovieLens with GRU4Rec embeddings, and 0.5511/0.4993 with SASRec embeddings; significance is p<0.05 on LastFM and marginal p<0.1 on MovieLens.
§3.7 Ablation of Joint Fine-tuning: Table 4 shows joint fine-tuning improves methods, with Cosine-LM/Contrastive-LM remaining above Direct/LLaRA.

arxiv:2608.08580.rationale: Pure computer-vision object detection challenge report (pollinator detection with Co-DINO/Swin-L). Although it uses a transformer backbone, it has no LLM/NLP/language methodology and is explicitly out of scope, so preference relevance is very low and the overall score is capped. Contributions are challenge-specific (class-aware crop Mosaic, fixed-ETF query regularization) with limited novelty; no quantitative ablation for the proposed loss/data schedule and no significance testing. Evidence is mainly leaderboard mAP and held-out comparisons. Reproducibility is partially supported by a code link and implementation details.
evidence: Abstract: reports the CVPPA@ECCV 2026 BuzzSpot Challenge for detecting bees, bumblebees, hoverflies, and moths and selects Co-DINO with Swin-L.
Section 3.1: reports FinalTest contains 4,763 keyframes with hidden annotations and uses COCO-style mAP.
Section 2.3: describes the 3-stage training schedule with class-aware crop mosaics and fixed-ETF loss active throughout.

arxiv:2608.08577.rationale: Out-of-scope financial fraud decision-support/risk-control paper. It addresses delayed/selective audit labels, finite-sample risk certification, and review workload, but has no preferred LLM/NLP/transformer/agent/multimodal methodology. Domain application without language methodology, so overall score is capped near 0.20 despite some formal analysis and experiments.
evidence: Abstract: describes FCAC for fraud operations audit evidence and review workload; no language-model component.

arxiv:2608.08575.rationale: Out-of-scope 3D medical image segmentation paper with no LLM/language/reasoning/agent/NLP methodology. It uses dual-scale self-attention and grouped channel attention, which intersect only weakly with transformer/attention preferences. The work reports standard benchmarks, comparisons, ablations, and quantitative results, but the domain application is explicitly out of scope and is capped at 0.20 overall.

arxiv:2608.08574.rationale: Federated learning robustness paper relevant mainly via adversarial defense/robustness and training optimization, but not LLM/NLP-focused. The proposed R2-NNM combines reputation with NNM and Multi-Krum, which is incremental rather than substantially novel. Empirical evaluation includes multiple datasets, attacks, baselines, and ablations, but reputation effectiveness is partly simulation-based and some table numbering is inconsistent.

arxiv:2608.08572.rationale: Theoretical statistical-mechanics/RG model of LLM distillation safety and reliability. It is relevant to LLM safety and distillation preferences, but empirical support is limited to digitized refusal-token data from one external study, with no code, baselines, ablations, or direct multigenerational validation. The binary/canonical/weak-alignment assumptions limit generalizability and reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: 'The predicted trade-off is consistent with refusal-token data [arXiv: 2412.06748].'

Supplemental Material III: 'We now use the data from Ref. Jain et al. 2025 to test the conclusions of this work.'

arxiv:2608.08570.rationale: Highly relevant LLM agent/code/training method for converting failed SWE-agent rollouts into procedural training signal. Evaluations include baselines, ablations, cross-harness and multilingual transfer, but novelty is moderate over hindsight-hint/skill extraction work and evidence lacks statistical significance or an explicit limitations analysis.

arxiv:2608.08569.rationale: Relevant to LLM efficiency, long-context memory, inference, and multimodal audio-language modeling; not pure audio. Method uses ASR text anchors for KV cache compression and includes ablations/efficiency measurements. However, the main comparison is confounded because VoxZip injects ASR transcriptions absent from the Full KV baseline, so claims of exceeding uncompressed performance are not controlled. Single model family (Qwen3-Omni) and promised code limit generalizability/reproducibility.
evidence: Table 1 reports VoxZip at 25% KV cache budget achieves average 69.75 vs Full KV 67.07 (PRR 104.00) and at 5% 61.31 (PRR 91.41).

Section 4.4.2 Table 4 evaluates text-only, audio-only, partial, and full fusion, but no Full KV+text baseline is shown.

arxiv:2608.08567.rationale: Graph-only paper relevant to GNN/knowledge-graph preferences but not core LLM/NLP. The SIG construction is moderately novel and formally justified, but node classification is weak, evidence is mostly benchmark tables with limited ablations, and no code availability is stated.

Section 5.3, Table 3: Sigil-nc achieves 66.10 average accuracy, best on 5/26 and top-2 on 10/26 node classification datasets, trailing TAG and RGVT.

arxiv:2608.08566.rationale: Medical imaging/object-detection application with no language-model methodology; out of scope. Quantitative slide-level evaluation and a hard-count baseline are present, but evidence is limited by single-site data, simulated slides without patient grouping, and no code/data release.

arxiv:2608.08563.rationale: Weather forecasting evaluation with generic AI/ML post-processing is a pure domain application outside LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning scope, so overall score is capped at 0.20. Standard verification metrics, single event, no controlled raw-vs-postprocessed experiment, and proprietary archived data limit quality and reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.08561.rationale: Out-of-scope medical diagnostic case study using DeepProbLog/ProbLog and a CNN for facial palsy; weak overlap with preferences limited to diagnostic reasoning and interpretability, with no LLM/NLP/agent/RAG language methodology. Evaluation compares self-derived probabilistic models and reports near-perfect CNN metrics but lacks independent validation or strong baselines.

arxiv:2608.08559.rationale: Out-of-scope differentiable-simulation/numerical-optimization paper with no LLM, NLP, transformer, agent, vision-language, or other core preference methodology. The work is methodologically strong within its domain, with controlled baselines, ablations, and reproducibility, but relevance to the stated preferences is minimal; final score is capped at 0.20 as a pure domain application.
evidence: §6.1 Table 1 shows exact reverse-sweep adjoint vs autograd and 37% equation-level error at K=1.

arxiv:2608.08558.rationale: Out-of-scope pure robotics/embodied AI paper focused on distilling video diffusion priors into World Action Models. Although it uses language instructions, it contributes no LLM/NLP or language-methodology advance; the technical content concerns robot policy learning, inverse dynamics, and video rollouts. Experimental sections are fairly detailed, but relevance to the stated preferences is minimal, so the overall score is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: proposes Vid2WAM for offline distillation from a video foundation model into a World Action Model for robot policy learning.

Ablation Studies: Table 5 compares Fast-WAM, Dual Action DiT, No Adapter, Pseudo Action Only, Future Latent Only, and Teacher Policy.

arxiv:2608.08557.rationale: Highly relevant agentic multimodal tool-use and training-data paper. The causal-utility filtering idea is a meaningful but incremental refinement over outcome-only SFT. Quantitative results are strong across four backbones and five domains with ablations and OOD tests, but rigor is tempered by an internal filter-threshold inconsistency (Section 3.4 δ=0.25 vs Appendix A.2 δ=0.1), no reported variance/statistical testing, and some confounded baseline tool environments. Code and detailed hyperparameters support reasonable reproducibility.
evidence: Table 1 (Section 4.3) reports consistent OpenVisTool-Bench gains across Qwen3.5-4B/9B/27B and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, averaging +10.7 over no-tool baselines.
Figure 3 and Section 4.5 ablation show requiring both outcome validity and causal utility outperforms each filter alone, by 1.7 and 3.4 points respectively.
Table 2 (Section 4.4) shows out-of-distribution gains on Agentic-MME and VTC-Bench for all four fine-tuned backbones.
Appendix G and Tables 6-7 supply training and evaluation hyperparameters, while Appendix A.2 states causal-utility retention threshold 0.1 and Section 3.4 states δ=0.25.

arxiv:2608.08556.rationale: Pure IoT/cyber-physical explainability position paper with no language-model or NLP methodology. It touches interpretability only in an applied IoT sense, so preference relevance is low. The work offers formal definitions and a conceptual architecture but no experiments, baselines, or implementation, limiting evidence and reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: introduces IoXT as a system-level paradigm for intelligent IoT, without LLM/NLP methods.
Section 5: defines trace completeness, orphan-actuation rate, temporal consistency, and semantic-preservation metrics, but provides no empirical validation.
Section 9: presents future research agenda, confirming the paper is conceptual rather than experimentally evaluated.

arxiv:2608.08555.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/diffusion image-to-image translation without language methodology; semantically calibrated self-attention for visible-to-infrared translation and downstream infrared detection does not engage LLM/NLP topics. Quantitative comparisons and ablations are present, but relevance is capped at 0.20 per scope rules.
evidence: Table II reports PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/FID on M3FD, FLIR, and KAIST.
Table V ablates clean condition encoding and SGSC components on FLIR.
Table IV reports downstream infrared object detection results on M3FD and FLIR.

arxiv:2608.08554.rationale: Out-of-scope wireless/RF power-amplifier linearization paper using transfer learning and a small feedforward network. No substantive alignment with LLM/NLP, reasoning, agents, safety, or other preferred AI/ML areas. Domain-adequate experiments and baselines, but transfer-learning contribution is not novel from an ML standpoint and generalizability is limited to APTBM-specific constraints.
evidence: Section V-A describes the simulation/measurement setup, PA models, and ACLR/IBO/PAE/EVM/BER metrics.

arxiv:2608.08553.rationale: Pure video super-resolution/computer vision paper with no language methodology, placing it in the explicit out-of-scope category despite sparse-attention and world-model terminology. Quantitative gains are claimed but lack statistical backing and comparability safeguards; reproducibility is limited by absent code/hyperparameter details.
evidence: Section 4.1 evaluates only on VSR benchmarks such as REDS, YouHQ40, SPMCS, UDM10, VideoLQ, and MovieLQ; no NLP/LLM tasks are used.
Table 1 reports MotionCraft PSNR 28.15 vs 25.38 for SeedVR2 on UDM10, but no confidence intervals or significance tests are provided.
Section 4.7/Figure 6 provide qualitative motion-reliability claims; no code, data, or detailed training hyperparameter availability statement appears.

arxiv:2608.08545.rationale: Pure RL/robotics navigation with no LLM or language methodology; relevance is minimal and falls under excluded pure robotics. The reparameterized curriculum is an incremental combination of existing curriculum learning and reparameterization ideas. Evaluation uses two Gym tasks, five seeds, and several baselines, but high variance, no significance testing, and mixed/inconsistent gains limit rigor and evidence. Generalizability is limited to two low-dimensional simulated continuous-control environments, while hyperparameters and architecture are documented enough for partial reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: proposes a reparameterized curriculum generation framework for structured continuous environment parameters using unidirectional gradient-based optimization.
Section 5.4, Table 1: Reparam-M achieves 650±134 mean reward vs Manual 617±166 in Car Racing.
Section 5.4, Table 2: Reparam achieves 127±136 vs Manual 117±142 in Bipedal Walker.
Appendix C: Reports training hyperparameters and five random seeds.

arxiv:2608.08542.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM safety, alignment, and red-teaming/evaluation, with direct study of jailbreak robustness in skill-merged models. Strengths include a controlled factorial benchmark, multiple attack families, paired statistical tests, cross-base replication, and detailed reproducibility material. Weaknesses are limited full-grid scale, moderate judge agreement (kappa=0.66), adaptive ASR as a budget-limited lower bound, and a geometric signal validated mainly for same-recipe abliteration-style refusal removal.
evidence: Section 5: static vs adaptive ASR across six bases shows Qwen/Gemma fragile and Llama/Phi-4 robust under template attack
Table 1: GCG 100-step static/adaptive ASR with Wilson 95% CIs on a seeded 50-behavior subset
Section 4: two-judge AND protocol reports Cohen's kappa=0.66 on a 100-item audit
Appendix S5: independent erosion sources and paired McNemar/bootstrap gap statistics
Section 7: SubSafe-Merge results at k=8 show safety recovery at held GSM8K capability

arxiv:2608.08541.rationale: Pure computer vision spiking transformer paper with no language/LLM methodology; matches only transformer/attention terminology and is out of scope under the rubric, capping relevance. The proposed SCLA-BCP locality mechanism is incremental within spiking vision transformers, with solid ablations and multi-dataset experiments but no LLM/NLP connection.
evidence: Section 5.2 reports ImageNet-1K deployment depth results for QKFormer and Spikingformer.
Tables 1-5 report classification/detection/segmentation comparisons across static and neuromorphic datasets.
Section 5.5 provides ablations decomposing SCLA and BCP and comparing shifted-window designs.

arxiv:2608.08537.rationale: Pure mathematical dynamical systems/PDE analysis of Wentzell boundary conditions; no LLM/NLP/agents/multimodal language methodology. Out of scope; rigorous theorem/proof structure does not contribute to AI/ML relevance.
evidence: Abstract: 'Two identical scalar dynamical systems coupled through a scalar diffusion equation...'
Section 1 Introduction: system (1.1) is motivated by biological membranes and diffusive coupling; no language-model or AI methodology.
Section 6 Numerical asymptotics: numerical continuation of PDE boundary-value problems, not ML benchmarks.

arxiv:2608.08536.rationale: Moderately relevant due to mechanistic interpretability of transformer computation graphs and GNN methods, though not an LLM/language-modeling paper and central graph-learning focus carries lower preference weight. Novelty is moderate: amortized cross-case circuit learning and the benchmark extension are useful, but the architecture largely combines existing GNN/alignment/pooling components. Rigor is moderate: detailed theoretical motivation, grouped validation, and ablations are present, but results are synthetic-only and the headline configuration is post-selected from held-out evaluation, which limits the strength of the evidence. Generalizability is limited to semi-synthetic Tracr-derived circuits with known ground truth. Reproducibility is fairly strong with code availability and extensive implementation details.
evidence: Section 5 reports best GCL median edge AUROC 0.902, control 0.825, and adapted PGExplainer 0.858.

Appendix F.1 describes grouped 5-fold cross-validation, 16 held-out InterpBench cases, and head-level score conversion.
Appendix D details the TracrBench-derived benchmark split with 50 cross-validation cases and outlines leakage-limiting grouping checks.
Appendix F states the implementation is openly available and Appendix B provides architectural and feature details.
Section 5 Discussion states the study is preliminary and limited to synthetic model-task pairs with known ground-truth circuits.

arxiv:2608.08535.rationale: Applied HCI/education system that uses LLMs and a multimodal LLM, but it does not advance core LLM/NLP methods and is primarily a domain application. The user study has controlled comparisons, blind expert ratings, and statistical tests, but sample sizes are small, detection precision is modest (0.634), and generalization/reproduction are limited.

Section 4.2.2: GPT-4.1 and Qwen-2.5-Omni drive interaction modules and multimodal practice evaluation.

arxiv:2608.08531.rationale: Out of scope: pure computer vision/event-based dynamic scene reconstruction with no language-model methodology; touches only low-weight Computer Vision/Video preferences. Method has some novelty and ablations, but evidence is simulated-event only and generalizability is limited; final score capped at or below 0.20 per out-of-scope policy.

arxiv:2608.08528.rationale: Relevant LLM/agent/code/inference cost-routing framework, but largely a systems design combining known routing, benchmarking, and difficulty-grading ideas. It provides a formal expected-completion-cost proof, yet empirical backing is thin: savings and difficulty splits are largely illustrative, with no ablations or live A/B results, and proprietary data/prices limit reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.08525.rationale: Federated distillation/OOD is tangential to core LLM/NLP preferences; the LLM is used mainly as a synthetic review generator rather than studied as a model. The proposed centroid/TopK proxy selection is relatively straightforward, and the evidence is limited to one Amazon-review sentiment task with few communication rounds, no reported variance or multiple seeds, and small performance differences. Code and prompts are partially available, but generalizability beyond product-review classification is weak.
evidence: Section 4.3 proposes a vocabulary-constrained LLM-based proxy generation strategy using few-shot system and user prompts.
Table 1 reports global F1 with and without proxy data but gives no variance or confidence intervals.
Section 5.2 reports only 5 communication rounds, 3 local epochs, and A100 training.
Section 6.4 provides computational complexity O((K+1)|D_P|d) for proxy selection.
Limitations acknowledges evaluation on only 5/10 clients and classification as a representative task.

arxiv:2608.08523.rationale: Relevant LLM/multimodal embodied-agent planning method combining Quality-Diversity prompt-policy search with online stall recovery. The combination is moderately novel but built on established MAP-Elites and prompt evolution. Quantitative comparisons and ablations support the main claims, but rigor is limited by point estimates without repeated runs or uncertainty, underspecified ablation of archive selection, abstract mutation/recombination operators, and missing appendix-level hyperparameters. Generalizability is supported only by TDW and a small VLN-CE pilot; code availability is claimed but details are incomplete.

Section 4.3, Table 4 reports ablations for online switching and archive selection.
Section 4.2, Table 3 reports VLN-CE pilot SR/SPL/NE gains.
Section 3.3, Algorithm 1 describes offline MAP-Elites archive construction.

arxiv:2608.08522.rationale: Out-of-scope robotics/event-camera simulation paper with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/safety methodology. Marginal relevance via synthetic data and robotics simulation, but the pure robotics cap applies. System performance is reported, but there is no quantitative real-data validation or ML baseline comparison.

arxiv:2608.08521.rationale: Pure computer vision/biometrics paper using classical handcrafted features for face spoof/disguise detection; no LLM/NLP/agent/transformer methodology, placing it out of scope and capping overall relevance. The comparison is systematic but limited: established methods, fixed training-set thresholds, within-database evaluation, no statistical significance tests or neural baselines.

arxiv:2608.08519.rationale: Pure event-camera/diffusion CV paper without language methodology; out-of-scope and capped low. It provides some quantitative tables and implementation details but lacks ablations, statistical tests, and code; limited generalizability.

arxiv:2608.08516.rationale: Topically highly relevant to LLM agents, multi-agent systems, and AI safety/governance. The paper provides a conceptual framework with formal definitions and mechanisms, but it explicitly lacks large-scale empirical validation; only small-sample prototype tests are mentioned. No quantitative results, baselines, ablations, code, or data are provided, so evidence strength is low and reproducibility is limited.

arxiv:2608.08514.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM reasoning, self-consistency, and reliability; independent reproduction with useful negative evidence but limited novelty, small/underpowered extension sets, and mostly null or model-dependent effects.
evidence: Abstract states code, data, and experiment logs are available at GitHub.

Section 5.1 reports exact reproduction of RPC original math grid: PPL 21.89/73.14, SC 24.82/13.37, RPC 26.15/12.32 versus reported values, with RPC improving accuracy and calibration; extensions show no significant edge over self-consistency (paired p>=0.28).
Section 5.1 Tables 2-4 show RPC ties or mixed differences on BIRD, KO-VER, KCC, LFUD, GSM8K, FOLIO, LogiQA; BIRD gap at K=32 is +2.5 (p=0.16) and reverses to -0.25 at n=200.
Section 5.2 reports LCF logic-validity probe separability 0.82 at best sub-layer versus 0.95 semantic control, Qwen3 ΔProb change p=0.56, and significant ΔProb degradation on Llama-2 and Mistral.
Limitations states evaluation sets are n=80-320, underpowered for gaps below about 5.0 accuracy points, and some generated valid labels are noisy, weakening the logic-validity target.

arxiv:2608.08512.rationale: Strong LLM/evaluation/RAG/temporal-reasoning benchmark paper with formalized version resolution over evolving regulatory documents. It reports a detailed multi-task, multi-setting protocol and quantitative results, so topical relevance is high. Novelty is moderate: formal amendment-centric benchmark and code-mixed dual-calendar corpus are distinctive, but related temporal/evolving QA datasets exist. Rigor is solid internally (expert verification, deterministic date gate, judge reliability, RAG ablations, limitations), though no human baseline and reliance on LLM generation temper strength. Evidence supports the main claims but lacks significance testing and broad external validation. Generalizability is limited by a single domain, language pair, and calendar system. Reproducibility is good due to detailed prompts, schema, metrics, and claimed code/data availability.
evidence: Abstract: TIDE, 3,050 QA pairs over 644 official instruments, nine LLMs, best macro-averaged accuracy 68.5%
Section 2.5: eight task types including Temporal MCQ, Event Sorting, Perturbation Detection, and Context Misalignment
Section 2.4: two SMEs rate 94.89% factually correct with Cohen's kappa = 0.91
Section 3.2: LLM-as-a-Council with three heterogeneous judges, Fleiss' kappa in 0.8297-0.861, and deterministic date gate

Limitations: single Bangladesh customs domain, specific language pair/calendar, unverifiable parametric assumptions, semantic retriever without temporal reranking

arxiv:2608.08510.rationale: Domain-specific analysis of audio-visual cocktail-party speech recognition; LLMs appear only as clustering/post-correction tools (Section 4.2), so core LLM/NLP relevance is limited. The paper is a descriptive challenge comparison with no statistical testing or explicit limitations, and no released code/artifacts from the paper itself.

Section 4.2: LLM-based semantic clustering uses Qwen-2.5/DeepSeek R1 and Qwen3.

arxiv:2608.08508.rationale: Out-of-scope computer vision/video super-resolution and quality assessment work; only tangential transformer/CLIP/SLM mentions. Quantitative tables show modest metric gains but lack significance tests, ablations, code availability, and detailed hyperparameters.
evidence: Table 1 lists baseline and TTA-VQA results for PLCC/SRCC/KRCC/RMSE across FVQA, Fast-B, Dover, COVER, SAMA (Section 3.1).
Table 2 reports VSR model results with and without adaptive quality loss on RVSR, MB, VLQ, K||Lens (Section 3.1).

arxiv:2608.08506.rationale: Directly relevant to Large Language Models and scaling/efficiency. The paper provides substantial experiments on Llama/Qwen3 across compression rates, baselines, ablations, and a 32B scaling study, but novelty is relatively incremental over prior PTQ/compression error-correction work, gains are mixed across model families, hyperparameters are sensitive, and no code release is stated.

arxiv:2608.08503.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM reasoning, CoT supervision, and multilingual fine-tuning. The matched answer-only vs CoT design, paired significance tests, contamination audit, and human reasoning-quality assessment are strengths. However, the study relies on a single small Bangla dataset, one inaccessible teacher model, limited seed robustness, co-author annotators, and omits code/data release and full training details.

Section 4.7 Table 10 reports human evaluation criteria, kappa, and pairwise significance tests.

arxiv:2608.08497.rationale: A visual analytics/domain application with LLM-derived personas and multi-agent simulation, giving moderate overlap with agents, LLM, and reasoning preferences but not advancing language-model methodology. Evaluation includes case studies, simulation fidelity metrics, and an N=13 user study; however, small samples, limited baselines, and SocialFi-specific scope constrain rigor, evidence, and generalizability.

arxiv:2608.08494.rationale: This is a medical report generation paper applying DPO/LLM alignment to chest X-ray and endoscopy data. Despite overlap with alignment and vision-language topics, medical imaging applications are explicitly out-of-scope and capped at 0.20. The paper reports quantitative comparisons and ablations, but lacks statistical significance testing, human evaluation, and public access to the in-house endoscopy data, and the DPO extension is relatively incremental.

arxiv:2608.08491.rationale: Relevant to reward-model/RLHF, preference learning, and vision-language judge methods, though embedded in robot manipulation rather than core LLM research. The main contribution is a PAVA/isotonic score-editing procedure for pointwise-pairwise consistency; it is a modest but clearly specified integration. Quantitative tables, ablations, theorem, and code/hyperparameters are provided, but statistical significance testing is absent and downstream validation is small (68 paired comparisons, no physical-robot closed-loop study).

arxiv:2608.08489.rationale: Moderate relevance through Transformer/BERT/NLP fine-tuning and robustness/adversarial settings, but not core LLM, Japanese NLP, reasoning, or agent preferences. Theoretical contribution applies known set-valued stochastic-programming consistency to S-divergence classifiers, with some novelty but limited depth. Rigor is weakened by proof sketches, an inconsistent Theta_0/v* notation, invalid beta=lambda=0 CCE recovery claim under B>0, and a stationarity proof resting on an unproven Adam descent/boundedness assumption. Empirical evidence uses public benchmarks and multiple baselines but lacks uncertainty quantification, and SDIV is not consistently best; FGSM-only adversarial evaluation limits strength.
evidence: Section 2 defines Theta_0 as g_theta(x)=p_0(x) and introduces v* = argmin_{theta in Theta_0} Psi(theta), later using v* as a scalar, creating notational/logical inconsistency.

Section 4.1 lists vision and NLP datasets and models, including fine-tuning bert-base-uncased for Emotion and PubMedQA.
Section 4.4/Figure 2 states all losses show catastrophic degradation on PathMNIST at epsilon=8/255, with no genuine FGSM resistance without adversarial training.
Section 5 acknowledges limitations: only FGSM attack, compactness/boundedness assumptions, and no formal unbounded Adam treatment.

It has no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agent, or safety relevance. Within its niche it offers a detailed mathematical framework, but the evaluation lacks baseline comparisons, quantitative posterior accuracy metrics, and code/data availability; evidence is mostly visual and surrogate R².

arxiv:2608.08487.rationale: Pure image matting/diffusion paper with no LLM or language methodology. arxiv:2608.08479.rationale: Out-of-scope SNN/neuromorphic simulator with no material match to LLM/NLP/reasoning/agents/safety or other preferred areas. Quantitative benchmarking vs NEST, Brian2, BindsNET, snnTorch is present but domain-specific; capped at 0.20.

arxiv:2608.08476.rationale: Pure camera-based 3D semantic scene completion using stereo geometry and 3D vision foundation models; no language, reasoning, agents, safety, or language-based multimodal methodology. Out of scope per rubric. Technically adequate with ablations and two benchmark datasets, but domain-limited and incremental.

arxiv:2608.08471.rationale: Highly relevant LLM safety/guardrail and multi-agent production paper with strong topical alignment to AI Safety, Agents, and Red Teaming. It reports quantitative F1 trajectories, baselines, ablations, and deployment data, but novelty is moderate over existing adaptive guardrails, and rigor/reproducibility are limited by production-specific evidence, a small set of six scenarios, lack of significance testing, and release of test sets rather than code or models.

arxiv:2608.08469.rationale: Moderately relevant as a streaming multimodal LLM (video/audio/text), touching multimodal AI, long-context memory, inference/serving, and training efficiency, but not core LLM/reasoning/agent methodology. Novelty is moderate: slot-aligned duplex generation and delta inference extend prior duplex speech and streaming VLM work. Rigor is limited by single-seed runs, no variance reporting, no systematic hyperparameter search, and a benchmark showing it trails strong baselines. Quantitative evidence exists (Tables 2-4, Figure 5-6), but some training-throughput claims are not directly shown for A100 and latency is demonstrated on one clip. Generalizability is plausible but weakly demonstrated. Reproducibility is partial: detailed hyperparameters are supplied, but data/code release and the proprietary data-generation model are not established.

arxiv:2608.08468.rationale: High topical relevance to agent security/AI safety, but research quality is limited by preliminary/under-controlled benchmarks, small per-category samples, no head-to-head baseline, inconsistent single-run vs CV metrics, and no stated code/adversarial-dataset release.

arxiv:2608.08467.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM tool use, MCP agents, instruction following, and evaluation. The study is a substantial factorial measurement across 24 LLMs and 54,000 trials, but novelty is incremental over prior tool-selection bias and instruction-compliance work. Rigor is moderate due to a single server/domain, fixed five queries, and first-call metric; evidence is strong for the narrow testbed but limited in generalizability. Reproducibility is aided by reported configurations and a data/code availability claim.
evidence: §2/Table 1 reports 54,000 trials across 24 LLMs under 9 conditions; baseline hit ratio spans 0-100% with 9 models below 15%.

§3 factorial analysis reports B and C main effects (+19.9 and +19.8 pp) with SD≈24 pp, and GPT-5.2 drops from 5% to 0% under B alone.
§4 Limitations state all evidence derives from a single server/domain, first-call efficiency only, single-turn trials, and one concrete wording per intervention.

arxiv:2608.08466.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM agents, self-improvement, reasoning on/off, and prompting/control flows. The hierarchical harness-evolution idea is moderately novel amid crowded related work, with useful ablations and held-out evaluation, but reliance on one benchmark/backbone, short evolution runs, and limited statistical testing constrain rigor and generalizability.

arxiv:2608.08463.rationale: Pure optimization theory for monotone variational inequalities; not aligned with LLM/NLP preferences except generic optimization. The paper claims novel faster rates, but has no empirical validation, relies on theoretical lemmas with some text artifacts, and lacks code/data.

arxiv:2608.08460.rationale: Out-of-scope image/video diffusion work for visual instruction generation; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent methodology. The paper has moderate empirical rigor with benchmarks and ablations, but relevance to stated preferences is minimal, so score is capped below 0.20.

arxiv:2608.08459.rationale: In-scope LLM/NLP benchmark for schema-driven document-to-database construction, with substantial relevance to LLM evaluation, long-context extraction, structured output, and relational reasoning. Novelty is moderate: the Doc2DB framing and reverse DB2Doc synthesis extend prior Doc2Table and SQUiD work, but this is largely a benchmark contribution rather than a method advance. Rigor and evidence are weakened by internal inconsistencies (e.g., Table 2 domain document counts sum to 201 while the text claims 203; several Table 3 F1 values do not match the stated P/R/F1 formula), no statistical significance testing, and authenticity claims based partly on AI detectors with limited human evaluation. Multi-domain coverage supports some generalizability, though synthetic LLM-generated provenance limits real-world transfer. Reproducibility is partially supported by a public URL, detailed prompts, and metric descriptions, but not fully verifiable from the document.

arxiv:2608.08453.rationale: Strong topical match to LLM agents, safety, and evaluation. arxiv:2608.08451.rationale: Relevant to AI safety, harmful-content NLP, and reasoning-chain regularization, with LLM backbones and LLM-assisted annotation, but not central LLM methodology. Rigor is weakened by omitted severity/binary and fine-tuned/LLM baseline results, reliance on weak linear-probe baselines, and inconsistent improvement claims (+23.3% vs Table 2 +33.2%). arxiv:2608.08449.rationale: Astrophysics study of cosmic-ray diffusion in supersonic/super-Alfvénic turbulence with MHD test-particle simulations. arxiv:2608.08430.rationale: This is a domain-specific visual analytics tool for causal graph refinement in virtual cells using single-cell transcriptomics. LLM use is peripheral (GO-term summarization), so the paper is out of core LLM/NLP/agent scope and is capped at or below 0.20. The mathematical development is thorough, with explicit assumptions, lemmas, theorems, worked instances, and acknowledged limitations, but there is no empirical validation or algorithmic implementation.

arxiv:2608.08411.rationale: Out-of-scope mathematical biology/transport modeling paper with no AI/ML methods or in-scope topical relevance. arxiv:2608.08408.rationale: Critical autoethnographic essay on AI research culture and sociotechnical harm, only tangentially related to AI safety/bias/fairness and not a technical LLM/NLP or ML methods paper. Offers a conceptual framework but lacks quantitative experiments, baselines, ablations, or empirical validation; authors explicitly limit generalizability and reproducibility is minimal.
evidence: Section 2 describes the collaborative autoethnographic method and thematic coding of 16 hours of discussion.
Section 6 presents an interpretive framework of alienation with preconditions, mechanisms, and harmful outcomes.
Section 9 acknowledges deliberate underspecification that limits interpretive validity.

arxiv:2608.08407.rationale: Pure domain application in takeover-auction/game-theory economics with no LLM/NLP/language methodology; only tangential overlap with Reinforcement Learning/MARL/PPO preferences. Despite careful epsilon-equilibrium checks and reported code release, out-of-scope cap applies.
evidence: Abstract: states the paper casts a multi-round ascending common-value takeover auction as a two-player imperfect-information game and solves for epsilon-equilibria.
Section 5, Table 1: reports two equilibrium profiles with near-identical bidder-0 value but deterrence 0.002 vs 0.333 at theta=0.05.
Section 10: acknowledges one instance, per-configuration rather than theorem, and partial grid robustness.
Section 11: states games, solvers, and experiments are released.

arxiv:2608.08406.rationale: Well-executed influence maximization study using a lightweight GNN surrogate and simulated annealing, but far outside the core LLM/NLP/agent preferences; only low-weight relevance via graph neural networks. Strong experiments and ablations for its domain, though domain-specific and lacking language methodology.
evidence: Abstract introduces SIMBA with a lightweight GNN surrogate and batched multi-swap simulated annealing.
Section 5.1 Table 1 reports influence spread across six datasets and three diffusion models with many baselines.
Section 5.2 Table 2 reports time-to-solution versus DeepIM and DeepSN.
Appendix D provides implementation details, hyperparameters, and hardware.

arxiv:2608.08402.rationale: Out-of-scope medical endoscopy application despite 'agentic' and VLM routing terminology. The VLM is used only to classify restored images and route among restoration experts, with no substantive LLM/NLP methodology or reasoning contribution. Methods and baseline comparisons are reported, but in vivo evaluation lacks paired ground truth, code/data are not available, and no formal limitations or ablations are presented. Capped at 0.20 as out-of-scope medical imaging.
evidence: Page 4: GAME uses a VLM to analyze the preliminary restored image and route the input to suitable restoration experts.
Page 8: in vivo real-world settings lack strictly paired, degradation-free ground-truth data, precluding standard quantitative evaluation with PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS.
Page 13: Code availability states 'Our source code will be available upon acceptance.'

arxiv:2608.08401.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging MRI super-resolution paper with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/alignment methodology. Some technical components and ablations are present, but evidence is limited by lack of isotropic HR T2w ground truth, a single external baseline, and no statistical significance testing.
evidence: Abstract: proposes VIPP-SR for cross-contrast super-resolution of anisotropic brain T2w MRI.
Section 4.1: evaluates on BraTS-MET and BraTS-GLI MRI cohorts.
Section 5.2: reports downstream nnU-Net segmentation Dice without significance testing.

arxiv:2608.08399.rationale: The paper is a theoretical study of multi-label F1 loss matrices and convex calibration dimension. It has only marginal relevance to the curator's LLM/NLP-focused preferences via multi-label classification and loss-function design; no LLM, agents, reasoning, or language-specific methodology. Theorems and proofs appear rigorous and novel within this niche, but generalizability beyond F1 loss is limited and no code/empirical artifacts are provided.
evidence: Theorem 4.3 and Appendix A.4 establish exact rank and affine dimension.
Theorem 5.1 and Appendix B construct a witness distribution and prove the quadratic CCdim lower bound.
Section 6 notes the remaining constant-factor gap and limited extension to F_beta/Jaccard.

arxiv:2608.08398.rationale: This is a pure domain-specific astronomy/computer vision application: uncertainty quantification for galaxy morphology classification using frozen vision foundation models. It has no LLM, Japanese NLP, reasoning, prompting, agents, or language methodology, so preference relevance is very low. The paper provides some methodological decomposition, quantitative comparisons, and ablations, but contributions are domain-specific, limited to two galaxy image datasets, and lack statistical significance testing or clear code availability. Overall out of scope for the stated preferences.
evidence: Abstract: proposes UEGMC, a post-hoc uncertainty estimation framework for Galaxy Morphology Classification using frozen foundation model backbones.
Experiments: evaluates on Galaxy10 DECaLS and GalaxyMNIST with ViT and ConvNeXt backbones.
Conclusion: states evaluation is currently restricted to galaxy image data and broader time-series spectra remain underexplored.
Qualitative Analysis and Ablation Experiments: reports lightweight estimators under 6M parameters/23 MB and over 0.5M frames per second, with an ablation on feature extraction layers.

arxiv:2608.08395.rationale: Formal economic theory of agentic commerce/search, relevant to Agents & Tool Use but not an LLM/NLP methodology or empirical study. The model is stylized and mathematically rigorous, but evidence is purely analytical with no computational or human evaluation.
evidence: Section 3 Model defines manual and agentic search with attention budgets, representation noise, and conversion mapping.
Theorem 4.4 and Theorem 5.2 state formal claims about manual-search collapse and agentic-search complexity attenuation.
Appendix A contains lemmas, theorems, and proofs supporting the main results.

arxiv:2608.08392.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM browser agents, agent evaluation, and agent-as-a-judge. The benchmark offers moderately novel cross-site complex-action/perception coverage and a verifiable rubric, but rigor is limited by mislabeling proprietary backbones as open-source agents, inconsistent evaluation-set size (198 vs 192 public), limited statistical testing, and live-web reproducibility constraints. Core low-success findings and judge validation have reasonable evidence, though some causal claims are somewhat speculative.
evidence: Section 5.2 Table 2 reports best agent success rate 8.0% and Comet partial completion 48.0%.
Section 5.1 states evaluation on 198 CAP tasks, while the footnote and Reproducibility Statement describe a 192-task public split.
Appendix I reports 96% judge-human agreement and Cohen's kappa=0.84 on 100 pass/fail verdicts.
Table 2 labels GPT-5 and Claude-4.5-Sonnet under Open Source Agents despite Section 5.1 clarifying they are Browser-Use agents driven by proprietary backbones.

arxiv:2608.08390.rationale: This is a theoretical high-dimensional statistics paper on lasso universality under dependent designs. It has no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, or safety relevance, so preference relevance is low. The formal proofs and simulations support the claims, but the domain is outside the preferred topic areas.
evidence: Section 2, Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 state the main oracle convergence and full-lasso equivalence claims under Assumptions 1-5.
Section 3.3-3.5 and Appendices A-C extend the deterministic results to random mixing matrices with concentration bounds.
Section 6 describes simulations with n=500, 50 trials, lambda=gamma, and FISTA; Figures 4-6 show overlap across latent distributions, but no code availability or quantitative error table is included.

arxiv:2608.08386.rationale: Out-of-scope visual analytics system for scientific lossy compression; no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, agent, or other weighted AI methodology. At most weak Scientific AI relevance. Claims are supported mainly by qualitative case studies rather than controlled ML evaluation, ablation, or statistical evidence.
evidence: Abstract: describes FZ-VIS as an interactive framework for human-in-the-loop feature-oriented lossy compression design and visual analytics.
Section 5 Case Study: provides qualitative compressor selection, developer analysis, topological, and spectral case studies but no formal ML evaluation.
Section 6 Limitations and Discussion: acknowledges constrained composition model, limited QoI coverage, and scalability concerns.
Supplemental Materials: claims OSF availability and MIT-licensed source code.

arxiv:2608.08383.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM safety, activation steering, and jailbreak robustness. Method is a solid incremental advance over refusal-direction ablation, with constrained optimization and broad empirical validation, though some table numbering inconsistencies and reliance on LLM judges limit full confidence.
evidence: Abstract states code URL and claims reduced steering-induced safety degradation across models and attack suites.
Section 5 lists Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B/14B-Instruct, three steering behaviors, and seven jailbreak attacks including GCG/AutoDAN/PAIR.
Section 6.1, Table 1 reports mean/worst ASR for baseline, original steering, refusal-direction ablation, and CAST.
Section 6.2, Figure 2 reports behavior score preservation ratios of 104.9% for Qwen-7B and 112.6% for Llama-8B.
Section 6.3, Table 3 reports FRR on Alpaca and XSTest, with worst-case increases around 3-4%.
Section 6.4 compares k=1,2,4,8 rank ablation and Section 6.5 ablates FRR and effect constraints.
Appendix A.2 lists training hyperparameters and Appendix A.7 provides CAST pseudocode.

arxiv:2608.08382.rationale: Relevant to LLM serving/inference infrastructure but presents an incremental piecewise-linear latency attribution model. Evaluation is limited to a token-count baseline with no ablations, statistical tests, or released code; efficiency and generality claims are only partially supported by the tables.
evidence: Abstract: claims near-perfect R2 and relative error reductions of up to 2.5x/3.3x for prefill and 3.5x/4.4x for decode versus VTC.
Table 1: reports prefill R2 and p90/p99 errors across Llama3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-14B/32B on A100/H100; LLMVisor R2 is 0.999-1.000 while VTC p99 errors reach 1.24.
Table 2: reports decode results; LLMVisor R2 stays >0.97, whereas VTC drops to R2=0.778 for Llama3.1-8B on H2.
Appendix A: describes vLLM v0.7.3 setup, hardware/tensor-parallel configurations, 128-2048 concurrent request workloads, and metrics, but no code or data release.

arxiv:2608.08381.rationale: Pure Wi-Fi sensing/human activity recognition domain application with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, RAG, agents, safety, or language methodology. It uses spherical Transformers/attention only as an incidental model component, so preference relevance is minimal and the overall score is capped at 0.20. In-domain evaluation includes quantitative comparisons and ablations, but only one small hand-gesture dataset.
evidence: Abstract: describes DoRF++ as applying spherical Transformers to Wi-Fi CSI-derived Doppler projections for human activity recognition, with no LLM/NLP/language methodology.
Section IV: UTHAMO-5G dataset uses 10 participants, 4 hand gestures, and leave-one-subject-out evaluation; Table I reports single-AP cross-user accuracy up to 80.4%.

arxiv:2608.08814.rationale: Out-of-scope embodied urban navigation benchmark: although it evaluates LMM-based agents, the core contribution is robotics/embodied simulation rather than LLM or language methodology, so relevance is minimal and score is capped. The benchmark has moderate novelty via photorealistic 360° video pose-graph navigation and seven task types, but it is limited to one district, fixed trajectories, small per-task samples, and lacks strong statistical testing. Evidence is reasonable from tables, human baselines, and sensitivity checks.
evidence: Section 3.1: environment built from 602 360° video segments over 85 streets, spanning about 750m north-south and 650m east-west around Akihabara.
Table 2 in Section 5.1: reports per-task human and model accuracies, with LMMs far below human results.
Section 3.4: fuzzy_match evaluator achieved 97.9% agreement with manual verification and threshold-sensitivity checks showed stable rankings.
Section 6: limitations include restricted exploration along captured trajectories and limited urban diversity from a single district.

arxiv:2608.08627.rationale: Out-of-scope recommendation-system compression. Though it touches MoE/compression/inference preferences, it has no LLM/NLP/language methodology and is a pure domain application, so the score is capped low. The paper is internally coherent with baselines, ablations, multi-run results, and limitations, but evaluates ranking metrics on Beauty/KuaiRec/TenRec rather than language tasks.
evidence: Abstract: reports source-relative five-run NDCG@10 ratios and A100 speedups.
Section 4.1: describes datasets, temporal split, seeds, optimization, and latency measurement.
Table 1: reports matched six-block results with NDCG@10, HR@10, AUC, params, and latency.
Table 2: ablation comparing behavior and routing-exposure signals.
Section 5: states limitations to RankMixer checkpoints, eight source experts, sampled ranking, and single-A100 inference.

arxiv:2608.08477.rationale: Relevant to LLM/multimodal/tool-use/reasoning preferences via a Spanish cybersecurity VLM, but quality is limited: it reports a negative preliminary visual-grounding result, pending remediated runs and NoPE×vision ablation, single-run evaluation, and a small unvalidated synthetic benchmark. Reproducibility is comparatively strong due released checkpoints, benchmark code, and renderer.
evidence: Section 7.3 Table 5 reports best VectraYX B6 tool-id 0.08 versus text-only control 0.02 and GPT-4o 0.940.
Section 9 states the NoPE×vision V0/V1/V2 ablation and remediated B6/B7 results remain pending and all reported numbers are single-run.
Section 6.6 claims release of GGUF exports, training checkpoints, benchmark harness, and synthetic image renderer.

arxiv:2608.08389.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, retrieval-augmented deep research, and context/efficiency management. However, novelty mainly integrates known pruning heuristics (MMR, DPP, submodular coverage) into a stage-comparison study. Rigor is limited by LLM-judge sensitivity, lack of significance testing, and inconsistencies such as two-stage Centroid Drift token/runtime values differing between Table 2 and Appendix Table 5. Evidence supports broad efficiency findings but quality conclusions are judge-dependent and not fully stable across benchmarks.
evidence: Section 6.4 reports a fixed rubric-based LLM judge; Appendix Table 4 shows substantial judge sensitivity.
Section 9 Limitations acknowledges judge-dependent quality scores and unstable method-level quality rankings across benchmarks.
Table 2 lists two-stage Centroid Drift at 138.2k tokens/1619.8s, while Appendix Table 5 reports 118.1k/1142.43s, indicating reporting inconsistency.

arxiv:2608.08374.rationale: Pure computational pathology/medical imaging with no LLM or language methodology; only incidental transformer-attention match makes it largely out of scope. arxiv:2608.08368.rationale: Medical imaging DR grading application with graph attention and interpretability, but no language methodology or LLM/NLP core; domain application is out of scope and capped at 0.20. arxiv:2608.08363.rationale: Out-of-scope power electronics prognostics/condition-monitoring paper. arxiv:2608.08361.rationale: Weakly relevant to the Code & Programming/GitHub software-engineering preference, but not an AI/ML or LLM paper. arxiv:2608.08359.rationale: Methodologically careful ordinal regression paper with formal unimodality analysis and broad experiments, but essentially no overlap with requested LLM/NLP/agent/multimodal/safety preferences; relevance is minimal, and generality is limited to ordinal classification.
evidence: Abstract states the proposed UPRL regularizer promotes predicted CPD to be unimodal and avoids scale-related bias.

arxiv:2608.08356.rationale: Pure robotics/underwater vehicle dynamics application with no LLM, NLP, language, or reasoning methodology. It has some tangential matches to Robotics & Embodied AI and Scientific AI, but falls under the explicit out-of-scope cap. In-domain work shows moderate novelty in geometric SPINNs and hardware evaluation, but evidence is limited to small field trials and domain-specific baselines; overall score capped near 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: describes stochastic physics-informed neural networks on Lie groups for underwater vehicle dynamics, indicating pure robotics domain focus.
Section V-A: reports simulation comparison against geometric PINN and Euclidean SPINN with chordal/geodesic FDM achieving best distribution matching.
Section V-B: reports hardware success rates 18/20 for geodesic FDM, 17/20 for chordal FDM, and 13/20 for geometric PINN.
Section V: states code will be made publicly available upon paper acceptance, but no current artifact link was supplied.

arxiv:2608.08355.rationale: Out of scope: nonparametric Bayesian quantile inference with Dirichlet processes; no LLM, Japanese NLP, reasoning, agents, vision, audio, or other preferred methodology. The paper is mathematically rigorous within its statistics domain, but it does not address curator preferences and is capped at 0.20.

Section 3: provides explicit Bayes estimator Q̂_0(y) as a Bernstein-type weighted sum of order statistics.
Section 7: presents large-sample Bernstein-von Mises theorems for quantile processes.

arxiv:2608.08354.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application: tropical cyclone weather forecasting with latent rectified flow and VAE, with no LLM/NLP/language methodology. The paper has quantitative results, ablations, and limitations, but is capped at <=0.20 as a pure domain application.
evidence: Abstract reports 16.35 dB PSNR and 0.759 SSIM overall
Section 4.5 Table 3 reports +9h track error 62.4 km
Section 4.7 reports sampler-budget sweep and ~30x faster sampling versus baseline
Section 4.9 reports ablations for temporal attention and multi-frame conditioning

arxiv:2608.08352.rationale: Relevant LLM/code-focused program reduction paper using prompt design and syntax-guided reduction. Moderate novelty in hybrid LLM+Perses workflow with long-tail detection and mutation strategies, though LPR already explores LLM-aided reduction. Rigor is limited by a 23-benchmark miscompilation-only scope, no significance testing or explicit limitations, and claims of broader applicability are unsupported. Evidence is quantitative but lacks dispersion and detailed per-benchmark tables in main text.
evidence: §5.2.1 reports 1.75x geometric-mean speedup over the better of Perses and LPR with max 2.55x
§5.2.2 reports all outputs under 60 LoC and no single reducer consistently smallest; largest gap on gcc116906 is 260 vs 115 tokens
§5.3 describes four ablation variants and reports size/time contributions of mutator, reducer, Perses, and prompt design
§4.1.1 defines long-tail detection using token threshold and score conditions

arxiv:2608.08350.rationale: Mathematically detailed deep-learning theory paper on critical initialization, correlation flow, Jacobian spectra, and NTK in fully connected networks. It falls broadly under training/optimization but is outside the curator's core LLM/NLP/agent interests. The derivations are substantial and supported by synthetic numerical experiments, but scope is limited to specific activations/architectures and no code or data release is indicated.
evidence: Abstract: claims a direct link between correlation propagation and the Neural Tangent Kernel at criticality.
Sec. VI.2: derives the asymptotic NTK block moment m^{(1)}_{Theta_infinity}^{alpha beta} = rho_infinity^{alpha beta}/(A sigma_w^2).
Sec. V.3: derives spectral standard deviation scalings for Gaussian vs orthogonal initialization in the end-to-end Jacobian.
Sec. IV.4: reports numerical correlation-flow experiments on sine networks, including Fig. 5.
Sec. VI.3 and Fig. 7: provide empirical confirmation of NTK block spectral predictions.

arxiv:2608.08349.rationale: Primarily an audio/HCI domain application (audio drama production) rather than AI/ML research. LLM is used as a component for object extraction/script generation, but the paper does not advance language-model methodology and falls under out-of-scope pure audio/domain application; score capped near 0.20.
evidence: §4.4 uses Gemini 3 Pro for all LLM calls and proprietary text-to-SFX/music models; system-level contribution, not a model or method advance.
§5.1.3 acknowledges ordering confound, self-reported times, and N=8 generalizability limits.
§5.3 listener evaluation provides N=300 ratings but is domain-specific to audio drama quality.
No code, data, or model availability statement is present in the document.

arxiv:2608.08344.rationale: Relevant LLM reasoning/prompt-ordering study with exact 720-order enumeration and a recorded pre-flight protocol. Quality is limited by the supplied text showing a single model and a small GSM8K subset, with several transfer/cross-domain claims only alluded to without detailed evidence; reproducibility is aided by caching, deterministic decoding, and a code link but missing full prompt/grader specifics.
evidence: Abstract: reports 6.3%-96.9% accuracy across all 720 orderings of six fixed reasoning instructions on a GSM8K subset.
Section 6: reports exact FDC=-0.063 and near-zero one-move autocorrelation, with elitist search hitting an optimum in 19/40 runs versus 30/40 for uniform sampling.
Section 7: states accuracy range 0.063-0.969, mean 0.717, and SD 0.230 with deterministic decoding.

arxiv:2608.08341.rationale: Out-of-scope pure domain application of differential privacy to Markov chain state trajectories; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/multimodal/vision/audio methodology. The theoretical work is somewhat novel in its niche and has formal proofs, but empirical support is simulation-only without code release, and generalizability outside finite Markov chains is limited.
evidence: Abstract and Section 1 frame the paper exclusively around differential privacy for Markov chain state trajectories, with no relevant LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent topic.
Section 5 reports comparisons to Chen et al. on credit migration, Gainesville traffic, and Wikispeedia using 10,000 Monte Carlo trajectories.
Appendix E contains formal proofs for the stated theorems, though not all notation is cleanly consistent.
Appendix F gives data preprocessing and simulation details but does not state code/data availability.

arxiv:2608.08340.rationale: Relevant systems paper on GPU-backed multi-stage RAG/agentic LLM orchestration, with clear in-scope topics. It reports quantitative speedups and includes multiple baselines, but rigor is limited by no error bars, no ablations isolating individual optimizations, a small two-A100 GPU setup, and no code/artifact availability. The operator-runtime idea is incremental but applied in a coherent RAG setting.
evidence: Section 5.3 reports OpRAG total 131.048s vs HigressRAG 156.309s for Llama3-8B and 132.525s vs 157.137s for Mistral-7B.
Section 5.5 reports Recall@5 = 1.000 for hybrid retrieval and generation-scenario latency reductions.
Section 7.1 states plans to add repeated runs and confidence intervals, indicating current results lack statistical variance reporting.
No code or artifact availability statement is present in the paper.

arxiv:2608.08338.rationale: Domain-specific edge inference/radio-GPU scheduling paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology; only tangential Inference & Serving similarity, so capped as out-of-scope. Simulation evidence is statistically careful but not generalizable to language model research.
evidence: Abstract: scheduler targets progressive edge inference over radio and GPU stages, not language models.
Section IV-C: reports frozen 30-seed paired evaluation with 4.27% timely-completion gain and bootstrap interval.
Table II: lists main system and scheduler parameters, supporting reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.08336.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/vision-transformer adaptation paper; no substantive LLM, NLP, language-model, agent, or language-methodology contribution. Despite moderate engineering quality, the topic relevance is minimal and the overall score is capped at 0.20 per out-of-scope policy.
evidence: Sec. 4.2, Table 6: CFT reports 72.4 mean VTAB-1k top-1 at 20.4 epochs and 1,351 TFLOPs, versus 44-96 epochs for PEFT baselines.

arxiv:2608.08333.rationale: Out-of-scope HCI/IS conceptual paper on selecting technology acceptance models (TAM/UTAUT). It does not use LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, agent, or other preference methods; LLM/AI are only mentioned in future work and a generative-AI statement. The framework is illustrative, with no empirical validation and no quantitative results, so overall score is capped at 0.20.

arxiv:2608.08330.rationale: The paper is a pure edge-computing/cooperative-perception system focused on GPU scheduling and wireless-completion-triggered DNN execution. It has no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, prompting, RAG, safety, or language methodology, and falls under out-of-scope computer vision/robotics applications; per rubric it is capped at 0.20. evidence: Abstract: centralized multi-agent cooperative perception and GPU execution

Section V-B: physical GPU paired latency comparisons

arxiv:2608.08326.rationale: Relevant to multimodal reasoning, RLHF/GRPO, and structured process rewards; moderate novelty via lightweight reference-conditioned reward alignment and rollout recycling. Rigor is limited by single-checkpoint reporting, no confidence intervals/multi-seed, and only 4B ablations. Quantitative tables show consistent gains but evidence is observational.

arxiv:2608.08323.rationale: Out-of-scope pure robotics/social-navigation MPPI paper; no LLM/NLP/language, transformer, reasoning, or agent methodology. The anisotropic Gaussian cost is an incremental modification. Evaluation is simulation-only with a single vanilla MPPI baseline, no statistical variance or relevant predictive baselines.
