arxiv:2608.08322.rationale: Physics-informed neural network for level-set advection is outside LLM/NLP/agent scope; only weak Scientific AI/Training overlap. Domain study is reasonably rigorous (pre-registered weight sweep, multi-seed, WENO comparison) but incremental and narrow; selected run (Table 8/9) uses seed 42, not seed-averaged. Overall capped as out-of-scope.
evidence: Section 4.1 defines a six-weight, three-seed sweep and pre-registered selection rule.
Section 4.2/Tables 2-5 report per-weight means and standard deviations.
Section 4.7/Table 8 reports the selected-weight run for seed 42.
Section 5/Table 9 compares against WENO5 + TVD-RK3.
Code and Data Availability claims source code at Zenodo.

arxiv:2608.08321.rationale: Out-of-scope pure geospatial hazard susceptibility/risk mapping using Random Forest, GIS, and SHAP. It has no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent methods; only tangential relevance via interpretability (SHAP), feature engineering, and data curation. Domain application cap restricts final score despite reasonable documentation, metrics, and code availability.
evidence: Abstract: framework for flood-landslide susceptibility/risk mapping using Random Forest and environmental conditioning factors, not LLM/NLP methods.
Section 4.6: SHAP analysis is used for model interpretation of susceptibility models.
Section 4.4: predictor screening via Pearson correlation and VIF; Sections 3.1-3.5 describe hazard inventories, conditioning factors, and exposure/vulnerability datasets.
Section 1: codebase available at https://github.com/GVCL/Susceptibility-Mapping-FL-Hetero.

arxiv:2608.08320.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application of LLMs to social human-robot interaction; no LLM/NLP methodology. Study compares Qwen3-VL 4B/8B/30B in brief HRI, but small N=19, acknowledged confounds, limited statistical testing, and no data/code availability. Capped at 0.20 for pure robotics/domain application without language methodology.
evidence: Abstract: 19 participants interacted with robot faces driven by Qwen3-VL models at 4B, 8B, and 30B parameters; reports no significant overall preference for 30B.
Section III: within-subjects design, two-minute open-ended interactions, distinct face colors as potential visual confound, and backend-only timing test.
Section IV: reports exploratory correlations only, e.g., AI interaction frequency vs 30B intelligence r(18)=-.621, p=.005; humor vs enjoyment r(18)=.539, p=.017.
Section IV-C: acknowledges limitations including color-to-model mapping confound and backend rather than end-to-end latency measurement.

arxiv:2608.08319.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging and image/video diffusion work with no language/LLM methodology; transformer architecture appears only as a vision backbone. The GBP continual-learning component has some novelty and the paper provides extensive experiments, but evidence is limited by overlapping confidence intervals, a single domain order, small postoperative n=49, and exploratory single-subject attribution maps. Code/weights are only promised, and clinical generalizability is limited.
evidence: Abstract: reports a brain MRI foundation model pretrained on >425,000 volumes with Graph-Blueprint Pruning and sequential clinical-domain expansion.
Methods: Model architecture describes 3D-SWIN Swin Transformer encoder-decoder and 3D-DiT latent diffusion transformer, with no LLM/language component.
Discussion: acknowledges a single domain sequence, retrospective clinical analyses, and a postoperative evaluation with only 49 participants.
Code availability: states code and model weights will be released upon publication, not currently available.

arxiv:2608.08317.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/neuromorphic SNN paper without language methodology; only incidental mentions of LLMs, edge environments, and MoE. Quality is moderate but quantitative inconsistencies (e.g., CIFAR-10 claimed as ~66% in Abstract vs 82.7-83.3% in Table 3) and limited benchmark scope keep the score capped below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: claims CIFAR-10 performance at ~66%.
Table 3: reports CIFAR-10 accuracies of 82.7% and 83.3% for D-SNN variants, contradicting the Abstract.
Section 4.8: states all reported accuracies are derived from SNN simulations only.
Data and Code Availability: provides a GitHub link for the code.

arxiv:2608.08315.rationale: Moderately relevant multimodal VLM/prompting study on temporal video grounding, with controlled interface comparisons and broad benchmark/backbone coverage. Novelty is reasonable but the method is a simple binary-VQA scan. Rigor is weakened by an internal inconsistency: Sec 3.3 specifies F=5 frames per probe while Sec 4.1 uses F=3, and Sec 5.6 reports a large +5.7 pp R@0.5 gain from F=3 to F=5 yet the main results still report 56.8. Evidence is otherwise extensive with paired tests, but selective/default reporting undermines confidence.
evidence: Sec 3.3 specifies F=5 frames per probe, but Sec 4.1 says F=3; Sec 5.6 reports a +5.7 pp R@0.5 improvement from F=3 to F=5 while the abstract and Table 3 report 56.8, indicating inconsistent default configuration reporting.
Table 6 provides controlled same-backbone interface comparison with +28 to +50 pp R@0.5 across four frozen backbones.
Sec 5.6 and Table 12 report paired McNemar p-values for frame-per-probe and resolution ablations, supporting statistical testing but also exposing the unrectified default configuration.

arxiv:2608.08311.rationale: Strong match to LLM agents, coding, safety, and evaluation preferences. Benchmark results and audit disclosures are detailed, but headline benchmarks use evolution off (Table 3), so the central self-development claim relies mainly on observational Hope deployment data and two fixes rather than controlled ablations.
evidence: Section 5 reports audited Terminal-Bench 2.1 86.74%, OSWorld-Verified 90.69%, CL-Bench 0.2301, and SWE-bench Pro McNemar p=0.40.
Table 3 discloses that evolution was off for all benchmark rows, weakening direct evidence for core evolution.
Section 4 gives Hope deployment counters and two experience-driven fixes as observational evidence.
Limitations acknowledges one lineage, SWE-bench Pro leakage, and LLM reviewer blind spots.

arxiv:2608.08309.rationale: Pure computer vision self-supervised representation learning with no LLM/NLP/language methodology; out-of-scope per rubric and capped accordingly. The work has some formalization and controlled ablations on ViT-Tiny/STL-10, but evidence is small-scale and not benchmark-level, limiting broad relevance to the target preferences.
evidence: Abstract and Section 1 frame the task as self-supervised visual representation learning, not language modeling or NLP.
Section 6 reports ViT-Tiny pretraining on STL-10 with linear-probe and patch-retrieval evaluations.
Appendix 0.E provides detailed hyperparameters, supporting reproducibility claims.

arxiv:2608.08308.rationale: Pure computer-vision semantic segmentation paper; no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, or language methodology. Out of scope under rubric and capped at 0.20.
evidence: {'section': 'Abstract', 'note': 'Focus is open-world semantic segmentation and anomaly detection, not language or agent methods.'}
{'section': 'Section 3', 'note': 'Method is a three-decoder encoder-decoder segmentation architecture with no language model components.'}

arxiv:2608.08307.rationale: Medical VQA is a medical imaging domain application and is out of scope under the rubric, so relevance is capped low despite multimodal/vision-language components. The method adapts existing frequency-domain fusion (FSRU) to medical VQA and reports an ablation, but the paper underperforms all listed baselines and has questionable implementation/reliability details.
evidence: Abstract and Introduction frame the work as Medical Visual Question Answering over radiological images, a medical imaging domain application.
Results and Analysis Table 1 reports Ours as 40.21 EM on VQA-RAD and 69.21 EM on SLAKE, below M3AE (77.0/83.2), MUMC (79.2/84.9), and other baselines.
Implementation Details claims experiments were run on a 'Google Colab G4 GPU (NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition)', which undermines reproducibility.
Results and Analysis reports Token F1 of 44.01 on VQA-RAD with Closed 56.4, appearing inconsistent with the Closed EM of 56.4 in Table 1.

arxiv:2608.08303.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, AI safety, red-teaming, and prompting/ICL. The paper presents a query-only backdoor attack with a clear threat model, multiple interaction-only baselines, component ablations, and evaluations across benchmarks, evolution systems, and backbones. Rigor is limited by self-reported seed averages without variance/statistical testing, missing skill-scanner results, and no limitations section. Reproducibility is supported by appendix prompts, budgets, seeds, and code availability claims.
evidence: Section 4.1 describes benchmarks, evolution systems, backbones, and metrics
Table 1 reports backbone generalization for TBA
Table 2 and Section 4.2 compare TBA with benign evolution and interaction-only baselines
Section 4.3 reports component ablation and robustness results
Appendix Sec. 5 gives reproducibility details including seeds and parameters

arxiv:2608.08301.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application using standard Random Forest classification on passive ultrasonic railway wheel defect data; no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent methodology. Within its domain, the work has moderate rigor (stratified CV, statistical feature ranking, quantitative metrics) but lacks baseline model comparisons, independent test validation, and code/data availability, and uses a small dataset, limiting generalizability.
evidence: ABSTRACT: Random Forest classifier trained on the top features achieved a balanced accuracy of about 0.66 and a Macro-F1 score of 0.65 across all nine classes.
Random Forest Classification: A Random Forest classifier with 500 trees was trained using stratified 5-fold cross-validation on the selected feature set.
EXPERIMENTAL SETUP: Data was collected from a library of eleven full-scale railway wheelsets provided by MxV Rail.

arxiv:2608.08300.rationale: Relevant LLM memory-safety and prompting study with multi-model comparisons and public code; however, it uses a single English benchmark, reports only modest leakage reductions without significance testing, and sycophancy remains unresolved, limiting generalizability and evidential strength.
evidence: Abstract: 'Across seven models on PersistBench... structured formats... consistently reduces cross-domain leakage... strongest method reducing leakage by 8.8% on average relative to the baseline.'
Section 3.2: 'Dynamic partitioning... reduces cross-domain leakage for all models, with an average of 8.8% and a standard deviation of 4.6%.'
Section 5 Limitations: 'experiments are limited to PersistBench... memory-induced sycophancy remains near the ceiling.'

arxiv:2608.08296.rationale: Out-of-scope pure theoretical parallel graph algorithms for MIS and coloring; no AI/ML/NLP relevance. Includes formal lemmas and complexity bounds but lacks empirical baselines, ablations, or code artifacts, so capped at low score.
evidence: Abstract: claims deterministic MIS and coloring in O(n+m) work and polylog depth.
Section 4, Theorem 4.2: ordered k-sparse partition construction with linear work.
Section 5, Theorem 5.1: bootstrapping scheme for extendable graph problems.

arxiv:2608.08294.rationale: Pure computer vision knowledge distillation study on CIFAR-100 with no LLM, language, reasoning, agent, or multimodal language methodology; explicitly out of scope under the stated policy. The paper has reasonably controlled paired comparisons, seed replications, and ablations, but its domain relevance is very low, limiting the overall score to at most 0.20.
evidence: Section 3.2 reports seed-42 test top-1 accuracy for scratch, logit KD, AT, and FitNets on CIFAR-100.
Section 3.3 reports AT effect versus parameter count with r=0.31, p=0.27, finding no clear capacity trend.
Section 3.6 reports FitNets below paired logit KD in all 15 paired runs.

arxiv:2608.08293.rationale: Pure autonomous-vehicle lateral control/robotics paper with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/vision-language methodology; out of scope per rubric. Domain work is simulation-only, with incremental controller enhancements and quantitative tracking errors but limited baselines, ablations, or code/data.
evidence: Section 2.2 describes clothoid lookahead enhancements (tangential check, segment classification, dual-adaptive rate control).
Section 2.3 describes lookup-table curvature control for tracking points in articulated vehicles.
Section 3.1 reports RMS cross-track errors on Shasta Lake for tractor-trailer and standalone tractor.
Section 3.2 reports RMS cross-track errors on Cabbage Hill for both configurations; no real-world testing or baseline comparison is included.

arxiv:2608.08290.rationale: Pure computer-vision open-vocabulary semantic segmentation with CLIP/DINO prototypes; no LLM, Japanese NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, or language-model methodology, so out of scope and capped low. Within CV it shows host generality and ablations, but lacks language relevance, statistical significance testing, and clear code/availability evidence.
evidence: §4.2 and Table 1 report mIoU gains across five OVSS hosts
§4.4 Tables 3-5 report component, threshold, and bank extractor ablations
§4.6 and Table 7 describe bank-size saturation, label-overlap robustness, and computational overhead

arxiv:2608.08288.rationale: Out-of-scope healthcare causal inference time-series paper with no language/LLM methodology; only tangential SSM/Mamba and medical AI preference matches, so capped at <=0.20. The paper has some architectural and theoretical novelty, but rigor is limited by informal proofs, internal inconsistencies, no significance testing, and single-site/single-outcome evaluation.
evidence: Section 5 Experiments, Table 1: CSSPD outperforms CT at gamma 0-3 but degrades to 2.270 at gamma=4.
Section 5 Experiments, Table S2/S3: per-step RMSE and ablation show CSSPD leads at tau>=2 but trails CT at tau=1.
Section 6 Discussion, Limitations: evaluation limited to a single MIMIC-III site and diastolic blood pressure; no formal significance tests reported.

arxiv:2608.08287.rationale: Out of scope for the stated AI/LLM research preferences: this is a GPU programming-language performance study of CUDA C++, Rust, and Triton on an irregular hash-blocked TSDF fusion kernel, with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/safety methodology. The only LLM mention is an AI-assistance disclosure, not the research subject. Methodological quality is nontrivial but capped at low overall relevance.
evidence: Section 1: implements the same hash-blocked TSDF fusion kernel in CUDA C++, Rust through cuda-oxide, and Triton
Section 5: reports stage-level ratios such as Rust/CUDA and Triton/CUDA across regular update and irregular allocate stages

arxiv:2608.08286.rationale: Pure-audio speech codec/tokenization research with only an autoregressive LM probe and downstream TTS evaluation; it lacks core LLM/NLP language methodology and is out-of-scope per rubric, capping the score at 0.20. The controlled diagnostic and ablations are reasonable, but generalizability is limited to English LibriSpeech and code is only promised upon acceptance.
evidence: Table 1 reports Spearman correlation of KNN phoneme accuracy with P-ACC 0.911 [0.76, 0.98] and P-PPL -0.901 across 24 representations.
Table 2 reports ReLMCodec@64K WER 3.96, SIM 0.804, and PESQ 2.40 versus X-Codec2 5.53/0.801/2.13, leading evaluated codec rows.
Table 4 module ablation shows C3 (PAPA+JMAS) P-ACC 9.63 and WER 4.16; SSL-only A0 has P-ACC 12.45 but worse WER/SIM/PESQ.
Limitations states the study is limited to observational 50-Hz English LibriSpeech and that multilingual, noisy, and other-rate settings remain future work.
Appendix E states code release upon acceptance and provides a detailed benchmark protocol.

arxiv:2608.08285.rationale: Out-of-scope as a pure egocentric/embodied capture hardware and dataset paper; it mentions VLA models and language captions but has no LLM/NLP or language methodology core. Technical sensor validation and open-source claims are present, but downstream policy/language value is explicitly not demonstrated and the deployment is geographically limited.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports residual visual-inertial drift of 700 µs and per-camera reprojection error below 0.03 px.
Section 4.4 reports 96% usable-session rate across 1,462 sessions, 550 hours per camera, 25 contributors, and 40+ environments.
Section 6 states no policy training demonstration and no ATE/RPE ground-truth evaluation for pose.

arxiv:2608.08284.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM fairness, interpretability, and evaluation; not a pure domain application despite the recommender setting. Novelty is moderate: it combines output-only fairness benchmarking with representation probing and adds a joint diagnostic/quadrant view, but is incremental over existing FaiRLLM and representation-engineering work. Rigor is moderate: multiple robustness and ablation studies are included, but some intervention results are estimated, model versions are not consistently specified, and statistical testing is limited. Evidence strength is moderate: quantitative tables support the main hidden-output decoupling claim, though many IBS effects are very small and quadrant conclusions depend on thresholding choices. Generalizability is moderate across six open-weight model families, three domains, and three protected attributes. Reproducibility is moderate: data/code are promised and datasets are public, but ambiguous model identifiers weaken exact reproduction.
evidence: Section 5.1 Table 3 reports ROA averages of 0.224 for MovieLens/Race and 0.055 for Goodreads/Race, with several near-zero or negative model-level ROA values.
Section 5.4 reports that for Qwen3-32B MovieLens/Gender, IBS falls from 1.08e-3 to 1.36e-4 while OBS rises from 0.359 to 0.764 under activation steering.
Appendix C.4 reports that under a stricter (75,75) percentile partition, Q4 hidden-internal mismatch remains 18.40% of users.

arxiv:2608.08283.rationale: Relevant NLP/MT evaluation study using LLM translation and LLM-as-judge metrics, but not Japanese-specific or a core LLM methods contribution. The work is an empirical diagnostic benchmark rather than a new model/method. It has solid mixed-effects analysis and released data/code, though synthetic perturbations, moderately low annotator agreement in some categories, and a domain-specific setting limit generalizability and evidence strength.
evidence: Abstract: investigates whether existing automatic evaluation metrics developed for modern languages are reliable for Classical Chinese to English translation.
Section 3.2: defines eight expert-grounded error categories and three acceptable-variation categories.
Table 2: reports LME estimates of metric sensitivity across error and acceptable-variation types with significance tests.
Section 5.1: states MetricX24 is most sensitive overall but has blind spots, and no metric reliably detects tense or title/rank substitution errors.
Appendix B: documents metric implementations and model cards used in evaluation.

arxiv:2608.08282.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents and constrained decoding. Rigorous formal treatment with honest negative matched-comparison results, but evidence is limited to bounded/enumerable workflows and the method's scalability boundary is explicit.
evidence: §6.2 reports analytic TV 1.5e-16 for the frozen-bank proposal on an enumerable 60-trajectory support.
§6.3 reports 299 policy invocations per accepted sample versus 2.5e4 for rejection sampling, but also 1365 versus 392 distinct forward passes, showing the residual recursion cost.
Appendix N.1 Table 18 reports matched observation-keyed root-prefix CARS versus Stateful CARS sampler-step ratio 0.942 [0.934,0.951], favoring the baseline.
§8 Limitations states exactness is verified only on enumerable workflows and no verified exactness is claimed on free-form tasks.

arxiv:2608.08281.rationale: Pure domain application of LLMs to maritime navigation with no new language-model methodology; relevance capped accordingly. Small real-world AIS dataset (n=50), class imbalance, limited validation, and partial quantitative evidence.
evidence: Section 3: dataset constructed from 50 AIS scenarios in Danish waters.
Section 5: evaluates GPT-5-mini, GPT-4o, Mistral 7B, Phi 4 Mini, and Gemma 3 1B.
Section 7: concludes off-the-shelf LLMs are not suitable without fine-tuning.

arxiv:2608.08277.rationale: Moderately relevant as an LLM-agent action-assurance benchmark with tool use and safety/evaluation components, but domain-specific to wireless network operations. The action-assurance framing is a modest combination of existing evidence-graph, provenance, critique/repair, and guardrail ideas. The evaluation protocol is detailed with baselines, ablations, and multiple backbones; however, reference labels and verification both derive from the same benchmark spec, a conflict/provenance slice is confounded, and near-ceiling gains rely on the authors' own benchmark. Generalizability beyond wireless operations is limited, and reproducibility is only partially supported by an anonymous benchmark link and metric definitions.
evidence: Section III-C defines the ordered reference policy and the 600-episode selection from 7,680 candidates.
Table III in Section V-C reports Exact Action Accuracy, Safe APPLY Recall, and Unsafe APPLY Rate across three backbones.
Table VI in Section V-E reports ablations showing drops when the integrity monitor, action governor, or utility repair are removed.
Section VI states limitations, including that the benchmark is a controlled setting rather than a live network deployment study.

arxiv:2608.08274.rationale: Qualitative study of visualization design practice; outside LLM/NLP/agent/AI methodology preferences. It mentions AI-assisted tools only as implications, not studied. Rigor is limited by reflexive thematic analysis, 11 expert participants, no inter-coder reliability, and retrospective accounts; evidence is illustrative episode analysis rather than quantitative verification.
evidence: Section 2.5: reflexive thematic analysis; no inter-coder reliability computed
Section 4.5: small corpus of eleven practitioners; retrospective material; no novice comparison
Section 3.2.1: illustrative episode analysis of John and Omar
Section 3.1: no quantitative results; unresolved situations described qualitatively

arxiv:2608.08273.rationale: Embodied-control/robotics domain application using a frozen VLM as trajectory evaluator. It is outside core LLM/NLP methodology and mostly in pure robotics/embodied AI; only tangential multimodal prompting relevance. Experimental rigor is moderate with baselines/ablations but lacks a direct one-stage VLM baseline and is simulation-only.
evidence: Section 5.1: Uses Gemini 1.5 Pro as primary VLM evaluator in ALFRED/AI2-THOR simulated household environments.
Section 5.2: Compares against CLIP, R3M, RoboCLIP, and Ground-Truth Oracle in an IQL pipeline.
Section 6.5: Ablation shows action logs and temporal annotations improve assessment accuracy/F1.
Section 7.1: Limitations include no direct one-stage VLM success-judgment baseline, no prompt-paraphrase/repeated-query evaluation, and simulation-only robustness.

arxiv:2608.08270.rationale: Out-of-scope HCI/data-visualization design theory paper. It is not LLM/NLP methodology and only treats AI-assisted design and LLM-based support as discussion implications, not as the research contribution. The paper is conceptual with no quantitative results, baselines, or ablations; evidence is primarily citation-based synthesis of design theory. Low relevance to the stated AI/ML curation preferences and weak empirical validation warrant a low score.
evidence: Abstract: frames the contribution as mapping design knowledge in data visualization through design theory.
Section 1.3: discusses AI/LLM-based design support only as part of the stakes of formalizing design knowledge, not as a method.
Section 2.1-2.4: presents a conceptual landscape with no empirical or quantitative evaluation.
Section 4.3: offers implications for AI-assisted design but no model experiments or technical validation.

arxiv:2608.08268.rationale: The paper is a formal multi-agent RL/game-theory study of radically uncoupled learning in LQ stochastic games, with no LLM/NLP/safety focus. It shows solid theoretical contributions (Theorem 1 convergence rates) and numerical Cournot experiments, but relevance is limited to broad RL/multi-agent topics; evidence is self-reported and no code/data availability is specified.
evidence: Abstract: claims first convergence guarantee for radically uncoupled learning in LQ stochastic games
Section 4: Theorem 1 states high-probability and almost-sure convergence rates
Section 5.1: numerical experiments report estimated decay exponents near theoretical 0.25
Appendix A: provides proof details and auxiliary lemmas

arxiv:2608.08266.rationale: Relevant LLM/code/interpretability study, but primarily an incremental robustness analysis of prior code-correctness probing. Rigorous setup with cross-validation, ANOVA, and controlled mutation data, though many results are noisy and near chance. Limited to 7-8B models and Python benchmarks.
evidence: Abstract and Section I state the paper studies robustness of LLM internal representations of code correctness across extraction methods, prompt framings, hidden-state locations, models, and benchmarks.
Section IV and Tables II/III provide a large configuration sweep and ANOVA, supporting the finding that no single configuration is best and mean-diff generally beats PCA.
Section V and Table V show controlled mutation pairs are separable in isolation but transfer poorly, especially on BigCodeBench (19.6% vs 56.7% in-distribution).
Section VII discusses threats including unit-test correctness proxy, mutation realism, and limited model/language coverage.

arxiv:2608.08265.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM evaluation/routing and inference deployment, with formal selection-valid diagnostics. The theoretical contribution is incremental over known oracle-gap comparisons but adds rigorous finite-sample post-selection intervals and a submodular pool guarantee. Empirical evidence from Tables 1-3 supports the claimed routing plateau and recovered fraction, though benchmark sizes are moderate and intervals wide. Reproducibility is strong with detailed design, model revisions, splits, prompts, and artifact protocols.
evidence: Table 1 reports selection-valid 95% intervals with positive lower limits on ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, GSM8K, and MMLU.
Table 2 reports simultaneous best-family gain intervals with lower limit exactly zero and positive residual opportunity intervals.
Table 3 reports best deployable router recovered fractions of 7.5-14.4% of the certified oracle opportunity.
Appendix D details predeclared confirmatory design, datasets, model revisions, splits, and scoring protocols.

arxiv:2608.08264.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, and AI safety, with a moderately novel workflow-level operational skill unlearning formulation. However, evidence is limited by exact 1.0/0.0 aggregate results, limited raw case-level evidence, no variability metrics, and no reported code/data release. Baselines and frozen defenses are described but not independently verifiable; evaluation is controlled and simulated, limiting generalizability.
evidence: Section VI-A defines the locked benchmark with 160 cases (88 attack, 8 benign near-miss, 64 utility) and a separate 40-case skill-attack-derived sandbox.
Table I in Section VII-A reports no-defense ASR 1.000 and OBLIVION ASR 0.114 with IWE 0.115, utility 1.000, and benign block 0.000.
Section IV-B describes Cross-Surface Coherent Erasure across six surfaces; Section IV-C describes frozen workflow remediation and guarded dispatch.
Section VII-D acknowledges 10 successful attacks remain under OBLIVION remediation.

arxiv:2608.08263.rationale: Pure wearable robotics/underwater sensing application using MMG and MiniRocket; no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, or language methodology. Some quantitative validation but small sample and preliminary, limited ML novelty and generalizability.
evidence: Abstract: reports MiniRocket classifier achieved 91.91% window-level and 97.56% file-level accuracy.
Section IV-D: controlled underwater validation repeated five times with CO2 release and airbag inflation within approximately 5 seconds.
Section IV-A: file-level split prevents leakage and temporal voting used for trial-level classification.

arxiv:2608.08256.rationale: Arabic MLM/SSM encoder is relevant to NLP and Mamba/SSM preferences but not Japanese/LLM/agent focus; methodology is detailed with multi-seed evaluation and ablations, but comparisons rely on unmatched published baselines and no matched-compute baseline, weakening evidence.
evidence: Section 4.2 Table 4 states the HARD split is a fixed seeded 80/10/10 split and results are informally, not strictly, comparable to AraBERT.
Section 4.7 Table 8 notes the ANERcorp and ARCD deltas combine MLM pretraining and task-adjacent prefinetuning, not isolating MLM alone.
Section 4.8 reports AraSSM trails the base-sized Transformer range by roughly 2-3 points on XNLI-ar and discusses dataset label/translation caveats.
Data and Code Availability provides a Hugging Face checkpoint link but does not describe shared code or data pipeline.

arxiv:2608.08255.rationale: Strong topical fit for LLM agents and RL credit assignment. EFCA adds environment-grounded short-term feedback and medium-term state-history credits via return reweighting, but the method is relatively incremental pattern matching and evaluation rigor is limited: many baseline results are reused, some table rows are duplicated across model scales, and no significance testing is reported. Results support moderate evidence of gains on ALFWorld/WebShop, but generalization is only demonstrated on two text-based benchmarks with Qwen backbones. Reproducibility is aided by pseudocode and hyperparameters but no code/data release is stated.
evidence: Section 1 proposes EFCA and frames credit assignment for long-horizon agentic RL using environment feedback.
Table 1 reports ALFWorld/WebShop scores; EFCA reaches 95.31 (1.5B) and 96.03 (7B) on ALFWorld and 89.81/89.06 WebShop task score.
Section 4.3.2 ablation reports removing state-history lowers score to 90.95 and disabling feedback lowers to 91.40.
Appendix E states limitations of surface-level pattern matching and future directions.

arxiv:2608.08254.rationale: Relevant LLM structured-output/prompting study with controlled placement, conflict probe, and reasoning-field intervention. Novel but incremental; rigorous within single-field setting but n=48, no formal significance tests, limited generalizability. Code/data release improves reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract reports schema placement underperformed system prompts by 11–13 points for GPT-4.1 and GPT-5.4 without reasoning and conflict drops of 5–45 points.
Section 3.1 Table 2 shows GPT-4.1 schema-only 77.08% vs system-prompt-only 89.58%; GPT-5.4 no-reasoning schema 80.00% vs system 91.25%.
Section 3.2 Table 3 shows conflict probe example: Claude Haiku 4.5 dropped from 52.50% system-prompt-only to 7.08% conflicting schema.
Section 3.3 Table 4 shows schema_with_cot improvements of 14.6–23.8 percentage points for models with headroom.
Section 5 Limitations states evaluation is single-field classification with a compact 48-item set and no claims about multi-field extraction, tool calling, or complex agent workflows.

arxiv:2608.08253.rationale: Highly relevant to agent memory, long context, RAG, and LLM-backed local agents. However, research quality is moderate: transparent scope limitations and component-level fault-injection evidence are present, but no external end-to-end benchmark or statistical inference, single-node scope limits generalizability, and reproducibility is incomplete despite open-source claims.
evidence: Section 10 Table 3 reports 2,200/2,200 deterministic property checks across component-level scenarios.
Section 11 Limitations states single-node, component-level scope and no end-to-end HTTP/multi-process fault injection.
Section 10.2 reports governed write-envelope overhead p50 1.687 ms and 60s RSS trace 436.4-440.7 MB on a 1,232 MB store.
Section 10.3 carries forward V3 LoCoMo retrieval evidence rather than a new V4 benchmark.

arxiv:2608.08247.rationale: Strong statistical methodology for functional distributional estimation, but essentially no match to the target LLM/NLP/agent/safety/vision preferences; only a weak connection to scientific/statistical ML. Within its own field it is reasonably novel and rigorous with simulations, theory, and a real-data NHANES application, but topic relevance drives the overall score down.
evidence: Abstract: proposes functional distributional random forests for estimating conditional laws of functional outcomes; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning content.
Section 2.2: defines MMD-based split criterion and random-feature approximation.
Section 4: simulation study comparing fDRF with KNN and functional linear models across heteroskedastic GP, mean-shift GP, mixture GP, warped GP, and roughness DGPs.
Section 5: presents consistency Theorems 1-3 under assumptions.
Section 6: applies fDRF to NHANES accelerometer data.
Supplementary Appendix A: proofs of weak consistency; Appendix D: fitting and prediction algorithms.

arxiv:2608.08245.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM evaluation, synthetic data generation, and drift detection; method has moderate novelty but evidence is weakened by private production data, small case-study samples, and no code/data release.
evidence: §7.1 Table 1 reports RA 0.917 for conditional sampler vs 0.897 basic and 0.284 legacy hand-curated.
§7.3 Table 3 reports mean proxy distance reduction from 0.282 to 0.158 after taxonomy refinement.
§7.4 Table 4 reports unguided discriminator accuracy 0.540 (p=0.144), near chance.
§7.6 Table 5 reports only five held-out DSAT cases per proxy category, limiting statistical strength.

arxiv:2608.08244.rationale: Out-of-scope wearable health domain application without language methodology; although it uses a transformer backbone and LoRA-style adaptation, it is not LLM/NLP/reasoning/agentic work. The paper is reasonably rigorous and honest about negative results, but the domain specificity and small independent-participant evidence limit relevance to the stated preferences.
evidence: Abstract: parameter-efficiently repurposing a pretrained general multimodal wearable backbone for women's health.
Section 5.2: nested leave-one-participant-out audit found no endpoint had a strictly positive corrected confidence interval.
Section 5.3: failed preregistered majority-task criteria against shared GRU and MMoE baselines.
Data and Code Availability: code and aggregate artifacts available, but raw participant-level datasets and checkpoints excluded.

arxiv:2608.08240.rationale: Directly relevant to AI safety/alignment and agent objective design, with axiomatic derivations and toy-model behavioral analyses, but purely theoretical; no empirical validation, baselines, or code to support claimed consequences.
evidence: Section 3.1 Proposition 8 analyzes confirmation-asking behavior in toy model
Appendix A.3 Proposition 10 analyzes pause/destroy button toy example
Section 4 states scalable estimation and empirical validation are planned in a follow-up paper

arxiv:2608.08239.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, agentic routing, and evaluation. The branching-rollout methodology with matched same-model controls is novel and the action-level divergence evidence is statistically reported, but outcome-level evidence is small-n and the study is limited to one scaffold, one model family, and quantized serving configurations.
evidence: Table 1 reports paired swap-control deltas with bootstrap 95% CIs excluding zero.
§4.5 Table 2 reports replay mispredicts every success-relevant outcome and patch similarity 0.00-0.11.
§6 Limitations notes n=30 per run pair, one scaffold, one model family, and FP8 vs AWQ entanglement.
Reproducibility section states code and full branched-trajectory dataset are released.

arxiv:2608.08237.rationale: Relevant adaptive RAG/LLM serving paper. The SLO-aware retrieval-budget policy is a useful production framing, but novelty is incremental over prior adaptive retrieval and evidence is limited: only static-k baselines, a small 334-query NQ test set, no statistical confidence, omitted hyperparameters, and cross-dataset/model claims rely on figure-level summaries. Reproducibility is low without code or full feature definitions.
evidence: Section VI-A, Table I: SAGE reports 95% SLO compliance vs 30% for static k=20, P95 latency 3.6s vs 5.6s, EM 22% vs 24%, on 334 Natural Questions test queries.
Section VI-B, Table II: Ablation reports full SAGE 95% SLO/22% EM; removing calibration gives 87% SLO/23% EM; dense-only retrieval gives 94% SLO but 15% EM.
Section VI-C: Cross-dataset and cross-model generalization claims of +46-52 and +49-51 SLO point improvements are provided as figure-level summaries (Figures 4-5) without full per-dataset tables.
Section V-E: The paper states 174 configurations and 58,116 queries, but Section V-A does not report test set sizes for HotpotQA and UnSeenTimeQA, limiting reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.08236.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM multi-agent memory and agentic workflows, with explicit conflict handling. The write-time conflict-aware memory primitive is a plausible but incremental combination of structured memory, symbolic checks, and selective LLM reconciliation. Main ConflictBank result is strong in the document, but sample sizes are small, evaluation uses a single hosted model, secondary planning results are mixed, and learned extraction transfers poorly. Reproducibility is documented but limited by unavailable raw logs and adapter checkpoints.
evidence: Abstract: LatticeMind reaches 0.97 accuracy versus 0.61 for strongest aggregation baseline on label-blind ConflictBank, with p<1e-6.
Section 4.2 and Figure 2 report LatticeMind 0.97 versus Single-Agent 0.63 and Majority Vote 0.61 on 75 ConflictBank examples.
Table 1 reports ablation accuracy 0.96 full, 0.84 without checker, 0.82 without reconciler on 50 samples.
Section 4.4 and Table 3 show mixed secondary planning results, including a TravelPlanner regression and small exploratory REALM JSSP gap.
Table 2 reports software-state budgeted long-noise 0.83 for StateMemory versus 0.70 for LLM-Merge-Inc, while repo bridge StateMemory is 0.51 below LLM-Merge 0.61.
Appendix A.1 states artifacts, prompts, and scripts are provided, but raw prompt/response logs and QLoRA adapter checkpoints are not reusable, and hosted-model changes may affect reruns.

arxiv:2608.08234.rationale: Pure mathematics paper on quantum coordinate rings, generalized quantum minors, and cluster algebra structures. No LLM/NLP/AI methodology or application; out of scope and capped at 0.20. The math may be rigorous, but relevance to the curator preferences is negligible.
evidence: Abstract: concerns quantized coordinate ring O_q(G) and generalized quantum minors
Theorem 5.3/Corollary 5.4: generation result for types G2, F4, E8; no AI/ML or language content

arxiv:2608.08227.rationale: Moderately relevant because it directly evaluates Llama 3.3 70B on scalar linguistic inferences, touching LLM and NLP preferences, but it is primarily a cognitive-science human-model comparison rather than LLM methodology. The study has some controlled conditions and mixed-effects analysis, but evidence is limited by a small stimulus set, incomplete reporting of format/mapping null effects, lack of exact prompts, and no code/data availability. LLM response variability and generalizability are limited.
evidence: Abstract: reports aggregate behavioral pattern reproduction but lack of response variability.
Method: uses Llama 3.3 70B via Groq API, 60 sentences, 4 scale configurations, 20 samples at temperature 1.0, and 108 human participants.
Results: reports a significant Particle effect (β=2.20, SE=0.09, p<.001) and Particle × Source interaction (β=1.38, SE=0.03, p<.001), with human means 2.07/4.31 vs LLM 1.41/5.00.
Discussion: reports a follow-up temperature sweep showing stable model responses from 0.0 to 2.0.

arxiv:2608.08226.rationale: Out-of-scope theoretical/quantum Hopfield-network paper on SU(d) symmetric spaces. It is not about LLMs, NLP, transformers, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, code, safety, or language-based multimodal AI; the only tangential link is the word memory/retrieval in associative-memory physics. Although it provides mathematical derivation and numerical/replica experiments, topic relevance is negligible and the overall score is capped below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: memories/neurons on Riemannian manifolds and SU(d) Hopfields with replica analysis and RGB image recall.
Section IV: color image encoding/decoding and SU(3) image recovery demonstration.
Section V.2: replica-symmetric equations and critical capacity estimates.

arxiv:2608.08224.rationale: Highly relevant LLM post-training, reasoning, RL, and mechanistic interpretability paper. The control-coefficient framing is a moderately novel adaptation, and the regularizer derivation is detailed. However, the empirical capability gains over matched GRPO are small and reported without benchmark confidence intervals, weakening evidence strength; rigor is strong on mechanism paired-difference analysis but limited by modest benchmark support. Reproducibility is good with code link, hyperparameters, and extensive appendices.
evidence: Section 6.3 Table 2 reports overall pass@1/pass@k changes for GRPO and CD-RFT across math, code, and logic domains.
Appendix L Table L.1 reports +7.9% measured overhead for the control regularizer under matched conditions.
Section 6.5 and Appendix K report transfer of control decoupling and capability gains to Llama-3.2-3B.
Appendix F.2 and Figure F.2 provide paired-difference control bottleneck measurements across probe seeds.

arxiv:2608.10016.rationale: Technically coherent federated representation-learning method using sheaf-based geometric alignment, but outside the stated LLM/NLP/agent-centric preferences. Novelty is incremental over existing sheaf-based federated and Procrustes alignment work. Evaluation is limited to MNIST classification with no reported variance or ablations.
evidence: Section 5 defines Sheaf-FRL alternating Procrustes and gradient updates; Appendix E gives deterministic and stochastic convergence proofs.
Section 6 and Figures 2-3 report MNIST-based comparisons with ComFed and Sheaf-FMTL, but no error bars or significance tests are shown.
Introduction states code is publicly available at the provided GitHub link; Appendix G details hyperparameters and architectures.

arxiv:2608.08220.rationale: Conceptual philosophy paper applying metanormative categories to RL-based value alignment and machine ethics; relevant to RL/alignment preferences but not core LLM/NLP. It provides qualitative analysis and illustrative examples only, with no experiments, baselines, ablations, or quantitative results, limiting evidence strength and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 5 and Table 2 map deontic, evaluative, fittingness, and reason-based categories onto RL components.
Section 6 analyzes Abel et al., Noothigattu et al., and Rodriguez-Soto et al. as illustrative RL-based value alignment approaches.
Table 3 summarizes strengths and weaknesses of the three illustrative approaches.
Section 7 states the contribution as making metanormative insights available for evaluating RL-based machine ethics and value alignment.

arxiv:2608.08219.rationale: Relevant multimodal agent/tool-use RL work with process-supervised reasoning, not pure CV. However, rigor is limited by absence of outcome-based RL or prior agentic VAD baselines, no statistical testing/limitations, single benchmark, and unverifiable availability claims.
evidence: Section 5.2, Table 2 reports VTO(Qwen3-VL-8B) All Whole accuracy 96.39 vs Qwen3-VL-8B SFT 86.19 and Qwen2.5-VL-72B 79.96.
Section 5.2, Table 3 ablation: removing R_comp drops interrelated Whole to 29.92; removing R_param drops Input to 78.02; removing R_LLM yields 93.70 vs VTO 95.14.
Section 5.1 and Table 2 list zero-shot/few-shot/SFT baselines and Qwen2.5-VL-72B, but no outcome-based RL or prior agentic VAD baseline is reported.
Section 3.4 reports 1,841 multi-step testing samples and >120k instruction-trajectory pairs; Section 5.1 provides SFT/GRPO hyperparameters.

arxiv:2608.08214.rationale: Domain-specific CPS/formal-methods application using automata learning and decision-tree abstraction; no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, or language-model methodology. Out of scope as a pure domain application, so score capped at 0.20. The engineering evaluation is moderately rigorous within its own field, but relevance to the specified preferences is minimal.
evidence: Section 4.2.4 reports an average 49.20% reduction in states/transitions and 41.71% average accuracy improvement for MELA versus ABLATION.
Section 4.5 discusses internal, conclusion, and external validity, including the two-case-study limitation and BH-adjusted p-values.
Data Availability states public sharing of implementation, data, evaluation scripts, results, and testbed.

arxiv:2608.08212.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM safety, alignment, in-context learning, prompting, tool-use provenance, and red-teaming evaluation. The paper provides paired causal controls, clustered inference, blinded human audits, and explicit negative results. Main limitations are model-dependent effects, reliance on closed aliases, and some small factorial cells.
evidence: Abstract: demonstration framing raises broad EM by 30-32 percentage points on a susceptible Gemini model.
Section 3.4/Appendix C: condition-blinded human audit finds judge-human agreement kappa=.871 and recovers the primary demo/document gap.
Section 4.1 Main Results: all ten content draws positive with exact sign-flip p=.002.
Section 4.5 Generality Across Models and Retrieval: effect is model-dependent; no effect found in GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, or Qwen3.5.

arxiv:2608.08211.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/low-light image enhancement; uses RAG/FAISS terminology but no language-model methodology, so capped at 0.20. Empirical ablations and multi-front-end evaluation exist, but relevance to LLM/NLP preferences is minimal.
evidence: Section 3.3 describes FAISS dual-index retrieval over VGG19 features.
Section 4.1.3 lists training setup and implementation details.
Table 1 reports LOLv1 quantitative results for CPGA-Net++ and the proposed module.

arxiv:2608.08210.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/agent/ToM evaluation paper. The MCQ-probing formulation for hidden disagreement is a reasonably novel task, but evaluation relies heavily on LLM judges/simulators and a small real-user study; the main benchmark gain over GPT-5.4 is not statistically significant. Strong ablations and quantitative tables support many claims, but generalizability is limited by dyadic English synthetic dialogues and modest human/downstream evaluation. Reproducibility is aided by detailed prompts/hyperparameters and promised release, though proprietary models are required for key pipeline components.
evidence: Section 5.1 Table 1 reports GPT-5.4 F1 49.5% and MCQ-probing gains over direct prompting.
Section 6.1 Table 3 reports IoA-Prober-8B F1 51.8% from a Qwen3-8B base of 28.0%, with p=0.14 versus GPT-5.4.
Section 6.2 Table 4 reports 2.89 validated hidden disagreements per meeting and significant advantage over baselines in the real-user study.
Section 6.3 Table 5 reports ablations showing RL and SFT warm-start contributions.
Section 6.4 Table 6 reports pass@1 gains on BigCodeBench-Hard and HiddenBench for IoA-Prober-8B.
Limitations acknowledges dyadic, synthesized, English-only data and single 8B training scale.

arxiv:2608.08207.rationale: Out of scope for the core LLM/NLP/agent/vision preferences; only weak relevance via mixture-of-experts and efficiency. The paper addresses multivariate time series classification using frequency-segmented hierarchical MLP experts, not language methods. Results are broad but lack statistical testing and show large per-dataset instability, so the final score is capped as a non-preferred domain application.
evidence: Abstract proposes FreSH, a Frequency-Segmented Hierarchical Multi-Expert Framework for MTSC; no LLM/NLP objective is stated.
Section 2.5 describes MoE-style local and global experts using lightweight MLPs rather than transformer attention.
Table 1 reports 30 UEA datasets but includes large per-dataset drops (e.g., EigenWorms 55.7 vs 90.1 best; Epilepsy 87.0 vs 99.3 best), weakening robustness claims.
Table 4 reports efficiency on real-world vibration data with 54,243 parameters and 94.37% accuracy, but provides no uncertainty estimates or significance testing.

arxiv:2608.08204.rationale: Out-of-scope statistical/econometric methodology using conditional diffusion and deep ReLU networks for nonparametric IV quantile regression; no LLM, language, transformer, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, or related preferred topics. Theory and experiments are present but do not lift relevance to the target curation area, and the final score is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: proposes two-stage deep nonparametric IVQR with conditional diffusion and kernel-smoothed conditional moment estimation
Section 3, Theorem 3.1: gives an excess-risk bound under Assumptions 3.1-3.4 with heavy-tailed polynomial envelope
Section 4.1: reports simulation results for d=p=10, tau in {0.25,0.50,0.75}, Gaussian and t3 designs over N_total 1000-3000
Section 4.2: reports NBER-CES real-data pinball-loss comparisons against Poly-Sieve, Nadaraya-Watson, and Kernel-Ridge IVQR baselines

arxiv:2608.08202.rationale: Out-of-scope credit-default domain application with no LLM/language methodology; fairness/bias angle gives slight AI Safety relevance but not enough. Quantitative checks exist, but effect sizes are small, SHAP-based causal claims are associational, and generalizability is explicitly narrow. Score capped at 0.20.
evidence: §4.2 reports a 16.86 percentage point TPR gap between low- and high-income defaults.
§4.3 shows a double-blind residual TPR gap of 2.56 pp on held-out test (Z=-4.04, p<0.0001).
§4.5 uses out-of-sample SHAP and Spearman correlation to identify loan amount and home ownership as residual proxies.
§5 and Appendix A document limitations and reproducibility scripts.

arxiv:2608.08200.rationale: Pure robotics/telemanipulation study on personalized motion scaling for delayed teleoperation. It has no LLM, NLP, agent, multimodal, or other in-scope language-related methodology, and pure robotics is explicitly out of scope, so score is capped at 0.20. The study includes detailed human-subject methods and statistical modeling, but contributions are domain-specific and not AI/ML research.
evidence: Section III-C describes four within-subjects factors and SimOnly/Sim2Real sessions; no language-model methodology is present.
Section IV reports assistance effects on overshoot, endpoint error, SAL, PSI, and nCET, but findings are limited to delayed telemanipulation tasks.

arxiv:2608.08199.rationale: Highly relevant to LLMs, multi-agent interaction, and safety evaluation, but the study has modest novelty, small sample sizes, no reported statistical significance testing, and limited generalizability beyond the Werewolf testbed. Code and prompts improve reproducibility, though participant data are unavailable.
evidence: Abstract: introduces DecisionQE and Werewolf framework and links findings to LLM safety evaluation
Methods: DecisionQE describes questionnaire construction across six domains and model evaluation protocol
Results: Tendency profiles differ across LLMs reports mean scores and within-model standard deviations
Results: Compliance tracks game performance reports win rates and role hit rates by tendency category
Methods: Human–LLM evaluation reports 12 eligible human participants and 20 mixed-group games
Data availability and Code Availability report HuggingFace dataset and GitHub repository

arxiv:2608.08195.rationale: LLM-specific ownership verification via constrained-answer counterfactual transfer strongly matches core LLM and adversarial/evaluation preferences. The method is clearly documented with algorithms, prompts, and baseline settings, but main evidence relies on small 20-fingerprint registries and limited suspect pools; perfect AUCs on three families may overstate reliability. Formal bounds are conditional on explicit transfer budgets and only partially validated empirically.
evidence: §VI-B Table III reports TCF average AUC 0.9861 versus TRAP 0.7931, ProFLingo 0.8880, and ZeroPrint 0.9128.
§VI-C evaluates robustness under decoding changes, input paraphrasing, score-space noise, and model merging.
Appendix A-D documents prompt templates, parser contract, Algorithm 1, and baseline configurations.

arxiv:2608.08192.rationale: Formal abductive logic paper with partial relevance to reasoning and neurosymbolic preferences, but not LLM/NLP-focused. It provides rigorous formal definitions and theorems, but lacks empirical evaluation, baselines, ablations, quantitative results, or code, limiting evidence strength and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 6 defines suspended derivation and governed commitment.
Section 7 provides formal theorems with proofs such as join reduction and non-associativity.
Section 8 presents a worked crisis-reasoning example with manually assigned weights rather than empirical data.
Section 10 describes a neurosymbolic division of labor but references external implementations without artifacts.

arxiv:2608.08191.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging paper: BAP-MOS uses bandit-based adaptive prompting for ultrasound multi-organ segmentation with SAM/MedSAM, but it contains no LLM/language-model/NLP methodology. It has domain-specific ablations and quantitative results, but the narrow medical application, small internal test sets, and lack of language relevance limit it; per rubric pure medical imaging must receive at most 0.20.
evidence: Section V-B reports BAP-MOS(SAM) Dice 0.982, HD95 0.482, and MSD 0.204 on the prostate-region TRUS benchmark.
Section V-D-1 reports the TPE search objective 0.1917 mm and selected parameters (tau=26, r_min=10, alpha=0.108, W=50, K=70).
Section V-D-3 reports bandit update costs and final prompt-selection rates with box, point, and both arms.

arxiv:2608.08189.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM-driven program/code discovery and evaluator-guided search; less relevant to Japanese NLP or transformer-specific preferences. Novelty is moderate as it combines AlphaEvolve-style LLM search with surrogate-assisted optimization, adding LLM-generated executable proxy evaluators and region-conditioned online credit. Rigor is moderate-strong: five benchmarks, three seeds, multiple baselines, and ablations on two domains, but no significance testing or explicit limitations section. Evidence is quantitative and sectioned, though backbone sensitivity shows inconsistent AUBC advantage. Generalizability is moderate across expensive-evaluation program-design tasks. Reproducibility is limited by lack of code-release statement despite detailed appendices.
evidence: Abstract: reports Janus reaches 99% of the baseline final improvement with 59.1% fewer real evaluations on average.
IV-B Main Results: reports AUBCΔ gap from 1.6 points on AQM to 45.1 points on Reactor and real-evaluator call reductions of 16.7%-82.8%.
IV-C: Figure 6 reports NDCG@3 gains from 0.688 to 0.970 on PyBaMM, 0.000 to 0.694 on AQM, and 0.612 to 0.923 on FDTD Demux.
Table III Component ablations: all four ablations reduce AUBCΔ and terminal improvement on AQM and FDTD Demux.
Appendix D Table IV: backbone sensitivity on PyBaMM shows Janus advantage depends on backbone; with Gemini 2.5 Flash Janus has lower AUBCΔ but higher terminal improvement.

arxiv:2608.08188.rationale: Strong topical match to LLM quantization, efficiency, and interpretability. The paper reports a large controlled PTQ evaluation (76 quantized configurations, 4 methods, 5 model families, 11 benchmarks) and supports its SNR-based source decomposition and cross-layer propagation analysis with sensitivity checks and binomial tests. Main limits are weight-only PTQ scope, moderate novelty relative to prior SNR/quantization-error work, and delayed availability of analysis code.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports 76 quantized configurations across 10 full-precision models, 4 PTQ methods, 4 bit-widths, and 11 downstream benchmarks.
Section 2.2 reports controlled pairwise binomial agreement between SNR and retention, e.g., 98.3% for bit-width and 86.8-89.4% for method comparisons.
Section 4.3 defines the additive M/S/N source-SNR decomposition, and Section 4.4 defines the cross-layer propagation recurrence with measured gains.
Appendix C.3 reports Spearman sensitivity correlations for source SNR of at least 0.962 under alternative summary statistics.

arxiv:2608.08184.rationale: Relevant survey of LLM-based multimodal agents in ITS with explicit agent, multimodal, safety, and evaluation framing. As a structured review, it has moderate novelty and rigor: self-reported repeat audits but no independent duplicate coding or PRISMA compliance, and no meta-analysis. Evidence is aggregated counts rather than primary effect sizes; findings are domain-specific but the framework is partly generalizable.
evidence: Section II-B describes the independent coding scales C0-C3/E0-E4/P1-P3/Q1-Q8 and label-masked repeat audits.
Table IV summarizes domain-level counts of capability, validation, and proposition evidence across 42 primary study families.
Section VII acknowledges limitations including no PRISMA compliance, no inter-rater reliability statistic, and domain concentration.

arxiv:2608.08183.rationale: Moderate relevance through offline LLM use (ChatGLM2-6B), code policy generation, multimodal vision-language integration, and local serving, but primarily a robotics application demo rather than a core LLM/NLP contribution. Novelty is limited to replacing online ChatGPT with a local ChatGLM in a Socratic Models/CaP-style pipeline. Evaluation is mostly qualitative and simulation-only, with self-reported scores and no rigorous baselines, ablations, or statistical validation. Reproducibility is limited by sparse implementation details and an unverified GitHub link.
evidence: Abstract frames the work as offline LLM-based multi-modal robotic arm control.
Section II-B describes ChatGLM2-6B generating code policies from user text prompts and ViLD visual descriptions, with CLIPort execution.
Section III-A reports 85-90% performance scores and 100% completion rates for single-instruction tasks but provides no baseline comparisons or ablations.
Section III-B reports continuous manipulation tasks with completion rates and qualitative scores but no rigorous quantitative or statistical evaluation.

arxiv:2608.08182.rationale: Out-of-scope clinical microbiology/MALDI-TOF domain application with no LLM/NLP methodology. Within its domain it has a multi-center benchmark, ablations, baselines, and code, but relevance to the stated preferences is minimal and pure domain applications are capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: DALMA is a probabilistic representation learning framework for MALDI-TOF MS microbial identification and AMR, not language-model research.
Section 5.2.1 and Table 2: reports OOD balanced accuracy across architectures and source-target settings.
Section 4.4: provides code availability and training hyperparameters.

arxiv:2608.08180.rationale: The paper is relevant to NLP, summarization, and hallucination/factuality evaluation, but it is an incremental extension of prior RHI/EHI work. Rigor is limited by internal inconsistencies in reported models, weak statistical reporting, and reliance on automatic metrics only. No code/data or parser/prompt details are provided, reducing reproducibility.
evidence: Section IV-B1 lists BART-large-CNN, PEGASUS, T5-large, and GPT-3.5 as evaluated models
Table II reports a DistilBERT row while Section V-B text calls it DistilBART, indicating inconsistency
Section V-C reports paired t-tests with p<0.01 but no test statistics or multiple-comparison details
Section IV-C describes extraction algorithms without code, parser settings, or prompt details for reproduction

arxiv:2608.08176.rationale: Central LLM post-training/reasoning paper. Proposes a unified token-selection and privileged-information adaptation framework for on-policy self-distillation, with a modest conceptual advance. Experiments on Qwen3 1.7B/4B/8B and math benchmarks show consistent but modest gains over baselines. Rigor is reasonable via the proposition and algorithm, but lacks statistical significance/multi-seed evidence and broader task coverage. Reproducibility is supported by a code link and detailed hyperparameters.
evidence: Table 1 reports Avg@12 on Qwen3-1.7B/4B/8B for AIME24/25/HMMT25; USD mean 58.7 vs vanilla OPSD 56.4 and GRPO 55.9.
Table 2 ablation shows joint token selection + PI adaptation outperforms single-axis variants at all scales.
Figure 5 and §4.4 describe training dynamics and sensitivity to capacity budget ε.
§4.1 and Algorithm 1 specify hyperparameters, LoRA settings, and code availability.

arxiv:2608.08175.rationale: Pure multi-agent path finding/robotics paper with continuous-time search, no LLM, NLP, language modeling, or other in-scope methodology. The repeated 'agent' terminology refers to physical robots and planning agents, not AI/LLM agents. Per rubric, pure robotics is out of scope and must receive at most 0.20.
evidence: Abstract defines the work as Multi-Agent Path Finding for mobile robots.
Section 1 states the setting is mobile robots and MAPF, with no language-model component.

arxiv:2608.08173.rationale: Medical imaging/deformable registration paper focused on MRI distortion vs atrophy disentanglement. No LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/transformer language methodology; out-of-scope under rubric and capped at <=0.20. Some methodological novelty within registration but limited baseline comparisons, no statistical tests, no code release, and narrow neuroimaging generalization.
evidence: Abstract: proposes DisMorph to explicitly decompose longitudinal deformation into technical and anatomical transforms.
Sec. 3.2: evaluates specificity on fBIRN distortion-only pairs and ADNI longitudinal AD pairs.
Sec. 3.1: reports AAE reduction relative to Naive composite field on simulated data.

arxiv:2608.08168.rationale: Strong in-scope relevance to LLM Chain-of-Thought reasoning and interpretability via Top-K SAEs. The work provides useful quantitative activation and intervention tables, but rigor is limited by a single model/layer, math-only tasks, no negative-control or random-feature intervention, no statistical significance testing, and no stated code release. Novelty is incremental given prior SAE-based CoT interpretability work.
evidence: Section 4.1.3: reports model, DeepMath-103K training corpus, layer 13, token counts, and Top-K SAE hyperparameters.
Section 4.2.1 and Figure 1/Figure 3: provide activation statistics and cross-difficulty dominance comparisons.
Section 4.2.2, Table 1 and Table 2: report feature source and token-category distributions.
Section 4.3 and Table 4: report causal suppression effects on LaTeX density, boxed answer retention, output length, and Distinct-1.
Appendix A.4: defines keyword-based metrics but does not provide statistical tests or negative controls.

arxiv:2608.08167.rationale: Relevant multimodal/LLM hallucination-suppression method using training-free Wiener spectral editing. Novelty is moderate relative to prior spectral filtering/Nullu hard projection. Evaluation across VLMs, video, and diffusion LM is broad, but internal table-reference inconsistencies and some overlapping/underreported results limit confidence; no code release noted.
evidence: Section 4.1 and Table 1 provide CHAIR_S/CHAIR_I results for LLaVA-1.5, MiniGPT-4, and mPLUG-Owl2.
Section 4.2 and Table 4 provide ablations for mean distortion subtraction, uniform shrinkage, and layer ranges.
Appendix L and Table 9 provide assumption diagnostics, showing paired additivity error 0.099 vs 1.413 for random pairs.
Appendix E and Figure 5 report sensitivity to sharpness parameter alpha.

arxiv:2608.08166.rationale: Out-of-scope scientific visualization/parallel scalability paper with no LLM, NLP, AI safety, or related methodology. It has modest domain-specific novelty in work-based scaling correction, quantitative experiments, limitations, and code availability, but relevance to the stated preferences is negligible and final score is capped accordingly.
evidence: Abstract: states the work focuses on weak scalability of visualization algorithms and shared-memory parallelism, not AI/ML language methods.
Section V: describes iterative quasi-Newton correction of data scaling based on measured single-core execution time.
Section VII-A: discusses limitations of the method, including memory constraints and approximation relative to Gustafson's law.
Supplemental Material: reports additional algorithm benchmarks and provides source code availability with a GitHub repository and Docker environment.

arxiv:2608.08165.rationale: Pure biomedical domain application of latent neural differential equations to blood-clot growth forecasting; no LLM/NLP/agent/transformer/reasoning language methodology. Methodologically moderate comparison across 10 seeds, but synthetic-only evaluation from one coagulation model and unavailable code limit generalizability. Weighted components before out-of-scope cap ~0.30; capped at 0.20 per scope rule.
evidence: Section 2.1: dataset generated from Panteleev et al. coagulation model with 1,000 trajectories and 121 time points.
Section 2.7 and Table 2: reports 10 independent retraining seeds with 95% CIs; SNODE future relative L2 error 0.01397 and sigma_TF MAE 162.8.
Section 4: limitations state evaluation used synthetic observations from a single computational model, requiring clinical validation and only one unknown input parameter.
Section 5, Data and code availability: code and data are not currently released and only promised upon publication.

arxiv:2608.08164.rationale: Topically strong: LLM multi-agent adversarial evaluation, red teaming, and knowledge-distillation identity concerns. However, the study lacks human validation, baseline comparisons, and statistical testing; the LLM judge is uncalibrated, and the findings are acknowledged as correlative. Novelty is moderate over prior ICE/GPTFuzzer work.
evidence: Section 3.1 describes the Probing/Reviewer/Judge agent pipeline.
Section 4.1 reports 12 prompts and 120 conversations per model in the primary setting.
Section 5.1 reports MiniMax-M2.5 Strict ASR 82% and Lenient ASR 96%.

arxiv:2608.08156.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM-driven optimization and code/program synthesis via frozen LLM structural search. Contribution of separating structure and numeric parameters with an inner numerical optimizer and parametric de-aliasing is moderately novel but incremental over prior LLM-as-optimizer and evolutionary program search work. Rigor is limited by small N=3 proposal counts, lack of statistical significance testing, and some claims of superiority despite reported ties; the formal proposition is useful but rests on simplifying assumptions. Evidence consists of multiple quantitative tables and domain experiments but lacks confidence intervals or replication details. Generalizability is plausible across pluggable solvers and domains, though tested on limited tasks. Reproducibility is partial: a code link is reported and algorithm/code listings are given, but no full experimental scripts or data release are verified.
evidence: Table 2 blocks A-I provide consolidated quantitative results for meta-optimizers, policies, and Bayesian inference tasks, including vanilla/numerical/hybrid comparisons and mean tuning gap.

Section 3.3 and Table 2 blocks F-I report approximate Bayesian inference results, including SBC calibration, horseshoe logistic regression, and curved-ridge banana cases.
Section 5 Limitations states the manifest must be parseable, CMA-ES degrades past a few dozen dimensions, and the method is best used as a human-in-the-loop copilot.

arxiv:2608.08154.rationale: Pure mathematics paper on Zarankiewicz numbers and computer-assisted proof; no substantive LLM/NLP/agent/vision/audio methodology. Section 11.4: Independent reproduction, second implementation, and peer review remain desirable.

arxiv:2608.08153.rationale: Pure low-light image enhancement / computer vision paper with no LLM, NLP, or language methodology; out of scope per rubric and capped at 0.20. The paper includes benchmark tables and ablations, but domain relevance is minimal for the requested preferences.

arxiv:2608.08148.rationale: Out-of-scope biology foundation model for multi-omics oncology. arxiv:2608.08143.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM/RAG/LLM-as-judge evaluation, but limited methodological novelty and one shared-task domain constrain the contribution. Quantitative results are reported, though without significance testing or strong ablations.

arxiv:2608.08139.rationale: Strong LLM/evaluation relevance via language-model provenance and lineage retrieval, with calibrated token-space fingerprints. arxiv:2608.08138.rationale: Pure vision federated image classification is out-of-scope despite LoRA/foundation-model vocabulary. Research quality is fair: extensive ablations and on-device validation, but incremental over FedPromo, no formal convergence proof, and some table-labeling errors.

arxiv:2608.08135.rationale: Medical image translation paper using latent flow matching; out-of-scope per rubric (medical imaging, no language methodology), so final score capped near 0.20. arxiv:2608.08131.rationale: Highly relevant to agentic LLM security, AI safety, red teaming, prompt injection, and RAG/memory poisoning. The paper is an analytical threat-model and position paper, not an empirical study. Novelty is moderate: it composes known mechanisms into a formal graph with cut sets and branching propagation, but individual components are not new. Rigor is moderate: formal propositions and clearly separated evidence levels are used, but assumptions are idealized and the core results are not empirically validated. Evidence strength is moderate: the document relies on prior work and incident reports with bounded claims and section-level evidence summaries, but provides no original data or direct verification. Generalizability is fairly strong as the framework is model-agnostic across deployment architectures. Reproducibility is limited because no code, experiments, or victim data are produced; only an ancillary evidence ledger is claimed.
evidence: Section 5.2 presents implant locations and Table 2 maps implant surfaces to evidence.
Section 6.3 defines the minimal cut sets for the three-path model.
Section 7.5 summarizes Back-Reveal as Level A controlled exfiltration evidence.
Section 8.6 describes the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident as Level C but explicitly states it was not a backdoor activation.
Section 13.4 lists recommended controls derived from the analysis.

arxiv:2608.08129.rationale: Out-of-scope for the stated preferences: this is a usable security/privacy study of AI-generated image labels, watermarking, and provenance with no language-model methodology. It has moderate qualitative/technical evidence, but relevance is limited to peripheral AI-safety/image-generation topics, so the overall score is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Section VI-A reports AI or Not mean detection 0.955 versus Hive 0.448 and false-positive rates of 17.5% versus 2.5% on human-authored images.
Section VI-B reports C2PA detection drops from 71.0% to 0.47% after manipulation (p<.001), while Stable Signature retains 100% detection under crop_090/crop_095 and JPEG recompression.
Section III-B states 6,000 images from 6 models and 16 manipulation flows, but the per-model counts are inconsistent (500 images each vs 1,000 images each).
Section IV-A and IV-B provide interview counts such as deepfake prevention 13/21 and data leakage 10/21.

arxiv:2608.08127.rationale: Relevant LLM-agent paper for constraint model improvement with ReAct-style tool use and empirical validation. Novel within CP but components are established; evidence is reasonable but limited by small instance count and overlapping baselines.

Section 3.3: solver-side variance max 4.5%, supporting outcome robustness.
Section 5: acknowledges empirical rather than formal correctness checks, small instance sets, and removed symmetry-breaking constraints.

arxiv:2608.08126.rationale: Relevant LLM explanation-fidelity audit in a credit-risk application, using Phi-2 and post-hoc XAI; moderately aligned with LLM and interpretability preferences but domain-specific. arxiv:2608.08125.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/image stylization using diffusion/flow-matching image editing; no LLM, NLP, or language methodology. arxiv:2608.08122.rationale: Ontology/RDF mapping paper with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, or language-model methodology; only marginal match to the knowledge graph preference. It is conceptual with a small worked example, no baselines, ablations, or quantitative evaluation, and limited reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.08114.rationale: Out-of-scope scientific/domain application for viscous Stokes flow using PINNs/FBPINNs; relevance to stated preferences is limited to low-weight Scientific AI and is not LLM/NLP/reasoning etc. Technically solid but final score capped at <=0.20 per out-of-scope rule.

arxiv:2608.08113.rationale: Core LLM/latent reasoning topic, but the document presents unsupported or weakly supported claims, no ablations, malformed results reporting, and non-equivalent comparisons to larger LLMs. This substantially reduces confidence despite favorable relevance.

arxiv:2608.08111.rationale: Out-of-scope VANET federated/multi-task learning paper with no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent/safety etc. It uses CIFAR-10/GTSRB/MNIST only as vehicular perception tasks, so preference relevance is very low and the overall score is capped at 0.20. arxiv:2608.08106.rationale: Out-of-scope domain-specific sonar/computer vision dataset paper. arxiv:2608.08103.rationale: Falls outside the core LLM/NLP/agent/safety/evaluation preferences; only marginal overlap with graph learning and continuous optimization. arxiv:2608.08101.rationale: Textbook-style survey of generative models (VAEs, GANs, diffusion, flow matching, score/SDE, U-Net/DiT/MM-DiT). It touches attention and CLIP-guided text-to-image generation but lacks LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology and is primarily image/video generative modeling; this caps preference relevance near the out-of-scope boundary. Mathematical rigor is moderate but unsupported by experiments.

Chapter 4 Flow-Based Models and Chapter 5 Score Matching and Stochastic Differential Equations present standard theoretical frameworks rather than original empirical findings.

arxiv:2608.08091.rationale: Theoretical dynamical-system/symmetry paper with only weak overlap with LLM-centered preferences via the low-weight scientific AI/mathematics topic; no language-model or NLP methodology. The formal theory and proofs are relatively rigorous and somewhat novel in its niche, but empirical evidence is minimal (one proof-of-concept, no baselines/ablations) and scope is limited to finite groups and noiseless feature-lifted linear systems.

arxiv:2608.08090.rationale: Moderately relevant NLP/multilingual text classification using LLMs and encoders, but not core LLM methodology. The multidimensional proverb annotation has some novelty, but evidence and rigor are limited by small human-validated seed, weak supervision, training instability, and a contradiction between Table 4 and the text about which figurative form helps Aya.

arxiv:2608.08086.rationale: Relevant systems/efficiency work on diffusion language models, KV caching, and code generation. Novelty is moderate: prompt-only state-aware caching for rollback-capable DLMs is a useful systems contribution but builds on existing DLM caching and sampling methods. The paper provides formal analysis, controlled interventions, sensitivity sweeps, and cross-backbone/cross-domain experiments; however, some empirical differences are small and selected Pareto points limit conclusiveness. Code and setup are described.

Section 8 Limitations: acknowledges the conservative prompt-only cache boundary and remaining generation-side caching opportunities.

arxiv:2608.08085.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/prompting/code-generation study. Empirical design has strengths such as prompt-development exclusion, multiple attempts, validation checks, and replication materials, but it is limited to one LLM, one hardware setup, and PolyBench, with no statistical uncertainty and some unsupported interpretive claims.

arxiv:2608.08082.rationale: Relevant to LLM/NLP and efficient masked-diffusion language-model decoding, with a clear focus on when classifier-free guidance remains necessary. arxiv:2608.08081.rationale: In-scope LLM inference/efficiency paper with a structured-rotation KV-cache method and fused compressed-space attention. Relevance is high because it directly targets large language models, transformer attention, quantization, and on-device serving. Novelty is moderate: combining WHT+SO(4) rotation and packed-tensor attention is a meaningful execution-model change, but it builds on existing quantization/rotation/offloading ideas. Rigor is limited by small evaluation sets, few baselines, mostly 2K-token perplexity validation, and weak statistical support. Evidence includes quantitative tables, ablations, limitations, and instrumentation, but some claims rely on limited self-reported tests. Generalizability is constrained by Apple Silicon Metal focus and MLA/RoPE incompatibility. Reproducibility is reasonably documented with hardware, bit-widths, pipeline details, and claimed code release, though not independently verifiable from the text.

Table 4 reports end-to-end tok/s and peak memory for Gemma 4-26B-A4B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, and Nemotron-H 120B.

arxiv:2608.08078.rationale: Low preference relevance: the paper is about tabular interval prediction and uncertainty quantification, not LLM/NLP/agents/reasoning; FT-Transformer is only an incidental encoder. The proposed next-interval prediction hierarchy is reasonably novel. Reproducibility is strong via code, pseudocode, environment, and dataset manifest. Overall score remains moderate due the 40% relevance weight.

Appendix E.5 Table E.8: identifies validation-to-test transfer gaps on a small set of datasets, indicating limitations.

arxiv:2608.08077.rationale: Embodied VLM evaluation with agentic navigation, spatial memory, and safety-critical decision-making; moderately relevant to multimodal agents, memory, and safety but not core LLM/NLP. EMRD and psychological-memory metrics are moderately novel, with multiple VLMs and controlled interventions, but limited by a single static environment, one prompt, weak external validation, and some internal reporting inconsistencies.
