Conclusion, Limitations: acknowledges single office, static hazards, one safety prompt, and text-biased inventory as limits.
Appendix C/D: provides hyperparameters and prompt details; code URL is given in the main text.

arxiv:2608.08075.rationale: The paper is a multimodal video retrieval/search infrastructure report with language-grounded analyzers, retrieval-augmented visual memory, and agentic Deep Search, hitting several moderate-weight preferences (multimodal, RAG, agents, long context). It is not a core LLM/Japanese NLP paper and remains primarily a systems/video paper. The evaluation is quantitative but based on a vendor comparison with limited reproducibility.
evidence: §9.3 Table 9 reports macro-averaged Recall@1/@3/@10 of 73.09/83.39/91.20 for VideoDB versus 65.75/77.13/89.10 for TwelveLabs across 9,800+ queries.
§9.4.1 Table 10 reports analyzer choice changes retrieval quality, with Qwen 3.5 9B at R@50 62.28 versus Gemini 3.6 Flash at 98.53.
Appendix C Table 17 reports median evidence-stream generation latency below one second for single-source and five-source streams.

arxiv:2608.08073.rationale: Out-of-scope pure domain application: microservice root cause analysis via graph random walks, with no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning or other listed preference topics. Research has some controlled ablations and quantitative simulation results, but evidence is synthetic and unlabeled real-data checks are inconclusive; capped at 0.20 for out-of-scope domain work.
evidence: Section 1 defines the task as microservice root cause analysis using service dependency graphs and aggregate anomaly vectors.
Section 4.1 describes simulated anomaly incidents and aggregate-metric baseline comparison on Alibaba topologies.
Section 4.6 reports real-anomaly windows without ground-truth labels and notes the third window is inconclusive.

arxiv:2608.08071.rationale: Materials science domain application using multimodal CNN/FCNN to predict strain localization from microstructure descriptors. Although it mentions multimodal deep learning, it has no LLM, NLP, language-model, agent, or reasoning methodology, so it is treated as out of scope and scored low.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: proposes a multimodal deep learning framework to predict local strain distribution from 3D microstructure images; no LLM or language methodology is present.
Page 3 Section 2.4 Deep learning model: describes FCNN and CNN components for numerical microstructure data and image data.
Page 10 Data availability statement: X-ray CT images, image segmentation results, DVC results, and Python codes are available.

arxiv:2608.08070.rationale: Domain-specific surgical video world-model benchmark for instrument motion planning; no LLM/NLP/language methodology and largely medical imaging/robotics/vision, so preference relevance is minimal. The benchmark introduces trajectory-level evaluation (LTF, CRS, RPS) but uses a narrow dataset and only four adapted baselines, with limited ablations or statistical analysis. Quantitative evidence exists but generalization and reproducibility remain weak.
evidence: Section 3.1 states SurgWMBench contains 1,637 valid motion segments and 32,740 surgical images with 2D trajectory annotations.
Table 1 reports PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, ADE, and FDE for pure generation versus joint generation and trajectory prediction.
Table 2 reports ADE and FDE under clean, Gaussian noise, and masking perturbations.
Table 3 reports rollout ADE and FDE at horizons 5, 10, and 15 future steps.

arxiv:2608.08069.rationale: Tangentially relevant foundation-model selection framework using LLM-based extraction and LLM recommenders; not an advance in language-model or NLP methodology. Evaluation has moderate rigor with proxy literature ground truth, time-bound zero-shot baselines, and a small n=10 user study, though ablations and statistical tests are reported. Reproducibility is better due to stated code/data release.
evidence: Section 5.2 reports functional feature extraction F1=0.801 and quality-attribute mapping accuracy=0.84.
Table 11 reports HugSelect model-level Coverage@10=0.61 and family-level Coverage@10=0.91.
Table 13 ablation shows removing functional features lowers model-level Coverage@10 from 0.61 to 0.23.
Table 12 reports exploratory n=10 TAM user study with Perceived Usefulness mean=1.62 and Perceived Ease of Use mean=1.48.

arxiv:2608.08068.rationale: Pure computer-vision continual-learning work with no language methodology; out of scope under the provided instructions, so capped at 0.20. It has modest methodological novelty in gradient scaling and KD reweighting, with supportive ablations, but relevance to LLM/NLP preferences is minimal and generality is limited to image classification benchmarks.
evidence: Section 4.1 Experimental Settings: evaluates CIFAR-100-LT, ImageNet-100-LT, Food-101-LT with ResNet-32/18 and five LT-CIL settings.
Section 4.3, Table 5: progressive ablation and fixed-scale control compare AGS against a constant scale across settings.
Section 5 Limitations: acknowledges assumptions of known task boundaries and a fixed replay budget.

arxiv:2608.08067.rationale: Speech-centric dialogue modeling with an LLM/TTS pipeline, so relevance is only moderate: it matches Speech & Audio, NLP dialogue, and LLM-adjacent topics but has low preference weight for audio. Novelty is incremental, closely related to echo-training/acoustic-semantic alignment ideas. Evaluation relies on automatic metrics only, a small 250-sample benchmark, and no statistical significance or human evaluation; however, ablations and quantitative gains are clear and open-source/training details support reproducibility.
evidence: Section 5.2, Table 1 reports DialectS2S language matching accuracy of 95.99% average versus 50.85% for the best baseline.
Section 5.3, Table 2 reports DialectS2S average response quality of 4.42, above all listed baselines.
Section 5.4, Table 3 reports CER of 3.28 for Mandarin and 8.69 for dialect speech versus a benchmark average of 11.67 for dialect.
Section 6, Tables 4-5 show self-aligned supervision preserves response quality and reduces average CER to 6.98 versus 10.15 for sft-2ep and 11.27 for sft-3ep.
Section 4.2 describes training on 8 NVIDIA A800 GPUs with DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 and AdamW, and the paper states model checkpoints, datasets, and code are open-sourced.

arxiv:2608.08066.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/computational photography paper on event-guided motion deblurring; not aligned with LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/safety preferences. Although it reports quantitative benchmarks, ablations, and implementation details, it does not address language methodology and is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: 'Motion deblurring... event-guided blur synthesis framework... domain-adaptive deblurring.'
Section 1: 'Motion deblurring... fundamental challenge in computational photography.'

arxiv:2608.08064.rationale: Topically out-of-scope for the LLM/NLP/agent-oriented preference rubric: the paper addresses causal spatial disaggregation with structural causal models and neural networks, not language models, prompting, reasoning CoT, RAG, agents, or code. The joint causal-deabstraction formulation has some novelty and limitations are candid, but evidence is largely synthetic/semi-synthetic with limited baselines and no general identifiability guarantee, so overall score is capped near the out-of-scope threshold.
evidence: Abstract: introduces Clam for estimating localized causal effects from coarse observations without LLM/NLP/agent methodology.
Section 6: evaluations are three synthetic studies and one semi-synthetic real-world gun-violence case study.
Section 7: states no identification guarantee from optimization alone and limited real-world validation.
Abstract: claims code availability at github.com/gerritgr/clam.

arxiv:2608.08061.rationale: Directly relevant LLM moral-reasoning, AI safety, alignment, and evaluation benchmark. Adapts Morality Chains to text LLMs with conditioned vs unconditioned moral controllability, but novelty is moderate. Rigor is limited by small/medium models, single-turn text-only dilemmas, minor inconsistencies (e.g., six vs seven providers), and summarized rather than fully tabulated results. Evidence is plausible but mostly summary figures/ranges without detailed CIs. Reproducibility is reasonably strong due to claimed release of outputs, scenarios, pipeline, and leaderboard.
evidence: Abstract: introduces CORDA as a benchmark for hierarchical harm-centric moral reasoning in LLMs with 90 dilemmas and four ordered ethical frameworks.
Section 3.4 Evaluation Protocol: describes unconditioned vs conditioned settings, T=0 deterministic and T=1.0 sampled runs, and refusal mapping to default outcomes.
Section 4.1 Conditioned Evaluation: reports mean morality metrics by chain and identifies gemma-4-26b-a4b-it as top-ranked.
Section 5 Limitations: acknowledges text-only transfer limits, contamination concerns, prompt brittleness, and evaluation of action selection rather than deliberation.
Reproducibility: claims raw outputs, scenario definitions, evaluation pipeline, and public leaderboard are released.

arxiv:2608.08060.rationale: Moderate relevance: multimodal CLIP prompt tuning and prompting/optimization align with preferences, but no LLM/reasoning/agent/safety focus. Research quality is decent with multi-benchmark results, ablations, and sensitivity checks; however the contribution is incremental (combining existing low-rank prompting and SPSA-GC), lacks an explicit limitations section, and provides no code release.
evidence: Table 1 reports 13-dataset few-shot averages: ZOMP 68.2% vs ZIP 62.2%, mean/std over 3 seeds.
Experimental Setup states frozen CLIP ViT-B/16, 16-shot splits, 5,000-query budget, and identical protocol across baselines.
Table 5 component ablation shows deep prompt 65.6%, cross-modal LoRA 67.2%, and full ZOMP 68.2%.
Appendix A provides hyperparameters, dataset splits, and query accounting details.

arxiv:2608.08059.rationale: Relevant as an NLP/machine-translation post-editing dataset with modest healthcare overlap, but not an LLM-methodology or high-weight topic contribution. Resource is somewhat novel for preserving document order and CAT-tool context, though descriptive and incremental. Rigor is limited by lack of baselines, ablations, significance testing, or propagation experiments; MT systems are assigned by document, preventing controlled comparison. Evidence is mostly descriptive statistics and case examples. Generalizability is low due to one language pair, one domain, few documents/post-editors, and one CAT tool. Reproducibility is strong with detailed workflow, Zenodo DOI, CC BY 4.0, and FAIR/datasheet documentation.
evidence: Section 4 and Table 1 report corpus-level TER 29.28, BLEU 62.38, COMET 0.88 across 42,108 words and 2,712 segments.
Section 5 acknowledges one language direction, one domain cluster, modest document count, few post-editors, and snapshot limitations.
Section 3.3 provides Zenodo DOI, CC BY 4.0 license, and FAIR/datasheet documentation.
Section 3.2 details Trados Studio 2024 workflow with four MT systems and three professional linguists.
Section 4 notes MT systems were assigned by document rather than enabling a controlled cross-system comparison.

arxiv:2608.08058.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM evaluation, fairness/bias, prompting, and alignment. Large-scale cross-country design, multiple models, robustness checks, and statistical corrections support moderately strong rigor and evidence, though the study is survey-specific and code/availability is not demonstrated.
evidence: Abstract: systematic analysis of representational equality across 59 countries and comparison of contextual adaptation and parametric modification.
Section 5.1: EqCV values range from 0.0286 to 0.0546; GLM-4-9B has highest average accuracy but EqCV=0.0486.
Section 6.2: additional information improves equality for almost every model; GLM-4-9B EqCV drops from 0.0486 to 0.0255 under BM25.
Section 7.2: preference alignment yields no systematic gains in simulation accuracy or representational equality.
Appendix C.1: first-token probabilities versus repeated generation show mean JSD-based similarity of 0.980.
Appendix F: supplementary ISSP evaluation supports the main WVS inequality patterns.

arxiv:2608.08056.rationale: Moderately relevant applied LLM/knowledge-graph metadata annotation system for medical data harmonization. It involves LLM prompting, constrained generation, and KG construction, but it is primarily a domain data-management architecture rather than advancing LLM/NLP methodology. Evaluation is quantitative but limited: no real human-in-the-loop, simulated HIL via another LLM, no strong baselines or ablations, and no significance testing. Reproducibility is aided by prompts and a claimed GitHub link, but dataset details remain partial.
evidence: Abstract: describes a semantic data lake architecture using LLM-driven metadata annotation with human-in-the-loop verification.
Section III-A: details generator-LLM and simulated HIL-LLM prompts with constrained target lists and output rules.
Section IV-B: defines micro-averaged recall, precision, and soft metrics from HIL-LLM decisions.
Section V-B, Tables II-IV: reports recall, precision, soft recall, soft precision, and mean LLM time for seven models across D1-D3.
Section I-A: states the implementation code and preprocessing scripts are available at https://github.com/itzortzis/h2.

arxiv:2608.08055.rationale: In-scope LLM-agent memory paper with strong topical overlap (LLM agents, RAG, temporal memory). However, the empirical support is weak: one benchmark, self-grading with the same Flash judge, best-of-N reporting, reconstructed baseline costs rather than a unified comparison, and no ablations or statistical testing. The method is an incremental combination of existing graph-memory and retrieval ideas.
evidence: Setup and Cost Protocol: states planner, reader, and judge are deepseek-v4-flash, with accuracy 464/500 best of N=3 and self-grading caveat.
Experiments: states baselines are compiled from primary sources rather than re-run under one harness.
Limitations: acknowledges a single store-of-record configuration under Flash self-grading and no unified re-run of all baselines.

arxiv:2608.08053.rationale: Relevant as a VLM-based multimodal reasoning paper using structured chain-of-thought and GRPO, but not a core LLM/NLP or Japanese-language contribution. Novelty is moderate: structured CoT for 3D and factorized geometry are incremental over PhysX-Anything and existing process-supervision methods. Rigor is moderate: includes baselines, ablations, reward ablations, and UE5 evaluation, but many metric definitions and details are deferred to appendix and some attributes are VLM-judged. Evidence is moderate: main numeric claims in Table 1/2/4 and Section 4.3/4.4 support central contributions, though some cost/token claims are not fully detailed. Generalizability is limited to simulation-ready assets from single images with real-image qualitative tests. Reproducibility is partial: backbone/GPUs/GRPO hyperparameters are given, but decoder is reused, no code/data release is stated, and appendix is absent.
evidence: Table 1 reports full PhysX-CoT CD 0.041, F-score 0.480, scale 6.57, and kinematic 0.73 versus PhysX-Anything CD 0.095, F-score 0.256, scale 12.43, kinematic 0.53.
Table 2 ablation shows PhysX-Anything+CoT Prompt is close to PhysX-Anything (CD 0.088 vs 0.095), while PhysX-CoT-SFT+Local Geo.+GRPO improves to CD 0.041 and F-score 0.480.
Section 4.3 states Unreal Engine 5 validity reaches 94.1% parse, 96.8% collision, and 92.0% joint validity.
Section 4.4 states oracle states improve kinematic score from 0.73 to 0.92 and scale error from 6.57 to 4.12, while perturbing predicted 3D boxes degrades scale error to 8.36.

arxiv:2608.08049.rationale: Pure robotics/control theory paper on LMI-based trajectory tracking for nonholonomic mobile robots under wheel slip. It does not address LLMs, NLP, Japanese LLM, transformers, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, code, safety, multimodal, or language methodology; it is explicitly out of scope per instruction (pure robotics must receive <=0.20). Within its domain it has formal math and simulations, but relevance to target preferences is nil.
evidence: Abstract: presents parameter-dependent LMI framework for trajectory tracking of nonholonomic mobile robots under multiplicative wheel slip; no language/LLM/NLP component.
Section 1: positions the work in mobile robot trajectory tracking, wheel slip, LPV/LMI synthesis, contraction analysis, not in language-model research.
Section 6: numerical validation comprises six reference trajectories, slip patches, sensor noise, and embedded feasibility for robot control, with no NLP/LLM methodology.

arxiv:2608.08048.rationale: Out-of-scope power-system dynamics/PINN application without LLM/NLP/agent/core AI methodology. Minor overlap with Training & Optimization and Scientific AI, so capped at 0.20. The work has domain-specific case studies and some quantitative results, but limited broader relevance.
evidence: Section V-A reports MSE and runtime comparisons for 2D/4D/6D synchronous machine models
Table I lists final loss values for ActNet, KAN, and PINN on the modified SMIB test case
Section V-C includes inverter NTK spectra and a short-horizon ablation
Section V states code and supplementary material are available at the GitHub repository

arxiv:2608.08046.rationale: Although the paper uses LLM prompt optimization and GRPO, the core task is chest X-ray generation/medical imaging, which the rubric places out of scope, capping preference relevance. The methodological contribution is moderately novel and includes useful ablations, but conclusions rely on point estimates without significance testing, some comparisons are not compute-matched, and generalizability is limited to one frozen generator and domain.
evidence: Abstract: reports RadDINO-FID reduction from 54.225 to 26.780 and code availability
Table 1: reports JustLLMGRPO RadDINO-FID 26.780 versus Sana 54.225 and BioViL-T 0.696 versus 0.695
Table 4: shows instruction-only rewriting reduces RadDINO-FID to 27.572 but lowers alignment to 0.609, while GRPO recovers alignment to 0.696
Table 5 caption: states the Sana-GRPO comparison is descriptive rather than a compute-matched ablation
Appendix C: reports preservation audit rates and notes the audit does not measure clinical correctness

arxiv:2608.08045.rationale: Moderately relevant: the paper centers on vision-language model evaluation in multi-agent ReAct embodied tasks, with prompting, communication, and benchmark diagnostics, but the main artifact is an urban robotics/city simulator rather than LLM/NLP methodology. Rigor is supported by detailed ablations and engine adjudication but lacks explicit limitations or statistical uncertainty; code/data availability is only planned.
evidence: Table 3 in Section 5.2 reports engine-adjudicated TSR for 12 vision-language backbones across 9 tasks.
Table 4 in Section 5.3 reports communication-mode comparisons with qwen3.7-plus.
Appendix B.5 Table R12 reports component ablations for sea rescue and fire response.
Section 5.5 Figure 6 reports scaling and robustness sweeps.

arxiv:2608.08043.rationale: Industry consensus paper on long-term A/B testing, surrogates, and causal inference for online platforms. It is outside the requested LLM/NLP/agent/transformer methodology scope; the only LLM mention is a tangential analogy to system prompts. The work is moderately structured with cited public evidence and open challenges, but it is consensus-based rather than an empirical or methodological study, with no code, data, or reproducible benchmark results.
evidence: Abstract states the goal is to share industry knowledge on decisions from short-term experiments aligned with long-term outcomes.
Proposition 2.1 reports participant agreement that sign reversals are rare and supported by public evidence from Google, Netflix, Microsoft, and Pinterest.
Proposition 4.4 states experimental surrogacy is preferable to observational surrogacy when possible.
Section 6 lists open challenges including scarce systematic evidence on treatment effect trajectories and mismatched experimental samples.
Conclusion recommends longer-running experiments for surrogate validation and repeats that no substitute exists for a well-run long-term experiment.

arxiv:2608.08040.rationale: Technically rigorous mathematical deep learning paper on approximating conditional laws of McKean-Vlasov SDEs with common noise. It is largely outside the LLM/NLP/agent-focused rubric, with only weak Scientific AI relevance (mathematics/simulation). The main theorem is a careful assembly of existing rough path, signature, Gaussian mixture, and cylindrical approximation ingredients rather than a fundamentally new architecture. Experiments and proofs support the claims, but the theory is qualitative without convergence rates and empirical scope is limited to specific SDE benchmarks.
evidence: Abstract: proposes conditional cylindrical neural networks for approximating functionals of conditional laws in McKean-Vlasov equations with common noise.
Section 3, Theorem 1: proves an L2 universal approximation theorem for continuous square-integrable functionals using Fourier moments, truncated signatures, an MDN, and a cylindrical network.
Section 4.4, Table 1: reports MDN conditional-law discrepancy below the empirical N=200 particle plug-in across six benchmarks, with seed-standard deviations.
Section 4.5, Table 2: reports downstream moment functional relative L2 error for empirical, MDN, and exact/independent reference measure channels.
Section 4.3: describes architecture, optimization, seeds, and companion repository for reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.08038.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM agents, multi-agent orchestration, and RAG, but applied to automotive MBSE rather than core NLP. The methodological idea of stateful adversarial validation with backtracking is moderately novel but builds on known critic-executor and RAG pipelines. Rigor is limited by single-scenario evaluation, no statistical testing, and incomplete model/prompt details; evidence is primarily one ablation table. Generalizability is constrained to VSS-grounded automotive diagrams, and reproducibility is weak without code/data or full prompts.
evidence: Abstract: reports 97% Entity Traceability, 87% Signal Conservation, and 85% F1-score for the proposed workflow.
Table II: ablation metrics show Zero-Shot F1 27% and Traceability 18%; Grounded RAG F1 62% and Traceability 34%; Proposed Workflow F1 85% and Traceability 97%.
Section VI-A: evaluation uses a single Child Presence Detection scenario with eight Ground Truths.
Section IV-B: defines a static JavaScript syntax guard and an independent AI Validator Agent with a six-bucket error taxonomy.
Section V-A: uses Pinecone VSS RAG and Gemini embedding; no code/data availability statement is present in the supplied paper.
Section VIII: lists limitations including single-scenario/simulation gap, critic hallucination, latency, context saturation, and model version drift.

arxiv:2608.08037.rationale: Directly in-scope for LLM agents, local LLM deployment, and tool use. The paper provides multi-dataset comparisons, ablations, cost analysis, and transferability checks, but lacks statistical significance testing, explicit limitations, and code/data availability, while novelty is incremental over prior skill-evolution methods.

arxiv:2608.08036.rationale: Pure embodied/robotics benchmark focusing on long-horizon task-state tracking and agent evaluation. It uses LLM/VLM agents in a closed-loop harness, but the contribution is a robotic task compiler and benchmark rather than LLM/NLP methodology, so it is capped as out-of-scope pure robotics. The paper presents quantitative comparisons and metrics, but no language-model methodology or broader NLP relevance.
evidence: Abstract: RoboGraph is a robotic task compiler that translates state-transition dependencies into executable symbolic graphs.
Experiments > Setup: We evaluate 15 foundation models... in both semantic and visual closed-loop environments.
Appendix A > Table 3: 84 source scenes instantiate one baseline and six intervention conditions each, yielding 588 independent episodes.

arxiv:2608.08035.rationale: This is a pure connected autonomous vehicle/traffic management domain application using decentralized multi-agent path planning and SUMO simulation. Despite terms like multi-agent and edge computing, it does not involve LLM/NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, AI safety, alignment, interpretability, or language-based agentic AI, so it is out of scope and capped at 0.20. Methodologically, it provides algorithmic detail, complexity analysis, four real-map SUMO scenarios, and baseline comparisons, but the baselines are car-following models rather than state-of-the-art AIM planners, and evidence is largely visual without formal statistical testing.
evidence: Abstract: describes VeloCity as a decentralized multi-agent spatio-temporal mobility profile planning framework for CAVs.
Section 5.2: baselines are Krauss, IDM, EIDM, and CACC under signalized and autonomous priority control.
Section 5.3: reports travel time, delay variance, and energy consumption across four SUMO scenarios.
Section 5.1: provides SUMO/OpenStreetMap simulation parameters and map metrics.

arxiv:2608.08034.rationale: Out-of-scope XR/HCI workshop paper on empathy-driven reality. It contains no substantive LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agent, or language methodology despite passing mentions of GPT-3 and AI-mediated empathy. Capped at 0.20. As research, it is a conceptual expert synthesis with moderate novelty and weak empirical evidence, explicitly not a validated system.
evidence: Abstract: framed as a conceptual design framework rather than a validated system
Section 6 Limitations: design space remains primarily theoretical, emerging from expert synthesis and conceptual analysis rather than empirical deployment
Section 2.3 Analysis Method: consensus coding rather than full inter-rater statistics

arxiv:2608.08033.rationale: Pure wireless physical-layer CSI foundation model using Transformer/SIREN; no language methodology, so out-of-scope. Experiments are broad but domain-specific without statistical testing or code release.
evidence: Abstract proposes WiFo-INR as an INR-based wireless foundation model for CSI.
Section IV-A describes the Transformer encoder, SIREN decoder, and compression autoencoder.
Table III reports time-domain channel prediction NMSE comparisons against WiFo-2, Transformer, LLM4CP, and extrapolation.
Table VII reports CSI feedback NMSE comparisons against WiFo-CF, CsiNet, and TransNet.
Table XII reports ablation results for Fourier bases, raw coordinates, and SIREN.

arxiv:2608.08032.rationale: Highly relevant LLM safety/interpretability paper on cross-lingual refusal circuits in multilingual MoE models. Strengths include multi-method attribution, layer sweeps, costed interventions, and a cross-model replication. Weaknesses include a small n=6 writer-amplification dose set, LLM-judge-only labels without human adjudication at scale, unmeasured perplexity for upstream steering, and limited architectural generalization.
evidence: Section 3 reports harm axes align at 0.90 English-Indic at L11 and refusal movement is near-orthogonal to harm axis (|cos|≤0.10).
Section 6 Table 2 reports damping attn18×0.5 yields recovery 0.54 at 1.09× perplexity while shared18×3 costs 23.7× perplexity and surgical head edits are inert.
Section 6 reports Qwen3-30B-A3B replicates the writer/opposer attribution but writer amplification saturates.
Section 8 Limitations cites n=6 writer-amplification dose set, LLM-judge labels without human adjudication at scale, and unmeasured perplexity for upstream detection steering.
Appendix D names ancillary files, transformers==4.57.x environment, and artifact-to-result mapping for reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.08030.rationale: Out of scope: pure CNN/computer-vision model extraction and cryptanalysis, with no LLM/language methodology. Although it touches adversarial model extraction, it does not fit the prioritized LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning areas. The work has some methodological novelty in defining RPCP/PSP and internal differential extraction, but claims are narrow to small ReLU/max-pooling CNNs with strong assumptions and limited generalizability. Final score capped near the out-of-scope bound.
evidence: Section 1.2 lists contributions including RPCP/PSP definitions and a unified extraction model
Table 1 reports query counts, functional-equivalence error, and max parameter error for several CNN architectures
Section 6.1 notes PSPs cannot recover bias and RPCPs are relatively rare
Section 7 describes end-to-end experiments on reduced and full modern LeNet-5 variants

arxiv:2608.08029.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM safety, interpretability, and evaluation. The work is an incremental reproduction/extension of an existing latent-safety-probe pipeline. It provides direct reproduction and cross-architecture F1 comparisons, but does not actually evaluate guard-model baselines despite claiming competitiveness, and its non-determinism analysis is limited because probes are trained only on seed-42 activations. Generalizability is restricted to a few open-weight 4B-8B aligned models and text-only binary harm prompts. Reproducibility is aided by detailed hyperparameters and released artifacts, though Appendix B values differ from main-table results.
evidence: Abstract and Section 5.1/Table 4 report reproduction within 0.37 F1 of original LLaMA-3.1-8B results.
Section 5.2/Table 5 reports cross-architecture F1 for Gemma-4-E4B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, and Qwen2-7B, but no direct guard-model baselines are evaluated despite the competitiveness claim.

Section 5.3/Table 6 and Section 5.4/Table 7 report zero F1 variance and identical activation digests across five seeds; however, probes are trained only on seed-42 activations, limiting the variance analysis.
Section 6 claims portability 'across modalities' but experiments use text-only binary harm datasets; Section 7 acknowledges limits to final-layer last-token activations and no cross-validation.
Appendix A provides hyperparameters and a code/activation release link; Appendix B raw F1 values differ slightly from main tables, noting possible different checkpoint use.

arxiv:2608.08027.rationale: Highly relevant LLM security paper on prompt-injection defense using prefill attention probes. Moderately novel extension of attention-based detection to breach-aware cascade and over-refusal metric. Strengths include multi-model/task evaluation, ablations, and formal threat model; however, saturated detection results (AUROC=1.000), small adaptive-attack sample size, naming inconsistencies (RAPID vs BASIS), and no code release limit confidence.
evidence: Section V-A1 Table I reports BASIS AUROC=1.000 and F1=1.000 on all four tasks for Qwen3-8B.
Section V-B2 Table III shows BASIS-Full reduces FPR-S to 6.2-12.4% on L0-L1 and 0.0-0.2% on L4-L5 while ASR_def remains <=3.8%.
Section V-C1 Figure 4 reports Spearman rho=-0.99 (p<0.001) between IRS and ASR_raw across 144 points.
Section V-C4 Table VI reports adaptive attacks with N=50 and shows GCG-to-Breach lowers Breach Recall to 73.3% and raises ASR_def to 24.0%.
Appendix B-C Tables XV-XVIII label the method RAPID-Full/RAPID-Existence rather than BASIS, indicating an internal naming inconsistency.

arxiv:2608.08026.rationale: In-scope LLM safety/social-bias study with quantitative multi-model experiments, but moderate novelty over known authority-bias findings; rigor limited by unspecified prompts, unstable elicited hierarchies, and no multiple-test correction. Evidence supports some directional shifts, especially the pooled Phase 3 contrast, though claims are partly descriptive. Generalizability is limited to four models, English prompts, Western names, and narrow scenarios; reproducibility is reduced by lack of prompt/code/data availability.
evidence: Section 4 Methodology: 100 runs per condition at temperature 0 for four models, with triage/SA hierarchies using 30 runs.
Appendix Table 1: Phase 1 B-series binomial counts and Wilson CIs, e.g., B2 GPT 69/100 and Grok 25/100.
Appendix Table 4: Phase 3 pooled document-holder contrast Δ=+0.258, z=7.94, p<.001.
Section 5.3: Document-holder inversion increases accountability attribution across all four models.
Section 6 Limitations: restricted to four models, English-language prompts, Western naming conventions, and limited SA dimensions.

arxiv:2608.08025.rationale: Out-of-scope pure robotics/active 3D reconstruction with no language-model, NLP, or agent-language methodology. The paper uses RL/PPO (only minor preference overlap), but does not target LLM/NLP. Research quality is moderate: it includes baselines, ablations, and cross-dataset simulation (Tables 1-3), but lacks real-world validation, statistical significance testing, and code/data availability.
evidence: Abstract: describes sea-state 3D reconstruction and next-best-view planning.
Method: formulates MDP and PPO training.
Experiments: Table 1 reports CR/CD/A_s/A_p on SeaShip-3D, Houses3K, OmniObject3D; Table 2 ablations.
Supplementary Material: provides implementation details but no code or data availability statement.

arxiv:2608.08024.rationale: Highly relevant LLM hallucination detection work with prompt-tuning-style adaptation. The method is a modest incremental extension of linear probes, but evaluation covers multiple datasets/models, bootstrap CIs, ablations, TBG, cross-model transfer, and OOD limits. OOD transfer is weak, and stronger probe/adaptation baselines are not compared.
evidence: Abstract: reports PEP evaluation on TriviaQA, GSM8K, and MedQA using Qwen3 models and claims improved hidden-state-based hallucination detection.
Table 2: main in-distribution ROC AUC values with paired-bootstrap differences and 95% CIs comparing tuned PEP and linear probe.
Section 5.2: claims TBG PEP outperforms SLT linear probe in 8 of 9 model-dataset combinations.
Section 5.6 / Table 6: OOD evaluation shows both methods transfer poorly across substantially different datasets.
Limitations: documents computational cost, OOD weakness, answer-level focus, and hyperparameter dependence.

arxiv:2608.08023.rationale: Out-of-scope embodied robotics/video WAM without language/LLM/NLP methodology; only peripheral transformer/training relevance. Incremental representation-alignment approach with motion/destination objectives; experiments span LIBERO, RoboTwin, OOD, and real-world, but in-distribution gains are small, no statistical significance/error bars or code release, and the work remains robotics-specific.
evidence: Table 1: In-distribution success rates on RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO.
Table 2: OOD success rates on LIBERO-Plus under perturbations.
Table 5: Ablation study of alignment layer and training objectives.
Appendix A: Training cost comparison and inference-equivalence claim.

arxiv:2608.08022.rationale: Conceptual essay on legal responsibility for LLM-based autonomous agents using Promise Theory. It is topically relevant to agents, tool use, and AI safety, but it provides no technical method, experiments, baselines, ablations, quantitative results, or reproducible artifacts; claims rely on informal conceptual argument.
evidence: Section IV Language Model Agents describes an AI agent as an integrator/orchestrator of LLM and tool services and assigns downstream responsibility.
Section III Responsibility argues from the Downstream Principle that receiver-side autonomous choices determine responsibility, but includes no empirical validation.
Section VI Conclusions states that responsibility tracing may have no unique logical end, while providing no quantitative evidence or reproducible method.

arxiv:2608.08021.rationale: Relevant VLM post-training paper using counterfactual visual evidence in GRPO rewards; fits multimodal, reasoning, RL, and training preferences rather than pure CV. Novelty is moderate relative to prior perception-aware RL methods. Evaluation spans multiple benchmarks and backbones, but rigor is limited by uneven baseline comparability in the main table, sparse statistical testing, and no explicit limitations or code release. Internal quantitative evidence supports the claims but should be treated cautiously.
evidence: Abstract and Section 3.1 define CED as a counterfactual evidence margin integrated into GRPO for visual grounding.
Table 2 reports Ours Avg 67.13 vs Qwen2.5-VL-7B base 61.19 and SophiaVL-R1 63.99 on nine benchmarks.
Table 3 in Section 4.3.1 isolates CED on Qwen3.5-9B; Answer-CED improves all nine benchmarks by +12.58 average over correctness-only.
Table 4 in Section 4.3.2 reports cross-backbone results with positive mean improvement on four backbones and non-negative gains on 36 cells.
Section 4.3.3 and Figure 5 show random object proposal collapses evidence margin from 0.268 to 0.015 and relevant-beats-random rate from 0.636 to 0.487.
Appendix A.1 provides hyperparameters and dataset splits; no code or model availability is stated in the paper.

arxiv:2608.08020.rationale: Highly relevant LLM reasoning/inference method. Introduces active thought-level beam search with hidden-state scoring and evaluates across multiple model families and reasoning benchmarks. However, claims of strict dominance are overconfident given no reported significance or variance, and token/latency results are not universally best, limiting rigor.
evidence: Section 5.2 and Table 1: reports +6.7% HMMT-24 and +3.3% AIME-25 gains over pruning baselines using the same scorer.
Section 5.3: reports up to 68.5% token reduction on HMMT-25 (1.75M tokens vs SC's 5.56M).
Appendix A.3 Table 3: reports beam-search overhead as 0.97% of wall-clock time.
Appendix A.4: reports hyperparameter ablation showing smooth performance across swap size, interval, warmup, and memory ratio.

arxiv:2608.08016.rationale: Out-of-scope pure egocentric computer vision/robotics 3D tracking with no LLM/NLP/agents/reasoning methodology, so relevance is capped near zero. The work is moderately executed but dense results rely on ground-truth masks/depth/poses, evaluation uses only eight ADT sequences, HD-EPIC is qualitative only, and sparse ablations show modest aggregate gains.
evidence: Section 4.1: dense setting uses ADT ground-truth masks, depth, and poses; HD-EPIC lacks quantitative PCL and is qualitative only.
Section 5.1 Table 1: EgoTrack3D-Dense reports average PCL 63.01%; no variance or statistical significance is reported.
Section 5.2 Table 2: sparse full F1 is 40.79 vs 39.28 and 40.43 for ablations, indicating modest component effects.
Section 6 Limitations: dense performance depends on accurate geometric inputs; sparse variant remains sensitive to BoxerNet errors.

arxiv:2608.08011.rationale: Out-of-scope cybersecurity operations centre blueprint with no LLM/NLP/AI methodology. Purely conceptual, with no experiments, quantitative baselines, or ablations; validation is only planned for future EU projects. Low relevance and limited methodological rigor for AI/ML curation.
evidence: Abstract: presents a conceptual blueprint for interoperable Cyber Security Operations Centres.
Section III: describes capacity pillars for situational awareness, incident response, and preparedness, plus standards-based interoperability.
Section IV: states validation will occur in future EU-funded projects JCOP and PHOENi2X, with no empirical results provided.

arxiv:2608.08010.rationale: Non-language time series foundation model RL post-training is outside the core LLM/NLP scope, with only weak intersection via reinforcement learning, training, and foundation-model terminology. The proposed GTN-R regularization is somewhat novel in identifying suboptimal collapse, but the paper lacks limitations, significance testing, and code availability, and many comparisons rely on prior baselines.
evidence: Theoretical Analysis: Proposition 1 describes a sufficient self-reinforcing mechanism for suboptimal collapse.
Empirical Analysis: Fig. 2a reports lower initial ground-truth-neighborhood probability for collapsed points.
Table 1: GTN-R improves several TPO and TS-GRPO forecasting results across ETT, ECL, and Weather datasets.
Implementation Details: hyperparameters lambda_m and lambda_u are set to 1 and neighborhood radius is specified, but no code release is stated.

arxiv:2608.08009.rationale: Directly relevant through MLLM reasoning, LLM-based RL optimization, and multimodal AI, but remains a domain-specific media forensics/computer-vision task rather than a core language-modeling contribution. The Anchor-and-Verify chain and Modality-Decoupled Advantage routing are moderately novel relative to prior explainable MLLM forgery detection and GRPO variants. Quantitative results and ablations are provided, but no error bars, significance tests, explicit limitations section, or code release are shown, and some terminology/dataset-size inconsistencies appear.
evidence: Abstract: Proposes EFR with Anchor-and-Verify reasoning and claims state-of-the-art performance with structured forensic reasoning records.
Sec. 3.2.1: Physical Evidence Binding requires visual evidence to satisfy b'≈b and text evidence to satisfy s'⊆s.
Table 1 (Sec. 4.2): EFR reports AUC 96.97, EER 9.18, ACC 90.82, CF1 87.19, OF1 87.05, IoU_m 83.49, and text F1 75.80.
Table 2 (Sec. 4.3): Adding token-level routing increases hard mAP to 81.58 and IoU_m to 83.49 versus the SFT+GRPO baseline.
Sec. 4.1: Implementation uses Qwen3-VL-7B with LoRA r=128, Stage 1 SFT on 50K samples for 3 epochs, and Stage 2 GRPO on 10K samples with group size G=8.

arxiv:2608.08008.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM reasoning, reward-model overoptimization, and adversarial evaluation. The paper contributes a formal coverage-certification framework and executes controlled plus real PRM stress tests with explicit limitations. Strengths include paired repair CIs, syntactic controls, and honest reporting that many real-data bounds are plug-in diagnostics rather than certified. Weaknesses include small trace subsets, a hand-designed 5x5 descriptor grid, strict zero-threshold sensitivity, limited cross-family generalization, and no clear code release link.
evidence: Abstract: states MAP-Elites PRM stress testing and Qwen/RLHFlow empirical results.
§6 Real-model protocol: Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B evaluated on GSM8K with strict correctness-flip threshold and mean/min readouts.
§6 An aggregation-dependent Qwen vulnerability: reports 44 strict mean-pooling exploits, max gain 0.294, and one min-readout exploit.
§6 Syntactic control: matched padding control yields 47 strict exploits, all from padding operators.
§6 Executed archive-guided repair: fresh unpaired re-attack reduces exploits to 1 with max gain 0.0012 vs 0.294.
§6 Paired repair with the method's loss: pre rate 0.148, post 0.037-0.074, max gain 0.333 to 0.177-0.212, AUROC 0.884 to 0.915-0.935.
Limitations: acknowledges small sample sizes, strict threshold, plug-in certificates, one operator family dominance, and unexecuted open-ended attack generator.

arxiv:2608.08007.rationale: Out-of-scope cosmology application using simulation-based inference; no LLM/NLP/agentic/code/safety relevance. Uses existing LtU-ILI/SNLE pipeline with validation and quantitative constraints, but domain relevance is minimal.
evidence: Abstract: uses LtU-ILI, CLASS simulators, SNLE with 6 rounds of 20000 simulations to infer w_i.
Section III: validation uses 1000 test pairs, N=400 posterior samples, rank statistics and P-P plots.
Table 1: reports 68% C.L. constraints; w5/w6 errors indicate unconstrained bins.
Section IV: states w5 and w6 cannot be constrained and attributes this to sparse BAO/SNIa data at z>1.

arxiv:2608.08003.rationale: Moderately relevant to interpretability/explainability and training/optimization preferences, but not an LLM/language/agent/reasoning paper. The spectral neuron is presented as a special case of parametric matrix models and synthesizes known eigenvalue results, so novelty is limited though real. Mathematical claims are referenced rather than fully re-derived, and typographical/mathematical errors reduce confidence. Experimental evidence is qualitative scaling curves with baselines but no numeric tables, exact hyperparameters, or significance tests; limitations are candidly acknowledged.
evidence: Section 2 states the spectral neuron is a special case of the parametric matrix model framework and that the authors focus on overlooked properties.
Section 8.4 describes Criteo and HIGGS scaling experiments and baseline comparisons but reports results primarily via Figures 12-13 without numeric tables.
Section 9 acknowledges O(d^3) eigenvalue cost and untested semidefinite parameterizations as limitations.

arxiv:2608.08002.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM judges, reward hacking, RLHF/DPO alignment, and evaluator ensembling. The covariance-geometry framing and finite-search guarantees are a meaningful but incremental contribution over prior correlated-error and disagreement-based work. Formal assumptions and proofs are explicit, but real-model evidence is limited: the certificate is valid but uninformative, the DPO pilot is underpowered, and empirical audits are mostly single-task/small-model with descriptive claims.
evidence: Section 4.3 Theorem 6 gives selected overstatement and target-quality regret bounds under a joint sub-Gaussian proxy
Section 5.1 fixed-seed Gaussian stress tests across 120 configurations validate the implementation under the assumed Gaussian model only
Section 5.5 reports the real-task bounded certificate is valid but uninformative across all 855 cells because the estimation correction dominates v_hat_s
Section 5.4 finds no aggregation rule separates from the uniform mean on selected target quality at J=5, K=32
Appendix G DPO pilot with three seeds gives a 95% t interval crossing zero, providing no reliable improvement or equivalence evidence

arxiv:2608.07999.rationale: Pure computer-vision AI-generated image detection with no language methodology; out-of-scope and capped at 0.20. The Mamba-style cross-layer aggregation is a modest incremental extension of existing ViT feature aggregation, with extensive zero-shot benchmarks and ablations but no statistical significance testing or code availability.
evidence: Abstract: PE-Mamba is proposed for AI-generated image detection using a pretrained PE-Core vision transformer with LoRA and bidirectional selective aggregation.
Section 4.2: Evaluation protocol trains solely on ProGAN and evaluates zero-shot on UniversalFakeDetect and AIGCDetect benchmarks.
Section 4.7: Ablations cover SSM hyperparameters, LoRA settings, aggregation components, backbone choices, and projection configurations.
Section 5: Limitations include independent per-image processing and challenging Midjourney/ADM generators; code is only stated for release upon acceptance.

arxiv:2608.07998.rationale: Out-of-scope POI recommendation domain application; no LLM/NLP/agent methodology. Provider fairness, synthetic user generation, GNN, and latent diffusion are only tangentially relevant to the stated preferences. The paper has ablations and quantitative results but is capped at low relevance.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 2 reports accuracy and fairness metrics across FPMC, LSTPM, GETNext, MTNet, and DiffuRec with/without SPACE.
Section 4.3, Tables 3-4 report ablations removing community inference, generation, inference loss, and physics anchor.
Section 4.1.1, Table 1 lists dataset statistics for NYC, TKY, and CA.
Section 3.2 and Section 3.3 describe unbalanced optimal-transport allocation and constraint-guided latent diffusion generation.

arxiv:2608.07994.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM/RAG/agentic retrieval preferences, proposing an agentic GraphRAG framework combining vector, directory, graph, and reflection. Method is mostly integration of known components; evaluation is limited to internal telecom QA with LLM-as-judge, no public data/code, no statistical testing, and GD lacks external baselines.
evidence: Section 1: Proposes VDGR-RAG as an agentic GraphRAG framework integrating vector retrieval, directory-driven reasoning, graph traversal, and iterative reflection.
Section 6.1: Uses four telecommunications QA datasets with Retrieval Recall and Answer Accuracy judged by an LLM-as-a-judge.
Section 6.2.1 Table 2: Reports VDGR-RAG outperforming LinearRAG, E2GraphRAG, HippoRAG, A-RAG, and BookRAG on ES, FM, and EA.
Section 6.2.2 Tables 3-5: Provides progressive ablations for retrieval tools, directory backtracking, and knowledge base routing.
Section 6.1: Open-source baselines are reproduced only on ES, FM, and EA; GD uses self-evaluation and ablation.
Section 6.3 Figure 3: Reports LLM-call efficiency, but no code or dataset availability is stated in the paper.

arxiv:2608.07993.rationale: Out of scope: core work is a human motion-text retrieval benchmark and granularity-aware dual-encoder model, not LLM/NLP methodology; LLMs are used only for filtering/rewriting. Overall capped at 0.20, with moderate niche novelty and quantitative rigor.
evidence: Abstract states MRBench contains 3,390 motions and 10,170 captions.
Benchmark Statistics reports multi-source composition and balanced category coverage.
Table 1 reports full-set retrieval results comparing baselines on H3D and MRBench.
Table 3 reports ablation results for motion extractor, text adapter, score calibration, and query extractor variants.

arxiv:2608.07989.rationale: LLM-based generative recommendation is moderately relevant to LLM and efficiency preferences but remains a domain-specific industrial application rather than a core LLM/NLP contribution. The online A/B evidence is relatively strong, but offline evaluation is limited to SID prediction without public baselines or external comparisons, and no code/data are released.
evidence: Abstract reports effective play rate relatively increased by 8.50% and dissatisfaction rate relatively fell by 37.70% in online A/B tests.
Table 1 reports Click PV +0.43%*, DAU +0.05%*, Dis. Rate -37.70%*, and Eff. Play Rate +8.50%*, significant at p<0.05.
Section 4.1 states a 14-day A/B test allocated 15% of platform traffic covering approximately 150M users and used CUPED.
Table 2 reports PushDualGen Pass@1/4/20 of 0.335/0.391/0.422, with w/o SID Adaptation dropping to 0.319/0.352/0.366.
Section 4.1 states training corpora of approximately 0.72B tokens for context compression and approximately 3.6B tokens/day for generation, using Qwen2.5-Omni-3B and Qwen3-0.6B.
Section 3.1 states parallel SID uses M=8 embedding slots and K=512 centroids per codebook.

arxiv:2608.07988.rationale: Pure wireless communications/cell-free massive MIMO optimization with no LLM, NLP, agents, safety, or other target-area methodology. The paper has formal optimization content, but it is outside the stated AI/ML research scope and must be scored very low.
evidence: Abstract: energy-efficiency maximization for cell-free massive MIMO with adaptive quantization resolution
Section II-H: formulates EE maximization over bandwidths, time split, quantization bits, fronthaul powers
Section V-B: numerical results compare proposed TD/FD IAF schemes against fixed benchmarks

arxiv:2608.07987.rationale: Relevant multimodal LLM/reasoning work: it proposes step/trajectory value gating for MLLM spatial reasoning rather than pure CV. Main strengths are four benchmark evaluations, ablations, and a theoretical policy-improvement framing. However, confidence is limited by lack of error bars/statistical tests, no explicit limitations, ablation mainly on ScanNet, and uncertain details for applying the learned gate to proprietary models.
evidence: Section V-B and Table I report ScanNet overall gains from 34.1 to 44.6 for GPT-5.4 Stepwise and 36.1 to 49.0 for Gemini-3.1-pro-preview Stepwise.
Table V ablation shows SAG only +1.7, TAG only +3.4, full +10.5, SWA removal -1.3, and single-head TAG -4.5.
Section V-D and Fig. 4 show AG outperforming Self-Consistency and ToT across 5-20 candidate budgets on ScanNet.
Section V-A states two-stage training with Qwen3-VL-4B and provides a public GitHub URL, but many dataset/tree-construction and API-generation details are incomplete.

arxiv:2608.07984.rationale: Out-of-scope agricultural computer vision/self-supervised visual pretraining with no language methodology; capped at 0.20. The paper is reasonably executed with quantitative downstream results, but relevance to LLM/NLP-focused preferences is minimal.
evidence: Section 3, Table 1: AgriField-40K aggregates 17 public datasets and retains 39,963 images.
Section 5.2, Table 2: AgriMAE + Adapters with L_feat reaches 94.72% top-1 on DeepWeeds, versus 92.23% full fine-tuning.
Section 5.2, Tables 3-5: Across PhenoBench, GrowliFlower, and CropAndWeed, feature reconstruction improves over pixel reconstruction and adapter baseline.
Section 5.3, Table 6: Ablations show increasing adapter rank improves linear probing, and L_feat outperforms L_pix.

arxiv:2608.07982.rationale: Paper is a pure remote sensing computer vision method using frozen DINOv3 for change detection, with no LLM/NLP/language methodology. Although it includes transformer/efficiency elements, it is explicitly out of scope per rubric for pure computer vision, so overall score is capped at 0.20. Within domain it reports ablations and efficiency measurements, but generalizability is limited to remote sensing change detection.
evidence: {'section': 'Abstract', 'claim': 'Uses DINO vision foundation model for bi-temporal remote sensing change detection.'}
{'section': 'Method', 'claim': 'Proposes CGLA, BSCS, CPGR for frozen DINOv3 backbone; no language model or NLP component.'}

arxiv:2608.07981.rationale: Video diffusion/world-model paper for physics-aware streaming generation. It uses VLM annotations and text conditioning but has no LLM/NLP/agent methodology; it falls under the out-of-scope image/video diffusion category. PhyS-120K and Temporal Credit Routing are incremental within physics-aware video RL, with multiple benchmarks and ablations but uneven/regressive gains and no statistical testing. Kept near the 0.20 out-of-scope ceiling.
evidence: Abstract introduces PhyS as a three-stage framework and reports gains on PhysicsIQ, VideoPhy, VideoPhy2, and PhyGenBench.
Section 5.2 Table 1 reports PhyS-120K SFT improves Wan2.1-14B PhysicsIQ from 26.9 to 31.8 and TCR improves Self Forcing PhysicsIQ from 16.9 to 20.9.
Section 5.4 Table 4 reports routing and reward ablations on 10-second rollouts.

arxiv:2608.07980.rationale: Out-of-scope pure audio/speaker-recognition and forensic speech review; no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent methodology. Although scholarly in its domain, taxonomy relevance is minimal (Speech & Audio weight 0.5), so the overall score is capped at 0.20 per out-of-scope policy.
evidence: Abstract: reviews voiceprint fallacy, forensic voice comparison, speaker recognition, and speech deepfakes.
Section 8.1: concludes the voiceprint concept is scientifically misleading and not a fixed unique mark of identity.
Section 6.1: covers GMM-UBM, i-vector, x-vector, and ECAPA-TDNN speaker representations.
Section 7: discusses speech deepfakes and source speaker tracing.

arxiv:2608.07978.rationale: Relevant to LLM multi-agent, RAG, external verification, and safety-oriented evaluation, though applied to structural engineering rather than core language-model methodology. Not a pure domain application because language-based agent/verification methodology is central. Novelty is moderate: external-verifier repair loops are known, and the dual-node/three-layer scheme is a domain-specific extension. Rigor has strengths (baselines, ablations, statistical tests, cross-model check) but concerns include a self-assessment composite metric, small ablation subset, and odd statistical reporting such as A1 p=1.00 despite large compliance drop. Evidence is quantitative with objective cross-checks, but validation is mostly self-reported. Generalizability is limited to five planar linear-elastic structure types and fixed topology. Reproducibility is claimed via open-source code, data, and scripts but cannot be independently verified from the document.
evidence: Section 3.3 defines the dual-node closed-loop feedback mechanism using external finite-element/code-checking verification and score-history decomposition.
Section 5.2, Table 5 reports B4 closed-loop compliance 98.6% and composite score 71.4 versus B3 open-loop 56.8% and 63.8.
Section 5.4, Table 9 reports ablations removing Node 1, Node 2, RAG, and optimization constraints; A2 score drop has p=0.039.
Section 6 acknowledges limitations including fixed topology, only two standards, assessment subjectivity, and limited cross-model statistical power.
Data and code availability section claims open-source release of code, 44-case benchmark, experiment scripts, and statistical pipeline.

arxiv:2608.07975.rationale: Out-of-scope biophysics/single-particle tracking paper; no LLM, NLP, agents, or AI/ML methodology. It presents turning-angle analysis for anisotropic fractional Brownian motion in live-cell trajectories, with simulations and experimental data, but does not match user preferences. Quality is moderate within its domain but relevance is minimal, capping overall score.
evidence: Abstract: proposes turning-angle analysis to uncover anisotropies in anomalous diffusion.
Results II.3: reports estimated anisotropy ratios for quantum dots, CD4, and Nav1.6.
Methods IV.5: describes numerical simulations using circulant embedding and look-up table generation.
Code availability: provides GitHub link for notebooks and analysis code.

arxiv:2608.07974.rationale: Relevant LLM fine-tuning/efficiency work with edge system focus. Novelty is moderate: local objective construction and LoRA are existing, though the theoretical treatment and Android prototype add some contribution. Rigor is limited because convergence is established for an auxiliary objective R_t rather than directly for the global objective, and empirical coverage is narrow. Evidence includes comparative memory/throughput and recovery measurements but limited variance reporting. Reproducibility is partly supported by a code link and detailed setup, though model/task scope is restricted.
evidence: Abstract: claims ZeroLock reduces memory by 26.5% and improves throughput by 4.9% versus BP-based baselines.
Section IV-A: evaluation uses TinyLlama on a fixed 10,000-example AG News subset, LoRA rank 4, and three chunk/stage assignments, limiting generalizability.
Section IV-B1 and Fig. 4: reports peak memory and activation reductions against GPipe, 1F1B, and PipeDream, e.g., 75.4%, 40.8%, and 48.8% per-stage average activation reduction respectively.
Theorem 1: states O~(1/sqrt T) convergence under stated assumptions, with proofs based on the auxiliary objective R_t rather than directly establishing global objective convergence.

arxiv:2608.07968.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM reasoning, test-time compute, prompting, and code reasoning. Introduces a novel shared-budget exam framework with controlled scoring/order/prompt ablations and model-adaptive value-density checks. Quantitative evidence is strong, with partial Spearman analyses and confidence intervals, but generalizability is limited by the Omni-MATH-centric factorial design and limited code-domain tests; reproducibility is moderately reduced by unspecified Omni-MATH budget values and API decoding defaults.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports overall effort-position partial Spearman -0.34, strengthening to -0.48 at N=20, and solving-order-position +0.68.
Table 2 reports mean top-density overlap 0.59 versus chance 0.59, while early-position overlap is 0.76 in the random-scoring ascending-difficulty condition.
Section 4.3 and Table 3 report planning improves coverage by +0.14 at N=20, but Table 4 shows order-position correlation remains high and effort-value correlation remains weak.
Section 4.5 and Table 5 show CRUXEval-O generalization with averaged effort-position -0.42 and solving-order-position 0.99.
Appendix A provides prompts and judge instructions, but the document does not numerically specify the Omni-MATH shared budget B, and API model decoding defaults are not fully detailed.

arxiv:2608.10011.rationale: Out-of-scope pure domain application in medical/hemodynamic inference using physics-informed neural operators; no LLM/language methodology, so preference relevance is minimal. The symmetry-aware quotient-space formulation has some methodological novelty, but evaluation is retrospective, single-center, and uses a pressure-derived proxy with weak monitor CO agreement. Overall score capped at 0.20 due to out-of-scope domain.
evidence: Section 3.3 describes separate convolutional Transformer encoders for ECG and PPG.
Section 5.1 reports 32% relative reduction in log tau_wave MAE versus a training median baseline.
Section 7 states the evidence is retrospective and from a single tertiary care center, limiting generalization.

arxiv:2608.07966.rationale: Relevant mainly via code synthesis/program synthesis under Code & Programming, but it is classical SMT-based OS code synthesis with no LLM/ML/NLP methodology. Systems evaluation is rigorous with ablations and artifact availability, but thematic alignment is limited.
evidence: Section 6.2 Table 1 reports x86_64 page table synthesis at 1,137 ms P50 versus Linux kernel build at 153,831 ms.
Section 6.3 Table 2 shows search space reduction from log10 38 to 13 with cumulative optimizations for x86_64.
Section 6.6 Table 3 reports comparable latencies between Velosiraptor-generated and hand-written Linux/Barrelfish code.
Appendix A provides artifact access via GitHub and DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14752297.

arxiv:2608.07965.rationale: Moderately relevant to LLM agents and knowledge-grounded evaluation, but framed as a cybersecurity education application. The framework combines known components such as multi-agent role decomposition, ontology validation, and schema-constrained behavior with incremental novelty. Empirical support is limited: a 24-student survey with descriptive Likert means, an LLM-as-judge ablation that is non-paired and explicitly descriptive, no significance testing, and no reported code/data availability.
evidence: Section 3 describes the layered multi-agent framework with ChallengeAgent, BuddyAgent, CriticAgent, RewardAgent, schema-governed behavioral control, and ontology-guided validation.
Section 4.2 reports a human study with 24 undergraduate students, Likert means such as scenario authenticity M=4.21, trust M=3.92, and challenge difficulty M=3.12, with Cronbach's alpha=0.90.

Section 4.3 Table 3 reports LLM-as-Judge scores for Cyberagents (n=74) versus ablation (n=26), e.g., challenge quality 4.20 versus 3.46, but states the ablation had less traffic and results are interpreted descriptively rather than as paired comparisons.
Section 4 describes implementation and evaluation but does not report code/data availability or statistical significance tests.

arxiv:2608.07964.rationale: Relevant to MoE/transformer distributed inference and efficiency preferences, but primarily a systems/infrastructure contribution rather than LLM language methodology. Novelty is moderate: cross-layer micro-batch scheduling without expert-map changes is a useful orthogonal direction, but the core contribution is an engineering heuristic. Evidence is supportive across three MoE LLMs, LongBench tasks, and EP sizes, though direct comparisons to expert replication/migration load balancers are limited, figures lack variance estimates, and Appendix D notes hardware and setup restrictions.
evidence: Abstract claims code availability at https://github.com/yize-wu/EasyInfra and GPU idling reduction mostly over 40%.
Section 5.1/Figure 2 reports end-to-end latency and GPU under-utilization across Qwen3-30B, Moonlight-16B, and Qwen3-235B on LongBench tasks.
Section 5.2/Figure 3 compares MaxUtil, CumUtil, and DiffPeak scheduling heuristics against baseline.
Section 5.3/Figure 5 reports additive gains when combined with EPLB on Qwen3-235B.
Table 4 reports GPU under-utilization across EP sizes 2/4/8 for Qwen3-30B and Moonlight-16B.
Appendix D lists limitations: no acceleration for non-MoE/no-EP, requires micro-batching, only A800 GPUs, and Attention-FFN disaggregation unverified.

arxiv:2608.07959.rationale: High relevance: LLM-based agentic tool use, CoT reasoning, and RL (GRPO) for long-video understanding; not pure CV. Novelty moderate: self-checking recovery, UPS-GRPO uncertainty selection, and turn-level advantage modulation are incremental over prior CoTT/GRPO work. Rigor moderate: formalized methods, multi-benchmark baselines and ablations, but no statistical significance, no error bars, no explicit limitations, and appendix details are missing. Evidence from Tables 1-4 and Figure 5 supports quantitative gains, though claims are not independently verified. Generalizability limited to long-video QA benchmarks. Reproducibility moderate/low: frameworks and data pipeline described, but no code/data release or availability statement shown.
evidence: Section 4.2 Main Results, Table 1: reports SCOUT-7B accuracies of 63.0 on Video-MME(long), 47.6 on EgoLifeQA, 49.0 on Ego-R1 Bench, and 35.8 on HourVideo.
Section 4.3 Ablation Study, Table 3: removing turn-level reward changes EgoLifeQA from 47.6 to 44.0; removing UPS changes EgoLifeQA from 47.6 to 45.8.
Section 3.3 Data Construction: describes RA-CoTT pipeline generating approximately 8k recovery-aware training trajectories.
Section 4.3 Ablation Study, Figure 5: reports training dynamics including gradient norm and trajectory reward comparisons.

arxiv:2608.07958.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision / industrial anomaly detection paper with no language-model, NLP, reasoning, or agent methodology. It has some multimodal vision relevance, but the work is a domain-specific imaging benchmark (Li-ion battery electrode inspection), so overall score is capped at 0.20. Methodologically it includes baselines, ablations, and limitations, but relevance to the stated preferences is minimal.
evidence: Abstract: introduces LIBAD, a multimodal anomaly detection benchmark for Li-ion battery electrode manufacturing using visible-light imaging and X-ray radiography.
Experiments Table 2: reports image-level FPR95, AUROC, AUPR, and F1-max for unimodal and multimodal anomaly detection methods.
Ablation Study Figure 3: DA-Core density-aware FPS reduces FPR95 from 60.4% to 54.3% at coreset ratio 0.05 compared with standard farthest point sampling.
Conclusion: states absolute FPR95 remains too high for direct deployment, indicating LIBAD is still an open challenging benchmark.

arxiv:2608.07955.rationale: Relevant to agents/tool use, reasoning, and multimodal LVLMs, but not core LLM methodology. The neuro-symbolic skill evolution idea is moderately novel but presented without adequate experimental rigor: no ablations, error bars, implementation details, or limitations, and only one results table supports claims.
evidence: Section 3.3 describes skill retrieval, action selection, tool/code execution, and state update
Table 1 reports average accuracy on MMSI, MindCube, and OmniSpatial but without statistical significance or confidence intervals

arxiv:2608.07954.rationale: Moderately relevant LLM/RAG-efficiency paper on caching knowledge-graph neighborhoods for KGQA with iterative ToG and one-shot RoG. It engages LLM grounding, retrieval, and efficiency preferences, but not core LLM methods or high-weight areas like reasoning, agents, or safety. The contribution is a straightforward entity-level and semantic cache layer; evaluation spans two benchmarks, multiple policies, backends, and LLMs, but semantic full-system speedup is marginal (1.06x), no repeated trials or statistical testing are reported, and generalizability is limited by Freebase-specific subgraphs.
evidence: Section 5.3 reports WebQSP LRU hit rates of 16.6% at cache size 10 and 34.6% at size 1000, with Oracle reaching 54.4% at size 1000.
Table 2 reports CWQ LFU KG retrieval speedup of 1.91x and Oracle speedup of 3.57x at cache capacity 1000.
Section 5.5 reports semantic-context full-system speedup up to 1.06x and WebQSP F1 differences of at most 1.7 percentage points without repeated trials.
Section 7 notes the cache is an in-memory dictionary and KG retrieval is a small fraction of total runtime, limiting end-to-end gains.

arxiv:2608.07953.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/ML robustness paper without language methodology; evaluated only on CIFAR-10. Proposes failure attribution under distribution shift, but relevance to tracked preferences is minimal. Novelty is modest and incremental. Rigor is limited by a single dataset, no statistical significance testing, and missing adversarial-shift evaluation despite claiming four failure types. Evidence includes quantitative CIFAR-10 tables but is insufficient for broad claims. Generalizability and reproducibility are low; no code release or detailed implementation/hyperparameter information is provided.
evidence: Page 1, Abstract: claims self-diagnosing models distinguish covariance shift, semantic shift, noise corruption, and adversarial perturbation.
Page 2-3, Section III Result: uses CIFAR-10 and reports classification accuracy 0.5983, failure attribution accuracy 0.9433, reliability accuracy 0.9440, and reliability AUROC 0.9864.
Page 3, Figure 1/confusion matrix: reports clean, covariate, noise, and semantic failure attributions; no adversarial perturbation results are shown.
Page 6, Table 2: compares uncertainty-only, MC Dropout, Deep Ensemble, Energy-Based Score, and Self-Diagnosing models.
Page 11, Table A: per-shift results show evaluations limited to CIFAR-10 and only clean/covariate/noise/semantic shifts.

arxiv:2608.07952.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, AI safety, and red-teaming evaluation. The PSE formalization is moderately novel, but rigor and evidence are limited by small per-cell samples, withdrawn significance tests, a partly tautological name-binding ablation, oracle-dependent SRV upper bound, and a non-independent LLM judge. Breadth across 24 models helps generalizability, but synthetic temperature-0 controlled scenarios and non-incident case studies constrain real-world validity. Reproducibility is mixed: a pinned 14,293-run corpus is released, yet several results are explicitly unretained or descriptive.
evidence: Abstract reports susceptibility across 24 models and type-dependent persistence but with narrow per-cell samples and caveats.
Table 3 shows name binding is necessary (0% without NB), while the text acknowledges this is partly by construction.
Table 2 reports 5.2% pooled drift with SD around 7pp and withdraws the significance test.
Appendix E states 14,293 released runs but flags several unretained/descriptive results.

arxiv:2608.07949.rationale: Demo paper on valuation-driven data discovery for autonomous agents; relevant to Agents & Tool Use and Data & Datasets, but peripheral to core LLM/NLP methodology. Architecture is described without quantitative evaluation, baselines, or ablations, weakening rigor and evidence. Claims of utility gains are unsupported by reported measurements.
evidence: Section 2.2 describes the three-phase valuation pipeline including proxy-label propagation and multi-round knapsack optimization.
Section 3 presents demonstration scenarios but provides no quantitative metrics, baselines, or ablations.
PVLDB Artifact Availability claims source code at https://github.com/guixu-project/guixu.

arxiv:2608.07948.rationale: Out-of-scope visual autoregressive text-to-image generation without language-model methodology; relevance to LLM/NLP preferences is negligible. The paper reports quantitative benchmarks and ablations, but rigor is limited by lack of statistical testing and reliance on layout planning, and generalizability is confined to VAR-based T2I models.
evidence: Table 1 reports Geneval and T2I-CompBench results for SynVAR compared with Infinity and Switti.
Table 2 provides ablation results for global guidance, receptive field constraint, and high-frequency compensation.
Section 4.1 describes implementation details and reports single A6000 experiments.
Section 4.2 summarizes quantitative and qualitative main results.

arxiv:2608.07947.rationale: Moderately relevant: integrates an LLM schedule predictor but centers on software testing/formal verification rather than LLM capabilities. Formal model and quantitative results are present, but completeness depends on an idealized stochastic oracle, baselines omit LLM-based testing tools, and reported aggregate improvements lack variance. Reproducibility is partially supported by pinned dependencies and code link.
evidence: Sect. 5.2 describes LLM-Guided Schedule Prediction using a fine-tuned Llama 3 8B model served via vLLM.
Sect. 8.2 Table 1 reports DNSSE detects 73 aggregate bugs vs 25 for P-Fuzz and raises mean branch coverage to 91.6% from 68.6%.
Sect. 8.4 reports ablations: replacing the LLM scheduler reduces bug detection by 58%; disabling SMT lowers coverage by 31%; SMT-only timeouts on 3 of 5 benchmarks.
Sect. 7 lists pinned dependencies, fixed seeds, cluster hardware, and a code availability link.

arxiv:2608.07946.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM/text-to-SQL evaluation and selective abstention, with a verification-harness framing and extensive negative/ablation reporting. Novelty is moderate: it repurposes existing selective-prediction and metadata-profiling ideas rather than introducing fundamentally new modeling. Rigor is decent for external BIRD/Spider studies with database-clustered intervals and paired comparisons, but internal validation remains self-authored and several results are backbone-dependent. Generalizability is limited by synthetic internal warehouses, per-database over-answering, and calibration not transferring across backbones. Reproducibility is supported by claimed frozen scripts/records, though the untrusted paper text limits independent verification.
