arxiv:2608.07945.rationale: Database/cloud autoscaling paper for Alibaba AnalyticDB; no LLM, NLP, agents, reasoning, or language methodology. Only tangential preference match via graph transformer query plan encoding. This is a pure domain database application, so scored near the out-of-scope cap despite moderate evaluation quality.
evidence: Abstract: reports evaluation on over 1.36 million production queries and a 76.7% relative improvement in configuration selection.
Section 5.2: reports prediction Q-error against GTN, XGB, MLP, and LGBM baselines on production datasets D1 and D2.
Section 5.3: reports auto-scaling constraint satisfaction under performance- and cost-optimization policies with FIHC ablation.
Section 5.4: reports training and inference overhead comparisons.

arxiv:2608.07943.rationale: Relevant multimodal document QA study using Qwen3-VL reasoner, retrieval, chain-of-thought prompting, and long-context/selection ablations, touching multiple high-weight topics. Rigor is moderate: controlled interventions and detailed ablations, but single benchmark/model family and LLM judge limit generalizability. Evidence tables support claims, though some effect sizes may not transfer.
evidence: §4.3 Data and Evaluation: uses MMLongBench-Doc, LLM judge Gemini 2.5 Flash, and document-level bootstrap.
§5.1 Table 2: TLV accuracy 52.5 vs V 45.6; parser spread 15.6 points reduced to 4.2 with vision.
§5.2 Figure 3(a): withholding a gold page drops TLV accuracy from 38.6 to 18.5.
§5.3 Table 3: single-page 64.6 vs multi-page 38.6 at TLV.
Limitations: only MMLongBench-Doc and Qwen3 family, page-level attribution, single LLM judge.

arxiv:2608.07941.rationale: Moderately relevant multimodal vision-language segmentation paper using LISA-7B/LMM/CLIP for instruction-conditioned camouflaged object detection, though the core contribution is computer-vision segmentation. LADVF is incremental over LISA/MM-SAM; comparisons and ablations are extensive but self-reported, limited to COD datasets with a fixed instruction, and lack code or significance testing.
evidence: Abstract claims best reported value in all 12 dataset-metric comparisons on CAMO/COD10K/NC4K.
Table 1 reports quantitative comparison and shows LAD-COD outperforming listed baselines.
Table 2 reports cumulative ablation isolating target embedding, four-stage features, and LADVF.
Appendix Table 5 reports input-resolution sensitivity from 384 to 1024.
Appendix Section 4 notes remaining failures on thin/occluded structures and look-alike background over-segmentation.

arxiv:2608.07940.rationale: Core contribution is geoeconomic mechanism design using switching dynamical systems; LLM/Claude usage appears only in an optional small generation and classification audit (Section 8.6), not as language-model methodology, so relevance to the stated LLM/NLP/agent preferences is minimal. The formal model and proof sketches are transparent, but empirical support is limited to an uncalibrated illustrative proof-of-concept simulation with no real-world calibration, baselines, or ablations, and the LLM audit uses only nine generations from one model.
evidence: Section 1 and Section 3.1 define the core geoeconomic/mechanism-design scope
Section 7 states the proof-of-concept uses illustrative parameterization and is not calibrated
Section 8.6 reports a small run with nine generations from a single prompt and single model
Table 3 describes three simulation studies but results are high-level rather than full quantitative comparisons

arxiv:2608.07937.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/3D reconstruction paper on feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting and novel view synthesis. It uses transformer/deformable attention components but has no language modeling, LLM, NLP, reasoning, or agent methodology. Ablations and datasets are reported, but relevance to stated preferences is minimal, capping the score at 0.19.
evidence: Abstract: describes FlexSplat for novel view synthesis from uncalibrated object-centric multi-view images using 3D Gaussians; no language methodology.
Section 4.4: reports four-view GSO results against posed baselines.
Section 4.8: ablation study on Objaverse-LVIS validation split.

arxiv:2608.07935.rationale: Relevant LLM post-training/self-distillation method with task adaptation; moderately novel context-separated adaptive anchoring. Controlled RQ diagnostics and ablations provide supporting evidence, but evaluation is limited to Qwen3 and two tasks, and exact code/hyperparameters are not shown.
evidence: Table 1 reports task acquisition across Qwen3-1.7B/4B/8B with SFT, GRPO, OPSD, SDS.
Table 2 reports capability preservation on Qwen3-4B for AIME24, MATH-500, ARC-Challenge.
Table 3 reports ablations isolating context separation, adaptive weighting, and endogenous scheduling.
Figure 2 reports teacher target-token accuracy under controlled prefix corruption and natural rollout binning.
Limitations states evaluation is confined to Qwen3 and two adaptation tasks.

arxiv:2608.07933.rationale: Highly relevant RAG/LLM knowledge-conflict work with training-free four-way attribution. The problem framing is moderately novel but largely a constrained evidence-classification layer over existing RAG conflict handling. Evaluation includes multiple datasets, baselines, ablations, cross-backbone checks, and attack budgets; however Track B is author-constructed/balanced and limitations acknowledge no natural-distribution or strict entity-level transfer. Evidence is moderately strong with quantified tables and a described statistical protocol, while full confidence intervals are relegated to supplement. Reproducibility is aided by detailed prompts/model settings but no code or data release is shown in the provided text.
evidence: Main Results: Table S2 reports EvoTrustRAG macro-F1 79.1% versus 72.2% for strongest baseline and Table S1 reports average accuracy 81.4%.
Ablation Study: Table S4 reports full-model F1 79.1 and drops to 72.0 without grounded transition, 75.3 without corroboration, and 74.7 without auxiliary consistency.
Limitations: states Track B is constructed under controlled label-specific procedures and does not represent natural distribution of conflict origins.
Implementation and cost: reports Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, E5-base-v2, K=10, thresholds, and latency values, supporting reproducibility but no code/data release.

arxiv:2608.07932.rationale: Moderately relevant as a multimodal/video language modeling paper, but not aligned with the highest-weight LLM/reasoning/agent topics. The method combines existing modules (OV-DINO, InternVL, LoRA, MPO) with an interleaved grounding fusion and action-aware supervision, offering incremental novelty. Evaluation has useful baselines and ablations, but is limited to synthetic 4-way MCQs on two sports datasets, with no error bars, no limitations section, no code/data release, and limited generalization evidence.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 1: SportsGrounder reports 51.8% Overall SoccerNet and 53.6% Overall FineSports, exceeding listed LoRA and prompt-injection baselines.
Section 4.3, Table 2: ablation shows IGF-only 47.2, +Action Supervision 48.9, +Preference Opt 49.6, and full SportsGrounder 51.8 on SoccerNet.
Section 4.1: implementation details include InternVL3.5-2B, OV-DINO, K=15, LoRA, three training stages, lambda=0.1, and AdamW with cosine decay.
Section 5 Conclusion: no limitations section appears; ablations are reported only on SoccerNet, limiting generalization evidence.

arxiv:2608.07931.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM reasoning, hallucination, abstention, and RLHF/GRPO alignment. The proposed REIN framework combines reflection-veracity and boundary-aware abstention rewards, but the core components are largely assembled from existing ideas. The paper provides detailed equations, ablations, and multiple benchmarks; however, internal data inconsistencies, particularly a duplicated base-model row in Appendix B Table 5, weaken confidence. Generalization is tested across several backbones and reasoning tasks, though training is limited to GSM8K and no statistical variation is reported.
evidence: Section 1 defines reasoning hallucination versus knowledge hallucination and states the contributions.
Section 3.3 and Equation 12 define the group-level boundary indicator B_K(x).
Table 1 reports Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B results, with REIN showing lower H-Proxy and higher Sel.Acc. across listed cells.
Table 2 provides a controlled component ablation on GSM8K for Qwen2.5-7B.
Appendix B Table 5 lists a DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B Base row identical to the Llama-3.1-8B Base row from Table 1, indicating a data duplication issue.
Appendix F Table 13 documents training hyperparameters.

arxiv:2608.07926.rationale: Moderate relevance as an LLM-based directed test-input generation method, but limited research quality: it is a work-in-progress with only four case studies, no baselines or ablations, and no released artifacts.
evidence: Section 3.1 reports four case studies from two projects with three successes and one failure, but no baselines or ablations.
Section 2.5 provides implementation details but no code/data or prompt-template availability.
Section 4.1 compares qualitatively to related work but lacks quantitative comparative evaluation.
Table 1 summarizes case-study results with a very small sample size.

arxiv:2608.07925.rationale: Strong relevance to LLM agents, tool use, code generation, and RAG; EDA is a domain setting but the methodology is language-model centered. Moderate novelty: execution-grounded EDA scripting and offline API self-exploration are domain-first but built on existing Cline/MCP patterns. Rigor is fair with baselines, ablations, and error analysis, though no statistical testing and the benchmark is not yet released. Evidence is quantitative from tables; generalizability is limited to EDA scripting, and reproducibility is constrained by promised rather than available code/benchmark.
evidence: Section 6.2, Table 3 reports ZhuLong Full Pass@1 78.5% vs Pure LLM 23.6% and RAG 32.3%; component ablation shows sandbox removal 37.3% and retrieval removal 34.2%.
Section 6.2.3, Tables 4-5 report self-exploration reduces average tool calls per trace by 22.1% and run_code calls by 27.0%.
Section 6.4, Table 8 reports interactive mode overall Pass@1 60.0% for PyAether and 50.0% for SKILL.

arxiv:2608.07924.rationale: Out-of-scope generative/drifting-model paper with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent language methodology. The Nesterov-inspired second-order extension is theoretically motivated but relevance to preferred topics is minimal; empirical validation is moderate with uneven baselines, no constant-damping ablation, and a minimal limitation section.
evidence: Abstract: claims Nesterov acceleration and one-step inference
Section 5.2 Table 2: MNIST FID comparison
Section 5.4 Table 4: robotics success rates
Section 6: limitation statement

arxiv:2608.07923.rationale: Low preference relevance: not an LLM/NLP, reasoning, agent, or safety paper; it only uses frozen CLIP/CLAP text encoders for open-vocabulary audio-visual event perception, so it matches multimodal AI weakly. Research quality is moderate: the false co-activation framing and sparse cross-modal prior exchange are reasonably novel, with formal analysis and multi-benchmark ablations, but baseline comparisons partly rely on reported values and are not paired by video, and no statistical significance tests are provided.
evidence: Section 4.2 reports SCoPE Stage 2 CLIP+CLAP Type@seg 51.25 vs AV2A 43.8 and Event@seg 39.74 vs 34.7.
Appendix B.2 notes the LLP comparison shares frozen encoders and vocabulary but is not paired by video.
Section 4.3 ablation shows target re-selection provides the clearest gain, with direct fusion trailing SCoPE by 6.61 Type@seg points.
Appendix B.1 lists solver configuration, external feature means, hyperparameters, and runtime protocol.

arxiv:2608.07922.rationale: Tangential relevance via reinforcement learning/sequential decision-making and memory constraints; otherwise outside the curator's LLM/NLP-centric preferences. Strong theory contribution within Lipschitz bandits, with formal upper/lower bounds and detailed appendices, but domain-specific and lacking code/experimental reproduction.
evidence: Abstract and Section 1 define the memory-batch Lipschitz bandit setting and claimed frontier.
Theorem 3.4 and Corollaries 3.6-3.7 state matched upper/lower bounds under the model.
Appendix B gives lower-bound proofs, including Lemma 4.3 routing obstruction and Proposition 4.4 low-memory obstruction.
Appendix D and Appendix E provide algorithmic upper-bound constructions and guarantees.

arxiv:2608.07921.rationale: Relevant transformer/LLM interpretability study using Marchenko-Pastur spectral decomposition with ablation validation. Moderate novelty for spatial outlier and cross-layer persistence analysis, and quantitative evidence is presented, but causal validation is limited: full outlier removal collapse is shown mainly for Mistral-7B, per-component strategies mix entry-outlier and random-bulk ablations, random bulk lacks seed averaging, and several models have omitted projections. Approximate MP threshold and limited controls further reduce rigor.
evidence: Table VI reports baseline and ablation accuracies, including Mistral-7B outlier removal reducing HellaSwag from .814 to .256 and MMLU from .627 to .269.
Table II reports average MP spectral outliers and energy ratios across models, showing Q dominance and reduced V outliers under GQA.
Section VII Limitations acknowledges approximate MP assumptions, lack of seed averaging for random bulk ablations, and limited Phi-3 projection coverage due to fused QKV weights.

arxiv:2608.07920.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM/VLM evaluation, red-teaming, and multimodal AI safety. The study has strong controlled conditions, including a matched-content label-only control and bootstrap CIs, but several net-effect CIs cross zero, Type B and Dataset B samples are small, the C7/C6 comparison is explicitly not content-matched, and artifact availability is not verifiable from the text.
evidence: Section 4.4 reports matched-content label-only control: broken-rate effect -0.17pp (95% CI [-0.68,0.35]).
Section 4.5 reports pooled differential-damage ratio 1.52x (95% CI [1.28,1.86]) for C7-wrong versus genuine wrong peer statements.
Section 4.6 reports LOO panel-consensus verification blocks 84.9% of fabricated attacks and reduces C7-wrong net harm from -20.3 to -0.50pp.
Section 6 Limitations notes Type B is small (49 rows) and Dataset B has 179 samples.

arxiv:2608.07917.rationale: Domain-specific OCR MLLM for Chinese historical documents using layout-aware blocking, tokenizer expansion, and transition tokens. Relevant mainly to low-to-medium preference topics such as multimodal AI, NLP, and SFT, but not to high-weight LLM reasoning/agent/safety topics. The paper provides extensive comparisons and ablations, but novelty is incremental, evaluation is limited to two Chinese historical OCR benchmarks, and test-split sensitivity tuning plus absent code limit rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 4.4, Table 4 reports M5HisDoc AR 93.76, NED 6.15, RO-ED 3.49 for TongGuOCR.
Section 4.5.1, Table 5 shows Block/Block training/inference outperforms Page/Page with AR 89.69 vs 83.50.
Section 4.5.2, Tables 7-8 support benefits of vocabulary expansion and transition modeling.
Section 5 states limitations regarding coverage of historical characters and dataset diversity.
Section 4.3 gives implementation details but no code availability beyond an online demo.

arxiv:2608.07916.rationale: Pure low-level computer vision demosaicing paper. It uses a frozen Qwen2.5-VL encoder only for task-instruction modulation and frozen DINOv2 for representation alignment, with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/prompting/RAG/agents/safety/alignment/evaluation methodology. Therefore it is out of scope and receives a score near the 0.20 cap; research quality is moderate with ablations and multiple backbones, but relevance weighting keeps the score low.
evidence: Abstract: 'Image demosaicing reconstructs a full-color image from incomplete color measurements produced by a sensor covered with a color filter array (CFA).'
§3.2: 'a frozen Qwen2.5-VL (2) encoder' is used only for cached task embeddings, not a language-model contribution.
§4.1: Experiments focus on LSDIR/COCO/SANet/MIT-Hard demosaicing benchmarks with EDMUNet, Restormer, and MambaIR backbones.

arxiv:2608.07915.rationale: Directly targets LLM KV-cache compression for long-context serving, making it highly relevant to LLM, long-context, and inference preferences. The method combines activation-weighted spectral low-rank factorization with reverse water-filling bit allocation, a meaningful but incremental unification of existing quantization/low-rank ideas. Rigor is limited by the omission of direct low-rank baselines such as Palu, the absence of RULER results despite an abstract claim mentioning RULER, no statistical significance testing, and only memory-capacity rather than end-to-end speedup validation. Quantitative evidence is extensive for LongBench and NIAH but confined to 7B/8B models and English tasks, with some NIAH results presented as figures without full numeric reporting. Reproducibility is comparatively strong due to a code link and detailed calibration/effective-compression accounting.
evidence: Abstract: claims near-lossless at 4x compression, competitive at 8x, and usable up to 12x on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B long-context benchmarks.
Section 4.1: evaluates on LongBench and NIAH; baselines are KIVI, TurboQuant, PolarQuant, OTT, and RotateKV, but no baselines are run for Qwen2.5-7B.
Table 1: Llama-3.1-8B LongBench average is 53.56 at 3.56x and 54.00 at 7.66x versus dense 53.24; SPECTRA remains 51.89 at 8.84x and 48.81 at 11.12x.
Section 6: states that turning saved memory into matching speedup is left to future work, and only memory capacity is validated.
Appendix F: calibration uses WikiText-2 windows, first 150 LongBench examples per task, and effective compression ratios include metadata such as scales and zero-points.

arxiv:2608.07914.rationale: Relevant to LLM evaluation and safety through benchmark contamination detection, but not core LLM architecture/capabilities. It adapts sparse-mixture detection into power-calibrated audits with careful negative results; novelty is modest. Formal theorems and predeclared gates support rigor, but empirical evidence is limited to small Pythia/GPT-Neo channels and SQuAD/Pile, with black-box/modern validation not run. Generalizability is constrained by assumptions and scale; no code/artifacts released, though protocol is detailed.
evidence: Abstract: formalizes behavioral contamination detection as a sparse mixture and defines efficacy
Section 6.2: reports Gaussian plug-in budget failure in 9/9 gate-passing channels and conservative finite-sample planner results
Limitations: states mixture channel is a modeling assumption, lists unexecuted black-box/modern validations, and notes the certificate never fires
Appendix M: provides detailed reproducibility protocol but explicitly does not release code or result artifacts

arxiv:2608.07913.rationale: Moderately relevant LLM/RAG selective-risk certification with strong theoretical rigor and transparent limitations, but incremental contribution and limited operational utility. Validates soundness but positive results are narrow or near-vacuous under privacy.
evidence: Abstract: 'We develop Fed-SRC, a score-agnostic certificate for federated, differentially private, adaptively monitored retrieval-augmented generation.'

§7: 'The primary target r*=0.10 certifies in no cell, privacy level, or policy... secondary target r*=0.20 likewise never certifies on RAGTruth... does certify on HaluEval question answering without privacy (200 of 200 trials).'

Limitations: 'Operational private utility is limited at the registered targets... The main privacy statement is event-level DP for one stream occurrence... not privacy for the 839 public support responses.'
Contributions: 'The contribution is this private federated anytime combination, not the contrast statistic or acceptance floor individually.'

arxiv:2608.07911.rationale: Directly relevant to MoE LLM serving, inference optimization, and caching, but not core language modeling or high-weight reasoning/agent topics. Methodologically strong with formal event-atomic replay, pre-registered criteria, and extensive ablations, though primarily trace-driven simulation on one main model limits generalizability.
evidence: Abstract: identifies replay semantics, workload contamination, and operating regimes; reports 84.3–96.6% future-victim share of offline-optimal gap.
§2.2 Definition 2: formalizes event-atomic replay and contrasts sequential replay.
§7.2 Table 14: reports admission share and future-victim share at B=8 and B=2.
§11 Limitations: states everything is trace-driven simulation and primary results rest on a single 128-expert model.
§13.1 Released artifacts: includes simulator, conformance trace, probe set, and pre-registration documents.

arxiv:2608.07905.rationale: Relevant LLM-based agent/planning paper, not pure robotics because LLM reasoning, graph prompting, and GRPO are central. Strengths include ablations and cross-environment tests, but limitations and code availability are absent, official leaderboard claim is not independently verifiable, and evaluation is simulation-only.
evidence: Section IV-A Table I reports GraphThink test unseen SR 68.52/GC 75.76 versus RoboGPT 62.00/72.09.
Section IV-B Table II ablations show removing replanning lowers valid unseen SR from 68.72 to 59.82.
Section IV-C2 Table IV shows removing GRPO drops long-horizon SR from 90.04 to 33.67.
Section IV-D Tables VI and VII report AI2-Thor new-task SR 80.50 versus RAG GPT-5.2 65.75 and VirtualHome adapted SR up to 93.00.

arxiv:2608.07904.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer-vision/image-diffusion application for industrial anomaly generation, with no LLM or language methodology; relevance is capped at 0.20. Within its domain, the paper provides a reasonable decoupling/recoupling framework with quantitative MVTec/VisA/Real-IAD comparisons and ablations, but lacks explicit limitations and statistical testing.
evidence: Section 5.3/Table 2 reports P-AP 68.0 vs AnoStyler 62.9 on MVTec AD
Section 5.4/Table 3 reports P-AP 41.5 vs 31.4/33.3 on VisA
Section 5.5/Table 4 ablation shows full method improves over base

arxiv:2608.07902.rationale: Topically relevant to AI safety and LLM chatbot evaluation, with a useful challenge to refusal-based safety metrics. However, it is a qualitative interview study rather than a technical contribution; evidence rests on 19 US practitioners and synthetic single-turn probes, with no quantitative benchmark comparisons or inter-rater reliability reported, limiting strength and generalizability.
evidence: Methods: semi-structured interviews with 19 practitioners working with youth; participants shown synthetic chatbot probes.
Findings: participants critiqued overlooked context, inappropriate refusal, and information presentation; supported resources/referrals and risk awareness.
Limitations: participants based in the United States; chatbot interactions were synthetic and single-turn.

Rigorous paired ablations, frozen blind holdout, bootstrap CIs, and artifact availability support the findings, but generalizability is limited by the primary synthetic delayed-binding mechanism and smaller external/second-mechanism validation.

arxiv:2608.07895.rationale: Out-of-scope robotics data curation/auditing under the pure-robotics exclusion; no core LLM/NLP methodology despite vision-language-action framing. Empirical evaluation is moderate and evidence is partly supported, but relevance cap applies.
evidence: Abstract and Section I define Instruction-Trajectory Mismatch auditing for multimodal robot demonstration datasets.
Table I and Table II report F1/AUROC/AUPRC results across LIBERO and real-robot benchmarks.
Table V provides ablations on the Bottle-mug benchmark, showing full MMPF F1 of 91.8.

arxiv:2608.07894.rationale: Relevant LLM/code embedding work, but mostly an incremental evaluation with a simple frozen LLM + LSTM aggregation method. Strengths include grouped CV, ablations, and quantitative comparisons; rigor is limited by test-set-based outer hyperparameter selection (Section IV-D), small/high-variance device-mapping evidence, and single-split algorithm classification.
evidence: Section III-D: chunked source/IR tokens are embedded by frozen pretrained LLMs and aggregated via separate LSTMs; the LLM is not fine-tuned.
Section IV-D, Table I: stratified NCV reports CodeLlama-7B 92.06 AMD / 88.38 NVIDIA, while LLMCompiler-13B reports 91.03 / 86.62.
Section IV-E, Table IV: LOGO NCV results are much lower (LLM 76.03 AMD / 50.88 NVIDIA), and the paper discusses test-set leakage in stratified CV.
Section V, Tables VII-VIII: algorithm classification reports LLMCompiler-13B error 1.54%, compared with FAIR 1.75% and OSCAR 1.92%.

arxiv:2608.07892.rationale: Directly targets LLM reasoning-model jailbreak defense, AI safety, red-teaming, and inference-time guardrails, so preference relevance is high. The capability-routing framing has some novelty but reuses known components. Quantitative ASR/FPR comparisons against baselines and ablations are reported, but rigor and reproducibility are limited by missing sample sizes, statistical testing, full implementation details, code/data availability, and some citation/reporting inconsistencies.
evidence: Abstract: States CRG mitigates reasoning-centric jailbreaks while preserving benign utility.

Experiments: Evaluates CRG against five reasoning-centric jailbreak families using HarmBench/AdvBench and two primary target LRMs (Gemini 2.5 Pro, ChatGPT o4-mini), with XSTest/MT-Bench for benign utility.
Table 1: Reports HarmBench/Gemini 2.5 Pro ASR reductions, e.g., CoT-Hijacking from 100% to 12% and FicDetail from 97% to 0%.
Analysis and Discussion: Provides component ablations, extractor sensitivity, open-weight generalization, and adaptive attack analysis.
Experiments: Does not report sample sizes or confidence intervals for ASR/FPR results, and the document provides no code/data availability statement.

arxiv:2608.07891.rationale: Domain-specific applied text-classification pipeline for legislative testimony; only weakly aligned with NLP/transformer preferences and not LLM-focused. Standard feature engineering plus XGBoost/BERT makes the contribution application-specific. Weak heuristic labels and a tiny, non-comparable BERT gold evaluation limit evidence strength; no significance testing or code/data release is provided.
evidence: Methodology, Section 3.2: labels are generated by a name-matching heuristic; positives 23,766 and negatives 26,201.
Results, Table 2: Decision Tree F1 0.9323, XGBoost F1 0.9747, XGBoost+BERT F1 0.9782.
Results, Section 4.1: standalone BERT is evaluated on only 39 manually labeled utterances and is explicitly not directly comparable to the weak-label test set.
Discussion, Section 5.2: future work acknowledges weak labels, the need for larger manually labeled data, and unbalanced-data experiments.

arxiv:2608.07890.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM/MoE efficiency and PEFT. The paper contributes an empirical extension of a prior router-sensitivity criterion, with controlled module, rank, and perturbation-geometry sweeps. Novelty is moderate, rigor and evidence are reasonable but limited by unmatched budgets across adapter families, cross-paper confounds, and single main model family for controlled sweeps. Reproducibility is strong with released code, checkpoints, and full configurations.
evidence: Abstract reports Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct baseline 44.83% MMLU-Pro and router-only LoRA training 0.002% of parameters retaining 27.54% with half the experts removed.
Section 5 Table 1 shows router-only LoRA outperforming all-module LoRA at matched rank under pruning.
Section 6 Table 2 reports monotonic improvement in pruned MMLU-Pro as LoRA rank increases.
Section 8.3 Table 7 reports Qwen1.5-MoE transfer retaining 49.7% mean mathematics accuracy with half the experts removed while random collapses to 4.4%.
Section 11 explicitly discusses limitations, including single model family for controlled sweeps, unmatched adaptation budgets, and open questions.

arxiv:2608.07887.rationale: Pure soft-robotic grasping study of a mixed-stiffness fingertip for coin pickup. It is out-of-scope as pure robotics/domain application with no language, LLM, NLP, agent, or multimodal methodology, so relevance is minimal. The paper has some experimental controls, statistical comparisons, and open materials, but tested only coins with one independently fabricated finger pair and limited isolation of stiffness patterning from overall stiffness.
evidence: Abstract: 'We fabricated anthropomimetic fingertips with Shore E10 silicone at the center and Shore A60 at the sides, and compared them with uniformly soft E10 fingertips.'
Methods: 'Ten trials were conducted per condition and recorded as binary outcomes; partial completion was classified as a failure.'
Results: 'The nail-free pair failed to form a geometric constraint in all 36 conditions.'
Discussion: 'Only one independently fabricated finger pair was tested for each condition, so between-specimen reproducibility remains unknown.'

Data Availability: 'The materials supporting this study are publicly available in the GitHub repository ... include Video S1, the source code and data used for the statistical analyses, the Arduino control source code, 3D CAD files, and 3D-printable part files.'

arxiv:2608.07886.rationale: Relevant to multimodal vision-language grounding and uses a pretrained VLM backbone, but not core LLM/reasoning/agent methodology. Novelty is moderate: bidirectional correspondence and bridge tokens reframe existing grounding/object-query ideas. Rigor is moderate: broad baselines and ablations are reported, but no significance testing and some future/proprietary model details are unverifiable. Evidence from Tables 1-3 and appendix supports the reported improvements, though no statistical validation is provided. Generalizability is moderate across caption, referring, and category inputs but tied to Qwen3.5 and curated benchmarks. Reproducibility is limited by unspecified code/data release and future/proprietary model baselines.
evidence: Abstract reports ConCor-1 improves correspondence F1 by 48% on COCONut-PanCap and 29% on zero-shot LVIS.
Table 1 reports image-caption results across COCONut-PanCap, GroundedRef, and Flickr30k with JointF1 88.8, 70.3, and 91.4 for ConCor-1.
Table 3 reports ablations for scoring function, segmentation head, attention, vision feature, and bridge token assignment.
Appendix A discloses limitations, including mask quality behind specialized models and dependence on correspondence-style supervision.

arxiv:2608.07885.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM reasoning, agentic tool use, prompting, and inference efficiency. The amortization framing is a useful incremental contribution, but rigor is limited by single distillation runs, three-seed evaluation only, narrow model/domain coverage, and no statistical significance testing. Evidence is quantitative but partly speculative for mechanisms.
evidence: Abstract claims skills recover 55%-100%+ of the reasoning gap for GPT-5.4-mini while emitting 2.7-6x fewer output tokens.
Table 1 reports benchmark-level scores and token reductions for think, no-think, and no-think+skill conditions.
Section 5.2 ablation shows mixed distillation-source results, including SSB-Verified no-think-only 0.560 vs paired 0.460.
Section 7 states skills were distilled once per model-domain pair and distillation variance was not measured.

arxiv:2608.07881.rationale: Centrally uses LLM prompting and transformer-based semantic encoding for mixed tabular clustering, matching LLM, prompting, transformer, training, and efficiency preferences; not a pure domain application. Novelty is moderate: the attribute-value-level one-shot grounding and dual-view consistency are sensible but combine known components. Rigor is decent with formal complexity and broad ablations, though some table inconsistencies and limited batch assumptions temper confidence. Evidence is mostly quantitative with multiple datasets, metrics, and robustness checks.
evidence: Abstract: proposes GRACE as an LLM-grounded framework for scalable mixed-data clustering with one-shot attribute-value semantic grounding.
Section III-B defines the 4P LLM querying strategy and transformer encoder f_theta for attribute-value descriptions.
Table III reports ARI/NMI/ACC across 13 categorical/reconstructed datasets with GRACE average rank 1.15-1.69.
Table IV reports mixed-dataset results with GRACE average rank 1.18-1.55 across metrics.
Section IV-C ablation isolates semantic representation and dual-view neighborhood consistency contributions.
Section IV-E reports LLM backend robustness with Friedman p=0.41 for GRACE and p=0.96 for GRACE-A.

arxiv:2608.07876.rationale: Out-of-scope surgical robotics/medical computer vision application without language-model or NLP methodology; matches only low-weight Robotics, Medical, CV, and Transformer topics. The method is an incremental domain-specific perception-to-control system using frozen DINOv3, spatial attention, latent memory, and RCM control, not a general AI/ML contribution. Experiments include benchmark comparisons, ablations, and ex vivo robotic validation, but lack statistical significance testing and in vivo evidence; code availability is claimed but unverified.
evidence: Table I reports IoU 0.604 and MCE 41.24 on SurgAtt-SZPH plus cross-domain SurgAtt-AutoLaparo and SurgAtt-Hamlyn results.
Section V-D Tables II-IV provide ablations for spatial prior, latent memory, heatmap decoding, and loss components.
Section V-C reports ex vivo robotic validation with improved IoU/smoothness versus SurgAtt-Tracker.
Section V-A3 claims code and video demo availability at a URL, which cannot be verified from the document.

arxiv:2608.07874.rationale: Out-of-scope network science/contagion-dynamics paper on harmful information spread with adaptive hypergraphs. No LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent/RAG or AI-safety model methodology; only tangential harmful-information domain. Theoretical derivations and simulations appear internally coherent, but relevance to AI/ML preferences is negligible and final score is capped low.
evidence: Opening summary: proposes an adaptive higher-order contagion model integrating platform-induced group dissolution and user rewiring.
Section 2.1: defines infection, dissolution, and rewiring rates on hypergraphs.
Section 3.1: compares theory and Gillespie simulations on synthetic 3-uniform hypergraphs with phase diagrams.
Section 3.2: validates findings on an empirical high school contact hypergraph.
Declarations: states real hypergraph data are openly available and code is available at GitHub.

arxiv:2608.07873.rationale: Relevant to LLM agents, tool use, code generation, and benchmark evaluation for spreadsheet tasks. The reverse-engineering of real workbooks and multi-level query design is somewhat novel, and quantitative results, failure analysis, and re-run standard deviations provide moderate evidence. However, rigor is limited by author-only human annotation, LLM-generated queries/necessity scores, absence of statistical significance tests for main comparisons, and reliance on unverified URLs/model specifications. Generalizability is moderate due to only 150 curated tasks from two English corpora.
evidence: Section 8, Table 3 reports model/API comparisons with Hard and Soft scores.
Section 5 describes WTM-Bench as a balanced 150-task evaluation subset.
Appendix G reports independent Python re-runs with standard deviations and failure taxonomy.
Appendix B reports a 3-annotator quality evaluation with inter-annotator agreement correlations.

arxiv:2608.07871.rationale: Pure domain geospatial poverty mapping using Google Places POI and ML regressors; no LLM/NLP, transformer, agent, reasoning, or language methodology. Although the paper has moderate domain-level rigor (spatial validation, bootstrap, interpretable decomposition), it is out of scope for the stated preferences, and the weighted score is capped accordingly.
evidence: Section 2.3.1 describes the buffered spatial train/validation/test split and income-bias check.
Section 3.1 reports held-out R2=0.646 (95% CI 0.62-0.67) for NMF K=50 GBR.
Section 4.1 notes limitations including São Paulo-only scope, temporal mismatch between 2026 POI and 2022 census, and informal-economy gaps.
Data Availability Statement claims a GitHub repository for code/data.

arxiv:2608.07870.rationale: Out-of-scope visual continuous-control RL architecture paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology; only tangential preference overlap via reinforcement learning and robotics. The work adapts Simba to visual RL with ablations and benchmarks, but is incremental and domain-specific, so overall score is capped at the out-of-scope maximum.
evidence: Section 5.2/Figures 5-8: reports benchmark comparisons across DMC, Adroit, and Meta-World over 5 seeds.
Table 1/Section 5.3: ablation study across normalization, residual, weight decay, and value-learning components over 3 seeds.
Appendix 8/Table 2: full hyperparameter list; abstract provides public code repository.

arxiv:2608.07867.rationale: Out-of-scope multimodal affective computing/emotion recognition application with no language/LLM/agent methodology; graph-based modality negotiation and weak-label calibration do not align with core preferences. Experimental comparisons and ablations are present, but the domain mismatch caps relevance and overall score at a low level.
evidence: Experiments and Results, Main Results: reports CONFER LOSO accuracy/F1 of 0.873/0.879 on AMIGOS-V and 0.854/0.783 on MAHNOB-V, with paired Wilcoxon p<0.05.
Ablation Study, Table 5: removing negotiation, sender reliability, or receiver concession degrades LOSO performance.

arxiv:2608.07864.rationale: Out-of-scope industrial anomaly generation using diffusion models, with no LLM/language methodology. The paper has ablations and benchmark results, but target preference relevance is minimal, so the overall score is capped at low relevance.
evidence: Section 4.1 introduces Error-Suppressed Multi-Scale Training with Multi-Scale Cropping, Joint-Scale loss, and Cross-Scale Perception loss.
Tables 1 and 2 report quantitative generation and downstream detection results on VisA and MVTec AD 2.
Appendix B reports small-scale subset evaluation comparing IS(a), IC-L(a), AUROC, AP, and F1-max.

arxiv:2608.07863.rationale: Moderately relevant as a VQA/VLM application to AI-generated image detection rather than core LLM/NLP methodology. The triple-branch design has incremental novelty over prior VLM-based detectors. Evaluation is broad but rigor is limited by unfair baseline settings (some official pretrained models), accuracy-only metrics, and no explicit limitations or uncertainty analysis.
evidence: Table I reports LHSDet average ACC 96.41% versus 87.04% for AEROBLADE; Table II reports 95.09% versus 84.24%.
Section IV-E ablations show removing the high-level branch drops average ACC to 58.73%, and removing LoRA drops it to 93.58%.
Table III reports LHSDet robustness average drop 3.27%, higher than DIRE at 1.55% and AntifakePrompt at 2.86%.

arxiv:2608.07862.rationale: Strong topical fit with LLM safety evaluation and multilingual NLP, though not Japanese-focused. The benchmark fills a real Indic-language gap but follows prior localized safety-evaluation methodology, limiting novelty. Evaluation scale is substantial (27 LLMs, 10 languages, PoLL judges), but dataset construction relies on one annotator per language and manual validation is narrow (Malayalam only) with only 69.2% LLM-judge/human agreement and weaker alignment for subtle sociocultural harms, capping rigor and evidence strength. Generalizability beyond Indic is asserted but untested. Reproducibility is decent due to released code/data, model URLs, decoding parameters, and vLLM details.
evidence: §4.4 Results reports combined safety pass rates and model rankings
§4.4 Manual Evaluation reports 69.2% PoLL-human alignment
§3.1 Data Collection and Verification describes one native speaker per regional context and PoLL filtering
§4.1 LLM Response Collection lists decoding parameters and vLLM inference
Table 3 reports alignment by harm type

arxiv:2608.07861.rationale: Directly relevant to multimodal VLM/VQA benchmarking with efficiency and evaluation implications; strong match to Multimodal AI and Inference/Efficiency preferences but not core LLM methodology. Novelty is incremental as a systematic benchmark rather than a technique. Rigor is moderate: large API-call count and controlled tokenization experiments, but some datasets are very small (DriVQA N=24) and no statistical significance/CI reporting. Evidence is quantitative but largely observational. Generalizability is limited by proprietary API snapshots and provider-specific accounting. Reproducibility is partially supported by protocol/package details and code URL, but depends on commercial API access and unverified artifacts.
evidence: Abstract: evaluates 12 preprocessing techniques across three VQA datasets and four commercial VLMs, totaling 95,168 API calls.
Table V: reports VQA soft accuracy by preprocessing technique and model on VQA-MHUG.
Table IV: reports token usage decomposition per request by preprocessing technique and provider.
Appendix C-A: describes provider-dependent tokenization and model-specific accounting rules.
Section III-D: defines task-specific accuracy metrics including VQA soft accuracy and LLM-judge rubrics.

arxiv:2608.07859.rationale: Well-developed preferential Bayesian optimization paper, but outside the stated LLM/NLP-centric preferences. The proposed prior-weighted Hessian correction is moderately novel within PBO, with formal propositions and a large benchmark study; however, relevance is low, generalizability is limited beyond PBO, and no code release is indicated.
evidence: Section 1 Contributions C1-C4 state the rank-deficiency analysis, KappaSharp correction, adaptive variant, and 11-benchmark evaluation.
Section 6.1 Setup reports 11 benchmarks, 5 initializations, 60 seeds, and 16,500 total runs.
Table 1 compares Adaptive KS against Static KS, Fixed20, Connected Querying, and baseline with percentage gains and significance tests.
Appendix B Table 2 ablations show Uniform jitter 0W/5L and indicate MAP correction is the main source of improvement.
Section 7 Discussion notes limitations including empirically chosen threshold and oracle-simulated preferences.

arxiv:2608.10010.rationale: Relevant LLM-efficiency/quantization work targeting language-model training and inference. The rational-radix logarithmic curve format extends LNS/APoT with closed product arithmetic and a phase count, which is moderately novel but incremental. Rigor is reasonable: matched protocols, ablations, paired GEMM diagnostics, and statistical caveats are present, though pretraining is limited to 128M-parameter models on 3B tokens and the hardware evidence is a preliminary tile only. Evidence is mostly parity rather than superiority, and reproducibility is only partially supported by protocol details without a clear code artifact link.
evidence: Section 4.2 and Figure 2 report CurveFP7 E3C3 at G64 beats tensorwise FP8 and stays within 1.32% of native perplexity on Llama-3-8B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3.5-9B, and Falcon-H1-7B.

Table 4 in Section 4.5 reports BF16-inference perplexity 22.5366 for CurveFP8 versus 22.5407 for FP8, with lower format-induced penalty in every seed and explicitly notes statistical parity rather than superiority.

Section 5 and Table 6 report a preliminary Nangate45 4x4 tile at 500 MHz: CurveFP8 P0 area 49,282.9 um^2 versus FP8 P1 51,646.8 um^2, while excluding memory/interconnect/system effects and measuring one physical seed.

arxiv:2608.07857.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/CT lung nodule application; no LLM, Japanese NLP, transformer language methodology, agents, or other preferred topics. Some interpretability and evaluation rigor exist, but domain application cap applies at <=0.20.
evidence: {'section': 'Abstract', 'claim': 'Study develops concept bottleneck models for lung nodule malignancy prediction from CT foundation-model embeddings rather than language-model methodology.'}
{'section': 'Results', 'claim': 'Concept-plus-size models achieved external AUROC 0.72-0.73, similar to nodule size alone, with modest concept fidelity.'}

arxiv:2608.07855.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM agents and KV-cache inference. The commit-transition lifecycle idea is moderately novel but evaluated mainly against generic KV baselines rather than cited agent-specific methods. Benchmarks and ablations are reported but lack significance testing, variance, or code release.
evidence: Table 1 reports accuracy across eight datasets and three model backbones at a 4096-token budget.
Table 2 reports Qwen3-14B accuracy at 2048 and 8192 token budgets.
Table 3 reports ablations on GAIA, GPQA, and Bamboogle for Qwen3-14B.
Figure 3 reports peak KV-cache memory and wall-clock time for Qwen3-14B on GAIA, xbench-DeepSearch, and GPQA.
Section 4.1 lists six backbones and the baselines FullKV, SnapKV, R-KV, and TriAttention.

arxiv:2608.07852.rationale: Highly relevant LLM interpretability study using sparse autoencoders, residual-stream steering, and persona/speaker representations. Strengths include human validation of LLM-judged steering effects, random-direction controls, and Llama replication, but evidence depends partly on heuristic filtering and an LLM judge, generalizability is constrained to English emotional synthetic interactions and few personas, and code/data release is not stated.
evidence: Section 3.1.1 Feature Taxonomy reports filtered feature counts and metaclass distributions at L9/L17/L22.
Section 3.3.1 Immersive Simulation Mode reports Table 1 with activation metrics for features 4360 and 133 across settings.
Appendix C reports steerinterp precision 0.90, recall 0.98, human agreement 93%, and Cohen's kappa 0.85.
Appendix G reports replication on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for four central claims.

arxiv:2608.07851.rationale: Relevant to LLM/Transformer parameter efficiency, but evaluation is small-scale and lacks statistical rigor; the tensorized routing idea is incremental over existing tensorized LLM components and results rely on one backbone/dataset.
evidence: Abstract reports TEMPER-Tucker CORE 0.206 at n=8 with 1.93M additional parameters versus 11.95M for mHC.
Section 5 describes nanochat backbone with D=12 blocks, d=768, context length 2048, ClimbMix-400B data, 4xA100 GPUs, and 6,000/7,000 training steps.
Table 1 reports baseline comparisons for n=4/n=8 with parameter counts, train loss, val BPB, and CORE.
Section 5.4 reports ablations including frozen Tucker core, Tensor Train variant, tensorizing only Wres, and CP rank sweep.

arxiv:2608.07848.rationale: Pure computer-vision/infrared-polarization image fusion with no language methodology; only tangential Mamba/SSM and CV keyword relevance. Method is incremental with attention/mask/wavelet modules; evaluation uses a 10-pair test set, lacks statistical significance, and provides limited training details; code availability is claimed but unverified.
evidence: Section 3.1: proposes IRPol-Fuse with PAF, IHJ, PTJ, and cross-modal Mamba interaction.
Section 3.6: LI-PI has 110 pairs, split 90/10/10; independent test set is 10 pairs.
Section 4.2, Table 1: reports best global metrics on LI-PI, but margins over TIPFNet/DT-F are small.
Section 4.2, Table 2: region-aware metrics show first on Pol Grad Corr/MAE and second-best IR CNR.
Section 4.4, Tables 5-6: M3FD/MSRS generalization shows competitive but not uniformly best results.
Section 4.6, Table 8: high computational cost reported at 2608.007 G FLOPs and 515.279 ms.

arxiv:2608.07846.rationale: Out of scope: the paper is a case study of decentralized identity and verifiable credentials, with no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, multimodal, or other preferred ML/AI methodology. It is a working paper with no quantitative experiments; operational metrics are explicitly deferred and the adversary model is informal, limiting evidence strength and reproducibility.
evidence: Page 1 Working Paper notice: operational metrics including DID issuance volume and latency will be added in a future revision once authorization is received.
Page 1 Abstract: describes China RealDID as verifiable credentials and decentralized identifiers, not LLM/NLP/ML research.
Page 3 Section 1: contributions are security architecture, policy and regulatory analysis, and generalizability.
Page 8 Section 3.0: adversary model is informal; a fully game-based treatment is out of scope.
Page 40 Competing Interests: author discloses material interest; no empirical results are reported.

arxiv:2608.07838.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM grounded reasoning, factuality/RAG, and evaluation. The counterfactual multi-structure benchmark and ORLF components are moderately novel but largely combine existing ideas. Quantitative tables, ablations, and sensitivity analyses provide evidence, though no significance testing/confidence intervals and some claimed improvements are not fully supported. Generalizability is limited to English Wikipedia/Wikidata and fine-tuned open backbones; replication is supported by hyperparameters/prompts but repository claim is unverified.
evidence: Section 3 defines TKFQA statistics and evaluation metrics
Table 2 reports SOTA LLM EM/RCA and order standard deviation
Table 4 reports ORLF baselines across four backbones
Table 5 reports ablation results across four backbones
Section 7 Limitations notes English/Wikipedia/Wikidata scope and closed-source API restriction

arxiv:2608.07835.rationale: Pure cross-view geo-localization/computer-vision and robotics paper with no LLM, NLP, or language-method relevance; explicitly out of scope and capped at 0.20. Internal experiments, ablations, and benchmark tables are present, but relevance to the target areas is minimal.
evidence: Table 2 reports recall improvements for OrienterNet, OSMLoc, and RHO with SeqLoc on CV-FSS and CV-RHO.
Table 5 ablates MGR, ETU, and PAS contributions on the Overgaard region.
Supplementary Table 10 reports robustness to noisy odometry on Neuanspach.

arxiv:2608.07834.rationale: Out-of-scope visualization perception paper; no LLM/NLP/agent methodology. Uses vision-science image-statistics models rather than language modeling, with only passing mention of LLMs/multimodal models in related work. Limited proof-of-concept on scatterplot correlation perception.
evidence: §1.3 mentions CNNs and multimodal/LLM-based chart QA only as related work
§3.2 reports model-human JND comparison for scatterplots

arxiv:2608.07827.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/confidence-calibration study on mathematical QA and reasoning trajectories. Empirical comparison is systematic, with multi-model/dataset tables and bootstrap CIs, but contributions are incremental and generalizability is constrained to open-weight models and verifiable math QA.
evidence: Section 6.1 reports five open-weight models and three math QA datasets (GSM8K, GSMHard, SVAMP).
Table 2 and Appendix D Table 7 report ECE/MCE/Brier with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals; sequence-based estimators generally achieve lower ECE than answer-based estimators.
Table 3 and Appendix D Table 8 report post-hoc calibration results for isotonic regression and Platt scaling, showing substantial in-domain ECE reductions.
Limitations acknowledges restricted open-weight models, mathematical QA focus, MC Dropout design choices, and regex-based answer extraction concerns.

arxiv:2608.08160.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM agents and LLM evaluation: formalizes Narrative Commitment Preservation and introduces NCP-Bench for long-horizon consistency under adversarial player interventions. The contribution is moderately novel in making facts, commitments, and trajectory progress explicit and checkable. Quantitative multi-model results are supported by tables and ablations, but evaluation relies substantially on LLM auditors with only partial human validation and no full benchmark-wide human baseline, limiting rigor and evidence strength. Reproducibility is decent due to released code/data/prompts and detailed prompts/algorithm.
evidence: Abstract: reports GPT-5.2 survival rate 42% after 20 turns, fact conflict rates 40-68%, and isolated runs satisfying achievement commitments.
Table 1: main results across six models with average turns, trajectory progress, satisfied commitments, and fact/commitment/player-input conflict breakdown.

Section 5.4 Auditor Model Sensitivity: three auditor backbones show broadly similar conflict profiles and high pairwise correlations, with human review of 100 GPT-4o-mini final results disputing only 4 fact-conflict false positives.
Section 5.5 Comparison with Memory-Augmented Agents: HiAgent extends average turns and reduces commitment conflicts but does not solve the benchmark.
Appendix B Human Narrator Baseline: human narrator resolves all 19 adversarial interventions on Iron Man, reaching 13/13 trajectory nodes and 7/12 commitments, suggesting task solvability.
Section 6 Limitations: acknowledges LLM auditor imperfections, provider-side nondeterminism, and restriction to linear narratives.

arxiv:2608.08119.rationale: Out-of-scope pure time-series domain application; only tangential relevance through time-series foundation-model adapters (Lag-Llama, Time-MoE) and transfer evaluation, with no LLM/NLP or language methodology. The toolbox offers modular integration and public code, but no new similarity method; results in Section 5 are modest correlational evidence without significance tests or explicit limitations.
evidence: Section 5 reports Pearson correlations between dataset similarity and downstream task loss on 25 GluonTS datasets.
Table 2 shows no similarity metric consistently achieves highest correlation across tasks, with correlations often weak to moderate.
Section 4 describes the modular Data, Similarity, Evaluation, and Analysis layers and public code availability.

arxiv:2608.08107.rationale: Strong LLM and multimodal relevance via language-preserving MLLM tuning. The neuron-aware plasticity allocation is moderately novel relative to existing replay, architectural, and merging methods. Multi-backbone experiments and ablations provide solid quantitative support, though no statistical significance/error bars are reported and generalization is limited to vision-language adaptation and moderately sized transformers. Reproducibility is aided by pseudocode, hyperparameters, and baseline details but no code release is claimed.
evidence: §5.2.1, Tables 1-2: NeuPAT recovers language average to 49.06 vs 43.92 for vanilla tuning, while multimodal average is comparable (61.05 vs 60.98).
§5.2.2, Table 3 and Appendix D.2: Results generalize across Qwen3-0.6B, Phi-4-Mini, Qwen2.5-7B/14B, and Llama3.1-8B.
§5.2.3, Tables 4-6: Ablations compare global update schemes, allocation strategies, and role-specific update constraints.
§7 Limitations: Notes unverified larger backbones, other modalities, and sequential/continual learning.
Appendix A and C: Provides Algorithm 1, training configurations, probing set construction, and baseline implementation details.

arxiv:2608.07825.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application: uses generative/agentic AI for indie game development and market analysis, with no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/prompting/RAG/safety methodology. Tangential agentic-AI/MCP mentions do not establish topical relevance. Research quality is moderate but constrained by proprietary single-platform logs, self-selected users, author conflict, verified-subsample control selection issues, and many argued-not-measured claims.
evidence: Abstract: frames the study around AI in indie game development and market dynamics, not language-model methods.
§4.1.1: reports mean 5.1 minutes and $0.27–0.58 per generated production plan, measuring only a planning artifact.
§4.4.2/Table 17: disclosed-vs-control comparison is bounded by a favorably selected control group and cannot identify a causal quality effect.

arxiv:2608.07824.rationale: Multi-agent RL freight-routing application matches the RL/MARL preference, but it is a pure domain application without language methodology and is therefore capped to low relevance. The work is a modest synthetic single-network IPPO/MAPPO comparison with reasonable ablations and metrics, but limited generalizability and no code/data release.
evidence: Abstract: reports IPPO throughput +12.7%, MAPPO RI=0.811, and no single policy dominating across throughput, delay, and Resilience Index.
Section 5.2: baselines RRN and MCH use privileged network state while learned policies observe only an 83-dimensional normalized vector.
Section 6.2: IPPO throughput 262,090 vs RRN 232,636 vs MCH 250,266; deterministic ablation drops throughput to 208,602.
Section 6.6: limitations include 15-hub synthetic network, exploratory 5-seed kappa sweep, and informational asymmetry.

arxiv:2608.07822.rationale: Pure computer-vision/quantum-ML benchmark with no LLM, NLP, language-model, reasoning, agent, or language-methodology content; therefore out of scope for the stated curation preferences. The empirical controlled comparison is somewhat novel and includes quantitative results and statistical tests, but conclusions are explicitly bounded to shallow VQCs on classical vision tasks, limiting generalizability.
evidence: Abstract: quaternion classifiers retain 94-97% of real-valued performance on CIFAR-10 and outperform shallow VQCs on classical vision benchmarks.
Table 2: QuatNet exceeds Quantum-NoEnt/Quantum-Ent across reported datasets, with product-state quantum gaps of 2.4-6.1 percentage points.
Robustness across seeds and sample sizes: Friedman test reports chi^2=12.796 and p=0.0051 for the five-seed MNIST ordering.
Scope, limitations, and future directions: authors state conclusions are bounded to shallow, measurement-limited VQCs on classical image-classification tasks without intrinsic quantum structure.

arxiv:2608.07816.rationale: The paper proposes centroid-based token initialization for LLM-based generative recommendation and diagnoses popularity bias in standard random SID initialization. It is relevant to LLM training/efficiency but domain-specific and lacks direct comparisons with prior SID alignment methods. Experiments span five datasets and multiple Qwen3 scales, with diagnostics, ablations, and theory supporting claims, though without error bars or statistical tests and no released code.
evidence: Section 3.1, Figure 2: after CPT+SFT, random-initialized SID embeddings show low neighborhood purity compared to original semantic embeddings.
Section 4.2, Table 2: centroid initialization reduces popularity variance captured by leading PCs and increases semantic variance relative to random initialization.
Section 5.1, Table 3: centroid initialization improves pure-SFT Recall@5 on Beauty from 0.044 to 0.051 and reduces peak optimizer step from 6989 to 4193.
Appendix B, Table 6: detailed hyperparameters and prompts support reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.07814.rationale: Core LLM MoE compression/efficiency topic with direct relevance. Novelty is incremental over prior delta-decomposition and merging/pruning but motivated by local dominants and permutation alignment. Quantitative results exist, but absolute degradation versus uncompressed models is large, main tables lack variance, and calibration speedup claims omit absolute costs; no code release or full hyperparameters.
evidence: Table 4 reports Qwen3-30B-A3B PPL/downstream results at ~50% expert compression; uncompressed PPL=8.50 vs best LorExperts M_soft PPL=11.99 at 40.6% compression.
Table 5 reports Gemma-4-26B-A4B results where Freq-Prune PPL=11.57 is lower than LorExperts M_soft PPL=13.32 at 41.4%, though LorExperts leads MMLU/ARC-C.
Section 6.2 claims stage factor fitting can be reduced from ~500 gradient steps to one whitened SVD (~100x) but says absolute wall-clock times are omitted.
Limitations states calibration is dominated by per-member SVD and reconstruction, and the closed-form activation-weighted solve is not yet the default.
Appendix A Table 6 reports BTExperts tree vs flat decomposition match within noise on Mixtral-8x7B, supporting quality-neutral inference amortization.

arxiv:2608.07813.rationale: Central LLM evaluation/reasoning/RAG paper with a useful judge-authority framing, negative results, and strong reproducibility plan; limited by single-seed small-scale evidence and borderline statistics.
evidence: Section 6.1, Table 2 reports EL-DGR 58.2% GSM8K vs scalar judge 56.8% and majority 55.8%; HotpotQA 17.33 EM vs 15.67 and 15.33.
Section 6.2, Table 3 reports on n=30 frozen-rule split: scalar judge 10.0 EM vs majority 20.0 and EL-DGR 26.7.
Section 7, Table 4 reports corrected HotpotQA channel-drop ablations with every drop vs full exact McNemar p=1.0.
Appendix C states code, per-question predictions, verifier prompts, timing logs, and bootstrap/McNemar scripts are released, with the frozen candidate pool distributed.

arxiv:2608.07812.rationale: Moderate relevance: the paper directly concerns foundation models/LLMs, reasoning, prompting, interpretability, and evaluation, but as a conceptual cognitive-science methodology rather than an LLM/ML technical or empirical contribution. Novelty is incremental, mostly formalizing prior guidance into a four-stage framework and linking-hypothesis analysis. Rigor is moderate for a perspective with structured arguments and acknowledged limitations, but there are no quantitative results, baselines, ablations, or original experiments. Evidence is citation-based rather than experimental. Generalizability is conceptually broad across cognitive tasks and models. Reproducibility is low with no code, data, or experimental procedure.
evidence: Abstract: proposes a four-stage framework for evaluating foundation models as cognitive and developmental models.
Section 2: details four stages: task adaptation, linking hypothesis specification, correspondence evaluation, and contrastive model comparison.
Section 3: analyzes linking hypotheses including similarity, surprisal, prompting, and process-trace.
Section 4: lists challenges such as theoretical underdetermination, mechanistic opacity, training/developmental mismatch, and variability.
Section 5: provides guidelines including diagnostic contrasts, task fidelity, triangulation, comparative evaluation, and mechanistic follow-up.

arxiv:2608.07810.rationale: Agent-based social simulation of convention tipping; only marginal topical match to the 'Agents & Tool Use' preference via multi-agent/ABM terminology, with no LLM/language methodology. arxiv:2608.07808.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM security, prompt injection, jailbreaking, and agentic safety. evidence: Abstract states the paper formalizes a seven-component model spanning carrier, delivery vector, concealment, context-break, privilege escalation, payload, and return channel.

arxiv:2608.07795.rationale: Low topical fit: conformal prediction for multimodal regression with frozen embeddings, no LLM/NLP/agentic/safety methodology; only weak Multimodal AI keyword alignment. arxiv:2608.07786.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM weight-space analysis and provenance, with a clear hierarchy of lineage regimes and controlled data-scale/algorithmic ablations. arxiv:2608.07772.rationale: Pure RL sample-complexity theory under mu-resets. It matches the reinforcement-learning preference only tangentially and lacks LLM/NLP/agent relevance. arxiv:2608.07725.rationale: The paper is directly within the stated reinforcement-learning preference, presenting finite-sample regret lower-bound certificates for average-reward MDPs. arxiv:2608.07713.rationale: This is a pure medical-image generative modeling study of tokenizer-generator coupling on ChestMNIST/PneumoniaMNIST/OrganAMNIST, with no language-model, NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, or agent methodology. arxiv:2608.07712.rationale: Out-of-scope robotics/control spiking world model with no LLM or language methodology; despite sparse transformer and multimodal image-text binding, the contribution is primarily embodied control. arxiv:2608.07707.rationale: Pure robotics/control paper on differentiable signed distance for convex polyhedra. It has no LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, safety, or other in-scope AI/ML methodology, so it is capped as out-of-scope despite moderate mathematical development.

arxiv:2608.07444.rationale: Out-of-scope wireless localization paper using classical ML regressors (KNN/RF/DT/SVR); no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent topics. Simulation-only with quantitative MAE/R2/latency results but limited novelty and generalizability, and no code/data release.
