Table 2 ablation shows SFT+DAPO yields 7B P-Hard Strict pass@1 30.6 versus 13.2 for the backbone and 25.2 for DAPO only.
Section 3.2 describes a three-stage reproducibility pipeline with answer keys computed from logged canonical reference code and expert audit.
Section 5.4 reports semantic-embedding similarity showing P-Bench tasks have no near-duplicate counterparts in the RL/SFT training corpus.

arxiv:2608.07436.rationale: Highly relevant to interpretability, transformer architecture, and training dynamics; not an LLM/Japanese/NLP application. Novelty is moderate because it extends known grokking/Fourier/Muon work. Rigor is decent with matched branches and ablations, but many causal analyses are single-seed and limited to toy tasks. Quantitative evidence is abundant but narrow. Reproducibility is good due to detailed setup and code availability.
evidence: Section 3.1 Table 5 reports all nine Muon configurations reached sustained 95% test accuracy and none was strictly stable.
Section 4.2 Table 8 reports matched branches where freezing either hidden or auxiliary group prevents collapse, while freezing only unembedding also prevents it.
Section 7.1 Table 13 reports addition family sufficiency of exactly 100.00% at 43 solved checkpoints and ablation leaving 1.71%.
Section 8.2 states circuit masking where the addition family alone gives 100% while the full model reaches 45.85%.
Section 5.2 Table 10 reports Stable Muon across five runs and 451,400 post-grokking steps with zero evaluations below 95%.
Section 11 acknowledges single-seed limitations for matched collapse, cross-readout, and layerwise causal analysis.

arxiv:2608.07435.rationale: Relevant VLM stress-test evaluation paper matching Multimodal AI and Evaluation preferences. It presents an automated benchmark construction pipeline with quantitative results, controls, and ablations, though novelty is moderate and the filtering VLM creates self-selection bias. Rigor is acceptable but small pilot instantiations and confidence intervals without significance testing limit strength. Reproducibility is partial: detailed appendices and planned release are described, but actual code/data availability is not demonstrated in the document.
evidence: Section 5.2 Main Results reports macro-average accuracy 17.8%-31.3% across six VLMs, with subset-specific scores and bootstrap confidence intervals.
Table 1 same-model comparison lists Gemini 3.5 Flash 22.3% on SABRE-Prior versus 60.3%-90.0% on existing benchmarks.
Table 7 provides detailed per-model subset accuracies, including Context, Texture, Attribute, and Language Elicitation.
Appendix D.3 blind user study reports 93.5% overall preference for localized patch repair with soft blending over baseline repair methods.

arxiv:2608.07434.rationale: Relevance is moderate-low: fits multimodal/video-language evaluation and uses a black-box VLM, but the contribution is conformal UQ for video temporal grounding, not core LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent methodology. Research is reasonably rigorous with formal coverage guarantees and multi-grounder experiments, though task-specific and largely an application of standard split conformal methods.
evidence: Abstract: Cover is a post-hoc, model-agnostic wrapper that turns any grounder into one emitting a temporal region with finite-sample distribution-free coverage.
Section 4: defines interval-widening and super-level-set scores with split-conformal calibration.
Section 7.1: reports realized coverage tracking target across three benchmarks and multiple grounders.
Section 8: limitations include marginal not conditional coverage and exchangeability assumptions.

arxiv:2608.07433.rationale: Theoretical RL/control paper matching the Reinforcement Learning preference (weight 1.5) but not higher-weight LLM/NLP/agent categories. Rigor is strong with formal assumptions, lemmas, and proofs; novelty is moderate as an exact LQ specialization of Wasserstein policy gradient. Generalizability is limited to linear-quadratic control, and reproducibility is limited by absence of code/data.
evidence: Abstract: states Wasserstein policy gradient for entropy-regularized discounted linear-quadratic control and exponential convergence without perturbative exp(-c/tau) factor.
Section 4 Proposition 4.2: proves exact closure of WPG direction on the linear-Gaussian policy class.
Section 5 Theorem 5.1: establishes global exponential convergence with explicit rate.
Appendix E: contains complete proof of Theorem 5.1.
Remark 5.2: notes unweighted covariance estimate can have prefactor proportional to 1/tau.

arxiv:2608.07430.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM safety, jailbreaking, interpretability, and red teaming; proposes SN-Guided Diffusion and cross-architecture safety-neuron transfer attacks on diffusion LLMs. Strengths include detailed methodology, ablations, and multiple target evaluations. Weakened by third-party baseline comparisons, no uncertainty quantification, and suspiciously perfect metrics such as AUROC=1.0.
evidence: Abstract introduces SN-Guided Diffusion and reports transfer ASR up to 86.9% on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and 74.3% against Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite, requiring 20 episodes per prompt.
Section 4.3 and Table 1 report self-pruning ASR increases for LLaDA/Dream and transfer pruning from Qwen2.5 to Dream/Fast-dLLM with utility measured on GSM8K.
Section 5.4 and Appendix B describe offline safety-neuron-guided token selection during denoising and adaptive logit boosting.
Table 3 provides ASR evaluations across open-source AR, DLLM, and proprietary targets; Table 4 covers defenses.
Appendix A includes ablation of SN loss formulations with AUROC values; Appendix I includes ablation of pure diffusion vs SN-Guided Diffusion and episode budgets.
Abstract states codebase availability at https://github.com/ellyoana/sn-guided-diffusion.

arxiv:2608.07429.rationale: Relevant language-agent memory work under Agents & Tool Use, RAG, and LLM preferences. It formalizes stale-memory pollution and keyed revocation with controlled, executable, preference-update, and MemoryAgentBench evaluations. Strengths include paired statistical tests and ablations; limitations include schema-based conflict-key dependence, weak multi-hop/long-context transfer, and no code release.
evidence: Results: Controlled Drift Exposes Memory Pollution reports append-only 0.210 and last-write-wins 0.210 versus no memory 0.309 and TEPA 0.950 under full reversal.
Results: The Effect Reproduces with Real File Execution reports append-only 0.203 versus no memory 0.298 and TEPA 0.950 under full reversal.
Table 4: Key paired statistical comparisons lists TEPA vs append-only reversal mean difference 0.740 with 95% CI [0.722, 0.756].
Results: Preference Updates Require Trial-Validated Revocation reports append-only 0.138 versus no memory 0.837 and TEPA-Full 0.872 full-reversal success.
Results: MemoryAgentBench Single-Hop Conflict Resolution reports TEPA-Rev 0.890, last-write-wins 0.890, and append-only 0.583 substring exact match.
Limitations: TEPA assumes useful conflict keys can be extracted from evidence and identifies multi-hop and very-long-context MemoryAgentBench settings as failure boundaries.

arxiv:2608.07427.rationale: The paper directly compares LLM text vs VLM image modalities for time-series anomaly detection and energy cost, matching multimodal AI, LLM inference, and efficiency topics, but it is a domain-specific systems evaluation rather than a language-modeling methodology contribution. Novelty is limited to energy benchmarking of an existing visual time-series idea. Rigor is weakened by internal inconsistencies (Table IV F1 values do not follow from reported precision/recall; Table I/II imply contradictory F1 estimates), limited runs, and unclear baseline details. Evidence is quantitative but partly unreliable. Generalizability is moderate across three VLM architectures and two datasets, but restricted to time-series anomaly detection. Reproducibility is limited by proprietary telecom data, no code release, and sparse fine-tuning details.
evidence: Section V-C, Table IV reports ARIMA P=0.202/R=0.268 but F1=0.186, whereas the standard F1 is ~0.230; LSTM and LLM rows show similar inconsistencies.
Section V-A, Table I and Table II imply inconsistent text F1 values: e.g., Pixtral text energy 39,663 J divided by 52,356 J/F1 gives F1~0.758, while Section V-A text states text mean F1 is 0.58-0.66.
Section III-B describes Zeus/NVML hardware-counter energy measurement with 3 runs, Section V-E Table V reports per-query energy reductions of 1.8-2.5x.

arxiv:2608.07648.rationale: The paper is a tutorial review on using generative models (normalizing flows, diffusion models) to assist Monte Carlo sampling in scientific computing. It has no connection to LLMs, Japanese NLP, transformer language modeling, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, code, AI safety, or other high-weight preferences. It may superficially align with low-weight Scientific AI but is a pure domain application without language methodology, so it is out of scope and must receive at most 0.20. Methodologically it is detailed and well-referenced, but as a review it provides no new empirical results, code, or data, limiting evidence strength and reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: 'Sampling high-dimensional probability distributions is a central task in scientific computing...'
Section 1.1: 'Sampling and its challenges'
Section 2.3: 'Diffusion models'
Section 4: 'Training generative models without data'

arxiv:2608.07425.rationale: Qualitative HCI study of area-chair practices and perceptions of AI support in peer review. It touches LLM-based tools, bias/fairness, and human-AI collaboration, but does not advance LLM/NLP methodology or provide technical ML contributions, limiting topical relevance. The method is reasonably rigorous for qualitative research (27 interviews, design probe, thematic analysis), but evidence is primarily self-reported and thematic rather than quantitative; self-selection and venue-specific sampling limit generalizability, and no data/code release is described.
evidence: §3 Method reports 27 semi-structured AC interviews with a design probe and reflexive thematic analysis.
§4.1 Existing Challenges documents reviewer/author coordination problems and cognitive overload with participant quotes.
§5.4 Venue-Specific Dynamics and Broader Implications distinguishes generalizable patterns from ICLR-specific ones.
§8 Interview Script provides the protocol, but no dataset, code, or full transcripts are described for reproduction.

arxiv:2608.07424.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM test-time reasoning/compute allocation, evaluation, and efficiency, though not Japanese/agent/safety domains. Contributions are incremental: adaptive routing across generation/verification/stopping builds on prior test-time scaling and adaptive-compute work. Quantitative evidence is fairly strong with shared-pool baselines, paired bootstrap CIs, ablations, and cost metrics, but many baselines are local proxies and empirical scope is limited to math/procedural symbolic tasks. Rigor is tempered by macro-vs-paired discrepancies and no explicit code release.
evidence: §5 Main Accuracy–Cost Results: Table 2 reports CoBa-Routed-Strong at 85.13% accuracy vs best-of-16 at 85.12%, using 58.9% fewer parameter-weighted tokens.

§5 Significance and Ablations: paired bootstrap tests show CoBa-Routed-Strong improves over greedy by +3.74 points (95% CI [+2.97,+4.54]) and remains below best-of-16 by 0.70 points (95% CI [-1.25,-0.16]).
§4 Offline Replay Protocol and Appendix D: all methods share identical generated candidate pools and cached verifier outputs, with oracle correctness reserved for evaluation.

arxiv:2608.07423.rationale: Pure speech/audio enhancement with no language-model methodology; the only LLM mentions are in a language-editing disclosure (Section 5). Within audio the paper has moderate novelty via server-edge feature boosting and collaborative MCWF, and Table 1 provides ablations, but this is out-of-scope under the pure-audio cap.
evidence: Table 1 reports SI-SDR/PESQ/STOI for the TinyGRU+MCWF baseline and incremental (a,b,c) ablations at 64 ms delay.
Section 2.4 describes extracting features from four SpatialNet depths and injecting them into TinyGRU via FiLM.
Section 2.5 describes fusing edge/server cross-covariance vectors with a learned per-frame alpha weight.
Section 5 states GPT and Claude were used only for language editing and manuscript polishing, not technical content.

arxiv:2608.11260.rationale: Moderate relevance: agentic MLLM/tool use, chain-of-thought, and RL are central, but the task is domain-specific video anomaly detection, limiting LLM/NLP preference alignment. Novelty is moderate given prior tool-augmented video reasoning (VITAL, LongVT) and extension of prior VAGU. Methods are described with ablations, but evidence is self-reported without significance testing or confidence intervals, and evaluation is narrow to VAGU-T with no cross-benchmark validation. Reproducibility is partial: hyperparameters are given, but code availability is not stated.
evidence: Table 5 (Sec 7.2) reports Agentic RL A.U. 7.35, JeAUG 5.91, FPS 148 versus SUVAD A.U. 5.73, FPS 0.19.
Table 8 (Sec 7.3) shows SFT only A.U. 6.62 versus SFT+RL with R_acc+R_format+R_time A.U. 7.35.
Sec 3.3 describes tool-calling trace generation and dual-criterion filtering with IoU >= 0.3 for trace retention.
Sec 5.4 defines reward R=R_acc+R_format+R_time, with R_time computed as IoU of the last crop video invocation.

arxiv:2608.07420.rationale: Out-of-scope model-based RL/world-model paper for continuous control and Atari Pong; uses a Transformer action encoder but no LLM/NLP language methodology, so preference relevance is low and final score is capped at 0.20. Internally it has controlled comparisons and ablations, but limited task breadth, no error bars/statistical tests, and no code release.
evidence: Section 3.2, Table 1: DPWM K=100 shows lower endpoint MSE than ADM K=3 and MoSim at horizons 100/200 on Cheetah, Humanoid, Hopper, Walker.
Section 3.2, Table 2: ADM K=100 substantially improves over ADM K=3 on humanoid_walk, supporting training objective over architecture.
Appendix D, Table 4: Pong pixel MSE at horizons 1-400 comparing DPWM K=100 and ADM K=100.

arxiv:2608.07419.rationale: Strongly relevant to LLMs, alignment/RLHF side effects, and training-time optimization; proposes bilevel entropy-maximizing calibration with first-order updates. Empirical coverage includes four aligned LLMs, MCQA and generative QA with domain shift. However, rigor is limited by uneven baseline tuning (CFT fixed alpha in MCQA while CALM has wider grid), high variance on Llama/Mistral in seed study, and possible overlap between hyperparameter selection and reported test ECE. Claims about best accuracy-calibration trade-off are partially overstated given nontrivial accuracy drops.
evidence: Section 5.2 Table 1: CALM improves conf-ECE over DPO/RLHF on all four OOD MCQA models, e.g. Mistral-7B 0.3351 to 0.0822, but Mistral accuracy drops from 59.80% to 51.60%.
Appendix D.1 Table 11: multi-seed OOD MCQA shows large variance for Llama-3.1 conf-ECE 0.110+/-0.085 and Mistral-7B 0.149+/-0.121.
Section 5.3 Table 3: CALM achieves lowest mean Sem-ECE 0.0671 under generative domain shift, versus DPO/RLHF 0.0846 and best-alpha CFT 0.1109.
Section 5.4 Figure 1: reliability diagrams on Mistral-7B OOD show CALM aligns bins closer to the diagonal than DPO, temperature scaling, and CFT.
Appendix C: code link, QLoRA settings, hyperparameter grids, and training-cost details support reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.07418.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM-based agents, multi-turn reinforcement learning, tool use, AI safety, and clinical NLP, but the medical/healthcare domain lowers preference versus general LLM/agent work. Methodologically this builds on existing GRPO and LLM-judge simulation with modest algorithmic novelty. Rigor is reasonable given controlled evaluations, ablations, statistical tests, and human review, but in-domain evaluation reuses the training reward rubric and external benchmark gains are often directional/non-significant. Evidence is fairly strong for in-domain and AMIE Mx but weakened by autoregressive judge bias and lack of real patient validation. Generalization is evaluated across multiple out-of-domain benchmarks but is clinical-text-only. Reproducibility is limited because code is not released and relies on proprietary infrastructure.
evidence: Section 3.3 and Table 2 define a structured LLM-judge reward across clinical dimensions and penalty flags; the same rubric architecture is used for training reward and in-domain evaluation in Section 4.1.
Section 4.4 Table 6 reports directional improvements on AgentClinic and CRAFT-MD but states these did not reach statistical significance (e.g., AgentClinic p=0.176 and p=0.079).
Section 5 Limitations acknowledges positive autorater bias toward the trained model, text-only telehealth scope, and that prospective real-world validation remains necessary.
Code Availability states the codebase is not open-sourced due to internal infrastructure and safety implications.

arxiv:2608.07417.rationale: Relevant multimodal MLLM video-reasoning benchmark and post-training paper with CoT/reward components, but the person-centric video focus keeps preference relevance moderate. The ICQ task, benchmark, and ESR reward are solid but incremental. Quantitative baselines and ablations support the claims, though rigor is limited by no statistical testing, no inter-annotator agreement, absent limitations, and some ambiguous/inconsistent details (e.g., 75K vs 74,578 samples; timestamp use in ESR despite claiming no shot-level supervision). Reproducibility is low because no code/data release or availability statement is included.
evidence: Section 5, Table 3 reports O.Avg and ICQ Q.Avg across GPT-5.2, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Qwen models, baselines, and ISYV-Model-RFT.
Section 5.3, Tables 4-5 report ablations for SFT/RFT reward combinations, ICQ token count, and frame count.
Section 3, Table 1 compares ISYV-Benchmark with prior video reasoning benchmarks on video count, QA pairs, task count, annotation, multi-input, and human-aligned cognition.
Section 4.3 defines the ESR reward and other reward components with equations supporting the training strategy.

arxiv:2608.07413.rationale: Wireless MU-MIMO movable-antenna placement via submodular optimization; unrelated to LLM/NLP/agent/multimodal preferences. Research quality is moderate within its domain, with formal proofs and simulation comparisons, but limited generalizability and no code/data release. Score kept at/below 0.20 as out-of-scope.
evidence: Section IV-B, Lemma 2 proves monotone submodularity and diminishing returns.
Section VI-C reports DCSPS at 30 dB achieves 14.522 bits/s/Hz, +3.280 over the fixed benchmark and 0.237 below BnB.
Section VI-F, Table I reports DCSPS runtime 5 ms vs BnB 172 ms and brute-force 297 ms.

arxiv:2608.07411.rationale: Relevant as an LLM evaluation benchmark with reasoning, but geo-specific and lacking Japanese NLP or core LLM methodology. Novelty is limited to aggregating existing datasets and adding metrics. Rigor is weak: no significance tests, error bars, ablations, prompt details, or limitations; baselines are limited to Qwen3 and GPT-OSS. Evidence from Table 3 is quantitative but single-run and only main metrics. Reproducibility is partially supported by GitHub/HF links but missing key experimental details.
evidence: Section 4.2 defines custom metrics and states metrics are available in a Hugging Face Collection.
Section 4.3 and Table 3 report main results for Qwen3 and GPT-OSS across seventeen subdatasets, showing thinking and size effects.

arxiv:2608.07409.rationale: Out of scope for the stated preferences: this is a pure vision/video/world-model/planning paper with no language methodology, LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, or agent-language components. It has only tangential relevance via transformer architecture, video, and embodied planning. Some unified JEPA novelty and ablations are present, but evidence is limited, the proof is informal, and reproducibility details are partial. Capped at 0.20 due to pure computer vision/robotics scope exclusion.
evidence: Abstract: presents UniJEPA for visual world modeling and planning; no language model or NLP task is described.
Section 4.3: reports ImageNet, Something-Something-v2, EK-100, and planning results; no language evaluation.
Table 2: ablation study includes photometric loss, temporal loss, and regularizer components.

arxiv:2608.07408.rationale: Out-of-scope video world model/video diffusion work without language methodology; capped at 0.20. It has some overlap with Transformer Architecture and Long Context/Memory via RoPE and KV-cache compression, but no LLM/NLP, reasoning, agents, or language grounding. Research quality is moderate: formalized slot indexing, ablations, and quantitative LoopBench results are reported, but the domain relevance is low and the evaluation is limited to video world models.
evidence: Sec. 2.1 identifies out-of-distribution RoPE offsets as the addressability bottleneck.
Tab. 2 reports TempSSIM and Scene Drift for WorldTrace-Field at N=32 and N=48.
Tab. 3 reports PAC and TempSSIM for WorldTrace-Landmark across LoopBench tiers.
App. E.3 Tab. 10 reports PAC sweep for ABA loops up to N=256.

arxiv:2608.07406.rationale: Geoscientific XAI regression review; partially matches Interpretability & Explainability terms but lacks LLM/language methodology, so treated as an out-of-scope domain application and capped at 0.20. The survey is systematic with L63 illustrations, but Section 4.7 admits no formal quantitative XAI evaluation; code availability supports reproducibility.
evidence: Section 4.7 states that no formal quantitative evaluation of XAI methods is included and that evaluation remains an open challenge due to absence of clear ground truth.
Section 3 describes the ANN architecture, training setup, Adam optimizer, early stopping, and test NRMSE ≈0.62%.
Data availability statement provides code for L63 illustrations at https://github.com/ichiggs/Evaluating-XAI-Methods-L63.
Section 5 surveys sensitivity-based, SHAP, LRP, and bespoke XAI applications in Earth system regression contexts.

arxiv:2608.07405.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/domain application: annotation-free spacecraft segmentation using SAM 3 pseudo-masks and geometry distillation, with no language-model or NLP methodology. Although the paper includes multi-seed experiments, ablations, lockbox evaluation, and confidence intervals, the contribution is domain-specific and not relevant to the stated LLM/NLP/agent preferences; capped at 0.20 per out-of-scope policy.
evidence: Abstract: proposes GeoDistill-Refine, an annotation-free spacecraft segmentation framework transferring offline SAM 3 pseudo-masks to a compact segmentation network; only single-frame RGB student retained.
Section IV.A: experiments on SpaceSense-Bench, SPEED+, and TANGO for binary spacecraft foreground segmentation; no language modeling or LLM methodology.
Section V: evidence limited to binary segmentation with validation masks used for checkpoint selection and threshold calibration; only SpaceSense-Bench supports unseen spacecraft claims.

arxiv:2608.07403.rationale: Out-of-scope computational biology/control paper on immune cell network topology inference. It has no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent/RAG or other weighted preference focus, and is a pure domain application. The mathematical modeling and proofs show moderate rigor, but evaluation is domain-specific, limited to 10 real experiments with no ground truth, no baselines/ablations, and no released code/data, so overall score is capped low.
evidence: Abstract: focuses on inferring the topology of immune cells from cell-depletion experiments
Section 2.3: proposed nonlinear model for immune network interaction
Section 3.2: validation on real immune cell experiments with 10 cell types, m=10, average relative error 0.327

arxiv:2608.07401.rationale: Topically out-of-scope as a pure materials/crystal-generation domain application with no LLM/NLP/language methodology; only weak matches are generic Transformer architecture and Scientific AI. The paper is internally detailed, but final score is capped near the out-of-scope threshold.
evidence: Section 5.1: evaluation on MP-20 with CHGNet primary and MACE-MP-0 independent relaxation, ~10,000 candidates per method.
Table 1: reports SUN/SSUN and median e_hull under two independent relaxation engines.
Appendix K Table 12: Marginal-G ablation lowers SUN@0 from 9.28 to 3.01, supporting dynamic space-group coupling.
Section 6 Limitations: acknowledges computational screening proxies and no experimental synthesis claim.

arxiv:2608.07400.rationale: Within-scope RAG/retrieval/NLP benchmark with curated hard negatives and evaluation tasks, but not an LLM methodology contribution. Novelty is moderate as a benchmark resource; rigor is limited by single-annotator construction, sampled review, no inter-annotator agreement, and confounded/skewed strata. Quantitative baseline results are documented, but no generation/LLM answer-quality evaluation or significance testing. Reproducibility is strong due to code, data, scripts, seeds, and model specs.
evidence: Section 7.1/Table 4: e5-mistral-7b-instruct reaches 44.8% Recall@10 on the pooled corpus.
Section 7.3: curated hard negatives reduce pairwise accuracy by 13.0-20.5 points versus random negatives.
Section 9: single-annotator with sampled review, no formal inter-annotator agreement, and skew toward 2025/10-K/qualitative records.
Appendix G/J: reports code, data, seed=42, model names, and deterministic baseline scripts.

arxiv:2608.07398.rationale: Out-of-scope industrial operations research application using inverse optimization for production planning. No listed AI/ML preference areas such as LLMs, NLP, reasoning, agents, safety, or multimodal AI. The paper has formal MILP modeling and quantitative case-study results, but as a pure domain application it is capped at <=0.20.
evidence: Abstract: proposes data-driven inverse optimization for production planning with a Dow industrial case study, with no LLM/NLP/AI methodology.
Section 4.2: reports RMSE comparisons for model-1, model-5, and model-7.
Section 4.3: presents inferred objective weights and expert interview hypotheses.
Section 4.5: reports training time and convergence behavior.

arxiv:2608.07397.rationale: Formal software-verification paper translating C programs into sequential circuits and using hardware model checkers; outside the LLM/NLP/agent/multimodal/safety preference scope. The work is technically substantial and empirically strong within its domain, but relevance to requested topics is minimal, so the hard out-of-scope cap of 0.20 is applied.
evidence: Abstract: presents CPV, translating C programs into sequential circuits and using off-the-shelf hardware model checkers for reachability-safety and termination.
Section 9.3 Table 1: reports more than 70% of 16,201 evaluated benchmark tasks successfully translated into sequential circuits.
Section 9.3 Table 9: reports CPV solved the second-largest number of ReachSafety and Termination tasks among evaluated tools.
Section 9.3 RQ4: reports approximately 95% of violation witnesses were confirmed by validators.

arxiv:2608.07396.rationale: Domain case study of using LLMs and Lean for mathematical research; relevant primarily as an LLM application, but lacks ML methodology, quantitative evaluation, baselines, or ablations. Evidence is qualitative and anecdotal, with limited generalizability and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 3.3 narrates LLM-assisted proof and Lean verification experiences without quantitative metrics.
Section 3.7 discusses hallucination and the specification gap qualitatively.
Section 3.8 reports LLM research-assistant successes and failures anecdotally rather than through systematic evaluation.

arxiv:2608.07395.rationale: Relevant LLM-based code evolution and algorithm design method with a modular primitive reuse mechanism and Thompson sampling. The idea is moderately novel, but evaluation rigor is limited: only three runs, large variances with overlapping baselines, some tiny ablation differences within noise, and no statistical significance testing. Reproducibility is partially supported by prompts and pseudocode but no public artifact confirmation.
evidence: Experiments: Table 1 reports means and standard deviations over three runs; several PACE vs baseline intervals overlap, weakening superiority claims.
Ablation Studies: Table 4 shows some ablation differences are very small, such as TSP-ACO 5.805 vs 5.815 without Thompson sampling.
Detailed Methodology: Prompts, hyperparameters, and pseudo-code are provided, supporting partial reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.07393.rationale: Out of scope as a pure medical imaging/fMRI federated learning domain application with no language methodology, so capped at 0.20. The method is domain-specific, with modest quantitative gains and limited generalization beyond neuroimaging biomarkers.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports evaluation on ABIDE-I, ABIDE-II, and ADHD-200; Section 4.4 Table 1 reports FedDOSE vs baselines with mean±std and p<0.05 markers.
Section 4.5 Table 3 reports ablation drops when removing phenotype/scanner losses, reconstruction loss, Procrustes, OT, and prototype regularization.

arxiv:2608.07385.rationale: Out-of-scope domain-specific wearable multi-modal HAR/VAE paper with no LLM, language, reasoning, agent, or NLP methodology. It mentions multimodal and interpretable representations, but does not match the curator's core language-model focus. Method quality is moderate, with a single dataset, no cross-modal/missing-modality experiments, and contradictory reported improvement percentages between abstract and conclusion, limiting calibration.
evidence: Abstract: proposes OmniDecVAEs for omni-modal wearable human activity recognition using up to thirty modalities.
Section IV-A: describes HARWE dataset and input modalities (audio, physiology, inertial); evaluation uses subject-dependent and subject-independent splits.
Section V-E Discussion: states 'we did not experiment with cross-modal inference and missing modality scenarios' and future work may include video or text.

Abstract vs Section VI Conclusion: inconsistent improvement figures are reported; Abstract gives 1.01% and 6.75% for activity and identity recognition respectively, while Conclusion reverses them as 6.75% and 1.01%, and similarly swaps MAE/MK-MMD percentages.

arxiv:2608.07643.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/embedded traffic sensing with no LLM/NLP/transformer/agent/alignment methodology. The work is a retrospective classical background-subtraction pipeline, so preference relevance is minimal. Method is clearly described but evidence is limited to four videos and one field deployment with manual ground truth, and no code or data are provided.
evidence: Section 6.2 reports resolution/frame-rate sweeps and an error floor near 40% at 5 fps.
Table 2 reports pre-calibration accuracy of 83.3%-100% across four videos, with long uncontrolled videos at 83.3%-85.6%.
Section 8.3 Limitations states evaluation covers four videos and one field site, manual counting, and no independent speed validation.

arxiv:2608.07383.rationale: Formal game-theory paper on mean-payoff bidding games and optimal strategies. No LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/RAG/agentic-tool methodology; only superficial 'agent'/'multi-agent' wording. Moderate niche novelty, but purely theoretical with no empirical validation, restricted to recurrent/repeated games and known strategy constructions, and has notation/proof artifacts.
evidence: Abstract: analyzes interaction of optimal strategies in mean-payoff bidding games
Section 2.2, Theorem 8: ultimate periodicity result for block strategies in recurrent games
Section 3.2, Theorem 16: finite bifurcation result for repeated bidding games
Theorem 8 statement in Section 2.2.3 contains malformed path notation

arxiv:2608.07382.rationale: Pure computer vision satellite object detection and dataset paper with no language methodology, so capped below 0.20. Within CV, it is a modest benchmark and lightweight baseline; reporting is transparent but single runs, unequal budgets, no ablations, mixed hardware, and limited comparative rigor constrain strength.
evidence: Section V-A Setup: describes twelve detectors, COCO metrics, 640x640 letterboxed inputs, and mixed GPU hardware.
Table IV: reports SkyDet at 60.5 mAP50, 24.32 mAP50-95, 1.22M parameters, 4.90 MB checkpoint, and 13.74 ms on Tesla T4.
Section VII Discussion and Limitations: notes single runs under unequal model-specific recipes, no ablation, no per-scale AP, mixed hardware, and no geographic split separation.
Data Availability: provides Mendeley DOI and Kaggle release with COCO/YOLO annotations.

arxiv:2608.07642.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM value alignment and multi-agent fusion, with DPO-fine-tuned Pythia moral agents and alignment-focused evaluation. Novelty is incremental over prior single-layer VAS-CFA/MCF work. Evidence is moderate: tables and ablations exist, but comparisons lack statistical significance and the Commonsense final-layer accuracy is lower than an earlier best combined model without adequate explanation. Evaluation relies narrowly on BERTScore/accuracy, while incomplete classifier training details and no code release limit reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.07378.rationale: Low relevance: this is a clinical speech-based Alzheimer's screening application using frozen LLM embeddings (Zephyr/Qwen/Llama) with PCA and simple classifiers, not an LLM/NLP methodology contribution. It has some cross-dataset/ASR/backbone comparisons, but small datasets, selected baselines, internal inconsistencies, and limited implementation details weaken rigor and evidence.

Section 3.2 says penultimate-layer embeddings while Equation 7 states final transformer layer.

arxiv:2608.07377.rationale: Out of scope: astrophysics/cosmology weak lensing analysis; no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, agents, or AI methodology. Uses Gaussian process emulators as a computational tool but the contribution is domain cosmology, so overall score capped below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: presents improved cosmological constraints from clipped cosmic shear; no AI/LLM/NLP methodology.
Sec 1: scope is weak lensing cosmology, systematics, and higher-order statistics.
Sec 3.2: Gaussian process emulators used for interpolation of simulation statistics, not as ML research contribution.

arxiv:2608.07376.rationale: Out-of-scope pure audio/music interaction paper with no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning methodology. It is a preliminary research framework: most stages are proposed or in progress, evidence is largely from one ensemble, and no public artifacts are available.
evidence: §1 states the paper presents a research framework, not a completed collective-state model.
§4 reports 40 aligned takes from ten rehearsals, mostly from one ensemble, and states the prototype is not publicly available.
§6 Table 1 marks state inference and agent/evaluation as proposed rather than implemented.

arxiv:2608.07371.rationale: Directly relevant to agentic LLM training, RL, and hindsight distillation; strongly matches Agents & Tool Use, Large Language Models, and Reinforcement Learning preferences. Novelty is incremental relative to dense hindsight/self-distillation and concurrent turn-aware methods. Rigor is limited by single-seed evaluation and no statistical significance testing, though controlled Uniform/Permuted ablations are useful. Evidence supports consistent gains on WebShop and ALFWorld but lacks variance estimates. Generalizability is limited to text-based discrete-action environments and two small backbones. Reproducibility is supported by detailed hyperparameters and a code link.
evidence: Abstract: reports TRIAL outperforms GRPO across all eight combinations of backbone, environment, and evaluation metric, with WebShop Qwen3-1.7B success rate from 56.4% to 75.2% and task score from 78.7% to 85.7%.
Section 4.2, Table 1: complete-set results for ALFWorld Seen/Unseen and WebShop success/task score across Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen3-1.7B.
Section 4.3, Table 2: controlled revision-profile results with Qwen3-1.7B; TRIAL outperforms Uniform and Permuted on all four aggregate metrics.
Section 6 Limitations: states runs use a single seed and cross-seed variance/statistical robustness remain unmeasured.
Appendix A.2, Table 3: lists training configuration, auxiliary coefficients, gap clipping bound, and activation step.

arxiv:2608.07370.rationale: Highly relevant to RAG, LLM evaluation, and dataset/benchmark topics, with a traceable literature-grounded QA formulation. Novelty is moderate: it combines paper retrieval, typed evidence grounding, and answer checking, but closely related scientific QA benchmarks exist. Rigor is limited by the absence of baseline evaluations, official splits, human QC results, and formal release details. Evidence strength comes mainly from corpus statistics and illustrative examples rather than validated system performance. Generalizability is moderate but constrained by venue concentration in recent vision/NLP papers. Reproducibility is weak because the full dataset and evaluation tooling are not yet released.
evidence: Abstract: describes the benchmark as requiring paper identifiers, supporting evidence locations, and answers, and reports a public split of 55 examples plus a local collection of 4,978 unique-question records.
Section 6 Evaluation Protocol: defines separated paper retrieval, evidence grounding, and answer correctness metrics with a strict joint success criterion.

Section 8 Limitations and Release Requirements: states that normalized locators, official splits, licensing documentation, human quality control, and baseline retrieval-augmented evaluations are still needed.
Section 5 Dataset Characteristics: reports 4,978 unique questions, 4,859 unique gold papers, evidence-type distributions, and venue concentration in recent vision and NLP venues.

arxiv:2608.07641.rationale: Strongly relevant to LLM evaluation and NLP, with a reviewer-aligned benchmark and fine-tuned Qwen3-32B evaluator. Moderately novel as a first peer-review-derived survey evaluation dataset, but methodologically incremental. Rigor is adequate with ablations and annotation reliability checks, though limited by missing explicit limitations/statistical testing and reliance on LLM-based rationale scoring.
evidence: Section 4.4 reports 675 survey papers and 1,630 peer review reports with a paper-level 75/25 train/test split stratified by source.
Table 2 in Section 6.2 reports SurveyAlign lowers average MSE from 2.28 to 1.38 and MAE from 1.15 to 0.69 versus GPT-5.2.
Appendix A.2 reports overall Krippendorff's alpha of 0.74 on 280 annotation units.
Section 6.3.2 Table 4 shows Crit-KA alone increases Criticalness MSE to 2.04, while Crit-KA+DPO reaches 1.52.
Appendix D lists LoRA rank 8, learning rate 5e-5, max sequence length 16,384, and DeepSpeed ZeRO-3.

arxiv:2608.07368.rationale: Pure medical-imaging domain application using off-the-shelf nnU-Net segmentation and geometric post-processing; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent methodology. Although clinical validation is reported with quantitative agreement and limitations, it lacks AI methodological novelty, baselines, ablations, and external validation, so overall score is capped low.
evidence: Abstract: Pipeline uses nnU-Net segmentation and geometric modeling to compute FAI angles from ZTE MRI, validated against manual reads.
Methods §2.4.3: Uses default nnU-Net 3D full-resolution configuration with five-fold cross-validation; no language-model or reasoning methodology.
Results §3.2: Reports Dice >0.96 for bone segmentation and landmark Dice 0.65-0.83 on 35 test hips.
Discussion §4: Notes single-institution, single ZTE acquisition, limited external validation, and landmark degradation concerns.

arxiv:2608.07367.rationale: Directly evaluates LLM value alignment across socio-demographic groups using ESS and 10 LLMs, matching LLM and value-alignment preferences. Moderate novelty as a cross-national socio-demographic alignment study, but largely incremental over country-level and US-only work. Methods are fairly rigorous with bootstrap CIs, IPW, CV-based variance decomposition, and extensive appendices. Evidence is quantitative but observational and MCQ-survey-based. Generalizability is limited to Europe, English prompting, and selected commercial models. Reproducibility is supported by public ESS data and code, though closed API model versions limit exact replication.
evidence: Abstract/Code: https://github.com/aida-ugent/LLMs-x-ESS
Section 3.2 Definition of alignment: normalized alignment score formula
Section 4.2 Within vs between country effects: test R^2 comparisons for country-only, SD-only, and Country+SD
Table 2: between-country standard deviation before and after IPW reweighting
Discussion/Limitations: acknowledges English-only prompting, majority-vote aggregation, and MCQ surrogate limitations

arxiv:2608.07364.rationale: Applied STEM-education paper that uses LLMs for LaTeX/Python instructional material generation. It touches LLM and prompting topics but is primarily a domain application rather than language-model or NLP methodology, so relevance is capped low. Validation is descriptive, single-institution, and lacks controlled comparisons or released prompts/code.
evidence: Section IV-A describes the six-phase AI-assisted workflow using LLM-generated LaTeX and Python.
Section V reports one-year deployment across 8 modules and 28 project contexts, with student material ratings of 8.5 to 9.9 in Table III.
Section VI-D notes the main limitation: authoring was conducted by a single instructor within a single institution.
Sections IV-B and IV-C describe tooling and validation at a high level, but no prompts, templates, or code artifacts are provided for reproduction.

arxiv:2608.07640.rationale: Out-of-scope remote sensing/climate spatiotemporal benchmark with no language methodology; only tangential use of Earthformer/cuboid attention. The paper provides a reproducible dataset and ablations but falls outside LLM/NLP/agents/safety/multimodal language scope, so final score is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: 124 U.S. cities, 30 m monthly LST forecasting, Earthformer 7.74 K RMSE.
Section 6.2: feature-set ablation reports auxiliary-no-LST Earthformer 7.72 K RMSE.
Section 9: limitations include one training run per baseline and known-city temporal split.
Section 4.6/Data and code availability: dataset, code, and checkpoints released under MIT.

arxiv:2608.07363.rationale: Time-series forecasting is a pure domain application with no LLM/NLP methodology; Transformer attention is only tangential. The work is an incremental integration of Quantformer and COTN ideas, and the quantitative claims are undercut by undefined ablation modules, missing hyperparameters/statistical tests, a private dataset, and a questionable LogTrans reference.
evidence: Section I positions the contribution as a practical integration/extension of existing ideas rather than new formal theory.
Section V-A Table IV reports 43.9% MSE improvement over HAT and 41.3% over COTN on ETTh2 at horizon 24, but no error bars or significance tests are provided.
Section V-C references 'FractalModulatedAttention' and 'QuantumSuperposition_LORS' in ablations, but these modules are not defined in the methodology.
Section IV-A states the A-share dataset is from a private data vendor, and no code or data release is mentioned.

arxiv:2608.07639.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, and safety. The bidirectional graph alignment formulation is moderately novel but builds on prior text-code consistency work. Evaluation is fairly rigorous with a 633-skill benchmark, baselines, ablations, and error audit, though lacks statistical testing and explicit limitations. Quantitative evidence is solid but limited by no confidence intervals and unclear code/data availability.
evidence: Abstract: reports 86.85% precision, 89.03% recall, 87.93% F1 for package-level detection and 67.60%/58.14%/62.52% for localization on 633 Skills.
Evaluation RQ2: compares LLM, LLM+RAG, C4RLLaMA, and SKILLSCOPE baselines across Skill-Inject and ClawHub.
Evaluation RQ3: ablates role separation, subgraph expansion, coverage checking, and model variant (Flash).
Problem Formulation: defines Conflict, Unimplemented, and Undeclared inconsistency types.

arxiv:2608.07361.rationale: The paper studies intermediate planning-token representations in a driving VLA, which is within interpretability/transformer/LLM scope but remains a single-checkpoint, open-loop domain-specific diagnostic. The trajectory-space native-head lens is a useful adaptation but not highly novel. Rigor is limited by acknowledged probe leakage, no route grouping, small per-family samples, and no equivalence testing, though pruning-order comparisons and CIs provide some support.
evidence: Section 5 reports command-probe accuracy reaches 97.7% at hidden state 1 vs 16.7% chance and frozen-planner Avg-L2 minimum 2.11 m at final layer.
Section 7 reports removing 8 of 32 layers within approximately 5% relative open-loop error increase and measured 1.33x decoder speedup.
Section 11 states the study is limited to one ORION checkpoint and Bench2Drive, with open-loop pruning and potential route-correlated folds.

arxiv:2608.07359.rationale: Pure audio/music-detection paper with no language methodology; out-of-scope cap applies. Research quality is moderate: a real-world broadcast dataset is a useful niche contribution, but evaluation is limited to two CNN variants and one generative model.
evidence: Abstract: focus is AI-generated music detection in real-world broadcast monitoring using CNN variants.
Section 3: BAMM is a 40-hour real-world broadcast dataset of AI-generated and human-made music.
Section 4.1: shared CNN architecture and preprocessing are described.
Table 1: reports F1/ROC for CFM, STB, and RTB scenarios.
Section 5.3: real TV broadcast performance degrades further and foreground music is easier than background music.
Section 6: authors state CNN detectors remain insufficient for reliable broadcast monitoring.

arxiv:2608.07353.rationale: Moderately relevant LLM concept-probing benchmark combining abstraction, compositionality, and grounding; quantitative but limited to geo-spatial concepts and selected models, with no significance testing and limited generalizability.
evidence: Section 5.1, Table 5 reports Binary-QA/MCQ accuracy and consistency across models

arxiv:2608.07349.rationale: Out-of-scope financial/tabular ML paper: gradient-boosted residual algebra on Chinese A-share data, with no LLM/NLP/agent/vision/audio methodology. Self-reported frozen audits, capacity controls, and paired bootstrap suggest moderate internal rigor, but evidence is untrusted proprietary and domain-specific, so overall score is capped below 0.20.
evidence: §5.1 Table 1 reports FPRC-PQ net return 19.10% vs 13.52% mean-of-fields baseline
§4 describes frozen selections through 2022-12-31 and 2023-2026 evaluation protocol
§7 acknowledges single-market limitation and that reflective rumination remains untested out-of-sample

arxiv:2608.07346.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM agent evaluation, tool use, and benchmark infrastructure, so preference relevance is high. The contribution is mostly an engineering integration over existing OpenInference/OpenTelemetry and prior evaluation frameworks; novelty is moderate. Empirical rigor is limited: Table 1 uses only 5 tasks per cell with 0.20 resolution, no statistical uncertainty, no ablations or quantitative comparison to Inspect AI/Phoenix, and Section 6.3/Table 2 contains contradictory correctness metrics for the LangGraph case. Generalizability of the framework design is reasonable, but demonstrated findings rely on small samples and two model backends.
evidence: Section 6.1/Table 1 reports 5 sampled tasks per harness-benchmark pair and acknowledges score resolution is 0.20 with high per-cell variance.
Table 2 lists LangGraph as successful with correctness=0.0 in its metric row while Section 6.3 text states LangGraph obtains correctness=1.0, indicating inconsistency.
Section 6 presents 1,035 scored runs but no confidence intervals, significance tests, or ablation/comparison against existing frameworks.

arxiv:2608.10002.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/pure computer vision image translation work with no language/NLP methodology; low preference relevance despite using LoRA. Method is moderately novel but evaluation is small-sample, preliminary, and lacks registration accuracy or statistical testing.
evidence: Section 3.1 reports decoder ablation FID values: plain 607.40, fusion 79.84, skip 77.18.

arxiv:2608.07637.rationale: Relevant as an LLM-based agent and workflow automation paper, but evaluation is limited: one scientific campaign, one production review state, two retrospective replay cases, no continuous-LLM or human-only baselines, and no independent replica statistics. Code/data availability is a strength.

Section 3.3 reports one K-LC0.4 RH=0.3 production review case and two retrospective Codex CLI replay cases.

arxiv:2608.07341.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM evaluation and contamination mitigation, with a new per-question probability metric and step-wise decoding intervention. Quantitative comparisons and ablations support the main claims, but rigor is limited by absent statistical significance testing, no explicit limitations section, and generalizability is confined to GSM8K-style math reasoning across three models.

arxiv:2608.07340.rationale: This is a pure medical imaging application: registration-based few-shot medical image segmentation using hyperbolic hierarchy-aware representations. It has no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, prompting, or language methodology, and only tangentially touches Computer Vision/Medical & Healthcare AI, which are out of scope for this rubric. The empirical work includes comparisons and ablations, but it should not be rewarded under these preferences and is capped below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: registration-based few-shot medical image segmentation and hyperbolic hierarchy-aware infusion.
Section 5: evaluation on Brain and Cardiac datasets using Dice, NCC, and HD95.
Table 1: segmentation comparison across methods.
Table 4: ablation study results on Brain dataset.

arxiv:2608.10001.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging representation paper: no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agents/safety methodology. It gives a unified framework and benchmarks Gaussian primitives against INR/feature-grid methods on BACH and NLST, but Section 4.0.3 reports only qualitative PSNR and relative speed/memory claims without exact tables; no ablations or code availability. Score capped at <=0.20 for out-of-scope medical imaging.
evidence: Section 4.0.1 specifies BACH histology and NLST lung CT datasets.
Section 4.0.2 lists Fourier-features, SIREN, WIRE, Neural Volumes, K-planes, and Gaussian additive/PoU baselines with ADAM and batch size 200k.
Section 4.0.3 states Gaussian PoU surpasses additive and gives relative speed/memory improvements but does not provide exact metric tables.
Section 3.4 discusses limitations only for generative modeling.

arxiv:2608.07335.rationale: Deep RL paper on CNN encoder and value-head benchmarking for Parallelized Q-Networks. It aligns with the RL preference (Q-learning, DQN, reward, environment) but has no language-model/NLP/agent methodology, limiting topical relevance. The work is largely an incremental combination of known components (Hadamax, distributional, ensemble, dueling) rather than conceptually novel. Empirical evaluation is extensive across Atari-57 and Procgen with statistical tests, but only four seeds, some unstable-looking per-game results, and no formal convergence guarantees weaken rigor and evidence. Reproducibility is relatively strong with open-source code, hyperparameters, and architecture tables.
evidence: Abstract reports Aftab IQM HNS 6.479 and 0.86 probability of improvement over PQN.
Section 6.1 Table 5 reports Phase 1 IQM HNS: PQN 2.692, Alpha 3.536, Gamma 3.481.
Section 6.3 Table 9 reports Aftab 6.479 IQM HNS (95% CI [5.890, 7.210]) vs Gamma-Hadamax-Valid baseline 5.343.
Section 7.3 acknowledges limitations: discrete-action tasks only, static hyperparameters, no formal convergence guarantees.
Section 5.3 states code/models/logs are open-sourced and four seeds were used.

arxiv:2608.07333.rationale: Out-of-scope GNN/time-series forecasting paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology; transformer models appear only as baselines. TCV and GLIDE have some novelty and provide quantitative tables/ablations, but reported gains are extreme (e.g., Electricity MAE 0.010 vs 0.051) and split descriptions conflict, limiting rigor. Domain relevance is minimal, so score is capped near 0.20.
evidence: Table 3 reports Electricity MAE 0.010 for GLIDE vs 0.051 for FourierGNN, an 80% relative gain.
Appendix 0.E.1 states a 7:1:2 split while Section 3.4 states 60/20/20 for synthetic data.
Section 3.8 and Figure 5 provide ablations for D1/D2.

arxiv:2608.07328.rationale: Pure robotics/legged locomotion using deep RL; out of scope per instructions despite RL component. Technically moderate with ablations and sim-to-real, but no comparison against state-of-the-art fault-tolerant baselines and limited generalizability (single platform, flat real-world deployment without perception).

arxiv:2608.07323.rationale: Relevant to LLM/Transformer architecture and pretraining through a controlled SwiGLU vs closed-tail MemGLU comparison, but narrowly focused on FFN gate geometry. Paired small-scale runs with seeds, diagnostics, and limitations provide moderate evidence; generalizability is explicitly limited to 9M/30M models and no code release is reported.

Section 7.2 states evidence is limited to 9M and 30M decoder-only models and notes no fused kernel.
Appendix B lists model/training configurations, seeds, token budgets, and RMS calibration c0 values.

arxiv:2608.11259.rationale: Industry LLM tutoring report with direct use of LLM prompting, LLM-as-judge evaluation, model selection experiments, and agent workflow modifications. Results are self-reported with confidence intervals, but the contribution is mostly applied and not externally reproducible.
evidence: Page 9, Section 5.1 Concise Math Agent response: Time to full response latency (P50) decreased by 32.7% ± 1.0%; Behavioral engagement increased by 4.65 ± 2.98%.
Page 10, Section 5.1 Limit specific Math Agent guidance: Tutor giving away final answer decreased by 85.5% ± 5.56%.
Page 12, Section 5.3 Migrating Exercise from GPT-4o to GPT-4.1: Tutor giving away final answer decreased by 96.66% ± 4.66%; Behavioral engagement increased by 9.93% ± 2.11%.
Page 13, Section 6.1 Offline Evaluation vs Live Experiments: primary metrics rely on user actions, offline datasets are O(100), and live experiments are used for hill climbing.

arxiv:2608.07317.rationale: Moderately relevant as an assurance/position paper for agentic software development, but lacks LLM methodology and empirical validation.
evidence: Section 1 states it is 'a position paper and research agenda rather than a proposal for a new verification method.'
Section 4 states the architecture is a hypothesis 'not an implemented solution' and presents research questions without quantitative results.

arxiv:2608.07316.rationale: Moderate topical relevance: uses LLMs with persona prompting and SHAP/network features for psychometric inference, touching LLM, NLP, interpretability, and mental health, but it is an applied psychometrics study rather than core LLM/NLP methodology. Quality is limited by synthetic training data, absence of strong NLP baselines, text-length confounds, and modest single-corpus human transfer; strengths include systematic ablations, nested CV, and explicit limitations.

arxiv:2608.07314.rationale: Out-of-scope robotics/VLA post-training paper: despite RL and vision-language-action elements, it is a pure embodied-robotics application with no LLM/NLP or safety/reasoning methodology, capped at low relevance. The two-timescale module-level TD3 idea is incremental over prior VLA-RL and asynchronous VLA work. Results rely on sparse simulation tables and two real-world tasks, but Table I lacks error bars/statistical tests and no limitations or full hyperparameters/code are provided.

Section IV-B Table III: 5:1 frequency ratio yields SR5 81.7% vs 1:1 equal-frequency 77.7%.
Section IV-C Fig. 3: real-world reward curves over three seeds show TEMPO reaching and maintaining higher later-stage rewards than FLOWER-RL.
Section IV-C: real-world evaluation uses two tasks and 60 demonstrations per task on one robotic platform.

arxiv:2608.07636.rationale: Moderately relevant as an adversarial attack on a generative OCR vision-language model (AI safety/multimodal), but not core LLM/NLP. The paper is transparent about an incomplete pilot with no formal attack success, so evidence strength is low and generalizability is limited; novelty and reproducibility are moderate.
evidence: Abstract states first pure black-box attack against a generative OCR vision-language model and pilot exposes failures but no strict threshold.
Section 5.2 reports ASR 0/9 at tau=0.05 and targeted phrase never produced.
Section 7 Limitations states evidence is limited to Deep-OCR and a small incomplete pilot, with final controls pending.

arxiv:2608.07304.rationale: Out-of-scope FinOps/cost-efficiency application: it applies DEA/composite-indicator benchmarking to AI token spend rather than advancing LLM, NLP, or language-model methodology. The reporting is reasonably careful (config-driven pipeline, fixed seeds, perturbation validation), but the evidence is small-sample and domain-specific, with no language-model or NLP contribution and limited generalizability beyond internal token usage.
evidence: Abstract: introduces the Token Efficiency Index as a peer-benchmarked composite indicator for AI token efficiency.
Section 3.2: sample comprises 75 accounts grouped into 39 organizations from a Tokscale snapshot.
Section 5.3: perturbation validation reports 665/684 expected-direction score changes and no wrong-direction movements.
Section 7.1: limitations include only internally generated token usage and lack of external production API billing data.

arxiv:2608.07303.rationale: A transparent self-audit of short-budget AutoML benchmarking, relevant mainly to evaluation/benchmark and automated ML preferences rather than core LLM/NLP/agent topics. The paper quantifies test-set selection bias and unenforced budgets, reports corrected non-significant results, and provides a checklist. Novelty is incremental and some figures are marked pending, but the within-run paired measurement design and release of per-dataset logs strengthen evidence and reproducibility.
evidence: §5.1 reports the original 57.1% win rate at 60s and large significance values
§6.2 reports median wall-clock of 120s against a nominal 60s budget and ratio to AutoGluon of 2.24x
§7.2 reports corrected win rate falling to 34.3% with pairwise p-values of 0.39 and 0.66, no longer significant
Appendix B describes per-dataset JSONL files and regeneration scripts for all numbers and figures

arxiv:2608.07302.rationale: Relevant multimodal/interpretability paper on LVLM object hallucination, with attention and logit-lens analysis plus training-free mitigation. Moderate novelty in reframing hallucination as semantic inconsistency rather than weak attention, but rigor is limited by no statistical significance tests, no explicit limitations, and some notational ambiguity. Results cover multiple models and benchmarks but lack uncertainty estimates.
evidence: Section 5.1.2 reports LLCC detection Precision 0.7870, Recall 0.7955, and F1 0.7932 against Uncertainty Score, InterConf, and SVAR.
Section 5.2.2 reports CHAIR and AMBER results across LLaVA-1.5-7B, LLaVA-1.5-13B, Shikra-7B, and Qwen2-VL-7B.

No explicit limitations section or statistical significance tests are provided in Sections 5-6, and Section 4.2.2 contains a malformed CLOSE marker in Equation 12.

arxiv:2608.07301.rationale: Theoretical MDP identifiability paper matches the Reinforcement Learning preference via reward, policy, and Q-value concepts, but has no LLM/NLP/agent/vision relevance. The formal theorem-proof structure is rigorous and the limitations section is present, but there are no empirical baselines, ablations, quantitative results, or code/data artifacts.

arxiv:2608.07299.rationale: Medical imaging domain application: chest X-ray report-grounded abnormality segmentation. Despite using a vision-language/causal-LM Actor and a Qwen2.5-VL Verifier, the primary contribution is domain-specific medical image segmentation, which is out-of-scope under the rubric and capped at 0.20. The paper is technically detailed with ablations and transfer, but relevance to the core language/agent/reasoning preferences is limited.
evidence: Abstract: Proposes EliSeg, a propose-verify-revise framework for report-grounded abnormality segmentation and states code availability.
Section 4.2, Table 1: EliSeg achieves Report-Inferred IoU 59.4 and Dice 74.5 on MIMIC-CXR-ILS, outperforming text-based baselines.
Section 4.4, Table 4: Ablation shows Verifier and Revision jointly improve IoU from 49.0-49.6 to 54.1 using a shared Actor.
Section 5: Limitations include only seven findings, fixed Kmax=3, and external evaluation limited to Actor because CheXlocalize lacks paired reports.

arxiv:2608.07295.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application: an education policy simulation using RL/PPO and multi-agent sorting, with no LLM/NLP/transformer/language methodology. Although reinforcement learning is a listed preference, the direct topical match is minimal. The paper has formal convex-program analysis and ablations, but evidence is simulation-only with small headline differences and no real-world validation or code availability shown.
evidence: Abstract: 'A government planner uses reinforcement learning (RL) to identify multiyear allocation policies...'
Learning Allocation Policy: 'We use PPO (29) to learn a policy over full trajectories.'
Simulations and Experiments: 'Table 2 reports long-term average performance... PPO policy provides the strongest balance... MA 0.478 and GA 0.0164.'
Ablation Study: reports full model MA 0.4641, HC 111.99, GA 0.0122; evidence is simulation-based.
Appendix D.6: provides baseline parameters and PPO hyperparameters, but no code or real-world validation is shown.

arxiv:2608.07294.rationale: Tabular flow-matching paper is outside core LLM/NLP preferences but partially relevant via attention, soft mixture-of-experts-style processing, and synthetic data. Method is an incremental combination of existing EF-VFM with type-specific adaptive mixture modules and joint attention. Theoretical analysis and ablations provide moderate support, but evaluation is limited to tabular benchmarks and no code release is stated.
evidence: Table 1 and Section 5.2 report Shape/Trend/C2ST/MLE results and average ranks across eight tabular datasets.
Section 5.4 and Table 2 provide component analysis comparing FUSE variants across five matched seeds.

Appendix C.2 and Appendix D specify architecture and training details such as L=4 blocks, hidden dimension 256, AdamW with learning rate 1e-3, and Section 5.1 states main results are averaged over 20 random seeds.
The provided paper text does not state a public code release, though Appendices C and D give implementation and hyperparameter details.

arxiv:2608.07291.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/CV application with no language methodology, so relevance is very low despite healthcare AI topic. The paper adapts existing CMR foundation models (CineMA, CMR Transformer, CMRCLIP) for segmentation and LVEF regression; validation results are quantitative but limited by small N, no significance testing, and limited ablations.
evidence: Abstract: describes multi-view multi-modal cardiac MRI segmentation and direct ejection fraction estimation using CineMA, CMR Transformer, and CMRCLIP, with no language methodology.
Table 1: reports validation segmentation comparisons (CineMA vs scratch nnU-Net) with small validation samples N=15 cine and N=7 LGE.
Table 2: reports direct EF regression metrics MAE 4.965, PCC 0.911, and segmentation-derived EF comparisons.
Section 2.1: describes fine-tuning CineMA segmentation specialists; no new architecture or language component is introduced.

arxiv:2608.11258.rationale: Generic PSO-gradient hybrid optimization with only broad Training & Optimization term overlap (optimizer, gradient, Adam); no LLM/NLP/multimodal/safety/reasoning relevance. Method is modestly novel and statistically analyzed, but budget-normalized results show conditional value and generalizability is limited to low-dimensional continuous benchmarks.
evidence: Section IV-G, Table V: budget-normalized comparison shows PSO with equal budget wins 52.5% vs AHPSO 20.0%, Friedman p=7.0e-5.
Section IV-F, Table IV: AHPSO-Adadelta ranks first of 9 methods with Friedman p=9.75e-4.
Section IV-H, Table VI: sensitivity analysis shows stable rankings for tau in [0.2,0.4].
Section V Limitations: dual learning rate requires prior problem-class knowledge; finite-difference gradients impose 2d extra evaluations per particle.

arxiv:2608.07287.rationale: This is a clinical/medical imaging application of a foundation model for rs-fMRI headache classification, with no language methodology; under the rubric, pure medical imaging/domain applications are out of scope and capped at 0.20. The study provides quantitative comparisons and some controls (demographic model, sex stratification), but uses a small single-site cohort, no external validation, and only modest rigor.
evidence: Abstract: reports NeuroSTORM AUROC 0.82 (95% CI 0.82-0.82) and AUPRC 0.93 for headache vs non-headache and macro-AUROC 0.69 for subtype classification.
Table 2: compares demographic model AUROC 0.61, FC-based models (best AUROC 0.67), and NeuroSTORM embeddings (AUROC 0.82, AUPRC 0.93).

Section 3 Materials and methods: describes CONN preprocessing, Harvard-Oxford atlas 48 cortical ROIs for FC, NeuroSTORM input preprocessing, and leave-one-out cross-validation excluding all visits of held-out individuals.
Section 6 Limitations: acknowledges small cohort size, heterogeneous headache subtypes, limited mechanistic interpretability, and use of only rs-fMRI.
Data availability: source code is available on GitHub, but study data cannot be shared publicly and are available upon request with approvals.

arxiv:2608.10000.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/CV diffusion application. Uses an existing latent bridge matching formulation for breast DCE-MRI synthesis with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/alignment methodology. Evaluation is small and single-cohort, with no statistical significance testing and an optimistic ground-truth tumor-mask condition.
evidence: §1.5: method uses Stable Diffusion VAE and latent UNet, building on existing LBM concept from reference [1].
Table 1: reports validation metrics on 91 DUKE cases but includes no significance tests and only one LDM baseline.
§3 Discussion: acknowledges ground-truth tumor-mask conditioning as optimistic, modest cohort size, and domain-shift limitations.

arxiv:2608.07285.rationale: Pure audio/music AI-detection work outside the LLM/NLP/agent/vision-language scope; only tangential Speech & Audio preference. The paper presents a controlled CNN regression study on codec artifacts with quantitative results and released code, but overall score is capped at 0.20 per out-of-scope policy for pure audio.
evidence: Section 5.1: binary detector reproduction achieves 99.97% accuracy and 99.98% F1 on held-out FMA evaluation set, with track-level splits preventing leakage.
Section 5.5, Table 1: regression CNN at 5-second windows achieves MAE=0.076, RMSE=0.102, R^2=0.854, Pearson r=0.925; binary implicit estimate reaches MAE=0.289, R^2=-0.851.
Section 5.3 and Figure 2: stem-level analysis shows instrument-dependent detection sensitivity, with drums/guitar separating more clearly than vocals/bass.
Section 6: limitations state single EnCodec at 3 kbps, codec-reconstructed stems, no production post-processing, and untested transfer to other codecs or commercial generators.
Section 4.3: methodology uses 240 MoisesDB tracks and yields 21,212 mixes; a reproducible Python library is released.

arxiv:2608.07283.rationale: Relevant as an LLM/NLP case study using gpt-oss-120b for low-resource Cantonese–Irish translation and LFG f-structure generation. Rigor is moderate: clear task design, expert manual evaluation with inter-annotator agreement and statistical tests, but only 50 sentences, a single model, no automated validation or strong baselines. Evidence supports limited and largely negative/qualified findings. Generalizability is limited to one low-resource language pair and one model; reproducibility is partially supported by prompts, data, and rating schema but lacks code and outputs.
evidence: Section 3.2 describes six zero-shot tasks using gpt-oss-120b with temperature 0 and provides prompt formats.
Section 3.2.2 states evaluation was manual expert assessment with inter-annotator agreement in Table 1 (Cohen's kappa 0.45-0.92).
Table 2 reports translation faithfulness/fluency/both rates, with overall success no higher than 24%.
Table 3 reports f-structure ratings, with Irish Task 2 at 2% Excellent and shared Task 4 at 4% Excellent.
Section 3.3 reports McNemar tests showing no significant prompt-language effect (p=1.00) and Friedman/Wilcoxon tests for f-structure ratings.

arxiv:2608.07282.rationale: Relevant to multimodal vision-language and interpretability preferences, but not core LLM work. The paper uses off-the-shelf CLIP bi-encoders and Integrated Jacobians to model visual-world gaze, which is a moderately novel application of existing attribution methods. Rigor is moderate: controlled mixed-effects analysis but one small English dataset (18 items), several per-model interaction effects not significant, and only qualitative replication of human predictive processing. Generalizability is limited to one experiment and four CLIP checkpoints. Reproducibility is partially supported by model URLs, normalization details, and runtime appendices, though code is only promised, not provided.
evidence: Abstract: The approach combines a simple multi-modal bi-encoder model of the CLIP family with a bimodal attribution method and claims to robustly replicate a seminal English visual world study without generative architecture or fine-tuning.
§5: Population-level mixed-effects model shows significant pre-object verb-type effect (β=0.267, t=4.60, p<0.001) and significant verb type × region interaction (β=-0.235, t=-2.86, p=0.005).
§4.1: The dataset consists of 18 images from Altmann and Kamide, each containing five referents: one subject and four objects.
Limitations: The study is limited to four CLIP models and a single visual world experiment; the encoder models are not incremental and the model operates at token granularity.
Appendix A: Model URLs are provided, and walltime for a complete run ranges from 10 minutes for B/16 models to 90 minutes for L/14 models.

arxiv:2608.07281.rationale: Statistical learning theory paper on high-dimensional ridgeless least squares under spiked covariance. It has weak overlap with preferred topics (only Scientific AI via mathematical theorem/proof) and is far from LLM/NLP/agent/vision-language methods. Main results are asymptotic risk limits with simulations, but there are no full proofs, code/data, baselines/ablations, or explicit limitations, and the idealized linear spiked model limits generalizability.
evidence: Section 3, Theorem 3.1 states asymptotic risk limits for gamma<1 and gamma>1.
Section 3.2 Risk analysis describes simulations in Figures 1-4 but no external benchmarks or ablation studies.
Section 4.1 Proposition 4.1 and Theorem 4.1 classify benign, tempered, and catastrophic overfitting.
Appendix contains lemmas only; no code/data availability statement or full proofs.

arxiv:2608.07280.rationale: Relevant to alignment, reward modeling, preference learning, and multi-agent RL, but outside LLM/NLP-centric topics. The paper is a proof-of-concept in a single environment with modest baselines and limited statistical support for social-metric improvements; it explicitly acknowledges limited generalization. Code and hyperparameters improve reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.07279.rationale: Moderately relevant MLLM/token-communication paper with multimodal LLM and transformer components, but not central to Japanese LLM/NLP or language-model methodology. arxiv:2608.07275.rationale: Pure group-theory paper on finite E-groups and nilpotency class three. arxiv:2608.07274.rationale: Weak topical match: only AI Safety adversarial/defense terms align; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent methodology. Method combines known detection and decoupling ideas with limited substantiated novelty. Quantitative comparisons and ablations are reported, but rigor is weakened by repeated Lemma 0, deferred proofs, and inconsistent figure/table references. arxiv:2608.07271.rationale: Paper is an AR/HCI empirical user study on incidental visualizations; it does not address LLMs, NLP, transformer methods, reasoning, agents, or any preferred topic, so relevance is out of scope and capped. Methodologically it has a small homogeneous sample, non-parametric tests with zero-variance groups treated as implicitly significant, no significant primary-task performance differences, and limited reproducibility information.

arxiv:2608.07635.rationale: Clinical-trials/medical statistics application using an LLM as an interface for variable selection, R code correction, and report generation. It does not advance language-model or NLP methodology, so it is treated as a domain application with low topic relevance despite LLM use. Quantitative comparisons with expert selections are provided in Table 1, but evidence is limited to one dataset and lacks uncertainty measures; generalizability is weak and acknowledged in Section 6.

arxiv:2608.07267.rationale: Vision-language navigation with generative world-action modeling is only partially aligned with the core LLM/NLP/agent/safety preferences; it mainly touches Multimodal AI, embodied/robotics, RL, and video/temporal topics. The method combines existing DreamZero flow matching, VGGT geometry features, DAgger, and DanceGRPO into an incremental adapter/curriculum design. Evaluation includes ablations and quantitative metrics, but lacks statistical uncertainty, baseline table values are placeholders, unseen gains over the 2D control are small, and the consistency study is restricted to near-goal XY motion.

The paper uses controlled symbolic experiments, logit lens, patching, linear probing, and ablations to support its claims. The proposed looped architecture is known from prior work, so novelty is moderate.

arxiv:2608.07256.rationale: Pure 3D computer vision/3D canonicalization paper using an image-to-3D generative prior. No language-model, NLP, reasoning, agent, safety, or multimodal-language methodology; out of scope under the given rubric, capping overall relevance. arxiv:2608.07254.rationale: LLM/embedding-based taxonomy extension is in scope and uses LLMs centrally, but it is an applied scientometric system rather than LLM methodology research. The contribution is incremental over existing taxonomy construction and OpenAlex; evaluation is modest due to a small author-curated tuning set and no baseline comparisons, though downstream expert precision and public dataset release provide moderate evidence. Reproducibility is limited by undisclosed prompts/code and proprietary data.

arxiv:2608.07251.rationale: Moderately relevant LLM/NLP application using prompt-based sentence classification, sentiment scoring, and a structural overlay; not Japanese-focused and no core LLM advances. Method is incremental over iSent and descriptive results lack held-out labels, inter-annotator agreement, or predictive validation, limiting rigor and evidence strength. Reproducibility is partial because code and annotations are supplied but raw texts and model configuration are not included.

arxiv:2608.07632.rationale: Out-of-scope biology foundation model/microscopy cell representation benchmark; no LLM, language modeling, agent, reasoning, or language-based methodology. Although the work is reasonably documented and reproducible, topic relevance to the requested preferences is negligible and the rubric caps out-of-scope domain applications at 0.20.

arxiv:2608.07250.rationale: Domain-specific but directly LLM-focused evaluation of structured evidence extraction, prompting, chain-of-thought, and hallucination. Relevant to LLM evaluation and AI safety; limited methodological novelty and generalizability due to single microbe-cancer pair and single-institution expert panel.

Results 3.2.2: Hallucinations were rare but more frequent in smaller models; methodology and contradiction identification were persistent weaknesses.
Results 4.5 Limitations: Single microbe-cancer pair, 24 papers, seven experts from one institution.
Methods 2.6: Friedman, Wilcoxon signed-rank, and mixed-effects models with Bonferroni correction are reported.

arxiv:2608.07249.rationale: Ancient Greek NLP with character-level masked diffusion and transformer; relevant to NLP/transformer/training/data/evaluation but domain-specific and outside high-weight LLM/agent/safety preferences. Strong matched controls, significance testing, and released artifacts; generalizability limited to historical text tasks, and the paper acknowledges missing ablations.

arxiv:2608.07248.rationale: Pure mathematical optimization paper on mirror descent convergence with no LLM/NLP methodology. Tangential match only via the broad optimization preference; no empirical ML validation or language-model relevance.

Section 5 applies the framework to Shannon entropy, Fermi-Dirac entropy, and power kernels, not to language/LLM tasks.

arxiv:2608.07243.rationale: Relevant LLM iterative-generation/evaluation study using LLM-as-judge and CoT-style prompts, but the creative recipe domain is peripheral to core preferences and the evidence relies on proxy LLM evaluators with limited human calibration.

arxiv:2608.09999.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging transferability estimation study; no LLM/NLP/language methodology or agent/reasoning component. Generic pre-trained/evaluation terms are not enough for relevance. Methodological work is modest and domain-limited, so overall score is capped at 0.20.

arxiv:2608.09998.rationale: Pure computer vision carbon-footprint study using CNN/U-Net/ResNet/VGG/EfficientNet on CIFAR-10; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agents, or language methodology. arxiv:2608.07230.rationale: Formal work on causal orientation in probabilistic logic programming; outside LLM/NLP/agent scope, with only weak keyword overlap via causal reasoning. arxiv:2608.07224.rationale: Directly relevant theoretical work on stochastic autoregressive LLM generation and chain-of-thought vs end-to-end sample complexity. Provides formal theorems, tight separations, and a logistic case study with LPN hardness. Strong rigor and novelty; limited empirical validation and abstract binary-token setting reduce generalizability and reproducibility evidence.
