arxiv:2608.07222.rationale: Core LLM scaling-law methodology highly relevant to LLM pretraining/compute allocation. Skaling is an incremental extension of Chinchilla/Kaplan with a single coupling exponent, and a similar untied outer-exponent form appears in prior distillation scaling work, limiting novelty. Empirical evaluation across Farseer, SK-Grid, Farseer-code, and Chinchilla datasets with CV, baselines, and ablations is fairly rigorous, but gains are dataset-dependent and no code/data release is stated.

arxiv:2608.07220.rationale: Relevant mainly to interpretability/explainability preferences via interpretable ML models compared with LSTM benchmarks, but outside LLM/NLP/agent core. Quantitative CV results are reported, but the study is limited to one game/dataset, lacks statistical inference, has weak identification of memory length, and provides no code availability.

arxiv:2608.07214.rationale: Position/vision paper proposing a Causal World System for agentic AI and decision-making. It is conceptually relevant to agent and causal/counterfactual reasoning preferences, but it is not an empirical study: it provides no implementation, baseline comparisons, ablations, quantitative results, or code/data. Rigor, evidence strength, and reproducibility are therefore low despite broad conceptual generalizability.

arxiv:2608.07213.rationale: Strongly relevant LLM/text-to-SQL agent-memory paper with controlled evaluation of replay, retention, and transfer. Main findings have paired statistical support and careful threat analysis, but generalizability is limited by same-database dev-set scope and several exploratory single-seed probes.

arxiv:2608.07208.rationale: Relevant LLM/interpretability/NLP benchmark comparing frozen-activation linear probes and RFM concept vectors on ESG text. Controlled baselines and explicit limitations support moderate confidence, but single-domain evaluation, binary-only labels, and absent code limit strength.

arxiv:2608.07204.rationale: Relevant LLM/RAG/NLP system for scientific claim verification; incremental hard-negative reranking plus retrieval-conditioned classifier. Ablations and official results are reported but on small dev set, with no significance testing or code release.

arxiv:2608.07202.rationale: Domain application of LLMs to research integrity assessment of RCTs with ontology/provenance knowledge graph. It uses an LLM for structured extraction and external evidence aggregation, but contributes no LLM/NLP methodology and is primarily a clinical research integrity tool, placing it out of scope per domain-application restrictions. arxiv:2608.07199.rationale: Pure computer vision/3D shape optimization paper with no language-model, NLP, reasoning, or agent methodology. Transformer, flow-matching, and optimization terms appear only incidentally within a generative 3D shape pipeline. Experimental sections and appendices provide quantitative baselines and ablations, but the topic is out-of-scope under the stated criteria, capping the score at 0.20.

arxiv:2608.07196.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM-based multi-agent systems, system-level evolution, and prompting/agentic optimization. The method is moderately incremental over graph-based MAS and trace-driven revision work, but adds recurrence gating and paired validation. Rigor and evidence are moderate: quantitative comparisons and ablations are provided, but headline results rely on retrospective best-checkpoint selection on Test, and many accepted revisions regress. Generalizability is supported by four benchmarks and two LLMs, while reproducibility is aided by a code link, detailed appendices, and documented thresholds.
evidence: Abstract and Section 4.1 Table 1 state EMAS attains the highest task-weighted overall accuracy for both backbones and is best or tied in six of eight model–benchmark settings.
Section 4.1 Table 1 reports Qwen3.6-27B on MBPP improves from 55.09% to 89.12% accuracy while tokens per task fall from 5.16k to 1.95k, a 62.2% reduction.
Section 4.3 Table 2 ablations report Full EMAS 94.73% accuracy versus kappa=1 89.58% and No gate 65.56% on Game24 Qwen3.6-27B, with smaller average regressions.
Section 5 Limitations acknowledges 39 of 93 committed E2 revisions with exact-predecessor comparisons regress on Test, and headline results use best checkpoints observed retrospectively on Test.

arxiv:2608.09997.rationale: Vision Transformer interpretability via persistent homology partially matches Transformer Architecture and Interpretability preferences, but is pure computer vision without language methodology and thus out of scope. The work applies standard TDA descriptors to ViT representations; findings are qualitative, with no baselines, ablations, numeric tables, or statistical tests, and sparse point-cloud limitations are acknowledged.
evidence: Section IV-B: fixed validation analysis subset of 1000 images and a single designated validation image were used for topology tracking.
METHODOLOGICAL CONSIDERATIONS: ViT-Small/16 provides only 197 token representations in a 384-dimensional embedding space, resulting in extremely sparse sampling.

Section V-A: Bottleneck distance decreases from Epoch 1 to Epoch 100, with localized peaks near Layers 3, 10, and 12.
Section V-B: beta_2 remains nearly zero across all experiments, indicating absence of persistent higher-dimensional cavities.

arxiv:2608.07193.rationale: Relevant multimodal/LLM efficiency work using LLM proposers and a DSL for visual token pruning, but with moderate novelty relative to prior LLM-driven algorithm design. Main weaknesses: the search objective (MME) is also included in the reported aggregate, creating selection leakage; no statistical significance tests; no code URL; some large benchmark gains are under-substantiated.
evidence: Abstract: reports 14 benchmarks, three MLLM backbones, 94.4% token reduction, >99% performance retention, 9.9x FLOPs and 6.4x prefill latency reduction.

Experiments and Results, Table 1: reports per-benchmark results including MME and MMBench in the aggregate for LLaVA-1.5 and LLaVA-NeXT.
Supplementary Material, Table 14: reports search stability over four random seeds with identical best MME score.

arxiv:2608.07192.rationale: Out-of-scope embedded computer vision/TinyML paper on infrared sensor on-device prototype learning; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent methodology. Contributions are incremental and domain-specific.

arxiv:2608.07190.rationale: Pure PDE inverse-problem mathematics (reaction-diffusion-convection stability) with no LLM/NLP/ML methodology. Only weak 'scientific AI' keyword match via mathematics/theorem/proof. Provides mathematical proofs but no empirical datasets, baselines, ablations, or code, limiting evidence/generalizability for the target rubric.
evidence: Abstract: states the paper investigates an inverse boundary value problem for a reaction-diffusion-convection system and derives double/triple logarithmic stability estimates.
Section 1.3: positions the work within PDE inverse-problem literature and not AI/ML.

arxiv:2608.07188.rationale: Domain-specific classroom sensing and seating optimization using LightGBM, video behavior recognition, and CP-SAT; no language-model or NLP methodology, so preference relevance is very low. The paper is an incremental integration of existing sensing and optimization components with small-sample deployment and limited validation.

Section 2.6: describes deployment stack including Python, PyTorch, LightGBM, and OR-Tools but no code/data release.

arxiv:2608.09996.rationale: Medical-imaging/computer-vision application with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agentic content; only tangential Green AI/efficiency overlap. Comparative benchmarking is incremental and limited by single-run estimates, small datasets, and image-level split leakage, so the out-of-scope cap applies.
evidence: Abstract states the paper compares seven DL models for breast cancer detection and CO2 emissions on Breast Ultrasound and BreakHis 400X.
Section II-C1 states CodeCarbon EmissionsTracker was used for training/inference CO2 estimates.
Section V-A notes image-level split in Breast Ultrasound and CodeCarbon estimation error as internal validity threats.

arxiv:2608.07183.rationale: Moderately relevant multimodal uncertainty/Transformer paper, but outside core LLM/NLP/agent preferences. Integrates existing TMC, Mondrian conformal, and MBT components with some novelty in mask-conditional evidential scoring. arxiv:2608.07631.rationale: Partially in scope as an LLM-based full-duplex spoken-dialogue system with evaluation, but the core contribution is audio playback alignment middleware rather than language-model methodology. Quantitative results are supported by a controlled benchmark, ablation, and paired tests, though limited to one black-box speech model and synthetic listing-task trajectories.

Section 6.4, Table 5: FDB v1 mean quality score changes from 4.975 to 4.995 and mean latency increases by 58.7ms.

Section 6.3, Table 4: Ablations compare delimiter phrasing and lookback windows, with 10s lookback substantially degrading RAA to 65.74%.

arxiv:2608.07181.rationale: Scientific-visualization/topology paper on trait-induced merge trees for bivariate fields; no LLM/NLP/agent/vision-language methodology. arxiv:2608.07167.rationale: Relevant to LLM agents, AI safety, and prompt-injection guardrails, but quality is limited by a domain-adapted-vs-zero-shot evaluation and internal reporting inconsistencies in latency and ablation metrics.

arxiv:2608.07162.rationale: Out-of-scope econometrics/statistical methodology on kink detection in panel data, with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, multimodal, safety, or other AI/ML language methodology. arxiv:2608.07161.rationale: Pure scientific/fluid-dynamics domain application with no language, LLM, or NLP contribution; only tangential Transformer Architecture and Scientific AI relevance. arxiv:2608.07158.rationale: Low preference relevance: dynamic graph sparsification/GNN-related work is outside the core LLM/NLP/agent focus. arxiv:2608.07157.rationale: Federated-learning sub-model training paper with no LLM/NLP alignment; only weak relevance via distributed training/edge optimization. arxiv:2608.07155.rationale: Pure medical imaging/PET application using a feed-forward neural network for inter-crystal scatter recovery; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methods. arxiv:2608.07154.rationale: Pure robotics/embodied system integration field report. arxiv:2608.07630.rationale: Paper develops frequentist uncertainty estimators for deep learning by adapting linear-regression Ho and HC3 sandwich estimators with tangent features and EKFAC. arxiv:2608.07152.rationale: Directly matches RAG & Knowledge via hybrid dense/sparse retrieval, rank fusion, and vector database exact top-k execution, though it contains no LLM/language-model methodology. The method is a solid integration of known threshold-algorithm/block-max ideas into RAG retrieval, with formal correctness bounds, temporal snapshots, ablations, and confidence intervals. arxiv:2608.07151.rationale: Moderately relevant to interpretability and RL, but not to high-weight LLM/NLP/agent topics. The pruning framework is incremental, and evaluation relies on proxies with no human validation; results are partial and lack statistical comparisons.

arxiv:2608.07148.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM, agentic AI, and multi-agent RL preferences, but as a structured critical review and architecture synthesis it offers no original empirical experiments. arxiv:2608.07144.rationale: Out-of-scope 3D computer vision/3D Gaussian Splatting paper. arxiv:2608.07143.rationale: This paper is a systems-security and cellular baseband re-hosting study. arxiv:2608.07129.rationale: Purely mathematical PDE paper on nonlinear Fokker-Planck/diffusion equations and entropy functionals. arxiv:2608.07040.rationale: Partially relevant: LLM-based text-to-DSL for combinatorial optimization touches LLM, agentic routing, and NLP, but is primarily an operations-research domain application rather than core LLM/NLP methodology. Novelty is moderate relative to text-to-MILP work. Evaluation includes multiple baselines, 44 COP types, scalability, and existing benchmarks, but rigor is limited by a self-constructed benchmark, mixed base LLMs across baselines, reported near-perfect scores without statistical significance or error bars, and no visible limitations section. Evidence is quantitative but mostly from the authors' own benchmark; reproducibility is partially supported by an anonymous code link but prompts and solver-selection details are not fully described.

arxiv:2608.07624.rationale: Pure robotics/mechanical design paper on a reconfigurable tracked robot. arxiv:2608.07037.rationale: Out-of-scope pure financial/accounting time-series forecasting domain; matches transformer/attention only superficially, with no language, LLM, reasoning, RAG, agent, or safety methodology. arxiv:2608.07036.rationale: Resource paper for hand-drawn UML-to-PlantUML dataset and validation tool. Rigor is limited to documented dataset construction and PlantUML syntax/XMI validation. Reproducibility is strong due to public artifacts and scripts.

arxiv:2608.07035.rationale: Out-of-scope ads ranking/recommender systems case study with no language-model or NLP methodology; only tangential relevance via interpretability/efficiency. arxiv:2608.07029.rationale: Low topical relevance to the stated LLM/NLP/transformer/agent preferences; only weak alignment via graph learning and link prediction. arxiv:2608.07023.rationale: In-scope LLM/agentic knowledge-graph pipeline with multilingual NLP and grounding, but evaluation is partial, lacks baselines/ablations, and depends on proprietary data; contribution is moderately novel.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports processing 36,037 raw expertise strings, resolving 27,743 (77% Global Coverage) into 13,298 canonical skill nodes.

arxiv:2608.07020.rationale: Empirical software-engineering study of visual regression testing in GitHub PRs; it intersects 'software engineering/code review' only as a domain and contains no LLM/NLP/AI methodology. Within its niche, it has clear RQs and quantitative comparisons, but is observational, small-sample, and out of scope for the requested ML/NLP focus.

arxiv:2608.07019.rationale: Strongly relevant to LLM efficiency and quantization, with clear matching of LLM, transformer, and scaling/efficiency preferences. The method is a practical but incremental post-hoc discrete refinement stage within PTQ. Evaluation is fairly rigorous with multiple models, bit-widths, initializers, and ablations, though benchmark comparisons are mostly single-run and no code release is stated. Evidence is extensive but self-reported; generalizability is broad across model scales.
evidence: Abstract: positions method as post-training quantization refinement for large language models.
Section 4.2, Table 1: reports zero-shot accuracy across W4A16/W4A4 for Llama-3 and Qwen3 with RTN/AWQ/GPTQ/GPTAQ initializers.
Appendix B.9: includes ablations on neighborhood size K, coordinate ordering, and QuaRot seed stability.
Section 5: states limitations including calibration dependence and offline refinement cost.

arxiv:2608.07018.rationale: Pure computer vision maritime horizon-detection dataset and benchmark; no LLM/NLP/agents/reasoning/alignment or language methodology. The work has moderate dataset novelty and reproducibility via public code/data, but limited relevance to the targeted AI/ML areas and limited generalizability beyond icy maritime horizon detection.

arxiv:2608.07016.rationale: Out-of-scope digital forensics study on parental controls. arxiv:2608.07012.rationale: A 3D scene reconstruction/CV paper that uses a fine-tuned VLM and agentic structured-output refinement, giving partial LLM/multimodal/agent relevance, but it remains domain-applied CV rather than advancing core LLM/NLP methods. arxiv:2608.07007.rationale: Federated learning paper outside core LLM/NLP priorities; limited relevance via distributed training only. Method is incremental over proxy-based weighting, with moderate theoretical and empirical rigor, standard image benchmarks, and no code release.

arxiv:2608.07006.rationale: Relevant to RAG, multimodal language modeling, and visual QA. The DLM-specific source-coherence analysis and blank-controlled evidence admission are fairly novel, but the formal results rely on a restricted local source process and main accuracy results lack variance estimates or repeated runs. Cross-backend validation is good but domain-limited to visual RAG benchmarks; implementation details are extensive though no code release is stated.

Table 3 reports cross-DLM validation across LLaDA2.0-Uni, LLaDA-V, and Dream-VL.

arxiv:2608.07005.rationale: Pure robotics/motion-planning paper for mobile manipulators; no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, agent, or language methodology. It is explicitly out of scope and capped at 0.20 despite domain-specific contributions and experiments.

arxiv:2608.07004.rationale: Moderately relevant LLM benchmarking and reasoning-distillation paper applied to feedback controller design. It engages LLM, reasoning/CoT-style distillation, evaluation, and training topics, but the control-engineering domain and task-specific focus limit preference alignment. The benchmark and distillation comparison are somewhat novel, with detailed pass/fail metrics and multiple runs, but there are no statistical significance tests, only three real-world trials, no code/data availability statement, and limited scope to fully actuated second-order systems.
evidence: Abstract: GPT achieved 94.8% overall design success vs Qwen 50.0%; reasoning-distilled model outperformed answer-distilled and base model.

Section V: GPT and Qwen success rates on high-dimensional subset reported as 91.0% vs 33.1%, with differences in gain selection and transient-limiting mechanisms.

arxiv:2608.07003.rationale: Out of scope: training-free high-resolution image generation with Diffusion Transformers (SD3/FLUX) is image/video diffusion without language methodology, so capped below 0.20. The work shows moderate methodological novelty and empirical ablations, but no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent relevance.

arxiv:2608.07002.rationale: Pure robotics/haptic-sensing paper for guqin playing; no LLM/NLP/agent methodology is contributed. Out-of-scope under the rubric, with some quantitative sensor calibration and task results but limited AI/ML generalizability.

arxiv:2608.07001.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM long-context inference and KV cache compression, matching Large Language Models, Long Context & Memory, Inference & Serving, and Scaling/Efficiency preferences. arxiv:2608.06997.rationale: Generative cross-domain recommendation is a domain application outside the stated NLP/LLM focus; transformer/MoE components provide only tangential relevance and the overall score is capped at 0.20 as out-of-scope. arxiv:2608.06996.rationale: Out-of-scope pure robotics/manufacturing automation paper on flat ribbon cable harness terminal-to-housing assembly. Although it reports quantitative experiments, success rates, and limitations, domain relevance is negligible under the rubric and the overall score is capped at 0.20.

arxiv:2608.06994.rationale: Pure robotics/embodied world-action model with no LLM/NLP methodology; capped as out-of-scope. arxiv:2608.06993.rationale: Time-series reliability/predictive maintenance paper using small-data encoders and NAS; not LLM/NLP/language methodology. Only tangential transformer component. Experimental validation on one proprietary cryocooler dataset with 95 labeled sequences lacks statistical significance testing and has no empirical comparison to relevant time-series baselines, limiting rigor and evidence.

arxiv:2608.06992.rationale: Demo paper on a disambiguated LLM-derived knowledge base; highly relevant to LLM/knowledge/NLP topics but not a core LLM-method contribution. Quantitative evaluation is sampled and limited, lacks strong baseline comparisons, and construction details are not fully self-contained. Availability claims are present and useful for a demo resource.

Section 4.4 describes the OpenLink Virtuoso SPARQL endpoint and example queries over all 38.4M triples.

arxiv:2608.06991.rationale: Pure robotics/control paper on bidirectional propeller thrust reversals; no LLM, NLP, or AI/ML methodology. Despite robotics being a low-weight preference, the pure-robotics out-of-scope rule caps relevance. Control-theoretic proofs and experiments are present but do not align with the requested AI/ML focus.
evidence: Section III Theorem 1 gives necessary and sufficient reproducibility conditions and Remark 1 states linear thrust reversals cannot be reproduced with bounded motor input.
Section IV-A Corollary 1 states continuous voltage references require zero-crossing order r>=5.
Section V reports speed MAE/RMS and thrust RMS errors for Cases 1,4,5, showing higher-order reversals avoid localized peaks.

arxiv:2608.06990.rationale: No LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/etc. preference match: this is a generic density-aware hierarchical clustering method. The method is somewhat novel in combining hierarchical, density, and graph clustering, but evaluation is limited to ten low-dimensional synthetic datasets with no ablation or statistical testing, which limits rigor and generalizability. Code availability is claimed and equations/parameters are provided, supporting moderate reproducibility. Overall score capped low due to out-of-scope topic relevance.
evidence: Abstract: claims source code availability; proposes DHC-ECS clustering algorithm.
Section 4.1: reports NMI, ARI, FMI, Purity on ten synthetic datasets.
Table 2: lists dataset-specific parameter settings.
Section 4.2: reports O(N^3) worst-case time and O(N^2) space complexity.

arxiv:2608.06989.rationale: LLM inference/serving hardware-memory paper with moderate topic relevance via Inference & Serving and Scaling & Efficiency; not primarily an LLM/NLP modeling contribution. Novelty is moderate: dual-view mapping and accessor-aware scheduling are incremental over prior unified NPU-PIM memory designs. Rigor is limited by simulation-only validation, blurred baseline equivalences, no component ablations, and no sensitivity analyses. Quantitative evidence is present but self-reported from simulator; no real-hardware validation. Generalizability is claimed across memory technologies and NPUs but only evaluated on specific HBM-PIM simulation. arxiv:2608.09993.rationale: Out-of-scope medical/dental point-cloud registration with no LLM/language methodology; only low-weight medical imaging/computer vision relevance. arxiv:2608.06985.rationale: Out-of-scope HCI/AR reading interface with no core LLM/NLP methodology. LLM and TTS appear only as study-material generation and presentation; matched preference is marginal text-to-speech. The user studies include quantitative statistics, but findings are limited to controlled VR, Japanese text, and a specific headset, so relevance and generalizability remain low.

arxiv:2608.06984.rationale: Highly relevant to agents/tool use, AI safety, and red-teaming/evaluation. The lifecycle-stage benchmark is a moderate advance over carrier-specific benchmarks, with clear controls and quantitative results, but single-run trials, permissive non-interactive settings, reduced support in some harnesses, and incomplete artifact evidence limit evidence strength, generalizability, and reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: presents HarnessSafe, a benchmark of 328 executable cases across seven persistent-carrier families with a multi-stage, trace-based evaluation.
Section 3.3: defines seven families F1 Memory, F2 Skill, F3 Tool/MCP, T2 Memory-to-Skill, T3-S Subagent, T3-C Session Summary, and T3-A Shared Artifact.

arxiv:2608.07621.rationale: Uses Qwen2 LLM and VLA/reasoning, so not hard-capped as pure robotics, but remains domain-specific autonomous driving with limited core LLM/NLP contribution. Evaluation relies on one baseline (SimLingo) and lacks ablations/statistical analysis; code release is only promised.
evidence: Abstract: claims CMU-Drive benchmark and V2V-VLA baseline and that code/benchmark/checkpoints will be publicly released.

Section 3.5 Training Details: 180K training samples, LoRA fine-tuning, 12 epochs, batch size 8, 8 NVIDIA H100-80GB GPUs for 48 hours.

arxiv:2608.06981.rationale: Pure computer-vision/diffusion image-restoration paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology or other in-scope preference; thus relevance is very low and overall capped. The paper provides some theoretical propositions, quantitative comparisons, and ablations, but evidence is limited by a non-usable code link, incomplete implementation details, and narrow image-restoration scope.

arxiv:2608.06980.rationale: Conceptual/position paper on social facilitation and AI companions in creative reflection. It mentions AI/LLM agents but has no LLM methodology, no empirical experiments, baselines, ablations, or quantitative results; claims are largely speculative. Relevance to agent-related topics is only conceptual, and research quality is low.

arxiv:2608.07620.rationale: Out-of-scope image/flow-matching diffusion concept erasure with no language-model methodology; per rubric capped at 0.20. The paper has quantitative ablations and baseline comparisons, but relevance to LLM/NLP preferences is minimal and evidence is limited to 12 concepts without statistical testing or code availability.

Appendix C Limitation acknowledges computational overhead and evaluation limited to 12 concepts.

arxiv:2608.06977.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM prompting, bias, and safety. The study has a moderately broad empirical design but is incremental; statistical choices such as the balanced-reasoning baseline of p=0.5 are weakly justified, and multiple topic-level tests are not corrected. Main manipulation effects are well evidenced, but some claims overgeneralize relative to the reported topic/model variation.
evidence: Abstract: reports evaluation of six LLMs using 160 distinct prompts spanning ten topics and varying prompting strategy, support/challenge, polarity, user beliefs, and domain.

arxiv:2608.06976.rationale: Out-of-scope finite element/PDE numerical analysis for mixed-dimensional diffusion. Contains no LLM/NLP/agent/vision/alignment methods or other preferred AI themes. The mathematical development appears internally rigorous within its domain, with proofs and convergence experiments, but relevance to the target AI/ML curation preferences is absent.

arxiv:2608.06975.rationale: LLM role-playing dialogue with structured character-state evolution, benchmark construction, and LLM-as-judge evaluation. Strong topical match to LLM/NLP/evaluation/memory/training but incremental over prior persona trees, state machines, and profile-to-LoRA adapters. Multi-dataset and multi-backbone comparisons, effect sizes, and human correlation support moderate rigor; however judge is the same model used for extraction, the human descriptive subset is small, and update thresholds are manually set, limiting strength.
evidence: §5.2 reports PT ranks first in 21 of 24 internal dataset–metric cells and all 12 long-dialogue external cells in Table 1/Table 2.

arxiv:2608.06973.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/ecology application using RGB-thermal aerial wildlife video; no LLM, NLP, language, reasoning, or agent methodology. Method is an incremental application pipeline combining YOLO, SORT, DINOv3, and triplet loss, with a small test set (26 individuals, 8 males, 2 juveniles), no confidence intervals, and weak re-id/life-stage evaluation. Reproducibility is aided by public data/model links but not full code.
evidence: Table 1 (Section 4.1) reports thermal detection mAP@50 0.876 vs RGB 0.809 in perspective, with orthographic RGB dropping to 0.724.

arxiv:2608.06972.rationale: In scope as multimodal vision-language embedding evaluation with a generative LM readout, not a pure CV/application paper. Strong relevance to multimodal AI, evaluation benchmarks, embeddings, and QA. The benchmark reframes embedding quality as generative recoverability, but builds on prior probing and generative-readout work. Rigor is moderate: held-out test split, controls, ablations, and leakage audits are present, but only one decoder LM is used, the answerable pool is model-dependent, and main results come from single training trajectories.
evidence: Table 4 reports test-set scores for seven embedding models in visual-only and VL-joint modes.
Table 5 shows matched embeddings outperform zero and shuffled controls, especially in VL-joint mode.
Table 3 and Section 5.2 report decoder sensitivity ablations.
Supplementary S4.2 explicitly states results are from one trained decoder per model and CIs reflect test-item sampling, not retraining variation.

arxiv:2608.06971.rationale: Out-of-scope Riemannian manifold/shape clustering and medical imaging paper; no LLM/NLP, transformer, reasoning, RAG, agent, or language methodology. Though mathematically rigorous within its domain, relevance to the stated preferences is negligible and the real-data application is pure medical shape analysis.

arxiv:2608.06967.rationale: Highly relevant LLM evaluation benchmark with a language-model methodology focus. arxiv:2608.06965.rationale: Out-of-scope robotics/embodied-AI camera-robustness work: language is only a conditioning input and no LLM/NLP/language methodology is contributed, so personal relevance is minimal and subject to the <=0.20 out-of-scope cap. Research shows controlled same-data comparisons and ablations but limited real-robot scale and generalization.

arxiv:2608.06963.rationale: Biologically plausible learning paper with weak relevance to the LLM/NLP-oriented preferences; only indirect overlap with Training & Optimization/backprop learning. arxiv:2608.09992.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/3D CT generative modeling survey; no core LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology. arxiv:2608.06958.rationale: Pure diffusion MRI / medical imaging application with no LLM, NLP, or language methodology; only tangential attention-based set processing. Out-of-scope domain requires a low overall score despite moderate domain-specific experimental quality.

arxiv:2608.06955.rationale: Directly studies LLM evaluative behavior and cultural bias across 8 models, 200 films, forced-choice comparisons, Bradley-Terry ranking, prompt framing, and scale effects. arxiv:2608.06953.rationale: Strong topical fit to LLM agent memory, memory compression, long context, and factuality/grounding. arxiv:2608.06952.rationale: Out of scope for LLM/NLP curation: this is a face recognition biometrics security paper with no language, transformer, reasoning, agent, or Japanese LLM methodology. arxiv:2608.06947.rationale: Highly relevant RAG/LLM safety and interpretability paper proposing document-level attention-collapse detection. arxiv:2608.06946.rationale: Decentralized gossip-learning training paper with no LLM/NLP content; it matches broad Training & Optimization and Scaling & Efficiency preferences only. arxiv:2608.06938.rationale: Topically relevant to MLLM reasoning, language-prior/hallucination mitigation, and LLM post-training. Moderate novelty: text-only decoder debiasing and FFD are interesting but built on SFT/DPO/LoRA and prior visual-hallucination work. Rigor is limited by a single backbone, possible baseline comparability issues, no error bars/significance tests, and no limitations section. Evidence supports the main performance and retention claims but lacks uncertainty quantification. Generalizability is weak beyond one model and similar prior-conflict benchmarks. Reproducibility is partial: detailed appendices exist, but no code/data release is stated.
evidence: Section 5.2, Table 1 reports TACT average Accuracy 80.4% and prior-bias 18.2% vs Qwen3-VL-8B 66.8%/31.5%.
Section 5.3, Table 3 reports retention within 0.3 points on MMBench-en/zh, HallusionBench, CDH-CS, and VLind-CS.
Section 5.3, Figure 4 shows two-stage ablation with Stage1 primary and Stage2 complementary gains.
Section 3.1, Figure 2 provides pass@k and prior-lock@k evidence for decoder-level prior bias.
Appendix C/D describe FFD filtering, scene expansion, and QA construction checks.

arxiv:2608.06934.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application in urban walkability perception using sidewalk imagery and tabular respondent attributes. No LLM/NLP/language methodology, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, safety, alignment, or generative AI. Transformer components (Swin, FT-Transformer, fusion) are incidental and not language-model relevance. Research is moderately careful with ablations, seeds, statistical viewpoint comparisons, and code/data availability, but model comparisons lack significance testing and generalizability is limited (Australia only). Final score capped at 0.20 for out-of-scope domain application.
evidence: Section IV-C3 Table I reports QWK 0.285±0.023 to 0.469±0.026 after user conditioning.
Section IV-B reports Wilcoxon signed-rank W=207.5, Z=4.385, p<0.001 for sidewalk vs streetview ratings.
Section V states limitations: Australian locations and predominantly Australian-raised respondent pool, transferability untested.

arxiv:2608.06933.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM evaluation, benchmark construction, and RL training; the paper presents a detailed environment with supported but modest transfer results. Novelty is moderate because calibrated self-play question generation has prior work. Rigor is solid on protocol with seeds and ablations, but downstream gains are small and not statistically tested; generalizability is constrained to math.
evidence: Abstract: frontier models achieve below 50% calibration
Section 4.2 Benchmark Results: Gemini 3.1 Pro achieves 44.9% calibration
Section 5.2 Training Results: Table 1 reports pass@8 improvements on AIME 2022-2024, HMMT, and IMO-AnswerBench with no new math data
Appendix G.2: regrading with Claude Opus 5 changes calibration rates by at most 0.6 pp and preserves asker ranking
Appendix G.3: no-probing baseline drops calibration from 44.9% to 16.3%

arxiv:2608.06931.rationale: Relevant as a multimodal LLM benchmark with agent/tool-use, reasoning, and evaluation components, though it is scientific-domain rather than Japanese NLP. The paper provides quantitative baselines, ablations, judge-sensitivity checks, and public-subset reproducibility, but novelty over existing scientific MLLM benchmarks is moderate, domain breadth is limited, and tool-agent findings cover only six proprietary models. Evidence is fairly strong but some claims about evidence-bounded reasoning outpace the ablations.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports the best model, GPT-5.6-Sol (Max), reaches 48.7% accuracy and no model exceeds 50% across 19 MLLMs.
Section 4.4 reports only 921 of 20,088 text-only instances (4.6%) explicitly acknowledged missing visual evidence.
Section 4.5 reports all six tool-augmented models improve, with gains from 1.9% to 7.6%, best accuracy 52.7%, 411 tool-attributed corrections, and 145 tool-attributed errors.
Supplementary Information B.4 reports inter-judge agreement above 99.5% and Cohen's kappa exceeding 0.989.
Supplementary Information B.6 reports public-subset accuracies on 1,049 released questions closely tracking full-set results.

arxiv:2608.06930.rationale: Relevant multimodal audio-video captioning work with LLM-based GRPO reward, evaluation, and dataset contributions, but lacks strong match to top preferences such as Japanese LLM, reasoning, or agents. Novelty is moderate: atomic QA-based reward is an incremental extension of existing fact-checking and QA metrics. Rigor is adequate with ablations and multiple benchmarks, though no limitations section and potential self-judge benchmark bias. Evidence is solid across external and internal evaluations with alternative-judge checks. Generalizability is constrained to audio-video captioning despite two backbones. Reproducibility is good due to detailed hyperparameters, prompts, and availability claims.
evidence: Section 3.2 defines Da-GRPO using Raise-Answer-Check atomic fact verification and GRPO objective.
Table 1 reports external benchmarks including Video-SALMONN-2 and UGC-VideoCap.
Table 4 ablates Da-GRPO against SFT, N-gram reward, and holistic semantic reward.
Appendix A.3 provides detailed GRPO and rollout/reward node hyperparameters.
Appendix B.3 reports manual audits of 1,000 training captions and 100 probe-answer pairs.

arxiv:2608.06929.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/image-editing paper using flow matching and mask-based diffusion; it does not advance language-model methodology. Some technical novelty in mask-aware probability path and Soft-Poisson de-seaming, with quantitative baselines and ablations, but no statistical testing and unclear code/data release.
evidence: Abstract: frames contributions around regional image editing, masks, and flow matching, not language-model methodology.
Section 5.1: lists implementation details and evaluation metrics for image-editing comparisons.
Table 2: reports ablation study for MaskFlow and Soft-Poisson de-seaming.

arxiv:2608.06928.rationale: Pure audio/music recommendation study with no LLM or NLP methodology; only tangential transformer use via SASRec/TIGER. Capped as out-of-scope pure audio domain. The benchmark is systematic and includes quantitative tables, but novelty is niche/incremental, evidence is limited to two small music datasets with offline metrics, and some Semantic-ID configurations are unstable or collapse.
evidence: Abstract: evaluates six audio encoders across content-based, sequential, and Semantic-ID-based generative recommender systems.
Table 2: reports R@50, NDCG@50, and MRR@50 across audio embeddings for KNN, SASRec, and TIGER.
Table 3 and Table 4: present Semantic-ID width/depth and RVQ prefix analyses.
Limitation: acknowledges two relatively small-scale music datasets of approximately five thousand tracks and offline evaluation only.
Experiment Settings and Model configurations: describe embedding extraction settings, model hyperparameters, and five-seed evaluation.

arxiv:2608.06927.rationale: Cosmology paper on galaxy intrinsic alignments and joint BAO/RSD constraints; no LLM, NLP, AI/ML, or adjacent methodology. Pure domain application outside curator scope, so capped below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: presents joint cosmological analysis from galaxy intrinsic alignments with BOSS and DESI imaging; no AI/ML methods.
Conclusions: discusses dark-energy constraints and future spectroscopic surveys; astrophysical methods are not relevant to the preferred topics.

arxiv:2608.06926.rationale: Team-communication NLP application using LDA/clustering with only a brief Llama prompting comparison and agent-intervention context, so relevance to core LLM/agent methodology is limited. The pipeline is standard and the contribution is mainly applied; statistical analyses are present but lack held-out validation, involve some causal overclaims, and no code release is described.
evidence: Early Prediction: 47% accuracy at 10% transcript vs 15.8% majority baseline
Method Comparison and Optimization: NMF(6)+GMM(16) achieved Rbar^2=0.254 vs baseline 0.185 and 24x speedup
Cross Domain Methodology/Performance Prediction: Study 4 Rbar^2=44.3%, DELI 14.8%, GAP p=0.253
Llama Behavioral Extraction: Llama 3.3 70B produced generic labels and failed to extract meaningful behavioral patterns

arxiv:2608.06922.rationale: Relevant LLM multi-agent negotiation study with emotion prompt conditioning and safety implications. Controlled design across five models, 350 products, and two budget levels, but no statistical significance testing, some table numbering inconsistencies, and limited generalizability to simulated price negotiation.
evidence: Experimental Setup: 36 emotion-pair matrix, 350 products, two budget levels, five LLMs, three repetitions.
Results RQ1: buyer emotion deal rates and PRR_B values reported.
Results RQ4/Appendix D: cross-model outcome rates and constraint violations.
Conclusion: limitations include controlled setting, limited discrete emotions, and prompt sensitivity.

arxiv:2608.06919.rationale: Out-of-scope pure LiDAR/computer vision/robotics self-supervised learning; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, or language methodology. Tangential keyword matches such as foundation model and transformer do not overcome the domain exclusion. Methodological ablations and code availability are moderate, but overall relevance is minimal.
evidence: Abstract: topic is self-supervised learning of LiDAR point representations, not language modeling or NLP.
Section III: method extends Sonata with sparse view augmentation, memory bank, and cross-modal distillation for LiDAR.
Table II: reports ablations for sparse view, memory bank, and cross-modal distillation on TartanGround and Waymo.
Section IV-C: compares against supervised PTv3 and notes gains only in low-data regimes.
Appendix Table VI: provides hyperparameters; Abstract gives GitHub availability.

arxiv:2608.06918.rationale: This is an ontology/digital humanities archival paper, not an LLM/NLP/AI methods paper. It has only weak topical contact via future knowledge graph/semantic search, so preference relevance is very low. It shows some formal methodology (BFO, ODK, OBO Foundry) but no quantitative results, baselines, ablations, or completed competency-question validation.
evidence: Abstract: presents BZKO ontology for BZK card index / Wiedergutmachung archival data; no ML/LLM methodology.
Section 4: describes two-layer BFO-based ontology design and ODK-based development.
Section 5.1-5.3: details ontology classes/relations; no quantitative evaluation or baseline comparisons.
Section 7: validation via competency questions is ongoing; future work includes knowledge graph generation and extensions.

arxiv:2608.06917.rationale: Moderately relevant multimodal LLM paper proposing a recipe graph generation dataset and two-stage SFT+GRPO framework. It engages with LLM/VLM topics, reasoning chains, and RL fine-tuning, but its food-computing domain focus and vision-heavy application limit alignment with core LLM/NLP preferences. Methodologically solid with diverse baselines, ablations, and human validation, though low absolute scores, single-reference evaluation, and limited backbones constrain impact and generalization.
evidence: Section 5.2 Evaluation Protocol
Table 8 Comprehensive performance comparison
Section 5.5 Ablation Study
Table 3 Annotation review consistency

arxiv:2608.06916.rationale: Hardware/software co-design for mixed-precision quantization is outside the core LLM/NLP/agent preferences; relevance is limited to quantization/efficiency and some TinyLLaMa edge evaluations. The empirical evaluation is broad with baselines and ablations, but lacks significance testing and explicit limitations, and claims are only modestly supported by reported tables.
evidence: Sec. VIII-C, Table XIV reports proxy-guided BitFusion latency ratios versus BOPs-guided ratios for VGG7 and ResNet-18.
Sec. VII-B, Table IV reports PTQ search accuracy across models and baseline methods.
Sec. VII-E, Table VII ablates orthogonal initial sampling and near-constraint sampling effects.

arxiv:2608.06914.rationale: Out-of-scope pure medical imaging/computer vision application without language methodology. The paper is a staged diagnostic study of biplanar rib-fracture detection/localization; despite some methodological care, it lacks LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning relevance and is capped at <=0.20.
evidence: Abstract: states staged diagnostic study of biplanar rib-fracture reconstruction from CT-derived projections; no LLM/language methodology.
Section 3.1 Data and projection: uses orthographic projections from RibFrac/RibSeg CT volumes with patient-disjoint splits.
Section 4.5 Sealed-test confirmation: reports 2.50% end-to-end commitment yield at 10 mm, 0.436 false 3D points per case, n=55; dual-view availability 61.1%.
Section 5 Limitations and Threats to Validity: simulated projections, small sealed cohort, and no fracture-negative cases in sealed cohort.

arxiv:2608.06913.rationale: The paper intersects multimodal AI and video/language modeling by using Qwen3-VL-8B as an LVLM with structured QA, but it is a surveillance video anomaly detection application rather than a core LLM/NLP contribution. The bidirectional LVLM-detector loop is incremental over prior mutual/cooperative and one-pass VLM transfer work. Evaluation is limited to UCF-Crime with one detector/LVLM and no uncertainty estimates, though ablations and implementation details are adequate.
evidence: Abstract reports UCF-Crime AUROC improvement from 88.15% to 88.63% and AP from 37.25% to 42.46%.
Implementation details section states the LVLM is Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and the detector is UR-DMU.
Ablation Studies Table 2 reports full configuration AP 42.46% and random clip selection AUROC 86.54%.
Conclusion claims improvements over one-pass representation transfer under same model and inference settings.

arxiv:2608.06912.rationale: This is a GPU differentiable top-k operator paper. It has only tangential relevance via sparse MoE/token routing/retrieval and efficiency, but no LLM/NLP/language modeling, transformer attention, reasoning, RAG, safety, or other core preferences. Main empirical applications are adversarial image attacks and image coding, which are out-of-scope; capped at 0.20. Technical content includes formal bracketing analysis and benchmark tables, but reproducibility is limited by no code/data release and narrow domain evaluation.
evidence: Section 4 and Appendix C present the binomial order-statistic bracket, Theorem 2, and Proposition 1.
Section 5 Table 2 and Table 3 provide runtime and budget accuracy comparisons against DFTopK and other operators.
Section 6 Table 4 and Figure 6 report sparse adversarial attack results and budget-success curves.

arxiv:2608.06909.rationale: Highly relevant LLM-agent trajectory attribution benchmark spanning agent tool use, safety, evaluation, and interpretability. Contribution is moderately novel via unified component schema, attack/execution chains, and reusable annotation skill, but only two simple baselines, LLM-assisted validation, and limited independent evidence reduce confidence.
evidence: Section 5.1 reports 1,351 trajectories from AgentDojo, Agent3Sigma Stage, and Agent3Sigma Canary.
Table 5 reports primary attribution Hit@1/MRR for incremental and leave-one-out baselines.
Table 6 stratifies primary attribution performance by attribution distance.
Section 9 notes the benchmark covers only three benchmark families and evaluates only two simple attribution baselines.

arxiv:2608.06908.rationale: Relevant to AI safety/fairness and NLP evaluation, but outside core LLM/reasoning/agent preferences; uses older embedding models. Method is incremental since ZCA whitening is established, though its application to WEAT is systematic. Broad 70-combination experiments with full result tables support main claims, but no empirical comparison to existing anisotropy corrections and limited sensitivity analyses temper rigor.
evidence: §5.1 Table 2 shows raw vs whitened mean pairwise cosine similarities across seven models, e.g., GPT-2 0.997→0.001 and GloVe 0.192→0.040.
§5.3 and Appendix C report 12 Disappearing and 10 Emerging significance changes among 70 model-task combinations (22/70, over 30%).
§5.2 Table 3 reports Spearman improvements on WordSim-353/SimLex-999 for GPT-2 (WS-353 0.263→0.620; SimLex-999 0.097→0.411).
§6.3 acknowledges limitations including no sensitivity analysis for ε and sensitivity to the reference corpus.

arxiv:2608.06907.rationale: Pure quadruped robotics/embodied AI paper using vision-guided reinforcement learning; no LLM/NLP/language methodology, so out of scope and capped at <=0.20. Research quality is moderate with simulation and real-world baselines, but limitations are acknowledged and evaluation is task/workspace-specific.
evidence: Abstract: ball-catching task for legged robots and no language model content
Section 4: simulation and real-world catching success rates
Section 5: limitations include flat terrain, external camera, and no isolation of time conditioning

arxiv:2608.06904.rationale: Out-of-scope HCI/VR perception paper with no LLM/NLP/AI relevance. It introduces a new questionnaire construct and reports expert review, but lacks empirical validation, quantitative results, psychometric reliability, or reproducible item-level details. The rubric caps such pure domain applications at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: proposes 42 Likert-type items; no quantitative validation reported
Section 2.2: two expert interviews provide preliminary content validity; one unclear item removed
Section 3: future work will evaluate in VR; reliability and internal structure not yet assessed

arxiv:2608.06902.rationale: Out-of-scope materials-science simulation study of Li-ion transport in ZIF glass electrolytes using a DeePMD machine-learning interatomic potential. It has no LLM/NLP, agent, reasoning, or language-methodology relevance; only weak overlap via Scientific AI/simulation. The simulation work appears reasonably careful within its domain, but it is a pure domain application and is capped near 0.20.
evidence: Abstract/Page 1: uses a machine learning interatomic potential to simulate Li+ transport in crystalline and glassy ZIF-4 and ZIF-62.
Page 8, Section 2.3: reports activation energy decreases from 0.36/0.34 eV to 0.16 eV and diffusion coefficient increases.
Page 19, Section 4.1: describes fine-tuning a pre-existing DeePMD potential with lithium-specific interaction data.
Page 27, Code and Data Availability: states complete simulation workflows and the trained deep learning potential are available on GitHub.

arxiv:2608.06901.rationale: Relevant multimodal/efficiency paper on VLM pruning, but not core LLM/reasoning/agent topics. Novelty is moderate: variance-based importance plus adaptive layer-wise sparsity builds on Wanda/SparseGPT/Multiflow. Rigor is moderate with multiple benchmarks and ablations, though no explicit limitations section and some zero-shot comparisons are less balanced. Evidence from tables supports the main claims, and generalizability across CLIP/BLIP/Qwen2-VL and tasks is good. Code is claimed but not verifiable from the document.
evidence: Section 4.1 (Experimental Setup): describes CLIP/BLIP/Qwen2-VL, datasets including CIFAR, ImageNet, MSCOCO, Flickr30K, ScienceQA, baselines Wanda/SparseGPT/ECoFLaP/Multiflow, and sparsity levels 45-65%.
Table 3: reports zero-shot retrieval and classification results for CLIP at 55-65% sparsity, showing PORTA competitive or better especially at 65% sparsity.
Section 4.5 (Ablation between Importance and Sparsity Allocation) and Table 6: cross-combination study showing both variance score and PORTA ratio contribute.
Section 4.4 (Calibration Data and Sample Size): reports robustness of PORTA across Flickr30K/MSCOCO/Visual Genome and calibration sample sizes.
Table 8: reports pruning time comparison, with PORTA ~195s vs SparseGPT 773s, Wanda 151.61s, ECoFLaP 402.28s, Multiflow 229.65s.
Appendix 0.A: reports Multiflow comparison with and without fine-tuning, indicating PORTA remains stronger under a fine-tuning protocol.

arxiv:2608.06900.rationale: Pure audio generation benchmark, outside core LLM/NLP scope despite using LLM-based annotation, LLM-as-judge metrics, and agentic audio orchestration. The paper is reasonably rigorous within its domain, with manual QC, multiple subsets, and quantitative metrics, but it does not advance language methodology and is capped as a pure audio application.
evidence: Abstract: introduces MMAG with approximately 4,000 manually verified clips, voice cloning and timestamp subsets.
Section 3.2: human quality control includes three rounds with approximately 90% final spot-check pass rate.
Section 4.2: automatic metrics include FD/KL/IS, WER/UTMOS/SPK-SIM, CLAP/AAJ, and speech/sound F1.
Section 6 Limitations: notes 10-second duration, single-speaker English restriction, and imbalanced sound/music categories.

arxiv:2608.06898.rationale: Relevant position paper on evaluating LLMs/foundation models for social robots, touching LLM-as-judge, safety benchmarks, agentic simulation, and deployment cost. But it is a workshop proposal with no empirical results, quantitative validation, or released artifacts; robot-centric domain focus and absent implementation limit rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: identifies five evaluation dimensions: conversational competence, user safety, embodied character, target scene effectiveness, audience appropriateness.
Section II: presents the three-tier evaluation funnel (Tier 1 curated static evaluation, Tier 2 simulated interactions, Tier 3 robot-specific evaluation).
Table I: maps benchmark exemplars across dimensions and tiers, with empty cells marking open gaps.
Section III: describes a Haru social robot case study with Japanese high-school students.

arxiv:2608.06896.rationale: Survey/chapter on weakly supervised classification (ConfDiff, complementary-label, partial-label benchmark). Marginal alignment with core LLM/NLP preferences; formal theorems are present but proofs and empirical benchmark results are deferred to external papers, weakening in-document evidence.
evidence: Abstract: describes confidence-difference classification, complementary-label learning, and PLENCH benchmark.
Section 3.3.1: Theorem 1 states an equivalent risk expression for ConfDiff classification.
Section 5.3: states detailed benchmark results are deferred to Wang et al. (2025b).

arxiv:2608.06894.rationale: This is a PDE neural-operator/scientific-physics domain paper with no LLM or language methodology, so preference relevance is capped at 0.20. The edge-conditioned spectral modulation and physics-aware reweighting are moderately novel but incremental over existing adaptive spectral operators. Quantitative benchmark coverage is broad, but evidence lacks uncertainty quantification and the paper lacks an explicit limitations section; code and training details improve reproducibility. Overall score remains low primarily due to out-of-scope domain relevance.
evidence: Abstract: claims state-of-the-art performance across nine PDE benchmarks and code availability.
Table 2: reports ESO best on all four structured-mesh benchmarks.
Table 3: reports ESO best on all five unstructured-mesh benchmarks.
Table 4: ablation shows PVMM and PAR both improve baseline performance.
Table 5: ablation of PVMM variants shows combined local statistics perform best.
Appendix C: provides training details and hyperparameters for structured and unstructured benchmarks.
Figure 5: reports resolution generalization on Darcy Flow.

arxiv:2608.06893.rationale: Out-of-scope image diffusion/Schrödinger bridge restoration paper with no language-model methodology; even though it contains formal theory and preregistered experiments, the domain cap limits overall score.
evidence: §4.3 Table 1 reports white FID 7.87±0.06 vs matched 8.45±0.13, showing matched-first ordering does not transfer on FFHQ.
§4.4 reports the converged recipe increases the matched–white FID gap from 1.36 to 2.43 at NFE 10 and from 0.58 to 1.18 at NFE 50, refuting the ridge-whitening prediction.
§4.5 states the white-over-matched inversion persists with real FFHQ statistics and vanishes on a Gaussian corpus, implicating non-Gaussian per-mode statistics.
§3.3 Theorem 3 and Proposition 1 provide finite-step proportionality and x*(T)=(2 ln T)^-1/2 claims for the Gaussian regime.

arxiv:2608.06892.rationale: Pure domain application of reinforcement learning and graph neural networks to distributed quantum circuit compilation; not LLM/NLP/agent/transformer work, so capped at low relevance despite some overlap with RL/GNN preferences. Quality is moderate: it provides quantitative heuristic comparisons and reward ablations, but scalability is limited and no code availability is stated.
evidence: Section IV-A4 defines the multi-term reward with latency, split, progress, lookahead, and completion terms.
Section VI-A and Figure 5 report RL is lower than Pytket-DQC on random circuits but substantially worse than DISQCO on quantum volume circuits.
Table III reports Full RL average split counts of 39.0 for random and 28.7 for QV, versus DISQCO 35.7 and 11.9 respectively.

arxiv:2608.06891.rationale: Highly relevant to agents, LLM interpretability, and evaluation; method is an incremental application of linear representation directions to SKILL.md quality scoring. Moderate evidence with positive-negative separation, downstream uplift correlation (r≈0.78), and revision gains, but C1/C2 discrimination is modest, no strong external baselines/confidence intervals, and dataset/code details limit reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: proposes SkillEval and decomposes quality into applicability, content quality, execution guidance, robustness.
Main Result: reports mean validation scores for 259 positive vs 259 negative skills, with gaps 0.98/1.36/1.28/1.10/0.86/0.75 across A2/B1/B2/D1/C2/C1.
Hidden-State Layer Analysis: at layer 16, C1 and C2 validation AUROC are 0.701 and 0.721.
Metric Correlation with Downstream Task Pass Rate: Pearson r=0.779-0.787 for B1/B2/C1/C2/D1; all-metric r=0.716.
Skill Diagnosis and Targeted Revision: mean downstream pass rate increases from 18.6% (D) to 38.3% (G) to 48.1% (M).
Bias Analysis: most metrics show weak length correlations, with B2 r=-0.355 as the highest.
Cross-Backbone Robustness: pairwise correlations 0.948 (Qwen family), 0.913 (Llama family), 0.811-0.845 cross-family.

arxiv:2608.06886.rationale: Pure computer vision image dehazing with no language/LLM methodology; despite Mamba/state-space mentions, topic is out-of-scope. Quantitative results use only no-reference perceptual metrics on unpaired real-image benchmarks, limiting strength of evidence.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: proposes HazeSpikeMamba for real-world dehazing and reports BRISQUE/NIMA on RTTS/URHI/HSTS.
Page 9 Section IV.A: evaluation uses RTTS, URHI, HSTS with no paired clear references, assessed by BRISQUE, SSEQ, NIMA.
Page 10 Table I: RTTS quantitative comparison shows adaptation changes BRISQUE from 30.13 to 27.72 and NIMA from 4.13 to 4.87.

arxiv:2608.06885.rationale: Out-of-scope cyber-physical GNSS spoofing/UAV swarm security paper with no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, agent, or language-model methodology. Security-adjacent keywords are not AI-safety/LLM evaluation; simulation-only domain study.
evidence: Abstract: rigid-covert GNSS spoofing of UAV swarms; no LLM/NLP/AI methodology
Section 7: Tier-1/2/3 simulations with ArduPilot and Gazebo; no RF hardware or physical swarm
Section 10: all results simulation-based, no physical validation

arxiv:2608.06884.rationale: Moderate relevance: uses an LLM (GPT-5.1) as one comparative georeferencing method and includes NLP-based place/relation extraction, but the core contribution is a geospatial/biodiversity application rather than LLM or NLP methodology. Quality is moderate: the pseudo-NGP benchmark and relation-type ablations are useful, but manual verification is small, no significance testing is reported, and the setting is New Zealand-specific and point-only.
evidence: Section 4, Table 4 reports probabilistic median error 1.43 km and A@1 36%; LLM median error 1.80 km and A@1 31%.
Section 3.2 estimates about 60% precision from a manual audit of 50 candidates and about 312 true NGP mentions.

Section 3.3.4 describes probabilistic likelihood construction and uncertainty parameter estimation.

arxiv:2608.06880.rationale: In-scope LLM agent skill adaptation with strong agent/RAG relevance. Evaluates on 3 benchmarks and 3 backbones with ablations and cost analysis, but quantitative evidence is self-reported without variance or significance testing, no code release, and novelty over prior skill composition/refinement is moderate.
evidence: Section 2.2 and Table 1 diagnose skill-induced regressions across ALFWorld, WebShop, and SearchQA for Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-32B, and Gemini 2.5 Pro.
Table 3 reports main results and stage ablations across all nine benchmark-backbone settings.
Table 4 reports instance-level transfer and regression analysis relative to no-skill execution.
Table 5 reports adaptation overhead and execution-cost savings.
Appendix A.6 includes the full SkillAligner prompt template and structured output schema.

arxiv:2608.06878.rationale: Out-of-scope image/video diffusion and computer vision paper: layout-guided multi-instance image generation for MM-DiTs. Relevance is limited to weak overlap with Transformer/RoPE and multimodal image generation; no LLM/NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, alignment, or language methodology. Quantitative tables and ablations are present, but final score is capped at <=0.20 by the stated out-of-scope policy.
evidence: Abstract: reports >80% latency and >50% memory reduction claims.
Experiments Table 2: self-reported efficiency comparison on A100.
Ablation Study Table 4: reports UILC mask ablation results.
Methodology: describes Anchored 4D-RoPE and UILC attention mask.

arxiv:2608.06876.rationale: Limited relevance: a federated video anomaly recognition method using CLIP/prompt learning and axial attention, overlapping multimodal/VLM and efficiency topics but not LLM/NLP. Research quality is moderate: extensive benchmark tables, ablations, and convergence analysis support the method, but no code/error bars and some SOTA claims are tempered by Fed-WSVAD outperforming on XD-Violence.
evidence: Section 4.2 introduces the global normality prototype aggregation and local re-centering.
Table 2 reports FedVAR mAUC 91.06 on UCF-Crime Random split.
Table 5 reports FedVAR AUC 86.36 on UCF Random and 84.97/86.35 on Event/Scene splits.

arxiv:2608.06871.rationale: Relevant to LLM agents, MCTS, LLM-as-judge, and code-based optimization, but empirical rigor is limited: one main quantitative benchmark with Optuna, single-run CEDAR results, no statistical significance tests, and LLM-judge circularity. In-depth experiments cover two systems, with broad domain claims insufficiently supported.

Experimental Details states 20 node selections with 5 new candidates each, totaling 100 expansions per search, and $10-$50, 30 minutes per run.
Fitting an Abstract Goal Described in Natural Language provides qualitative World Dynamics trajectories but no quantitative scoring of the abstract-goal result beyond the LLM judge.

arxiv:2608.06869.rationale: Multimodal video QA and NLP evaluation for medical instructional videos; uses BERT/CLIP retrieval and temporal grounding but lacks LLM, Japanese NLP, reasoning, agentic, or safety/alignment themes, so relevance is modest. The difficulty-aware planner is incremental over VCMR methods. Rigor and evidence are moderate due to official leaderboard and validation ablations, but limited by single run, no significance tests, and domain-specific assumptions.
evidence: Table 2 reproduces official leaderboard results
Table 4 reports validation-set component ablations
Section 5 discusses limitations including no repeated-seed variance or significance tests
Section 4.2 provides implementation details

arxiv:2608.06867.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM routing, evaluation, agentic/multi-agent orchestration, and cost-aware inference. Contributes a unified routing formulation, a multi-scenario benchmark, and an open-source library. Rigor is moderate: broad router comparisons and deployment studies, but no statistical significance/error bars, small vision/video and real-user subsets, and some weak multi-turn results limit evidentiary strength.
evidence: Abstract states LLMRouter provides a unified formulation, xRouteBench, and an open-source library with 16+ routers.
Section 5.2 Table 2 reports GraphRouter average 45.46 versus Largest-LLM baseline 38.72 in the performance-first setting.
Section 5.4 Table 4 reports PersonalizedRouter accuracy 83.05 on held-out real-user Slack preference sessions.

arxiv:2608.06865.rationale: Relevant multi-agent MLLM reasoning for deepfake video forensics, touching agents, multimodal AI, reasoning, and AI safety. The dataset and four-agent decomposition are useful but incremental; OOD gains are modest (F1 53.28), and rigor is limited by the absence of significance testing, a clear limitations section, and independent validation beyond the authors' benchmark. Reproducibility is aided by detailed prompts and training settings but no explicit data/code release statement is given.

arxiv:2608.07619.rationale: Embodied robotics/VLA application with only incidental use of a Qwen3-VL-2B vision-language backbone; core contribution is geometric world modeling for robot control, not LLM/NLP methodology. This falls under the pure-robotics/domain-application out-of-scope cap. Reported LIBERO/Plus and real-world results provide some quantitative support, but ablations are limited and no code/data release is stated.

Experiments: Experimental Setup: Qwen3-VL-2B backbone, VGGT-Ω encoder, LIBERO/LIBERO-Plus benchmarks and baselines
Table 1 and Table 2: LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus success-rate comparisons

arxiv:2608.06862.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, agent security, red teaming, and persistent memory. The self-synthesized persistent-artifact attack is a meaningful twist, but rigor is limited by a small base dataset (30 chains), no error bars, no code/data release, and reliance on LLM judging, so high ASR claims need independent verification.
evidence: Abstract: reports >93% Chain-1 and >72% Chain-2 ASR
Section 4.1: describes CuaChain dataset, frameworks, defenses, and QLoRA training
Table 1: Chain-1 ASR across No Defense/Sandwich/Skill Vetter/GuardAgent
Appendix C.2: supervision budget ablation with 50-149 SFT pairs
Appendix C.4: human validation reports 96% agreement and Cohen's κ=0.911

arxiv:2608.06861.rationale: Highly relevant LLM-agent RL method with substantial ablations and reproducibility artifacts. Novelty is incremental over GAGPO/GraphGPO and evidence lacks significance testing; some internal numeric inconsistencies reduce confidence (e.g., claimed ALFWorld gains vs Table 2 arithmetic, Sokoban SD mismatch).
evidence: Abstract claims critic-free Bellman fixed-point credit assignment, confidence gating, and success-rate gains up to 4.1%, with a GitHub code link.
Table 2 reports Gated-BEPO against prompting and RL baselines on ALFWorld and WebShop for Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen2.5-7B.
Table 4 shows component-wise ablation on WebShop: outcome-only 62.50, plus FP credit 66.41, plus gate 73.83, full Gated-BEPO 75.91.
Appendix A provides environment details, compute setup, evaluation metrics, and final hyperparameters; Appendix M gives algorithm pseudocode.
Main text reports ALFWorld improvements over HGPO of 2.78% and 2.95% at 1.5B and 7B, while Table 2 values differ arithmetically (74.0-70.5 and 77.0-72.8 percentage points).
Table 3 shows Sokoban Gated-BEPO as 80.0±3.2, but the main text reports 80.03±0.32, an apparent SD inconsistency.

arxiv:2608.06860.rationale: The paper proposes NysHD for hyperdimensional computing via Nyström kernel approximation, with formal analysis and multi-dataset comparisons. It is outside the curator's core LLM/NLP/transformer/agent preferences: HDC and kernel methods are not among listed topics, and BERT/ESM appear only as baselines. Research quality is moderate but relevance is low, capping the overall score.
evidence: Abstract claims 11% and 17% average accuracy improvements on graph and string datasets respectively.
Encoding Process section presents Theorem 1 on expected dot-product preservation of normalized kernel values under NysHD.
Evaluation section Tables 2 and 3 report accuracy and training time against HDC baselines and several DNN/LM baselines.
Overhead & Scalability section acknowledges added kernel computation cost and future work on landmark sampling.

arxiv:2608.07618.rationale: The paper addresses SGD with discontinuous gradients, partially matching the Training & Optimization preference but not LLM/NLP/agent themes. It offers a modest theoretical extension of codimension-one discontinuous-drift analysis to higher codimension, but relies heavily on cited results and lacks self-contained proofs, experiments, or implementation details; rigor is reduced by typos and sketchy theorem statements.
evidence: Section 4 states the main theorems and notes the measure result is a direct consequence of [19], without a complete standalone proof.
Section 5 discusses time evolution but states that non-isolated accumulation points cannot be ruled out.

arxiv:2608.06850.rationale: Pure computer-vision object-detection/benchmark paper with only tangential vision-language evaluation via open-vocabulary detectors; out of scope for LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent methods and capped at 0.20. It provides broad baseline comparisons and clear tables, but lacks ablations, statistical/annotation-quality evidence, and only states data will be released.
evidence: Abstract: 'RegionDet contains eight region categories... We systematically evaluate representative closed-set and zero-shot/open-vocabulary detectors on RegionDet.'
Table 4: 'RF-DETR-L achieves the best overall AP of 37.6, while DEIMv2-L obtains a comparable AP of 37.0 and the best AP50 and AP75 scores.'
Table 5: 'The best overall AP is only around 1.0, and AP50 remains below 3.0 for all models.'

Conclusion and Discussion: 'Zero-shot/open-vocabulary detectors perform poorly, indicating that current vision-language detectors remain strongly object-centric and limited in localizing region targets beyond object instances.'

arxiv:2608.06849.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM/transformer/long-context inference and sparse attention. The data-free effective-rank head classification is a meaningful novelty, though it extends existing retrieval/streaming-head work. Rigor is moderate: controlled baselines and ablations on LongBench/MMLU are useful, but results lack variance/statistical tests and efficiency uses eager attention rather than optimized kernels. Evidence is quantitative but partly limited by benchmark scope and untrusted claims. Generalization across three dense LLMs plus one MoE is reasonable but decoder-only and not multimodal/encoder-decoder tested. Reproducibility is moderate: algorithm and hyperparameters are described, but no verified code artifact is evident.
evidence: Section 6.1 and Table 2 report LongBench comparisons against SnapKV, Quest, H2O, DuoAttention, Random, and Reverse for Qwen3-8B and Llama3.1-8B.
Section 6.4 and Tables 4-6 report ablations for spectral metric choice, GQA aggregation, and RoPE-aware ranking stability.
Appendix H Tables 11-13 report prefill/decode latency and KV-cache memory across sparsity levels and context lengths.

arxiv:2608.06848.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/code-security empirical study with comprehensive multi-model evaluation, ablations, and statistical tests. Novelty is moderate as the main method is post-edit regularization and model editing for security is under-explored but not conceptually new. Evidence is fairly strong but security relies primarily on static-analysis proxies, and some results have wide confidence intervals.
evidence: Section 3.1.1 and Table 2: model editing methods generally provide larger security gains than CoSec; DINM +11.27% average vs CoSec +1.46% on seen CWEs.
Section 3.4.1 and Tables 6-7: SafeEdit is evaluated across eight LLMs with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, showing significant SR improvements over CoSec (p<=0.039) and Pass@1 (p=0.008).
Section 4.6 and Table 14: UltraEdit hardening completes within 50-100 seconds, while CoSec increases inference latency 1.4-3.2x.
Section 4.11 reports manual inspection of 40 generated outputs with CodeQL agreement on 37/40 and acknowledges static analysis is a security proxy.

arxiv:2608.06847.rationale: Out-of-scope visual place recognition / robotics computer vision paper. It borrows linear concept erasure techniques from NLP but contains no LLM, language modeling, or textual reasoning methodology. Quantitative experiments are domain-solid, but relevance to the stated preferences is minimal and the out-of-scope cap applies.
evidence: Page 5 Table III: reports R@1, DAR@1, and RSR@1 across six datasets and eleven VPR methods.
Page 6 Fig. 8: reports condition suppression effects on DAR@1 and R@1.
Page 7 Table IV: reports single- vs multi-condition suppression equivalence across method-dataset pairs.

arxiv:2608.06846.rationale: Quantum-embedded transformer with classical attention decoder and hybrid quantum-classical component attribution is largely outside core LLM/NLP preferences; only attention/transformer architecture and a text dataset are tangentially relevant. The paper is a careful negative result with paired interface-matched controls, but its controlled evidence is limited to one saturated tabular dataset, five seeds, and two qubit counts, so rigor and generalizability are moderate.
evidence: Section 5.1 Table 2 reports four paired quantum-minus-classical 95% CIs; three include zero, and the +1.63 n_q=4 attention contrast reverses at n_q=8 and does not survive correction.
Section 5.2 Table 3 reports all 40 planned factorial runs completed with no majority-class collapse.
Section 6.6 Limitations states the controlled evidence is limited to BCW, five paired seeds, two qubit counts, and near-ceiling accuracy.
Section 4.5 Reproducibility states canonical cells have versioned config files, run-level CSVs, a dependency lockfile, and scripts for regenerating tables and figures.

arxiv:2608.06845.rationale: Out-of-scope visualization/HCI empirical study on dashboard reading order. It has no meaningful overlap with the requested LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agents/safety/evaluation preferences, so preference_relevance is negligible. Within its own domain it presents a mixed-methods study with interviews and flow instances, but sample and dashboard diversity are limited, evidence is largely qualitative/self-reported, and reproducibility is constrained beyond a cited supplemental protocol. Assigned low final score consistent with out-of-scope domain research.
evidence: Abstract: describes a mixed-methods study of dashboard reading order with authors and end-users, focusing on layout, visual saliency, semantics, function, interaction, and user context.
Introduction: frames contributions around dashboard reading flow, design factors, and reading-order patterns, not language-model or ML methodology.
Limitations: notes reliance on self-reported reading sequences rather than eye tracking or interaction logs, limiting behavioral evidence strength.
Methodology sections 2-3: report small participant samples (13 practitioners, 16 end-users, 7 authors) and a custom annotation tool, indicating moderate rigor but limited generalizability.

arxiv:2608.06842.rationale: This is an economics application using a frozen tabular foundation model (TabFM) with transformer/ICL components, not an LLM/NLP contribution. It mentions foundation model, in-context learning, and attention, but the core object is random utility and economic behavior across risk/time/social choice. As a pure domain application outside language methodology, it is capped at very low relevance. Quantitative experiments are extensive with ablations, held-out tests, and bootstrap intervals, but claims are domain-specific and pretraining data are not public.
evidence: Abstract: 'I hide a decision maker’s choices in one domain and ask a frozen tabular foundation model to recover them...'
Section 4.1: 'TabFM is a pretrained regression and classification model for mixed-type tables... It alternates attention across columns and rows...'
Section 5.1: held-out domain test compares frozen TabFM against training-sample population median and shuffled decision-maker conditions.

arxiv:2608.06841.rationale: Pure computer-vision detection paper with no LLM/NLP language methodology, so treated as out-of-scope and capped near 0.20. It contributes a benchmark and detector with ablations, but topic relevance is minimal.
evidence: Abstract: introduces ECAD, BTCO-Bench, and ECADet with GAER and PGQM.
Main Results: Table 2 reports ECADet DINOv3-L achieves 41.0 AP on BTCO-Real (Test).
Component Ablation: Table 4 reports GAER+PGQM improves AP from 24.5 to 41.0 over RF-DETR DINOv3-L.
BTCO-Bench: Table 1 reports BTCO-Real Test has 5,000 images and 145,631 boxes, and BTCO-XDomain has 18,639 images and 134,143 boxes.

arxiv:2608.06839.rationale: Interpretability-focused study with LLM/CNN/PointNet experiments; moderately relevant via interpretability and LLM topics, though not a language-methodology contribution. Novelty is limited by prior symbolic-interaction work and mostly extends existing formulations with criteria. Rigor is weakened by damaged cross-references/notation, small hand-selected variable sets, sparse model pairs for transferability, and lack of comparative baselines or formal statistical tests. Evidence supports directional claims but relies on self-reported figures and limited ablations. Generalizability across architectures is promising. No code availability or complete LLM extraction hyperparameters limits reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.06837.rationale: Out of scope for AI/ML/NLP preferences: pure cryptographic side-channel/fault-attack research using MILP for block cipher cryptanalysis (DEFAULT/BAKSHEESH), with no language models, transformers, agents, safety, or machine learning methodology. Although the paper reports simulations and quantitative fault counts in Sections 3.1 and 4.3, these do not establish relevance to the rubric; score capped near floor.
evidence: Abstract: proposes an MILP-based DFA framework and reports DEFAULT/BAKSHEESH fault injection results.
Section 3.1: reports 1,000 independent experiments for DEFAULT and BAKSHEESH unique-trail searches.
Section 4.3: provides quantitative fault counts for 6-/7-/8-round DFA key recovery.

arxiv:2608.07617.rationale: Relevant LLM evaluation/repair benchmark but domain-specific; strong transparency and released artifacts, though taxonomy reliability and external validity are limited.
evidence: Section 1 Contributions claims 10,437 mutation instances from 743 openly licensed seeds and a seven-model campaign at ~$200.
Section 3.1 reports a mining pipeline yielding 168 localized LaTeX hard crashes from TeX.SE, GitHub, and package documentation.
Section 5.1 Table 2 reports three-model cross-benchmark with DocMut gaps of 5.6-9.2 pp and exact McNemar p-values.
Section 7.3 reports a complete balanced matrix of 6,613 instances x 7 models and provider-pinned routing with allow_fallbacks=false.
