Section 11 Threat to Validity discloses open-coding kappa=0.34, LaTeX-only taxonomy, synthetic mutations, and seed limitations.
Data Availability states DocMut v0.2.0 and a Zenodo research package with ledgers and harness scripts are released.

arxiv:2608.06836.rationale: Pure RGB-D 3D vision and geometry-guided image generation paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology; out of scope under the stated rubric despite some methodological ablations on a synthetic benchmark.
evidence: Abstract: The paper addresses 3D pose inference and geometry-guided image generation for furniture insertion from single-view RGB-D, not language-model research.
Section V-A1: Experiments use a synthetic Front3D-Insertion benchmark built from 3D-FRONT/3D-FUTURE with BlenderProc.
Section V-B Table I: Main result reports GOPI-Dual Overall@M 68.0% and TransAcc@0.3m 69.5%, with ablations in Table II.

arxiv:2608.06834.rationale: Partially relevant architecture paper extending Transformers with edge mechanisms for relational reasoning; not LLM/NLP/Japanese LLM. Moderate novelty and ablations, but single benchmark, small seeds, no significance testing, and limited generalizability.

arxiv:2608.06833.rationale: Pure embodied visual navigation/robotics paper with no LLM, NLP, or language methodology; falls under out-of-scope pure robotics/CV. Technical evaluation is moderately thorough within its domain, but topic relevance is minimal, capping the overall score.
evidence: Section 4.1 evaluates in NVIDIA Isaac Sim/GRScenes and CARLA using topomap, localization, and Habitat ImageNav metrics, all embodied navigation tasks.
Table 7 compares navigation SR/SPL against Uni-Navid, UniGoal, ViNT, and NoMaD; no LLM or language-based method is introduced.

arxiv:2608.06832.rationale: Pure computer vision image restoration paper; no LLM, NLP, Japanese LLM, reasoning, agents, RAG, safety, or language methodology. Although it uses vision Transformer blocks and deformable tokenization, the submission is out of scope per the rubric, so overall capped below 0.20. Internal experiments and ablations are present, but relevance to the requested research priorities is minimal.
evidence: Abstract: all-in-one image restoration for diverse degradations; no language methodology.
Method: FIT uses DGDE, DGDT, AdaLN Transformer for image restoration.
Experiments: Evaluation on BSD68, Rain100L, SOTS, GoPro, and LOLv1.

arxiv:2608.06830.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, multi-agent security, AI safety, and red teaming; not pure robotics because the attack surface and methodology are language-based LLM communication. Novelty is moderate: formalizes two attacker access settings across communication architectures and a CPV gate, but builds on existing multi-agent propagation and LLM-robot jailbreak work. Rigor is moderate: clear threat model, algorithms, and trace-based metrics, but defense evaluation is limited and there are no real-robot experiments or statistical significance tests. Evidence is strong for attack propagation from extensive simulation but weaker for mitigation. Generalizability is supported by three architectures, three LLMs, and five tasks, though all are simulated. Reproducibility is partially supported by environment and model versions but lacks code/data availability.
evidence: Section V-A2 Target LLMs states evaluation includes GPT-3.5-Turbo, Qwen3-235B-A22B, and GPT-4o.
Section V-A3 Task Scenarios and Table I define five multi-robot tasks: warehouse patrol, hospital, formation escort, warehouse air-ground patrol, and secure item-carrier matching.
Section V-C2 Results reports average C_act 0.484 external vs 0.618 privileged under balanced prompt and 0.645 vs 0.878 under no safety constraint.
Table IV reports CPV Gate lowers any violation rate from 70.0% Baseline to 36.6% CPV across six architecture-access pairs with Qwen3 only.
Section V-A1 Experimental Environment specifies NVIDIA Isaac Sim 4.5.0, Isaac Lab 2.1.0, ROS 2 Humble, and Unitree interfaces.

arxiv:2608.06829.rationale: Centrally relevant to LLM reasoning, code generation, and AI safety/fairness. The paper provides a systematic empirical study with multiple models, statistical significance tests, an ablation, and a proposed reasoning-stage mitigation method. However, reasoning-bias labels rely partly on LLM-as-judge outputs, and generalization is limited to three decision scenarios plus a small external subset.
evidence: Section 4.1.3 reports average Bias Rate drops from 0.64 to 0.40 with p=0.0117 and Cliff's delta=0.704.
Table 6 reports ProbeDebias reduces average BR from 0.56 to 0.09 while quality is 0.76 vs. 0.77.
Table 5 reports ProbeDebias reasoning-bias detection F1 of 87.76%.
Section 4.2.2 reports GPT-5.1 reasoning-bias labels validated on 216 pairs with 81.94% accuracy and 84.71% F1.

arxiv:2608.06828.rationale: RAG/LLM legal QA paper with rhetorical-role chunking, hybrid retrieval, and reranking is topically relevant to RAG/NLP but remains a domain-specific application. Method is largely a combination of known components; no baselines or ablations, small 30-judgment/25-query evaluation, only LLM-judge metrics with low contextual relevancy (0.376-0.443), and no code/model release or expert evaluation.
evidence: Section 3 Methodology: describes rhetorical-role-aware chunking, dense/sparse retrieval, intent filtering, and cross-encoder reranking.
Section 4.1 and Tables 5-7: reports only Qwen3-32B, Gemini-2.5-flash, and Gemini-2.5-Pro LLM-judge metrics; contextual relevancy ranges 0.376-0.443.
Section 6 Limitations: evaluation limited to Indian Supreme Court judgments and automated LLM metrics without legal expert review.
Sections 3.2-3.3: no identifiers for bi-encoder/cross-encoder models and no code/data availability statement.

arxiv:2608.06827.rationale: Out-of-scope real-to-sim robotics/computer-vision/diffusion paper with no language-model, NLP, reasoning, agent, or AI-safety methodology. The paper reports controlled visual metrics and real-robot ablations, but topical relevance to the preferred LLM/NLP/reasoning areas is negligible, so the 0.20 out-of-scope cap applies.
evidence: Abstract reports 19.062 dB PSNR vs 14.226 dB for the strongest reported R2S baseline and 82.5% real-G1 sitting success vs 10.0% for GaussGym.
Table II reports quantitative comparison on frozen G1 ego views for Vanilla 3DGS, GenFusion, Difix3D+, GaussGym, and R2S-EGO.
Table IV reports simulation and real-world sitting success rates across five independently trained policies.

arxiv:2608.06826.rationale: This is post-quantum isogeny-based cryptography and does not align with any weighted preference topic (LLMs, Japanese NLP, transformers, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, code, AI safety, multimodal AI, etc.). The paper provides explicit KEM algorithms and benchmark tables, but its contribution is domain-specific and incremental from the curation perspective.
evidence: Abstract: comparative performance analysis of POKÉ-based key exchange and SIDH variants.
Section III-B, Algorithms 1-3: specifies a Fujisaki-Okamoto-based KEM from POKÉ.
Section IV-B, Table II: reports POKEx key exchange at 306.95 ms versus terSIDH 6510.83 ms and CSIDH 19941.20 ms.

arxiv:2608.06825.rationale: Theoretical online inverse optimization/learning from correct demonstrations with cover-based multiscale hedging. It has formal theorems, lower bounds, and reproducible audits, but lacks LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/safety substance; only tangential RL/reward terminology. General result is inefficient and improper, limiting practical relevance.
evidence: Section 7.1 reports a stress test with multiscale mean cumulative gap 2.07 versus 88.92 and 21.32 for single-tolerance baselines.
Section 7.2 reports MovieLens audit mean latent gap 3.53 for multiscale versus 7.74 proper baseline and 14.82 demonstrated-rating policy.
Appendix G describes fixed-seed scripts and invariant checks for both audits and reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.09991.rationale: Medical imaging application for breast cancer pCR prediction; out of scope per rubric and capped at 0.20. It uses a Transformer and a radiology foundation model, but no LLM/NLP/reasoning methodology. The paper has ablations and quantitative baselines, though limited external validation and domain relevance.
evidence: Section 1 states the objective is pCR prediction from serial DCE-MRI in neoadjuvant breast cancer, a medical imaging application.
Section 3.2 describes a Transformer encoder with multi-head self-attention but no language-model methodology.
Section 4.1 reports 982 patients from the combined I-SPY2/ACRIN-6698 cohort.
Section 5.3 reports ablation results with full model AUROC 73.6 versus imaging alone 55.5.

arxiv:2608.06824.rationale: Out-of-scope pure single-cell genomics/biology application with no LLM/NLP/agent/safety relevance; only weak Scientific AI overlap. Method has moderate novelty and matched ablations, but domain cap and limited topical relevance keep the score at most 0.20.
evidence: Abstract and §1 frame the task as single-cell transcriptional perturbation response prediction, a pure computational biology application.
§4.1 and §4.2 describe perturbation-conditioned gene geometry and control-anchored residual flow matching; no language-model methodology is present.
§5.2 and Table 1 report Norman additive Pearson Delta 0.8979; §5.4 reports matched ablations including graph-free and explicit-propagation controls.
Supplementary Appendix A provides implementation details, Table S4 optimization settings, and reproducibility information including seed and hardware.

arxiv:2608.06823.rationale: Numerical PDE/neural solver for the Boltzmann equation with no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, or language methodology; only marginal relevance via the low-weight Scientific AI preference. The method extends prior WANPM work and includes useful weak-form derivation, but the collisional operator is not numerically validated: Section 5 reports only collisionless free transport and forced experiments, weakening evidence for the paper's central claim.
evidence: Section 5.1 and 5.2 contain only collisionless free-transport and harmonic-force experiments; the collision operator derived in Sections 3-4 is not numerically tested.
Section 5.2.6 explicitly notes variance bias, marginal shape error, and seed sensitivity, indicating limited robustness.
Table 1 and Sections 5.1.2-5.1.3 provide architecture and hyperparameters, but no code or data availability statement is present.

arxiv:2608.06822.rationale: Pure mathematics phase-retrieval paper; none of the specified AI/ML/NLP preferences are addressed. The paper is out of scope for this curation rubric, and the zero relevance dominates the weighted score.

arxiv:2608.06819.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/reasoning/inference method for SLM-LLM token-level collaboration. The future-compatibility supervision idea is a clear but incremental extension over prior token-selection and future-guided methods. Main headline gain over greedy is substantial, but the gain over the strongest comparable token-level baseline S2T is only 1.24 Math Avg. points, with no reported significance tests or per-cell variance. Ablations and reproducibility details are strong, but evaluation is limited to Qwen models and mathematical reasoning, limiting generalizability.
evidence: Table 1 reports FutureBridge Math Avg. 50.38 vs S2T 49.14 and greedy 37.30 for Qwen3-1.7B, a gain of 1.24 points over S2T.
Table 3 reports SLM-only and LLM-only pools reduce Math Avg. by 2.5 and 2.1 points, and Direct LLM score reaches 47.2 vs FutureBridge 50.38.
Appendix A states that reported FutureBridge results use three training seeds but the main-table Math Avg. reports the seed mean without per-cell standard deviations.
Appendix A provides detailed LoRA, request-policy, data-filtering, hardware, and software reproducibility information.

arxiv:2608.06811.rationale: Highly relevant LLM-agent/code-repair paper. Bidirectional plan-memory coupling is a moderate incremental contribution over existing planning and memory work. The empirical design includes repeated runs, cluster bootstrap, McNemar tests, and factorial ablation; cross-model/framework/benchmark probes support generalization but are single-run. Evidence is quantitative but some trajectory/verdict subsets are small.
evidence: Section V-A, Table III reports repeated-run SWE-bench Verified resolved counts and 95% CI for the +25.0 mean improvement.
Section V-B, Table V reports trajectory-level behavioral signatures for failed-action recurrence, empty-patch, context exhaustion, and recovery.
Section V-D, Table VIII and factorial test report plan-memory interaction contrast +10.3 (F(1,8)=10.92, p=0.011).
Section VII discusses threats to validity including FP8 non-reproducibility and single-run generality probes.

arxiv:2608.06809.rationale: Low preference relevance: primarily a dimensionality-reduction/visual-analytics geometry paper with only tangential interpretability connections; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology. Quality is moderate-strong: formal framework, theorems, and quantitative validation, but scope is limited and no code availability is demonstrated.
evidence: Abstract: claims unified geometric framework for differentiable embeddings; no LLM/NLP methodology.
Sec. VIII/Table III: reports Spearman 0.963-0.999 for curvature-based trust estimates on single-cell embeddings.
Sec. IX: states nondifferentiable or stochastic embeddings are out of scope; no code release or availability statement is given.

arxiv:2608.06808.rationale: Moderate relevance: central LLM-driven heuristic/code synthesis for algorithm portfolios, with synthetic-data and optimization aspects, but not core LLM/NLP safety or Japanese LLM work. Novelty is incremental over co-evolutionary ACP. Rigor is moderate: formal setup, ablations, statistical tests, but only 3 runs, small training set, no variance/confidence intervals, and some future/unverifiable LLM identifiers. Generalizability limited to TSP/CVRP.
evidence: Section V-A describes 8 training instances, 100 test instances per spatial pattern, and 3 independent repeats.
Table II reports TSP/CVRP constructive results across six distributions with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
Section V-B2 reports PIAC vs PIAC(RND) and PIAC(GAP) ablation gap reductions.
Section V-E uses DeepSeek-V3.2, DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K2.6, and GPT-4.1 mini, which are future/unverifiable model identifiers.

arxiv:2608.06805.rationale: Out-of-scope wireless physical-layer authentication/RFF framework with no LLM, NLP, ML, or AI methodology; superficial security vocabulary does not match AI safety preferences. Conceptual framework with no experiments, benchmarks, baselines, ablations, or quantitative evidence, limiting rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: §I states the article does not aim to benchmark a specific RFF-based authentication algorithm or dataset

arxiv:2608.06801.rationale: Pure computer vision adversarial attack against person detectors; no LLM, NLP, language methodology, or agent/reasoning relevance. arxiv:2608.06795.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM safety/backdoor defense, LoRA/transformer interpretability. Evaluation is fairly rigorous across 75 adapters, 5 models, 5 attacks, and 3 tasks with ablations and runtime comparisons, but no adaptive-attack evaluation and only white-box access. Evidence is strong from multiple tables with standard errors; generalizability is good within autoregressive Transformers but limited elsewhere. Reproducibility is moderate because hyperparameters and benchmark are specified but code availability is not stated.
evidence: Abstract: introduces LoRAScan as an inference-time, sample-level backdoor detector for LoRA adapters and reports 98.49% rejection of malicious inputs.

Limitations: scope is autoregressive Transformer LLMs, white-box intermediate activations, and the paper notes no black-box API visibility; adaptive attacks are only briefly noted in ethical considerations.

arxiv:2608.06671.rationale: Out of scope for the target LLM/NLP/AI-methodology preferences: this is an applied epidemiological time-series forecasting study using wastewater surveillance and VAR/ARIMA models, with no language-model methodology. arxiv:2608.06670.rationale: Out-of-scope statistical methodology on Bayesian bootstrap for semi-parametric models; no LLM/NLP/vision/robotics/audio/AI-agent relevance. arxiv:2608.06669.rationale: Domain-specific quantum chemistry numerical solver for coupled cluster equations; no LLM, NLP, or AI methodology. arxiv:2608.06663.rationale: Highly relevant survey of long-horizon LLM agents across planning, memory, execution, training, evaluation, and safety. arxiv:2608.06659.rationale: Out-of-scope biology foundation model for spatial transcriptomics; no LLM, language, agent, reasoning, or safety methodology. arxiv:2608.06655.rationale: Classical game-theoretic intrusion detection/ISAC domain application with no LLM/NLP/transformer/multimodal/reasoning methodology. Formal proofs and experiments exist but are outside AI/LLM curation scope, with only tangential adversarial/defense keyword overlap.
evidence: Abstract: formulates graph security game for resource-aware intrusion detection under ISAC; no LLM/NLP methodology.
Section 7.4: reports RADAR mean normalized gap 3.64% vs exact optimization over pure configurations.
Theorem 4.3 with Appendix A: proves NP-hardness for pure defender optimization by Clique reduction.

arxiv:2608.07645.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM coding agents and self-improving agent workflows. The comparative evidence operators are an incremental extension of archive-based self-improvement, but primary empirical claims rely on small 60-task subsets with no reported seed diversity or confidence intervals, and the text contains an internal inconsistency on SWE-bench Verified-60 accuracy (78.3 vs 61.7), reducing rigor and evidence strength. Theory and simulations are heavily simplified. Code links and hyperparameters are provided but unverified.
evidence: Section 5.1, Table 1 reports MGM accuracy of 78.3 on SWE-bench Verified-60 and 93.2 on Polyglot-60 under 200 evaluations.
Appendix F.2 states that MGM reaches 61.7% on SWE-bench Verified-60, contradicting Table 1's 78.3.
Section 5.2, Tables 2-3 report cross-benchmark and cross-model transfer without confidence intervals or multiple seeds.
Section 5.3 ablation shows full MGM at 93.2 versus 79.7 without Phi_RM and 74.6 without Phi_CH on Polyglot-60.
Appendix A.1 provides pseudocode and Appendix C.2 lists hyperparameters, supporting reproducibility but not independent verification.

arxiv:2608.07458.rationale: Strongly relevant to RAG, long-context LLM inference, KV cache reuse, and efficiency. The method has moderate novelty in combining offline nugget extraction with contextualized KV slicing, but it builds substantially on existing chunk-level CAG and nugget-based RAG work. Experimental evidence with multiple baselines, ablations, and latency/length Pareto analyses is useful, though evaluation is limited to three LongBench multi-hop QA datasets with no statistical significance testing. Generalizability is constrained by single-model and single-task-family evaluation. Reproducibility is aided by detailed appendices on hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, and costs, but no code release is stated.
evidence: Section 4.2 and Table 3: under P99 latency ≤100 ms, CoinRAG average F1 41.7 vs TurboRAG 39.6; with no latency limit, 42.7 vs 40.6.
Section 4.3 and Figure 4: ablations compare isolated nugget encoding, one-stage retrieval, no position alignment, and no fine-tuning, reporting peak F1 changes.
Section 5 Limitations: acknowledges coupling of cached KV to model checkpoint, retrieval recall bounds, and absence of cross-chunk attention.
Appendix F and G: specify hardware, storage, I/O management, fine-tuning costs, and hyperparameters.

arxiv:2608.06729.rationale: Primarily a robotics/VLA paper; the 7B LLM is used only as a semantic component, so it falls near pure embodied/robotics domain application and is capped low for preference relevance. The dual-memory method shows moderate novelty relative to MemoryVLA/MEM, and benchmark tables provide substantial self-reported results, but no confidence intervals, limitations, external validation, or code release are present, limiting rigor, evidence, and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 3.2 describes the voxel-hashed persistent world state, sliding-window update, and first-frame anchor.
Table 1 reports LIBERO success rates for wrist-only AtlasVLA versus third-person and multi-view baselines.
Table 5 reports ablations for world-state memory, ego-working memory, update strategy, spatial/temporal PE, and world conditioning.
Appendix A.2 and Table 6 provide hyperparameters and loss details, but no code availability or limitations are stated.

arxiv:2608.03216.rationale: Pure computer-vision segmentation paper with no LLM/NLP/agent methodology; out of scope and capped at 0.20. It uses vision-transformer query-based mask transformers but only weakly matches CV/transformer preferences. Ablations and benchmark results are present, but the domain-specific contribution limits relevance.
evidence: Method: iFAN introduces Adjusted Probability-Mask Ranking (APMR) and Cross-Layer Self-Distillation (CLSD) for plain mask transformers.
Experiments: Reports COCO, ADE20K, and Cityscapes results across panoptic, instance, and semantic segmentation.
Ablation Studies: Table 4 isolates global mask-quality, APMR, and CLSD contributions.
Table 1: iFAN improves PMT and EoMT baselines on COCO and ADE20K panoptic segmentation.

arxiv:2608.06654.rationale: Out-of-scope statistical causal inference paper on principal stratification and effect modification with truncation by death using Medicare claims. It does not address LLMs, NLP, transformers, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, safety, alignment, multimodal, or other targeted AI/ML areas. Though it has methodological development, simulations, and an R package, relevance to the requested AI/ML preferences is effectively zero, so the final score is capped at a low out-of-scope value.
evidence: Section 1.2 Methodology review: principal stratification, principal ignorability, pseudo data-based robust estimation; no LLM/NLP/transformer/agent/safety methods appear.
Section 3: Application to Medicare claims for ADRD/hip fracture, confirming clinical/statistical domain focus.

arxiv:2608.06652.rationale: Moderately relevant LLM/NLP application: uses Qwen3-8B for prompt-based metaphor detection and interpretation, but focuses on metaphor/framing analysis rather than advancing LLM capabilities. The combination of LLM-generated framing implications with CMT-grounded constrained clustering is somewhat novel, though prior LLM metaphor and structured-clustering work limits novelty. Evaluation includes multiple datasets, ablations, and annotation, but single-run prompt results, small annotation samples, modest/unstable gains, and no significance testing weaken rigor and evidence. English-only US-centric data and unassessed podcast transcription restrict generalizability; code/data are only promised, reducing reproducibility.
evidence: Section 4.1 reports Qwen3-8b F1=81.61 vs RoBERTa F1=81.22 on LCC, and F1=64.15 on an unseen immigration split.
Section 4.2 reports interpretation quality averages of 3.76/5 for immigration, 4.12/5 for gun control, and 4.23/5 for abortion; Gwet's AC1 ranges from 0.612 to 0.873.
Section 4.3 Table 2 shows structured clustering improves purity and polarity F1 over K-means, but absolute polarity F1 remains modest (52.88-55.47).
Section 7 Limitations acknowledges English-only, US-centric evaluation and unassessed podcast transcription accuracy.
Section 1 states code and data will be released upon publication, but no availability is demonstrated at evaluation time.

arxiv:2608.06651.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM agents, AI safety, and red-teaming/evaluation, but evaluated on a small private automotive benchmark with no strong empirical validation of the central safety-guard claims beyond detection precision/recall.
evidence: Section IV-C reports Fast coverage 34.0% and Deep coverage about 70% with 1.000 precision on clean controls, but these are detection metrics rather than guard safety metrics.

Section III-B describes the deterministic SecurityGuard and independent action-alignment oracle, while Section IV-D claims unsafe actions cannot commit but provides no adversarial evaluation of the guard.

arxiv:2608.06650.rationale: Pure soft-robotics/differentiable simulation and control paper; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology. High-quality engineering within robotics, but out of scope per instructions, capped below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: introduces SoRoMoX for soft robot models in JAX, GPU-parallel and differentiable; no language-model methodology.
Section V-F: uses PPO reinforcement learning for a tendon-actuated soft continuum arm, a robotics application.
Section I: focuses on Cosserat-rod/soft-robot modeling and control.

arxiv:2608.06648.rationale: Out-of-scope pure aerospace/multi-agent trajectory coordination and collision-avoidance research; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, or language-model methodology. Superficial overlap with 'agents' and 'multi-agent' keywords does not satisfy the topical preferences. Empirical results and mathematical formulation are present, but domain relevance is too low to score above the 0.20 cap for pure robotics/domain applications.
evidence: Abstract: 'real-time Plan–and–Avoid framework for coordinating cooperative multi-agent airspace operations'
Index Terms: 'Multi-Robot Systems; Autonomous Agents'
Section VI-D: 'all 575 unique conflict encounters' and 'worst-case end-to-end response time of 5.7 s'

arxiv:2608.06641.rationale: LLM-driven fuzzing directly uses LLMs, RAG, and constraint solving, making it relevant to LLM/RAG/code/security preferences, though it is a domain-specific software-testing application. The combination of LLM-based specification inference, grammar generation, and SMT-enforced API relationships is a useful contribution but incremental over prior LLM fuzzers. Evaluation includes coverage, vulnerability discovery, ablations, and LLM accuracy, but rigor is limited by a missing/placeholder vulnerability table, small spot-check samples, and no explicit limitations section. Generalizability is only partially demonstrated via a VBA feasibility study. An artifact URL supports reproducibility, but detailed prompts/configurations are not all present in the provided text.
evidence: Section 4.5 describes two-stage RAG-based relationship inference and SMT-LIB2 constraint generation.
Section 6.1 reports coverage gains up to 48% over Cooper and 16-49% over Claude-3.7-Sonnet.
Section 6.2 reports 57 crashing inputs triaged to 31 unique crash signatures, though Table 1 is a placeholder in the provided text.
Section 6.6 reports spot-check accuracies of 94% for specification inference, 97-98% for grammar generation, and 93% for relationship inference.
Appendix B provides an artifact URL at https://github.com/ucsb-seclab/PDFuzzer.

arxiv:2608.06640.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM code generation and software engineering, with large-scale production provenance data. The production-lifecycle focus is somewhat novel, but the study is observational, has limited statistical rigor, a small intervention sample, and some internal inconsistency about build-failure results. Single-enterprise C++ scope and private data limit generalizability and reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: reports 3.52M code changes and 10.46M lines of C++ with informative authoring provenance.
Section 4.2 Table 3: reports Interface and Coupling Burden and Copy and Allocation Overhead account for 82.21% of the positive absolute rate gap.
Section 4.3 Figure 4: reports AI-generated changes received 1.92x blocking threads and 1.39x total comments, with normalized compute reaching about 1.31x vs 1.25x baseline.
Section 4.4 Table 6: reports Stage 3 reduces targeted findings from 1.26 to 1.12, an 11.1% reduction relative to Stage 1 on a 50-function benchmark.
Section 6: acknowledges enterprise-internal data cannot be released, the analysis is single C++ monorepo, and model mix/prompt evolution confounders limit attribution.

fallback:0342be0d4f2fee63.rationale: Non-research conference/event report from MIRU2026 with only a passing mention of 'Ambient Agent' and business workflow. It contains no methods, baselines, ablations, quantitative results, limitations, or reproducibility information, so all research-quality components are zero and overall relevance is minimal.

arxiv:2608.06638.rationale: Directly in-scope via mechanistic interpretability (probing, logit/tuned lens, activation patching/steering) and analysis of an LLM-based generator (Llama 3.2 1B); however, the symbolic-music domain is niche and not a language-task contribution, limiting preference relevance. Quality is strong with grouped CV, shuffled-label controls, self/neutral patch controls, bidirectional steering decomposition, and explicit limitations, but only two models and code is promised rather than available.
evidence: Abstract: proposes mechanistic interpretability of text-to-MIDI models via probing, lenses, and steering.
Section 4.1: uses 5-fold grouped CV and shuffled-label control probes that collapse to majority baseline.
Table 3 (Section 4.2): reports full-generation probing accuracy, baseline, and lift per concept for both models.
Section 5.1, Table 5 and Figure 4: logit lens shows gradual refinement in text2midi vs late vocabulary rotation in MIDI-LLM.
Figure 5 (Section 5.1): tuned lens makes MIDI-LLM predictions readable earlier, smoothing the layer 13-14 jump.
Section 7.2-7.3, Tables 6-7: bidirectional steering decomposes directional and symmetric components with SE-based rule.
Section 8: discusses limitations including proxy metrics, label noise, and inability to isolate architecture differences.

arxiv:2608.06637.rationale: Relevant only via AI safety/adversarial robustness topics; it is a federated-learning backdoor attack, not in core LLM/NLP/reasoning preferences. The method has moderate novelty as a selection-aware Krum proxy with two-stage optimization, but builds closely on prior aggregation-aware poisoning work. Empirical results are presented with baselines and ablations, though no significance testing or code release is shown. Generalization is tested across several datasets and heterogeneity levels, but the method is explicitly limited to Krum-style aggregation.
evidence: Table I reports final MTA/ASR under Krum and Multi-Krum, including Krum-Proxy ASR 100% under Krum.
Table III ablation shows removing two-stage optimization produces 22 post-convergence MTA crashes and lowers average MTA.
Section V-E reports malicious selection increases from 9 to 29 rounds under Krum and malicious inclusion from 62/300 to 175/300 under Multi-Krum.
Section IV-A describes the federated setup with N=100 clients, 10 selected per round, and Krum/Multi-Krum aggregation.

arxiv:2608.06632.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/agentic conversational recommendation paper with SFT, DPO, and LLM-as-judge components. Novelty is moderate: mainly an industrial system integration of known techniques. Evaluation includes offline, human, A/B, and ablation evidence, but lacks confidence intervals/sample sizes, has some ambiguous table-to-text details, and gives no code/data or full dataset specifications.
evidence: Section 6.1.2 and Table 1 report SFT+DPO accuracy 98.85% and latency 323ms versus 650ms for few-shot baseline.
Section 6.2.3 and Table 6 report online ablation results with significance markers for the full system.
Section 5.2.2 provides DPO training configuration but no dataset sizes or code/data availability.

arxiv:2608.06631.rationale: Relevant to AI safety/security and LLM/Transformer components, but limited to isolated GLU block extraction rather than end-to-end LLM functionality. Novel extension of cryptanalytic extraction to bias-free GLU blocks; moderate rigor due to single runs, heuristic repairs, and no direct baseline comparisons. Quantitative results support functional recovery but not storage-exact finite-precision recovery. Generalizability is constrained by known metadata and an isolated block interface; reproducibility is partial via equations, pseudocode, and scripts but code is withheld.
evidence: Abstract states the isolated-block experiments are not an end-to-end model-API attack.
Section 6.1 Table 5 reports high-precision Qwen validation medians from 3.91e-8 to 8.84e-6 across six layers.
Section 6.4 Table 6 reports four finite-precision configurations with median validation errors 0.003056 to 0.046269, and states none reproduces every stored weight.
Section 7 explicitly limits claims: no model-API feasibility, single runs, and isolated block interface required.
Appendix C provides base-stage reproduction scripts for Qwen3-0.6B layer 0.

arxiv:2608.06630.rationale: Directly relevant LLM efficiency/pruning paper. Introduces difference-informed saliency/Hessian methods (Wisp, Wisp+, Whisper), moderately novel but incremental over Wanda/SparseGPT. Strong ablations across sparsity types, model families, scales, and composability with RIA/ALPS; limitations discussed. Quantitative results with standard errors and raw appendix tables provide solid evidence. Code, pseudocode, and hyperparameters support reproducibility.
evidence: Section 3.4 Evaluation protocol: 128 sequences of 4096 tokens from WikiText-2 training set; LM Evaluation Harness used for downstream tasks.
Section 4.1: Whisper improves over SparseGPT at every reported sparsity and model size; Wisp and Wisp+ consistently outperform Wanda.
Section 4.6 Table 5: Generalization to Mistral 7B v0.3, Qwen3 8B Base, and Qwen3 14B Base at 2:4 sparsity.
Section A.10: Pseudocode for Wisp, Wisp+, and Whisper provided.
Section 5 Limitations: Focus on dense pretrained LMs, one-shot pruning, and no subsequent finetuning.

arxiv:2608.06628.rationale: Moderate in-scope relevance via LLM/attention/efficiency/inference, but not aligned with high-weight reasoning/agents/safety topics. Novelty is incremental: block-hybrid attention combines block diffusion, Hedgehog linear attention, and LoLCAT-style retrofitting. Rigor is limited by single-model evaluation, limited benchmarks, and no statistical testing, though ablations and limitations are present. Main speed/memory claims are supported by tables. Generalizability is limited to one dLLM and moderate generation lengths, and code availability is stated but unverified.
evidence: Abstract reports LLaDA-Hybrid achieves up to 1.7x higher decoding throughput and provides a GitHub code link
Table 1 reports teacher vs hybrid benchmark results, e.g., HumanEval 75.6 vs 72.0 and GPQA-Diamond 38.9 vs 30.8
Table 2 reports end-to-end decode throughput speedups of 1.50x-1.73x under SGLang continuous batching
Appendix A Table 3 reports isolated kernel latency speedups that grow with prefix length
Appendix A Table 4 reports max concurrent batch of 704 for LLaDA-Hybrid vs 544 for the teacher
Limitations and future work notes only 6 layers are linearized, moderate generation lengths, and fixed inference block size

fallback:ceca04c1082fc733.rationale: Introductory blog/tutorial on Genkit Go, mentioning LLM and tool calling, so marginally relevant, but abstract-only with no research methods, quantitative results, baselines, ablations, or evidence; novelty and rigor are absent.

arxiv:2608.06622.rationale: Data-center energy-efficiency measurement study outside the requested LLM/AI/NLP preferences; out-of-scope cap applied. The work has detailed measurements and reproducibility, but no relevance to the target topics.
evidence: Abstract: measurement-based case study of high-throughput computing energy efficiency
Section V-A: experimental setup
Section VI: recommendations for server energy reduction

arxiv:2608.06621.rationale: Moderately relevant: motivated by LLM hallucination and hypothesis certification, with formal e-value/CRT tests, but no real LLM/NLP experiments. Empirical support is limited to a synthetic ads-recommendation world; the diversity routing threshold is calibrated against planted labels, weakening evidence and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 5 / Table 3: reports only synthetic ads-recommendation results with eight planted rules and a naive held-out baseline; no real LLM-generated hypothesis certification is evaluated.
Appendix A: tau_div is calibrated per world as the midpoint between a known glocal and a known confound, using planted ground-truth labels.
Section 5: all numbers are means over 10 random worlds; no per-rule variance or confidence intervals are reported.
Section 4, Theorem 1: provides formal e-value validity and an intersection-union certification error bound under the stated exchangeability nulls.

arxiv:2608.06620.rationale: Out-of-scope software engineering energy study. Core contribution concerns energy impact of Java refactoring; LLMs are used only as auxiliary tools for workload generation and energy-regression classification, with no language-modeling methodology. Final score capped at 0.20.
evidence: Section 5.1.1 Table 6: 199 of 384 refactoring-workload comparisons (51.8%) exhibit statistically significant energy differences.
Section 5.1.2 Table 9: 36 of 481 real-world commits (7.5%) show significant energy changes.
Section 5.4 Table 15: gpt-5-mini achieves F1 0.096 for identifying refactoring-induced energy regressions.

arxiv:2608.06618.rationale: Finance portfolio optimization paper using jointly learned factor and graph representations via ADMM. It does not address LLMs, NLP, reasoning, prompting, agents, RAG, safety, or other preferred topics; it is a pure domain application and is therefore out of scope, with preference relevance very low. The paper has a coherent technical formulation, benchmarks, and ablations, but evaluation is limited to financial backtests and generalizability/reproducibility are constrained.
evidence: Abstract: proposes MINGLE, a factor-graph framework for portfolio diversification; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methods are involved.
Section 3 Methodology: objective couples factor decomposition and graph smoothness via ADMM.
Section 5 Experimental Results: evaluates portfolio metrics on S&P 500, Nikkei 225, and STOXX 600 backtests.

fallback:b8c7e2e64a1feb9d.rationale: Abstract-only Japanese business/agile article about user-value-first product development; no LLM, NLP, AI methodology, evaluation, or empirical evidence. Out of scope for the stated preferences.

arxiv:2608.06614.rationale: Relevant LLM-based retrieval-to-taxonomy work with RAG/NLP aspects, not Japanese/agent/safety. Factorized hypothesis search is moderately novel but bounded by hand-defined dimensions. Strong ablations, baselines, CIs, cost/robustness analyses and code release; generalizability limited by Qwen3-32B and two structured-taxonomy domains.
evidence: Section 5.4/Table 4 and Table 5 report main FHS gains over baselines on Financial Tagging and CodiEsp.
Table 6 reports component ablations, attributing gains to structured path, definition-form rendering, and candidate-level verifier.
Appendix E.4 reports retriever robustness under sparse, dense, and hybrid retrieval.
Appendix B.5 lists deployed hyperparameters and Section 5.3 states the shared Qwen3-32B backbone and selector.
Limitations note reliance on predefined semantic dimensions and a single model family.

arxiv:2608.06613.rationale: This is a medical-imaging / 3D foundation-model robustness study, outside the core LLM, Japanese NLP, reasoning, RAG, agent, and safety scope. Despite a reasonably controlled experimental setup, the contribution is domain-specific medical imaging with limited language/NLP relevance, so the final score is capped near the out-of-scope threshold.
evidence: Abstract: reports robustness is strongly model- and artifact-dependent; CKA often decreases while RankMe remains comparatively stable.
Section 4.3: reports ghosting mean Dice decreasing from 0.79 at L1 to 0.69 at L5, with Rician noise second-largest degradation.
Table 1: lists five pretrained 3D encoders and their extracted representation dimensionalities.

arxiv:2608.06612.rationale: Out-of-scope geospatial/remote-sensing foundation-model paper with no LLM/NLP/language methodology. Though it presents a distillation-based location encoder with quantitative benchmarks, ablations, and released assets, relevance to the stated preferences is minimal.
evidence: Abstract: introduces SLED as a distillation-based location encoder pretrained on Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and Landsat imagery.
Introduction: motivates against CLIP-style InfoNCE location encoders and states SLED uses MSE with batch size 128.
Methodology: describes frozen modality-specific teachers and trainable alignment heads with location as binding modality.
Benchmarking: reports CHELSA, TorchSpatial, and SustainBench linear-probe results over 5 seeded runs.

arxiv:2608.06609.rationale: Applied NLP/LLM study using DeBERTaV3 fine-tuning and Qwen3-generated critiques for educational item evaluation. Relevant to LLM/NLP and transformer preferences, but domain-specific and methodologically incremental. Quantitative comparisons are clear, with threshold and rejection-reason analyses, though limited by single split, sparse rejection-reason labels, no confidence intervals, and unavailable code/data.
evidence: Abstract: fusion model achieved Accuracy=.75, F1=.64, AUC=.80; math F1=.73 AUC=.86 vs ELA F1=.51 AUC=.72.
Section 3.2.2: DeBERTaV3-large fine-tuned with LoRA rank=32, epochs=3, weighted cross-entropy loss.
Table 1: zero-shot F1=.23, raw text-only F1=.59, critique-only F1=.55, fusion F1=.64.
Section 4.2: fusion sensitivity=.27 for bias/sensitivity/fairness/accessibility concerns; Section 3.3.1 notes only 19% of rejected test items had usable rejection reason data.

arxiv:2608.07610.rationale: Out-of-scope pure domain application in NMR metabolomics/chemometrics; no LLM, language, agent, vision, or safety methodology. Only weak Scientific AI match. The Bayesian shift-invariant NMF is a moderate methodological extension within its domain, but relevance to the stated preferences is negligible.
evidence: Abstract: proposes Bayesian Shift-Invariant Non-negative Matrix Factorization for recovering overlapping metabolites from 1D 1H NMR spectra.
Section 2.1: compares BSI-NMF with NMF, B-NMF, and B-CoShiftNMF on simulated and urine datasets.
Section 4.5: defines the Bayesian Shift-invariant NMF generative model, priors, and uniqueness discussion.

arxiv:2608.06607.rationale: Applied LLM routing for document field extraction is directly relevant to LLM cost-efficiency and inference, but remains a narrow application. The diagnostic and pre-inference feature routing are somewhat incremental over existing LLM routing/cascades, though the paper is fairly rigorous with baselines, ablations, sensitivity tests, limitations, and negative results. Generalizability is explicitly low: routing must be refit per corpus and transfers poorly. Reproducibility is aided by pinned models and released code claims.
evidence: Sec. V-C reports 33% CORD and 31% SROIE savings within 0.02 F1 of always-large.
Sec. V-D reports DeepForm held-out AUC 0.916 and no-peek saving 77% within tolerance for Haiku/Opus.
Sec. V-J and Sec. VI state the router does not transfer across datasets/genera and must be refit per corpus.
Sec. VI Limitations notes positive evidence is concentrated in receipts and DeepForm, with threshold refit per model pair.
Sec. IV-D/Reproducibility states code is released and models are pinned, with deterministic downstream analysis after oracle labeling.

arxiv:2608.06599.rationale: Out-of-scope medical/surgical AR domain application using point-cloud registration and HoloLens; no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/alignment methodology. It reports a phantom study with statistical tests, but the contribution is domain-specific and incremental. Capped at 0.20 per out-of-scope policy.
evidence: §3.1 reports median TRE of 4.05 mm full exposure, 6.10 mm teeth/nearby surface, and 7.10 mm teeth-only, with Friedman p=1.87e-9.
§3.2 reports median motion-to-display latency 0.805 s across 30 trials.
§4 acknowledges limitations including blood, saliva, instrument occlusion, fewer teeth in extraoral approaches, and rendering trade-offs.

arxiv:2608.06597.rationale: Deep linear network regularization theory is outside core LLM/NLP scope but touches training/optimization and interpretability. Analytic treatment is detailed but empirical validation is limited, with no code/data availability statement.
evidence: Summary of Key Findings: Phases correspond to (basins around) rank-restricted optima of the regularized loss landscape.
Appendix B, Table 5: Overview of hyperparameters used in the numerical experiments.
Section IV.2 Beyond the Alignment Condition and N_data to infinity: discusses finite-sample smearing and non-aligned covariance deviations.

arxiv:2608.06595.rationale: RL-focused neural ODE regularization paper; partially matches Reinforcement Learning and Training & Optimization preferences, but lacks LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning relevance. The idea has moderate novelty, but empirical support is weakened by high-variance results, overlapping standard deviations, an internal inconsistency in reported seed counts, limited ablations, and no significance testing. Reproducibility is moderate due to detailed hyperparameters but no code/availability statement.
evidence: Section 5.1 (Table 1) reports mean episode rewards; Riverraid baseline 1862.27±2399.58 vs FlowReg 2947.95±2798.64, and BeamRider 960.66±748.23 vs 1593.11±961.77, showing overlapping standard deviations without significance tests.

arxiv:2608.06589.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM and NLP as a corpus/stylometry study of LLM outputs, but primarily descriptive and not addressing model methods, training, or alignment. Novelty is incremental: idiolect framing is acknowledged as prior work, with the 2024 vs 2026 cohort comparison as the main addition. Rigor and evidence are moderate: explicit pipelines, PCA, and contraction counts with specific numbers, but no statistical significance tests or formal hypothesis testing. Generalizability is limited by English-only data and health-misinformation focus. Reproducibility is partial because prompts/settings are reported and code/data are promised, but artifacts are not yet available.
evidence: Section 5.2 reports PC1=37.6% and PC2=11.6%, with five of six 2026 models negative and all six 2024 models positive on PC1.
Table 6.1 reports Claude-Haiku-4-5 at 30,611.9 contractions per million words versus GPT-3.5 at 120.2.
Section 4.2 reports disclaimer opening rates of 46% for Claude-4.5 Haiku and 0.2% for GPT-5.4 Mini, and Mistral repetition loops around 12-14% for health misinformation.

arxiv:2608.06587.rationale: Pure swarm robotics paper using TCN and decentralized consensus for behavior classification. No LLM/NLP/language-model methodology; only minor mention of Transformer as a time-series architecture baseline. Quality is moderate but limited by small runs, no statistical testing, and constrained generalization to three behaviors and one robot/sensor setup.
evidence: Abstract: decentralized swarm behavior classification and synchronized autonomous control on real robots
Section VI-B: evaluates GRU, 1D-CNN, TCN, RNN, LSTM, and Transformer architectures for local ToF classification

arxiv:2608.06583.rationale: Astrophysics paper on JWST atmospheric retrieval for exoplanet VHS 1256 b using the Brewster framework. It has no substantive LLM/NLP/agent/vision-language methodology and is out of scope, so relevance is zero. Although the astronomy analysis includes quantitative retrieval and model comparison, it does not contribute to the preferred AI research areas.
evidence: Abstract describes retrieval modeling of JWST NIRSpec/MIRI spectroscopy for VHS 1256 b using the Brewster retrieval framework.
Section VII.9 mentions machine learning only as a possible future direction for computational bottlenecks.

arxiv:2608.06582.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application for crystal/materials generation with no language/LLM methodology; only weak relevance via reinforcement learning and scientific AI. Research quality is moderate within its domain: systematic ablations and cross-backbone comparisons exist, but no statistical significance reporting or code availability is disclosed, and the out-of-scope cap limits the overall score.
evidence: Abstract: reports both variants reduce one- and twenty-sample RMSE across MP-20 and MPTS-52 with PXRDGen and OMatG backbones.
Section 6.2: reports CrystalGRPO-Q improves MP-20 MR@1 from 59.06% to 64.63% and MPTS-52 MR@1 from 18.67% to 23.04%.

arxiv:2608.06490.rationale: Out of scope: pure computer vision/diffusion image insertion with no LLM, language methodology, reasoning, agents, or NLP focus. The paper reports ablations and training details, but relevance to target preferences is negligible, so the score is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: presents InsertFuse for multi-category reference-guided image insertion.
Method: Task Formulation and Framework Overview uses VAE encoding and flow matching, with no language methodology.
Experiments: Ablation Study (Table 2) reports module-level ablations and IOPD comparison.
Appendix A: Training and Implementation Details documents hyperparameters and training stages.

arxiv:2608.06488.rationale: Pure surgical-robot force actuation system with no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent methodology; only weak relevance via robotics/medical application preferences. The paper is a preliminary systems description with small quantitative results and no baselines, ablations, or broad generalizability.
evidence: Abstract reports force actuation errors less than 1 N.
III Preliminary Results reports mean absolute errors of 0.80 N, 0.79 N, and 0.44 N in X, Y, and Z directions.
IV Conclusions states future work includes training neural networks to estimate external force without extra sensors.

arxiv:2608.06486.rationale: Out-of-scope biology foundation model: the paper explains a BiomeGPT-style microbiome transformer, with no LLM/language methodology. It touches transformer interpretability, but the domain is explicitly capped at low relevance. The proposed source-derived IG baseline is a limited incremental contribution. Experimental evidence is proof-of-concept only: Section 4 reports fine-tuning on 8,000 samples and validation accuracy ~0.93 but no external held-out evaluation; Section 5 provides aggregate IG statistics and single-sample figures rather than a systematic benchmark against attention. Limitations in Section 6 acknowledge no clinical generalization or causal validity. Reproducibility is partially supported by a code link and training details, but model/data specifics are limited.
evidence: Section 1: describes signed Integrated Gradients for a BiomeGPT-style microbiome transformer, with no language modeling.
Section 4: reports proof-of-concept fine-tuning on 8,000 samples with validation accuracy ~0.93 and no external held-out dataset.
Section 5: presents aggregate IG means and a single sample comparison, but lacks systematic attention-vs-IG benchmark with significance.
Section 6: explicitly states this is not a clinical generalization benchmark and attribution should not be interpreted as biological causality.

arxiv:2608.06485.rationale: Relevant LLM-agent personality-evolution benchmark with strong multi-model design, human-prior anchoring, and validation suite. Moderately novel relative to prior LLM personality-stability work, and rigorous in statistical controls, but the psychometric niche, weak scenario-behavior convergence, and reliance on self-report BFI-44 constrain generality and construct validity.
evidence: Section 3.3 describes a four-stage pipeline with baseline BFI-44, life-event presentation, post-event BFI-44, and change computation over 100 personas x 11 events x 44 items.
Section 4.2 and Table 2 report pair-level kappa 0.58-0.86 and DCR 0.60-0.81 across 11 models, supporting item-level reliability claims.
Section 4.3 reports DC% 48.1-70.4% and only 11.0-16.4% of responses within the human magnitude band, with retirement reversed by all models.
Section 6 Table 5 shows event-plus-reflection excess over retest noise of 1.6x-9.0x, paraphrase sign agreement 80.0-92.7%, and delayed direction retention.

arxiv:2608.06481.rationale: Out-of-scope pure robotics/control sim-to-real paper; no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agents/language methodology. Though formal SMC verification and hardware experiments provide moderate rigor, relevance is negligible and overall is capped below 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: proposes LyEvO combining constrained Evolutionary Optimization, SMC-based verification, and Lyapunov stability analysis for sim-to-real control.
Section V-B Tables I-II report simulation violation probability and worst-case return comparisons.
Section VI Discussion and Limitations acknowledges ES sample inefficiency and step-size sensitivity.

arxiv:2608.06477.rationale: Highly relevant to agent/AI safety and red-teaming preferences: LLM-driven computer-use agents, indirect prompt injection, and safety benchmarking. The multi-step indirect prompt injection attack class and automatic decomposition pipeline are novel, though multi-turn jailbreaks exist for chatbots. Quantitative results and ablations are reported, but single-run evaluation, no confidence intervals, limited adversarial goals (12, k<=3), and exclusion of one model from averages temper rigor and evidence strength. Code/data availability and detailed prompts support reproducibility.
evidence: Section 7.2 Main Results and Table 1: fixed-depth ASR for GPT-5.4-mini rises from 41.7% at k=1 to 72.9% at k=3; average excluding EvoCUA rises from 31.3% at k=1 to 36.9% at k=3.
Section 6 Pipeline configuration and total: 480 test examples per CUA across platforms, 12 adversarial goals, depths k∈{1,2,3}; dataset/code at https://github.com/BorealisAI/StepJack.
Section 7.3 Effectiveness under Defenses and Table 4: under DSP for GPT-5.4-mini ASR goes from 15.6% at k=1 to 36.5% at k=3; PID per-sub-step detection no more than 22.9%, overall 37.5% at k=3.
Limitations: results are single-run due CUA API cost, and benchmark is limited to 12 adversarial goals and k≤3.

arxiv:2608.06474.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/code/agent/RL paper on constructing self-evolving browser-executable rewards for web development. Methods and ablations are detailed, with paired statistics and a large supplement. However evidence relies heavily on a private verifier benchmark and future/unverifiable model APIs, no explicit limitations section, and generalizability beyond web generation remains limited.
evidence: Abstract reports WebGrader-RL 52.01% FSR and WG-core-250 44.953 Full Score.
Table 1 reports matched VLM+Base-Script-RL baseline 44.13 FSR vs WebGrader-RL 52.01 FSR, plus WG-core-250 Score 38.372 vs 44.953.
Table 4 reports WebGrader verifier precision 99.3% and fault recall 85% on the WebGen-Verifier-100 Test split.
Supplementary Table 22 and Table 23 list RL hyperparameters and environment details.

arxiv:2608.06471.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, code/security tasks, synthetic training data, and fine-tuning. The framework is moderately novel via repository-level vulnerability injection with differential PoV validation, and the paper provides ablations, multi-scale student-teacher experiments, and out-of-distribution benchmark evidence. Main limits are the absence of a dedicated limitations/statistical analysis and unverified artifact availability despite detailed hyperparameters.
evidence: Abstract claims 1,034 validated vulnerabilities across 80 projects and 63 CWE categories, with SEC-bench gains of +3.3 to +14.7 points.
Section 5.1 Table 2 reports SEC-bench and PatchEval improvements across six student-teacher configurations.
Section 5.2 reports 16,172 injection attempts, 1,034 validated instances, and a KS distance of 0.165 for injected edits versus real CVE patches.
Appendix D provides fine-tuning hyperparameters and teacher-trajectory cleansing details.

arxiv:2608.06469.rationale: Moderately relevant to AI Safety via fairness, adversarial robustness, and Byzantine defenses, but outside LLM/agent/NLP areas. The work offers a simple absolute-score weighting rule with formal monotonicity, participation, and non-gamesmanship properties, including machine-checked proofs and explicit assumptions. Empirical evidence supports aggregation-weight containment under stealthy poisoning in specific regimes, but downstream fair-client EOD gains are conditional and sometimes negative; evaluation uses only three datasets, three seeds, one attacker, and omits the strongest published baseline FairTrade.
evidence: Section 5, Theorems 5.1-5.3 establish MWR, DP, and NG, with Proposition 2 bounding clipped adversarial influence.

Section 6.4 and Table 1 show stealthy Taiwan Credit adversary weight reduced by about 41% at alpha=0.5, but Adult Income gives the adversary more weight than uniform when honest clients are already unfair.
Section 7.2 explicitly lists limitations: honest score reporting assumption, local vs population fairness, missing GLocalFair/SFFL/FairTrade baselines, and limited seeds.
Section 6.2 and Table 2 show Fairis does not dominate routine non-IID fairness; FairFed attains lower EOD on Taiwan and Adult in several settings.

arxiv:2608.06467.rationale: Relevant via CLIP vision-language test-time adaptation, but narrow video facial-expression domain and no LLM/reasoning/agent/RAG focus. Method moderately novel in using energy-based sampling for personalized caches, though many components are existing cache/TTA ideas. Rigor is moderate: solid baselines, ablations, subject-level results, and complexity analysis, but limited by lack of error bars/multiple seeds, no explicit limitations section, and only one reported significance test. Evidence from tables and ablations supports the main performance claims. Generalizability is limited to three video FER datasets with one CLIP backbone. Reproducibility is supported by code availability and detailed hyperparameters.

arxiv:2608.06459.rationale: Out-of-scope quantum many-body physics/statistical mechanics paper with no LLM, NLP, transformer, agent, or AI/ML methodology. Only tangential overlap with the low-weight Scientific AI preference via physics/simulation content. The analytical and tensor-network numerical work appears moderately reasoned within its own domain, but relevance to the target areas is negligible and no code/data availability is provided.
evidence: Abstract: predicts KPZ scaling and states tensor-network numerical confirmation
Strong noise: TEBD simulations at gamma≈0.667 averaged over N≈5000 circuit samples
Weak-noise scaling: TEBD simulations of two-copy transfer-matrix dynamics for gamma∈[0.02,0.06] using N=1500 disorder samples

arxiv:2608.06377.rationale: Strongly relevant to LLMs, reasoning, prompting, AI safety, alignment, and evaluation. The selective-trust framing, matched four-condition benchmark, paired SC2W metric, and balanced DPO preference construction are meaningful contributions, though training evaluation is limited to two small open-weight families and several claims rely on deterministic exact-match scoring with proxy uncertainty for some baselines.
evidence: Table 1 reports Clean, Misleading, Correct-Context, Irrelevant, Overall, and SC2W metrics for frontier and open models, including SCOPE versus baselines.
Section 5.4 and Appendix Table 2 report zero-shot external transfer results on GSM-IC, GSM-Plus, and Sharma-style sycophancy examples.
Section 5.3 and Appendix Table 3 report construction ablations, including misleading-only and unmatched/random pair variants.
Appendix I provides training details, including DPO beta, LoRA rank, optimizer settings, and retained training-set sizes.

arxiv:2608.06375.rationale: Primarily a humanoid robot loco-manipulation/world-action model paper; language and VLM components serve only as conditioning, not core LLM/NLP methodology. Under the rubric, pure robotics/embodied AI is out of scope and capped at 0.20. The paper reports real-world baselines, ablations, and per-trial tables, but lacks statistical significance testing and remains outside the intended topic focus.
