arxiv:2608.06374.rationale: Despite the VLA framing, this is cross-embodiment robot manipulation with a VLM used as a perception backbone, not a language-model/NLP research contribution; per rubric, pure robotics is out of scope and capped at 0.20. The paper has quantitative benchmark results, ablations, and real-world rollouts, but lacks statistical uncertainty and code-release documentation.
evidence: Section 4.2 reports single-checkpoint results on LIBERO (98.0%), RoboCasa-GR1 (59.25%), and RoboTwin 2.0 (89.02%).
Section 4.4 Table 5 ablates future prediction, MoE action head, and embodiment metadata.
Section 4.3 Table 4 reports real-world average success of 75.6% across three embodiments.
Section 3.5 states the future generation head is skipped at inference.

arxiv:2608.06371.rationale: Pure mathematical PDE analysis of the Cahn-Hilliard equation; no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agent, code, safety, or other in-scope AI/ML methodology is present. The work is out of scope despite having formal mathematical arguments, so it receives minimal credit.
evidence: Abstract: studies global weak solutions to the Cahn-Hilliard equation with degenerate mobility and singular diffusion
Section 1.1: literature review of Cahn-Hilliard mathematical theory; no AI/ML content identified
Section 4: existence proof uses approximation scheme and compactness arguments

arxiv:2608.06370.rationale: Highly relevant to agentic tool use and code execution, but the study is an incremental benchmark comparison with moderate evidence. It uses a small BFCL v4 subset, echo-return stubs, no significance testing, and some headline claims (e.g., chain-length gap) lack supporting tables; overall PTC underperforms JSON in parallel categories.
evidence: Section 3.3 describes the 309-entry BFCL v4 subset and deterministic scorer.
Section 4.1 Table 2 reports JSON vs PTC accuracy and Wilson CIs for 14 models.
Section 4.2/Table 3 reports chaining ablation but does not show the claimed 18.8% gap at chain lengths >=12.
Appendix A Table 6 shows mean PTC lower than JSON overall and large parallel-category drops.

arxiv:2608.06366.rationale: Topically overlaps with multi-agent LLM workflows, structured output, and healthcare AI, but it is a domain-specific clinical feature-engineering application rather than a language-modeling contribution. The pipeline is detailed and includes ablations and an LLM comparator, but evaluation relies on 500 dummy single-institution records, lacks external validation, uses phenotype-unknown comparators, and acknowledges potential feature-label overlap; generalizability beyond heart failure is unproven.
evidence: Abstract reports HFrEF AUROC improved from 0.895 to 0.963 and HFpEF from 0.870 to 0.910 on 500 dummy records.
Section 6 Discussion states evaluation was limited to a dummy, single-institution cohort of 500 patients and external validation is needed.
Appendix A.11 reports equal-weight and random-weight rubric ablations reduced HFrEF AUROC by -0.060 and -0.058, respectively.

arxiv:2608.06364.rationale: Qualitative case study on AI transparency and digital sovereignty in Nigerian mobile shopping apps. It is not LLM/NLP methodology research and only tangentially mentions LLMs, so preference relevance is very low. Method is a three-app forensic/document analysis with inferred AI integration, limited sample, single-country scope, and no code or statistical validation.
evidence: Methodology (Page 3): Uses forensic analysis of three Android apps and document analysis; no runtime AI observation, only artifact inference.
Results and Analysis (Page 4): AI-related artifacts recovered include SQLite databases and SDK identifiers, but authors state no direct evidence of model execution or algorithmic decision-making.
Artificial Intelligence Transparency Analysis (Page 6): None of the Google Play descriptions explicitly reference AI; only Jiji's privacy policy explicitly acknowledges AI.
Conclusions and Future Work (Page 8): Authors acknowledge single-country scope and analytical rather than statistical generalization.

arxiv:2608.06363.rationale: Classical PAC learning theory with detailed proofs; not aligned with LLM/NLP/agent preferences. Rigorous theoretical contribution within its field, but no empirical or benchmark evidence and limited relevance to target topics.
evidence: Abstract
Theorem 2 (Section 2)
Lemma 3.3 (Section 3.3)

arxiv:2608.06362.rationale: Relevant mainly as an evaluation/sequential-inference method for LLM agents in imperfect-information games, but not a language-modeling contribution. The theoretical integration of AIVAT with confidence sequences is moderately novel, and formal rigor is reasonable, but empirical certification is weakened by descriptive EB-CS bounds, asymptotic miscalibration, and limited domain scope beyond poker.
evidence: Section 6.1 reports HUNL variance ratio 54.4x, AsympCS stopping ratio 74.17x, but EB-CS ratio only 1.365x and notes the HUNL EB-CS bound is descriptive.
Section 6.2 provides Leduc analytic bound B_Y=117 and reports EB-CS exact-coverage counts of 2 raw and 0 AIVAT exclusions out of 400 replications.
Section 9 states AsympCS finite-horizon exclusion rates of 7.1067% averaged over P0 conditions and 10.4% under A2 continuous monitoring.
Appendix D states P0 did not have an independently timestamped preregistration and corrected-stream EB-CS summaries remain descriptive absent an independent bound argument.

arxiv:2608.06361.rationale: Relevant to multimodal/video evaluation and temporal reasoning, but not core LLM/NLP/Japanese; primarily visual event counting limits preference match. Trace-grounded profiling is moderately novel, and the controlled protocol is fairly rigorous, but primary results rely on one proprietary VLM and natural-video transfer is weak. Quantitative evidence is provided, though no code/data release is noted.
evidence: Section 4/Table 1 Part A reports macro-average final EM 21.1%, trace F1 36.4%, and State Machine highest at 37.1% EM / 53.9% trace F1.
Section 5 states high-count, high-frequency trials recover only 18.1% of true events and report only 28% as many timestamps as occur.
Section 6 reports 4-FPS sampling raises Bounce Ball accuracy from 19.6% to 29.3% but reported sequence agrees with ground truth only 3.7% of the time.
Section 7 reports a natural-video count-pattern check with 151 TransRAC clips and 456 trials, with accuracy concentrated in low count bins.
Appendix A.1 specifies the Manim renderer, N and F ranges, 10 seeds per cell, and the resulting 2,190 videos.

arxiv:2608.06354.rationale: Pure robotics/medical hardware paper on MRI needle teleoperation; no LLM/NLP/ML methodology, so out of scope and capped at <=0.20. Engineering validation is moderately detailed but lacks ML-style baselines, statistical tests, and broad generalizability/reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: presents an MR safe master-slave robot manipulator for abdominal interventions in the MRI chamber.
Section IV-A: reports 0.11% bedside and 0.59% in-bore SNR differences and small distortion effects.
Section V-A: reports motion-transmission correlations, force transparency >85%, and frequency response data.

arxiv:2608.06353.rationale: Relevant to Agents & Tool Use and AI Safety via compute-gated governance of deployed AI agents, but not language-model or NLP methodology. The paper provides formal mechanism design with lemmas and theorems; novelty is moderate as it integrates existing PPM/QF/hardware-governance ideas. Evidence is theoretical only with no empirical, baseline, or quantitative validation, and scope is explicitly limited to club-or-commons-good agents.
evidence: Abstract: formal mechanism-design model for continuous participatory governance of a deployed AI agent
Section 5: proves sided incentive compatibility, early commitment, and breadth-weighted authorization theorem
Section 7: discusses limitations including manipulation-robustness open problem and trusted-verifier scope limit
Section 4.3: characterizes governable agent class and excludes general-purpose chatbots and irreversible actuation

arxiv:2608.06352.rationale: Highly relevant LLM-agent/code-agent training-data paper, directly matching agents/tool use, code, LLM fine-tuning, and synthetic data. The solver-calibration idea is moderately novel but builds on ZPD/solver-feedback and environment-design ideas. Empirical evaluation is fairly rigorous with shared distillation, matched ablations, decontamination, and transfer benchmarks; however, reproducibility is limited by proprietary future models, large compute, and no explicit limitations section.
evidence: Section 2.3 defines multi-solver and contrastive calibration retention criteria and the author-solver loop.
Table 1 reports Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench Pro, and Doc2Repo results for two Qwen backbones, with CalibForge outperforming baselines.
Table 3 ablates No Solver, Single Solver, Multi Solver, and Contrast Solver under matched 1,300-task settings, showing larger gains from adversarial solver calibration.
Section 3.1 describes benchmark decontamination and shared trajectory distillation; Appendix E provides SFT hyperparameters and hardware.

arxiv:2608.06351.rationale: Primarily an explainable AI/interpretability position paper with no LLM, Japanese NLP, language-model methodology, or transformer focus. It matches the interpretability and AI-safety-related preferences only moderately. The paper synthesizes prior case studies rather than presenting new primary experiments, lacks baselines and ablations, and provides limited implementation detail.
evidence: Section 3.1 describes DetoxAI using CRP saliency maps and reports improvement in group fairness metrics such as EqualizedOdds and Demographic Parity.
Section 3.2 reports a human survey of 148 completed responses with ranking point totals ProtoPNet 1,045, ACE 763, RISE 643, and correlations with expected animal features.
Section 4 states counterfactual evaluation measures are often unaligned or contradictory and that there is no single definitive best method.
Section 5 describes adapting prototypes and group counterfactuals to concept drift, using measures such as cosine similarity between vectors over time.

arxiv:2608.06347.rationale: Directly relevant to multilingual LLM reasoning transfer and includes Japanese among evaluated languages; the RPT-gate self-distillation mechanism is moderately novel. Strengths include multiple languages, strong baselines, ablations, and cross-family/out-of-domain checks, but rigor is limited by single-run main results without variance or significance testing and no explicit limitations section.
evidence: Section 3.1: Uses Qwen3-1.7B/4B, 17 target languages, 500 OpenThoughts training examples, AfriMGSM pass@12 and PolyMath DW-ACC evaluation.
Table 1: RP-OPSD reports AfriMGSM averages of 19.07 (1.7B) and 26.83 (4B), and PolyMath averages of 17.97 (1.7B) and 31.87 (4B).
Section 4.1/Table 2: TG reaches 26.0 SWA pass@12 and 74.8 FRA ACC@1 compared with RG 20.8/74.0 and BG 15.6/73.2; removing reference anchoring drops full RP-OPSD from 29.6/76.8 to 27.6/73.6.
Appendix I: Provides training hyperparameters including learning rate, LoRA rank, EMA decay, gate sharpness, and anchoring coefficient; Abstract claims code availability.

arxiv:2608.06346.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents/tool use and agent failure attribution. The staged error-lifecycle framework and TrajErrBench are moderately novel but build on prior critical-error detection work. Rigor is moderate: multiple benchmarks, ablations, annotation agreement, and limitations are provided, but no significance testing, exact-step accuracies remain low, and model/version claims are unverified. Evidence is quantitative but limited by modest absolute gains and no confidence intervals. Generalizability across seven benchmarks and transfer experiments is decent; reproducibility is supported by detailed prompts and code/data release claims but not independently verified.
evidence: Section 5, Table 1 reports main exact-step accuracy and baselines
Section 5.3, Table 2 reports ablation results
Section 6, Table 3 reports application repair and transfer results
Section 9 notes LLM dependence and staged-pipeline false negatives

arxiv:2608.06340.rationale: Out-of-scope statistical time-series/econometrics paper on scalable VARMA estimation. It has no LLM, NLP, transformer, agent, reasoning, alignment, or other listed AI/ML theme; its 'evaluation/benchmark' content is forecast MSE on time-series data, not LLM evaluation. Although the paper is methodologically strong with formal proofs, synthetic and real-data experiments, ablations, significance tests, and posted code, the strict relevance rubric and out-of-scope domain cap limit the final score to 0.15 (at most 0.20 for non-AI/domain work).
evidence: Abstract: describes a scalable VARMA estimation framework with partial-autocorrelation reparametrization, sufficient statistics, and Fourier/Parseval evaluation; also seasonal VARMA and VARMAX extensions.
Section 5.6: Theorem 6 states recovery guarantees for infinite-VAR coefficients under approximate empirical minimization.
Section 7.1: reports synthetic forecast MSE comparisons among RLS, JMAP, and bigtime.
Section 7.2-7.4: reports real-data evaluations on Dominick's retail, Singapore meteorological, and Beijing air-quality benchmarks.
Code availability: states implementation and experiment drivers are available at https://github.com/paulindani/VARMA.

arxiv:2608.06337.rationale: The paper is a theoretical statistical learning result on minimax rates under monotone adversarial insertions. It has little relevance to the stated LLM/NLP preferences; the only tangential link is adversarial robustness. The work is rigorous within its narrow setting, with formal theorems and proofs, but no empirical or language-model methodology, limiting overall fit.
evidence: Abstract states minimax expected error rates under monotone adversaries.
Theorem 3.1 states optimal VC-dimension rates, including the dimension-one bound.
Theorem 3.5 provides a projective-plane lower bound for d=2.
Proposition 3.14 establishes the VC dimension one upper bound.

arxiv:2608.06332.rationale: Robotic manipulation world model using video diffusion and visual actions; falls under pure robotics/video generation, which is out-of-scope and capped at 0.20 despite weak embodied/video relevance. The paper provides baselines, ablations, OOD metrics, real-robot policy evaluation, and data-synthesis experiments, but evidence is mostly self-reported tables without statistical testing or code release.
evidence: Table I reports Clean-to-Clean and Clean-to-Random metrics with baselines and ablations.
Section IV-A defines the RoboTwin evaluation protocol and metrics.
Appendix A provides architecture, hyperparameters, and inference details.
Table III reports per-task real-world policy success rates across data regimes.

arxiv:2608.06331.rationale: Relevant LLM application: uses LLM semantic inference with deterministic DB grounding and clarification, touching LLM/RAG/grounding/evaluation. Not core LLM methodology, and is limited to relational schema construction. Evaluation includes 8 DBs, ablations, blind test and retrieval checks, but references are partly self-annotated and section/table reporting has inconsistencies (e.g., 2 vs 21 miscategorized attributes); code availability is only claimed.
evidence: Section 4.1 describes deterministic structural profiling of tables, columns, keys, samples, cardinalities, and nulls.
Section 5.3/Table 2 reports 100% pass across self-generated retrieval tests for all domains.
Section 5.7 reports metadata ablation: hospital FK recovery drops from 25/25 to 13/25 with 4 spurious joins when metadata stripped.
Limitations states scope is relational/tabular data; hierarchical/graph sources are outside scope and value-overlap checks assume full database access.

Section 5.4 says two miscategorized attributes were corrected, while Table 3 caption reports 21 miscategorized attributes, and Table 3 roles show 93.9%-100%, contradicting the text's 100% characterization claim.

arxiv:2608.06329.rationale: Relevant to LLM/agent evaluation and LLM-as-judge, but limited to tau-bench/IntellAgent-style conversational benchmarks. Validation uses controlled perturbations and human correlation, yet human validation is from one author, generator and judge model overlap creates self-preference risk, only two domains are tested, and no code/data availability is shown.
evidence: Abstract: proposes reference-free LLM-judge metrics for benchmark consistency, complexity, and policy coverage
Section 5.2 and Table 2: reports ordering scores across generators, judges, and domains
Section 5.4 and Table 3: reports human-validation Kendall correlations
Limitations: restricts scope to tau-bench- and IntellAgent-style benchmarks and excludes code/computer settings

arxiv:2608.06325.rationale: This is a theoretical fair-division/economics paper on existence of EF1 and fPO allocations under balancedness and category constraints. It is outside the stated AI/LLM/NLP/vision/robotics scope; mentions of GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude are only as proof-checking/writing aids, not as the research subject. Formal proof content is present but there is no empirical validation, model, dataset, or code, so relevance and reproducibility are low.
evidence: Abstract: 'All the proofs in this document were obtained using GPT-5.6-Sol with guidance from the authors.'
Section 1 Introduction: 'We study the existence of fair and efficient allocations of indivisible goods to agents under the balancedness constraint...'
Acknowledgements: 'All the mathematical proofs and counterexamples were derived by OpenAI Codex (GPT-5.6-Sol at Max effort)...'

arxiv:2608.06322.rationale: This is a conceptual vision/position paper on applying AI to education and student success, briefly mentioning LLMs, agentic systems, and RAG, but it is a pure domain application rather than an LLM/ML methods study. It provides no experiments, baselines, ablations, or new quantitative results, and its claims rely on prior institution-reported deployments with acknowledged causal limitations.
evidence: Section 13: 'the evidence base remains thin. Much of the flagship data is institution-reported and correlational, and independent causal evaluation is limited.'
Section 12: lists future research questions rather than presenting completed empirical work.
Section 5: Student Digital Twin is presented as a conceptual simulation framework, not an evaluated model.

arxiv:2608.06315.rationale: Formal verification of security protocols (Tamarin-to-ProVerif translation) is outside the target LLM/NLP/agent/code/AI-safety preference scope; no relevant topic match. Despite internal formal proofs and an artifact, the relevance is effectively zero, and the overall score is kept low under the out-of-scope cap.
evidence: Section 7.4 Verification Outcome reports 237/238 non-XOR definitive pairs agree, with the sole non-XOR disagreement flagged as an incomplete dp3t model.
Appendix B Soundness and Completeness Proofs presents weak simulation, state relation, and soundness/completeness arguments.
Appendix A Open Science provides a Docker recipe, evaluation inventory, result JSONL, and DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21827126.

arxiv:2608.06312.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM benchmarking, multi-agent orchestration, and evaluation, but domain-specific. Novelty is moderate: a first GB/T standard-review benchmark and taxonomy plus an agent framework, though the underlying techniques are largely known. Experiments are extensive across 14 models and include ablations, but lack statistical error bars, repeated runs, direct agent-framework baselines, and clear code/data release. Generalizability beyond GB/T standards is asserted but not demonstrated.
evidence: Abstract: claims GB/T-Bench with 7,306 traceable error instances and GB/T-Reviewer multi-agent framework.
GB/T-Bench Construction and Quality Control: reports 488 documents, 64,991 sections, 7,306 errors, and human validation agreement.
Experiments and Results: Table 2 reports human and LLM performance, with strongest LLM at 0.3280 CMCS versus human 0.6640.
Ablation Study: reports component removal effects for GPT-5.5.
Appendix E: provides prompt specifications and rule configurations.

arxiv:2608.06311.rationale: Pure medical imaging study of FLAIR super-resolution and white-matter hyperintensity segmentation. No LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning/language methodology, so it falls into the explicitly excluded medical imaging domain and gets minimal relevance. Within that domain the controlled simulation, multiple segmenters, and bootstrap CIs provide moderate evidence, but findings are limited by one cohort, simulated thick slices, a single expert reference, and no code/data availability claim.
evidence: §2.3 Lesion-level analysis and statistics
§3.2 Super-resolution recovers lesion signal, with ECLARE leading
Table 3

arxiv:2608.06310.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM RLHF/reward modeling. The proposed RRC method is moderately novel but largely combines ranking-based rewards with generative reward models. Empirical evaluation is broad across LLaMA/Qwen backbones and several benchmarks, but rigor is limited by no error bars, no explicit limitations, and a clear query-complexity error (m(m-1)/2 is O(m^2), not O(m log m)).
evidence: Abstract reports 35.8%→41.3% on AlpacaEval2 and 8.0%→11.2% on ArenaHardV2.
Table 1 compares DRM, GRM w/ PRC, RRC-SCR, and RRC-AGR across AE2/AH2/WiB/MMLR/MATH.
Section 5.1 describes LLaMA/Qwen backbones, HelpSteer3 training data, GRPO settings, and baselines.
Appendix C.1 computes SCR pairwise cost as m(m-1)/2 but incorrectly labels it O(m log m).

arxiv:2608.06307.rationale: Pure LiDAR scene-coordinate localization with uncertainty estimation; no LLM/NLP/language methodology, so out-of-scope under the stated criteria. Technical contribution is incremental over LightLoc, and evaluation is limited to two LiDAR benchmarks with some baseline inconsistencies.
evidence: Section 4.3 Table 2 reports UQ-Loc average 0.68 m/0.70° vs LightLoc 0.81 m/1.08° on QEOxford.
Section 4.5 Table 3 config A reports mean TE 0.63 m, while full model D reports 0.68 m; Section 4.3 Table 1 reports LightLoc reproduction mean TE 0.81 m, showing a baseline inconsistency.
Section 4.4 reports ECE 0.014 on QEOxford and 0.01 on NCLT.
Section 4.2 provides implementation details including Adam, cosine decay, λ=0.001, and A100 GPU.

arxiv:2608.06305.rationale: Strong match to RAG, agentic tool use, interpretability, long-document retrieval, and evaluation. Methodology includes paired baselines, ablations, Holm-corrected tests, and honest null results, but sample is one document/one backbone/51 questions, which limits generalizability and evidence strength.
evidence: Section 8.1 / Table 8 reports Read 58.8% vs dense 15.7%, Δ +43.1 pp, Holm-corrected p=2e-5.
Section 8.2 states BM25 is not statistically separated and narrows the claim to embedding-based vs embedding-free retrieval.
Section 9 lists limitations: one document, one backbone, 51 questions, author-built benchmark, and one converter.
Code and Data Availability states code, benchmark, and raw result records are released under MIT at the READ repository.

arxiv:2608.06301.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM, agentic systems, coding agents, and evaluation/benchmarking. The benchmark contribution is moderately novel: it standardizes harness optimization under held-out evaluation, but builds on prior VeRO/MetaHarness work. Rigor is moderate: controlled budgets, held-out splits, and resolution bands are strengths, but two runs per configuration and descriptive rather than formal statistical inference limit fine-grained conclusions. Evidence is reasonably quantitative with tables and ranges, though some claims are correlational and small-sample. Generalizability is moderate across four tasks and multiple harnesses, but restricted to Python and one target model per task. Reproducibility is strong per the described pinned splits, sandboxing, versioning, and artifact release.
evidence: Table 1 reports normalized gain and task resolution bands across optimizer model-harness configurations.
Section 5.1 reports model choice moving gain by 0.142 on average versus 0.079 for harness choice.
Appendix E describes pinned datasets, committed split manifests, sandboxed evaluations, lockfiles, and release of seed agents and evaluation harness.
Limitations acknowledges candidates are restricted to Python and each task uses one pinned target model.

arxiv:2608.06300.rationale: Moderate relevance: CAV/SAE bias auditing of transformer speaking graders aligns with interpretability and AI safety/fairness preferences, but the speech-assessment domain and absence of LLM-specific methodology limit fit. Method is a reasonable extension of prior CAV work with clear experiments across two models/datasets and seed variation; evaluation is moderately rigorous but lacks statistical significance testing, and reproducibility is limited by BULATS/checkpoint/code availability.
evidence: Abstract: extends CAV-based bias analysis to BERT and Whisper speaking assessment and investigates SAEs.
Table II: grader performance PCC 0.68-0.79; Section V-C describes architecture/depth sensitivity differences.
Table IV: BERT Layer 2 Dutch B_gr 0.52 vs SAE-CAV 0.92; Section V-D describes attenuation toward baseline.
Section IV-A: S&I corpus is public; BULATS metadata and S&I inferred gender described.

arxiv:2608.06296.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/reasoning post-training method. Replaces ground-truth teacher context in OPSD with self-consistency-derived pseudo-solutions; meaningful but incremental over prior self-consistency/OPSD work. Quantitative benchmarks across multiple Qwen sizes/modes support claims, with ablations and limitations, but single model family/domain, no seed-level error bars, and best-checkpoint reporting limit certainty.
evidence: Table 1: Qwen3-4B non-thinking u-OPSD avg 49.49 vs base 40.96 and OPSD 46.29; Qwen3-8B u-OPSD 54.31 vs base 43.57 and OPSD 52.04.
Table 2: thinking-mode u-OPSD 77.05 (4B) and 77.99 (8B), roughly matching OPSD.
Section 4.3 ablation reports threshold sweep tau=0.3 best 58.59 vs default 57.10 and tau=0.9 44.40.
Limitations states error bars 'pending' and domain is competition mathematics requiring extractable answers.

arxiv:2608.06294.rationale: Predominantly a clinical EHR mortality prediction application, out-of-scope despite agentic LLM feature selection and QLSTM components. The paper does not provide controlled comparison against conventional feature selection, results are from a single MIMIC-IV cohort with no external validation, and quantum results are noiseless simulations.
evidence: Abstract claims agentic LLM-guided feature selection outperforms conventional feature selection, but Section 4.1/Table 5 only compares against random selection in controlled experiments.
Section 3.3.2 states all VQCs are simulated on PennyLane default.qubit and reported results reflect ideal noiseless conditions without gate errors, decoherence, or readout noise.
Section 3.3.3 gives prompt/hyperparameter details but contains no code or dataset availability statement.
Section 5/Table 7 shows the main AUROC advantage over parameter-matched LSTM is 0.852 vs 0.835 with no external validation.

arxiv:2608.06292.rationale: In-scope neuro-symbolic RAG paper combining LLM-based Prolog synthesis with retrieval, reasoning, and explainability. Strong topical relevance to RAG, LLMs, reasoning, and interpretability, but evaluation is limited to one legal QA benchmark (ShARC) with a single baseline family, no statistical testing or code release, and limited evidence for broad generalization.
evidence: Section 4.3 reports NeSy-RAG 61.1% accuracy (k=10) versus LLM RAG 42.8% with gpt-oss:20b on ShARC.
Section 4.1 describes using random distractor snippets and a simulated user that answers follow-up questions from withheld context.
Section 5 identifies over-generation of dynamic predicates as the primary limitation, causing yes instances to be misclassified as more.
Appendix B provides the LLM prompts used for Prolog generation, query generation, and baselines.

arxiv:2608.11256.rationale: Relevant LLM-detector evaluation with adversarial humanization, careful proxy-label and clustered-inference framing, but limited by narrow English-abstract corpus, two detectors, one rewrite model/humanizer, and only modest novelty over prior detection-reliability work.
evidence: Section 2.1: 642 OpenAlex English abstracts across chemistry, computer science, political science, and theology for 2013-15 and 2023-25, with three Gemini 3 Flash rewrite conditions, Pangram/GPTZero scoring, and Undetectable AI v11 humanization.
Table 2: reports 2013-15 proxy FPR 0.0% for Pangram/GPTZero, 2023-25 original flag rates 15.0% (Pangram) and 8.9% (GPTZero), and post-humanization FNR >96% for AI-labeled rewrites.
Table 3: pre-humanization FNR for refine (abstract only) is 35.6% Pangram/62.4% GPTZero in 2013-15 and 19.9%/51.5% in 2023-25.
Table 6: long-token ratio and AWL token ratio correlate positively with detector scores (Pangram rho 0.336/0.346; GPTZero 0.304/0.320, p<0.001).
Appendix C: paper-clustered bootstrap intervals include 2023-25 Pangram original flag rate 15.0% [11.4,19.2] and refine flag rate 80.1% [75.9,84.5].
Appendix A: limitations include English published abstracts, proxy labels at tau=0.50, one generator (Gemini 3 Flash), two commercial detectors, one humanizer, and corpus-size/cost constraints.

arxiv:2608.06291.rationale: Relevant quantization/compression method for Transformer LLMs, matching Scaling & Efficiency and LLM efficiency preferences. Strong formal complexity analysis and proofs support the algorithmic contribution, and runtime/end-to-end experiments provide quantitative evidence, though end-to-end accuracy gains are mixed and no code release is documented.

Table 3: runtime benchmarks show speedups over BaKron-antidiagonal up to 60.0x for 8192x8192.
Appendix D, Tables 5-10: experiments on Llama-3 and Qwen3 models up to 8B report Wikitext2 PPL, PIQA, Winogrande, time, and core share vs GPTQ/RTN.
Table 1 and Appendix C: asymptotic sequential steps and total cost are stated and proved.

arxiv:2608.06290.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application for athlete monitoring; only a small Transformer encoder connects to preference topics. arxiv:2608.06287.rationale: Centrally uses LLMs with few-shot prompting for NL-to-LTL translation, fitting LLM/NLP/reasoning preferences. However, the contribution is mainly an empirical snapshot rather than a new method; the benchmark is small (15 requirements) and manually evaluated without reported inter-annotator checks or statistical significance testing, limiting rigor and evidence. Generalizability is limited by the single formal language and small sample. Reproducibility is partially supported by a repository and description of prompt/trials, but exact hyperparameters and proprietary model access are not fully specified.

arxiv:2608.06283.rationale: Optimization-focused Langevin sampling paper with a real LLM-pretraining application (nanochat/GPT-2 lineage), so moderately relevant to Training & Optimization and Large Language Models, but not to language methodology or NLP. The theoretical contribution is substantial and comparisons against prior rates are explicit; however, empirical evidence is limited to small-scale pretraining runs with single final values, and some cross-references/section markers are incomplete. Reproducibility is only moderate due to missing code/data and reliance on hyperparameter tables.
evidence: Abstract: introduces SG-TULA, claims W2 convergence and excess-risk bounds, and states verification/pretraining on a GPT-2 lineage LLM against AdamW and Muon.

Appendix I: derives curvature bounds for the regularized nanochat potential, with Proposition 8 claiming A1-A3.

arxiv:2608.06281.rationale: Out-of-scope nuclear many-body physics benchmarking; no LLM/NLP/ML methodology or preference match. The paper provides systematic FCI-vs-PHF comparisons and detailed methods, but relevance to requested AI/ML topics is nil and out-of-scope cap applies.

arxiv:2608.06276.rationale: The paper is a topological data analysis/reinforcement learning study on persistence diagrams, with no LLM, NLP, transformer, prompting, agent, or safety content. RL is present but is peripheral to the requested language-model-centric preferences, so relevance is low. No code or data availability statement is provided, and hyperparameters such as the weighting coefficients are not fully specified.

arxiv:2608.06275.rationale: Out-of-scope domain-specific medical/dental computer vision application using Mask R-CNN; no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, prompting, agents, or language methodology. arxiv:2608.06270.rationale: Directly relevant multimodal LLM/tool-use causal audit, matching LLM, tool-use, reasoning, multimodal, and evaluation preferences. arxiv:2608.06265.rationale: Out-of-scope healthcare/clinical benchmark dataset paper with only tangential mentions of enterprise AI agents and reasoning; no LLM/NLP methodology is developed. Research quality is modest: deterministic rule-based revisions and quantitative realism panels are provided, but evaluation is internal, lacks code/data or gold annotation, and has limited generalizability outside care-gap workflows.

Table 1 compares Base, Refinement-A, Refinement-B, Dense Control, and Reference Cohort on missingness, actionable rows, zero-actionable patients, token share, recommendation outputs, and source fidelity.

Table 2 shows all benchmark variants meet the 0.90 measure-enrichment utility floor while temporal grounding remains weak, especially for Dense Control.

arxiv:2608.06448.rationale: Out-of-scope materials-science/electron-diffraction domain application with only weak overlap to Scientific AI and graph attention; no LLM/NLP/agent methodology. The paper has quantitative simulated benchmark results and ablations, but is capped because it is a pure domain application without language methodology and lacks experimental transfer.

Results: Table 2 and signal ablations report paired confidence intervals and input intervention outcomes.

Code and Data Availability: public code/checkpoints and a 256-structure subset; full 138.38-GB ED-CS payload is not hosted.

arxiv:2608.06264.rationale: Medical imaging segmentation data augmentation paper out of scope for LLM/NLP preferences; only weak overlap with synthetic data/training/medical preferences. Method applies optimal transport but is limited to brain lesion MRI tasks; comparisons and statistics are present but training sets are small and no ablations.
evidence: Abstract: introduces OTLesMix using Wasserstein barycenter and optimal transport plan; evaluated on three brain lesion segmentation tasks, improving Dice by 2.9-6.6 points over no synthetic data.
Experiments: compares OTLesMix against MixUp, CutMix, and CarveMix using nnUNet on BraTS 2020, ATLAS v2.0, and ISLES 2022.
Discussion and Conclusion: reports generation time around 1 second for 2D and 1-3 minutes for 3D; notes linear interpolation can yield unrealistic inpainted lesions.

arxiv:2608.06262.rationale: Low topical relevance: the core contribution is statistical hypothesis testing with conditional queries, only motivated by model evaluation and benchmarks rather than LLM/NLP/agent methods. The work is formally rigorous with detailed proofs for learnability and adaptivity-gap bounds, but evidence is theoretical only and generalizability is limited by the finite-outcome conditional-sampling assumptions.
evidence: Section 3, Theorem 3.1 states the exact learnability criterion and zero-separation risk 1/2.
Section 4, Theorem 4.1 states the universal non-adaptive simulation bound O(N^2(T+log(1/rho))).
Section 5, Theorem 5.1 states the matching quadratic lower bound Theta_epsilon(N^2).
Section 6, Scope and Limitations discusses model assumptions and limits.
Appendices A, B, and C contain proofs of the learnability criterion, simulation bound, and lower bound.

arxiv:2608.06261.rationale: Formal verification of cryptographic game-hopping proofs in Lean is outside the stated AI/LLM/NLP preferences. LLM mentions appear only as tooling/future work, not as research contribution. Assessed as out-of-domain despite apparent formal rigor.

Use of AI tools section states GPT-5.5, DeepSeek-V4, and Aristotle were used for Lean code and manuscript preparation, not as the research focus.
Conclusion mentions future investigation of whether large language models can construct formal game-hopping proofs.

arxiv:2608.06259.rationale: Pure chemistry reaction-modeling paper with no LLM/NLP methodology. It matches only low-weight generic tags such as foundation model, GNN, and scientific AI, so relevance is capped low. The method combines known CRG, GIN, and SimCLR-style contrastive learning with limited novelty. Yield comparisons across four datasets and repeated splits provide some quantitative evidence, but marginal gains on proprietary datasets, absent statistical testing or ablations, and qualitative OOD analysis weaken robustness. Missing code, data availability, and many training details limit reproducibility.
evidence: §2.8 describes pretraining on 1.7M Pistachio reactions and four downstream yield datasets.
§2.7 reports 80/5/15 train/validation/test splits with five seeds and early stopping.

arxiv:2608.06257.rationale: Out of scope for the stated LLM/NLP-focused preferences: this is a multiplayer video world model / game-simulation paper using a decoder-only Transformer but no language methodology. The only weak preference connections are low-weight Transformer Architecture, Computer Vision, and Video/Temporal categories. Methodologically, the typed authoritative state is somewhat novel within world models, and the appendix reports detailed protocols, but evaluation is on toy grid games with small test sets, no error bars, and some long-horizon claims are under-evidenced. Capped at 0.20 due out-of-scope status.
evidence: Section 4.5 / Table 2: MASS parser 0.764 vs B-PV 0.128, but on a custom matched Snake benchmark with N=2 and only eight test episodes per Appendix 7.1

arxiv:2608.06253.rationale: MetaboLLM is a biology/domain-specific foundation-model application for metabolomics, so the explicit out-of-scope cap applies despite using LLM fine-tuning, RAG, and graph methods. It reports quantitative comparisons and ablations, but clinical validation is limited (small single-center CABG cohort, no independent clinical cohort), internal description metrics partly measure agreement with GPT-5-mini-generated references, and edge-count selection within cohorts likely makes performance optimistic.
evidence: Results/Page 15: MetaboLLM-GIN reports AUC 0.8616 ± 0.0297 for stress hyperglycemia prediction with p<0.0001 versus baselines.
Discussion/Page 20: internal metrics partly measure agreement with teacher GPT-5-mini-generated descriptions rather than biochemical correctness.
Discussion/Page 22: primary clinical evaluation involved a small, single-center CABG cohort; repeated cross-validation does not replace independent validation.
Methods/Page 29: source code, adapted model weights, and corpus availability are stated on GitHub/Hugging Face, though clinical data require request/approval.

arxiv:2608.06252.rationale: Pure computer-vision Bangla sign language recognition with a lightweight CNN; no LLM, NLP language modeling, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, or code methodology. The paper has relatively thorough domain-specific ablations, cross-dataset tests, and deployment measurements, but topic relevance is out of scope per the rubric, capping the score below 0.20.

Section 6.2 reports 96.37% test accuracy on RSBdSL38 and 95.72% ± 0.54% over five seeds.
Section 6.10 reports Grad-CAM/Grad-CAM++ localization and deletion/insertion faithfulness checks.

arxiv:2608.06250.rationale: The paper is a theoretical statistical learning study of early-stopped GD for Gaussian mixture classification. It only tangentially matches the Training & Optimization preference via gradient descent/loss functions and lacks LLM/NLP/agent/vision/language relevance. Theoretical contributions (new calibration, lower bounds, optimality for FCD spectra) are moderately novel and rigorously developed with appendices, but scope is narrow, stopping time is oracle-based, and no code/data are provided.

arxiv:2608.06246.rationale: Relevant survey/taxonomy of post-training adaptation for LLMs and foundation models covering RAG, alignment, reasoning, prompting, interpretability, and safety. arxiv:2608.06243.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM reasoning, RLVR, and training optimization. arxiv:2608.07600.rationale: Pure robotics/visuo-tactile grasping application with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, or agent language methodology; incidental multi-head attention does not make it in-scope. arxiv:2608.06241.rationale: Pure weather-forecasting domain application. arxiv:2608.06240.rationale: Paper is a pure computer vision/medical imaging method for unpaired image-to-image translation using flow matching; no LLM, language-model, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, code, safety, or interpretability methodology. arxiv:2608.06228.rationale: This paper studies Agile software development project success factors using PLS-SEM. It contains no LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agent, alignment, safety, or other in-scope AI methodology and is a pure domain application outside the stated preferences. Methodologically it has some rigor (EFA, measurement model checks, bootstrapping), but relevance is zero and the final score is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: PLS-SEM with SmartPLS was used to analyze data and test hypotheses about Agile project success factors.
Introduction and Background: the focus is Agile software development project success and critical success factors, not AI/LLM/NLP.
Research Results: final significant factors are Project Governance, Project Management, and Team Effectiveness.
Conclusion: limitations include sampling strategy and sample size of 208.

arxiv:2608.06227.rationale: Out-of-scope physical AI/wireless digital-twin framework; only incidental LLM/agent mentions. Conceptual vision with formal equations but no experiments, baselines, ablations, or quantitative validation, yielding low evidence and reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract and Section I frame the paper as a networked holonic digital twin framework for physical AI over wireless networks, not as an LLM/language-model methodology study.
Section II-B3 mentions LLM-based agentic frameworks only as a limitation; core methods are causal Markov blankets, active inference, category theory, and integrated information theory.
Section IV presents formal equations such as expected free energy and cognitive value but reports no quantitative results, baselines, or ablations.
Section V and Section VI provide open challenges and conclusions without experimental validation, code/data release, or reproducibility details.

arxiv:2608.06223.rationale: Time series forecasting with RAG is a non-language domain application; despite using retrieval-augmented generation and transformer/attention components, it lacks LLM/NLP relevance under the stated curation scope. The paper provides benchmark comparisons and ablations, but no significance tests, uncertainty, limitations, or code availability, limiting confidence.
evidence: Section 3.2.1: reference tokens are prepended to patchified inputs.
Table 1: reports averaged MSE/MAE on ECL, ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2, and Weather.
Section 4.2.3: TCN retrieval time is 0.004s versus 14.27s for DTW and 0.002s for ED.
Section 4.2.2: best results use a single retrieved reference sequence.

arxiv:2608.06221.rationale: Pure robotics/LfD paper on handwriting trajectory learning via GMM+GMR and human-likeness evaluation; no LLM/NLP or language methodology. Though it has a moderate user study, quantitative results, and open-source data/code, the out-of-scope cap limits the overall score.
evidence: Section IV-B describes GMM+GMR extensions with force and normalized time and multi-segment stroke processing.
Section V reports overall mean human-likeness score of 71.50 (SD=22.56) from 1,092 ratings.
Section III-B states the dataset and code are publicly available in a GitHub repository.

arxiv:2608.06219.rationale: Pure robotics/teleoperation HRI study with no language-model, NLP, reasoning, or other prioritized methodology; out-of-scope despite the low-weight robotics category. The work has a controlled user study and quantitative results, but limited novelty/generalizability and a small non-professional sample.
evidence: Section VI-A: median completion time 2.50 min (touchscreen) vs 5.38 min (joystick), Wilcoxon p=0.028; sinusoidal coverage 90.7% vs 84.1%, p=0.004.
Section VI-B: NASA-TLX 43 vs 52; CLI ordering C1>C2>C3; trust ANOVA F(2,38)=4.12 p=0.023, with C1>C2 trust posterior mean +0.06.
Section VII: limitations include 20-participant sample, single short familiarization, non-professional operators, laboratory setting.

arxiv:2608.06218.rationale: Optimization-theory paper on Muon/Stiefel manifold with only indirect LLM/NLP relevance via general training optimization and LoRA/orthogonality constraints. The mathematical derivation and convergence analysis show moderate rigor, but empirical evidence is limited to CPU subproblem runtime/error comparisons and no language-model or end-to-end training evaluation is provided.
evidence: Section 2, Proposition 1: presents a closed-form solution to the Skewon problem via SVD and gives optimal objective value as negative nuclear norm.
Section 4, Algorithms 1-2: specifies Skewon steps and asymptotic complexity; Section 6 describes CPU experiments with CVXPY/SCS reference and 50 runs.
Section 5, Theorem 3: provides first-order convergence guarantees for smooth non-convex objectives under Assumption 1.

arxiv:2608.06216.rationale: Highly relevant LLM/agentic-AI continual-learning survey with a tri-axial When/Where/How taxonomy. It is a conceptual/narrative survey without new empirical results, systematic search protocol, or code/data, limiting rigor, evidence strength, and reproducibility.
evidence: Abstract: proposes a tri-axial framework across When, How, and Where learning occurs to characterize continual learning transition.
Section 1: motivates the survey via LLM and Agentic AI advances and frames CL as continual capability evolution.
Section 3.3.2: discusses memory, skills, and protocols as external harness capability carriers.
Section 5: acknowledges limitations including classification ambiguity, coverage cutoff, and evaluation gaps.

arxiv:2608.09988.rationale: In-scope LLM agent evaluation benchmark with substantial alignment to LLM, agents, and evaluation preferences, though specialized to financial portfolio management. Novelty is incremental, integrating point-in-time gating, cost-aware labels, and enforced natural-language mandates. Rigor is moderate: good deterministic evaluator, baselines, and ablations, but single-window, few-seed evidence and no validated alpha. Reproducibility is well documented via saved run artifacts and code/data URLs.
evidence: Abstract: OpenPM code and data available at github.com/aslcai/OpenPM-Bench and huggingface.co/datasets/aslcai/OpenPM-Bench.
§3.2: availability gate requires ts_available ≤ T for agent-visible records.
§5: frozen S&P 500 universe, 44 trading days, 3,432 five-minute bars, six analyst captures replayed through five constructors.
Table 2: on gpt-5 analyst capture, gpt-5 constructor ΔEW +5.3 but on DeepSeek capture ΔEW -1.0; same-pool EW returns 7.2% vs 8.0%.
§6.2: replacing DeepSeek analysts with gpt-5 analysts raises constructor performance while same-pool EW changes only from 8.0% to 7.2%.
§6.4/Table 3: daily-cadence net returns vary with turnover (22-44), high-turnover constructors slip below SPY.
Limitations: single-window, no-market-impact upper bounds, not validated alpha.
Appendix E: runs backed by saved directories, manifests, hashes, per-stage logs, and redacted prompts.

arxiv:2608.06213.rationale: Recommender-systems paper with generative retrieval and distillation, but it is a pure domain application outside the specified LLM/NLP/agent scope, with only weak overlap via transformer/distillation. Method is incremental over Gryphon; it has offline baselines, ablations, and an online A/B, but evidence is domain-specific and several metrics are teacher-relative. Single music surface and no code/data release limit generalizability and reproducibility. Overall capped as out-of-scope.
evidence: Section 5.2, Table 1 reports Gryphon-v2 R@1000 0.8615, T-R@10 0.5654, T-R@100 0.7344, and WPA 0.5892.
Section 5.3, Table 2 reports online A/B relative changes: +1.41% active users, +1.62% total listening time, +7.12% likes, and -9.65% unfinished-track ratio.
Section 6 states the experiment ran on a single music recommendation surface and does not establish long-term or full-population effects.
Appendix A gives architecture hyperparameters and training details, but no code or dataset release is reported.

arxiv:2608.06211.rationale: Image-only adversarial/poisoning and watermarking paper with no LLM, language, or NLP methodology; falls under out-of-scope pure computer vision/security domain and is capped at 0.20. It shows moderate novelty in combining reversible unlearnable examples with dual watermark extraction and mutual-information minimization, and includes experiments across image datasets, but relevance to the requested language-focused topics is minimal.
evidence: Abstract describes reversible unlearnable examples and watermarking for copyright protection in deep learning.
Section III-C proposes mutual information minimization for generating class-wise unlearnable perturbations.
Table II reports semantic information protection and ownership verification results on ImageNet-100, Pets, and CIFAR10.
Section IV-B reports BER and PSNR for watermark extraction with and without perturbations.
Section IV-E compares unlearnable perturbation methods across ResNet18, VGG19, MobileNetV2, GoogLeNet, and Dense121.

arxiv:2608.06210.rationale: Pure robotics/embodied manipulation paper using a diffusion policy and CLIP-pretrained vision features, with no LLM, NLP, agent, or language methodology. In-domain evaluation includes real-robot trials and quantitative tables, but the topic is out-of-scope per rubric, capping the final score at 0.20.
evidence: Section IV-A introduces TP-DAMM for trajectory distribution estimation.
Section V-B Table I reports clustering metrics versus GMM, DAMM, and TP-GMM.
Section V-C Table II reports overall and phase-wise success rates across 20 rollouts per method.
Section V-D Table III and Figures 4-5 report tracking error, interaction forces, and mechanical work.
Section VI lists limitations such as predefined task reference frames and occluded contacts.

arxiv:2608.06447.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application for intrusion detection in IoT, with no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology. Only tangential relevance via knowledge distillation under Scaling & Efficiency. Method recombines known federated transfer learning, robust aggregation, and KD components; evaluation lacks direct baselines, ablations, exact per-scenario numeric tables, and sufficient hyperparameter/code availability.
evidence: Page 1 Abstract: claims 'accuracy of 99.18% and a recall of 99.99%'.
Page 4 Section IV-A: describes Google Colab CPU-only environment with Intel Xeon CPU and 13.61 GB RAM.
Page 6 Section IV-B: states 'values above 0.98 in most cases' and presents confusion matrices for Node 0 in Fig.3.

arxiv:2608.06208.rationale: Pure robotics/embodied tactile surface-coverage work using ergodic control and Gaussian Process Implicit Surfaces. It has domain-appropriate real-robot and simulation evidence, but it contains no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent-language methodology and is therefore out of scope for this preference set, capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract proposes online ergodic control with simultaneous unknown surface reconstruction via GPIS and tactile sensing.
Section 5.1 reports ergodic cost and Chamfer distance comparison against an uncertainty-gradient baseline on the Stanford bunny.
Table 1 summarizes Bunny, Chair, and Backpanel step counts, point cloud sizes, and start-to-end metric changes.
Section 6 lists limitations such as smooth-surface assumptions, fixed GPIS hyperparameters, thin-object point-cloud issues, and computational scaling.

arxiv:2608.06207.rationale: Exoplanet atmospheric retrieval study of TRAPPIST-1f using POSEIDON/PandExo and JWST simulations. It does not address LLMs, NLP, transformer architecture, reasoning, agents, or other listed AI/ML preferences, so it is out of scope for this curation. Methodological work within astronomy is present but irrelevant to the requested topics.
evidence: Abstract states the study evaluates atmospheric detectability of TRAPPIST-1f using atmospheric retrievals accounting for stellar contamination; no AI/LLM/NLP topics are addressed.
Section 2 describes POSEIDON Bayesian atmospheric retrieval and PandExo simulated JWST observations, confirming domain-specific exoplanet spectroscopy rather than requested AI/ML methodology.

arxiv:2608.06206.rationale: Conformal prediction theory with finite-sample guarantees; no direct match to core LLM/NLP/agents preferences, only weak Scientific AI/mathematics relevance. The work is mathematically rigorous with explicit assumptions, appendix proofs, and documented experiments, but its topic relevance is low for the stated preferences.
evidence: Section 3, Theorems 2 and 3: fixed-score uniform local length and coverage bounds are stated with explicit calibration and bandwidth terms.
Section 4, Theorems 6 and 7: learned-score oracle bounds separate calibration and score-estimation error.
Appendix M: reproducibility details include seed 20260710, package versions, and simulation conventions.
Section 5 and Appendix M: synthetic diagnostics report fitted slopes and acknowledge non-validation of constants.

arxiv:2608.06205.rationale: Pure computer vision/multispectral object detection with no LLM/NLP/language methodology; despite cross-attention, it falls outside core preferences and is capped at 0.20. The work is a modular combination of existing RepViT, GELAN, EMA/ELA, CBAM, DenseNet, and PGI components, with moderate ablations and reproducibility but single-run accuracy and limited VEDAI split evaluation.
evidence: {'s': 'Section 1', 'e': 'Paper targets RGB-T object detection using visible and infrared imagery, a pure computer vision task.'}
{'s': 'Section 3.2.2', 'e': 'Multi-head attention is applied within a CNN object-detection backbone, not language-model methodology.'}
{'s': 'Section 4.5', 'e': 'Ablation studies show the main gains combine existing RepViT, PGI, SE/MHA/MFE, MBatt, and cross-attention components.'}
{'s': 'Section 4.2', 'e': 'mAP accuracy is reported as single-run point estimates rather than repeated training runs.'}
{'s': 'Abstract', 'e': 'Code, data, and fine-tuned models are claimed available at a GitHub link, supporting reproducibility.'}

arxiv:2608.06202.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM safety and evaluation preferences; the API vs chat UI/search audit is moderately novel among prior benchmarking critiques. Methods include stratified sampling, mixed-effects models, and BH correction, but evidence is limited by one model family, two benchmarks, a single collection window, and very sparse abstention observations. Dataset link supports some reproducibility, though chat UI automation is difficult to replicate.
evidence: Section 3.1 Audit Design describes the 2x2 modality/search comparison with three runs per prompt.
Section 4.1 reports search reduced accuracy and reversed the SafetyBench modality gap.
Section 4.4 reports low source overlap, with only 4% URL overlap between modalities on both benchmarks.
Section 5.5 Limitations states results are based on one model family and a single collection period.
Datasets header links to GitHub repository.

arxiv:2608.06200.rationale: LLM-as-evaluator application to score written physics explanations; relevant to NLP/LLM evaluation and prompting but domain-specific and not a core language-modeling contribution. Human/LLM agreement is reported with kappas and effect sizes, but calibration sample is small, complex constructs (STP/Physics) have only moderate agreement, full LLM significance is underreported, and rubric/prompts/data are not fully provided.
evidence: Section III.3 reports LLM agreement against a 50-student subset: DP kappa=0.90/93%, MSP kappa=0.78/85%, CPP kappa=0.69/74%, Physics Correctness kappa=0.53/70%, STP kappa=0.48/67%.
Section III.2 reports human-coded paired t-tests for N=50: DP p<0.001 d=1.03, CPP p<0.001 d=0.52, STP p<0.001 d=0.45, Physics Correctness p=0.008 d=0.31, MSP p=1.000 d=0.00.
Section II.3.2 states GPT-5.4-mini API with temperature 0.2, image+prompt+response input, structured role/reasoning prompts, and three-run majority vote for full N=936 deployment.

arxiv:2608.06197.rationale: Core LLM agent/tool-use RL paper, strongly aligned with Agents & Tool Use, RL, and LLM preferences. World rehearsal is a meaningful but moderate advance over existing world-model and self-play approaches. Empirical coverage is broad across four benchmarks and model scales, but rigor is limited by no reported variance/error bars, one model family/dataset, and modest performance gaps. Code, prompts, and hyperparameters support reproducibility, though generalization beyond tool-interactive settings is untested.
evidence: Section 5.2, Table 1: EnvACE-8B Overall 32.91% vs EnvScaler-8B 31.92% and AWM-14B 32.54%.
Section 5.3: EnvACE improves tau2-Bench average from 31.2% to 36.7% over standard GRPO at 8B.
Section 5.5, Table 3: parallel EnvACE rehearsal with N=2 achieves Overall 40.9% vs Non-TTS 36.7%.
Section 7: limitation states evaluation only up to 8B and focused on tool-interactive tasks.

arxiv:2608.06196.rationale: Directly relevant to agentic tool/skill retrieval and RAG/knowledge-graph retrieval, with LLM-assisted edge generation and efficiency evaluation. The negative result and pre-filter topology bound are useful but incremental; rigor is moderate with matched-budget comparisons and statistical tests but small single-corpus evidence, single-judge audits, and explicit generalizability limits. Reproducibility is well documented.
evidence: Abstract: reports hybrid hit@5 73.5%±8.0 and graph deficit -11.2 points with p=0.0007.
Section 5.3: Table 2 shows adding 1421 typed edges leaves connectivity unchanged; 98.6% of typed pairs are also similar_to pairs.
Section 5.4: Table 3 matched-budget comparison hybrid@1+graph(6)=0.632 vs hybrid@6=0.744; 73% of missed queries unreachable; reranking p≈1.000.
Section 5.2: author-written queries inflate hit@5 by up to 44.2 points for keyword retrieval.
Section 6.5: threats include single corpus, single organisation, single embedding model, n=117 queries, audit n=48.
Reproducibility: repository praetorian-inc/palatine, tag skill-graph-paper-v2, commit 17223a95, with documented setup and no API call required for measurements.

arxiv:2608.06195.rationale: Paper extends probabilistic regression trees to handle missing covariates, a niche statistical-learning topic with essentially no overlap with the stated LLM/NLP/agent/transformer preferences. The extension is incremental but formally defined; empirical evaluation is moderate, comparing only to CART across five tabular datasets without imputation baselines or statistical testing. Reproducibility is relatively strong due to detailed configuration and R package availability.
evidence: Section 3.2 defines three fill_type strategies and their proxy functions
Section 5.5.1 reports relative predictive error and win rates vs CART
Table 1 summarizes datasets and missingness levels
Table 2 and Section 5.5.2 report computational cost

arxiv:2608.06192.rationale: Pure computer vision/video hand-object pressure estimation with no language-model methodology; out-of-scope cap applied. The work is reasonably novel in unifying heterogeneous pressure/contact supervision and includes quantitative tables, ablations, and robustness checks, but topic relevance to LLM/NLP preferences is minimal.
evidence: Abstract states HOPE predicts per-vertex normal pressure and contact on the hand mesh from monocular video.
Section 4.2 Table 1 reports vertex-level MAE 1.808 kPa and RMSE 4.998 kPa on OpenTouch.
Section 4.3 Table 4 shows adding HOI contact supervision improves ARCTIC frame F1 to 0.947 and vertex F1 to 0.498.
Section 4.3 Table 6 reports largest vertex-F1 drop of 0.013 under 20-degree per-joint pose noise.

arxiv:2608.06190.rationale: Out-of-scope applied mathematics/inverse problems paper on inferring ODE dynamics from marginal observations via Liouville equation characteristics. It does not address LLMs, NLP, transformers, reasoning, RAG, agents, safety, or other targeted language-model methods. Research quality is moderate within its domain, but final score is capped by out-of-scope relevance.
evidence: Abstract and Section 1 frame the method as ODE dynamics inference from marginal PDFs using the Liouville equation and stochastic gradient descent; no language modeling or NLP methods.
Section 3.2 Proposition 7 presents the unbiased crossed U-statistic gradient estimator; Section 4 Theorem 9 gives variance/convergence bounds.
Section 5 reports four synthetic numerical experiments (linear hidden modes, Gompertz growth, bistable latent dynamics, particle drag inference), not LLM/NLP benchmarks.

arxiv:2608.06188.rationale: This is an LLM-serving systems/sustainability paper: carbon-aware routing of vLLM/Llama-3.1-8B inference. It is not a language-modeling method paper, so relevance is limited to inference/serving and efficiency. Live feasibility is demonstrated, but magnitude claims derive from a perfect-foresight historical replay with synthetic workload and strong assumptions; release of code/data is restricted.
evidence: Abstract and §5.2 report ~1.96M request-turns, zero dispatch errors, and only 1.45% lower settled attributed emissions for eco-high vs off, without confidence intervals.
§6 and Table 3 describe the historical replay as perfect-foresight dispatch against historical MOER, with 50.9% reduction vs round-robin and conditional block-bootstrap CI 48.5–53.3%.
§6 shows zero-MOER handling materially changes results: the α-sweep gives 34–51%, while dropping zeros yields ~24.5% reduction.
§7 lists limitations including single model, synthetic load, shared-resource interference, and no prefix-cache modeling.
§6/Table 3 note MOER data are licensed and routing logic is patent-pending and not released.

arxiv:2608.06184.rationale: Pure event-camera reflection removal / low-level computer vision paper; no LLM/NLP/language methodology and thus subject to the 0.20 out-of-scope cap. Within its niche it contributes a first event-driven benchmark and has ablations, but relevance to requested preferences is minimal.
evidence: Abstract: claims >1.6 dB and >1.2 dB PSNR gains and code/dataset availability.
Table 1: SIR2 average PSNR 29.09 for EvReflection vs 27.46 for DAI.
Table 2: EVR2 real benchmark average PSNR 27.25 vs 25.97 for RDNet.
Section 4.4: Ablation studies Table 3 investigate event modality, dynamics cues, and fusion strategy.
Limitation: notes failure in static scenes, low-light noise, and computational overhead.

arxiv:2608.06183.rationale: Domain-specific LLM application to microarchitecture DSE, not core LLM/NLP methodology; under the rubric this is treated as an out-of-scope pure-domain application, so relevance is low and the overall score is capped. The paper combines known MCTS and evolutionary ideas and reports self-contained but untrusted quantitative claims, with no limitations section or statistical significance testing and limited prompt/LLM disclosure.
evidence: Abstract: reports up to 36.2% HV improvement over NSGA-II and 10.6x search efficiency.
Section 4.1: describes GEM5/McPAT setup, five independent trials, HV/ADRS metrics, and evaluation budgets; Table 1 reports comparative results.
Section 4.3: ablation study reports performance degradation after removing AKA/SAD, tuner, explorer, Pareto analysis, pairwise analysis, utility, and directive components.
Section 4.4: reports scaling to XiangShan Kunminghu and claims 8.6% geometric mean energy efficiency over the manual design.
Document has no separate Limitations section; statistical significance tests are not described.

arxiv:2608.06182.rationale: Out-of-scope pure optimization/mathematics paper on stochastic extragradient for monotone variational inequalities; no LLM, NLP, agent, reasoning, or multimodal language methodology. The results are substantial within its domain but irrelevant to the curator's focus.
evidence: Abstract: 'We study stochastic extragradient (SEG) methods for solving monotone variational inequality problems (VIPs)'
Section 1.3 Summary of main contributions: states restricted-gap theory, almost-sure last-iterate convergence for S-SEG, and DSEG separation from I-SEG
Theorem 4.2: constructs stochastic VIP where S-SEG diverges almost surely under DSEG step-sizes

arxiv:2608.06179.rationale: Highly relevant LLM alignment/preference optimization paper using parser-derived rewards. Novelty is moderate/incremental; rigor is limited by inconsistent sample-size and human-eval reporting, use of the same parser family for DA/NB, and disclosed selection bias, though ablations and independent checks exist.
evidence: Section 5.2 and Table 5 report Icelandic Stanza PSR improvement (75.8 to 80.3 best run; 79.1 three-run mean) and 80% native-speaker preference (n=43 pairs; 129 judgment-level counts).
Table 2 legend notes pass 2 Stanza PSR uses n=200 while pass 1 uses n=400, weakening the pass-to-pass degradation comparison.
Section 6 and Table 6 show ablations: removing MATTR or using binary 0/1 parser labels triggers reward-hacking flags (oracle/Stanza gap >0.20, MATTR drop).
Limitations discloses model selection on same held-out prompts, small human evaluation, DA/NB reliance on the same parser family, and factual recall drop on nqii from 24.5% to 14.3%.

arxiv:2608.06177.rationale: Low relevance: the paper targets efficiency/early stopping for binary-activation CNNs, aligning only weakly with Scaling & Efficiency/Inference preferences and lacking language/NLP/agent methodology. Contribution is incremental over prior ReLU early-termination work, with moderate experimental rigor but limited to VGG11/CIFAR-10 and idealized arithmetic savings.
evidence: Section 6.1 reports 86.58% local reduction and 0.37pp drop for F7 percent_4
Section 6.4 reports natural ordering reduces local reduction by 22-36pp
Section 7.3 states savings are idealized and no hardware latency is modeled

arxiv:2608.06174.rationale: Pure computer-vision analysis of frozen vision encoders (DINOv3/SigLIP2) with no language-model or NLP methodology; out-of-scope hard cap applies. The paper has controlled baselines, ablations, and limitations, but minimal relevance to the stated LLM/NLP-focused preferences.
evidence: Abstract: reports DINOv3 known factorial assignment 0.874 on Shapes3D-Extended and 0.799 on COCO.
Experiments/Table 1: MuJoCo learned assignment is 0.569 with DINOv3 and 0.484 with SigLIP2, with collapse rates 43.3% and 51.1%.
Limitations: states no identifiability claim and that the MuJoCo boundary is not isolated to intervention geometry, representation, or interaction.

arxiv:2608.06171.rationale: Relevant to LLM-based web agents and agent routing under Agents & Tool Use, but not a core LLM methodology paper and has no Japanese NLP component. Methodologically strong with rerun controls, noise-floor thresholds, and multiplicity notes; novelty is moderate as a careful negative result rather than a new method. Evidence is strong within its benchmarks but limited by small success rates, few replicates, imported noise bands, and offline cascade estimates. Generalizability is narrow across two VisualWebArena/WebArena task sets and specific Qwen/Gemma backbones.
evidence: Section 4: rerunning one condition changes 12.1-14.3% of task outcomes, with resolution threshold 3.8-4.2pp.
Section 5: cost ceiling at matched success cuts cost 9.5-30.6% in 8 of 8 cells, while six-arm union headroom is mostly rerun variance.
Section 6: five routing policies fail to robustly beat fixed single-mode policies.
Section 7: label supply and routing opportunity correlate at 0.95 across cells, tying the negative result to low agent success rates.

arxiv:2608.06170.rationale: Moderately relevant through its use of an LLM-generated prior graph and CLIP-based vision-language features, but the core contribution is robotic 3D scene graph region segmentation rather than LLM/NLP methodology. The paper shows reasonable rigor with multiple datasets, baselines, ablations, and quantitative metrics, though open-vocabulary claims are constrained by fixing region classes to ground truth in benchmarks, and reproducibility is limited by internal data and no code release.
evidence: Section VII-E (Table I) reports semantic and geometric segmentation metrics across HM3D, TartanGround, CODa, and Train Station datasets.
Section VII-F (Table II) reports expert toggle ablation results.
Section VII-B2 states the region set is fixed to ground-truth classes for all quantitative benchmarks.
Section VIII notes limitations including global graph cut optimization and single abstraction layer inference.

arxiv:2608.06167.rationale: Relevant LLM/NLP information extraction application with schema-based prompting and LLM-as-judge semantic evaluation. Novelty is incremental over existing structured-output, constrained decoding, and recursive schema extraction. Rigor is limited by single-expert gold standard, small development set, sparse baseline/statistical detail, and figure-only transferability metrics. Evidence includes quantitative F1 on NICE and cross-model/organization checks, but many comparisons lack full numerical detail. Reproducibility is partly supported by promised GitHub artifacts but limited by proprietary model deprecation.
evidence: Section V: zero-shot, single-call schema-based extraction using Claude Opus 3.
Section V-C1: path-based semantic matching with exact/semantic/useful/non-match rubric.
Section VI-A: reports 12/14 attributes >90% F1; outcome_rea F1 0.88; clinical_restrictions F1 0.83.
Section VI-C: extraction ~0.5 min/doc vs ~15 min human, ~30x time efficiency.
Section VI-E/F: generalizability across four models and transferability to ZIN/HAS shown in figures.
Section VII: acknowledges single-expert gold standard and need for inter-rater reliability.

arxiv:2608.06166.rationale: Direct out-of-the-box LLM evaluation on Italian legal professional exams, relevant to LLM/evaluation/reasoning but not to Japanese, architecture, or agent topics. Blind expert evaluation with official grids is a strength, but design has small sample (1 human paper, 4 models, 3 evaluators), no repeated sampling or quantified inter-rater reliability, and findings are jurisdiction/task-specific. Evidence is partly quantitative but limited by missing detailed per-criterion table data.
evidence: Abstract: blind Turing Test on Italian Bar, Judges and Notary exams using out-of-the-box LLMs.
Section IV: four LLMs (Claude 4 Opus, GPT-5, DeepSeek R1, Gemini 2.5 Pro), minimal prompts, OCR human papers, three expert evaluators.
Section VI.1: Bar exam Gemini 2.5 Pro scored 79 vs human 62; ChatGPT-5 65; DeepSeek R1 underperformed.
Section VI.2: Judicial exam Gemini 2.5 Pro 21/24 vs human 18/24; ChatGPT-5 10.
Section VI.3: all LLMs failed notary exam; inter vivos best Gemini total 10 vs human 42; mortis causa best GPT-5 total 20 vs human 42.
Section X Limitations: Italian legal context, small evaluator pool, internet access asymmetry, out-of-box/no RAG.

arxiv:2608.06165.rationale: Pure audio/music transcription work using a Transformer decoder and pre-trained audio features, but no language-model methodology; out of scope and capped near 0.20. The paper has ablations, quantitative SER results, limitation discussion, and dataset/code availability, but domain generalizability is narrow.
evidence: Abstract: reports 4.98% SER on Quartets and 20.92% SER on SheetSage-A2S
Table 2: ablation shows Quartets SER improving from 15.3 baseline to 4.98 and SheetSage-A2S SER from 66.85 to 20.92
Section 3.2: describes pitch-shifting and time-stretching data augmentation
Section 6.1: discusses user-annotation variabilities as limitations
Section 2.4: reports dataset statistics of 9,468 clips and 61 hours

arxiv:2608.06164.rationale: Out-of-scope differentiable physics/3D reconstruction paper; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, or language methodology. It is a domain-specific bending-aware extension over PhysTwin with quantitative ablations, but under the stable rubric it is a pure computer vision/physics application and must be capped at 0.20 overall.
evidence: Abstract: video-based physical reconstruction and deformable-object dynamics, no language methods
Section 3.1: PhysTwin benchmark non-cloth sequences; primary baseline PhysTwin
Table 1: quantitative reconstruction and future-prediction metrics
Table 2: downsampling ablation at ratios 0.05 and 0.1
Table 3: interior-node removal ablation
Section 5: conclusion, no explicit limitations section

arxiv:2608.06163.rationale: Astroparticle neutrino telescope analysis; uses a Boosted Decision Tree for event selection, but no LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent/evaluation methodology. Domain-specific physics application and out of scope.
evidence: Abstract: reports all-sky and Galactic Ridge diffuse neutrino emission search using KM3NeT/ARCA data.
Section 3.2: describes Boosted Decision Tree classifier for background rejection.

arxiv:2608.06161.rationale: Partially relevant: the LLM-agent reward synthesis and diffusion RL align with agent/RL preferences, but the core task is 3D scene generation/CV rather than language modeling. The combination of Eureka-style reward reflection with DDPO is somewhat novel but incremental. Quantitative experiments include baselines and an ablation, but task-specific compliance is not directly measured, some results are mixed or worse than filtered subsets, FID worsens, and hyperparameter conflicts (1e-5 vs 3e-4) weaken rigor and reproducibility. No code release and only bedroom/3D-FRONT evaluation limit generality.
evidence: Section 4.1 Experimental Setup states RL learning rate 1e-5, while Appendix B Training Configuration states 3e-4.
Table 1 shows iARCS FID 1.60 versus MiDiffusion 1.34, with improved collision/walkability but no significance tests.
Section 4.4 Table 3 reports generic physical/diversity metrics but not direct task-constraint satisfaction, and several task metrics are worse than constraint-satisfying 3D-FRONT subsets.
Section 4.6 Limitations mentions only LLM reward ambiguity and compute cost, not conflicting hyperparameters or lack of task-specific metrics.

arxiv:2608.06158.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging study of photon-counting CT for coronary stenosis quantification. No LLM, NLP, reasoning, agents, or other in-scope methodology. Quantitative phantom results do not align with rubric preferences.
evidence: Page 1: title and abstract describe a coronary CT phantom study for stenosis quantification, not language models or in-scope AI methodology.

arxiv:2608.06155.rationale: Out-of-scope for the stated LLM/NLP/agent-centric rubric: a theoretical kernel methods paper on conditional expectation operators, CMEs, and Koopman operators, with no language-model, reasoning, or prompting methodology. The mathematical development is rigorous, but the final score is capped at 0.20 due to out-of-scope domain application.
evidence: Section 3.1, Proposition 3.1: proves eta in L^2(nu_Y;H) implies T_eta is Hilbert-Schmidt.
Section 4.1, Theorem 4.2: verifies density regularity for nonparametric regression.
Appendix A.1: contains proofs for Section 4.1 results.

arxiv:2608.06154.rationale: In-scope multimodal VLM evaluation with moderate preference relevance via Multimodal AI and Red Teaming & Evaluation. The blind-input/noise-floor/symmetry battery is a useful methodological contribution, and statistical controls (bootstrap CIs, permutation, Holm correction, replication) are relatively strong. However, findings are tied to simulated control environments and specific model snapshots, with narrow directional-action evidence and one exploratory MPC arm lacking a digest; generalizability is limited.
evidence: Abstract states the study analyzes 32,874 scored calls over two embodiments and three simulation environments using blind-image controls, reflection, and non-visual baselines.
Section V-B/Table IV reports the symmetry-consensus guardian achieves 0.956 accuracy and 0.954 balanced accuracy on a 272-frame held-out set, with bootstrap 95% CI [0.895,0.990].
Section V-C/Table V reports VLM intent source reaches 8/25 goals versus 23/25 for MPC-only/oracle, and mirrored/blank controls show grounding failure.
Code Availability states all code, data, and artifacts are publicly available at a GitHub repository.

arxiv:2608.06153.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, and code/software engineering. The globalized skill evolution framework adds incremental novelty via Skill Relation Graph and cluster-based consolidation. However, research quality is limited by modest-scale evaluation, single-point estimates without significance testing, internal inconsistency in reported improvement ranges, and closed data/code with insufficient implementation detail.
evidence: Abstract and Section 5.1.2/Table 1: the 6.1% precision gain is computed against Human Skills (0.33 to 0.35), while the abstract groups it under existing evolution techniques, conflating baseline comparisons.
Tables 1-3 report only point estimates with no standard deviations, confidence intervals, or significance tests across Sections 5.1-5.3.
Section 4.1.2 and Section 4.5: IndustrialBugs is proprietary and no code/data release, prompts, or clustering thresholds are provided, weakening reproducibility.
Section 7 describes a one-project-held-out protocol but does not report per-project variance or exact run counts.

arxiv:2608.06151.rationale: Well-conducted RCT evidence on using LLM dialogues to reduce unfolding conspiracy beliefs, with preregistration for Study 2, controls, follow-ups, and validated strategy coding. Relevance is moderate: it centrally uses LLMs for persuasion/misinformation and touches AI safety, but it is a social-science application rather than an LLM methodology contribution. Effect sizes are modest and generalizability is limited to two US crisis events, though reproducibility is strong with code/data availability.
evidence: Results, Main effects: reports Trump b=-6.95, p<.001, d=.38 and Kirk b=-7.56, p<.001, d=.38 for the debunking dialogue.
Materials and Methods, Study 2 design: states the experiment was preregistered (AsPredicted #247,423).
Materials and Methods, Strategy identification analysis: reports 91.75% overall agreement and kappa=.62 between LLM and human coders.
Discussion: acknowledges the research focuses on two specific unfolding events and should be considered case studies.
Data and Code Availability: states code and data are available at https://osf.io/dmu9k.
