arxiv:2608.06150.rationale: Domain-specific remote sensing open-vocabulary change detection using CLIP/SAM3 and text prompts, but not core LLM/NLP/reasoning/agent work; effectively a pure domain/CV application, so relevance is very low. The perception-memory-verification formulation has moderate novelty, and the paper provides extensive ablations and sensitivity analysis, but claims rest on self-reported baselines, some margins are tiny, no statistical testing is shown, and generalization is only within remote sensing. Reproducibility is supported by detailed hyperparameters and architecture descriptions, though the code link is unverified.
evidence: Abstract: proposes CogVis for open-vocabulary change detection in remote sensing with SCP, SMC, and ARF modules.
Experimental Settings: evaluates on seven remote sensing benchmarks and describes implementation using frozen SAM3 and CLIP ViT-B/16.
Table 1: reports state-of-the-art results across seven benchmarks, with some gains as small as 0.05 points.
Table 2 and Table 5: provide component ablation and hyperparameter sensitivity results.
Appendix C: provides extended class-wise and mechanism evidence, including threshold calibration and ARF evidence ablation.

arxiv:2608.06146.rationale: Multimodal document-parsing MLLM with layout-grounded parallel decoding; relevant to multimodal AI, transformer attention, and inference/serving, but not core LLM/reasoning. Strong controlled comparisons and ablations support the efficiency/quality claims, though generalizability is limited to document-parsing structured generation.
evidence: Abstract reports Overall layout F1 91.1, Overall 94.24, and fastest end-to-end parser at five concurrency levels.
Table 1 reports layout analysis on OmniDocBench with countable/acceptable PageIoU.
Table 2 reports end-to-end parsing quality on OmniDocBench v1.6 Full.
Table 3 reports single-A800 throughput and P95 latency, including same-backbone Sequential SFT baseline.
Training Paradigm describes ancestor attention and packed tree-varlen realization.
Table 8 ablates dense SDPA vs Flex Attention vs tree-varlen training backends.

arxiv:2608.06144.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, agentic workflows, and evaluation. Novelty is moderate: the paper contributes a longitudinal self-evolution benchmark with paired non-evolving controls, but not a new model or method. Rigor is moderate: it includes ablations, three shuffled runs, and expert validation, but lacks significance testing and uses only one backbone. Evidence is reasonably detailed with tables and appendices, though source cases are not independently verifiable. Generalizability is limited to professional financial workflows and one backbone; reproducibility is limited by no clear dataset/code release claim.
evidence: Abstract: reports 120 real-case-grounded tasks, 20 business scenes, four scaffolds, and paired non-evolving controls.
Section 4.2: reports ICC(A,1)=0.95 (95% CI: [0.93,0.97]) for automated rubric judging against a financial expert.
Table 3: reports evolved scores, paired gains, compliance reductions, and agent-side cost across four scaffolds.
Section 4.4: reports memory/skill carrier ablations and rubric-feedback vs reference-answer comparisons.
Section 5: states limitations including one backbone, 20 scenes, non-parametric evolution only, and a five-scene cross-scene diagnostic.

arxiv:2608.06142.rationale: Out of scope: pure computer vision/computational aesthetics for artwork and photograph composition, with no language methodology. Object-centric learning + GAT is compared against fine-tuned DINOv2 for composition classification, retrieval, and saliency. LLMs are only briefly mentioned as a future annotation-generation source, so personal relevance is minimal and the paper is capped at 0.20 despite moderate CV experimental rigor.
evidence: Abstract: 'Learning visual representations for compositional analysis of artworks and photographs' and compares object-centric models with fine-tuned foundation models.
Section 4.1: Primary datasets are PICD (49k images over 24 composition categories) and APDDv2 (10k painting images).
Section 5: 'current LLMs are trained on internet-scale data... promising source for generating such annotations automatically' is the only language-model-related mention, framed as future work.

arxiv:2608.06141.rationale: Position/framework paper on ASR linguistic bias and decolonial speech AI; falls in the pure speech/audio domain and lacks LLM/language-model methodology. It presents no quantitative results, baselines, ablations, or empirical validation. Contributions are conceptual (3M taxonomy, situatedness model, participatory audit), with citation-based evidence rather than experimental findings.
evidence: Abstract: states contribution as human-centered evaluation framework and no new ASR architecture or benchmark result.
Section 5.4: proposes minimum 3M audit protocol with documented steps but no empirical results.
Section 8: acknowledges framework is broad and empirical validation is future work.
Section 4.2: discusses WER and TER metrics via citations, not new measurements.

arxiv:2608.06137.rationale: Partially relevant through agent-like skill evolution and LLM-based optimizer proposers, but the core contribution is tabular foundation model adaptation rather than language modeling or NLP. The method is a somewhat novel combination of evidence-gated repair and validation-gated skill updates, yet evaluation is mostly synthetic, lacks nontrivial adaptation baselines, and the real-world electricity forecasting result is narrow and not independently reproducible.
evidence: Abstract claims AUC improvements of 0.128-0.142 and zero observed harm on boundary settings.
Table 1 reports controlled boundary benchmark AUC improvements and fallback rates.
Table 2 ablates evidence-conditioned retrieval, runtime certificate, and skill evolution.
Table 4 reports held-out electricity forecasting MAE reduction from 53.02 to 25.16 across 288 points; raw market data are not released.
Appendix B provides pseudocode, and compute environment is an Apple M4 Max CPU, but no code or data release is stated.

arxiv:2608.06135.rationale: In-scope LLM inference/serving systems work. The online EMA/Savitzky-Golay threshold adaptation for WAIT is a lightweight incremental extension, evaluated only via synthetic MMPP-2 simulation without real workload traces. Rigor is limited by largely narrative figures and no numeric tables or uncertainty quantification, though methodology and hyperparameter tuning are described. Reproducibility is moderate due to a code link and algorithm details.
evidence: Abstract: 'simulation-based evaluation demonstrating that the proposed method achieves higher throughput than Sarathi-Serve, ORCA, and vLLM in the evaluated low arrival-rate shift scenarios while maintaining comparable latency.'
Section V.2.1: reports optimal preprocessing parameters with average MAE 15.39 and MAPE 14.37%.
Section VI: 'In terms of latency, our algorithm exhibits performance on par with WAIT under high-shift scenarios, outperforming other algorithms.'
Section VI: 'While latency remains suboptimal across all settings for both versions of WAIT, performance improves significantly in the Low Shift regime.'

arxiv:2608.06132.rationale: Out-of-scope HCI/VR perceptuomotor study with no LLM/NLP/transformer/reasoning/agent/multimodal AI methodology. The paper is methodologically careful for its domain, but relevance to the specified preferences is essentially nil, so the score is capped at the out-of-scope maximum.
evidence: Abstract: reports a same-headset comparison of visually guided manual pointing in VR and MR-VPT with UR pre/post phases.
Section 3.2 XR Phase: reports opposite initial endpoint biases, different adaptation rates, and distance-dependent endpoint error.
Section 4.1 Limitations and Future Directions: acknowledges bundled modality-level factors and inability to isolate individual causes.

arxiv:2608.06130.rationale: Directly relevant to AI agents/tool use, MCP, and AI safety/prompt-injection evaluation. The work integrates established hardware keystore and zero-trust primitives rather than introducing fundamentally new methods. Evaluation reports strong protected-vs-baseline ASR reduction but is limited by small per-model/benign samples, reliance on SoftHSM emulation for primary security claims, and deterministic blocking by construction.
evidence: Section V-B Table II reports combined baseline ASR 19.3% and protected ASR 0% (n=192).
Section V-B Table III reports benign TSR 100% with n=4 only.
Section VII Discussion acknowledges SoftHSMv2 is a reproducibility proxy and the RAV-only ablation uses n=10 with CI upper bound 27.8%.
Section IV Implementation states primary evaluation uses SoftHSMv2 and TPM2 validation only for integration.

arxiv:2608.06128.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM search agents, RAG, reasoning, and RL. EALR masking is a moderate novelty. Rigor is reasonable but lacks statistical significance/error bars and limitations. Evidence supports claims via ablations and benchmark comparisons, though generalization is primarily QA search agents with two Qwen scales.
evidence: Table 1 reports seven benchmark F1 results for 3B/7B models.
Section 4.3 ablates outcome and EALR rewards.
Appendix C documents hyperparameters and prompt template.
Section 4.5 reports RL algorithm comparisons.

arxiv:2608.06126.rationale: Out-of-scope medical imaging/radiography application using CNNs and synthetic depth/radiograph generation. It has quantitative ablations and statistical significance tests, but no LLM, language, reasoning, agent, or multimodal language methodology, so the score is capped at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract: framework generates synthetic training data from CT scans and claims pretraining improves pose assessment by up to 11 percentage points.
Section 4.1: synthetic dataset generated from 10 CTs in 3077 poses, resulting in 30770 depth images.
Section 5.3: uses two EfficientNet-B0 models with MSE regression, Adam optimizer, and 200,000 training steps.
Section 6.1: reports one-sided paired permutation tests with p=0.0049 and p=0.0020 for MAE improvements.

arxiv:2608.06125.rationale: Image/video diffusion post-training without language methodology; out of scope per instructions and capped at 0.20. The sample-adaptive latent reward uncertainty idea has moderate novelty, but the evaluation lacks main error bars, implementation details are largely relegated to supplementary material, and there is no code release, limiting reproducibility and independent verification.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 1: SURE-LRM achieves mean pairwise accuracy 73.54 on SD3.5-Medium versus DiNa-LRM 71.49.
Section 4.3, Table 4: SURE-REFL ranks first in eight of nine backbone-metric comparisons and improves HPSv2.1 on every image backbone.
Section 4.4, Table 5: SURE-REFL achieves highest VBench quality, semantic, and total scores, with total increasing from 0.8092 to 0.8357.
Table 6: Full reward-model objective averages 73.54; removing the variance regularizer drops it to 68.72.

arxiv:2608.06124.rationale: Out-of-scope for the curated AI/ML preferences: the paper presents a microarchitectural CPU instruction (dfence), hardware-software Spectre defense, and a Jasmin type system. It contains no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agent, RAG, or multimodal language methodology. Although it includes formal proofs, a RISC-V Proteus implementation, and security/performance evaluation, domain relevance is near zero, so the score is capped at the out-of-scope level.
evidence: Abstract: introduces dfence, a CPU instruction to mitigate Spectre-PHT and Spectre-STL
Section 5: describes hardware implementation in the Proteus RISC-V CPU
Section 6.1: presents security evaluation using generated secure and insecure programs
Appendix C: contains formal soundness proof for the type system

arxiv:2608.06123.rationale: Directly relevant to LLM bias/safety evaluation, sycophancy, and LLM-as-judge benchmarking. The counterfactual country-swap framework with five bias dimensions and fictional-pair controls is moderately novel, but rigor is limited by reliance on a single LLM judge, lack of statistical significance testing, reported direction disagreement in human validation, small human study, and data available only upon acceptance.
evidence: Section 3.1.2 defines five bias dimensions and the Political Bias Index (PBI).
Section 5.1.1 reports PBI scores across 13 models, e.g., Grok-4.5 3.36, GPT-OSS-120B 3.30, Qwen3-32B 5.75.
Section 4.3 states Claude 4.5 Opus is used as judge, and Appendix G reports anonymized evaluation correlation r=0.945.
Appendix F reports 80.6% human-judge agreement, with 29% of disagreements attributed to incorrect direction, and notes direction-level analyses were excluded from main results.
Limitations notes the study is limited to English, single-turn interactions, and the paper states Poli-Bias will be open-sourced upon acceptance.

arxiv:2608.06122.rationale: Out-of-scope medical time-series classification paper with transformer encoders and self-pretraining, but no language/LLM/NLP methodology. Experimental comparisons and masking ablations are present, though novelty and reproducibility are limited.
evidence: Title and Abstract: evaluates self-pretraining for transformer-based models on medical time-series classification tasks (Camargo, Non-EEG Stress, Gait Parkinson's).
Section II, Table II: datasets are medical/biomechanical/physiological time-series collections; no language or NLP component.
Section III-B: describes four masking strategies (point-wise, column, block, mixed) for SPT.
Section V-B, Tables IV-V: report quantitative accuracy, F1, recall, and specificity for from-scratch vs SPT variants across datasets and depths.
Section IV: training used NVIDIA A100, but reports 10 scratch epochs vs 100 SPT + 15 fine-tuning epochs; no code/availability statement is provided.

arxiv:2608.11255.rationale: Pure domain application of symbolic regression to chemical-engineering VLE prediction. Despite tangential Scientific AI/interpretability relevance, there is no LLM/NLP/agent/transformer methodology, so the paper is out-of-scope and capped at or below 0.20. Research quality is moderate: quantitative comparisons with PR-EOS and pooled SR exist, but evaluation uses a single 80/20 split without system-wise holdout, uncertainty quantification, or ablations, and generalization is limited to six N2/n-alkane systems.
evidence: Table 4 reports pressure prediction metrics for Two-level SR, SR, and PR-EOS with train/test split.
Table 1 shows only six N2 + n-alkane binary systems totaling 660 data points.
Appendix A and Appendix B provide explicit basis constants and system-specific coefficients.

arxiv:2608.06117.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/3D reconstruction paper on 3D Gaussian splatting with multi-view geometric priors. It does not address LLMs, NLP, reasoning, agents, safety, or language methodology. Evaluation is competent within its domain (DTU/TnT/Shiny Blender, ablations), but relevance to the stated preferences is minimal.
evidence: Abstract: '3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS)... novel view synthesis... integration of geometric priors'
Section 1: '3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has recently emerged...' focused on geometric reconstruction
Section 4.1: datasets are DTU, Shiny Blender, and Tanks and Temples, not language/NLP benchmarks

arxiv:2608.06115.rationale: LLM-based human simulation using per-cluster LoRA fine-tuning, bias mitigation, and survey evaluation. Relevant to LLM/training/evaluation preferences but is a domain-specific social-simulation application rather than core language-model methodology. Novelty is an incremental integration of authorship embeddings, clustering, QLoRA, and chain-of-emotion. Rigor is limited by proprietary/customer data, uncontrolled cross-dataset comparisons, missing dataset and hyperparameter details, and no statistical significance testing. Evidence is quantitative but not fully comparable or reproducible. Generalizability is intentionally narrow, and no code/data are released.
evidence: §3.3: A separate high-rank LoRA adapter is trained for each cluster on a Gemma 4 12B base using QLoRA.
§3.2: Training balances positive/negative framing and shuffles response options to reduce sycophancy/prompt brittleness.
§4.2: Reports median ordinal alignment 0.775 and median top-1 accuracy 0.679 on a mined survey set.
§4.1: Reports residual signed error mean +0.437 and per-cluster standard deviation median near 1.85.
§5: Acknowledges bias and variance remain and aggregate population-level fidelity is not yet shown.

arxiv:2608.06113.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, code agents, and planning. Novelty is moderate: it extends existing CLI API interception and trajectory collection, but the explicit-vs-implicit planning decomposition and cross-scaffold SFT transfer are useful. Rigor is adequate but limited by one executor model, one benchmark, and no significance testing. Evidence is quantitative and section-anchored. Generalizability is bounded to SWE-bench Verified and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct. Reproducibility is strong with code, models, data, and logs released.
evidence: Section 4 Table 4 reports Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct Pass@1: 42.8% baseline, 48.2% self-plan, 57.8% Claude Sonnet 4.5 external plan on SWE-bench Verified.
Section 5 Table 5 reports PlanOnly no-plan 53.8% with no self-plan benefit, while Plan+Exec reaches 52.8% no-plan and 55.8% self-plan.
Section 6 Table 6 reports Plan+Exec SFT self-plan gains over base no-plan on OpenCode (49.4% vs 46.0%) and mini-swe-agent (42.4% vs 35.4%).
Section 9 acknowledges external validity limits to SWE-bench Verified and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, and does not test Codex CLI or Gemini CLI.

arxiv:2608.06112.rationale: Paper is a healthcare-specific agentic AI platform architecture and business case, not a language-model methodology contribution; prototype uses gradient boosting and lightweight Python classes rather than LLMs, placing it at the domain-application boundary despite agent/compliance terminology. Methodology is descriptive, relies on synthetic data and unverified 18-month pilot/ROI projections, and lacks code/data or formal evaluation.
evidence: Abstract describes synthetic dataset and prototype architecture but no experimental LLM contribution.
IV. METHODS: triage model is Gradient Boosting; agents are implemented as lightweight Python classes.
V. RESULTS: ROC-AUC 0.892 and workflow savings are reported on synthetic data with no external validation; ROI is projected.
DISCLAIMER: compliance coverage is design-time policy alignment and does not substitute for regulatory approval.

arxiv:2608.06111.rationale: Core transformer/NLP language-model work with systematic syntax-informed positional embedding ablations across PE families. Relevance is strong through transformer architecture, NLP, and pretraining/fine-tuning topics, though not LLM-scale or agent/reasoning. Evidence tables support the main claims, but several encoder GLUE gains are small relative to reported std and no significance tests are shown; limitations disclose English-only, small models, and KV-cache incompatibility.
evidence: Abstract and §4.2 report SyntaxGym +10.3% relative, perplexity -9.0% relative, and GLUE +8.2% relative for Transformer-XL positional-pathway SiPE.
Table 2 compares decoder baselines and SiPE variants, showing PP-SiPE SyntaxGym 80.60 vs 73.09 for the vanilla Transformer-XL baseline.
Table 4 reports GLUE macro averages with std over 3 seeds; encoder gains are modest (RoBERTa 72.30->72.84, DeBERTa 69.69->70.10, ModernBERT 68.63->69.32).
Limitations states scope is English-only, small models, limited pretraining budgets, and that efficient incremental decoding with KV-cache is unresolved.

arxiv:2608.06110.rationale: Highly relevant to agentic LLMs, tool use, safety guardrails, RAG/memory, and multimodal NLP, though partly a healthcare/audio system application. System-level integration is incremental and evaluated on relatively small scenario/test sets without statistical testing; quantitative tables and ablations provide moderate evidence, but privacy, cost, and local-deployment claims are not strongly validated. Reproducibility is limited by absent code/data availability.
evidence: Abstract and §III state the agentic chatbot uses a ReAct loop via LangGraph with 17 clinical tools and a temporal knowledge graph for cross-session memory.
§IV Table I reports GPT-5 Mini tool-execution pass rate 94.92% and argument F1 0.977 on a 59-scenario benchmark.
§IV-A Table III reports signed GNN safety classifier accuracy 0.888 and unsafe recall 0.906, outperforming Llama 3.3 70B on balanced accuracy.
§IV-B Table IV reports mean macro F1 0.652 for the multimodal speech assessment versus 0.607 for the Whisper-only baseline.
§V lists limitations including rare symptom presentations and limited depression detection data.

arxiv:2608.06108.rationale: Relevant to LLM agents, reasoning, and benchmark evaluation, but the paper is a financial-domain benchmark with weak methodological detail and internal inconsistencies. Scoring is not credible: Section 4.0.1's formula is not reconcilable with Table 2's Overall Scores, and Section 4.1's 26.9% vs 25.7% gap claims conflict. Proprietary SIL Engine and unvalidated LLM judge reduce rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: Section 4.0.2 Table 2: DeepSeek-V3 Event Coherence 2.8 and Logical Plausibility 4.1 average to 3.45, yet Overall Score 7.8 cannot be recovered from the Section 4.0.1 scoring formula if outcome is perfect as claimed.
Section 4.1: Figure 4 caption states a 26.9% LLM performance gap while the body text states a 25.7% gap.
Section 3.1: benchmark construction relies on a proprietary Stock Investment Logic (SIL) Engine and an automated high-capacity judge LLM without reported validation or inter-judge reliability.

arxiv:2608.06107.rationale: PDE/physics foundation-model emulation is outside the core LLM/NLP scope; although it uses transformer fine-tuning and generative modeling, it is a pure domain application, so the overall score is capped at 0.20. The work has reasonable ablations and quantitative comparisons but minimal relevance to language-model research priorities.
evidence: Section 3.6 describes evaluation on 10 2D datasets from The Well with M=8, T=32, and two initial contexts per trajectory.
Section 4.2 reports MPR improves FGN and diffusion baselines across representative datasets (Figure 7).
Appendix C.11 Tables 1-2 provide per-variable fCRPS and Ensemble Mean RMSE comparisons against the Walrus baseline.
Section 5 Limitations acknowledges remaining calibration and divergence issues.

arxiv:2608.06105.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application of inverse RL to Arctic shipping; no LLM/NLP/agent/transformer methodology. It overlaps only weakly with preferences via RL/reward robustness, but the controlled evaluation is not aligned with the requested LLM/NLP focus, so it is capped at 0.20 per out-of-scope policy. Internal methodology is reasonably rigorous with controlled comparisons, ablations, and artifacts.
evidence: Abstract
Results
Limitations
Appendix C
Appendix F

arxiv:2608.06091.rationale: Out-of-scope HCI/e-commerce user study of a rule-based product advisor; no LLM, Japanese NLP, transformer, reasoning, or agentic methodology. Despite moderate experimental control and OSF materials, domain-application cap applies; subjective self-report measures and single domain limit strength.
evidence: Abstract: chatbot-assisted laptop search scenario, conditions T/TC/TE/TCE.
Section 3.1: Cleo implemented as rule-based system with predefined interaction flow.
Section 7: limitation notes rule-based advisor and scripted prompts reducing ecological validity.
Section 5.1.1: novices rated TCE more appropriate than T and TC; experts showed no significant differences.

arxiv:2608.06088.rationale: Moderate technical quality in software-testing domain but low relevance to core LLM/NLP preferences: the LLM is used as a black-box tool for code segmentation/mutation rather than studied. Evaluations include ablations and statistical tests, but are limited to Isaac Sim with few runs; generalizability is weak and reproducibility relies on an unverified package claim.
evidence: Abstract: proposes IcFuzz, first fuzzing approach for Isaac Sim, with LLM-based semantic stage segmentation, multi-level mutation, and MAB.
Sec. 3.1.2: describes chain-of-thought prompt and LLM segmentation; Sec. 4.3.2 reports 93.5% average segmentation accuracy.
Sec. 4.3, Table 2: IcFuzz (GPT-5-mini) covers 20,771 lines vs 10,136 Atheris and 10,940.7 GzFuzz; 3.7 unique crashes vs 0 for baselines.
Sec. 4.4, Table 5/6: ablations show coverage drops when removing object/operation/argument-level operators; UCB outperforms random by 1,200.7 lines.
Sec. 5: threats to validity note only Isaac Sim evaluated and transfer requires engineering; Data Availability states Zenodo replication package.

arxiv:2608.06085.rationale: Relevant LLM evaluation/fairness study with a thoughtful randomized provenance design; main disclosure attenuation result is null and the panel is small/post-hoc, while verified-country utility is consistently positive; limited target/country/prompt coverage constrains generalizability.
evidence: Introduction: randomized provenance contrast with opaque/disclosed random labels and verified survey country; assesses direction and held-out Brier loss.
Experimental Design: five fixed API models, six countries, seven development-selected targets, two panels; no LLM judge; balanced assignment.
Results: disclosed-random movement βR=0.214, attenuation A=0.0003 [-0.0157,0.0166], verified utility UV=0.040 [0.024,0.056]; RQ1 p=0.498, RQ2 p<0.001.

Discussion and Limitations: authors note the separate 72-record panel was not prospectively powered, the mixed-coverage 504 panel is not a full seven-target replication, and external validity is limited.

arxiv:2608.06082.rationale: Out-of-scope applied weather-domain spatiotemporal forecasting. Uses a transformer encoder but no LLM/NLP/language methodology; relevance is minimal. The paper reports quantitative metrics and a U-Net baseline but has limited novelty, no ablations or significance testing, single-region/dataset evaluation, and no code availability.
evidence: Page 1 abstract and Section 3.4 (pages 4-8) indicate the method uses DenseNet, residual connections, and a transformer encoder for precipitation nowcasting.
Page 10 Table 3 reports 30-minute MAE 0.235, RMSE 0.735, KGE 0.816 and comparison with a U-Net baseline.
Page 8 Section 3.5 gives training details using GPM IMERG data, Adam optimizer, and 100 epochs, but does not mention code release.

arxiv:2608.06078.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application in astronomy/cosmology/particle physics with no LLM/NLP or language-methodology focus. The paper provides a descriptive test bed for Bayesian samplers with characterization axes and a Docker image, but lacks comparative algorithm evaluation or strong empirical validation, limiting rigor and evidence.
evidence: Abstract states the paper studies parametric Bayesian inference applications from astronomy, cosmology and particle physics and proposes a standard test bed for samplers.
Section 3 defines characterization axes including dimensionality, information gain, modes, non-Gaussianity, tail weight, inequality, and phase transitions.
Table 1 lists the collated problems and derived characteristics.
Section 5.1 discusses strengths and limitations and notes availability of a reproducible GitHub/Docker installation.

arxiv:2608.06075.rationale: The paper uses a commercial VLM/generative editor inside an agentic candidate-selection pipeline for shadow removal, matching Agents & Tool Use, Multimodal AI, and Prompting topics, but it remains a domain-specific computer-vision application with shallow language-method contribution. Quantitative benchmark and ablation results are present, but there is no statistical testing, limited generalization beyond shadow removal, and non-shadow preservation is worse than prior methods.
evidence: Table 1 reports Ours-Physics mean CDD 7.45 (displayed x10^3) vs SRR 14.06, supporting the claimed CDD improvement.
Table 2 shows selected variants improve over probe-only variants and physics-oriented prompting outperforms generic prompting.
Table 3 reports Ours-Physics non-shadow RGB RMSE 28.79 vs SID 3.44, evidencing preservation limitations.

arxiv:2608.06445.rationale: Out-of-scope domain application of inverse reinforcement learning and game-theoretic QRE to traffic cut-in prediction; no LLM/NLP/agent/reasoning methodology. The work is detailed and quantitative but limited by single-dataset evaluation, no cross-validation or significance testing, and baseline comparability concerns; overall capped due to out-of-scope domain application.
evidence: Section 4.2 describes L-BFGS-B, focal loss, and threshold optimization but no cross-validation or statistical significance testing.
Section 5.2 Table 3 reports IRL Enhanced accuracy 76.4% while Section 4.1 shows a majority-class proportion of 78.5% Stay, making the trivial majority baseline superior in overall accuracy.
Section 3.4.1 states the Wang et al. benchmark was calibrated on NGSIM, whereas Section 4.1 states all models were calibrated using highD, raising baseline comparability concerns.

arxiv:2608.06069.rationale: Relevant LLM training-free adaptation with RAG/token-level steering for co-writing; not an out-of-scope pure domain application. Broad empirical comparisons exist, but there are no significance tests/confidence intervals and no explicit limitations section; SOTA claim is limited to selected training-free baselines.
evidence: Section 1 introduces SteerWrite as a training-free token-level framework for personalized co-writing and states code/resources are available at the GitHub link.
Table 1 reports SteerWrite versus seven training-free baselines across CodeNet, HMR, UER, and Law for Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B/4B.
Appendix C reports generalization results on Llama-3.2-1B and Llama-3.2-3B using the CodeNet dataset.
Appendix F ablation shows removing rank-based calibration or temporal momentum degrades performance across Qwen3 model sizes.
Section 6.3 and Table 3 report TTFT and TPOT latency showing only modest overhead.
Appendix A Table 4 gives dataset statistics, with HMR test and supplementary subsets each having only 10 documents.

arxiv:2608.06068.rationale: Relevant to LLM/RAG/explainability preferences as a conversational search demo, but it is an HCI/IR system demonstration with no quantitative evaluation, limited novelty beyond hybrid LLM/ranker separation, and descriptive rather than empirical evidence.
evidence: Abstract: describes Cleo as a transparent and controllable conversational product advisor with a hybrid architecture separating deterministic ranking from language generation.
Section 3.4: deterministic ranking uses categorical filters and numeric loss functions over 3,638 laptop specifications.
Section 3.5: response generation follows RAG principles grounded in current user requirements and laptop recommendations.
Section 4: acknowledges limitations including rigid loss weights and mental workload, and proposes future user studies; no quantitative evaluation is reported.

arxiv:2608.06065.rationale: Highly relevant GUI-agent/VLM training work involving RL, reasoning traces, and privileged future-state distillation. Method is a moderate extension of hindsight/privileged-information distillation with controlled ablations and quantitative gains, but scope is limited to two agent benchmarks and two Qwen VLM backbones; no significance testing or explicit limitations section.
evidence: Table 3 reports controlled SFT/GRPO/GHD Pass@1 means and std over three runs on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.
Table 2 isolates component gains from GRPO (47.13) to +Gate (47.84), +DS (49.56), and full GHD (52.73).
Table 4 shows next observation as privileged info yields the largest gain (+5.62 over SFT) versus action/reasoning only.
Experimental Setup specifies base models, hardware, learning rate, group size, lambda, top-K, and optimization steps.

arxiv:2608.06062.rationale: Out of scope as pure chart/document computer vision with no language/NLP/LLM methodology; only tangential transformer and CV relevance. The paper has moderate internal rigor and ablations, but the strict out-of-scope cap limits the total score.
evidence: Abstract: states pipeline uses JEPA encoder and decoders to recover per-bar numerical values from bar charts.
Section 3.2: describes I-JEPA finetuning with variable-resolution patch extraction and ViT encoder.
Table 1: reports F1 and accuracy for variable/fixed/vanilla models on UB PMC and synthetic charts.
Section 5: lists limitations including only vertical bar charts, no SoTA, and difficulty integrating with multimodal language models.

arxiv:2608.06061.rationale: This is a cryptographic note on zero-length nonce key recovery for GCM/GMAC. It matches none of the target preferences (LLMs, NLP, agents, AI safety/ML, etc.) and is out of scope. The note provides mathematical definitions and an attack sketch but no empirical evaluation or broad applicability.
evidence: Abstract: states attack recovers the GCM/GMAC hash key using a zero-length nonce
Section 1: frames prior GCM/GMAC cryptanalysis and standards
Section 3: presents the zero-length nonce attack and forgery equations

arxiv:2608.06060.rationale: Highly relevant to reasoning/CoT, multimodal retrieval, RL, and embedding training. The retrieval-feedback CoT idea is reasonably novel, and the paper reports broad multimodal evaluation, but quantitative tables are placeholders, with no significance tests or explicit limitations, reducing rigor and evidence strength.
evidence: Abstract introduces UniME-R1 with RC-CoT, dual-mode embedder, hard negatives, and GRPO.
Section 4.4 reports MMEB-V2 overall scores of 69.9 (2B) and 70.3 (4B).
Section 5.1 reports query-only CoT 65.6, random candidates 66.5, actual top-k 68.5, and removing <cot_focus> lowers to 67.9.
Tables 1-5 are presented as nicematrix placeholders lacking quantitative content.

arxiv:2608.06059.rationale: Domain-specific continual remote sensing image-text retrieval. It is cross-modal and uses CLIP-style dual encoders, giving modest multimodal AI relevance, but it is remote-sensing-focused with little LLM/NLP/agent relevance. The method (spatial fusion adapter, routed text experts, ranking distillation) is a reasonable but incremental combination; evaluation is fairly extensive with baselines, ablations, and some significance tests, but lacks an explicit limitations section and generalization beyond RS benchmarks is limited.
evidence: Section 4.2, Table 2 reports DARAD's task-wise C-mR and F-mR with standard deviations over five runs.
Section 4.3, Table 3 reports ablations showing that removing BRD leads to negative F-mR values.
Section 4.4, Table 4 reports ranking-consistency metrics (Kendall tau, Spearman rho, Overlap@10) favoring BRD over Feature KD and Replay + Feature KD.
Section 4.1 provides implementation details, including ViT-B/32, Top-2 routing, 1,000 historical anchors, AdamW, learning rates, and batch size.

arxiv:2608.06057.rationale: Core LLM agent/tool-use robustness paper with strong relevance to agents and tool calling. The controlled paired benchmark, ablations, and external transfer results are credible, though synthetic two-domain construction and unverifiable supplement claims limit full confidence.
evidence: Table 3 reports Oracle-OPD BTA 0.8703 versus Gold-SFT 0.6628 and off-policy OD 0.8499 on Test-Indist.
Table 6 isolates teacher view, soft supervision, and student prefix source, showing Oracle-OPD at 0.8703 BTA.
Appendix B reports a stratified 1,000-example cross-audit with 92.5% human/model agreement.
Table 8 shows external BFCL, When2Call, and hallucination transfer for the 1.7B deployment model.
Appendix C documents training hyperparameters, pipeline scripts, and cost, though the supplement itself is not externally verified.

arxiv:2608.06053.rationale: Out-of-scope econometrics/statistics paper on fixed-effect saturation, weak identification, and measurement error in panel regressions. It does not address LLMs, NLP, reasoning, prompting, RAG, agents, safety, alignment, multimodal AI, or any listed preference area. Despite apparent formal content, simulations, and applications, preference_relevance is 0.0 and the overall score is capped at 0.20 under the out-of-scope rule.
evidence: Abstract: focus is fixed-effect saturation, Stock-Yogo-style critical values, and classical measurement error; no language-model or NLP content.
Section 1 Introduction: frames the problem as an econometric analogy to weak instruments in fixed-effect OLS.
Section 7 Applications: empirical cases are democracy-growth panels and PSID earnings, not LLM/NLP tasks.

arxiv:2608.06049.rationale: Relevant to interpretability/explainability but not LLM/NLP methodology; conceptual requirements-engineering paper with no quantitative evaluation, baselines, or systematic review. Proposes definitions and a taxonomy, illustrated by a case study, but evidence is qualitative and limited.
evidence: Section VIII states the work relies exclusively on qualitative data analysis and acknowledges possible subjectivity and limited literature coverage.
Section VI presents traffic-management scenarios S-1 and S-2 but reports no quantitative results or empirical evaluation.
Sections IV-V propose definitions and requirements; no experiments, baselines, or ablations are reported.

arxiv:2608.06046.rationale: The paper addresses distributed ML training/network co-optimization, not LLM/NLP methods; it is only tangentially relevant via Training & Optimization and Scaling/Efficiency. The joint-knob perspective is moderately novel, but the study is preliminary: limited to two knobs, one foreground model, simulated replay traces, and no error bars or code/data release.
evidence: Section 3.2 reports Decoupled first-crossing-time ratios of 1.13-1.42x relative to Joint at 1.01 L_min under GPT-1B background loads.
Section 3.3 reports Joint reaches all four target losses first, with Decoupled slowdown 5.4-20.8%.
Section 3.1 describes the two-knob setup (BF16/MXFP4, GA4/GA16) and timing model T_iter = gT_c + T_dp.

arxiv:2608.06043.rationale: Pure database/query optimization paper on SQL window functions; no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agents, or other preference topics. Formal definitions and experiments exist within its domain, but out of scope and synthetic microbenchmarks limit overall assessment.
evidence: Section 1: contributions and claims
Section 6: Co-Evaluation definition
Section 8: experimental speedups up to 40.7x
Artifact Availability: code at GitHub

arxiv:2608.06041.rationale: Strong relevance to LLMs, code generation, reasoning-trace analysis, and evaluation. The benchmark is a useful but incremental contribution; rigor is moderate due to single-annotator trace labeling and limited statistical testing, while quantitative evidence across 25 models is substantial. Generalizability is bounded to project-level programming-language choice. Reproducibility is strong with released data, code, package, and detailed metric definitions.
evidence: Abstract reports 35.3% Python implementation rate vs 10.7% Python recommendation rate and 9,826 reasoning traces analyzed.
Section 3.2 describes construction over 7 areas and 28 tasks, validated by two developers with 87.8% specific agreement on the weak label.
Section 4.2 reports average recommendation-implementation rate of 48.8% and mean alignment of 0.17 across 25 LLMs.
Section 5.2 reports trace classifications: 69.8% automatic Python, 20.5% Python for ease, 7.8% phantom evidence, 1.9% language mismatch.
Appendix A.1 lists GitHub, Hugging Face, and PyPI availability; Appendix A.5 gives precise metric definitions.

arxiv:2608.06037.rationale: Pure medical imaging application using graph-based multiple instance learning and self-supervised patch representations. No LLM, language, reasoning, agent, or NLP methodology; relevant only peripherally via GNN, computer vision, and medical AI preferences. Per out-of-scope rule for medical imaging and pure domain applications, score is capped at 0.20. Rigor and evidence are limited but present; no strong novelty or generalizability beyond the two skin lesion datasets.
evidence: Abstract: Experimental results on the ISIC-2018 and ISIC-2019 skin lesion diagnosis benchmarks.
Methodology: Graph construction over patch representations and GNN with MIL pooling.
Availability of data and software code: code available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

arxiv:2608.06033.rationale: Relevant mainly as agent-serving infrastructure rather than LLM/NLP/reasoning methodology. The paper offers a formal network-control formulation and a safety theorem, but evidence is limited to small paired replay studies with modest effect sizes and some confidence intervals including zero.
evidence: Section IV-A reports all 20 evaluation tasks expose at least one result-conditioned call bindable before connection (94/124 calls).
Section IV-C/Fig. 8 reports moderate-contention gains of 8.75 points over rolling horizon (95% CI 1.25-17.5) and 10 points over CATS (1.25-20.0), while saturation differences include zero.
Section IV-B/Fig. 6 reports Docker latency reductions under contention but also a forecast-miss delay penalty.
Theorem 1 in Section III-I provides hard feasibility guarantees under declared demand bounds.

arxiv:2608.06031.rationale: Graph/dynamic-graph MoE paper is only weakly within stated preferences (GNN category; MoE mention), with no LLM/NLP/agent/safety relevance. Novelty is moderate: combines dynamic graph prompting, Riemannian experts, and topology-routed MoE, but builds directly on existing DyGPrompt and mixed-curvature expert work. Rigor is moderate: broad baselines and ablations, but no significance tests or explicit limitations/failure analysis. Evidence from Tables 1-3 and Figs 3-4 supports mixed-curvature gains, routing adaptation, and component contributions. Four datasets and transductive/inductive settings aid generalizability, but domain is narrow. Reproducibility is partial: environment, dataset statistics, and architecture details are provided, but code/checkpoints are not stated and auxiliary-loss sensitivity is acknowledged.
evidence: Table 1 reports AUC-ROC across Wikipedia, Reddit, MOOC, and Genre, showing CurvPrompt best on all 8 link-prediction settings and 2 of 4 node-classification settings.
Table 2 ablation on Reddit and MOOC shows degradation when removing topology routing, expert prompts, geometric regularization, balancing, or experts.
Table 3 compares Mixed Curvature, Single Curvature, and Euclidean MoE with matched expert count, attributing gains partly to multi-curvature specialization.
Figure 3 shows temporal shifts in Reddit expert gate usage, indicating routing redistributes mass across curvature regimes over days.
Appendix A.1 lists OS/CPU/GPU/RAM environment and Appendix A.2 provides dataset statistics.

arxiv:2608.06030.rationale: Out-of-scope pure computer vision/chart extraction work with no language-model methodology beyond VLM baselines. Although it is a competent niche CV pipeline with synthetic quantitative evaluation, ablations, and released code, the absence of quantitative real-world evidence and limited scope cap it at 0.20.
evidence: Abstract claims the first deep learning approach for parallel coordinate data extraction and provides a GitHub link for code/models/data scripts.
Section 5.2 reports quantitative LC-MAE and sAP comparisons against VLMs, DHT, and DHLP on the synthetic test set.
Section 7 states the absence of quantitative evaluation on annotated real images and limits scope to standard straight polyline parallel coordinates with regular axes.
Section 3.2 describes a synthetic dataset with 5,000 training/validation images and 1,000 test images.
Section 4 describes the pipeline: cropping, category separation, U-Net restoration, DHLP extraction, and masked filtering.

arxiv:2608.06027.rationale: Relevant LLM-driven voice agent with structured form filling and a Hindi benchmark, though application-heavy rather than core LLM methodology. Moderate novelty relative to existing voice-agent benchmarks, but grounded in a real maternal-health deployment. Rigor is decent with multi-model component and end-to-end benchmarking, confidence intervals, and calibration, but evaluation uses only 5 simulated users and scripted Hindi speech, limiting external validity. Quantitative evidence supports the main claims, including propagation/cancellation of errors and rule-based recovery. Generalizability is constrained to one low-resource form, one language, and rural Indian users. Reproducibility is aided by prompts, implementation details, and a code/data link, but hosted APIs and no determinism reduce confidence.
evidence: Table 4 reports per-turn extraction accuracy across 11 LLMs with reference and three STT transcripts.
Table 5 reports form-completion accuracy, and Section 5.4 notes drops of up to about 41 percentage points with error-prone transcripts.
Section 7 Conclusion acknowledges limitations: scripted answers, five simulated users, Hindi-only coverage, and no TTS evaluation.
Appendix C provides 95% confidence intervals, and Appendix B describes LLM-judge calibration on a 50-test held-out batch.

arxiv:2608.06025.rationale: Pure reinforcement-learning/simulation-systems performance tuning with no LLM, NLP, or language-based agent methodology; out of scope for this curation rubric despite touching RL and inference preferences. Method is an incremental combination of physics-informed prediction, queueing constraints, and feedback tuning; evaluation has some ablations and baselines but limited rigor and internal inconsistencies.
evidence: Section 4.2 reports AutoThread saves up to 83.8% runtime vs ADAPT-T and 18.4% average speedup over Static, but no confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.
Section 4.3 reports PCS average throughput 536.83, below Reinforcer's 718.55, conflicting with the abstract's claimed throughput advantage over Reinforcer.
Algorithm 1 line 16 contains an apparent self-comparison 'usr_cpu<usr_cpu', indicating a likely control-flow typo in the proposed tuning algorithm.

arxiv:2608.06023.rationale: This is a pure domain affective-computing paper on physiology-to-video knowledge distillation for emotion recognition. It does not involve LLMs, NLP, language methodology, or language-model-related areas, so it is out of scope under the rubric and capped at 0.20. Although it reports ablations, quantitative results, and implementation details, the preference relevance is minimal and the contribution is domain-specific rather than aligned to listed AI topics.
evidence: Abstract: proposes BioKD, a reliability-aware physiology-to-video knowledge distillation framework for emotion recognition.
Section IV-A: evaluates on DEAP and AMIGOS multimodal emotion recognition benchmarks.
Section IV-C: reports ablation study on DEAP arousal under subject-wise protocol.
Section III-D: describes progressive distillation strategy with staged training objectives.

arxiv:2608.06022.rationale: This is an LLM benchmark for antibody/epitope reasoning, which is a domain-specific biomedical application rather than a core language-model methodology contribution. While it touches LLMs, reasoning, CoT prompting, and evaluation, the antibody-drug-discovery focus places it near the out-of-scope domain-application boundary. The paper provides structured task definitions, baselines, ablations, and failure analysis, but lacks statistical significance testing and uses unverifiable/future model names; generalizability is limited to epitope-centered decisions.
evidence: Section 3.2 defines five benchmark tasks: targetable region discovery, antibody-conditioned epitope identification, epitope binning, functional epitope assessment, and escape assessment.
Table 2 reports zero-shot performance of nine LLMs with random and specialized-model baselines.
Section 4.2 stratifies Tasks 1-4 by antigen sequence length.
Section 4.3 compares explicit CoT prompting with an implicit direct-answer setting.
Appendix C.1 provides prompt templates and a deterministic JSON output format.

arxiv:2608.06021.rationale: Out-of-scope pure robotics/visual localization with no LLM, NLP, reasoning, agentic, or language-model methodology. Technically it presents a modular topometric VPR plus feed-forward 3D localization framework with benchmarks and ablations, but relevance is minimal and the contribution is domain-specific and incremental; no statistical significance is reported and code is only promised upon acceptance.

arxiv:2608.06020.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, agentic economies, multi-agent simulation, and RL training environments, but this is a systems roadmap/survey rather than an empirical ML contribution. It provides a conceptual six-level taxonomy and code-like protocols, yet lacks quantitative experiments, baselines, ablations, and external validation of its LLM-assisted classification pipeline.
evidence: Section 1 defines Economic World Models as generative engines and describes iterative co-improvement between economic agents and the EWM.
Section 3.2 reports a three-stage LLM-assisted screening pipeline from 7,836 candidate papers yielding 737 validated EWM papers.
Section 4.2 presents specification and runtime interfaces for agents, environments, co-evolution, and real-world alignment as code-like protocols.
Section 8 acknowledges open challenges including behavioral realism, economic closure, co-evolution, scalability, and world-level evaluation.

arxiv:2608.06015.rationale: Relevant LLM+RL paper using LLM-generated programmatic dynamics priors, but the contribution is primarily RL initialization rather than LLM/NLP methodology. The integration is reasonably novel, though many components exist in prior LLM world-model and LLM-enhanced RL work. Evidence is moderate: aggregate Gym/DMControl results and ablation/transfer/robustness analyses support sample-efficiency gains, but per-task details are relegated to an appendix, the backbone baseline is anonymized, and no code availability is stated. Empirical scope is limited to state-based continuous control, which constrains generalizability and reproducibility.
evidence: Table 1 (Section 5.2) compares aggregate normalized Gym and DMControl returns with and without ProDVI, reporting bootstrap confidence intervals.
Table 2 (Section 5.3) reports Deep-SAC-normalized Gym scores for transfer to SAC-based variants.
Table 3 (Section 5.4) reports large LLM-generated dynamics prediction errors, ruling out accurate simulation as the source of gains.
Table 4 (Section 5.4) compares dynamics predictor training losses from scratch versus dynamics-prior initialization.
Table 5 (Section 5.5) reports results using two independently generated dynamics-prior programs.

arxiv:2608.06014.rationale: Methodologically careful controlled study of test-time iterative refinement for LiDAR semantic scene completion under corruption, with preregistered contrast, paired bootstrap intervals, and release audits. However, this is pure 3D/computer vision/robustness research with no language-model, NLP, agent, reasoning, prompting, or multimodal-language methodology. The rubric explicitly caps pure computer vision or domain-application work at 0.20, and the paper does not fit the stated preferences beyond a weak robustness keyword.
evidence: Section 5 reports primary contrast: augmented-base refiner gains 0.911 mIoU over parameter-matched wide control under occ40, 95% bootstrap interval [0.804, 1.040].
Section 5.5 Table 3 reports full refiner cost: 4.217M parameters, 214.8 GFLOPs, 10.74 ms, 0.75 GiB.
Section 9 reports automated release gate loading all 40 final checkpoints and verifying completion markers, hashes, and registered arguments.

arxiv:2608.06013.rationale: Strongly relevant via MLLM reasoning, GRPO RL, multimodal training, and dataset construction. Not out-of-scope because methodology is language-model-centric rather than pure CV/audio. Evidence is moderately strong with multiple benchmarks, ablations, and human evaluation, but main results lack confidence intervals, repeated runs, and significance tests; closed-model baselines and LLM-judge reliability are not fully verifiable. Novelty is mostly integration of existing SFT/RL components into a unified affective pipeline.
evidence: Abstract: describes OneEmo, EmoWorld-130K, and Emo-Chord with state-of-the-art claims
Section V-A Implementation Details: reports training hyperparameters and code availability
Table II: reports main results on emotion perception and understanding against baselines
Table V: reports ablation study of reward functions
Section VI-E: reports two-backbone generalization experiments
Section IX Limitations and Future Works: acknowledges dataset and deployment limitations

arxiv:2608.06012.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, RAG/grounding, reward hacking, and RLHF safety. The paper presents a careful paired counterfactual audit with detector-lattice ablation, CIs, exact zero-event bounds, and limitations, but policy-transfer evidence is constrained by one matched run and narrow structured-citation benchmarks, limiting generalizability.
evidence: Introduction: RL increasingly trains language models to search, call tools, and answer with citations; reward decomposition includes evidence support and anti-hacking terms.
Reward-Audit Results/Table 2: reports ASR for same-final, laundering, and fake-ID attacks with zero-event upper bounds.
Experimental Setup: describes strict 5M-token matched Search-GRPO runs and paired tail evaluation.
Limitations: states structured citation IDs/local retrieval only; dense retrieval and free-form citations remain untested; one matched run per arm.

arxiv:2608.06009.rationale: Paper is character animation via video diffusion, a pure computer vision/video generation application without language-model methodology; text-driven viewpoint LoRA is a control interface, not NLP. Out of scope per rubric. Within its domain, it proposes dual-branch DiT, time-aligned RoPE, sparse attention, and distillation for real-time animation, but evidence is mostly qualitative with a user study and one hardware-specific fps figure; lacks ablations, quantitative metrics, limitations.
evidence: §5.3 Comparison with State-of-the-Art presents only qualitative comparison
§5.4 User Study reports preferences but no statistical details or sample sizes
§5.5 Real-Time Inference reports 24 fps at 400x720 on 4-GPU cluster
§6 Conclusion contains no limitations section
Abstract claims model weights will be released but no code/data availability details

arxiv:2608.06008.rationale: Autonomous driving video-diffusion/world-model paper using Wan2.2-5B and trajectory diffusion heads. It has no LLM/NLP/language methodology and is a pure embodied/domain application with video diffusion, so it is capped at or below 0.20. Internal experiments and ablations are moderately detailed, but the topic is out of scope for the stated preferences.
evidence: Abstract: describes Adaptive-WAM on a Wan2.2-5B video diffusion backbone for driving trajectory planning without language methodology.
Section 4 Method: defines multi-exit trajectory decoding, DINOv2-Small scorer, and quality-guided adaptive inference.
Section 5 Experiments: reports 90.8 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and zero-shot nuScenes 0.88m L2 / 0.08% collision.
Appendix M: states passing the quality threshold is not a formal safety certificate.

arxiv:2608.06007.rationale: LLM-serving systems paper directly matching LLM, inference serving, KV cache, and agent-workload preferences. It offers a coherent tensor lifecycle abstraction and quantitative vLLM/SGLang evaluations, but novelty is incremental over specialized tensor management systems, with limited ablations/no error bars and training-scope applicability only discussed rather than implemented.
evidence: §6.1 reports TensorCast-cold reduces Qwen3-30B-A3B weight load time by 60.7x vs Default and reduces end-to-end ready time by 28.5x.
§6.3 reports KV-cache TTFT reductions comparable to Mooncake with RDMA and better without RDMA for Qwen3-32B and Qwen3-235B-A22B.
§6.4 reports median TTFT reductions of 71.4%, 93.2%, and 70.4% for fast, medium, and slow agent workloads compared with a Mooncake load-aware router.

arxiv:2608.06004.rationale: Low preference relevance: tabular foundation model/transformer evaluation, not language or agent methodology, though it uses foundation-model and transformer concepts. Within its domain, the work is formally and empirically strong: it defines testable consistency conditions, proves their relationship, and evaluates multiple TFMs across many datasets with detailed quantitative results.
evidence: Section 3.1 defines marginalization consistency
Section 3.2 defines factorization consistency
Table 1 reports total-variation violations across models and datasets
Table 2 reports factorization-consistency violations
Appendix B provides dataset and preprocessing details
Appendix C describes regression discretization

arxiv:2608.06002.rationale: Pure biostatistics/causal-inference simulation of treatment-effect heterogeneity and discrimination metrics; no LLM, NLP, transformer, agent, or language methodology. Out-of-scope domain application, so preference relevance and overall score are capped low.
evidence: Abstract: 'Analyzing the heterogeneity of treatment effects is crucial in personalized medicine...' indicates a medical/statistical scope rather than AI/LLM.
Methods: defines CATE as tau=Pi^1-Pi^0 and specifies Beta/Dirichlet distributions for numerical simulation.
Results: reports ranges for PAPE, concentration of benefit, and c-statistic for benefit across 20 simulated distributions.
Discussion: notes limitation that the oracle c-statistic for benefit requires specifying the joint distribution of potential outcomes.

arxiv:2608.06001.rationale: Pure domain application of hybrid ML to precision livestock/agriculture, with no LLM, NLP, transformer, reasoning, agent, or language methodology. Only weak tangential relevance via data/training/interpretability preferences. Out-of-scope cap applies. The paper reports baseline comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and limitations, but uses a single enterprise and lacks external validation or code/data availability.
evidence: Abstract: describes hybrid ML framework for herd-level cattle weight forecasting using ARIMA, LSTM, GRU and GB/RF/SVR/XGBoost-NN hybrids.
Section 2.5: defines baselines ARIMA, LSTM, GRU and residual/stacked/cascade/ensemble-assisted hybrid architectures.
Section 3.2 Table 9: reports ARIMA R² 0.701, RMSE 31.844; cascade GB→RF→NN R² 0.889, RMSE 21.319.
Section 4.6: limitations include single grazing enterprise, no external validation, and random sparsity removal not fully representing systematic visitation gaps.

arxiv:2608.05999.rationale: Robotics-heavy VLA/embodied manipulation work; matches some preference areas (multimodal VLA, RL, task planning) but the core domain is robotic manipulation, which limits preference relevance. The method combines existing hierarchical planning, SFT, and GRPO components, with quantitative LIBERO results and ablations but no statistical tests or code release, and some reporting inconsistencies.
evidence: Methodology, Training Planner by SFT: planner is optimized via SFT to generate subgoals conditioned on current observations.
Experiments, Table 1: HiRoC reports average success rates across LIBERO suites, including 93.5 overall.
Ablation Study: removing the planner is reported to degrade final performance.
Conclusion: future work is limited to end-to-end training and robust decomposition for real-world uncertainty.

arxiv:2608.05995.rationale: The paper is a rigorous uncertainty-disentanglement benchmark and formalization, but it is not LLM/NLP/agent/transformer work; only tangential AI-safety relevance via safety-critical uncertainty. Theory, ablations, and reproducibility are solid, but the semi-synthetic GP tabular setting and MSE-only oracle limit generalizability.
evidence: Section 5.2 reports most epistemic Spearman correlations below 0.5 and states no method is uniformly reliable.
Section 6 admits the oracle is restricted to GP-generated semi-synthetic regression under squared-error/MSE risk.
Appendix D specifies hyperparameter search spaces and implementation details supporting reproducibility.

arxiv:2608.05993.rationale: Relevant LLM/NLP synthetic-data survey with clinical application; weighted down because most evidence is on held-out synthetic data and transfer to authentic communication is largely unproven.
evidence: Page 2, Section 1: scope pipeline clinical source → LLM-generated communication → downstream healthcare NLP model
Page 7, Table 6: headline results for thirteen application studies
Page 15, Section 4.1: train-on-synthetic, test-on-real protocol remains the field's most trustworthy yardstick
Page 17, Data and Code Availability: datasets, generation scripts, and model configurations shared in repository and Zenodo

arxiv:2608.05990.rationale: Highly relevant to LLM agents, tool use, and reward hacking/specification gaming, though domain-specific to optical experiments. Strong prespecified factorial design, statistical controls, and hardware transfer; moderate novelty and limited demonstrated generalization beyond optics.

evidence: Abstract: reports AgentOPSD results on ALFWorld, WebShop, and Search-QA with Qwen2.5-3B/7B and states code availability.

§3.4: reports hyperparameter sensitivity sweeps for λ, γ, and ε_high across configurations.
Appendix F: lists shared hyperparameters and environment-specific training configuration.

arxiv:2608.05983.rationale: Moderate relevance via adversarial robustness/red-teaming and vision-language segmentation, but not core LLM/NLP. The method is incremental over prior SAM universal attacks, with solid multi-dataset ablations and transfer evidence, though limited training set, no confidence intervals, and no code/availability weaken rigor and reproducibility.
evidence: Experiments > Comparison Study: UCD reduces average mask AP from 59.43 to 18.73 and average cgF1 from 50.32 to 20.49.
Ablation: Full UCD achieves 18.73 Mask AP Avg and 20.49 cgF1 Avg; removing feature divergence gives 57.45 Mask AP Avg and 44.33 cgF1 Avg.
Attack Transferability: SAM3-trained perturbation transfers to SAM3.1 with average mask AP dropping from 45.75 to 13.66.
Defense-Oriented Evaluation: prompt ensembling, lightweight head fine-tuning, and temporal filtering provide limited recovery without clean-performance cost.
